**Bottom line**: every library in the stack is mutually compatible on every target.
The matrix has **one open conflict with the contract**: Navigation.

### 1.2 The Navigation 3 Question (contract Section 16 trigger)

Contract Section 2 mandates **Navigation 3 (Nav3 — AndroidX Navigation Multiplatform / latest Nav3 APIs)**.

Contract Section 16 mandates: *"If Navigation 3 is not stable or compatible with the
selected Compose Multiplatform version, stop and propose the closest stable navigation
alternative before coding."*

Current state of Nav3 (verified via web search 2026-05-25):

- **AndroidX `androidx.navigation3`**: at `1.0.0-alpha10`. Still alpha; no stable release date announced. KMP targets (incl. iOS via Kotlin/Native) were added in alpha08 and are functional.
- **JetBrains port `org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation3:navigation3-ui`**: at `1.0.0-alpha05` (with `1.1.0-alpha01` previews). First-class CMP support shipped in CMP 1.10.0 (January 2026).
- **Stability classification**: alpha on both publication tracks. No vendor declares it production-ready.
- **iOS caveat**: Non-JVM targets cannot use reflection-based serialization → destination keys must be polymorphically serialized manually.
- **Web navigation**: deferred to Nav3 1.1.0.

The project currently uses **JetBrains Navigation Compose 2.9.2** which is fully stable
on all three targets and is already wired into every feature route (`AppNavHost` in
`App.kt:259+`, all 20 routes listed in baseline §4).

### 1.3 Options on the table

| Option | Pros | Cons | Contract compliance |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Stay on Navigation Compose 2.9.2** (the current code) | Fully stable on Android+iOS+Desktop, already integrated, zero risk to working features, satisfies functionality-preservation gate trivially. | Deviates from contract §2 (which says Nav3). Misses Nav3 ergonomics (direct stack manipulation, `RememberNavBackStack`, edge-pan gesture support). | §16: "Prefer stable APIs whenever possible" — satisfied. §2 mandate would be documented as a deviation. |
| **B. Adopt Nav3 alpha** (`org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation3` 1.0.0-alpha10 + JetBrains `navigation3-ui` 1.0.0-alpha05) | Satisfies contract §2 literally. Gets newer API ergonomics. | Alpha. APIs will change before stable. iOS serialization needs polymorphic `@Serializable` setup per destination key. Higher risk to functionality preservation gate. Requires rewriting all 20 routes. | §16 prefers stable; would record this as an accepted-risk decision. |
| **C. Voyager or Decompose** (community libs) | Both fully stable, both KMP-native. Decompose has been the gold standard for KMP nav for years. | Third-party, diverges from contract §2 entirely (which names AndroidX nav). Throwing away all current AndroidX nav code. Larger churn. | Diverges from contract §2 explicitly. |

### 1.4 Recommendation (per contract §16)

**Recommend Option A: Stay on Navigation Compose 2.9.2** and document the deviation.

Reasons:
1. Section 16 explicitly says "Prefer stable APIs whenever possible." Alpha → not preferred.
2. The functionality-preservation gate (no regressions, no broken features) is non-negotiable per the goal. Migrating to Nav3 alpha would require rewriting every route and risks subtle behavioral regressions.
3. The project's `kmp-migration` branch landed `2.9.2` precisely because it's stable on all three targets; the comment at libs.versions.toml line 15-18 records this finding.
4. We can revisit and migrate to Nav3 once it reaches RC/stable. The presentation layer will own routing via `:ui` so the swap will be local.

If the owner overrides this and picks B or C, document the choice here and proceed.

**This decision is the one outstanding Phase 1 question and the contract requires
stopping until the owner confirms.**

### 1.5 Decision (resolved 2026-05-25)

**Option A selected by owner.** The rework will stay on **JetBrains Navigation Compose
2.9.2** (`org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation:navigation-compose`). This is a documented
deviation from contract §2's literal "Navigation 3" requirement, taken under §16's
"Prefer stable APIs whenever possible" override.

Migration to Nav3 is deferred to a future task once Nav3 reaches RC/stable. The rework
will encapsulate routing inside `:ui` so the future swap is a single-module change.

Phase 2 (`:core` module) is now unblocked.

## Phase 2 — `:core` Module

### 2.1 Scope (per contract §4)

`:core` is the foundation layer — utilities, base classes, error types, dispatchers, base contracts.
It depends on nothing in the layer graph (no `:domain`, `:data`, `:presentation`, `:ui`, `:platform`).

### 2.2 Files added

| File | Purpose | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `core/build.gradle.kts` | KMP module — Android+Desktop+iOS targets, minimal deps | 75 |
| `core/src/commonMain/.../result/AppResult.kt` | Sealed Success/Failure wrapper carrying `AppError` (contract §10/§19) | 66 |
| `core/src/commonMain/.../error/AppError.kt` | Sealed `AppError` hierarchy: Network/Storage/Validation/Auth/Platform/Cancelled/Unexpected (contract §9) | 74 |
| `core/src/commonMain/.../dispatchers/DispatcherProvider.kt` | DI-friendly Dispatchers abstraction (contract §6 DIP, §13) | 53 |
| `core/src/commonMain/.../dispatchers/IoDispatcher.kt` (+ 3 actuals) | expect/actual for `Dispatchers.IO` (Native-internal workaround, documented per §12) | 4×~12 |
| `core/src/commonMain/.../logging/Logger.kt` | Kermit-backed SPI (contract §10) | 58 |
| `core/src/commonMain/.../flags/FeatureFlagProvider.kt` | Feature-flag SPI + in-memory default (contract §9) | 52 |

### 2.3 Build verification

| Target | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Android compile | `:core:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ passed |
| Desktop compile | `:core:compileKotlinDesktop` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (arm64) | `:core:compileKotlinIosArm64` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (sim) | `:core:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` | ✅ passed |
| Legacy app | `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ still passes (functionality-preservation gate green) |
| iOS framework link | n/a | not executed (Windows; deferred to macOS host) |

### 2.4 Decisions recorded

- **`platformIoDispatcher` expect/actual**: `Dispatchers.IO` is internal in `kotlinx-coroutines-core` 1.9.0 on Kotlin/Native. iOS actual routes to `Dispatchers.Default` per Kotlin coroutines KMP guidance. Documented in `IoDispatcher.kt` KDoc.
- **`Logger` adapter lives in `:core`**: the default behavior is identical on every platform (route to Kermit's global logger). When `:platform` ships a Crashlytics-aware logger, Koin swaps the binding without changing call sites.
- **`InMemoryFeatureFlagProvider`** is the production default until a remote-config backend ships. Map is immutable; flag mutation = binding swap (OCP-friendly).
- **No `:core` ↔ `:shared` package collision**: `:shared` continues to publish `me.manga.kira.core.ads.*` etc., `:core` claims new subpackages (`result`, `error`, `dispatchers`, `logging`, `flags`). Subpackages remain disjoint, so KMP compiles both modules into the same import-path root without conflicts.

### 2.5 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 2

All 7 source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md`. Phase 2 closed.

## Phase 3 — `:domain` Module (Library Slice)

### 3.1 Scope (per contract §4 + §15 step 3)

`:domain` is the pure-Kotlin contract layer — entities + repository interfaces + use cases.
Zero framework deps (no Compose, Room, Ktor, Koin, Coil, serialization).

The contract Build Order says "use cases for first feature" — so Phase 3 doesn't model
every feature at once. **Library** is the first feature slice (central, well-defined entities,
clear use cases). Remaining features land incrementally in later phases.

### 3.2 Files added

| File | Purpose | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `domain/build.gradle.kts` | KMP module, pure-Kotlin (no AGP-only plugins) | 67 |
| `domain/src/commonMain/.../model/Manga.kt` | Source-shape entity, no annotations | 28 |
| `domain/src/commonMain/.../model/LibraryManga.kt` | Manga + user-library metadata (addedAt, unreadCount) | 24 |
| `domain/src/commonMain/.../repository/LibraryRepository.kt` | Library aggregate root contract + `MangaKey` | 44 |
| `domain/src/commonMain/.../usecase/library/ObserveLibraryUseCase.kt` | Reactive library snapshot | 20 |
| `domain/src/commonMain/.../usecase/library/ToggleInLibraryUseCase.kt` | Library membership toggle policy | 29 |

### 3.3 Build verification

| Target | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Android compile | `:domain:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ passed |
| Desktop compile | `:domain:compileKotlinDesktop` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (arm64) | `:domain:compileKotlinIosArm64` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (sim) | `:domain:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` | ✅ passed |
| Legacy app | `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ still passes |
| iOS framework link | n/a | not executed (Windows; deferred to macOS host) |

### 3.4 Decisions recorded

- **Identity composition for `Manga`**: `api + language + title` triple — mirrors the legacy
  `SavedMangaEntity` composite PK. Required by the functionality-preservation gate: the future
  `:data` mapper must preserve wire-format compatibility with existing user libraries.
- **`MangaKey` as a typed composite**: carried explicitly rather than collapsed into a single
  string so callers can't accidentally mix encodings (URL-encoded title vs. raw, etc.).
- **`kotlin.time.Instant` over `kotlinx.datetime.Instant`**: contract §18 forbids deprecated
  APIs; `kotlinx.datetime.Instant` is a deprecated typealias in datetime 0.8.0. The kotlinx-datetime
  dep stays in :domain build.gradle (LocalDate / TimeZone remain needed).
- **Repository returns `AppResult` on mutations, `Flow` on reads**: contract §10/§19 require
  `AppResult` at module boundaries; reads stay reactive via `Flow` so the UI never sees stale data.
- **Use cases retained even when thin** (e.g. `ObserveLibraryUseCase`): contract §6 DIP requires
  presentation to depend on use cases, not repositories. Thin pass-through is the right SOLID
  shape even when the body is one line today.

### 3.5 What Phase 3 deliberately does NOT include

- Mappers from data DTOs / Room entities → `Manga` (those live in :data, Phase 4).
- Repositories for Chapter, History, Download, Source — added as their feature slices come up.
- Use cases for other features. Phase 3 establishes the pattern; future phases follow it.

### 3.6 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 3

All 5 source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md`. Phase 3 closed.

## 4. Phase 4 — `:data` module skeleton (Library slice)

### 4.1 Scope

Contract §4 / §15 Build Order step 4: introduce the `:data` module and ship the first concrete
repository implementation. Library slice was chosen first because it has the smallest surface
(6 methods) and the existing Room DAOs in `:shared` already cover every operation it needs, so
nothing in `:shared` had to change.

### 4.2 Module shape

- KMP module, same target set as `:core` / `:domain` / `:shared` (Android JVM_11, Desktop JVM_17,
  iosArm64, iosSimulatorArm64).
- Dependencies:
  - `api(project(":core"))` — `AppResult` / `AppError` cross the surface.
  - `api(project(":domain"))` — repository interfaces live here.
  - `implementation(project(":shared"))` — **transitional**. Provides `MangaDao` + `LibraryDeo`
    + `SavedMangaEntity` until Room relocates into `:data` in a later phase.
  - `kotlinx-coroutines-core`, `kotlinx-datetime` — for `Flow` and `Instant`.
- Forbidden in `:data`: Compose, presentation/UI types, Android-only SDK APIs (those go to `:platform`).
- No KSP / Room compiler in `:data` yet — Room generation still happens in `:shared`.

### 4.3 Files added

|---|---|---|
| `data/build.gradle.kts` | 73 | KMP module config with transitional `:shared` dep |
| `data/src/commonMain/.../data/mapper/LibraryMappers.kt` | 46 | `SavedMangaEntity` ↔ `Manga` / `LibraryManga` mappers (internal) |
| `data/src/commonMain/.../data/repository/LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt` | 152 | `LibraryRepository` impl wired through `MangaDao` + `LibraryDeo` |

Plus `settings.gradle.kts` (`include(":data")`).

### 4.4 Build-verification matrix

| Target | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Gradle configure | `:data:tasks` | ✅ passed |
| Android compile | `:data:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ passed |
| Desktop compile | `:data:compileKotlinDesktop` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (arm64) | `:data:compileKotlinIosArm64` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (sim) | `:data:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` | ✅ passed |
| Legacy app | `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ still passes |
| iOS framework link | n/a | not executed (Windows; deferred to macOS host) |

### 4.5 Decisions recorded

- **Transitional `:data → :shared` dep.** The safer alternative is to relocate Room into `:data`
  in this same phase. Rejected because Room schemas / KSP wiring / migrations have load-bearing
  Desktop-invalidation-tracker behavior (baseline §11, "Bug 3") that we will not risk on a
  late-night refactor pass. The dep is documented and time-bounded — it goes away when Room
  relocates in a later phase.
- **`observeLibrary()` mirrors `getDisplayItemsFlow` verbatim.** The legacy `LibraryRepository`
  in `:shared` combines `mangaDao.getAllSavedMangaFlow()` + `mangaDao.getAllChapterMetricsFlow()`
  instead of using the `LEFT JOIN ... GROUP BY` query — see baseline §11 for the Desktop
  `BundledSQLiteDriver` invalidation context. The new impl preserves this pattern verbatim.
- **Membership lookup uses `api + title`, not the full `(api, language, title)` triple.** The
  legacy schema's `getIdByApiAndTitle` ignores language, and the existing UI keys off the same
  pair. Preserving that wire format exactly avoids any observable behavior change. Language is
  still part of the domain `MangaKey` (forward-compat) and is round-tripped through the entity.
- **`runCatchingStorage` private helper.** All five suspend mutations wrap their bodies in the
  same `try`/`catch(CancellationException)`/`catch(Throwable) → AppError.Storage.Io` shape. The
  inline helper avoids the duplication. Cancellation is rethrown so structured concurrency works
  (contract §9 / §10).
- **`SavedMangaEntity.description` / `.status` default to `""` for new inserts** because the
  domain `Manga` doesn't carry them. Existing entries in the DB keep their values — only fresh
  add-to-library calls from the new path default. This matches what the legacy "add to library"
  path does for source-list adds where description isn't known yet.
- **No Koin binding yet.** `LibraryRepositoryImpl` is unwired. Phase 6+ (when the first
  feature ViewModel migrates) will add the Koin module that binds it. The existing legacy
  `MangaRepository` / `LibraryRepository` in `:shared` keep serving every current screen until
  then — observable behavior is unchanged.

### 4.6 What Phase 4 deliberately does NOT include

- Repositories for Chapter, History, Download, Source, Notification — added with their feature
  slices.
- Mappers for Chapter / History / Download — same.
- Relocation of Room entities, DAOs, or migrations into `:data` — deferred to a dedicated phase.
- Network (Ktor) data sources — added when the first networked feature migrates.
- Koin bindings — added when the first feature actually consumes the new repo.

### 4.7 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 4

All 3 source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md`. Phase 4 closed.

## 5. Phase 5 — `:platform` module (first SPI slice: AppVersionProvider)

### 5.1 Scope and migration strategy

Contract §4 / §15 Build Order step 5: introduce the `:platform` module. The legacy `:shared`
module currently houses ~25 expect/actual platform facades (per baseline §6). Migrating them
all in one phase would either (a) risk breaking the legacy app's compile or (b) require
extensive Strangler Fig plumbing.

Strategy chosen: **side-by-side SPIs**, not in-place relocation.

1. New SPI declared as an **interface** in `:platform/commonMain` (not `expect class`) — per
   contract §6 DIP: high-level defines interfaces; low-level implements; inject via Koin.
2. Per-target implementations in `:platform/{androidMain, iosMain, desktopMain}`.
3. The legacy `:shared` `expect class` stays untouched. Existing callers (`SharedModule`,
   `WhatsNewViewModel`, `AboutScreen`, `PlatformModule.*`) keep compiling and running.
4. Phase 6+ feature migrations rewire one consumer at a time from the legacy SPI to the new
   interface. The legacy `expect class` and its 3 actuals are deleted only when no caller
   remains.

Why interface over `expect class`:
- `expect class` couples the SPI shape to a specific Kotlin Multiplatform feature that can't
  be mocked or substituted in tests without writing platform-specific test doubles.
- An interface is trivially mockable (LSP) and can have multiple implementations on the same
  target (useful for fakes, in-memory variants, feature flags).
- Contract §6 explicitly favors DIP via interfaces.

### 5.2 Module shape

- KMP module, same target set as the others (Android JVM_11, Desktop JVM_17, iosArm64,
  iosSimulatorArm64).
- Dependencies:
  - `api(project(":core"))` — Logger / FeatureFlagProvider / DispatcherProvider are platform
    facade prerequisites.
  - `androidMain` adds `androidx-core-ktx` for Context conveniences when an SPI impl needs them.
  - No `:domain` / `:data` / `:shared` dep — platform facades are independent of business
    contracts.
- Android namespace `me.manga.kira.platform`. iOS framework name `platform`.

### 5.3 Files added (first slice)

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `platform/build.gradle.kts` | 70 | KMP module config |
| `platform/src/commonMain/.../platform/version/AppVersionProvider.kt` | 22 | SPI interface |
| `platform/src/androidMain/.../platform/version/AndroidAppVersionProvider.kt` | 20 | Android impl |
| `platform/src/iosMain/.../platform/version/IosAppVersionProvider.kt` | 17 | iOS impl |
| `platform/src/desktopMain/.../platform/version/DesktopAppVersionProvider.kt` | 13 | Desktop impl |

Plus `settings.gradle.kts` (`include(":platform")`).

### 5.4 Build-verification matrix

| Target | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Gradle configure | `:platform:tasks` | ✅ passed |
| Android compile | `:platform:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ passed |
| Desktop compile | `:platform:compileKotlinDesktop` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (arm64) | `:platform:compileKotlinIosArm64` | ✅ passed |
| iOS klib (sim) | `:platform:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` | ✅ passed |
| Legacy app | `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ still passes |
| iOS framework link | n/a | not executed (Windows; deferred to macOS host) |

### 5.5 Decisions recorded

- **Interface SPI shape**, not `expect class`. Rationale in §5.1.
- **`:shared` legacy SPIs left in place.** Zero changes to existing platform code in this
  phase — keeps the legacy compile and runtime path identical. The transition is gradual.
- **Package layout `me.manga.kira.platform.{category}.{Type}`.** Categories are functional
  (`version`, `intent`, `toast`, `files`, `crash`, `analytics`, `push`, …) so that as more SPIs
  land, the package tree stays grokkable.
- **No Koin module wired yet.** Feature migrations in Phase 6+ add the Koin binding next to
  the consumer's wiring. The `:shared` Koin modules are not touched.
- **Android impls take `Context` via constructor.** Same convention as the legacy `:shared`
  actuals — Koin's `androidContext()` injection plugs straight into the new impl unchanged.

### 5.6 SPIs deliberately deferred to later sub-phases

Per the Strangler Fig plan, the remaining ~24 platform facades are migrated as their feature
consumers move into the new layered code. Approximate batching:

1. **Phase 5.x — straightforward facades** (no callbacks, no streams):
   `IntentLauncher`, `ToastShower`, `AppFileSystem`, `FileSizeFormatter`, `LocaleProvider`,
   `ClipboardWriter`, `BrowserLauncher`.
2. **Phase 5.y — observable / push-style facades**:
   `NetworkConnectivity`, `NotificationPresenter`, `PushTokenProvider`, `ScreenshotProvider`,
   `BackgroundJobScheduler`.
3. **Phase 5.z — third-party service facades**:
   `AdProvider`, `AnalyticsClient`, `CrashReporter`, `ConsentFlowClient`,
   `RemoteDocStore`, `InAppReviewClient`, `AppUpdateClient`.
4. **Phase 5.w — image pipeline (load-bearing)**:
   `ImageDecoderRegistry`, `Base64ImageConverter`, `DominantColorExtractor`, `CbzWriter`.
   These must preserve all 6 load-bearing image-quality fixes verbatim (baseline §10).
5. **Phase 5.v — security / state**:
   `SecureStorage`, `SettingsFactory`, `AppStateMonitor`.

## 6. Phase 6.1 — `:presentation` module + base MVI contracts

### 6.1.1 Scope

Contract §4 / §15 Build Order step 6: introduce the `:presentation` module and the base MVI
plumbing every feature ViewModel will subclass. This phase ships ONLY the base contracts —
no feature-specific code. Phase 6.2 will add the first concrete slice (Library) that exercises
the contracts end-to-end across `:presentation` → `:domain` → `:data`.

### 6.1.2 Module shape

- KMP module, same target set (Android JVM_11, Desktop JVM_17, iosArm64, iosSimulatorArm64).

  - `api(libs.androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel)` (2.10.0) — KMP ViewModel base class lives here.
  - `api(libs.kotlinx.coroutines.core)` — StateFlow / Channel are public.
  - NO `:data` / `:platform` / `:shared` dep — ViewModels never touch the data layer directly

| Legacy app | `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✅ still passes |
| iOS framework link | n/a | not executed (Windows; deferred to macOS host) |

### 6.1.5 MVI contract decisions

- **Marker interfaces (`MviIntent`, `MviState`, `MviEffect`), not sealed classes.** The base
  contract itself is open — feature hierarchies are sealed within their own files. This lets
  the base ViewModel parameterize on `<S : MviState, I : MviIntent, E : MviEffect>` without
  forcing every feature to extend a shared sealed root (which would couple features at
  compile time).
- **`Channel<E>` with `Channel.UNLIMITED`** for effects. Rationale: effects must survive
  configuration changes and brief view detachment. A `SharedFlow` with replay=0 drops
  events while no collector is attached; an unlimited Channel buffers them. The contract's
  strict-MVI requirement that "effects fire exactly once" is preserved because Channels
  are single-consumer.
- **`submit(intent)` launches a fresh coroutine** in `viewModelScope` for each intent rather
  than feeding intents through a Channel into a single processing coroutine. Reason: features
  vary in their concurrency requirements (some serial, some parallel, some debounced). Putting
  the serialization choice in the feature ViewModel (via Mutex / actor) is more flexible than
  forcing one policy in the base.
- **`updateState` is a protected reducer hook**, not a public setter. Subclasses use it; the
  view cannot mutate state. Compile-time enforcement of the strict-MVI rule "State is owned
  by the ViewModel".
- **Local `MutableStateFlow.update` inline extension** rather than `import` of the public one.
  Avoids an additional import-line per feature for a one-line CAS loop; keeps the
  base file self-contained.

### 7.4 Reducer behavior decisions

- **Intents cover 9 user actions.** OnEnter / OnRefresh / OnItemClick / OnItemLongClick /
  OnSelectionToggle / OnSelectionClear / OnDeleteSelected / OnToggleInLibrary /
  OnSearchQueryChange. Adding more becomes a new sealed subclass and a new `when` arm
  (compile-time exhaustiveness).
- **Local search filtering.** Library is local-only; filtering an in-memory list is simpler
  than round-tripping through Room. The ViewModel holds the unfiltered snapshot in
  `allItems` (private field, NOT in state) and projects the filtered slice into
  `state.items`. Strict MVI is preserved because the view only ever sees `state.items`.
- **`OnEnter` is idempotent.** Calling it twice does not double-subscribe — the existing
  `observeJob` is checked for `isActive`. The view is free to re-fire OnEnter on every
  configuration change.
- **Selection mode toggles atomically with the selected set.** `isInSelectionMode = selection.isNotEmpty()`
  is computed inside `updateState` so the two fields never desync.
- **`OnDeleteSelected` emits the success effect but does not yet call the repository.**
  Bulk delete will land in a follow-up slice that adds `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` — the
  hook is here so the view can already wire up its confirmation dialog. The intermediate
  state cleanup (clear selection, exit selection mode) happens unconditionally so the UI
  behaves correctly even before the bulk wiring lands.
- **`OnRefresh` is a no-op for now.** Library is reactive (Room Flow emits on every write);
  swipe-to-refresh has no work to do beyond triggering the platform spinner animation.
  Kept as an Intent because the future remote-sync hook will reuse it.
- **Effect channel survives view detachment** (per Phase 6.1 base ViewModel). Bulk-remove
  success snackbars trigger reliably even if the user backs out and returns.
- **No `lateinit` / `!!` / `Any` in this file** — contract §6 forbids them in
  domain/presentation; the build would have caught it but worth restating.

### 8.7 Phase 7.x — Library composable end-to-end

First :presentation → :ui slice with a real screen. `LibraryScreen` collects state via
`StateFlow.collectAsState`, dispatches intents through `viewModel::submit`, and consumes
one-shot effects through `LaunchedEffect(effects) { effects.collect { … } }`. Snackbar
host owns the `ShowError` + `ShowBulkRemoveSuccess` UX; `NavigateToDetails` routes out
via an `onNavigateToDetails` callback (no Compose-Navigation coupling in the
composable — that's Phase 8's job).

**Stateful + stateless split.** `LibraryScreen` is the wired entry point; `LibraryScreenContent`
is the same Composable with explicit `state` / `effects` / `onIntent` parameters so previews
and screenshot tests don't need a real ViewModel. SRP between "wire to VM" and "render state".

**Scope discipline.** Visual parity with the legacy screen is **not** in this slice:
- No image loading. Cards render a tinted placeholder + title + unread badge.
- No filter/sort sheets, no swipe-to-refresh chrome, no tab strip — the new domain doesn't
  model those yet.
- No string resources — placeholder text is inlined. Localized resources migrate when

The legacy `composeApp/.../LibraryScreen.kt` (307 lines) is the user-facing binding and
keeps running. The Phase 8 swap only fires once the new screen reaches parity through
follow-up micro-slices.

| `DispatcherProvider` | `single` | Stateless delegation; pure singleton suffices. |
| `LibraryRepository` | `single` | Underlying DAOs are singletons; the impl holds no per-call state. A fresh instance per resolve would be wasteful. |

## 10. Phase 8.x — thread `allReworkModules()` through every host

### 10.1 Scope

Wire the rework feature graph into the live Koin container on every platform: Android,
Desktop, iOS. After this phase, `LibraryViewModel` + `LibraryRepository` resolve at
runtime on every host even though no UI route renders the new screen yet. The Phase 8.y
slice will then add a guarded debug route.

### 10.2 Signature change

`initKoin(appDeclaration: KoinAppDeclaration = {}): KoinApplication` becomes
`initKoin(extraModules: List<Module> = emptyList(), appDeclaration: KoinAppDeclaration = {})`.

**Parameter order matters.** `extraModules` sits FIRST and `appDeclaration` (function-type)
LAST so the idiomatic trailing-lambda syntax `initKoin(allReworkModules()) { … }` binds the
lambda unambiguously to `appDeclaration`. The first attempt put `extraModules` last with
`initKoin(extraModules = ...) { … }` and Kotlin's overload resolver couldn't combine the
named argument with the trailing lambda — `androidContext(...)` failed to resolve because
the lambda was inferred with the wrong receiver. Reordering fixed it.

The legacy zero-arg call (`initKoin()` from Desktop, `initKoin { … }` from Android) keeps
working because both parameters default.

`doInitKoin()` in `:shared/iosMain/KoinHelper.kt` gets the same defaulted
`extraModules: List<Module>` parameter.

### 10.3 iOS bridge — why a new file in `:composeApp/iosMain`

`:shared` cannot see `:composeApp` (module dependency direction). The iOS Swift entry
historically called `KoinHelperKt.doInitKoin()` which lives in `:shared/iosMain` and
therefore can't reference `allReworkModules()`. Phase 8.x adds
`composeApp/iosMain/.../di/IosKoin.kt::fun bootstrapIosKoin()` which sits at the right
layer (sees both `doInitKoin` from `:shared` and `allReworkModules()` from
`:composeApp/commonMain`) and the Swift `iOSApp.swift` swaps to call it.

### 10.4 Files changed

| File | Change | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `shared/.../di/KoinInitializer.kt` | signature | Add `extraModules` parameter; reorder so function-type is last. |
| `shared/iosMain/.../di/KoinHelper.kt` | signature | Same defaulted `extraModules` parameter. |
| `composeApp/iosMain/.../di/IosKoin.kt` | new | `bootstrapIosKoin()` Swift entry bridging `:shared`'s `doInitKoin` with `:composeApp`'s `allReworkModules()`. |
| `app/.../MyApp.kt` | call site | `initKoin(allReworkModules()) { androidLogger(); androidContext(this@MyApp); workManagerFactory(); modules(appKoinModule) }`. |
| `desktopApp/.../Main.kt` | call site | `initKoin(allReworkModules())`. |
| `iosApp/iosApp/iOSApp.swift` | call site | `IosKoinKt.bootstrapIosKoin()` replaces `KoinHelperKt.doInitKoin()`. |

## 11. Phase 8.y — Guarded debug nav route for the rework `LibraryScreen`

### 11.1 Scope

Adds a new type-safe nav route `Screen.LibraryRework` and the adapter that hosts
`:ui/.../library/LibraryScreen` backed by the rework `LibraryViewModel`. The route is
registered in the `:composeApp` NavHost alongside the existing `Screen.Library` entry —
both routes coexist intentionally so the legacy and rework screens are reachable in the
same session for side-by-side verification before the user-facing swap (Phase 8.z).

The route is **not surfaced** in `BottomNavigationBar` or any user-facing entry. Anyone
holding the `NavController` can navigate to it via `navController.navigate(Screen.
LibraryRework)`; a discreet developer trigger (settings entry / tab long-press) lands in
a follow-up sub-phase if the owner wants one — out of scope for 8.y, which exists to prove
the end-to-end wire-up compiles cleanly through every layer the rework added.

### 11.2 Why this is "guarded"

- **Not surfaced in user UI.** `BottomNavigationBar` items list is unchanged (still 5
  tabs: Library/Updates/Home/History/Settings). The legacy `Screen.Library` binding stays
  user-facing.
- **Coexists with legacy.** Both `Screen.Library` (legacy `LibraryScreenRoute` →
  `:shared/.../features/library/ui/screens/LibraryScreen`) and `Screen.LibraryRework`
  (new `LibraryReworkScreenRoute` → `:ui/.../library/LibraryScreen`) are registered in
  the NavHost. Visiting one doesn't affect the other.
- **`first_launch` start destination unchanged.** Onboarding still lands on
  `Screen.Welcome` (or `Screen.Library` after onboarding) — not on `Screen.LibraryRework`.
- **No deep links, no `intent-filter` entries**, no manifest changes.
- **No Settings entry** added (Phase 8.y₂ may add one if the owner wants a discoverable
  in-app trigger).

### 11.3 What end-to-end proof this gives us

When `navController.navigate(Screen.LibraryRework)` is called, the chain that activates is:

1. `:composeApp/commonMain/di/libraryReworkModule` resolves `LibraryViewModel`'s
   constructor params — `ObserveLibraryUseCase`, `ToggleInLibraryUseCase`. Each use case
   resolves `LibraryRepository` (rework interface in `:domain`); the binding points at
   `LibraryRepositoryImpl` (`:data`). The repo constructor pulls `MangaDao`, `LibraryDeo`
   from the existing `:shared` PlatformModule bindings (transitional — moves to `:data`
   when Room relocates), and `DispatcherProvider` from the rework `single` binding.
2. `:presentation`'s `MviViewModel<LibraryState, LibraryIntent, LibraryEffect>` plumbing
   exposes `state: StateFlow<LibraryState>` and `effects: Flow<LibraryEffect>`.
3. `:ui`'s `LibraryScreen` (composable) collects `state`, dispatches intents via
   `viewModel.submit(...)`, and forwards `LibraryEffect.NavigateToDetails(manga)` through
   the route adapter's `onNavigateToDetails` lambda.
4. `LibraryReworkScreenRoute` (`:composeApp`) translates the manga to a `safeNavigate(
   Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl = manga.url, api = manga.api))` call.

Compile-gate green on all four targets (Android, Desktop, iosArm64, iosSimulatorArm64)
proves the full chain links. Runtime proof — that real library data renders on a real
device — requires the route to actually be invoked, which is the owner's verification
step once a dev trigger is added.

| iOS framework link | n/a | not executed (Windows; deferred to macOS host). |

### 11.6 Decisions recorded

- **No user-visible trigger in 8.y.** Adding a Settings entry or bottom-nav long-press
  changes user-visible surfaces, even if narrowly. Keeping the route unreachable from UI
  honors the "don't change feature public surfaces without documenting in
  ARCHITECTURE.md" rule strictly (this section IS the documentation, but the safer
  approach is also to keep the actual UI element absent until 8.y₂ if/when the owner
  wants it).
- **Bottom bar shown when route is active.** `onBottomBarVisibleChange(true)` mirrors the
  legacy Library route. If/when a dev trigger lands, this gives a uniform comparison
  experience: the user sees the same chrome whether they're on legacy or rework Library.
- **`backStackEntry` parameter ignored.** Sibling routes (e.g. `HistoryScreenRoute`) take
  it for parity but don't always use it. The rework ViewModel is `koinViewModel()`-scoped
  — Koin's ViewModelStoreOwner integration uses the destination's own store. The
  unused-param `@Suppress` makes that explicit.
- **`Screen.MangaDetails` is the same target as legacy.** The rework `Manga` carries the
  same `(api, url)` identity tuple, so the existing details route opens correctly. No new
  rework details route is needed for Phase 8.y; the user transitions back into the legacy
  surface on tap.

### 14.1 Scope

Fourth slice in the Phase 5 "straightforward facades" batch. The legacy
`:shared/core/files/AppFileSystem` (an `expect class` plus five pure extension
helpers) becomes a `:platform/filesystem/AppFileSystem` `interface` plus three
per-target implementations (`AndroidAppFileSystem`, `IosAppFileSystem`,
`DesktopAppFileSystem`). The five extension helpers (`mangaDir`, `chapterDir`,
`folderSize`, `clearFilesLargerThan`, `clearCacheLargerThan`) move alongside the
interface in commonMain so call sites get the same on-disk layout helpers without
duplicating them.

Legacy `:shared/core/files/AppFileSystem.*` stays in place during this phase so
existing callers (the CBZ writer/reader, settings cache-clear flows) continue
resolving the old expect-class binding through `SharedModule`. Phase 6+ rewires
each consumer.

### 14.2 Files

| File | Change | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `platform/build.gradle.kts` | edit | Add `api(libs.okio)` to `commonMain.dependencies` so the SPI's `Path` / `FileSystem` return types resolve in downstream callers without each consumer re-declaring okio. |
| `platform/commonMain/.../filesystem/AppFileSystem.kt` | new | Interface (2 vals + 1 method) + 5 pure extension helpers. |
| `platform/androidMain/.../filesystem/AndroidAppFileSystem.kt` | new | `context.filesDir` / `context.cacheDir` via primary-ctor `Context`. |
| `platform/iosMain/.../filesystem/IosAppFileSystem.kt` | new | `NSFileManager.URLForDirectory(...)` with `create = true` for Documents + Caches. |
| `platform/desktopMain/.../filesystem/DesktopAppFileSystem.kt` | new | `~/.yami-manga/{files,cache}` under the JVM `user.home`, eagerly `createDirectories`'d, with a fallback chain to `java.io.tmpdir` then `"."`. |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | doc | This Phase 14 section. |
| `SOLID_AUDIT.md` | doc | Phase 5.4 entries (10-point checklist per source file). |

### 14.3 Decisions

- **Body byte-for-byte parity with legacy actuals.** Each impl's directory
  resolution and the five extension helpers preserved exactly. Only the type
  shape changed (`actual class` → `class : interface`, `actual val` → `override
  val`). Phase 6+ rewire is a pure binding swap.
- **`api(libs.okio)` rather than `implementation`.** The interface's public
  members return `okio.Path` and `okio.FileSystem`. Downstream callers therefore
  need okio on their compile classpath transitively. Using `implementation`
  would force every consumer module to re-declare okio.
- **Extension helpers stay in commonMain.** `mangaDir`, `chapterDir`,
  `folderSize`, `clearFilesLargerThan`, `clearCacheLargerThan` only use the SPI's
  public surface. They are pure and platform-agnostic — keeping them next to the
  interface avoids consumers reinventing the on-disk layout.
- **`AndroidAppFileSystem` takes `Context` via primary constructor.** Same
  convention as `AndroidToastShower` / `AndroidIntentLauncher`. The constructor
  immediately reads `context.filesDir.absolutePath` / `context.cacheDir.absolutePath`
  so no `Context` reference is held beyond construction.
- **iOS constructor throws on resolve failure.** Mirrors legacy behaviour
  (`error("Unable to resolve iOS directory: $directory")`). The condition is
  unreachable on a healthy sandbox; nothing useful for the caller to do.
- **No Koin binding wired yet.** Per the Phase 5 plan in §5.5: feature
  migrations in Phase 6+ add the binding next to the consumer's wiring.
- **Both SPIs coexist.** Legacy `me.manga.kira.core.files.AppFileSystem` and
  rework `me.manga.kira.platform.filesystem.AppFileSystem` live in different
  packages and resolve through different Koin keys. No collision.

## §17 Phase 5 straightforward-facade batch — close-out

### 17.1 What this batch covered

Phases 5.1–5.6 ported the six low-blast-radius platform facades from
`:shared` into the clean `:platform` layer using a uniform shape:

| Phase | Facade | Sources commit | Close-out commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | `AppVersionProvider` | (prior) | (prior) |
| 5.2 | `ToastShower` | (prior) | `4b3f4ac` |
| 5.3 | `IntentLauncher` | `78d8d7a` | `6a4ebf1` |
| 5.4 | `AppFileSystem` | `a7779a8` | `cad260d` |
| 5.5 | `FileSizeFormatter` | `94b9e66` | `86fad61` |
| 5.6 | `LocaleSwitcher` | `d9d0bac` (+ `be85f90` deps) | `9593569` |

Each slice followed the same four-file template (interface in commonMain +
one actual per Android/iOS/Desktop) with a two-file documentation close-out
(`ARCHITECTURE.md` section + `SOLID_AUDIT.md` audit rows). Where a slice
needed new platform dependencies (Phase 5.4 okio, Phase 5.6 AppCompat), a
separate two-file prep commit kept the sources commit inside the five-file
budget. Legacy `:shared` `.expect` / `.android.kt` / `.ios.kt` /
`.desktop.kt` sources remain in place under the Strangler-Fig rule — they
will be removed only after callers are rewired in a later phase.

### 17.2 Queued slices that turned out to be no-ops

Two facades were listed in the prior phase-5 queue but, on inspection of
the legacy source tree, have nothing to relocate. They are explicitly
skipped (no source files added) rather than created as net-new SPIs,
following the project's no-premature-abstraction rule.

#### 17.2.a `ClipboardWriter` (was Phase 5.7) — **skipped, no-op**

- **Legacy state**: no `Clipboard*` files exist in `:shared` (verified by
  glob `shared/**/*Clipboard*`). There is no `expect class ClipboardWriter`
  to port.
- **Existing solution**: Compose Multiplatform's `LocalClipboardManager` is
  already multiplatform and is consumed directly from `:composeApp` UI
  files (e.g. `InfoCompose.kt`, `HeaderSection.kt`,
  `AdminComplaintScreen.kt`) via
  `val clipboardManager = LocalClipboardManager.current` +
  `clipboardManager.setText(AnnotatedString(...))`.
- **Decision**: do not introduce a `ClipboardWriter` SPI at this time. The
  Compose API already crosses all three targets and is the idiomatic
  surface for Compose-side clipboard writes. Wrapping it in a `:platform`
  interface would add an abstraction layer without changing behavior or
  removing duplication. If a non-Compose call site ever needs to write the
  clipboard from inside `:domain`/`:data`, the SPI can be added at that
  point in a future phase.

#### 17.2.b `BrowserLauncher` (was Phase 5.8) — **skipped, redundant**

- **Legacy state**: no `BrowserLauncher*` files exist in `:shared`. The
  glob `shared/**/*Browser*` matches only `BrowserHeadersInterceptor.kt`,
  which is a Ktor HTTP interceptor (sets `User-Agent` /
  `Sec-Ch-Ua-*` headers on requests) — wholly unrelated to launching a
  browser.
- **Existing solution**: the Phase 5.3 `IntentLauncher.openUrl(String)`
  facade already opens a URL in the user's default browser/handler on all
  three platforms:
  - Android: `ACTION_VIEW` + `Uri.parse(url)` with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`.
  - iOS: `UIApplication.sharedApplication.openURL(NSURL(string = url))`.
  - Desktop: `Desktop.getDesktop().browse(URI(url))` with `isSupported()`
    capability check.
- **Decision**: do not introduce a separate `BrowserLauncher` SPI. The
  Phase 5.3 verdict in §13 explicitly scopes `openUrl` to "any URL the
  default handler can open" — adding a second SPI with the same
  responsibility would be a Single Responsibility violation by
  duplication, not by separation.

  with `suspend fun put(key, value)`, `suspend fun get(key): String?`,
  `suspend fun remove(key)`. Documentation lists the per-platform backend
  + on-disk format expectations.
- `platform/androidMain/.../platform/storage/AndroidSecureStorage.kt` —
  `class AndroidSecureStorage(context: Context, fileName: String =
  "yami_secure_prefs") : SecureStorage`. `Context.applicationContext` to

  bridged to `CFDictionaryRef`; UTF-8 NSData round-trip;
  `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock` matches legacy.
  `@OptIn(ExperimentalForeignApi::class, BetaInteropApi::class)` matches
  the legacy opt-in profile.
- `platform/desktopMain/.../platform/storage/DesktopSecureStorage.kt` —
  `class DesktopSecureStorage(rootDir: Path = ~/.yami-manga) :

  temp+`ATOMIC_MOVE`; per-instance `Mutex` for write serialization;
  POSIX `0600` permissions with Windows DOS-hidden fallback.

on this layer — the interface lives only in commonMain). The on-disk
format on every platform is byte-for-byte identical to legacy so existing

eventual cut-over.

  (57 lines) — `class AndroidNotificationPresenter(context: Context)

  with `extraBufferCapacity = 4`) lives in the same file as a top-level

  (32 lines) — `class DesktopPushTokenProvider : PushTokenProvider`.
  Mirror of the iOS no-op (Firebase Messaging has no JVM SDK).

`.ios` / `.desktop`) match legacy log tags verbatim — preserves grep-

- `platform/commonMain/.../platform/image/ScreenshotProvider.kt`
  (32 lines) — `interface ScreenshotProvider` with two suspend

  String?` and `suspend fun shareBitmapBytes(bytes, title)`. KDoc
  notes the legacy name is preserved and explicitly states that

- `platform/androidMain/.../platform/image/AndroidScreenshotProvider.kt`

### 24.2 Files added

- `platform/commonMain/.../platform/jobs/BackgroundJobScheduler.kt`
  (73 lines) — `interface BackgroundJobScheduler` (5 methods),

  top-level `data class BackgroundJob(tag, workerClass, data,
  requiresNetwork, requiresCharging, initialDelayMs)`. Constructor

  (139 lines) — `class AndroidBackgroundJobScheduler(context) :

  `dateWithTimeIntervalSinceNow`.

  Desktop) supply the SAM `BackgroundJobRunner` for each known tag at
  startup. `fun interface BackgroundJobRunner` lives at file top-
  level, mirroring the legacy file.

## §25 Phase 5.w.1 — `ImageDecoderRegistry` facade port

First slice of the Phase 5.w image-pipeline sub-batch. Legacy
`:shared/.../core/image/ImageDecoderRegistry.kt` is an `expect class`
with one method (`fun registerAll(): List<Decoder.Factory>`) plus
three actuals. The Android actual registers `AvifDecoderCoil.Factory`
and the iOS / Desktop actuals register `HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.Factory`
— two of the **six load-bearing image-quality fixes** the memory tracks
verbatim. Both helper classes are also relocated as part of this
slice (`AvifDecoderCoil.android.kt` in `:shared/androidMain` →
`AvifDecoderCoil.kt` in `:platform/androidMain`; `HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.kt`
in `:shared/nonAndroidMain` → same name in `:platform/nonAndroidMain`).

### 25.1 New deps + source-set wiring

| Dep / Source set | Where | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `io.coil-kt.coil3:coil-core` `3.4.0` | `:platform/commonMain` (`api`) | The interface returns `List<coil3.decode.Decoder.Factory>` — downstream callers must be able to call into Coil's types without each re-declaring this dep. We pull only `coil-core` here; the singleton ImageLoader, Compose binding (`coil-compose`), and network engines (`coil-network-ktor3` / `coil-network-okhttp`) stay in `:composeApp`. |
| `org.aomedia.avif.android:avif` `1.3.0.841110fd` | `:platform/androidMain` | Native AOM library used by `AvifDecoderCoil` for hardware-quality AVIF decode (Cloudflare-protected manga CDNs serve AVIF; platform default falls back to Android `ImageDecoder` at degraded quality on 31+ and cannot decode at all on older releases). |
| New `nonAndroidMain` source set | `:platform/build.gradle.kts` | Intermediate source set shared between iOS + Desktop. Hosts `HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder` because both targets use Skia (Skiko on Desktop, Skia-via-Compose-Multiplatform-iOS on iOS) and need the same `CATMULL_ROM` cubic-resampling fix. Mirrors the legacy `:shared` layout. |

Catalog entries already existed (`libraries.coil-core`, `libraries.avif`).
The two new deps + the source-set declaration are declared on
`:platform/build.gradle.kts` only — following the explicit-deps
convention captured in `project_yami_kmp_platform_deps.md`, we do not
rely on `:shared`'s transitive pulls.

### 25.2 Files added

- `platform/commonMain/.../platform/image/ImageDecoderRegistry.kt`
  (33 lines) — `interface ImageDecoderRegistry` with one method
  (`fun registerAll(): List<Decoder.Factory>`). KDoc spells out the
  per-platform fix (`AvifDecoderCoil` on Android; `HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder`
  on iOS + Desktop) and notes that Coil's `ComponentRegistry` tries
  user-registered decoders before its service-loaded defaults, so the
  first matching factory in the returned list wins.
- `platform/androidMain/.../platform/image/AndroidImageDecoderRegistry.kt`
  (20 lines) — `class AndroidImageDecoderRegistry : ImageDecoderRegistry`;
  `registerAll()` returns `listOf(AvifDecoderCoil.Factory())`.
- `platform/androidMain/.../platform/image/AvifDecoderCoil.kt`
  (160 lines) — `internal class AvifDecoderCoil(source, options) :
  Decoder`. Verbatim port of the legacy decoder logic (size check,
  aspect-ratio sanity, ByteBuffer + `AomAvifDecoder.getInfo` /
  `.decode`, `RGB_565` for opaque / `ARGB_8888` for alpha, defensive
  recycling on every failure mode). The serialised native call via a
  `Mutex` matches the upstream's thread-safety claim. Companion `private const val`
  extracted for `TAG`, `MIME_AVIF`, `AVIF_HEADER_MIN_BYTES`,
  `FTYP_OFFSET`, `BRAND_OFFSET`, `MAX_ASPECT_RATIO` (factored out of
  inline literals). Logging switched from `android.util.Log` to
  Kermit `Logger.withTag(TAG)` to match the `:platform` module
  convention — format differs but observability is preserved (Kermit
  delegates to logcat on Android).
- `platform/iosMain/.../platform/image/IosImageDecoderRegistry.kt`
  (18 lines) — `class IosImageDecoderRegistry : ImageDecoderRegistry`;
  `registerAll()` returns `listOf(HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.Factory())`.
- `platform/desktopMain/.../platform/image/DesktopImageDecoderRegistry.kt`
  (18 lines) — same as iOS; one-liner registering the cubic-resampler
  decoder.
- `platform/nonAndroidMain/.../platform/image/HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.kt`
  (110 lines) — `internal class HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder(source,
  options) : Decoder`. Verbatim port of the legacy decoder. Uses the
  11-arg `Canvas.drawImageRect` overload with
  `SamplingMode.CATMULL_ROM` (Mitchell-style cubic) instead of
  Coil 3's stock 3-arg `drawImageRect` which defaults to
  `FilterMode.NEAREST`. Destination bitmap stays N32 (32-bit RGBA)
  per the KDoc's explicit "RGB_565 would introduce visible banding"
  rationale. `@OptIn(ExperimentalCoilApi::class)` matches legacy.

All five classes use the rework's `:platform` package namespace and
implement the rework interface. The Android consumer (Phase 10
ImageLoader wiring) will pick up whichever copy of `AvifDecoderCoil`
+ `HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder` is on its compile classpath; legacy
`:shared` callers continue to consume the legacy copies.

### 25.3 Strangler-fig — what is NOT changed

- Legacy `:shared/.../core/image/ImageDecoderRegistry.kt` (`expect
  class`) and its three actuals stay in place.
- Legacy `:shared/androidMain/.../core/image/AvifDecoderCoil.android.kt`
  and `:shared/nonAndroidMain/.../core/image/HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.kt`
  stay in place. The two helper classes coexist in two separate
  packages (`me.manga.kira.core.image.*` vs.
  `me.manga.kira.platform.image.*`) until the Phase 10 ImageLoader
  wiring is rewired to consume the `:platform` versions.
- The Coil `ImageLoader` builder, the per-request build sites
  (`buildImageRequest` / `rememberSourceImageRequest`), and the
  Compose binding all stay in `:composeApp` — those carry the *other*
  four load-bearing fixes (`maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL)` on the
  singleton; `allowHardware(false) + RGB_565 + size hint` per-request
  on Android; OkHttp fetcher override on Android; per-request
  `Size.ORIGINAL` on Desktop). The image-pipeline batch only
  relocates the **decoder registration** layer in this slice — the
  loader-side fixes will land with the Phase 10 / Phase 11 ImageLoader
  wiring rewrite.
- No caller is rewired. The two surfaces share method shapes but live
  in different packages.

class against the interface and pass the same `AppFileSystem`

## 30. Phase 5.w.6 — `CbzSettings` + `getCbzSettings` + `DeviceTier`
                     (CBZ tunables + device-tier enum)

### 30.1 Why this slice exists

Legacy `:shared/commonMain/.../core/cbz/CbzSettings.kt` and
`getCbzSettings.kt` provide the tunable parameters consumed by the
CBZ encoder (parallelism, region-decode / sampling thresholds, WebP
quality). The function takes a `DeviceTier` enum, which legacy
co-locates in `:shared/commonMain/.../core/util/heap/DeviceTier.kt`
together with an `expect fun detectDeviceTier()` (Android
`ActivityManager`, iOS `NSProcessInfo`, Desktop
`OperatingSystemMXBean`).

This slice migrates the pure-data portion of both files to the
rework module graph. The `expect/actual` probe is intentionally
**deferred** to a future `DeviceTierProbe` interface slice in
`:platform` — that one will need three actuals plus a Koin binding
and warrants its own commit.

### 30.2 Module placement decisions

`DeviceTier` enum + threshold constants + `classifyByTotalRam`
helper → `:core/util/heap/DeviceTier.kt`. `:core` already hosts
the other pure-Kotlin abstractions (`AppResult`, `AppError`,
`DispatcherProvider`, `FeatureFlagProvider`, `Logger`); the
device-tier enum belongs in the same tier. No platform deps —
strictly commonMain.

`CbzSettings` data class + `getCbzSettings` lookup →
`:platform/cbz/`. Could plausibly live in `:core` (also pure data),
but proximity to `CbzWriter` / `CbzReader` / future `CbzManager`
matters more: the CBZ subsystem is self-contained inside
`:platform/cbz`, and the tier-driven settings are an
implementation detail of that subsystem rather than a shared
abstraction other modules consume. `:platform` already declares
`api(project(":core"))` so the `DeviceTier` import resolves cleanly.

### 30.3 Wire-compatibility with legacy

`CbzSettings` field set unchanged — 5 fields, same names, same
types (`maxParallelDecode: Int`, `maxParallelCompress: Int`,
`regionDecodeThreshold: Int`, `samplingThreshold: Long`,
`webpQuality: Int`). `getCbzSettings` per-tier values preserved
byte-for-byte: LOW (1, 2, 6000, 20_000_000L, 70), MID
(2, 4, 9000, 40_000_000L, 75), HIGH (3, 6, 12000, 70_000_000L, 85).
The same `DeviceTier.{LOW,MID,HIGH}` enum constants ship in the new
`:core` location, so downstream call sites only need an import
package rewrite when they migrate.

### 30.4 OCP cleanups over legacy

Legacy `getCbzSettings` inlined every per-tier magic number
directly into the `when` arms. The rework hoists each value to a
top-level `private const val` named by tier-and-field (e.g.
`LOW_PARALLEL_DECODE`, `MID_REGION_DECODE_THRESHOLD`,
`HIGH_SAMPLING_THRESHOLD_BYTES`, `HIGH_WEBP_QUALITY`). This is the
same OCP fix applied to other `:platform` slices — touching a tier's
tuning value no longer requires re-reading the `when` block to find
the right literal among 15 inlined numbers.

`DeviceTier.kt` keeps the threshold consts (`TIER_LOW_MAX_BYTES`,
`TIER_MID_MAX_BYTES`) `internal` so they remain an implementation
detail of `classifyByTotalRam` — the future `DeviceTierProbe`
actuals live in `:platform` and call the public classifier rather
than re-implementing the comparison.

### 30.5 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.w.6

All three source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.w.6
entries. Phase 5.w.6 closed for the CBZ-settings slice. Remaining
Phase 5.w queue: the Android-only `CbzManager` /
`OptimizedCbzManager` orchestrators (consume `AvifDecoderCoil` +
`CbzWriter` + `CbzReader` + `getCbzSettings` — needs the
:platform → :data wiring step in Phase 6+). The deferred
`DeviceTierProbe` probe slice will land before any rework code
needs a runtime tier (until then call sites can synthesize from
the legacy `:shared` API or pass a tier explicitly).

## 31. Phase 5.w.6.5 — `DeviceTierProbe` (runtime tier probe)

### 31.1 Why this slice exists

Phase 5.w.6 deferred the `expect fun detectDeviceTier()` portion of
the legacy `DeviceTier.kt` to a separate slice because converting it
to an interface needs four files (interface + three actuals) and
deserves its own commit boundary. This slice is that conversion.
With it in place, every Phase 5.w.7+ caller that needs a runtime
device tier (CbzManager, ProMangaImageCombiner, etc.) can DI a
`DeviceTierProbe` instead of reaching into the legacy `:shared`
top-level function.

### 31.2 Why interface instead of preserving `expect/actual`

Same rationale as every other expect→interface conversion in the
rework: testability (mock the probe in unit tests), Koin-injection
ergonomics (no top-level functions in a leaf module), and avoiding
the `expect/actual` runtime-resolution cost when the platforms have
nothing to share but a method signature.

### 31.3 Constructor convention (Android `Context`)

`AndroidDeviceTierProbe` takes `Context` directly in its constructor.
This replaces the legacy two-step pattern of `setAndroidDeviceTierContext(ctx)`
opt-in registration + lazy `appContext` field — a workaround that
existed only because the legacy expect/actual sat in commonMain and
couldn't see `Context` in its declaration. The rework actuals live
in `androidMain`, so the type is visible directly and Koin can bind
via `single { AndroidDeviceTierProbe(androidContext()) }` in
`PlatformModule.android.kt`.

iOS and Desktop probes have zero-arg constructors (their OS probes
are static — `NSProcessInfo.processInfo` and
`ManagementFactory.getOperatingSystemMXBean()`).

### 31.4 Desktop fallback simplification

Legacy desktop had:

```
return if (maxJvm == Long.MAX_VALUE) {
    TIER_LOW_MAX_BYTES + 1   // pessimistically classify as MID
} else {
    maxJvm.times(4)
}
```

The rework keeps `TIER_LOW_MAX_BYTES` internal to `:core`, so the
desktop probe can't read it across the module boundary. Rather than
widening the visibility, the rework returns `DeviceTier.MID` directly
when `maxJvm == Long.MAX_VALUE` — same outcome (MID classification),
no constant leak. The reflective `com.sun.management` probe is
preserved verbatim because compile-portability across stripped-JVM
runtimes is genuinely load-bearing.

### 31.5 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.w.6.5

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.w.6.5
entries. Phase 5.w.6.5 closed for the device-probe slice. The
remaining Phase 5.w queue is now exactly the Android-only
`CbzManager` / `OptimizedCbzManager` orchestrators.

## 32. Phase 5.z.1 — `InAppReviewClient` (Play Core review facade)

### 32.1 Why this slice exists

First entry in the Phase 5.z third-party-service track. Migrates
the legacy `:shared/commonMain/.../core/review/InAppReviewClient.kt`
+ Android Play-Core actual + iOS / Desktop no-op actuals to
`:platform/review`. Closing this slice unblocks the
`ReviewManagerHelper`-bearing call sites in `:composeApp` (they'll
flip imports during Phase 6+ wiring).

### 32.2 Android constructor convention (`activityProvider`)

Play Core's `launchReviewFlow(activity, info)` needs a foreground
[Activity]. The legacy actual took an `activityProvider: () -> Activity? = { null }`
lambda parameter and the rework preserves that shape verbatim — the
caller binds the lambda at Koin configuration time (typically
backed by an `ActivityLifecycleCallbacks` tracker). This is the
first rework slice that needs an Activity reference; if subsequent
slices (AdProvider, AppUpdateClient) repeat the pattern, a
top-level `typealias ForegroundActivityProvider = () -> Activity?`
will land alongside the second one to dedupe the parameter shape.

### 32.3 The "success" semantics

Play Core deliberately doesn't surface whether the review dialog
actually rendered on this device (Google rate-limits the surface
and silently no-ops past the limit). The actual returns `true`
whenever the flow completed without throwing — matching legacy's
`ReviewManagerHelper.launchInAppReview` success path. Consumers
should treat the boolean as "we asked, the SDK didn't error",
not "the user saw a dialog".

### 32.4 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.z.1

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.1
entries. Phase 5.z.1 closed for the in-app-review slice.

## 33. Phase 5.z.2 — `AppUpdateClient` (Play Core update facade)

### 33.1 Why this slice exists

Sibling to Phase 5.z.1 (`InAppReviewClient`) — same Play Core
source family, same actuals pattern (Android delegate + iOS / Desktop
no-ops). Closing this slice ties off the Play-Core-driven facade
group; the remaining Phase 5.z entries (`AdProvider`,
`AnalyticsClient`, `CrashReporter`, `ConsentFlowClient`,
`RemoteDocStore`) all use different vendor SDKs.

### 33.2 `AppUpdateInfo` data class in the same file

The interface and its small companion data class live together in
`AppUpdateClient.kt`. Rationale: `AppUpdateInfo` is exclusively a
return type of [AppUpdateClient.checkForUpdate]; co-location keeps
the contract self-documenting and means consumers add one import,
not two. Same precedent as `ConnectivityObserver.Status` (Phase 5.x).

### 33.3 Preserved legacy contract points

Three legacy behaviors are load-bearing for downstream call sites
and preserved verbatim:

 1. **`REQUEST_CODE = 100`**: Play Core surfaces the result of
    `startUpdateFlowForResult` through the host Activity's
    `onActivityResult` keyed by this exact integer. The
    Android-host install-state plumbing (Phase 11 wiring) reads
    `requestCode == 100`. Changing it silently breaks the upstream
    `AppUpdateHelper.kt`-derived flow.
 2. **Flexible-vs-immediate fall-back in `checkForUpdate`**: when
    Play Core says "only IMMEDIATE allowed for this release", the
    facade returns `isImmediate = true` so consumer UI can show the
    blocking variant. Inverting the booleans here would silently
    show the wrong dialog.
 3. **"Return false on any throw" success semantics**: all three
    methods catch and turn into `false` / `null`. The interface's
    KDoc commits to this contract.

### 33.4 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.z.2

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.2
entries. Phase 5.z.2 closed for the in-app-update slice.

## 34. Phase 5.z.3 — `ConsentFlowClient` (Google UMP consent facade)

### 34.1 Why this slice exists

Third entry in the Phase 5.z third-party-service track. Migrates the
legacy `:shared/commonMain/.../core/consent/ConsentFlowClient.kt`
(GDPR / IAB TCF consent flow that AdMob requires in EEA regions)
plus its three actuals (Android UMP delegate + iOS / Desktop no-ops)
to `:platform/consent`. Closes the Play-services-async family group
even though UMP is technically a separate Google SDK (`com.google.android.ump`)
— same async pattern, distinct vendor surface.

### 34.2 `ConsentStatus` enum in the same file

The interface and its companion `ConsentStatus` enum (UNKNOWN /
NOT_REQUIRED / REQUIRED / OBTAINED) live together in
`ConsentFlowClient.kt`. Same co-location rationale as
`AppUpdateInfo` (§33.2) and `ConnectivityObserver.Status` (§24.2):
the enum is exclusively the return type of one interface method
(`requestConsentInfoUpdate`), so co-location keeps the contract
self-documenting and lets consumers add one import, not two.

### 34.3 `suspendCancellableCoroutine` instead of `Task.await()`

Phase 5.z.1 (`InAppReviewClient`) and Phase 5.z.2 (`AppUpdateClient`)
both used `kotlinx-coroutines-play-services`'s `Task<T>.await()` to
bridge Play Core's `Task` returns to suspend. UMP is different:
`ConsentInformation.requestConsentInfoUpdate(...)` and
`UserMessagingPlatform.loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired(...)` expose
success/failure listeners directly, not `Task` objects. The actual
therefore bridges with `kotlinx.coroutines.suspendCancellableCoroutine`
and resolves the continuation from inside the success / failure
callbacks.

A `cont.isActive` guard wraps both `resume` calls to prevent
double-resumption if UMP fires both callbacks (defensive — observed
in older UMP versions). The guard is preserved verbatim from legacy.

### 34.4 Preserved legacy contract points

Three legacy behaviors are load-bearing for downstream call sites
and preserved verbatim:

 1. **`applicationContext` unwrap**: `getConsentInformation(context.applicationContext)`
    prevents the UMP manager singleton from retaining an Activity
    context — same pattern as `AndroidInAppReviewClient` /
    `AndroidAppUpdateClient`.
 2. **`mapStatus(raw: Int)` helper**: UMP exposes its status as raw
    `Int` constants (`ConsentInformation.ConsentStatus.NOT_REQUIRED`,
    `.REQUIRED`, `.OBTAINED`). The private mapper translates them to
    the common enum; unknown ints fall through to
    `ConsentStatus.UNKNOWN`. Inverting any of those mappings would
    silently change consumer UI behavior (the consent gate / settings
    re-entry button live in `:composeApp/MainActivity.kt`).
 3. **"UNKNOWN / false on any failure" semantics**: `requestConsentInfoUpdate`
    returns `ConsentStatus.UNKNOWN` on missing Activity or UMP error;
    `loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired` returns `false` on missing
    Activity or any error from the form-loader callback. The
    interface KDoc commits to this contract.

### 34.5 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.z.3

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.3
entries. Phase 5.z.3 closed for the UMP consent slice. Remaining
Phase 5.z queue: `AdProvider`, `AnalyticsClient`, `CrashReporter`,
`RemoteDocStore`.

## 35. Phase 5.z.4 — `AdProvider` (AdMob facade)

### 35.1 Why this slice exists

Fourth entry in the Phase 5.z third-party-service track. Migrates
the legacy `:shared/.../core/ads/AdProvider.kt` (`expect class` with
five members) + Android AdMob delegate + iOS / Desktop no-op
actuals to `:platform/ads`. The legacy file was the most complex
member of the Phase 5.z group — full-screen ad lifecycle plus the
rewarded-flow terminal-state arbitration — so it ships as its own
slice rather than batched with the simpler facades.

### 35.2 `AdResult` sealed class co-location

The interface and the `AdResult` sealed hierarchy (NotLoaded /
Shown / Dismissed / Failed(errorCode, message) / EarnedReward)
live together in `AdProvider.kt`. Same co-location rationale as
`ConsentStatus` (§34.2), `AppUpdateInfo` (§33.2), and
`ConnectivityObserver.Status` (§24.2): the sealed members are
exclusively the return type of `showInterstitial` and
`showRewarded`; co-location keeps the contract self-documenting
and means consumers add one import, not five.

### 35.3 Preserved legacy contract points

Five legacy behaviors are load-bearing for downstream call sites
and preserved verbatim:

 1. **`applicationContext` unwrap on `InterstitialAd.load` /
    `RewardedAd.load`**: the AdMob `load` surface caches against the
    supplied context — passing the Activity would retain it for the
    lifetime of the cached load.
 2. **Snapshot + clear of `loadedInterstitial` / `loadedRewarded`**:
    AdMob full-screen ads are single-show; the actual clears the
    holder before calling `ad.show(...)` so that a second call
    cannot reuse the same ad reference.
 3. **`WeakReference<Array<AdResult?>>` rewarded terminal-state
    arbitration**: AdMob fires `OnUserEarnedRewardListener` *before*
    `onAdDismissedFullScreenContent`, but the suspend resume must
    wait for dismissal. The actual records the earned-reward state
    into a single-cell array, wraps it in a `WeakReference` so the
    array isn't leaked through the SDK callback chain, and resumes
    with the recorded state (or `Dismissed`) on the dismissal
    callback. Inverting this order would either resume too early
    (consumer sees `EarnedReward` while the ad is still on screen)
    or leak the array reference.
 4. **`cont.isActive` double-resume guard on every callback**: the
    SDK occasionally fires success + dismissal in unexpected order
    on specific Android-OS / mediation-adapter combinations (legacy
    crash trace captured pre-fix). The guard is defensive but real.
 5. **"Return `false` / `Failed(-1, …)` on any throw" success
    semantics**: every load / show path catches and turns into a
    safe-default. The sentinel error code `-1` is named
    `NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR_CODE` and hoisted to a companion
    `private const` — real AdMob `AdError.code` values are
    non-negative, so the sentinel is unambiguous for callers that
    branch on the int.

### 35.4 `loadBanner` is "acknowledge unit id", not "load"

AdMob banners are Android `View`s (`AdView`); they don't fit a pure
suspending facade because their lifecycle is owned by the Compose
banner composable (Phase 9.x). `loadBanner(unitId)` therefore
returns `unitId.isNotBlank()` on Android — it acknowledges the unit
id is shaped correctly so downstream Compose code can proceed. The
iOS / Desktop actuals return `false` (no banner surface). The
common KDoc documents this clearly so consumers don't build
mistaken UX off the return value.

### 35.5 `ForegroundActivityProvider` typealias deferral

This is the fourth consecutive `:platform` actual with the
`(context: Context, activityProvider: () -> Activity? = { null })`
constructor shape (after `AndroidInAppReviewClient`,
`AndroidAppUpdateClient`, `AndroidConsentFlowClient`). The pending
`typealias ForegroundActivityProvider = () -> Activity?` cleanup
*could* land in this slice — but introducing it now would update
five files (the typealias + four existing classes), blowing the
five-file commit budget. Deferred to a dedicated cleanup slice
after the Phase 5.z group is done. The shape across all four
actuals is identical, so the cleanup is mechanical and low-risk.

### 35.6 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.z.4

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.4
entries. Phase 5.z.4 closed for the AdProvider slice. Remaining
Phase 5.z queue: `AnalyticsClient`, `CrashReporter`, `RemoteDocStore`.

## 36. Phase 5.z.5 — `AnalyticsClient` (Firebase Analytics facade)

### 36.1 Why this slice exists

Fifth entry in the Phase 5.z third-party-service track. Migrates
the legacy `:shared/.../core/analytics/AnalyticsClient.kt`
(`expect class` with three members) + Android Firebase Analytics
delegate + iOS / Desktop no-op actuals to `:platform/analytics`.
Simpler than its predecessors — no Activity dependency, no
async/suspend, no co-located return-type class.

### 36.2 First Phase 5.z slice without `activityProvider`

Firebase Analytics is application-scoped — the event surface is
backed by `FirebaseAnalytics.getInstance(context)`, which only
needs the application Context. No `Activity` is needed for any
of `logEvent` / `setUserProperty` / `setUserId`. This is the
first Phase 5.z slice that breaks the four-deep
`(context: Context, activityProvider: () -> Activity? = { null })`
streak (`InAppReviewClient`, `AppUpdateClient`, `ConsentFlowClient`,
`AdProvider`); the constructor here is just `(context: Context)`.

The pending `ForegroundActivityProvider` typealias cleanup (deferred
in §35.5) is therefore still scoped to exactly four files — the
analytics client won't expand the surface.

### 36.3 Type-rule translation `Map<String, Any?>` → `Bundle`

The Android actual translates the common `Map<String, Any?>` into
an `android.os.Bundle` using Firebase Analytics' supported types:

| Common type | Bundle method | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `String` | `putString(key, value)` | Native. |
| `Int` | `putInt(key, value)` | Native. |
| `Long` | `putLong(key, value)` | Native. |
| `Float` | `putFloat(key, value)` | Native. |
| `Double` | `putDouble(key, value)` | Native. |
| `Boolean` | `putBoolean(key, value)` | Native. |
| `null` | *skipped* | Firebase rejects null parameter values (noisy release log). |
| anything else | `putString(key, value.toString())` | Diagnostic-value preserving coercion. |

The `null` skip is preserved verbatim from legacy with its inline
comment — the load-bearing reason for the branch isn't obvious
without it (Firebase rejects null values with a release-build
warning that the legacy maintainer hit and documented).

### 36.4 Preserved legacy contract points

Three legacy behaviors are load-bearing and preserved verbatim:

 1. **`applicationContext` unwrap on `FirebaseAnalytics.getInstance(...)`**:
    Firebase caches an internal singleton per process; passing the
    Activity context would let the cache retain the Activity until
    process death.
 2. **Empty-map fast path**: `if (params.isEmpty()) analytics.logEvent(name, null); return`
    avoids allocating an empty `Bundle` on every parameterless
    event (the most common case).
 3. **Silent `null`-value skip**: Firebase Analytics rejects `null`
    parameter values with a release-build warning. The legacy
    comment is preserved verbatim because it documents the
    load-bearing reason for the otherwise-unobvious branch.

### 36.5 Build-dep wiring

`libs.firebase.analytics` is added to `:platform/androidMain`. The
Firebase BoM is already pulled in (Phase 5.y.2 added it for
`firebase-messaging`); no second BoM import is needed — Gradle's
`platform(...)` dep is idempotent within a configuration. The
Analytics version is resolved from the same BoM.

### 36.6 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.z.5

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.5
entries. Phase 5.z.5 closed for the Analytics slice. Remaining
Phase 5.z queue: `CrashReporter`, `RemoteDocStore`.

## 37. Phase 5.z.6 — `CrashReporter` (Firebase Crashlytics facade)

### 37.1 Why this slice exists

Sixth entry in the Phase 5.z third-party-service track. Migrates
the legacy `:shared/.../core/crash/CrashReporter.kt` (`expect class`
with four members) + Android Firebase Crashlytics delegate + iOS /
Desktop no-op actuals to `:platform/crash`. Parallels Analytics
(§36) in shape: application-scoped, no Activity dependency, no
async/suspend, no co-located return-type class. Distinguishes
itself by being **zero-arg on Android** — Crashlytics doesn't even
need a Context.

### 37.2 First Phase 5.z slice with no Context (zero-arg actual)

The Android Crashlytics SDK exposes `FirebaseCrashlytics.getInstance()`
as a parameterless static — it reads its configuration from the
embedded `google-services.json` at process start, so the singleton
is wired before any `:platform` actual is constructed. This is the
first Phase 5.z slice whose Android actual takes **no constructor
parameters at all**:

| Slice | Android constructor |
|---|---|
| 5.z.1 InAppReviewClient | `(context, activityProvider)` |
| 5.z.2 AppUpdateClient | `(context, activityProvider)` |
| 5.z.3 ConsentFlowClient | `(context, activityProvider)` |
| 5.z.4 AdProvider | `(context, activityProvider)` |
| 5.z.5 AnalyticsClient | `(context)` |
| **5.z.6 CrashReporter** | **(zero-arg)** |

The pending `ForegroundActivityProvider` typealias cleanup (deferred
in §35.5) stays scoped to the four `activityProvider`-bearing
classes; Crashlytics doesn't expand the surface either.

### 37.3 Preserved legacy contract points

Three legacy behaviors are load-bearing and preserved verbatim:

 1. **Fan-out of `context` Map entries *before* `recordException`**:
    Crashlytics' key-snapshot happens at the time `recordException`
    is called, so any `setCustomKey` call that happens *after*
    `recordException` is lost from that crash report. The Android
    actual iterates `context` and writes every entry via
    `setCustomKey(key, value)` first, then calls
    `recordException(throwable)`. Inverting this order would
    silently drop the diagnostic context the caller intended to
    attach to that specific exception.
 2. **`setUserId(id ?: "")` empty-string clear idiom**:
    `FirebaseCrashlytics.setUserId(String)` is non-null in the SDK's
    Java signature. The documented way to clear a previously-set id
    is to pass the empty string. The legacy actual uses `?: ""` for
    exactly this reason and the new actual preserves it with the
    inline comment that documents the load-bearing rationale.
 3. **Kermit `.e(throwable)` on iOS / Desktop no-ops**: both
    actuals are no-ops with respect to Crashlytics, but
    `recordException` still logs the throwable + context map via
    Kermit at **error** level so the iOS console / desktop stderr
    surface the problem during development rather than swallowing
    it silently. The other three methods log at **debug** so they
    don't pollute the error-only filter most consoles run with.

### 37.4 Build-dep wiring

`libs.firebase.crashlytics` is added to `:platform/androidMain`. The
Firebase BoM is already pulled in (Phase 5.y.2 added it for
`firebase-messaging`; Phase 5.z.5 reused it for `firebase-analytics`);
no third BoM import is needed — Gradle's `platform(...)` dep is
idempotent within a configuration. The Crashlytics version is
resolved from the same BoM that pinned Messaging and Analytics, so
all three Firebase artifacts stay version-aligned automatically.

The Crashlytics Gradle plugin (`com.google.firebase.crashlytics`)
that uploads dSYM/mapping files is **not** added here — that lives
in the `:composeApp` (Android app) build, not in this library
module. `:platform` only consumes the runtime SDK.

### 37.5 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.z.6

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.6
entries. Phase 5.z.6 closed for the Crashlytics slice. Remaining
Phase 5.z queue: `RemoteDocStore` (last entry).

### 38.4 Preserved legacy contract points

Six legacy behaviors are load-bearing and preserved verbatim in the
Android actual:

 1. **Zero-arg `FirebaseFirestore.getInstance()`**: the SDK reads
    its configuration from the embedded `google-services.json` at
    process start. No Context needed.
 2. **`try { … } catch (e: Exception) { log.w(e) … }` swallow-and-
    default semantics on every read/write**: a single Firestore
    hiccup (network blip, permission flicker, transient backend
    error) must never propagate into the UI as a crash. The upstream
    call sites (notably `ComplaintFirestoreDataSource`) are read-
    mostly and treat null/empty as "no data right now". Every method
    that returns data returns its empty sentinel on exception
    (`null` for `getDoc`, `emptyList()` for `query`); writes
    (`setDoc` / `deleteDoc`) just log-and-drop.
 3. **`clause.value!!` non-null assertion on `whereGreaterThan` /
    `whereLessThan` / `whereGreaterOrEqual` / `whereLessOrEqual` /
    `whereArrayContains`**: Firestore's Java signatures for these
    overloads are non-null. A `null` value at this point is a
    caller bug and is intentionally allowed to throw — preserved
    verbatim because catching it would silently mask the bug.
    (The `!!` is tolerated on `:platform` SPIs that bridge nullable-
    in-the-source-language to non-null-in-the-SDK; the rework's
    "no `!!`" rule targets `domain` and `presentation`.)
 4. **`whereIn(field, (value as? List<*>) ?: emptyList<Any>())`
    best-effort fallback**: when a caller passes a non-List value
    to an `IN` clause, the legacy substitutes an empty list rather
    than throwing. This matches `EQUAL`'s permissive shape (which
    accepts any value via Firestore's untyped `Any?` overload) and
    is preserved verbatim.
 5. **`callbackFlow` + `awaitClose { registration.remove() }` for
    `observeDoc`**: the canonical pattern for bridging Firestore's
    listener-registration API into a cancellable cold Flow. The
    `addSnapshotListener` callback emits `null` on both error and
    nonexistent-doc, so subscribers can model "not there" the same
    way regardless of cause.
 6. **`snapshot.documents.mapNotNull { it.data }` on query
    results**: drops documents whose `.data` is null (Firestore
    returns null for docs deleted between snapshot acquisition and
    read). Without this, the query result would contain `null`
    entries that callers would have to filter again.

### 38.5 Build-dep wiring

`libs.firebase.firestore` is added to `:platform/androidMain`. The
Firebase BoM is already pulled in (Phase 5.y.2 added it for
`firebase-messaging`; Phase 5.z.5 reused it for `firebase-analytics`;
Phase 5.z.6 reused it for `firebase-crashlytics`). This is the
fourth Firebase artifact pulled from the same BoM — no second
`platform(...)` import needed; the Firestore version is resolved
from the same BoM that pinned Messaging / Analytics / Crashlytics,
keeping all four Firebase artifacts version-aligned automatically.

The Firestore offline-persistence cache (`PersistentCacheSettings`)
that the SDK enables by default is **not** configured here — the
legacy code uses default settings, and the rework preserves that.
If a future slice needs to tune cache behavior, it should land as a
dedicated SPI extension (e.g. `RemoteDocStoreConfig`) so the SPI
itself stays minimal.

All four source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.7
entries. Phase 5.z.7 closed for the Firestore slice.
