## 39. Phase 5.z.cleanup — `ForegroundActivityProvider` typealias hoist

### 39.1 Why this slice exists

After the Phase 5.z group closed (§38.7), the same constructor-
parameter shape

```kotlin
private val activityProvider: () -> Activity? = { null }
```

appeared verbatim in **four** Android actuals — `AndroidInAppReviewClient`
(5.z.1), `AndroidAppUpdateClient` (5.z.2), `AndroidConsentFlowClient`
(5.z.3), and `AndroidAdProvider` (5.z.4). The repetition was flagged
during the 5.z.4 audit (§35.5) and explicitly deferred so the slice
didn't blow the five-file commit budget; this cleanup slice claims
exactly the planned 5 files (1 typealias decl + 4 existing actuals).

### 39.2 Why a `typealias`, not a `fun interface`

Two viable shapes for the cross-cutting type:

| Shape | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| `typealias ForegroundActivityProvider = () -> Activity?` | Call-site stays a plain lambda (`provider()`); construction sites stay `{ activity }` with no SAM ceremony; default `{ null }` still works | No subtype identity; tooling lists the underlying function type in some places |
| `fun interface ForegroundActivityProvider { fun get(): Activity? }` | Named subtype; reflective tooling shows the interface name | Forces `ForegroundActivityProvider { … }` at every construction site; the default `{ null }` becomes uglier; gains nothing because no consumer subtype-tests the provider |

A typealias wins for this slice — there's no behavior worth
subtype-testing, every consumer calls the provider exactly once
per method, and the call-site ergonomics matter more than reflective
discoverability. The SOLID Guardian's "no anonymous function-typed
constructor params" preference is satisfied because the parameter
is now named via the alias.

### 39.3 Default contract preserved

Every consumer of the typealias keeps the `= { null }` default. The
default contract — "if no host wired an activity provider, treat
every Activity-requiring method as if no Activity were available"
— is identical across the four actuals: each returns its SPI's
safe-default (`false` for `requestReview` / `startFlexibleUpdate`
/ `loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired`, `ConsentStatus.UNKNOWN` for
`requestConsentInfoUpdate`, `AdResult.Failed(NO_ACTIVITY_ERROR_CODE, …)`
for `showInterstitial` / `showRewarded`). Hoisting to a typealias
does not change this contract — the consumer code is unchanged,
only the constructor parameter type expression is.

### 39.4 Import cleanup

The hoist removes `import android.app.Activity` from each of the
four actuals — the type only appeared in the constructor parameter
declaration and in KDoc references. Local variables fed by the
provider (`val activity = activityProvider() ?: …`) are inferred
from the typealias's `Activity?` return; the unwrapping `?: return …`
narrows the local to `Activity` without an explicit type annotation.
KDoc `[Activity]` references that depended on the import are
adjusted to unbracketed `Activity` so they don't dangle.

### 39.5 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 5.z.cleanup

All five source files pass per `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 5.z.cleanup
entries. The typealias hoist is a pure restructuring — no
behavioral change — so the per-file checklists are tightly focused
on (a) the new file's own shape and (b) the unchanged
behavior of the four updated actuals.

The pending-cleanup list documented at §35.5 / §36.2 / §37.2 /
§38.3 / §38.7 is now empty for the Phase 5.z group.

## 40. Phase 6.2.x — `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` + wire into `LibraryViewModel`

### 40.1 Why this slice exists

Phase 6.2 (`LibraryViewModel`, §6) shipped `onDeleteSelected()` as
a UI-only stub: it cleared the selection state and emitted
`LibraryEffect.ShowBulkRemoveSuccess(count = keys.size)` **without
ever touching the repository**. The handler carried an explicit
in-code TODO at `LibraryViewModel.kt:104-107`:

> Bulk remove is wired in via `repository.removeAllFromLibrary` in
> a subsequent slice that adds the `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`.
> For now the per-item toggle path is the public API; the bulk
> effect is emitted so the view can show the success snackbar.

This is that subsequent slice. With the Phase 5.z group + cleanup
done (§38.7, §39), `:platform` is feature-complete for the
rework's third-party-service SPIs, and the next forward motion is
Phase 6+ MVI / use-case completion. The Library bulk-delete TODO
is the narrowest available 6.x slice (one use case + one VM
wiring + one Koin binding = 3 files), so it lands first.

### 40.2 Use case design — `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`

```kotlin
class BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase(
    private val repository: LibraryRepository,
) {
    suspend operator fun invoke(keys: List<MangaKey>): AppResult<Int> {
        if (keys.isEmpty()) return AppResult.Success(0)
        return repository.removeAllFromLibrary(keys).flatMap { AppResult.Success(keys.size) }
    }
}
```

Three deliberate choices:

1. **Returns `AppResult<Int>`, not `AppResult<Unit>`.** The
   repository contract is `removeAllFromLibrary(keys): AppResult<Unit>`
   (the DAO doesn't report row counts back). The ViewModel needs
   the count for `LibraryEffect.ShowBulkRemoveSuccess(count = ...)`
   so the view can render a localized "removed N items" snackbar.
   Doing the `keys.size` map inside the use case rather than in
   the ViewModel keeps the orchestration rule "removed N where N
   is the count of keys we attempted to remove" in **one** place,
   and means a future swap to a count-returning DAO is a one-line
   change here, not a behavioral change in the VM.

2. **Empty-keys fast path returns `Success(0)`.** If the
   multi-select list happens to be cleared between the user's tap
   and the dispatch (e.g. a competing `OnSelectionClear` intent
   races ahead), the use case returns success-with-zero instead
   of round-tripping to the DAO with an empty list. The VM still
   gets the count and skips the snackbar via its own empty-keys
   guard (the VM checks `keys.isEmpty()` before calling), and the
   DAO is spared a pointless query.

3. **`flatMap` from `core.result`, not a manual `when`.** The
   `flatMap` extension on `AppResult` already exists for exactly
   this shape: succeed → transform, fail → propagate verbatim.
   Manual `when` branches would re-implement the propagation rule.

SRP (contract §6): owns one rule — "remove a batch of library
entries and tell the caller how many were targeted". Per-item
removal policy stays in `LibraryRepository` / the data layer;
bulk-vs-single orchestration belongs in a use case, **not** in
the ViewModel and **not** in the repository.

DIP: constructor-injected `LibraryRepository` interface. Koin
binds it as a `factory` (cheap, no per-call state).

### 40.3 ViewModel wiring

`LibraryViewModel` gains `bulkRemoveFromLibrary` as a third
constructor parameter (after `observeLibrary` and
`toggleInLibrary`). The `onDeleteSelected()` body becomes:

```kotlin
private suspend fun onDeleteSelected() {
    val keys = state.value.selection.toList()
    if (keys.isEmpty()) return
    updateState { it.copy(selection = emptySet(), isInSelectionMode = false) }
    bulkRemoveFromLibrary(keys)
        .onSuccess { count -> emit(LibraryEffect.ShowBulkRemoveSuccess(count = count)) }
        .onFailure { emit(LibraryEffect.ShowError(it)) }
}
```

**Selection-clear is eager.** The selection is cleared **before**
the repository call. This matches the legacy UX — the chips and
the "delete N" action button disappear the instant the user taps
delete, so the screen feels responsive even if the DB write takes
a frame. If the call fails, the selection stays cleared (the user
can re-select); the error is reported via `ShowError`. The
alternative — clear-on-success-only — would leave stale chips on
screen for the DB latency window and is not how the legacy app
behaved.

**Both terminal branches emit exactly one effect.** No effect on
the empty-keys early return (consistent with the legacy behavior;
the user tapped delete with nothing selected, so nothing should
appear).

### 40.4 Koin binding

`LibraryReworkModule` gains:

```kotlin
factory { BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase(get()) }
```

and the `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(get(), get(), get()) }`
binding picks up the third arg.

Factory scope matches `ObserveLibraryUseCase` /
`ToggleInLibraryUseCase` — stateless use cases don't need
singleton allocation, and a fresh instance per resolution stays
scope-friendly for any future test override.

### 40.5 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 6.2.x

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 6.2.x. All three files clear the
10-point checklist; no `!!` / `Any` / `lateinit` introduced in
`:domain` / `:presentation`; the use case has a single suspend
operator function with one orchestration concern; the VM gains
exactly one new dependency that maps 1:1 to the new use case.

## 41. Phase 6.3.1 — Details feature `:domain` foundation

### 41.1 Why this slice exists

With the Library feature fully wired end-to-end (`:domain` →
`:data` → `:presentation` → `:ui` → `:composeApp`, route flipped
at Phase 8.y), the natural next feature is **Details** — the
navigation target of `LibraryEffect.NavigateToDetails(manga)`.
Closing that navigation loop end-to-end is the highest-signal
next port (the Library route already declares the target; the
rework just needs to terminate it instead of falling back to the
legacy screen).

This slice ships the foundation only — the **`:domain`** types
that every later Details slice depends on. Strangler-fig: legacy
`:shared` still handles real fetches; no caller is rewired.

### 41.2 Two-model split — `Chapter` and `MangaDetails`

Legacy `MangaInfo` (see `:shared/.../domain/model/MangaInfo.kt`)
ships chapters as `MutableList<ChapterItem>`, and legacy
`ChapterItem` ships pages as `List<ChapterImage>`. The rework
unflattens this:

| Rework type | Source of truth | Mutability | Embeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Chapter` | per-chapter list entry | `val` (immutable) | metadata only — no pages |
| `MangaDetails` | per-manga details record | `val` (immutable) | `List<Chapter>` — no pages |
| _future_ `ChapterPages` | per-chapter page fetch (Reader slice) | TBD | `List<String>` URLs |

Two deliberate splits:

1. **Pages out of `Chapter`.** Pages belong to the Reader feature,
   not to the chapter list. Embedding them in the chapter list
   inflates every Details payload and forces the source-mapper to
   fetch pages eagerly for chapters the user may never open.
2. **`MutableList` → `List`.** Domain entities are immutable in
   the rework (contract §4). Mutations happen at the `:data`
   layer boundary (DAO writes, in-memory cache updates).

The `@Serializable` annotations from legacy are also dropped —
contract §4 forbids framework annotations on domain entities.
Serialization concerns are added by the `:data` mappers at the
layer boundary (next slice, Phase 6.3.2).

### 41.3 String-typed source fields (rating, status, etc.)

`MangaDetails.rating` / `ratingCount` / `favoritesCount` /
`yearOfProduction` / `status` stay `String` rather than typed
values (`Float?`, `Int?`, `MangaStatus enum`). Rationale:

Sources hand these back in widely-varying formats:
- rating: `"4.8 / 5"`, `"9.2"`, `"⭐⭐⭐⭐"`
- ratingCount: `"1.2K votes"`, `"452"`, `""`
- status: `"Ongoing"`, `"Completed"`, `"Hiatus"`, `"In corso"`
- yearOfProduction: `"2018"`, `"2018-2020"`, `""`

Premature typing here would force every source-mapper to parse
and reformat — losing source-specific nuance (the rating string
the user expects to see) and adding parse failures that the rework
doesn't currently model. The UI just renders the string. If a
specific feature (e.g. sort-by-rating) needs typed values later,
it lands as a typed view of the string field, not as a base-type
change.

### 41.4 Single-method repository — no `Flow`, no `refresh`

```kotlin
interface MangaDetailsRepository {
    suspend fun fetchDetails(manga: Manga): AppResult<MangaDetails>
}
```

Three intentional omissions:

1. **No `Flow<MangaDetails>` "observe" method.** Legacy details
   fetches are stateless network calls — no local cache to
   observe. A future cache slice adds `observeCachedDetails(...)`
   separately; today's contract is "go fetch from the source".
2. **No `refresh(...)` variant.** Legacy re-fetches on every
   Details screen entry; the rework preserves that. Pull-to-refresh
   either re-invokes `fetchDetails` or lands a dedicated method
   if a cache distinction matters.
3. **No streaming / incremental delivery.** The `:data` impl
   waits for the source to return everything, then succeeds with
   the full `MangaDetails` or fails with a typed `AppError`.
   Matches every existing source-repository's one-shot return
   contract.

The KDoc commits to the `AppResult.Failure` mapping:
`Network.NoConnectivity / Timeout / Http` for transport,
`Network.Serialization` for parse failure, `Unexpected` (with
preserved `cause`) for unclassifiable failures. This matches the
existing `AppError` hierarchy in `:core` (§9).

### 41.5 One-line use case (`FetchMangaDetailsUseCase`)

The use case is a single suspend `operator invoke` that delegates
to `repository.fetchDetails(manga)` with no transformation.

Why have it at all when the body is `repository.fetchDetails(manga)`:
- **Stable presentation-layer dependency.** The future Details VM
  depends on `FetchMangaDetailsUseCase`, not on
  `MangaDetailsRepository`. Future enrichment of the fetch policy
  (cache fallthrough, library-state merge, history-mark update)
  lands here without changing the VM signature.
- **Test seam.** Mocking one suspend operator is cheaper than
  mocking the full repository for the Details VM unit tests.
- **Consistent with the Library slice.** `ObserveLibraryUseCase`
  / `ToggleInLibraryUseCase` / `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`
  follow the same one-verb-per-use-case pattern.

### 41.6 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 6.3.1

  `MangaDetailsMappers` (legacy `MangaInfo` → rework
  `MangaDetails` + legacy `ChapterItem` → rework `Chapter`).
- **6.3.3** — `:presentation` MVI: `DetailsViewModel` +

## 42. Details feature `:data` impl + mappers (Phase 6.3.2)

### 42.1 Why this slice exists

Phase 6.3.1 declared the Details `:domain` surface
(`MangaDetailsRepository` + `FetchMangaDetailsUseCase` +
`MangaDetails` / `Chapter`). Phase 6.3.2 is the concrete `:data`
implementation that satisfies that surface by delegating to the
legacy source-routing code in
`:shared/sources_repositry/...` — exactly the strangler-fig edge
the Library slice already uses (see §32 / Phase 4.x).

Two source files land in this slice (well under the 5-file cap):
- `data/src/.../data/mapper/MangaDetailsMappers.kt`
- `data/src/.../data/repository/MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl.kt`

### 42.2 Mapper file: legacy DTOs → rework domain types

`MangaDetailsMappers.kt` owns the legacy `MangaInfo` →
`MangaDetails` and legacy `ChapterItem` → `Chapter` translation.

Why aliased imports (`import ... MangaInfo as LegacyMangaInfo`):
both packages share the FQN `me.manga.kira.domain.model` — the
legacy `:shared` package and the rework `:domain` package collide
on the simple names `MangaInfo` / `ChapterItem` vs `MangaDetails` /
`Chapter`. The aliases scope the legacy types to this file so
`:data`'s public surface (the impl signature) only exposes rework
types.

Translation choices (all lossless w.r.t. what the Details screen
renders today, per contract §13 functionality-preservation gate):
- **`imageUrl` → `coverUrl`** — rework picked the conventional
  name (matches `Manga.coverUrl` from §30 / Phase 3).
- **`MutableList<ChapterItem>` → `List<Chapter>`** — domain models
  are immutable (contract §4). The mapper produces a *fresh* list,
  so any legacy code still holding the underlying `MutableList`
  reference can't mutate the rework model after the fact.
- **`ChapterItem.chaptersImages: List<ChapterImage>` is dropped** —
  chapter pages belong to the Reader slice's future `ChapterPages`
  model (per §41.2 and the `Chapter` KDoc). Embedding pages in the
  chapter list inflated every Details payload for no benefit.
- **Everything else** (`api`, `language`, `title`, `url`,
  `description`, `author`, `artist`, `rating`, `ratingCount`,
  `favoritesCount`, `otherNames`, `yearOfProduction`, `status`,
  `genres`, `tags`, and on `Chapter` the `number`, `name`, `url`,
  `date`, `isDownloaded`, `isBookmarked`) is a 1:1 copy — same
  nullability, same string-vs-typed shape. See `MangaDetails` KDoc
  (§41.3) for why `rating` / `status` / `yearOfProduction` stay as
  `String`.

Both mapper functions are `internal` — only callers in the same
module (`:data`) reach them. No serialization annotations cross
the seam: the rework type is plain Kotlin; the legacy type's
`@Serializable` annotation stays scoped to `:shared`.

### 42.3 Repository impl

`MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl` is the typed-error seam between the
legacy `Flow<State<MangaInfo>>` world and the rework
`AppResult<MangaDetails>` world.

**Constructor**:
- `private val sourcesRepository: SourcesRepository` — legacy
  `:shared` source registry (`getOrRepoByName(api): BaseMangaRepository?`).
  Transitional — removed in the future phase that relocates sources
  into `:data`.
- `private val dispatchers: DispatcherProvider` — `:core` dispatcher
  facade. The collect runs inside `withContext(dispatchers.io)`,
  matching `LibraryRepositoryImpl` (§32).

**Method body (`fetchDetails(manga)`)**:
1. Look up the source by `manga.api` via
   `sourcesRepository.getOrRepoByName(...)`. Null → typed failure
   `AppError.Unexpected("Unknown source api=...")`. **This is the
   one observable-behavior difference from the legacy path**:
   `getRepoByName` (the non-null variant) silently returns
   `EmptyMangaRepository` whose `fetchMangaChaptersF` emits a
   success with all-empty fields, hiding the integrity issue. The
   rework's Details VM doesn't exist yet (Phase 6.3.3), so there is
   no live consumer whose behavior changes; the new contract is
   chosen fresh.
2. Collect the legacy flow with `.first { it !is LegacyState.Loading }`
   — drops the Loading emission (MVI tracks loading via state, not
   via the source flow) and pulls the first terminal value.
3. Map:
   - `LegacyState.Success(info)` → `AppResult.Success(info.toDomain())`
   - `LegacyState.Error(code, message)` → typed `AppError` via
     `toAppError()`
   - `LegacyState.Loading` is unreachable (filtered above); the
     branch is `error("Filtered above")` so an unexpected
     impl change would fail loudly.
4. Catch:
   - `CancellationException` → rethrow (structured-concurrency
     invariant; no swallowing).
   - Any other `Throwable` → `AppResult.Failure(classifyThrowable(t))`.

**Error classification** (`toAppError()` / `classifyThrowable()`):
- HTTP status in `400..599` → `AppError.Network.Http(statusCode)`.
- `code == 0` with connectivity-hint substring in the message
  (`unknown host` / `no address associated` / `nodename nor servname` /
  `unable to resolve host`) → `AppError.Network.NoConnectivity`.
- `code == 0` with timeout-hint substring (`timeout` / `timed out`)
  → `AppError.Network.Timeout`.
- Anything else → `AppError.Unexpected(message, cause)`.

The two classifiers (one for `LegacyState.Error` emissions, one for
exceptions thrown during collect) share the same substring rules so
both paths produce the same buckets — many legacy sources throw
instead of emitting `State.Error`, and the rework Details screen
shouldn't see a behavior cliff between the two paths.

**No `runCatching*` helper** was introduced for this impl: only one
suspend method needs the wrapping, and the `try/catch` pattern is
small enough that hoisting it into a helper would obscure the
two-branch classifier logic. If a second method joins the impl
later (e.g. cached observe), the helper can extract then.

### 42.4 Koin wiring — deferred

No Koin binding is added in this slice. `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl`
and `FetchMangaDetailsUseCase` live in `:data` / `:domain`
respectively, but no `:composeApp` consumer of them exists yet —
the Details VM (Phase 6.3.3), screen (Phase 7.x), and module +
nav route (Phase 8.x) land in subsequent slices. Binding the impl
now would be dead wiring.

When Phase 8.x adds `DetailsReworkModule`, the bindings will follow
the Library precedent verbatim:
```kotlin
single<MangaDetailsRepository> {
    MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl(get(), get())
}
factory { FetchMangaDetailsUseCase(get()) }
viewModel { DetailsViewModel(get()) }
```

## 43. Details feature `:presentation` MVI (Phase 6.3.3)

### 43.1 Why this slice exists

Phase 6.3.2 closed the `:data` side of the Details feature
(`MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl` + mappers, §42). Phase 6.3.3 lands
the strict-MVI ViewModel + Intent/State/Effect contracts that the
future `:ui` `DetailsScreen` consumes. It is the second use of the
MVI base contracts (Library was first, see §38 / Phase 6.2) and
the first stateful-fetch slice on top of [AppResult] — Library's
state stream was a Flow; Details is a one-shot suspend.

Four files in `presentation/src/commonMain/.../details/`:
- `DetailsState.kt`
- `DetailsIntent.kt`
- `DetailsEffect.kt`
- `DetailsViewModel.kt`

### 43.2 State shape: split flags, not a sum type

The legacy `MangaDerailsViewModel` exposed
`StateFlow<State<MangaInfo>>` — a sealed `Loading | Success | Error`
sum the screen had to `when`-match on. The rework state replaces
that with four independent fields:
- `isLoading: Boolean = false`
- `manga: Manga? = null` (the identity the screen renders)
- `details: MangaDetails? = null`
- `error: AppError? = null`

The reason to split rather than wrap:
- **Stale-while-revalidate is free.** A future pull-to-refresh sets
  `isLoading = true` while keeping `details` populated; the screen
  can show the previously-fetched chapter list with a spinner
  overlay. The sum-type version would have forced
  `Loading | Success(stale) | Error` shape gymnastics.
- **Independent rendering.** The cover, the metadata header, and
  the chapter list can each react to whichever of the four fields
  matters to them without the screen needing to fan out the same
  `when` block five times.
- **Configuration-change replay safety.** `manga` lives in state,
  so the StateFlow re-emission to a fresh host after a config
  change carries enough identity to render immediately. The legacy
  VM stashed `currentUrl` as a private mutable field set by the
  navigation host via `initialize(...)`; the rework folds that
  into the [DetailsIntent.OnEnter] intent payload.

Two computed conveniences (`hasDetails`, `isInitialLoading`) live
on the data class so the screen can render terminal states without
re-implementing the same boolean math.

### 43.3 Intent surface — four cases, no init side door

Sealed intents: `OnEnter(manga)`, `OnRetry`, `OnChapterClick(chapter)`,
`OnBackClick`.

- **`OnEnter(manga)`** is the entry point. The navigation host
  submits it after Koin resolves the VM. The reducer **short-circuits
  on identity match** (api+language+title triple) so a configuration
  change re-attaching the screen to a fresh VM doesn't re-trigger
  the network fetch — the StateFlow already carries the cached
  details.
- **`OnRetry`** is the explicit re-fetch lever. It pulls the manga
  from current state (no payload needed) and resets `isLoading +
  error`. This is the one path that always hits the network.
- **`OnChapterClick(chapter)`** routes through the VM (rather than
  directly emitting from the screen) so the reducer can check
  in-state manga + emit the [DetailsEffect.NavigateToReader] effect
  with both halves of the navigation target.
- **`OnBackClick`** is a passthrough; the VM emits
  [DetailsEffect.NavigateBack] and the host pops.

### 43.4 Effect surface — pure triggers, no render data

Three effects: `NavigateBack`, `NavigateToReader(manga, chapter)`,
`ShowError(error)`.

The recurring-vs-one-shot split (state vs effect) follows the same
rule as Library (§38.4): anything the screen wants to render
across recompositions lives in state; anything that fires exactly
once (a toast, a nav transition) is an effect. The `error` lives
in **both** state (for an inline error banner) and an effect (for
the snackbar), which is by-design — they have different lifetimes.

`NavigateToReader` carries the [Manga] + [Chapter] pair because
the Reader feature (future slice) needs both: the manga identity
for header lookup and the chapter for page fetch.

### 43.5 ViewModel — thin orchestrator

`DetailsViewModel` has one collaborator (`FetchMangaDetailsUseCase`,
constructor-injected) and one job (translate intents into state
updates + effects). The reducer body is ~30 LOC:

```
override suspend fun handle(intent: DetailsIntent) {
    when (intent) {
        is DetailsIntent.OnEnter        -> onEnter(intent.manga)
        DetailsIntent.OnRetry           -> onRetry()
        is DetailsIntent.OnChapterClick -> onChapterClick(intent)
        DetailsIntent.OnBackClick       -> emit(DetailsEffect.NavigateBack)
    }
}
```

`onEnter` and `onRetry` both funnel into `runFetch(manga)` which
runs the use case and threads `AppResult` through `onSuccess` /
`onFailure` — the same `.onSuccess { ... }.onFailure { ... }`
pattern the Library VM uses (consistency by precedent, not by
extracted helper).

**No `SourcesRepository`.** The legacy VM held a direct reference
to the source registry to read `blackListGenres`. The rework VM
doesn't — the adult-content gate from the legacy code is
intentionally **not ported** in this slice. It lands as a separate
`IsAdultContentUseCase` (future slice) without changing
[DetailsViewModel]'s signature.

### 43.6 Koin wiring — still deferred

Same as §42.4: no Koin binding is added yet. The
`DetailsReworkModule` lands in Phase 8.x alongside the guarded debug
nav route. The binding sketch:

```kotlin
single<MangaDetailsRepository> {
    MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl(get(), get())
}
factory { FetchMangaDetailsUseCase(get()) }
viewModel { DetailsViewModel(get()) }
```

## 44. Details feature `:ui` composable (Phase 7.x)

Closes the Details surface by translating the MVI surface from §43
(`DetailsState` / `DetailsIntent` / `DetailsEffect` / `DetailsViewModel`)
into a Compose Multiplatform screen. Mirrors the Library precedent
(§31) — stateful wrapper for VM wiring, stateless content for testing
and previews — so the two slices stay structurally identical and easy
to compare side-by-side.

### 44.1 Why

The MVI surface from Phase 6.3.3 is fully usable, but it has no live
consumer. Until a composable subscribes to its `state`/`effects` and
dispatches intents, the slice's only verification is that it compiles.
Phase 7.x adds the rendering half so the surface can be exercised
end-to-end behind the future debug-only nav route.

The work is intentionally narrow: this is the **minimum-viable** Details
screen — no Coil cover, no share/bookmark/download actions, no sort or
filter sheets, no visual parity with the legacy `MangaDetailsScreen`.
Those features land in later micro-slices on top of this baseline.

### 44.2 Stateful / stateless split

```
DetailsScreen(viewModel, manga, onNavigateBack, onNavigateToReader)
  └─ collectAsState() + viewModel::submit
     └─ DetailsScreenContent(state, effects, onIntent, …)
```

Same shape as `LibraryScreen` / `LibraryScreenContent`. The wrapper
owns the VM ↔ Compose plumbing (collecting the state flow,
forwarding intents). The content composable owns rendering and is
driveable by previews/tests with canned `DetailsState` + a hand-rolled
`Flow<DetailsEffect>`. Splitting these two roles is the SRP cut that
makes the screen testable without a real ViewModel — a habit we apply
to every screen the rework adds.

### 44.3 Entry-intent dispatch

```kotlin
LaunchedEffect(manga.api, manga.language, manga.title) {
    onIntent(DetailsIntent.OnEnter(manga))
}
```

Keyed on the identity triple, not on the `Manga` instance itself —
config-change replay re-attaches a fresh host with the same identity
but a possibly-different reference, and we don't want that re-firing
the use case. The VM's `OnEnter` already short-circuits when the
in-state manga matches (§43.4 / §43.5), but keying the
`LaunchedEffect` correctly means the intent isn't even dispatched in
the steady-state replay case — one less suspended job churning per
recomposition.

### 44.4 Effects routing

A second `LaunchedEffect(effects)` collects the shared one-shot flow:

| Effect                              | Target                                       |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `DetailsEffect.NavigateBack`        | `onNavigateBack()`                           |
| `DetailsEffect.NavigateToReader`    | `onNavigateToReader(effect.manga, …chapter)` |
| `DetailsEffect.ShowError`           | `SnackbarHost` via `error.toUserMessage()`   |

`AppError.toUserMessage()` is a file-private extension matching the
`LibraryScreen` precedent — keeps user-facing copy out of `:core`
(where strings would be presentation-policy contraband) and lets each
screen pick its own tone if they ever diverge. The same shape is
documented in `LibraryScreen.toUserMessage` (Phase 7.x for Library).

### 44.5 Body branches

The body is a single `when` over the state. Three valid renders, one
silent fallback:

| Predicate                                          | Render                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `state.isInitialLoading`                           | `CircularProgressIndicator` centered                                   |
| `state.error != null && !state.hasDetails`         | `DetailsErrorPane` (typed error message + retry button)                |
| `state.details != null`                            | `DetailsBody` (LazyColumn of header / description / genres / chapters) |
| (none of the above — first frame before any fetch) | `Unit`                                                                 |

`isInitialLoading` and `hasDetails` are the derived flags exposed on
`DetailsState` (§43.2). They keep the predicates declarative — the
screen never reads the raw `isLoading`/`details` pair together, which
would have to re-state the "loading-with-cached-data" rule.

The error pane is shown only when there are **no cached details**.
Mid-session refresh failures with stale details still on screen show
the snackbar (via `ShowError`) and leave the details body intact, same
shape as the Library slice's stale-while-revalidate behaviour.

### 44.6 Sub-composable inventory

All file-private; no API leak. None take a VM — they're pure
state-in / callback-out.

- `DetailsTopBar(title, onBack)` — minimal Material3 `TopAppBar`. Title
  prefers `state.details?.title` over `manga.title` so the typed-in
  identity is replaced by the source-of-truth as soon as the fetch
  lands. Back arrow uses the same character glyph as
  `LibraryScreen.LibraryTopBar` (no icon dependency added yet).
- `DetailsErrorPane(error, onRetry, modifier)` — typed error message
  + `Button` retry. Retry submits `DetailsIntent.OnRetry`; the VM
  re-uses the in-state manga to drive the fetch (§43.5), so the
  screen doesn't have to re-thread `manga` here.
- `DetailsBody(details, onChapterClick)` — `LazyColumn` with stable
  string keys for `header` / `description` / `genres` /
  `chapters-header`, then the chapters keyed by `chapter.url` (the
  rework's stable identity per `Chapter.url` KDoc).
- `DetailsHeader(details)` — placeholder cover Box (96.dp width, 0.7
  aspect ratio, `surfaceVariant` fill) + title / author / status
  column. The Box stands in for the Coil cover that lands in a later
  micro-slice — kept as a deliberate visual hole so reviewers see
  where image loading is missing.
- `GenreChipRow(genres)` — single `Row` of `AssistChip`s, capped at
  `MAX_GENRE_CHIPS = 8`. Cap chosen empirically to fit one line on
  typical phone widths without horizontal scroll; matches the legacy
  screen's overflow-truncate behaviour. Future slice can swap in a
  `FlowRow` if we want to wrap.
- `ChapterRow(chapter, onClick)` — clickable Row with
  `Chapter.displayLabel()` (`"Ch. N — name"` when name present, just
  `"Ch. N"` otherwise) + optional `date.toString()` + small dot when
  `chapter.isDownloaded`. The downloaded dot is the same visual
  affordance the legacy screen uses; the dot colour follows the
  Material primary so dark/light theming carries through.

### 44.7 Smart-cast workaround across module boundaries

Inside `DetailsScreenContent`, the body block captures
`state.details` / `state.error` into locals before the `when`:

```kotlin
val details = state.details
val error = state.error
when {
    state.isInitialLoading -> …
    error != null && !state.hasDetails -> DetailsErrorPane(error = error, …)
    details != null -> DetailsBody(details = details, …)
}
```

Kotlin's compiler refuses to smart-cast a public-API property
declared in a different module (`DetailsState` lives in
`:presentation`, the screen in `:ui`). The local-capture trick is the
standard idiom; the alternative would be `requireNotNull` or `!!`,
both of which we've banned in `:presentation`/`:ui` per the project
non-negotiables. The comment in the source spells out the reason so
the next reader doesn't try to "simplify" it.

### 44.8 Scope discipline — what's explicitly deferred

| Concern                                          | Where it lands                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cover image loading (Coil)                       | future Details micro-slice (after the cross-cutting Coil setup is ported)         |
| Share / bookmark / download action buttons       | future Details micro-slice                                                        |
| Sort + filter sheets                             | future Details micro-slice                                                        |
| Adult-content / blacklist gate                   | `IsAdultContentUseCase` slice — VM signature is already future-proofed (§43.5)    |
| `:composeApp` Koin binding for the rework slice  | Phase 8.x (`DetailsReworkModule`) — sketch in §42.4 / §43.6                       |
| Guarded debug nav route in `:composeApp`         | Phase 8.x — same shape as the Library debug route from Phase 8.y                  |

The legacy `MangaDetailsScreen` in `:composeApp` remains the
user-facing binding for Details until Phase 8.x ships the debug-only
route to this screen — strangler-fig stays intact.

### 44.9 Build gates

- `:ui:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green
- `:ui:compileKotlinDesktop` — green
- `:ui:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green
- `:ui:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green
- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` (functionality-preservation
  gate) — green

iOS framework link not executed (Windows host). No new warnings. No
new module dependencies added; the screen only consumes `:presentation`
+ `:domain` + `:core` + the `:ui` theme tokens already imported by
`LibraryScreen`.

### 44.10 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 7.x

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 7.x. The single source file clears the
10-point checklist. No `expect/actual` (pure commonMain). No `!!` /
`Any` / `lateinit`. The stateful wrapper has exactly one collaborator
(the VM); the stateless content composable takes raw state +
callbacks and is referentially transparent given its inputs.

Remaining Details feature slices:
- **8.x** — `:composeApp` `DetailsReworkModule` + guarded debug

## 45. Details feature `:composeApp` wiring (Phase 8.x)

Closes the rework Details slice as a reachable end-to-end surface:
the `:domain` interface + `:data` impl + `:presentation` MVI VM +
`:ui` composable are now bound through Koin and exposed behind a
debug-only nav route. Mirrors the Library precedent (Phase 8 +
8.y) so the two slices stay structurally identical.

### 45.1 Why

The MVI surface (§43) and the screen (§44) were both already
implemented, but neither had a live consumer in the `:composeApp`
nav graph. Phase 8.x is the final wire — without it the
`DetailsViewModel` can't be resolved from Koin (no module declared
it) and the `DetailsScreen` is unreachable from runtime navigation
(no `composable<Screen.…>` block dispatched to it). The slice is
purely additive: legacy `MangaDetailsScreen` /
`MangaDerailsViewModel` are untouched and remain the user-facing
binding for Details.

### 45.2 Files touched

Five files, within the 5-files-per-commit budget — two new, three
edited:

| File                                                                                    | Change |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `composeApp/.../di/DetailsReworkModule.kt`                                              | NEW    |
| `composeApp/.../di/ReworkModules.kt`                                                    | EDIT   |
| `composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt`                                                   | EDIT   |
| `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute.kt`                     | NEW    |
| `composeApp/.../App.kt`                                                                 | EDIT   |

### 45.3 Koin module shape

```kotlin
val detailsReworkModule: Module = module {
    single<MangaDetailsRepository> {
        MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl(
            sourcesRepository = get(),
            dispatchers = get(),
        )
    }
    factory { FetchMangaDetailsUseCase(get()) }
    viewModel { DetailsViewModel(get()) }
}
```

Same shape as `libraryReworkModule` (§42.4 / §43.6 sketched
binding). Three things deserve calling out:

1. **`SourcesRepository` resolves from the legacy `:shared`
   `SharedModule`** (specifically the `single` at
   `SharedModule.kt:305`). The strangler-fig boundary is the
   rework `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl` (§42.2): it consumes the
   legacy registry, delegates to `getOrRepoByName(api).fetchMangaChaptersF(url)`,
   and maps the legacy `MangaInfo` into the pure-domain
   `MangaDetails`. The rework graph never reaches into `:shared`
   above this single seam.
2. **`DispatcherProvider` resolves from `libraryReworkModule`**.
   Library landed first and declared it as `single`; declaring it
   again here would trip Koin's duplicate-binding guard. The
   `KDoc` on `DetailsReworkModule` documents this so the next
   reader doesn't try to add a parallel declaration "for
   isolation".
3. **Use case is `factory`, VM is `viewModel`** — matches the
   contract's stated lifecycles (`:domain` use case KDoc says
   "Koin binds it as a factory"; VMs always go through Koin's
   `ViewModelStore`-aware binding to survive config changes).

### 45.4 Aggregator append

`allReworkModules()` now returns `[libraryReworkModule,
detailsReworkModule]`. OCP-friendly: adding the next feature slice
(reader, sources picker, etc.) is a one-line append. Hosts never
change — `initKoin { … allReworkModules() … }` already loads the
returned list verbatim, established in Phase 8.x for Library.

### 45.5 `Screen.MangaDetailsRework` arg shape

The rework route's nav args are wider than the legacy
`Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)`:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class MangaDetailsRework(
    val api: String,
    val language: String,
    val title: String,
    val url: String,
    val coverUrl: String,
    val rating: Int?,
    val genres: List<String>,
) : Screen("…Screen.MangaDetailsRework")
```

Reasons:

- The rework `DetailsScreen` needs `manga.title` as the **top-bar
  placeholder** before the fetch lands — the legacy screen got
  away with `(url, api)` because it could fall back to
  `SourcesRepository.getRepoByName(api)` + cached `MangaInfo` for
  the title, but that's a `:shared`-only lookup the rework's pure
  `:ui` layer deliberately doesn't perform.
- The rework VM's `OnEnter` re-entry guard (§43.4 / §43.5) keys
  on the (api, language, title) **identity triple**. Carrying
  those three through nav args lets us reconstruct a `Manga`
  whose `matches(other)` check is correct on first frame, so
  config-change replay doesn't re-fetch.
- `coverUrl`, `rating`, `genres` aren't load-bearing for this
  slice (cover is a placeholder Box, rating isn't rendered, and
  genres get overwritten by the fetched `MangaDetails`), but
  carrying them preserves the option for the next micro-slice
  (Coil cover loading) to render *something* during the initial
  fetch instead of an empty grey rectangle.

`Serializable` is from `kotlinx.serialization`, the same
mechanism that powers every other type-safe Nav route in this
project. `Int?` and `List<String>` are both supported by Nav
2.9.2's `typeMap` defaults.

### 45.6 Route adapter responsibilities

`MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute(navController, backStackEntry)`:

1. Resolves `DetailsViewModel` via `koinViewModel()` and the
   legacy `ToastShower` via `koinInject()` (used only for the
   "reader not wired yet" toast).
2. Reads args via `backStackEntry.toRoute<Screen.MangaDetailsRework>()`.
3. Reconstructs a `Manga` from the args. This is a pure
   value-class construction — no I/O, no `remember` needed; the
   `LaunchedEffect` inside `DetailsScreen` is keyed on the
   identity triple, so repeated recompositions don't re-fire
   `OnEnter` even if the `Manga` reference changes.
4. Calls `DetailsScreen(viewModel, manga, onNavigateBack,
   onNavigateToReader)`:
   - `onNavigateBack = { navController.safePopBackStack() }` —
     same idiom as the legacy `MangaDetailsScreenRoute`.
   - `onNavigateToReader = { _, chapter ->
     toastShower.showShort("Reader rework not wired yet …") }` —
     deliberate no-op (see §45.7).

### 45.7 Why `onNavigateToReader` is a no-op for this slice

The rework Details screen surfaces `NavigateToReader(manga,
chapter)` as a one-shot effect when the user taps a chapter row.
The legacy Reader entry point is
`Screen.ChapterImagesFragment(isHome, api, language, mangaId,
chapterId, mangatitle, mangaUrl, mangaImgUrl, chapterNumber,
chapterUrl, paths, isDownload)` — twelve fields, most derived
from a `SavedMangaEntity` row that **doesn't exist for an
un-bookmarked manga reached via this debug route**. Wiring the
rework Details to the legacy Reader would require either:

- a pre-fetch into the SavedManga table just to satisfy the args
  (changes observable behaviour for the debug route — taps now
  silently bookmark the manga), **or**
- a parallel Reader route that takes a different arg shape (the
  Reader rework's actual job — out of scope here).

The toast is a deliberate dead-end so the slice ships **without
backing into the legacy Reader's arg shape** and without invading
SavedManga write paths. Reader rework picks this up later.

### 45.8 `App.kt` NavHost registration

Same shape as `Screen.LibraryRework` (Phase 8.y):

```kotlin
composable<Screen.MangaDetailsRework> { backStackEntry ->
    SideEffect { onBottomBarVisibleChange(false) }
    MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute(
        navController = navController,
        backStackEntry = backStackEntry,
    )
}
```

`onBottomBarVisibleChange(false)` matches the legacy `MangaDetails`
behaviour — Details is a leaf route, not a tab. The comment block
above the registration documents that no user-facing entry points
here yet, that the rework Library still navigates to legacy
`Screen.MangaDetails`, and that the swap waits on Reader + image
loading + parity actions.

- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 8.x. All five files clear the 10-point

### 45.11 What the Details rework still owes

The slice is end-to-end, but **deliberately minimal**. Picked up
by future micro-slices, in roughly this order:

- **Cover image loading via Coil** — restores the load-bearing
  fixes (Android `RGB_565` + `allowHardware(false)` for reader
  pages, Desktop Skia `maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL)`, AVIF decoder
  factory on Android, OkHttp fetcher override on Android, iOS +
  Desktop `HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder` registration) at the
  composition root. None of these regressions are reproducible
  yet because the rework Details screen renders a placeholder Box,
  not an `AsyncImage` — but they all have to land in the same
  slice that adds the `AsyncImage`.
- **`IsAdultContentUseCase`** — port the legacy blacklist gate
  without leaking `SourcesRepository` into the rework VM.
- **Share / bookmark / download / refresh actions** — match the
  legacy Details screen's action bar.
- **Sort + filter sheets** for the chapter list.
- **Reader rework** — own arg shape, own MVI surface, own
  route. When that lands, this route's `onNavigateToReader` toast
  is replaced with a real `safeNavigate(Screen.ReaderRework(…))`

- **User-facing route swap** — once parity is reached, the
  bottom-nav and the rework Library route both point at this
  surface, and the legacy `MangaDetailsScreen` /
  `MangaDerailsViewModel` are deleted in a separate cleanup slice.

## 46. Phase 6.3.4 — `IsAdultContentUseCase` foundation + `:data` impl + Koin wiring

### 46.1 Why this slice exists

The legacy `MangaDerailsViewModel.isPlus18(gens, api)` reaches
directly into `SourcesRepository.getRepoByName(api).blackListGenres`
to decide whether to gate the chapter list / blur the cover / show
a content warning. That coupling violates DIP (presentation
depends on `:shared` data) and SRP (the VM owns both render policy
and classification policy).

The Details slice already lists this gap explicitly in §45.11
("`IsAdultContentUseCase` — port the legacy blacklist gate without
leaking `SourcesRepository` into the rework VM"). Phase 6.3.4
lands the policy abstraction across all three modules in one
slice, so the follow-up VM-wiring slice has the typed dependency
ready to inject — mirroring the **land + wire** split that worked
for `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` (§40).

### 46.2 Files touched

Three new files plus one Koin edit — well under the 5-file budget:

- NEW `domain/src/.../domain/repository/AdultContentClassifier.kt`
  — synchronous policy interface (`fun isAdultContent(api, genres): Boolean`).
- NEW `domain/src/.../domain/usecase/details/IsAdultContentUseCase.kt`
  — `operator fun invoke(manga: Manga): Boolean` delegate.
- NEW `data/src/.../data/repository/AdultContentClassifierImpl.kt`
  — `SourcesRepository`-backed blacklist lookup.
- EDIT `composeApp/src/.../di/DetailsReworkModule.kt` — adds
  `single<AdultContentClassifier>` + `factory { IsAdultContentUseCase(get()) }`.

No VM changes in this slice. The wiring slice (a separate commit)
will inject `IsAdultContentUseCase` into `DetailsViewModel` and
fold the result into `DetailsState` — same shape as the
`BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` two-step pattern.

### 46.3 Classifier interface — design choices

**Synchronous, not `suspend`.** Every source's `blackListGenres`
is a `val Set<String>` initialised at construction time of the
`BaseMangaRepository` subclass — no I/O, no network, no DB. The
classification is `genres.any { it in blacklist }`, a pure
in-memory lookup. Marking the interface `suspend` would force
Compose callers (`remember {}`, `derivedStateOf {}`) to hoist the
call into `LaunchedEffect`, paying coroutine cost for a
synchronous decision. If a future source-rating policy adds
remote lookup (parental-rating service, age verification API),
that policy lives on a **sibling** interface
(`RemoteContentRatingService`) so this in-memory contract stays
stable.

**Takes a `String` api, not a typed `Source` value object.** The
legacy source registry (`SourcesRepository.getRepoByName(name: String)`)
already keys by string identifier; user-library entries and nav
args carry the same string. Introducing a typed `Source` wrapper
here would mandate a parallel mapping at every call site for no
behavioural gain — the rework can lift the type later without
breaking the observable contract.

**Returns `Boolean`, not `AppResult<Boolean>`.** The function has
no recoverable error mode: unknown api strings are *not* errors,
they're a defined "treat as not adult" branch (`false`). Wrapping
in `AppResult` would force consumers to pattern-match a `Failure`
branch that the impl can never produce.

**Unknown sources → `false`.** Matches legacy effective
behaviour: `SourcesRepository.getRepoByName(name)` falls back to
`EmptyMangaRepository` whose `blackListGenres = emptySet()`, and
`genres.any { it in emptySet() }` is always `false`. The rework
impl reaches the same conclusion via the nullable
`getOrRepoByName(...)?` accessor introduced in §42.2 — no
behavioural delta from the user's perspective.

**Case-sensitivity matches legacy verbatim.** The lookup compares
`genres` against the source's `blackListGenres` set as-is.
Sources that want case-insensitive matching pre-normalise their
own blacklist (lower-cased strings) — same constraint
`Manga.genres` already declares in its KDoc ("lower-cased +
trimmed"). Introducing normalisation here would diverge from the
legacy and could flip outcomes for sources that intentionally
mixed casing.

### 46.4 Use case — why take `Manga` instead of `(api, genres)`

`IsAdultContentUseCase.invoke(manga: Manga): Boolean` over
`invoke(api: String, genres: List<String>): Boolean`:

- The single live caller (the future `DetailsViewModel`) holds a
  `Manga` in state already; threading the `api` + `genres` pair by
  hand would be a redundant deconstruction at the call site.
- A single argument is easier to mock in unit tests (one
  `Manga.fixture()` builder vs two correlated params).
- The use case body is the policy seam — if a future variant
  needs more `Manga` fields (e.g. `language`-aware blacklist), the
  signature stays stable and only the body changes. Compare to
  `(api, genres)` where the caller would have to learn the new
  field shape.

The classifier interface stays at the raw `(api, genres)` shape
because the `:data` impl doesn't care about anything else on
`Manga` — passing the whole entity through the policy seam would
make the interface harder to fake in `:domain` tests later.

### 46.5 `:data` impl — why a separate class from `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl`

Both classes consume the same legacy `SourcesRepository`, so a
"bundle them" instinct is natural. The slice rejects that:

- **Different SRP.** `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl` owns a network /
  parse policy (I/O on the dispatcher, typed-error classification
  for HTTP / connectivity / timeout buckets). `AdultContentClassifierImpl`
  owns a synchronous in-memory predicate. Bundling them would
  produce a single class whose first method runs on
  `dispatchers.io` and whose second method must explicitly avoid
  `withContext` — the kind of "two unrelated concerns in one
  file" smell SRP exists to prevent.
- **Different lifecycle ergonomics.** A future caching layer on
  fetches (in-memory LRU keyed by manga URL) is a credible
  near-term change; a future caching layer on the classifier
  is not — the lookup is already a `Set.contains`. Keeping them
  separate means caching one doesn't ripple into the other.
- **Different test surface.** Mocking the classifier is one
  one-line stub; mocking the repository requires standing up the
  whole `LegacyState` → `AppResult` translation. A unit test for
  a future "blur cover when adult" branch in the VM only needs
  the classifier — the bundled class would force the test to
  wire up the irrelevant fetch path too.

The impl uses the nullable `getOrRepoByName(api)?.blackListGenres ?: return false`
accessor for the same reason §42.2 does — the rework treats
unknown sources as a typed "no blacklist" condition rather than
silently relying on the legacy `EmptyMangaRepository` fallback.
Two early-return short-circuits (`genres.isEmpty()` and empty
blacklist) skip the `Iterable.any` allocation in the common case
where the manga has no genres listed yet.

### 46.6 Koin wiring — lifecycle choices

`detailsReworkModule` gains two bindings (added between the
existing `factory { FetchMangaDetailsUseCase(get()) }` and the
`viewModel` declaration):

```kotlin
single<AdultContentClassifier> { AdultContentClassifierImpl(sourcesRepository = get()) }
factory { IsAdultContentUseCase(get()) }
```

- **Classifier → `single`.** The impl holds the legacy
  `SourcesRepository` reference (itself a `:shared` singleton)
  and is otherwise stateless. Re-creating it per resolution would
  allocate a wrapper that immediately re-resolves the same source
  registry — wasteful for a class that has no per-call state.
  Same scope discipline as `MangaDetailsRepository` (also
  `single` for the same reason — see §46.4 of `DetailsReworkModule.kt` KDoc).
- **Use case → `factory`.** Matches every other rework use case
  (`FetchMangaDetailsUseCase`, `ObserveLibraryUseCase`,
  `ToggleInLibraryUseCase`, `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`).
  Stateless wrappers don't need singleton allocation and a fresh
  instance per resolution stays scope-friendly for future test
  overrides.

`SourcesRepository` (consumed by the classifier impl) is the
same legacy `:shared` singleton declared by `SharedModule.kt` —
the strangler-fig boundary stays at the rework `:data` impl, not
in `:composeApp`.

### 46.7 Build gates

- `:data:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green (21s).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green (56s combined Desktop + iOS run).

No new warnings in any of the four touched/new files; all
reported warnings are pre-existing legacy-code deprecations
(`TabRow`, `LocalClipboardManager`, `Preview`, `menuAnchor()`,
etc.). iOS framework link not executed (Windows host) — deferred
to macOS verification.

### 46.8 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 6.3.4

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 6.3.4. All four files clear the
10-point checklist. No `expect/actual` (all `commonMain`). No
`!!` / `Any` / `lateinit` introduced in `:domain` / `:data` /
`:composeApp`. The interface declares exactly one method; the use
case has exactly one operator; the impl has exactly one
collaborator (`SourcesRepository`); the Koin module gains two
binding lines that map 1:1 to the two new types.

### 46.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **VM wiring.** `DetailsViewModel` is unchanged. The next slice
  injects `IsAdultContentUseCase` as a constructor dependency,
  folds the boolean into `DetailsState` (likely a derived `val
  isAdult: Boolean` or a `derivedStateOf` in `:ui`), and re-runs
  the SOLID checklist. Same shape as `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`'s
  "land + wire" split (§40).
- **`:ui` surface.** No content-warning UI, no blur, no chapter-list
  gating until the VM exposes the flag. The screen renders the
  same body branches as before.
- **`SourcesRepository` migration.** The classifier still depends
  on the legacy `:shared` source registry. Future relocation of
  sources into `:data` would change the classifier's constructor
  injection but not its interface — same strangler-fig posture as
  `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl`.

## 47. Phase 6.3.4.wire — `IsAdultContentUseCase` into `DetailsViewModel`

### 47.1 Why this slice exists

Phase 6.3.4 (§46) landed the abstraction. This slice consumes it
— `DetailsViewModel` gains the adult-content gate as its second
use-case dependency, and `DetailsState` exposes the result as
`isAdult: Boolean` for `:ui` consumers. The actual UI gating
(cover blur, content-warning chip, chapter-list gate) is a
*separate* `:ui` surface slice; this step is the
presentation-layer plumbing that makes the flag observable.

Mirrors the `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` two-step pattern
(§40): "land" (Phase 6.2.x sources) + "wire" (Phase 6.2.x VM
extension). Same shape here, three slice-numbers ahead.

### 47.2 Files touched

Three edits, no new files:

- EDIT `presentation/src/.../details/DetailsState.kt` — add
  `val isAdult: Boolean = false`.
- EDIT `presentation/src/.../details/DetailsViewModel.kt` — add
  `IsAdultContentUseCase` constructor dependency; classify in
  two places (OnEnter tentative + post-fetch authoritative);
  refresh the VM-class KDoc to reflect the new two-use-case
  shape.
- EDIT `composeApp/src/.../di/DetailsReworkModule.kt` — change
  `viewModel { DetailsViewModel(get()) }` to
  `viewModel { DetailsViewModel(get(), get()) }`.

### 47.3 Why classify twice (OnEnter tentative + post-fetch authoritative)

The legacy `MangaDerailsViewModel` only ever classified once,
inside the screen's render path against `info.genres` — the
*fetched* `MangaInfo`. So the simplest port would be a single
post-fetch classification. But that leaves a window between
`OnEnter` and fetch completion where:
- the nav arg already carries genre data (e.g. came from a
  Library card that knows the genres), AND
- the screen has rendered, AND
- `isAdult` is still `false` purely because the fetch hasn't
  returned yet.

Two-stage classification closes that window without changing
authoritative behaviour:

1. **OnEnter tentative.** `isAdultContent(manga)` with the
   nav-arg `Manga`. If the nav route plumbed the genres through
   (the rework's wider `Screen.MangaDetailsRework` arg shape does
   — see §45.5), `isAdult` is correct from the first frame. If
   genres are empty (search-result origin), the classifier
   returns `false` (no overlap with anything ⇒ no overlap with
   the blacklist), which is the conservative default the
   unknown-source contract on `AdultContentClassifier` also
   produces.
2. **Post-fetch authoritative.** `isAdultContent(manga.copy(genres = details.genres))`
   on success — same identity, fetched genres. This is the
   legacy parity point. If the source's actual genres reveal
   adult content that the nav arg didn't carry, the flag flips
   `false → true`. If the source returns fewer genres than the
   nav arg knew, the flag can flip `true → false` (and a future
   policy that treats this case differently can land here without
   breaking the contract).

Both classification calls are synchronous in-memory `Set.contains`
operations (per `AdultContentClassifier` KDoc), so they fold into
the same `updateState` block as the surrounding state transitions
— no extra suspension point, no additional MVI intent. Compare
to a `suspend` design where every classification would have to
launch a coroutine and `emit` a state-update intent.

### 47.4 Why `manga.copy(genres = details.genres)` rather than building a fresh `Manga`

The post-fetch classification needs a `Manga` whose `api` matches
the source the details came from and whose `genres` match the
fetched data. Building a `Manga(...)` from scratch with all 7
fields would duplicate the nav-arg values and create a maintenance
burden if the `Manga` constructor adds fields later. `manga.copy(genres = details.genres)`
expresses the intent ("same identity, refreshed genre list")
precisely and keeps the change localised — adding a field to
`Manga` doesn't require an update here.

The `MangaDetails` model also carries its own `api` field (mapped
from the source's response in §42.2). Cross-checking
`manga.api == details.api` would be defensive at a layer that
shouldn't be defending — the repository (`MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl`)
guarantees these match by construction (it routes the fetch by
`manga.api` and the mapper preserves it). Adding an `error("api mismatch")`
here would protect against an impossible state.

### 47.5 Why no MVI intent for "re-classify"

The two natural alternatives — surfacing classification as its
own intent (`DetailsIntent.ClassifyAdult(manga)`) or as its own
effect — were rejected:

- **Intent.** Classification is a *pure derivation* from already-in-state
  data; it has no caller-side decision to make. MVI intents
  exist for user/system actions, not for VM-internal data folds.
  Adding `ClassifyAdult` would make `isAdult` look like a
  user-controlled toggle, which it isn't.
- **Effect.** Effects are for view-side reactions (navigate,
  toast, focus). `isAdult` is render-relevant state, not a
  one-shot trigger. The view reads it from `DetailsState` and
  renders accordingly — no `LaunchedEffect` needed.

Folding it into the existing `OnEnter` + `onSuccess` transitions
keeps the intent surface stable and matches the reducer-only
write discipline strict MVI requires.

### 47.6 `DetailsState.isAdult` default value

`false` is the only correct default:
- It matches `AdultContentClassifier`'s unknown-source contract
  (returns `false`), so initial state and the "no manga yet"
  branch agree.
- It matches the legacy initial behaviour: `MangaDerailsViewModel`'s
  `isPlus18` was a `Boolean` *computed* per render — the initial
  state before any fetch produced `false` because `info.genres`
  was empty.
- It keeps the view's render path simple — the
  default-on-construction state needs no special
  "adult-not-yet-classified" sentinel.

A nullable `Boolean?` (where `null` = "not classified yet") was
considered. Rejected because:
- The view would need a third branch (`null` → show what? a
  spinner? same as `false`?). In practice every "not classified"
  scenario maps to the same render as `false`, so the extra
  state buys nothing.
- A nullable `Boolean` in `:domain`/`:presentation` invites
  defensive `?: false` at every call site. Banning that pattern
  is one of the reasons typed errors live in `:core`/`AppError`
  in the first place.

### 47.7 Koin wiring — single-line change

```kotlin
viewModel { DetailsViewModel(get(), get()) }
```

Koin resolves `get()` by type at the call site. The first `get()`
is `FetchMangaDetailsUseCase` (bound earlier in this module); the
second is `IsAdultContentUseCase` (bound earlier in this module,
added by Phase 6.3.4). No DSL acrobatics required because the VM
constructor's positional arguments map 1:1 to the bindings in
declaration order — same shape as `LibraryViewModel`'s wiring
(§40.4).

### 47.8 Build gates

- `:presentation:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green (48s
  combined run for all five targets).

No new warnings in any of the three touched files; all reported
warnings are pre-existing legacy-code deprecations (`TabRow`,
`LocalClipboardManager`, `Preview`, `menuAnchor()`, etc.). iOS
framework link not executed (Windows host) — deferred to macOS
verification.

### 47.9 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 6.3.4.wire

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 6.3.4.wire. All three files clear the
10-point checklist. No `expect/actual` (all `commonMain`). No
`!!` / `Any` / `lateinit` introduced in `:presentation` or
`:composeApp`. The VM gains exactly one new dependency that maps
1:1 to the new use case; the state gains exactly one new field
that maps 1:1 to the VM-managed flag; the Koin module gains
exactly one positional argument to an existing `viewModel`
binding.

### 47.10 What this slice deliberately defers

- **`:ui` surface.** No content-warning chip, no cover blur, no
  chapter-list gate. The flag is observable in state but no
  composable consumes it yet. Lands in a follow-up `:ui` slice
  (likely paired with the Coil cover loading slice, since the
  cover blur effect is most naturally implemented on the
  `AsyncImage` modifier path).
- **Per-user override.** Some users want to see adult content
  even from sources flagged as adult, or hide it from sources
  not flagged. That's a settings + use case sibling, not a
  classifier change — out of scope for the legacy-parity port.
- **Age-verification flow.** No platform native API integration.
  When that lands (likely as a `:platform` facade), the
  `IsAdultContentUseCase` either composes it (`isAdultContent(manga) && !userVerified()`)
  or the gate becomes a separate use case — same DIP posture.

## 48. Phase 7.x.adult — `:ui` adult-content gate

### 48.1 Why this slice exists

Phase 6.3.4 landed the abstraction; Phase 6.3.4.wire fed it into
the VM and surfaced `isAdult` on `DetailsState`. This slice is the
first `:ui` consumer of that flag — a confirmation dialog that
matches the legacy `AdultConfirmationDialog` behaviour shown by
`MangaDetailsScreen` when `isPlus18(genres, api)` returns `true`
on a `State.Success` emission.

Without this slice the flag would be dead state (observable from
inspector tooling but invisible to the user). Landing the
dialog **before** the Coil cover-loading slice means the
adult-gating UX is testable on the existing placeholder cover —
no image pipeline coupling, no load-bearing fixes pulled in by
proxy, no extra build deps.

### 48.2 Files touched

A single `:ui` edit — no new files, no new module boundaries:

- EDIT `ui/src/.../details/DetailsScreen.kt` — add imports
  (`AlertDialog`, `TextButton`, `mutableStateOf`, `setValue`),
  a `remember`-keyed visibility flag, a `LaunchedEffect` that
  raises the flag when `state.isAdult` becomes `true`, the
  dialog rendering inside the existing `Box`, and a `private fun
  AdultConfirmationDialog` composable at the bottom of the file.

The "one screen file, sub-composables inline" convention from
the Library slice (`LibraryScreen.kt`) and the existing
DetailsScreen (`DetailsTopBar`, `DetailsErrorPane`, `DetailsBody`,
`DetailsHeader`, `GenreChipRow`, `ChapterRow` are all `private`
in the same file) is preserved — no `details/components/`
subdirectory introduced.

### 48.3 Visibility-flag design (legacy parity)

```kotlin
var adultDialogVisible by remember(state.manga?.url) { mutableStateOf(false) }
LaunchedEffect(state.isAdult, state.manga?.url) {
    if (state.isAdult) adultDialogVisible = true
}
```

The legacy was:

```kotlin
val dialogState = remember {
    if (isPlus18(state.data.genres, state.data.api)) {
        mutableStateOf(DialogState.AdultWarning)
    } else {
        mutableStateOf(DialogState.None)
    }
}
```

Three deltas, all deliberate:

1. **`remember` keyed on `manga.url`**, not unkeyed. Legacy's
   unkeyed `remember` survived as long as the `MangaDetailsScreen`
   composable did — navigation to a different manga in the same
   screen instance would have kept the dialog dismissed (a
   correctness bug for users who follow links between adult and
   non-adult titles). Keying on `manga.url` resets the dialog
   each time the screen targets a new manga.
2. **Separate `LaunchedEffect` raises the flag**, not the
   `remember` initialiser. Legacy classified inside `remember` at
   first composition only. The rework re-classifies post-fetch
   (§47.3), so the flag can flip `false → true` after the screen
   has already rendered. A `LaunchedEffect` keyed on
   `state.isAdult` + `state.manga?.url` is the canonical Compose
   idiom for "react to state changes" — the dialog appears the
   moment the fetched genres reveal adult content, even if the
   nav-arg genres were empty.
3. **`Boolean` flag, not a `DialogState` enum.** The legacy enum
   carried four cases tied to the monetization MStep flow
   (`AdultWarning`, `MStep1`, `MStep2`, `None`). The rework has
   no MStep flow yet, so the dialog is a one-bit concern —
   represented directly as `Boolean`. When/if the MStep flow
   lands in the rework, this becomes a typed state (likely on
   `DetailsState`, not a local `remember`), but that's a Phase
   X.y problem.

### 48.4 Action semantics

- **Continue** → `adultDialogVisible = false`. Legacy advanced
  to `DialogState.MStep1`; the rework has no MStep flow, so
  Continue is a plain dismiss. Once dismissed, the screen body
  is fully interactive — chapter list rows fire navigation
  intents normally.
- **Go Back** → `adultDialogVisible = false` *and*
  `onIntent(DetailsIntent.OnBackClick)`. Mirrors the legacy
  "cancel" button's user intent ("no, take me back") without
  binding to the legacy MStep machinery. The `OnBackClick`
  intent already exists and is routed through the existing
  `DetailsEffect.NavigateBack` → `onNavigateBack()` path — no
  new effect, no new intent.
- **System dismiss** (back gesture, scrim click) →
  `onDismissRequest = onGoBack`. Treating outside-tap as
  cancel-and-go-back is friendlier than dismiss-but-stay because
  the user explicitly tried to leave the dialog — the implication
  is "I don't want to see this", which on this screen means
  "navigate away".

### 48.5 Why no resource dependency

Strings are hardcoded English literals ("Adult content",
"Continue", "Go back", and the body explanation). Three reasons:

1. **Pattern match.** The rest of `:ui` already hardcodes user
   strings — `DetailsErrorPane` ("Retry"), `DetailsBody`
   ("Chapters ($n)"), `toUserMessage()` ("Network error",
   "Cancelled", etc.), `LibraryScreen` similar. The rework `:ui`
   module hasn't decided its resource story yet; this slice
   doesn't unilaterally introduce one.
2. **No Compose Resources access from `:ui`.** The legacy
   `AdultConfirmationDialog` lives in `:composeApp` and uses
   `composeapp.generated.resources.Res.string.adult_filter_removal_*`.
   That resource bundle is owned by `:composeApp`'s Compose
   Resources plugin configuration; `:ui` doesn't depend on
   `:composeApp` (and the dependency direction would invert the
   clean-arch layering if it did). Wiring a generic
   `stringResource(Res.string.X)` from `:ui` would require either
   moving the resources out of `:composeApp` (separate concern,
   bigger slice) or threading a string-provider abstraction
   through every `:ui` composable (over-abstraction for one site).
3. **No icon dependency.** The legacy dialog displayed
   `Res.drawable.ic_pluss18`. Same `:composeApp` ownership
   problem. A future polish slice can re-introduce the icon once
   the resource story is decided — until then, the dialog leans
   on the red-tinted title and the explanation text for
   adult-content visual signalling.

A future i18n slice can lift these strings into the rework's
chosen resource story without changing the dialog's API.

### 48.6 No new `DetailsIntent` / `DetailsEffect`

Compose-local UI state (dialog visibility) lives in `remember`,
not in MVI state. Two reasons:

- **It's render-only concern.** The visibility doesn't survive
  process death and doesn't need to — re-showing the dialog
  after a process restart is arguably correct (treat each fresh
  process as a fresh visit). Hoisting it into `DetailsState`
  would couple the VM to a UI rendering detail that has no
  back-end effect.
- **No cross-screen effect.** The dialog's actions are scoped
  to the current screen instance (dismiss or go back). The
  back-navigation route through `DetailsIntent.OnBackClick` →
  `DetailsEffect.NavigateBack` → `onNavigateBack()` already
  exists; no new effect needed.

This matches strict MVI's "state for what survives, remember for
what doesn't" guidance.

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green (41s
  combined run for all five targets).

No new warnings in the touched file; all reported warnings are
