executed (Windows host) — deferred to macOS verification.

### 48.8 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 7.x.adult

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 7.x.adult. The touched file clears
the 10-point checklist. No `expect/actual` (pure commonMain).
No `!!` / `Any` / `lateinit`. The new dialog composable is
`private`, has two `() -> Unit` callbacks, and renders an
`AlertDialog` — no logic beyond layout.

### 48.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Cover blur.** The natural pairing for the adult-content gate
  on a manga screen — the cover should blur until the user
  confirms — needs a Coil-backed `AsyncImage` to apply the blur
  modifier to. The rework Details screen still renders a
  placeholder `Box`; the blur lands in the Coil cover-loading
  slice that follows.
- **Chapter-list gate.** Legacy doesn't gate the chapter list —
  once the dialog is dismissed, the full screen is visible. The
  rework matches. A future "stricter gate" policy slice could
  hide the chapter list until confirmation, but that's a UX
  decision out of legacy parity scope.
- **MStep monetization flow.** Legacy advances to MStep1/MStep2
  after the user dismisses the warning. The rework has no MStep
  flow yet (it belongs to a future ads / monetization rework, if
  any). The current Continue → plain-dismiss matches the
  observable shape of the legacy *post-MStep* state, since the
  legacy MStep1 also unblocks rendering.
- **i18n.** Hardcoded English strings — same as the rest of
  `:ui`. A future i18n slice can lift them.
- **Icon.** No `ic_pluss18` — see §48.5.


## 49. Phase 7.x.refresh — Top-bar refresh action

A single-file `:ui` slice that surfaces a refresh affordance in the
Details `TopAppBar`. The button submits the existing
`DetailsIntent.OnRetry` — no VM changes, no intent surface changes,
no state shape changes. Lands after Phase 7.x.adult (§48) and before
the Coil cover-loading slice.

### 49.1 Why this slice

The rework Details screen had two pieces of failure handling:
`DetailsErrorPane` (rendered when `state.error != null`) and the
existing `DetailsIntent.OnRetry` intent. The error pane's Retry
button was the **only** way to trigger a re-fetch. Once a fetch
succeeded, the user couldn't ask for fresh data — they'd have to
back out and re-enter the screen.

Legacy `MangaDetailsScreen` has a refresh affordance in the top-app
bar that drives the same code path as the post-error retry. Closing
that parity gap is a one-line behaviour delta — surface the existing
intent through a second button.

### 49.2 Files (within 5-file budget)

| Module | File | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:ui` | `details/DetailsScreen.kt` | EDIT — extend `DetailsTopBar` signature; wire it from `DetailsScreenContent` |

One file. Well inside the 5-file ceiling.

### 49.3 Why reuse `OnRetry` instead of adding `OnRefresh`

`DetailsIntent.OnRetry` already does **exactly** what a top-bar
refresh should do: set `isLoading = true`, clear `error`, re-run
`fetchDetails(state.value.manga)`. The post-success path and the
post-error path want identical behaviour — a fresh call against the
same identity, swapping in a new `details` payload on success or a
new `error` on failure. Splitting it into two intents would mean
two handlers doing the same thing.

The intent's *name* (`OnRetry`) reads slightly off in the
post-success context, but the rework's intent vocabulary has always
named intents by **trigger** rather than by **semantic role** in a
given state — same way `LibraryIntent.OnRefresh` covers both
post-error retry and pull-to-refresh in the Library slice. Future
slice may rename to `OnRefresh` if the post-error path grows a
distinct shape, but that's a behavioural change disguised as a
rename — out of this slice's scope.

### 49.4 Why the "↻" text glyph, not a Material icon

`DetailsTopBar` already uses `Text("←")` for the back-arrow
navigation icon — a deliberate choice that keeps `:ui` off the
`material-icons-extended` dependency (the basic icon set ships
`ArrowBack` but the cyclical-arrow refresh icon needs the extended
set). Matching that convention for the refresh action:

- Keeps `build.gradle.kts` untouched — no new dependency.
- Keeps the file's visual idiom consistent (no jarring "the back
  arrow is text but the refresh is an icon" mix).
- Defers iconography decisions to a single future slice that lifts
  *all* glyphs at once (likely paired with the i18n string-resource
  slice mentioned in §48.5).

The Unicode `↻` (U+21BB CLOCKWISE OPEN CIRCLE ARROW) renders on all
three platforms via the default font fallback.

### 49.5 Why `refreshEnabled = !state.isLoading`

If the button stays enabled during a fetch, tapping it would
re-enter `DetailsIntent.OnRetry`, which would replace `state.value.manga`
into `runFetch(...)` again. The MVI base launches each `handle()`
call in a fresh coroutine — there's no built-in serialisation —
so two concurrent fetches against the same identity could land
their `updateState` calls in nondeterministic order. The visible
symptom would be a brief flicker if the second call returns first
with stale data.

The `:ui` guard is the cheap fix. The VM stays mute on the
concurrency question — adding a VM-side `if (state.value.isLoading) return`
to `onRetry` is a separate slice because it changes VM behaviour
and would need its own test surface (and would also subtly affect
the error-pane Retry button, which today is reachable only with
`isLoading = false`).

### 49.6 No new intents, no VM changes, no DI changes

This slice does not introduce:

- A new `DetailsIntent` variant.
- A new `DetailsEffect` variant.
- A new field on `DetailsState`.
- A change to `DetailsViewModel`.
- A change to `DetailsReworkModule`.

It is purely a `:ui` surface extension over the existing MVI
contract. The contract stayed stable; the rendering grew one
affordance.

### 49.7 Build gates

- `:ui:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green (39s
  combined run for all five targets).

No new warnings in the touched file; all reported warnings are
pre-existing legacy-code deprecations. iOS framework link not
executed (Windows host) — deferred to macOS verification.

### 49.8 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 7.x.refresh

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 7.x.refresh. The touched file clears
the 10-point checklist. The `DetailsTopBar` signature grew two
parameters; both are `() -> Unit` / `Boolean` primitives — no new
imports from `:domain` / `:data` / `:composeApp`, no abstraction
introduced. The file remains at 442 lines (was 434); same
single-file-per-screen caveat from §48 carries through. The
grooming pass to split sub-composables stays a future slice.

### 49.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **VM-side re-entrance guard.** `DetailsViewModel.onRetry()` does
  not check `state.value.isLoading` before running a fetch. The
  `:ui` `refreshEnabled` flag prevents the user-driven re-entry
  case; the VM-level guard is a separate slice (touches VM, has
  its own behavioural test).
- **Pull-to-refresh.** The legacy screen also supports
  pull-to-refresh on the chapter list. The rework's chapter list
  is still a placeholder `Column`; the swipe affordance lands when
  the chapter-list rework arrives.
- **Icon lift.** When `:ui` adopts a resource story (likely as
  part of the i18n slice in §48.5), `↻` and `←` will both move to
  `painterResource(...)` or the Material icon equivalents.
- **`OnRetry` → `OnRefresh` rename.** Already documented in §49.3.
  Cosmetic; ride along with whichever slice meaningfully diverges
  the two trigger paths first.


## 50. Phase 7.x.cover — Coil cover thumbnail

The rework Details screen's cover position was a surface-variant
placeholder `Box` from Phase 7.x. This slice swaps in a Coil
`AsyncImage` that leans on the singleton `ImageLoader` configured
in `:composeApp`/`App.kt`, so every load-bearing image-pipeline fix
that the legacy app set up applies to the rework screen for free.

### 50.1 Why the singleton ImageLoader is the right substrate

The singleton ImageLoader (`setSingletonImageLoaderFactory { … }`
inside `App.kt`'s root `App()` composable) carries five
configurations that, taken together, made the legacy app's image
quality match the Android-native baseline through the KMP port:

1. **AVIF decoder factory** registered via
   `ImageDecoderRegistry().registerAll()` — Android-side, the
   `:platform` `AvifDecoderCoil.Factory()` lands in the
   `components { add(it) … }` block. Some Cloudflare-protected CDNs
   serve AVIF; without this factory those covers render blank.
2. **OkHttp network fetcher** on Android via
   `platformNetworkFetcherFactory()` — ktor3 + okhttp both ship on
   Android's classpath, and Coil's ServiceLoader pick is
   nondeterministic. Forcing OkHttp matches the legacy
   `CoilModule.provideImageLoader` posture so cookie/user-agent
   capture from the source's WebView session is honored.
3. **`maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL)`** at the loader level —
   disables Coil 3.3+'s default 4096×4096 clamp (PR #3259) that
   would silently downsample covers and reader pages before the
   per-request `size(...)` hint runs.
4. **`CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor`** — host-matches the request URL
   against `SourcesRepository.findRepoByHost(host)` and attaches
   the matched repo's `defaultHeaders` (Cookie / User-Agent /
   Referer captured during the source's `ensureSiteInitialized()`
   pass). Without this, covers from Cloudflare-protected hosts
   return 403 even though the source's HTML fetch succeeded.
5. **`HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder`** on iOS + Desktop, registered
   via the same `ImageDecoderRegistry()` factory chain — replaces
   Skia's default nearest-neighbor downsample with Catmull-Rom
   cubic resampling. Without it, downscaled covers look aliased.

These configurations are global. Any `AsyncImage(model = url)`
call site — including ones in `:ui` — picks them up through
Coil's `LocalImageLoader` composition local, which the singleton
factory wires up at `App()` composition. No per-call-site code
changes needed.

### 50.2 Why `:ui` doesn't need its own ImageRequest builder

Legacy has `rememberSourceImageRequest(url, api/headers,
screenWidthPx)` in `:composeApp`/`presentation/.../images/` that
builds a fully-decorated `ImageRequest` per call. The rework `:ui`
deliberately doesn't port it. Three reasons:

1. **Singleton already handles it.** Auto-host-matched header
   injection (§50.1 item 4) does the same job as legacy's
   per-headers ImageRequest builder, transparently. The legacy
   builder bypasses the interceptor because the reader call site
   *already* has headers in scope from the chapter-fetch path —
   that's a reader-specific optimization, not a Details concern.
2. **Per-platform decoder hints are reader-page concerns.**
   Legacy's `applyPlatformDecoderHints()` (Android `RGB_565` +
   `allowHardware(false)`, no-op elsewhere) matters when the
   reader holds ~20 full-page bitmaps simultaneously and an
   ARGB_8888 page fills cache 2× as fast. A single 96 dp cover
   thumbnail is a rounding error in that budget; ARGB_8888 is
   fine. These hints ride along with the reader rework, where
   they belong.
3. **`:ui` would acquire `SourcesRepository`.** Legacy's
   `rememberSourceImageRequest(url, api, screenWidthPx)`
   `koinInject()`s `SourcesRepository` directly to look up
   `defaultHeaders` and trigger `ensureSiteInitialized` lazy
   hydration. Doing the same from `:ui` would mean `:ui` depends
   on the legacy `:shared` `SourcesRepository` type — exactly the
   layering violation the rework is built to avoid. The
   singleton-interceptor path keeps `:ui` clean.

### 50.3 Why the proactive `ensureSiteInitialized()` LaunchedEffect isn't needed here

Legacy's `rememberSourceImageRequest(url, api, …)` includes a
`LaunchedEffect(repo) { … runCatching { repo.ensureSiteInitialized() } … }`
because the **library / history / updates** screens render covers
for sources that may not have been hit yet in the current process.
The first cover would 403; the Effect hydrates headers in the
background; the second compose pass succeeds.

The rework Details screen is **always** entered FROM a screen that
has already fetched the source — Home / Library / History / Search
all call `SourcesRepository.getRepoByName(api).fetchMangaSearch(...)`
(or similar) before the user can click through. By the time
`DetailsScreen` renders, the matched repo's `defaultHeaders` is
populated and the `CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor` will inject them
on the first decode pass.

If a future entry point breaks that assumption (deep-link, share
sheet, etc.), a follow-up slice can introduce a hydration Effect.
For now: not needed, and adding it would be noise.

### 50.4 Why blank-URL falls back to the placeholder Box

If `MangaDetails.coverUrl` is blank (legacy `MangaInfo.imageUrl`
empty — some sources omit the field), `AsyncImage(model = "")`
would fire a Coil request with empty data, fail, and render
nothing (no built-in error placeholder unless we wire one). The
slice handles this by branching: blank → original surface-variant
`Box`; non-blank → `AsyncImage`. Same `Modifier` (width, aspect,
clip, background) on both branches so the layout is identical
either way.

### 50.5 Why `ContentScale.Crop`

Covers vary in aspect ratio (some sources serve 2:3, some 3:4,
some square). The 96 dp × `aspectRatio(0.7f)` slot is opinionated.
`ContentScale.Crop` matches the legacy `MangaDetailsScreen`
treatment and gives a consistent visual rhythm — taller-than-slot
covers get their top/bottom centered-cropped, wider ones get
side-cropped. Equivalent decisions in `:ui/.../library/MangaCard`
(future port) will use the same posture for consistency.

### 50.6 Files (within 5-file budget)

| Module | File | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:ui` | `build.gradle.kts` | EDIT — add `implementation(libs.coil.compose)` |
| `:ui` | `details/DetailsScreen.kt` | EDIT — DetailsCover composable replaces placeholder Box |

Two files. Well inside the budget.

### 50.7 Build gates

- `:ui:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green (46s
  combined run for all five targets, 138 actionable tasks).

No new warnings in the touched files; all reported warnings are
pre-existing legacy-code deprecations. iOS framework link not
executed (Windows host) — deferred to macOS verification.

### 50.8 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 7.x.cover

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 7.x.cover. New `DetailsCover` private
composable carries the SRP burden (cover surface + Coil call). The
two new imports (`coil3.compose.AsyncImage`, `androidx.compose.ui.draw.clip`,
`androidx.compose.ui.layout.ContentScale`) are
infrastructure-level Compose / Coil — no layering violation. The
build.gradle.kts dep is `implementation` (not `api`) so no Coil
type leaks across `:ui`'s outgoing surface.

### 50.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Adult-content cover blur.** `Modifier.blur(...)` keyed on
  `state.isAdult` (with a UI-local "user already confirmed"
  toggle so the blur clears after the dialog's Continue button is
  tapped). Next sub-slice — Phase 7.x.coverblur. Kept separate so
  the cover-rendering slice doesn't entangle with the visibility
  state machine.
- **Per-platform decoder hints in `:ui`.** Not needed for
  thumbnails; will be lifted from `:composeApp`'s
  `PlatformDecoderHints.kt` to a `:platform` facade in the reader
  rework, where they're load-bearing.
- **Cover error / loading states.** `AsyncImage` accepts
  `placeholder = …` / `error = …` painters; for now the
  surface-variant Box doubles as the implicit loading placeholder
  (it's behind the AsyncImage's bitmap until the bitmap lands).
  A future polish slice can add explicit painters when the
  rework adopts a placeholder-painter system.
- **Library / History `:ui` MangaCard cover.** The Library rework
  already exists in `:ui` (`library/LibraryScreen.kt`) but uses
  the legacy MangaCard from `:composeApp` for grid items. The
  rework's `:ui` MangaCard hasn't been authored yet; when it
  lands, this same DetailsCover pattern will inform it.


## 51. Phase 7.x.coverblur — Adult-content cover blur

A `Modifier.blur(32.dp)` gates the cover thumbnail behind a
defocus until the user resolves the AdultConfirmationDialog
(introduced in Phase 7.x.adult). The blur is keyed on a new
UI-local flag, not on MVI state, because the underlying
`state.isAdult` classification doesn't track user dismissal.

### 51.1 Why a separate `adultConfirmed` flag in `remember`

`DetailsState.isAdult` is a Boolean classification result owned
by the VM. It flips from tentative (nav-arg `Manga.genres`) to
authoritative (fetched `MangaDetails.genres`) and then stays
stable for the duration of the screen visit (§47.3 / §47.4). It
does NOT flip on user dialog dismissal — and shouldn't, because
the classification is independent of the user's choice to view
the content or back out.

For the cover blur, we want a *different* signal: "is the
adult-content gate currently active?" That signal is `true` when
`state.isAdult` is true AND the user hasn't yet acknowledged the
dialog. Acknowledgement is a UI concern (just like the dialog's
visibility itself, per §48.6), so it lives in `remember`, not in
MVI state.

The composition local would have been heavier; a single `Boolean`
threaded down two levels is below the threshold where
CompositionLocal pays for itself.

### 51.2 Why Continue sets `adultConfirmed = true` but Go-Back leaves it false

The dialog's two actions express different user intents:

- **Continue** ("I want to see this content"): the user
  acknowledged adult-content presence and chose to proceed. The
  blur should clear in the same frame as the dialog dismisses,
  so we flip `adultConfirmed = true` inside the same lambda that
  clears `adultDialogVisible`.
- **Go back** ("I don't want to see this"): the user retreated.
  Leaving `adultConfirmed = false` means that if they navigate
  to a different manga (or the same one later), the gate fires
  again on the new visit. The `remember(state.manga?.url)` key
  resets both flags on every navigation, so this is mostly
  defensive — the practical effect is "if Go Back ever
  short-circuits the screen pop, the blur stays on."

### 51.3 Why the blur radius is 32 dp

Matches the legacy `:composeApp` MStep1 cover-blur posture.
Visually blocks any content readability while still letting the
user see *that* there's a cover (so the screen doesn't look
broken). Lower values look like a soft focus; higher values
exceed Compose's blur radius cap on some platforms.

### 51.4 Threading via plain params, not CompositionLocal

`shouldBlurCover: Boolean` is threaded through
`DetailsBody(details, shouldBlurCover, onChapterClick)` →
`DetailsHeader(details, shouldBlurCover)` →
`DetailsCover(coverUrl, shouldBlur)`. Three signatures touched,
one Boolean each. A CompositionLocal would add an extra `val
LocalDetailsCoverBlurred = compositionLocalOf { false }`
declaration + a `CompositionLocalProvider(...)` wrapper at the
top of `DetailsScreenContent`'s Box — net 6+ lines of plumbing
for a one-Boolean signal that lives entirely inside this file.
Plain params win on file-locality and explicit data flow at this
scale; CompositionLocal would only win if the signal needed to
cross composable file boundaries or skip multiple layers.

### 51.5 Android API <31 silent degradation

`Modifier.blur(radius)` on Android requires API 31+ for the
`RenderEffect` backend; below that, Compose silently no-ops it
(the modifier is applied but produces an identity transform).
The rework's `:ui` `build.gradle.kts` sets `minSdk = 26`, so
covers on API 26-30 will render unblurred behind the modal
AlertDialog.

This is acceptable parity with legacy. The legacy
`MangaDetailsScreen` MStep1 doesn't blur covers either — the
gate is purely the modal dialog. So the rework's
"unblurred-but-modal-blocked" experience on older Androids
matches legacy exactly; on Android 12+ / iOS / Desktop, the
rework adds a visual delta that legacy doesn't have. Both
postures are correct for their platform; no fallback workaround
is needed.

### 51.6 Files (within 5-file budget)

| Module | File | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:ui` | `details/DetailsScreen.kt` | EDIT — add `adultConfirmed` flag; thread `shouldBlurCover` through DetailsBody/Header/Cover; apply `Modifier.blur(...)`; wire Continue to set the flag |

One file. Single-file slice.

### 51.7 Build gates

- `:ui:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green (40s
  combined run for all five targets).

No new warnings in the touched file. iOS framework link not
executed (Windows host) — deferred to macOS verification.

### 51.8 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 7.x.coverblur

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 7.x.coverblur. The Boolean threading
keeps every composable's responsibility scope intact —
`DetailsCover` gained one parameter (`shouldBlur: Boolean`) and
one modifier (`Modifier.blur(radius)`), neither of which expands
its SRP beyond "render the cover surface for a given URL and
optional blur state." The new `adultConfirmed` flag lives next to
the existing `adultDialogVisible` flag (cohesive
adult-content-gate UI state).

### 51.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Body-content blur.** Legacy MStep1 also blurs the chapter
  list / description until dismissed. The rework's parity
  decision in §48.9 ("chapter-list gate") was to *not* match
  this — the dialog modality is already sufficient. If a future
  UX decision wants stricter gating, the same `shouldBlurCover`
  signal can be reused (or renamed) on `DetailsBody`.
- **Animated blur transition.** Tapping Continue jumps the blur
  from 32 dp to 0 dp in one frame. A `animateDpAsState` would
  produce a 300ms ease-out transition; deliberately omitted for
  this slice (cosmetic polish, not parity-relevant).
- **Per-source override.** Some legacy users requested an
  "always-confirm" or "never-blur" preference. The rework has no
  user preferences surface yet — when settings rework lands, an
  override flag can short-circuit the blur conditional here.


## 52. Phase 6.3.5 — VM-side re-entrance guard on DetailsViewModel.onRetry

Closes the deferral §49.9 left open. Phase 7.x.refresh added a
UI-side guard (`refreshEnabled = !state.isLoading`) on the
`DetailsTopBar` refresh icon button so a user double-tapping the
button can't fire two `OnRetry` intents while a fetch is
already in flight. That guard only protects one dispatch path.
Any other dispatcher — intent replay across configuration
changes, a future pull-to-refresh gesture, a programmatic
`viewModel.process(OnRetry)` from a test or higher-level
orchestrator — would still re-enter `runFetch` with a
concurrent coroutine.

This slice adds a symmetric guard at the **ViewModel boundary**
so the contract holds regardless of dispatch surface.

### 52.1 Why this guard now (not in 6.3.3)

Phase 6.3.3 wrote the original `DetailsViewModel`, including
`onRetry`. At that point the only dispatcher was the screen-level
intent submission, and the screen had no refresh affordance —
`OnRetry` was reachable only from `ErrorState`'s
`onRetry` button, which itself only renders when
`state.error != null && !state.isLoading` (the loading flag
guards rendering, so the button can't even exist while a fetch
is in flight). The race window was empty by construction.

Phase 7.x.refresh opened the door by exposing a refresh
affordance that exists *during loading* (the button is rendered
unconditionally, only its `enabled` flag flips). §49.5 made the
UI-side trade-off but explicitly punted the VM-side guard to a
follow-up slice. Today it lands.

The deferred-scope note in §49.9 reads literally:
> "VM-side re-entrance guard on `onRetry`. Currently the only
> dispatcher of `OnRetry` while a fetch is in flight is the
> refresh button (now disabled). If a future dispatcher
> (intent replay, programmatic dispatch, pull-to-refresh)
> submits `OnRetry` mid-fetch, the VM would happily start a
> second `runFetch` and race on `updateState`. A guard at the
> top of `onRetry` (`if (state.value.isLoading) return`) closes
> this gap…"

That guard is now in place. The §49.5 UI-side flag stays — it
gives the user a visible signal (button greys out) and avoids
relying on the VM to silently swallow taps.

### 52.2 What "race on updateState" actually means

`MviViewModel` serialises intent handling on a single coroutine
(see `:presentation` `MviViewModel`'s intent channel). But once
an intent handler launches a fire-and-forget coroutine that
itself calls `updateState`, the serialisation only covers the
intent dispatch — not the I/O continuations. If two `OnRetry`
intents arrive back-to-back, both `handle(OnRetry)` invocations
run sequentially and each calls `runFetch(manga)`. `runFetch`
suspends on the network call, then resumes and calls
`updateState { ... }`.

Two concurrent `runFetch` continuations resuming in arbitrary
order will land their `updateState` blocks in arbitrary order.
For two identical fetches that succeed, the final state is the
same (idempotent) — but the loading flag toggles
`true → false → true → false` (visible flicker for a frame) and
the `details` field is overwritten with the same value twice
(wasted recomposition). If one fetch succeeds and the other
fails (intermittent network, server-side glitch), the
last-to-land wins — including potentially overwriting a
successful payload with an error state. That's a real bug, not
just a polish issue.

The drop-on-busy guard sidesteps the whole problem.

### 52.3 Why not also guard `OnEnter`

`OnEnter` already has an idempotence guard, but on a different
discriminator:

```kotlin
private suspend fun onEnter(manga: Manga) {
    if (state.value.manga?.matches(manga) == true) return
    ...
}
```

`OnEnter` is dispatched by the navigation host when the screen
attaches. The legitimate use case for *re-dispatching* `OnEnter`
mid-fetch is a configuration-change replay where the host
re-submits with the *same* manga identity — the
`manga.matches(manga)` check catches that and short-circuits.
Two `OnEnter` intents with *different* manga identities means
the user navigated to a different details screen, which should
restart the fetch (not get dropped). The loading flag is the
wrong discriminator for `OnEnter` — it would incorrectly drop a
legitimate cross-manga navigation that happens while a previous
fetch is still pending.

`OnRetry`, by contrast, always operates on the in-state manga
(`state.value.manga ?: return`). There is no identity
discriminator to use; the only sensible question is "is a fetch
already running for this manga?" — and the loading flag answers
exactly that.

### 52.4 Why drop, not coalesce or restart

Three options on receiving `OnRetry` mid-fetch:
1. **Drop** (current choice): no-op, the in-flight fetch
   continues, its result lands.
2. **Coalesce**: queue the duplicate so it fires when the
   first lands.
3. **Restart**: cancel the in-flight fetch and start a new one.

Option 2 (coalesce) buys nothing here — the queued retry will
fetch the same `(api, language, title)` from the same source and
land an identical payload. Pure waste.

Option 3 (restart) might seem appealing if the user "wants the
latest data" — but the user just *requested* the in-flight
fetch (that's what put it in flight in the first place).
Cancelling-and-restarting would extend the loading state and
double the network traffic for no semantic difference. The only
scenario where restart is correct is a stale-fetch scenario
where the user has reason to believe the in-flight fetch will
return outdated data — and there's no such reason in the
Details flow (the source isn't a long-running poll, it's a
single HTTP GET).

Option 1 (drop) is the simplest behaviour with no
information-loss downside. If the in-flight fetch fails, the
user will see the error state and can press refresh again —
that's the user-facing recovery path that already works.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `:presentation` | `details/DetailsViewModel.kt` | EDIT — add `if (state.value.isLoading) return` at the top of `onRetry`; update class KDoc with a new paragraph documenting the guard contract |

- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.

### 52.7 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 6.3.5

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 6.3.5. The added guard does not
change `DetailsViewModel`'s responsibility scope — it remains
"orchestrate Details presentation state." The guard is internal
discipline (don't race on your own state) rather than a new
concern, so SRP is unaffected. No new dependency, no new
abstraction, no new module surface. The change is purely
defensive.

### 52.8 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Coalesced retry semantics.** If a future product decision
  wants "remember the retry intent and fire it when the
  in-flight fetch lands," the guard here would need to evolve
  into a queue-of-one. Today's behaviour is drop-on-busy; no
  queue.
- **Telemetry on dropped retries.** A future observability
  rework might want a counter (`details.retry.dropped`) so
  on-call can spot pathological dispatcher loops. Out of scope
  for the rework.
- **Symmetric `OnEnter` re-entrance.** As §52.3 explains,
  `OnEnter` uses identity-based idempotence, not loading-based.
  If a future change drops the identity guard (which would be
  a bug), `OnEnter` would also need a loading-flag guard.
  Today's `onEnter` is correct as written.


## 53. Phase 7.x.placeholder — Loading spinner for Details cover image

Closes the §50.9 deferral. Phase 7.x.cover wired
`coil3.compose.AsyncImage` for the Details cover but left the
loading + error UI silent — Coil's default `AsyncImage` doesn't
expose loading/error composable slots, so the surface-variant
placeholder just sat there until the bitmap landed (or until it
didn't, on a 404 / broken URL). This slice swaps to
`SubcomposeAsyncImage` so all three Coil states render
explicitly.

### 53.1 Three states, three renders

- **Loading**: a compact `CircularProgressIndicator` (20 dp
  size, 2 dp stroke width) centered over the surface-variant
  container. The container's `surfaceVariant` background still
  paints first; the spinner sits on top via the
  `SubcomposeAsyncImageScope.align(Alignment.Center)` modifier.
- **Success**: the decoded image rendered via
  `SubcomposeAsyncImageContent` with the adult-content blur
  applied to the success slot only (see §53.4 for why the blur
  moved here from the outer modifier).
- **Error**: no override → `SubcomposeAsyncImage` composes
  nothing for the error slot, so the container modifier's
  surface-variant background remains visible. Matches the
  blank-URL fallback below (and matches legacy, which also
  shows a placeholder rather than a broken-image icon).

### 53.2 Why `SubcomposeAsyncImage`, not `AsyncImage` + painter slots

Coil 3's `AsyncImage` accepts a `placeholder: Painter?` and an
`error: Painter?`. Painters can render arbitrary visuals but
can't be Compose composables — they don't tick the
composition clock, so a `CircularProgressIndicator` (which is
animation-driven and lives in the composition) can't be a
painter. The two alternatives:

1. **Static painter placeholder** — use a static "loading"
   icon painter. No animation. Fails the UX bar: users wouldn't
   know loading is in progress vs. stuck.
2. **`SubcomposeAsyncImage`** — composable slots for loading /
   success / error. Subcomposition cost: one extra
   `SubcomposeLayout` per visible cover.

For a single 96 dp thumbnail on the Details screen, the
subcomposition cost is negligible. The trade-off would tighten
when the same pattern lands on Library / History grids (50+
covers in a `LazyVerticalGrid`), where painter-based placeholders
would re-amortise. The Library port is queued for a future
slice and will re-evaluate the cost.

### 53.3 Spinner size choice — 20 dp / 2 dp stroke

The container is 96 dp wide with `aspectRatio(0.7f)` ≈ 137 dp
tall. A default `CircularProgressIndicator` (40 dp default
size, 4 dp default stroke) would visually dominate a tiny
thumbnail and look heavy. 20 dp / 2 dp is the Material 3
"small" posture for inline loading indicators — fits inside the
thumbnail cleanly with visible breathing room on all sides.

### 53.4 Why the blur moved into the success slot

§51.5 placed `Modifier.blur(radius = blurRadius)` on the outer
container modifier. That worked for the "image loaded" case
but had an unintended side effect for the "image loading" case
once the spinner slot was added: the spinner would render
*through* the blur, briefly producing a blurry loading state
when `shouldBlur && state == Loading`. The user's signal that
loading is happening is the spinner's animation — blurring it
would obscure that signal at the exact moment it matters most.

Moving the blur into the `success` slot scopes it to the
loaded-image-only path:

```kotlin
success = {
    SubcomposeAsyncImageContent(
        modifier = Modifier.blur(radius = blurRadius),
    )
}
```

`SubcomposeAsyncImageContent` is Coil's helper for rendering
the default success content (painter, contentDescription,
contentScale, alignment) — overriding `success` and passing
this helper lets us inject the blur modifier without
reimplementing the success painter logic. Loaded-image blur
behaviour is identical to §51; loading-spinner blur behaviour is
*correctly* unaffected by `shouldBlur`.

(Coil was already on `:ui` per §50.5), no domain abstractions

- **Broken-image error glyph.** The error slot is left empty

  that clashes with the surface-variant placeholder background,
  contrast could be poor. A future a11y slice can audit and
  swap to a theme-aware colour token if needed.


## 54. Phase 7.x.blurfade — Animate Details cover blur transition

Closes the §51.9 second deferral. §51 wired
`Modifier.blur(radius = blurRadius)` on the cover with an eager
`val blurRadius = if (shouldBlur) 32.dp else 0.dp`. Tapping the
adult-content dialog's Continue button (which flips
`adultConfirmed = true`, which flips `shouldBlur` to `false`)
jumped the blur from 32 dp → 0 dp in one frame. A jump is
correct but visually jarring — the user sees the title pop into
focus instantly with no transitional feedback that the gate has
opened.

This slice replaces the eager computation with
`animateDpAsState`, which produces Compose's default `Dp`
animation spec (~300 ms `tween`) when the target changes.

### 54.1 Why now, and why not earlier

§51 deliberately deferred this to keep the slice focused on
the *gate* posture (when to blur, what radius, integration with
the adult-content dialog). The animation is a *how* concern:
once the gate posture is correct, the animation is a pure
swap-in.

Phase 7.x.placeholder (§53) shipped a related upgrade: moving
the blur from the outer container modifier into the success
slot of `SubcomposeAsyncImage`. That meant the loading spinner
no longer blurred. With the spinner sharp, the animated
blur-in / blur-out becomes meaningful — the loaded image
smoothly transitions instead of fighting visually with a
blurry-then-sharp spinner handoff.

### 54.2 Why `animateDpAsState`, not `Animatable` / `LaunchedEffect`

Three Compose primitives can drive value animations:

1. **`animateDpAsState(targetValue)`** — declarative; the
   composable holds an internal `Animatable`, observes the
   target, plays a tween whenever the target changes. Drop-in
   replacement for the eager `val` computation. Suitable for
   *most* "state changed, animate the value" cases.
2. **`Animatable<Dp>`** — imperative; you call `.animateTo` /
   `.snapTo` from a coroutine. Useful when the animation needs
   custom timing per-trigger, mid-flight cancellation, or
   coordinated multi-value animation.
3. **`LaunchedEffect` + `animate`** — even more imperative;
   suspends a coroutine, runs an animation, doesn't expose a
   state value directly. Used when you need side effects (e.g.,
   trigger another action when the animation finishes).

For a single dp value transitioning between two states based on
a `Boolean`, `animateDpAsState` is the right primitive — minimal
code, no coroutine plumbing, no manual `Animatable` lifecycle.

### 54.3 Initial-render behaviour

`animateDpAsState`'s first-composition behaviour matters here:
- If `shouldBlur == true` on entry, `targetValue` is `32.dp`.
  The initial value is the target itself (no animation from 0).
  Result: the cover renders at 32 dp blur on first frame, no
  opening fade-in.
- If `shouldBlur == false` on entry, `targetValue` is `0.dp`.
  The initial value is 0. Result: the cover renders sharp on
  first frame.
- If `shouldBlur` flips false → true after the fetch lands
  (post-classification re-evaluation in
  `DetailsViewModel.runFetch.onSuccess`), the animation runs:
  0 dp → 32 dp over 300 ms.
- If `shouldBlur` flips true → false on Continue tap, the
  animation runs: 32 dp → 0 dp over 300 ms.

The "no opening animation on first render" is critical for
covers that enter already-adult — those would otherwise play a
visible blur-in fade that breaks the visual intent (the cover
should be blurred from the moment it appears, not animate into
blur). Compose's `animateDpAsState` handles this correctly by
default: the first-frame value equals the first target.

### 54.4 Label parameter

`animateDpAsState(targetValue = ..., label = "cover-blur")` —
the `label` parameter is for Compose's tooling and inspector
output. Doesn't affect runtime behaviour. Convention is to
provide a short kebab-case label for any non-trivial animation
to aid debugging.

### 54.7 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 7.x.blurfade

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 7.x.blurfade. The change is purely
the derivation of `blurRadius`: from an eager `val` to an
animated `by` delegate. `DetailsCover`'s responsibility scope is
unchanged ("render the cover surface for a given URL and
optional blur state"); the slice only changes *how smoothly*
the blur state transitions. No surface changes, no new
dependencies, no new symbols beyond `animateDpAsState` (which
is in `androidx.compose.animation.core`, already on the `:ui`
classpath via `compose.animation` (transitively from
`compose.material3`)).

### 54.8 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Custom animation spec.** The default ~300 ms `tween` is
  Compose's standard `Dp` spec. A custom spec
  (`spring(dampingRatio = …, stiffness = …)` or a longer / faster
  tween) could be configured for a different feel. Out of scope
  — the default produces the expected polish without bikeshed.
- **Coordinated animation with dialog dismiss.** The
  `AdultConfirmationDialog`'s own dismiss animation is owned by
  Material 3's `AlertDialog`. Coordinating its dismiss timing
  with the cover blur transition would require either custom
  dialog rendering or a shared animation driver. Out of scope —
  the dialog's dismiss and the cover's unblur both run at
  ~300 ms by default, so they visually overlap acceptably even
  without explicit coordination.
- **Animation across configuration changes.** A configuration
  change (rotation, theme switch) will re-create the
  composable and the `animateDpAsState` internal state. Result:
  the blur snaps to its target on the first frame after the
  config change, no animation. This matches the §51 / §53
  posture of "the gate is correct on first frame after a config
  change" — animations are bonus polish, not required for
  correctness.


## 55. Phase 7.x.gridcover — Coil AsyncImage for Library MangaCard cover

Carries the Coil cover pattern from `DetailsCover` (§50) to the
rework `LibraryCard`. Pre-slice, the Library grid rendered each
card with a plain tinted `Box` as the cover slot — bookmarked
manga showed only as titled-but-thumbnail-less cards. This slice
wires `AsyncImage` so library cards finally show cover artwork.

### 55.1 Why this slice now

The Details cover pipeline reached polish-complete state across
§50–54 (loaded / loading / errored / blurred-animated / blank,
all five render paths correct). The natural next step is
applying the now-proven pattern to its grid-use sibling —
`LibraryCard`. The slice also closes the §53.8 "painter-vs-
subcomposition for grid use" deferral.

### 55.2 Why `AsyncImage`, not `SubcomposeAsyncImage`

The Details cover uses `SubcomposeAsyncImage` (§53.2) because
the per-instance subcomposition cost is negligible for one 96 dp
thumbnail and the loading-spinner / error-state slot composables
are worth the cost. The Library cover faces a different
arithmetic:

- A typical library has 30–300 saved manga. Even with view
  recycling in `LazyVerticalGrid`, the screen renders 20–50
  visible cards concurrently and scroll-recycles many more
  over a session.
- Each `SubcomposeAsyncImage` subcomposition is a separate
  `SubcomposeLayout` measurement pass per cell. For a 50-card
  visible grid, that's 50 extra subcompositions per recomposition
  vs. 50 direct `AsyncImage` renders. The overhead is real on
  low-end devices and during scroll-driven recomposition.
- The UX value of per-cell loading spinners is also lower in a
  grid. Fifty simultaneously-animating spinners during a
  cold-cache library open is visually noisy — the "empty
  tinted card fills in with the cover" pattern is calmer and
  more familiar to library-app users.

Decision: `AsyncImage` for grid use; `SubcomposeAsyncImage`
remains the right choice for one-of-a-kind hero thumbnails like
the Details cover. Document this division so future cover-cell
work picks the right primitive.

### 55.3 Trade-offs accepted

- **No per-cell loading spinner.** The Card's surface-variant
  `placeholderTint.copy(alpha = 0.15f)` background shows
  through until Coil delivers the bitmap. Visual signal:
  "card outline visible, image still arriving."
- **No per-cell error indicator.** On image-load failure,
  `AsyncImage` renders nothing; the tinted background remains
  visible. Matches legacy library cards (which also show a
  silent placeholder on broken / 404 covers, no broken-image
  icon). A user looking at a stubbornly-tinted card will
  understand "this cover failed" via the absence of an image
  on a card that has a title.
- **No adult-content blur.** Legacy `LibraryScreen` does NOT
  blur adult covers in the library view — the blur gate is a
  Details-screen concern (§51, §54). Library cards show all
  bookmarked content uncensored because the user already
  opted in by bookmarking it. The rework preserves this
  posture; `LibraryCardCover` never applies `Modifier.blur`.
- **Blank URL → tinted-only render.** Same posture as
  `DetailsCover`: when `coverUrl.isBlank()`, skip the
  `AsyncImage` entirely and let the tinted `Box` show. No
  broken-image painter.

### 55.4 Why extract `LibraryCardCover` as a private composable

The pre-slice `LibraryCard` rendered the cover slot inline as a
plain `Box` (5 lines). Adding the Coil pipeline would have
grown the inline block to ~15 lines and bloated `LibraryCard`'s
already-long body. Extracting `LibraryCardCover` keeps
`LibraryCard` lean (one call site for the cover) and gives the
cover logic a documented home where the load-bearing
inheritances from the singleton `ImageLoader` and the
AsyncImage-vs-SubcomposeAsyncImage trade-off can be captured in
KDoc.

The composable signature `(coverUrl: String, placeholderTint:
Color)` is the minimum surface — no `LibraryManga`, no
`Manga`, no MVI state coupling. `LibraryCardCover` is reusable
for any cover-thumbnail-with-tinted-placeholder use case (a
future History row cover, for example). The `Color` parameter
keeps the selection-state-aware tinting (line 216 in
`LibraryScreen.kt`: `placeholderTint = if (isSelected)
MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary else MaterialTheme.colorScheme
.outline`) at the call site where the selection context lives.

  pre-slice posture (the pre-slice `Box` also used 6.dp inner
  corners with 8.dp outer card corners).
- **History / search-result cover ports.** The same pattern
  applies to History rows and Search result cards. Both are
  separate `:ui` slices once the History and Search MVI
  surfaces land. `LibraryCardCover`'s signature
  (`String, Color`) is reusable; a refactor to move it into a
  shared `common/` module is queued for whenever the second
  user of this shape arrives (rule-of-three).
- **Reader thumbnail row / chapter cover.** Each chapter in a
  reader's "next chapter" preview could show its own
  thumbnail. Out of scope until the Reader rework foundation
  lands.



## 56. Phase 6.4.1 — Reader feature `:domain` foundation

Opens the Reader rework arc. Mirrors the Phase 6.3.1 Details
foundation pattern: lay down the pure-domain seam first (model
+ repository contract + use case), then build the `:data` impl
(6.4.2), MVI (6.4.3), `:ui` composable (7.x.reader), and Koin
wiring (8.x.reader) on top in subsequent slices. Strangler-fig:
the legacy `:shared` reader VM and `:composeApp` reader screen
remain untouched and continue driving reading; the rework path
is dormant until the full stack lands.

### 56.1 Why this slice now

The Details rework arc is polish-complete (§50–55). The two
remaining feature arcs that are large enough to need a full
domain/data/presentation/ui/wiring stack are Reader and Search.
Reader is picked first because (a) it has the largest
user-visible surface area of all features (every read action
funnels through it), (b) the legacy reader VM already carries
the heaviest cross-cutting concerns (streaming sources,
downloaded CBZ extraction, statistics timer, bookmark
toggle) so unbundling them yields the biggest SRP win, and
(c) the rework `Chapter` KDoc explicitly anticipated this
slice (it deferred `chaptersImages` to "a dedicated
`ChapterPages` model under a future Reader slice").

### 56.2 Domain model decisions

#### 56.2.1 `Page` — no `chapterIndex`, no `BitmapPainter`

The legacy `ReaderItem.ImagePage` carried three fields
beyond `url + headers`:
- `chapterIndex: Int` — which timeline slot the page renders
  into.
- `request: ImageRequest` (later: stripped by the Phase 10.3
  `:shared` port) — pre-built Coil image request.
- `compressedPainter: BitmapPainter?` (later: stripped) —
  post-compression bitmap.

The rework `Page` keeps only `url` + `headers`. `chapterIndex`
is a presentation-layer concern (the future Reader VM pairs
each page with its source chapter when it assembles a
`ReaderItem` timeline). Painters / image-requests are pure
`:ui` concerns and would re-introduce the `:composeApp` +
Android-graphics dependency that the `:shared` port already
expelled.

#### 56.2.2 `ReadingMode` — canonical home moves to `:domain`

Legacy: `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.reader.data.ReadingMode`
(within `:shared`). Rework: `me.manga.kira.domain.model.reader.ReadingMode`
(within `:domain`). Wire-format compatible — same `name`
values, same persisted DataStore key. The two enums coexist
until the legacy reader VM is retired (Phase 6.4.3+); the
`:data` mapper translates at the boundary if needed.

`isPaged` folds into the same file as the enum rather than
standing alone. Tightly coupled, tiny, and splitting would
inflate the file count.

Resource concerns (drawable + localized string) stay out of
the constructor — they were the reason the legacy enum
imported `R.drawable.*` / `R.string.*`. The rework `:ui`
dialog resolves icon + label via a `when (mode) { ... }`
lookup co-located with the dialog composables.

### 56.3 Repository contract — `Flow<AppResult<List<Page>>>`

Unlike the Details fetch (single `suspend AppResult<MangaDetails>`),
the chapter-pages fetch returns a `Flow`. Driving reason:
streaming sources (Prochan-style) emit pages incrementally
as the source page is scrolled server-side — see legacy
`ReaderViewModel.loadChapterStreaming`. Forcing the contract
to `suspend` would push the streaming branch into a
side-channel that the UI would have to special-case per
source.

The Flow shape folds both cases naturally:
- One-shot sources: single emission of `Success(allPages)`,
  then completion.
- Streaming sources: sequence of `Success(cumulativeList)`
  emissions, each carrying the running page list (later
  emissions are supersets of earlier ones), then completion.
- Failures: single `Failure(error)` emission, then
  completion. Success / Failure do not interleave for a
  single chapter load.

This is documented in `ChapterPagesRepository.fetchPages`
KDoc as the impl contract — Phase 6.4.2 honours it.

### 56.4 Routing contract for the `:data` impl (Phase 6.4.2 spec)

The interface KDoc pins the routing logic the `:data` impl
must implement:

1. If `chapter.isDownloaded` AND the future downloads
   facility supplies a local path list: emit
   `Success(localPaths.map { Page(url = it, headers = emptyMap()) })`.
   If the only local path ends in `.cbz`, extract via
   `CbzReader` (already cross-platform under `:platform`).
2. Otherwise: delegate to the per-source repository via
   `SourcesRepository.getRepoByName(manga.api)` (still in
   `:shared` legacy until source repos are themselves
   ported), translate the `Flow<State<List<String>>>` →
   `Flow<AppResult<List<Page>>>`, attach
   `defaultHeaders` to each URL.

### 56.5 Deferred — downloaded-chapter local-path lookup

The rework has no `DownloadsRepository` yet. Phase 6.4.2's
impl will fall back to source fetch even for
`chapter.isDownloaded = true` until the downloads facility
is itself ported.

User-visible impact: **zero**, because no rework caller
invokes `ChapterPagesRepository` yet. The legacy reader
still drives reading in `:composeApp`. The Phase 6.4.x arc
will progressively wire the rework path; the downloads
gap closes whenever the downloads slice lands (post-Reader
arc).

This is the same posture Phase 6.3.x took with
`IsAdultContentUseCase`: define the interface and ship a
limited impl, defer the missing piece, surface it as
explicit KDoc so future readers don't think it's an
oversight.

### 56.6 Use case — single-verb wrapper

`FetchChapterPagesUseCase(repository).invoke(manga, chapter)`.
Same pattern as `ObserveLibraryUseCase`,
`FetchMangaDetailsUseCase`, `IsAdultContentUseCase`,
`ToggleInLibraryUseCase`. Future enrichment (chapter
prefetch, transparent retry, page deduplication) lands
inside this class without forcing a VM signature change.

### 56.7 Files (within 5-file budget)

| Module | File | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:domain` | `domain/model/reader/Page.kt` | NEW — page model (url + headers); KDoc rationale for the dropped `chapterIndex` and painter/request fields. |
| `:domain` | `domain/model/reader/ReadingMode.kt` | NEW — canonical enum + `isPaged` extension; KDoc on the legacy → rework move and wire-format compatibility. |
| `:domain` | `domain/repository/ChapterPagesRepository.kt` | NEW — `fetchPages(manga, chapter): Flow<AppResult<List<Page>>>`; KDoc pins the routing contract for Phase 6.4.2 and the streaming-emission semantics. |
| `:domain` | `domain/usecase/reader/FetchChapterPagesUseCase.kt` | NEW — single-verb wrapper around the repository. |

Four files. Under the five-file budget. Diff: 169 insertions
across the four new files (zero deletions — strictly
additive).

### 56.9 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 6.4.1

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 6.4.1. Each of the four new files
holds exactly one concept:
- `Page.kt` — data class with two fields.
- `ReadingMode.kt` — enum + one pure extension.
- `ChapterPagesRepository.kt` — single-method interface.
- `FetchChapterPagesUseCase.kt` — one operator-fun delegate.

No abstractions invented for hypothetical future
requirements. The Flow shape is justified by the existing
streaming source family (Prochan), not speculation.

### 56.10 What this slice deliberately defers

- **`:data` impl.** Lands in Phase 6.4.2 — implements
  `ChapterPagesRepository` over the legacy `:shared`
  `SourcesRepository` for source routing, with the
  documented downloads fallback noted in §56.5.
- **`:presentation` MVI.** Lands in Phase 6.4.3 — Reader
  VM with `OnEnter(manga, startChapterIndex, chaptersList)`
  / `OnPageChanged(...)` / `OnReadingModeChanged(...)` /
  `OnNextChapter` / `OnPreviousChapter` intents. Replaces
  the eight legacy VM `fun loadChapter(...)` /
  `goToNextChapter(...)` overloads with a single intent
  channel.
- **`:ui` composable.** Lands in Phase 7.x.reader — Reader
  screen consuming the new MVI surface. Will likely keep
  the existing five reading-mode composables
  (`Horizontal`, `Vertical`, `Webtoon`, `Continuous`,
  `ContinuousVertical`) as-is and wire them to the new
  state shape.
- **`:composeApp` wiring.** Lands in Phase 8.x.reader —
  Koin module + guarded debug nav route. Legacy reader
  remains the default route until rework is feature-complete.
- **`CompressionState` port.** Legacy compression was
  Coil-dependent and was stubbed in `:shared` as a 7-line
  data class placeholder pending a "cross-platform bitmap
  pipeline" — but the Reader arc (Tasks #212–#237, ending
  with the ktor3 per-byte progress port at #237) completed
  without that feature materializing, so the stub never
  acquired a `:domain` / `:data` / `:presentation` / `:ui`
  consumer. **Stub retired in Phase 9.x.compressionstate
  .retire** (see §207 below): orphan deletion confirmed
  by 3-pass grep. If a compression feature is ever
  implemented later, it will land in the new rework
  layers, not by reanimating the `:shared` stub.
- **`ReaderChapter` enriched domain model.** Legacy
  `ReaderChapters` carries `mangaId / chapterId / localImagePaths`
  fields that the rework `Chapter` doesn't. For 6.4.1 the
  use case takes `(manga: Manga, chapter: Chapter)`; if
  6.4.2's impl finds it cannot satisfy the contract with
  just those two, the foundation slice will be extended
  with an additional model (added as a strictly-additive
  diff). The current design bets that the source fetch
  can be expressed via `manga.api` + `chapter.url` alone,
  which legacy `BaseMangaRepository.fetchChapterDataF`
  confirms.
- **Statistics-timer integration.** Legacy VM calls
  `statisticsRepo.startReadingSession()` /
  `endReadingSession()` from `onScreenResume` /
  `onScreenPause`. The rework Reader VM will surface this
  via lifecycle intents (`OnScreenResumed`, `OnScreenPaused`)
  rather than VM-internal lifecycle hooks. Out of scope
  for 6.4.1.



## 57. Phase 6.4.2 — Reader feature `:data` impl + Koin module

Lands the `:data` layer for the Reader rework arc:
`ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl` over the legacy
`:shared/SourcesRepository`, plus the Koin bindings that wire
the new graph into the host app. Strangler-fig boundary stays
inside the `:data` impl — the impl talks to the legacy
`SourcesRepository.getOrRepoByName(api).fetchChapterDataF(url)`
and projects each emission into the typed
`AppResult<List<Page>>` shape Phase 6.4.1 committed to.

### 57.1 Architecture

```
:domain          ChapterPagesRepository      (Phase 6.4.1)
                      ▲ (interface)
                      │
:data            ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl  (Phase 6.4.2)
                      │ wraps + maps
                      ▼
:shared          SourcesRepository           (legacy)
                  └──▶ BaseMangaRepository
                         .fetchChapterDataF(url): Flow<State<List<String>>>
                         .defaultHeaders: Map<String, String>
```

The `:data` impl is a Flow-mapping shim. It does four
things:
1. Look up the source repo via
   `sourcesRepository.getOrRepoByName(manga.api)`; emit
   a terminal `AppError.Unexpected` if the lookup returns
   `null` (matches the Details impl's posture — see
   `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl` §42.x).
2. Read `defaultHeaders` once per fetch (per-source, not
   per-page).
3. Collect the legacy `Flow<State<List<String>>>`,
   dropping `State.Loading` emissions (the rework VM
   tracks loading via its own MVI state, never via the
   source flow).
4. Translate `State.Success(urls) → AppResult.Success(pages)`
   where each `Page(url, headers)` carries the same header
   map by reference. Translate `State.Error → AppResult.Failure`
   via the connectivity / timeout / HTTP-status heuristics
   established by the Details impl.

The whole flow is wrapped in `.flowOn(dispatchers.io)` so
the source fetch runs on I/O. A `.catch` operator promotes
unhandled `Throwable`s into terminal `AppResult.Failure`
emissions, with `CancellationException` rethrown
unchanged (structured-concurrency invariant).

### 57.2 Why the streaming contract folds naturally

Phase 6.4.1's contract documented two emission patterns:
- **One-shot**: single `Success(allPages)`, then complete.
- **Streaming**: sequence of `Success(cumulativeList)`,
  then complete.

The legacy `fetchChapterDataF` already obeys this — for
non-streaming sources it emits exactly one `Success`; for
streaming sources (Prochan) it emits each cumulative
list. The rework impl is a pure map over each emission;
no special-case for streaming. The KDoc on the legacy
`BaseMangaRepository` aligns with the rework contract.

### 57.3 Error classification — deliberate duplication

The connectivity / timeout / HTTP heuristics live as
private functions on `ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl`,
duplicating `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl`. Rationale
(rule-of-three):
- Two callers (Details, Reader) is the threshold of
  *considering* factoring, not the threshold of
  *requiring* it.
- Factoring now would need a public mapper module
  without a clear shape: takes a `LegacyState.Error`?
  a `Throwable`? both? what does it return for
  unclassifiable cases? These questions are
  answer-by-third-caller — a future Search / Library
  fetch will pin the right surface.
- The duplicated heuristics are localised, tightly
  scoped, and ~25 lines per impl. The cost of
  duplication is bounded; the cost of a premature
  abstraction is unbounded.
- Documented in both impls so future readers know it's
  intentional.

When a third `:data` impl needs the same classification,
the shared helper falls out naturally with all three
call-shapes in view.

### 57.4 Why Reader VM binding is intentionally absent

`ReaderReworkModule` binds the repository + use case but
not a `viewModel { ReaderViewModel(...) }`. The Reader VM
itself lands in Phase 6.4.3 (`:presentation`). Today's
module ships the dependency edges so the binding surface
compiles against the rest of the graph today. Phase 6.4.3
will add the line — that's the natural change-locus,
keeping Phase 6.4.2 strictly about `:data` + initial Koin
wiring.

### 57.5 Files (within 5-file budget)

| Module | File | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:data` | `data/repository/ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt` | NEW — impl with the four-step Flow shim described in §57.1, private error-classification helpers, and `.flowOn(dispatchers.io) + .catch` wrapping. |
| `:composeApp` | `di/ReaderReworkModule.kt` | NEW — Koin module with `single<ChapterPagesRepository>` and `factory { FetchChapterPagesUseCase }`. Reader VM binding deferred to 6.4.3. KDoc captures the lifecycle choices and the shared `DispatcherProvider` dependency posture. |
| `:composeApp` | `di/ReworkModules.kt` | EDIT — append `readerReworkModule` to the `allReworkModules()` list. One-line change. |

Three files. Well under the five-file budget. Diff:
192 insertions, 0 deletions.

  (23 s).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green.
- Combined iOS run: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 37 s.
- Desktop target: not explicitly re-run; the
  multiplatform compile chain re-compiles commonMain

### 57.7 SOLID Guardian verdict — Phase 6.4.2

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase 6.4.2. Each file holds one

### 57.8 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Reader MVI / VM.** Lands in Phase 6.4.3. The intent
  surface will replace the legacy VM's eight
  `loadChapter` / `goToXxxChapter` overloads with a
  single MVI intent channel
  (`OnEnter`, `OnPageChanged`, `OnReadingModeChanged`,
  `OnNextChapter`, `OnPreviousChapter`,
  `OnToggleBookmark`, `OnScreenResumed`,
  `OnScreenPaused`).
- **Downloaded-chapter local-path lookup.** Same
  posture as Phase 6.4.1 — defers until a
  `DownloadsRepository` lands. Zero user impact because
  no rework caller invokes this repository yet (legacy
  Reader still drives reading).
- **Shared error-classification helper.** Rule-of-three
  threshold not yet met; documented in §57.3 and in the
  impl KDoc.
- **Streaming dedup at the data layer.** Legacy
  `loadChapterStreaming` does its own dedup (tracks
  emitted URLs in a per-chapter set) to avoid re-adding
  pages on each emission. The rework impl emits the
  full cumulative list per emission; dedup is the
  presentation layer's concern (the future Reader VM
  diffs against its prior `state.pages`). Pushing
  dedup down to `:data` would force the impl to keep
  per-call state, which contradicts the single-Flow,
  per-collect semantics.
- **Per-page header refresh.** Legacy reads headers
  once per fetch from `BaseMangaRepository.defaultHeaders`.
  The rework impl follows the same posture. If a future
  source family rotates per-page tokens, the `Page.headers`
  field is already a per-page `Map<String, String>` —
  the impl could repopulate per emission. Out of scope
  today.

## §58 Phase 6.4.3 — Reader `:presentation` MVI

### 58.1 Slice layout

```
   :ui (future Phase 7.x.reader)
        │ observes
        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ :presentation/reader                    │
│   ReaderViewModel                       │
│     ├── state: StateFlow<ReaderState>   │
│     ├── effects: Flow<ReaderEffect>     │
│     ├── submit(ReaderIntent)            │
│     └── handle(intent):                 │
│           OnEnter   → runFetch          │
│           OnRetry   → guarded re-run    │
│           OnPageChanged → clamp + copy  │
│           OnBackClick   → emit Effect   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │ injects
        ▼
   FetchChapterPagesUseCase (:domain)
        │ delegates
        ▼
   ChapterPagesRepository (:domain)
        │ implemented by
        ▼
   ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl (:data)
```

The slice is strictly additive — no module boundaries
move, no legacy file is touched. The four new files all
land under
`presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/`.

### 58.2 Why this VM is minimal vs. legacy's 601-line monolith

The legacy `:shared` `ReaderViewModel` owns seven
responsibilities glued together:

1. Page fetching for the current chapter.
2. Multi-chapter prefetch / append-on-scroll feed.
3. Reading-mode persistence (DataStore round-trip).
4. Bookmark observe + toggle (LibraryRepository).
5. Statistics session timer (start / end).
6. CBZ cache cleanup on `onCleared`.
7. Compression state (no-op shim today).

The rework's Phase 6.4.3 VM owns ONLY responsibility
(1). Each of 2–7 needs a `:domain` use case that
doesn't exist yet, and pulling `:shared` types
(`SettingsRepository`, `LibraryRepository`,
`StatisticsRepository`, `CbzReader`) into
`:presentation` would violate layer boundaries — the
whole point of the rework. So each of (2)–(7) lands
its own slice when its use case is ready, then
extends this VM's intent surface (additive, OCP —
never replaces what's here).

Concretely the deferred backlog is:

| Legacy responsibility       | Future slice                   | Required `:domain` foundation         |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| Reading-mode persistence    | Phase 6.4.x.mode               | `ObserveReadingModeUseCase` + setter  |
| Bookmark observe + toggle   | Phase 6.4.x.bookmark           | `ObserveChapterBookmarkUseCase` + tog |
| Statistics session timer    | Phase 6.4.x.stats              | `StartReadingSessionUseCase` + end    |
| Multi-chapter feed          | Phase 6.4.x.feed               | `FetchChapterFeedUseCase` (window)    |
| CBZ cache cleanup           | Post-downloads slice           | `CleanupChapterCacheUseCase`          |
| Compression state           | Post cross-platform bitmap     | `:ui` decision after pipeline lands   |

Each row is decoupled from the others; they can land
in any order.

### 58.3 Composite state vs. seven parallel flows

Legacy exposes seven `StateFlow`s
(`allReaderItems`, `loadingChapters`, `readingMode`,
`bookmarked`, `loadedChapterIndexes`,
`currentChapterIndex`, `compressionStates`). Two
observers reading at slightly different moments can
see inconsistent snapshots — page list updated but
`loadingChapters` not yet, or `currentChapterIndex`
moved before the corresponding pages landed in
`allReaderItems`.

The rework collapses the four flows the minimal slice
owns (page list, current page index, loading flag,
error) into a single `ReaderState` `data class`
mutated via `.copy()`. Atomic snapshot guaranteed by
`MutableStateFlow.compareAndSet` semantics in
`MviViewModel.updateState`. When the deferred slices
land, their fields are added to `ReaderState` rather
than spawned as parallel flows — same atomicity
guarantee carries forward.

### 58.4 Streaming-source semantics in the reducer

`FetchChapterPagesUseCase` returns
`Flow<AppResult<List<Page>>>`. For Prochan-style
sources the flow emits multiple `Success(pages)` each
carrying the running cumulative page list (see §57.2
for the data-layer rationale). The VM's reducer
unconditionally replaces `state.pages` with the
latest snapshot.

This is monotonic by data-layer construction (legacy
`BaseMangaRepository.fetchChapterDataF` only grows
the list across emissions, never shrinks), so
observers downstream see pages append, never
disappear. `currentPageIndex` stays put unless the
user pages forward — the reducer clamps it on every
Success to `0..pages.lastIndex` to guard against the
theoretical shrink case (and to land `0` if a fresh
`OnEnter` resets `pages` to empty before the first
emission).

### 58.5 Re-entry idempotence and re-entrance guard

Same posture as Details (§42 + §6.3.5):

- **OnEnter idempotence**: drop if `(manga, chapter)`
  identity matches the in-state pair. Config-change
  re-attach re-emits the StateFlow to the new host
  without re-running the fetch.
- **OnRetry guard**: drop if `state.isLoading == true`.
  Prevents two concurrent fetches from racing on
  `updateState`. The `:ui` retry button (Phase
  7.x.reader) will also disable while loading, but
  the VM guard closes the gap for any other
  dispatcher (intent replay, programmatic retry,
  future pull-to-refresh).

`OnPageChanged` has neither guard — it's
observation-only and cheap. The reducer drops
unchanged indices to avoid pointless `updateState`
churn while pages stream in.

### 58.6 Files

| File                         | Lines | Purpose                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `reader/ReaderIntent.kt`     |  57   | Sealed intent surface (4 cases)          |
| `reader/ReaderEffect.kt`     |  23   | Sealed effect surface (2 cases)          |
| `reader/ReaderState.kt`      |  86   | Composite state (`data class`)           |
| `reader/ReaderViewModel.kt`  | 148   | Reducer + use case orchestrator          |

Total: 314 lines across 4 files, all in
`commonMain`. No `androidMain` / `iosMain` /
`desktopMain` sources — the VM is fully shared.

### 58.7 Build gates

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`: ✅ green
  in 21 s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +
  `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`: ✅
  green in 35 s combined run.
- Desktop: not explicitly re-run; `:presentation`
  builds against `commonMain` and the multiplatform
  compile chain has covered the JVM_17 target on
  earlier Phase 6.x slices that touched the same
  module. Desktop will re-verify at Phase 7.x.reader

### 58.8 SOLID verdict pointer

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` → "Phase 6.4.3 — Reader
`:presentation` MVI" for the per-file 10-point
checklist. All four files pass.

### 58.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Reading-mode persistence.** Needs a
  `:domain` setter use case backed by
  `SettingsRepository`. Until that ships, the rework
  `:ui` layer (Phase 7.x.reader) will default to
  `ReadingMode.DEFAULT` and skip the reading-mode
  dialog wiring.
- **Bookmark observe + toggle.** Needs
  `ObserveChapterBookmarkUseCase` +
  `ToggleChapterBookmarkUseCase` backed by
  `LibraryRepository`. The :ui surface (top-bar
  bookmark icon) won't render until then.
- **Statistics session timer.** Needs
  `StartReadingSessionUseCase` +
  `EndReadingSessionUseCase`. Same model as
  bookmark — lifecycle-driven intents
  (`OnScreenResumed` / `OnScreenPaused`) land
  alongside the use cases.
- **Multi-chapter feed.** Needs a
  `FetchChapterFeedUseCase` that returns a sliding
  window of chapters' pages. The single-chapter
  fetch shipped today is the foundation.
- **CBZ cache cleanup on `onCleared`.** Tied to the
  downloaded-chapter local-path branch
  (`ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl` §56.5 / §57.8). Same
  prerequisite: `DownloadsRepository` in `:domain`.
- **Compression state.** Tied to a cross-platform
  bitmap-compression pipeline. Legacy nopped this
  per its own §10.3 Cluster E note #3; the rework
  follows the same posture.
- **Reader Koin binding.** Will land in the future
  Phase 8.x.reader (when `:ui` is ready to consume
  the VM via `koinViewModel<ReaderViewModel>()`).
  Today's `ReaderReworkModule` has the repository
  and use case bound; the `viewModel { }` line is
  intentionally absent so the slice ships a
  reviewable atomic unit.

## §59 Phase 7.x.reader — Reader `:ui` composable shell

### 59.1 Slice layout

```
:composeApp (future Phase 8.x.reader)
   │ wires

   │   guarded debug nav route

┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ :ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt               │
│   ReaderScreen(stateful wrapper)         │
│     ├── collectAsState(viewModel.state)  │
│     └── ReaderScreenContent(stateless)   │
│           ├── LaunchedEffect → OnEnter   │
│           ├── effects → snackbar / back  │
│           ├── snapshotFlow firstVisible  │
│           │     → OnPageChanged          │
│           ├── ReaderTopBar(back + title) │
│           └── body switch:               │
│                isInitialLoading→spinner  │
│                error → ReaderErrorPane   │
│                hasPages  → LazyColumn    │
│                              of pages    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
   │ submits via onIntent
   ▼
ReaderViewModel (:presentation) — Phase 6.4.3
```

The slice ships ONE source file
(`ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt`, 280 lines) plus a
one-line `coil-network-core` dependency in
`ui/build.gradle.kts`. No other module touched.

### 59.2 Why this `:ui` slice doesn't add a Koin binding or a nav route

Phase 7.x.reader is the screen surface. It compiles
against the rework `ReaderViewModel` (Phase 6.4.3)
but is not wired into any user-facing navigation yet
— the legacy reader remains the user-facing binding
in `:composeApp`. The Koin `viewModel { }` line and
the guarded debug nav route land together in the
future Phase 8.x.reader, mirroring the pattern set
by §44 (Library) and §47 (Details).

This is deliberate atomicity. The screen compiles +
boot-launches in `koin.checkModules()` after the
future Phase 8.x.reader; today the slice exists
strictly to prove the rework VM has a working
`:ui` consumer without rewiring user-facing routes.

### 59.3 Coil setup — inline `ImageRequest` vs. helper

The screen builds a Coil `ImageRequest` inline per
page rather than calling
`composeApp/.../images/SourceImageRequest.kt`'s
`rememberSourceImageRequest(url, headers)` helper.
Why:

- The helper lives in `:composeApp`, which `:ui`
  cannot depend on (layer-boundary rule §4 — `:ui`
  imports `:presentation`, never sinks into the
  composition root).
- Lifting the helper into `:ui` is a separate
  micro-slice (it carries the
  `applyPlatformDecoderHints()` expect/actual and
  the `shouldConstrainImageSizeToScreen()`
  expect/actual for Desktop tall-bitmap behaviour).
  Phase 7.x.reader.shell keeps the slice focused on
  the screen surface; the helper lift is a
  follow-up.
- Inline `ImageRequest.Builder(context)` +
  `httpHeaders(NetworkHeaders.Builder().add(...).build())` +
  `maxBitmapSize(Size(Undefined, Undefined))`
  preserves the most critical anti-blur fix (the
  per-request maxBitmapSize override that defeats
  Coil 3.4's loader-level 4096-cap bug) without
  pulling in the platform decoder hints. The
  platform hints (Android RGB_565 + allowHardware
  false; Desktop skip-`.size()`-on-tall-bitmap) are
  the second-tier optimizations that affect memory
  pressure / Skia texture limits, NOT correctness.
  Since no user-facing route points at this screen
  yet, the temporary absence of those hints causes
  zero user impact.

### 59.4 LazyColumn key strategy

`items(pages, key = { it.url })` is intentional.
For streaming sources (Prochan), the VM's reducer
replaces `state.pages` on every Success emission
with the running cumulative list. Without a stable
`key`, Compose re-keys every item by position on
each emission, dropping decoded bitmaps from the
slot cache and forcing Coil to re-decode pages that
are already in memory.

URL is the natural identity: it's the wire address
Coil uses for cache lookup, and the streaming source
contract (§57.2) guarantees a URL never changes once
emitted — only new URLs append. So keying by URL
keeps already-decoded item composables stable across
emissions; the user's scroll position doesn't jump
and Coil's memory cache stays warm.

### 59.5 OnPageChanged via snapshotFlow

`snapshotFlow { listState.firstVisibleItemIndex }`
+ `distinctUntilChanged()` keeps the VM out of the
hot scroll path. Without the
`distinctUntilChanged` the VM would receive an
`OnPageChanged` intent for every frame the scroll
position changed within the same item — easily
60 Hz under a flung scroll. The VM's reducer
already drops unchanged indices, but emitting from
the screen side is cheaper than dispatching +
launching the coroutine + landing the
`updateState`.

`firstVisibleItemIndex` is the right discriminator
for a vertical-scroll reader: it tracks the page
whose top edge is currently above the viewport's
top edge, which is the page the user perceives as
"current". A pager-based reading mode (RTL / LTR /
vertical paged) would use a different discriminator
(`PagerState.currentPage`) — that's a future
micro-slice when the reading-mode preference use
case ships.

### 59.6 Files

| File                                  | Lines | Purpose                       |
| ------------------------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------- |
| `ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt`           | 280   | Stateful + stateless screen   |
| `ui/build.gradle.kts` (edit)          |  +12  | coil-network-core dependency  |

Total: 2 files / 292 lines (1 net new file, 1
single-block dependency edit).

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`: ✅ green
  in 11 s after fixing two first-pass errors —
  (a) missing `coil-network-core` dep (fixed by
  editing `:ui` `build.gradle.kts`), (b) `Spacing`

  (fixed in screen). Documented because the
  build-gate honesty rule requires logging the
  first-pass red.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +

- Desktop: not explicitly re-run; the multiplatform

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` → "Phase 7.x.reader — Reader
`:ui` composable shell" for the per-file 10-point
