### 59.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Non-vertical reading modes.** RTL / LTR pager,
  webtoon, continuous-vertical. Each is a layout
  micro-slice that ships alongside the
  reading-mode preference use case (deferred from
  §58.9). Until then the shell defaults every
  chapter to vertical scroll.
- **Tap-to-toggle UI chrome.** Legacy hides the
  top bar on tap. Needs an `OnUiToggle` intent in
  `:presentation` or a UI-local toggle state — a
  pure presentation concern that fits a later
  UX-polish slice.
- **Page indicator HUD as an overlay.** Today the
  page counter `"3 / 27"` lives in the top bar
  subtitle. A future slice can lift it to an
  auto-hiding overlay above the page list once
  tap-to-toggle ships.
- **Bookmark / share / settings actions in the top
  bar.** Each needs its own future intent + use
  case (see §58.9 / Phase 6.4.3 deferral table).
- **Per-page Android RGB_565 + allowHardware(false)
  decoder hints.** Live in `:composeApp`'s
  `applyPlatformDecoderHints` expect/actual today.
  A follow-up `:ui/.../reader/internal/`
  micro-slice lifts them via expect/actual without
  changing the composable's contract.
- **Coil placeholder + error transitions for
  in-page loading.** The shell uses bare
  `AsyncImage` — Coil's natural fade-in is the
  only transition. A future slice adds
  `placeholder` / `error` slots that match the
  legacy reader's per-page loading affordances.
- **Pinch-to-zoom on pages.** Legacy uses
  `me.saket.telephoto.zoomable-image-coil3` for
  zoomable webtoon strips. Out of scope today;
  the shell renders each page as a fixed-width
  `AsyncImage` with `ContentScale.FillWidth`.
- **Koin VM binding + debug nav route.** Phase
  8.x.reader.

The deferrals are individually small; the shell
intentionally trades feature coverage for atomic
reviewability of the screen-MVI integration.


## §60 Phase 8.x.reader — `:composeApp` Reader Koin binding + debug nav route

Five-file `:composeApp` slice that lights up the
Phase 7.x.reader screen end-to-end behind a debug-
reachable nav route. Mirrors §44 (Library) and §47
(Details). Build gates: Android green in 21 s,
iOS combined green in 33 s on first attempt.

### §60.1 Slice layout

```
composeApp/commonMain/
├─ di/ReaderReworkModule.kt        — added `viewModel { ReaderViewModel(get()) }`
├─ navigation/Screen.kt            — added `Screen.ChapterImagesRework(...)` route type
├─ navigation/routes/
│  ├─ ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt   (new) — adapter VM ↔ ReaderScreen ↔ NavController
│  └─ MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute.kt    — replaced placeholder toast with real nav call
└─ App.kt                          — registered `composable<Screen.ChapterImagesRework>`
```

### §60.2 Nav argument shape

`Screen.ChapterImagesRework` carries an eight-field
identity tuple: `(api, language, title, mangaUrl,
coverUrl, chapterNumber, chapterName, chapterUrl)`.
The adapter reconstructs `Manga` with `rating =
null` and `genres = emptyList()` (neither consumed
by the Reader screen — no rating row, no chip bar
in the reader), and reconstructs `Chapter` with
`date = null`, `isDownloaded = false`,
`isBookmarked = false` (none consumed by the
Reader screen, and `LocalDate?` would force a
`kotlinx.datetime.LocalDateSerializer` registration
on the nav graph just to carry an unused value).
This is the deliberate boundary between
navigation-layer identity and full-domain shape:
nav args carry just enough to drive `OnEnter`'s
re-entry key `(api, language, title) + chapter.url`
and the top-bar title strings (`title`,
`chapterNumber`, `chapterName`).

### §60.3 Routing source: Details adapter chapter taps

Phase 8.x (Details) lit up `DetailsScreen` with a
chapter-list section that emits
`DetailsEffect.NavigateToReader(manga, chapter)`
when a row is tapped. `MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute`
previously dropped that effect on a
`ToastShower.showShort("Reader rework not wired
yet — chapter N")` placeholder (documented at §47
KDoc point "No `Reader` rework yet").

This slice replaces that placeholder. The
`onNavigateToReader` callback now packs the
`(manga, chapter)` tuple into a
`Screen.ChapterImagesRework(...)` and calls
`navController.navigate(...)`. `ToastShower`
inject + `koinInject` import are removed from
the Details adapter (no longer used), keeping the
file's import set lean.

### §60.4 Koin lifecycle additions

`readerReworkModule.kt` adds exactly one line:
`viewModel { ReaderViewModel(get()) }`. The Koin
`ViewModelStoreOwner` integration scopes the VM to
the `NavBackStackEntry`, so popping the route
clears the VM; entering the route via a new
`composable<...>` entry creates a fresh one.
Identical lifecycle posture to `DetailsViewModel`
(§47.4) and the legacy `:shared` reader.

The repository (`single<ChapterPagesRepository>`)
and use case (`factory { FetchChapterPagesUseCase
(get()) }`) bindings were already in place from
Phase 6.4.2 — the missing piece was the VM, which
landed in Phase 6.4.3 but didn't have a Koin
binding because there was no caller. Phase 7.x.reader
added the caller (`:ui`), Phase 8.x.reader wires it.

### §60.5 Debug-reachability vs. user-facing

`Screen.ChapterImagesRework` is NOT surfaced from
any user-facing entry point. The only path into it
is from `MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute`, which is
itself only reachable from a developer-trigger
`navController.navigate(Screen.MangaDetailsRework
(...))`. So the rework Reader is reachable from:

```
debug trigger → Screen.MangaDetailsRework
                                        ↓ chapter tap
              → Screen.ChapterImagesRework (rework Reader)
```

The legacy path
`Screen.MangaDetails → Screen.ChapterImagesFragment`
stays unchanged. Both graphs coexist; the legacy
flow remains the user-facing default.

### §60.6 Bottom-bar visibility

`composable<Screen.ChapterImagesRework>` calls
`onBottomBarVisibleChange(false)` in a `SideEffect`
— matches the legacy Reader's full-screen page-list
experience. Matches `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment`'s
existing posture (legacy reader hides the bottom bar).

## §61 Phase 7.x.reader.chrome — tap-to-toggle UI chrome + page-indicator HUD

Four-file pure-presentation slice that closes two of
the deferred items from §59.9 (tap-to-toggle top
bar + page-indicator HUD). No new modules, no new
dependencies, no domain or data changes. Restores
two pieces of the legacy reader's UX while keeping
the surface narrow.

### §61.1 Slice layout

```
presentation/.../reader/
├─ ReaderIntent.kt        — added `OnUiToggle`
├─ ReaderState.kt         — added `isUiVisible: Boolean = true`
└─ ReaderViewModel.kt     — `OnUiToggle` branch + reset on `OnEnter`

ui/.../reader/
└─ ReaderScreen.kt        — AnimatedVisibility on TopBar + pointerInput tap detector + ReaderPageIndicatorHud
```

### §61.2 Why state, not local `remember`

The legacy `:shared` reader tracked `isUiVisible`
in a Compose `remember { mutableStateOf(true) }`
local to the screen. The rework hoists it into MVI
state because:

- **Configuration changes**: a screen-rotation
  destroys and recreates the Compose host. A
  `remember` value resets to default; an MVI
  `StateFlow` survives via the VM. Hoisting makes
  the user's tap-toggle choice durable across the
  re-create cycle.
- **Testability**: the reducer's `OnUiToggle`
  branch is a pure function over the in-state
  Boolean — a future MVI VM test can assert the
  toggle behavior without a Compose snapshot
  harness or a UI test framework.
- **Single source of truth**: the screen reads
  `state.isUiVisible` and submits intents; never
  owns the value. Same posture as every other
  rework UI-state concern (no presentation-layer
  fields stored in Compose locals).

The cost is one extra reducer dispatch per tap.
Negligible — taps are a low-frequency event.

### §61.3 `OnEnter` resets `isUiVisible = true`

When the user navigates to a *different* chapter
(distinct `(manga, chapter)` pair), the reducer's
`onEnter` branch resets `isUiVisible = true` —
the user sees the top bar + HUD on entry,
regardless of whether they had hidden chrome on
the previous chapter. Matches legacy behavior
(legacy's local `remember` re-initialized to
default each time the screen was re-entered).

The `OnEnter` re-entry idempotence guard already
short-circuits when `(manga, chapter)` matches
the in-state pair, so a configuration-change
re-emission does NOT reset `isUiVisible` — the
user's hide/show choice survives rotation. Only
genuine chapter changes reset the chrome.

### §61.4 Tap detector vs. scroll

The tap detector attaches to the outer `Box` that
hosts the page list, NOT to the `LazyColumn`
itself. Rationale:

- `pointerInput { detectTapGestures(onTap = ...) }`
  on a Box wraps the page area in a tap-only
  listener. `detectTapGestures` waits for ACTION_DOWN,
  watches for movement past `touchSlop`, and only
  fires on ACTION_UP if no drag was detected.
- A vertical drag inside the LazyColumn is consumed
  by the `LazyColumn`'s scroll machinery; the
  Box's `detectTapGestures` sees the drag exceed
  `touchSlop` and abandons the tap candidate. So
  scrolling and tap-toggling coexist cleanly.
- Tap detection on the outer Box (rather than the
  LazyColumn) means taps in the loading-spinner
  and error-pane states also toggle chrome — same
  posture as the legacy reader, where the user can
  tap-to-toggle even before pages render.

### §61.5 HUD design

`ReaderPageIndicatorHud` is a `Surface` with
rounded corners + `surfaceVariant` tonal background
+ `onSurfaceVariant` content color. Renders
`(currentPageIndex + 1) / pages.size` (via the
existing `pageIndicator(state)` extension) as a
`labelLarge` text inside `horizontal = md /
vertical = xs` padding. Bottom-padded `lg`. No
elevation — flat overlay over the page list.

Visibility uses the same `AnimatedVisibility`
pattern as the top bar (fade + slide), but slides
*down* (from the bottom) instead of up. This
mirrors the typical reader HUD pattern: chrome
slides off the top, HUD slides off the bottom,
giving the user an unobstructed view of the page
content in between.

The HUD is conditional on `pageIndicator(state) !=
null`, which itself short-circuits when
`state.pages` is empty. So loading + error states
show no HUD at all — only the top bar (when
`isUiVisible`).

### §61.6 Top-bar subtitle removed

The Phase 7.x.reader top bar carried a `Column`
title with `chapterDisplayTitle` + a
`pageIndicator` subtitle. This slice removes the
subtitle (the HUD owns that role now). The top
bar becomes a single-line title — cleaner,
matches `DetailsScreen`'s top-bar shape, and
avoids the visual redundancy of two indicators
both bound to `isUiVisible`.

### §61.7 Files table

| File | Lines | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `presentation/.../reader/ReaderIntent.kt` | 57 → 67 | +`OnUiToggle data object` + 10-line KDoc |
| `presentation/.../reader/ReaderState.kt` | 78 → 91 | +`isUiVisible` field + 12-line KDoc |
| `presentation/.../reader/ReaderViewModel.kt` | 149 → 153 | +`OnUiToggle` branch + reset on `onEnter` |
| `ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt` | 280 → 348 | +AnimatedVisibility on TopBar + tap detector + HUD composable |

Four files = within the contract's per-commit cap.

### §61.8 Build gates

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green
  in 22 s on first attempt.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +
  `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` —
  green in 35 s combined on first attempt.
- Desktop deferred (no Desktop-specific code
  touched).

### §61.9 SOLID verdict pointer

Per-file 10-point checklist + end-of-slice verdict
recorded in `SOLID_AUDIT.md` § "Phase
7.x.reader.chrome". All 4 changes pass.

### §61.10 Deliberate deferrals

- **Auto-hide after N seconds.** Some readers
  fade the chrome automatically after a quiet
  period. The legacy reader does NOT auto-hide,
  so the rework matches — chrome stays as the user
  last set it until they tap again or navigate to
  a new chapter.
- **Tap zones for previous/next chapter.** Some
  readers reserve left/right edge taps for
  chapter navigation. Out of scope today
  (multi-chapter feed slice isn't shipped yet —
  no concept of next/previous chapter at the VM
  level).
- **Pinch-to-zoom on pages.** Still deferred per
  §59.9 — needs
  `me.saket.telephoto.zoomable-image-coil3`.
- **Reading-mode picker.** Still deferred — needs
  `SettingsRepository` use case.
- **Chapter-bookmark toggle.** Still deferred —
  needs architectural decision on the chapter-
  identity strategy (legacy `LibraryRepository.
  toggleChapterBookmark(chapterId: Long)` is keyed
  on the Room PK, but the rework `Chapter`
  identifies by URL). Block-and-ask candidate
  raised in task log.
- **System-bar chrome (status / nav bar) hide
  on tap.** The legacy reader uses
  `WindowInsetsController` (Android) /
  `setStatusBarHidden(true)` (iOS) to give the
  page area more vertical space. Cross-platform
  via expect/actual — adds a `:platform` facade
  for `SystemBarController`. Out of scope today;
  fits a future micro-slice paired with the
  reading-mode picker.

The slice ships exactly the two §59.9 deferrals it
targeted (tap-to-toggle top bar + page indicator
HUD) — no more, no less.

## §62 Phase 6.4.x.mode — reading-mode persistence

Reading-mode preference now persists across the
strangler-fig boundary. The user picks one of the
six [ReadingMode] entries from the rework reader's
top-bar dropdown; the choice is written via
[SetReadingModeUseCase] to the same disk cell the
legacy `DataStoreHelper.readingModeFlow` reads
from, and is observed back into state via
[ObserveReadingModeUseCase] launched in VM `init`.

### §62.1 Slice layout

Files modified across four modules, in three
commits (per the 5-file/commit cap):

| Module | File | Role |
|--------|------|------|
| `:domain` | `repository/ReadingModeRepository.kt` | Interface — observe + set |
| `:domain` | `usecase/reader/ObserveReadingModeUseCase.kt` | Live-stream verb |
| `:domain` | `usecase/reader/SetReadingModeUseCase.kt` | Persist verb |
| `:data`   | `repository/ReadingModeRepositoryImpl.kt` | `ObservableSettings`-backed impl |
| `:data`   | `build.gradle.kts` | `api(multiplatform.settings)` + coroutines |
| `:composeApp` | `di/ReaderReworkModule.kt` | Repository + 2 use case bindings; VM gains 2 ctor args |
| `:presentation` | `reader/ReaderState.kt` | `readingMode: ReadingMode = DEFAULT` field |
| `:presentation` | `reader/ReaderIntent.kt` | `OnReadingModeChanged(mode)` case |
| `:presentation` | `reader/ReaderViewModel.kt` | `init { observe collect }` + handler |
| `:ui` | `reader/ReaderScreen.kt` | Top-bar action → `DropdownMenu` of 6 modes |

### §62.2 Wire-format compatibility (load-bearing)

The `:data` impl writes to the literal key
`"reading_mode"` — byte-identical to
`StorageKeys.READING_MODE` in legacy `:shared`.
The value on disk is the [ReadingMode] enum
`name`, also identical to legacy
`DataStoreHelper.setReadingMode(mode)` semantics.

This is the whole point of the slice: until the
user-facing route swap promotes the rework
reader, both readers must agree on which mode
the user picked. A change to either key or value
format would lose user preferences during the
strangler-fig transition.

The constant is duplicated inside
`ReadingModeRepositoryImpl` rather than imported
from legacy `:shared/.../StorageKeys.kt` because
the rework `:data` layer is forbidden from
depending on legacy presentation/storage helpers
(contract §6 DIP, layer boundary). The
duplication is deliberate and KDoc on both sides
documents the invariant.

### §62.3 Unknown-value fallback (departs from legacy)

Legacy `DataStoreHelper.readingModeFlow` produces
a raw `String` and the reader calls
`ReadingMode.valueOf(string)` which throws on an
unknown name (corrupt write, removed-in-downgrade
enum entry). That posture would crash the
rework's collector and tear down the VM.

The rework swaps the crash for a deterministic
fallback to [ReadingMode.DEFAULT] via
`entries.firstOrNull { it.name == raw }`. The
fallback never writes back to disk — the next
explicit user pick overwrites the bad value
normally.

User-visible delta: a manga that the user had
configured to RTL becomes Default after a corrupt
write, instead of producing an uncaught
exception. Both outcomes are acceptable; the
rework's is safer.

### §62.4 Why observe-collect in VM `init` (not `onEnter`)

The reading-mode preference is independent of
which chapter is loaded. Launching the collector
in `init` means the first emission lands as soon
as the VM is constructed — before or shortly
after the first `OnEnter` — so the first frame
of the reader picks up the right mode even when
the user opens a chapter while the preference is
being read.

`onEnter` would still work but would re-launch
the collector on every chapter switch within a
single VM lifetime, which is wasteful (the
upstream Flow is hot anyway) and adds a one-
emission lag whenever the user changes mode
mid-chapter. `init` is the single, lifetime-
scoped subscription.

### §62.5 Why no inline-optimistic update on `OnReadingModeChanged`

The handler does NOT do an inline
`updateState { it.copy(readingMode = mode) }`
before writing. It only calls
`setReadingMode(mode)`. The observer launched in
`init` re-emits with the new value (the
`ObservableSettings.getStringFlow` is hot and the
impl `set()` triggers an emission), which
updates state.

The disk write is the single source of truth.
If the store ever rejected a write (today
impossible, future-proof for synchronous
Desktop-Preferences exceptions), the UI would
not show a stale optimistic value that doesn't
match disk.

A no-op guard (`if (state.value.readingMode ==
mode) return`) sits in front of the setter to
skip identical writes. Multiplatform-settings
already short-circuits when the underlying value
is unchanged (no re-emission), but the explicit
guard avoids even attempting the write.

### §62.6 Picker UI choice — DropdownMenu, not Dialog

Legacy uses a full-screen `ReadingModeDialog`
with painted icons per entry. The rework ships a
`DropdownMenu` anchored to a top-bar action
button — the minimum-viable picker that exposes
the slice's value end-to-end.

Tradeoff: dropdown is faster to dismiss (tap
outside) and uses less screen real-estate, but
doesn't visually communicate the layout each
mode produces. A later polish slice can swap to
a dialog once the rework's icon system arrives;
the dropdown contract here is stable behind the
`OnReadingModeChanged` intent.

### §62.7 Build gates

- `:data:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`,
  `:presentation:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`,
  `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` →
  green (22 s).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +
  `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
  → green (1 m 9 s combined).
- `:ui:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` +
  `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` after
  picker added → green (9 s).
- `:ui:compileKotlinIosArm64` +
  `:ui:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` after
  picker added → green (9 s).

iOS framework linking and on-device validation
remain Windows-impossible and are deferred to
the user's Mac.

### §62.8 Layer boundaries respected

- `:domain` declares the interface and verbs;
  no `:data` / `:platform` / coil / multiplatform-
  settings imports.
- `:data` impl imports `ObservableSettings`. The
  legacy `PlatformModule.*` already binds it as
  a `single<ObservableSettings>` and the rework
  re-uses that cell.
- `:presentation` consumes only the two use
  cases — never the repository.
- `:ui` reads `state.readingMode` and dispatches
  `OnReadingModeChanged` — no use case, no
  repository, no platform import.
- `:composeApp` instantiates the impl in Koin.
  Required `api(multiplatform.settings)` in
  `:data/build.gradle.kts` because the
  composition root sees the constructor
  signature of `ReadingModeRepositoryImpl`.

### §62.9 SOLID checklist pointer

Per-file 10-point checklists for all 6 modified
files in `SOLID_AUDIT.md` under the
Phase 6.4.x.mode section.

### §62.10 Deliberate deferrals (post-slice)

- **Per-mode page layout in the reader page
  list.** Today the page list is always a
  `LazyColumn` vertical scroll regardless of
  `state.readingMode`. Each non-vertical mode
  (RTL pager, LTR pager, webtoon strip,
  continuous vertical) is a layout micro-slice
  that ships when its rendering treatment is
  designed — the persistence foundation here is
  what unblocks them.
- **Per-mode reader settings (e.g. zoom posture
  per RTL vs LTR).** Each future per-mode toggle
  follows the same observe/set pair pattern this
  slice establishes.
- **Per-manga reading-mode overrides.** Legacy
  has none either; if it lands, it is a sibling
  use case (`ObserveReadingModeFor(api, title)`
  with a per-manga key namespace) that the VM
  composes with this slice's global default.
- **Picker icons.** Pending the rework's `:ui`
  icon system. Top-bar uses a text glyph today;
  legacy used `R.drawable.*` painters per entry.
- **Dialog UX for the picker.** Dropdown ships
  today; dialog is a polish swap when icons
  land.

## §63 Phase 7.x.reader.systembars — Hide the navigation bar in the rework Reader

### §63.1 Goal & legacy parity

Restores native pre-KMP `HideSystemBars()` parity
to the rework Reader: the Android navigation
bar is hidden while the rework Reader route is
on the back stack, and restored on dispose. The
status bar is **not** touched (native code
deliberately scoped to `navigationBars()` only).
Visibility is **not** bound to
`ReaderState.isUiVisible` — native behaviour
was unconditional hide-on-enter / restore-on-
exit, independent of in-app chrome toggle.

The legacy KMP build had this functionality
DROPPED during the initial port (see TODO in
`composeApp/.../presentation/features/reader/ui/screens/ReaderScreen.kt:124`).
This slice restores native parity exclusively
for the rework Reader; the legacy KMP reader
remains as-is until that route swap lands.

### §63.2 File layout (5 files)

```
composeApp/src/commonMain/.../core/platform/
  HideNavigationBarSideEffect.kt         (expect)
composeApp/src/androidMain/.../core/platform/
  HideNavigationBarSideEffect.android.kt (actual — real implementation)
composeApp/src/iosMain/.../core/platform/
  HideNavigationBarSideEffect.ios.kt     (actual — no-op)
composeApp/src/desktopMain/.../core/platform/
  HideNavigationBarSideEffect.desktop.kt (actual — no-op)
composeApp/src/commonMain/.../navigation/routes/
  ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt      (call site)
```

Mirrors the existing
`FastScrollerGestureExclusion.kt` / `.android.kt`
/ `.ios.kt` / `.desktop.kt` quartet under
`composeApp/.../core/platform/` — same naming
convention, same source-set layout, same
expect/actual pattern for Compose-specific
platform behaviour.

### §63.3 Why not a `:platform` SPI

The Phase 5 `:platform` module hosts
non-Compose service facades wired through Koin
(toast, file system, secure storage,
connectivity, etc.). The system-bar hide is a
**Compose-specific side-effect** that:

1. Doesn't need DI (the Activity is reachable
   from `LocalContext` directly).
2. Doesn't need a service abstraction (one
   `@Composable` per platform is enough).
3. Is short-lived (lifetime equals the
   composition), unlike injectable singletons.

The existing
`composeApp/.../core/platform/` Compose-helper
convention is the right home. This keeps the
`:platform` module focused on its actual role
and avoids spinning up a Koin binding +
`ActivityHolder` plumbing that the rework graph
doesn't have yet (Phase 11 dependency).

### §63.4 Why not in `:ui`

`:ui` is contractually multiplatform-pure per
Contract §4: it must not import Android-only
APIs (`androidx.core.view.WindowInsetsCompat`,
`android.app.Activity`, etc.). Hosting the
side-effect at the `:composeApp` route adapter
keeps `ReaderScreen`'s parameter contract clean
and preserves its testability — previews and
tests can compose `ReaderScreenContent`
directly without any system-bar coupling.

### §63.5 Why not bound to `isUiVisible`

Three reasons:

1. **Behaviour preservation.** Native pre-KMP
   behaviour was unconditional hide-on-enter /
   restore-on-exit. Binding to `isUiVisible`
   would change what a returning user sees
   (chrome reveal now also reveals the nav
   bar), which is a UX change, not a port.
2. **Scope discipline.** The Phase
   7.x.reader.chrome slice introduced the
   `isUiVisible` toggle for in-app chrome only.
   Adding a system-level coupling is a separate
   design decision.
3. **Composability.** Keeping the side-effect
   parameterless (no Bool input) means it has
   no state to track — `DisposableEffect(Unit)`
   fires once on enter and once on dispose,
   matching the native cleanup pattern exactly.

If a future design wants the nav bar to track
chrome, that's a deliberate UX slice with its
own design review.

### §63.6 Android actual — line-by-line parity

Native pre-KMP source
(`yami-manga-apk-main/.../ReaderScreen.kt:768-786`):

```kotlin
@Composable
fun HideSystemBars() {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    DisposableEffect(Unit) {
        val window = context.findActivity()?.window
            ?: return@DisposableEffect onDispose {}
        val insetsController = WindowCompat
            .getInsetsController(window, window.decorView)
        insetsController.apply {
            hide(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.navigationBars())
            systemBarsBehavior = WindowInsetsControllerCompat.BEHAVIOR_DEFAULT
        }
        onDispose {
            insetsController.apply {
                show(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.navigationBars())
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The rework `HideNavigationBarSideEffect.android.kt`
ports this body verbatim — same Activity-resolve
walk, same `WindowCompat.getInsetsController` call,
same `hide(navigationBars())` + `BEHAVIOR_DEFAULT`,
same `show(navigationBars())` on dispose. The
only structural change is splitting the `.apply`
block into two statement lines (purely
stylistic).

### §63.7 iOS / Desktop — no-op

- **iOS**: no analog. The closest equivalent is
  the home-indicator auto-hide, which is a
  different visual surface and changes a
  different observable thing. Native pre-KMP
  iOS build also did not run this code path —
  no-op is parity-correct.
- **Desktop**: no analog. Window-system chrome
  is owned by the user's shell (Win32 / AppKit
  / Wayland / X11), not the app.

### §63.8 Build gates passed

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` —
  green in 21 s (warnings unchanged; all
  pre-existing).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +
  `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
  — green in 37 s combined.

### §63.9 SOLID footprint

Full 10-point Guardian checklist for every file
in this slice lives in `SOLID_AUDIT.md` under
the Phase 7.x.reader.systembars section.
Highlights:

- **SRP**: each file has exactly one job — the
  expect declares a side-effect; the Android
  actual hides/shows; the iOS / Desktop actuals
  are documented no-ops; the route adapter
  composes it.
- **OCP**: extending the side-effect for a new
  target = drop in a new actual file. No
  upstream contract changes.
- **DIP**: no DI involved; the side-effect
  reads `LocalContext` (Compose's standard
  CompositionLocal pattern), not an injected
  service.
- **No new abstractions**: deliberately avoided
  inventing a `SystemBarController` interface +
  `:platform` SPI + Koin binding + actual class
  for what is effectively a 6-line side-effect.

### §63.10 Deliberate deferrals (post-slice)

- **Status bar hide.** Native scoped to
  navigation bar only; the slice preserves
  that.
- **Bind to `isUiVisible`.** Out of scope per
  §63.5.
- **iOS home-indicator hide.** Behaviour change
  vs native; can land as a separate UX slice
  with design review.
- **Legacy reader parity restore.** The legacy
  KMP reader still has the Phase 10.x TODO;
  this slice scope is the rework reader only.
  When the route swap takes the rework reader
  user-facing, the legacy reader can be
  deleted.

## §64 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout — branch the rework Reader page-list on `state.readingMode`

### §64.1 Goal

Close the loop on Phase 6.4.x.mode by finally
surfacing the persisted `state.readingMode`
as a user-visible behaviour change in the
rework Reader. Until this slice the field was
stored, observed, and reduced through the
full clean-architecture stack but never read
by the layout code — every chapter rendered
as a vertical `LazyColumn` regardless of the
selection. This slice introduces the first
layout branch.

### §64.2 Rule-of-three branch

The slice ships exactly one new layout:
`ReadingMode.RIGHT_TO_LEFT` →
`HorizontalPager(reverseLayout = true)`. The
other five entries (`DEFAULT`,
`LEFT_TO_RIGHT`, `VERTICAL`, `WEBTOON`,
`CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL`) fall through to the
existing vertical `LazyColumn` placeholder.

**Why one mode, not all six.** The rule of
three: ship one to establish the branch
pattern, then extend. Each remaining mode
needs its own rendering treatment that
diverges from "horizontal pager, fit
contents" — `WEBTOON` is gapless vertical
strip with no inter-page padding,
`CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL` is paged-but-vertical
(`VerticalPager`), `LEFT_TO_RIGHT` is the
mirror of the new RTL branch, etc. Each will
land as its own micro-slice when the
treatment is designed. Listing them
exhaustively in the `when` keeps the
fall-through explicit (the compiler enforces
that every enum value is matched) without
forcing this slice to design five new
layouts.

### §64.3 State ownership pushed down

The previous version of `ReaderScreenContent`
hoisted a `LazyListState = rememberLazyListState()`
and a `LaunchedEffect(listState)` that
observed `firstVisibleItemIndex` via
`snapshotFlow`. That works for a single
list-type layout but doesn't compose with a
second one — `PagerState` and `LazyListState`
are unrelated types, so the parent would
either need both (one always idle) or a
sealed type wrapping them.

The simpler answer: each layout composable
owns its own state and installs its own
`snapshotFlow → onPageChanged` effect.
`ReaderScreenContent` now passes only
`(pages, readingMode, onPageChanged)` down,
and `ReaderPageLayout` dispatches to whichever
layout composable matches the mode. The
contract between the screen and the layout is
just "emit page indices via `onPageChanged`" —
the screen no longer knows which list type
backs the rendering.

This also explains why
`ReaderVerticalListBody` is a separate
composable from `ReaderVerticalList` even
though it has only one caller today: the body
takes an externally-owned `LazyListState`
parameter, which is the seam a future preview
/ test composable can use to drive the
LazyColumn with canned scroll state without
running the snapshotFlow side-effect. The
wrapper composable bundles the state +
effect; the body renders.

### §64.4 ContentScale: Fit for pager, FillWidth for list

Vertical scroll and horizontal pager want
different image fits:

- **Vertical scroll**: each image stacks below
  the previous one; overflow becomes scroll
  distance. `ContentScale.FillWidth` with
  `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` is the natural
  fit — width matches viewport, height
  scales to preserve aspect ratio, and the
  page can be arbitrarily tall.
- **Paged horizontal**: each page is a
  separate snap target; the image needs to
  fit inside the viewport without cropping.
  `ContentScale.Fit` with
  `Modifier.fillMaxSize()` ensures the page
  is as large as possible while fully
  visible (letterboxed if aspect ratio
  differs from viewport).

`ReaderPageItem` takes these as parameters
with the vertical-scroll defaults. The pager
overrides at the call site. No duplication of
the Coil `ImageRequest` building (which is the
non-trivial part with the
`maxBitmapSize(Undefined, Undefined)` anti-blur
fix carried over from Phase 7.x.reader).

### §64.5 State reset on mode toggle ~~(deferred)~~ — **resolved by §69**

~~When the user toggles `readingMode` mid-
session, `ReaderPageLayout` recomposes a
different child composable; the previous
layout's state (`LazyListState` /
`PagerState`) is discarded. The VM's
`currentPageIndex` (in `ReaderState`)
persists across the swap, but the new layout
mounts with a fresh state and renders at
index 0.~~

~~This matches the legacy reader's mode-toggle
behaviour. A future polish slice could read
`state.currentPageIndex` and pass it to
`rememberPagerState(initialPage = ...)` /
`rememberLazyListState(initialFirstVisibleItemIndex = ...)`
so the user lands on the same page after the
swap.~~

**Retired by §69 (Phase
7.x.reader.modelayout.scrollpos).**
`state.currentPageIndex` is now threaded
through `ReaderPageLayout` to each layout's
`remember*State` `initial*` parameter. The
streaming-anchor concern flagged in the
deferred note turned out to be a non-issue:
`currentPageIndex` is always a valid `0..pages.lastIndex`
value (the VM's reducer clamps it), and
mode-toggle happens after the user has been
on the page long enough for any streaming to
have stabilised. See §69 for the design
analysis.

### §64.6 Build gates

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`
  green in 32 s. Only pre-existing
  deprecation warnings (all in legacy
  `:composeApp` files).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` green
  in 1 m 32 s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
  green in 1 m 17 s.
- iOS framework linking + on-device verification
  of the RTL pager: Windows-impossible,
  deferred to user's Mac. On Android the
  pager + mode-toggle interaction is
  verifiable when the device-attached run
  happens (no new platform APIs in this
  slice, so no new platform-specific bugs
  are expected).

### §64.7 SOLID footprint

- **SRP**: each layout composable has exactly
  one job. `ReaderPageLayout` dispatches;
  `ReaderVerticalList` / `ReaderHorizontalPager`
  each own a layout + its scroll observer;
  `ReaderVerticalListBody` renders a list
  given external state; `ReaderPageItem`
  builds a Coil request + renders an
  `AsyncImage`. The screen-level orchestrator
  was simplified (the hoisted list state was
  removed from `ReaderScreenContent`).
- **OCP**: adding a new layout for one of the
  five deferred modes = add a branch to the
  `when` in `ReaderPageLayout` + a new
  composable. No other code changes.
- **DIP**: the screen depends on `ReadingMode`
  (the abstraction); the layout composables
  depend on Compose primitives.
- **No new abstractions**: deliberately
  avoided inventing a `ReaderLayout`
  interface, a `LayoutFactory`, or any
  pattern that would generalise the dispatch.
  A `when` over an enum is the natural shape
  for a five-state branch.

### §64.8 Deliberate deferrals (post-slice)

- **`LEFT_TO_RIGHT` mirror branch.** Same
  layout as RTL but `reverseLayout = false`.
  Trivially small; deferred to keep this
  slice scoped to "establish the pattern with
  one mode".
- **`WEBTOON` gapless variant.** Vertical
  strip with no inter-page padding /
  margins. Needs a `LazyColumn` variant
  without the implicit item spacing the
  current placeholder uses.
- **`CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL` (`VerticalPager`).**
  Compose has `VerticalPager` since 1.5;
  the layout is straightforward; the
  question is whether snap-on-swipe matches
  user expectations for "continuous
  vertical" (which legacy treats as a
  scrolling variant of vertical paging).
- **`DEFAULT` per-source default resolution.**
  Currently `DEFAULT` falls through to
  vertical scroll. The legacy app resolves
  `DEFAULT` against the source / manga's
  preferred mode before picking a layout —
  this would mean either resolving
  `DEFAULT` in the VM (so `state.readingMode`
  is never `DEFAULT` at render time) or
  resolving in the dispatch composable.
  Deferred until the rework has a sources /
  manga-metadata story for the
  "preferred mode" property.
- **Mode-toggle scroll-position preservation.**
  ~~See §64.5.~~ **Retired by §69 (Phase
  7.x.reader.modelayout.scrollpos)** —
  `currentPageIndex` is now threaded through
  the dispatch to each layout's `initial*`
  parameter.

## §65 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.ltr — `LEFT_TO_RIGHT` mirror branch

### §65.1 Goal

Pattern-extension follow-up to §64. Route
`ReadingMode.LEFT_TO_RIGHT` to the
just-introduced `ReaderHorizontalPager` with
`reverseLayout = false`, removing it from the
"falls through to vertical scroll"
placeholder bucket.

### §65.2 Scope

Single branch added to the `when` in
`ReaderPageLayout`. `LEFT_TO_RIGHT` removed
from the fall-through list. Two KDocs updated
to reflect the new state of branched-vs-
fallthrough modes. Three fall-through entries
remain: `DEFAULT`, `VERTICAL`, `WEBTOON`,
`CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL`.

### §65.3 Why a separate slice, not folded into §64

Rule-of-three: §64 established the pattern
with one branch. Folding a second branch
into the same slice would have made the
diff harder to review (more code in a slice
that was already 136 insertions) and would
have obscured the rule-of-three boundary —
a future reader of the commit history sees
"§64 introduces the pattern; §65 extends it"
rather than "§64 introduces the pattern and
two of its applications." Each branch is
also independently verifiable: if §64 alone
broke RTL reading on some device, the §65
LTR branch is unaffected because it uses
the same shared composable.

### §65.4 Build gates

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`
  green in 27 s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` green
  in 1 m 12 s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
  green in 1 m 14 s.

### §65.5 Deliberate deferrals (post-slice)

Same list as §64.8 minus the now-graduated
`LEFT_TO_RIGHT` entry:

- **`WEBTOON` gapless variant** — needs a
  `LazyColumn` without inter-page spacing.
- **`CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL` `VerticalPager`** —
  Compose `VerticalPager` is available; the
  open design question is snap-on-swipe
  ergonomics vs free scroll.
- **`DEFAULT` per-source default resolution**
  — needs the rework sources-metadata
  story.
- **Mode-toggle scroll-position
  preservation** — ~~see §64.5.~~ **Retired by
  §69 (Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.scrollpos)** —
  `initial*` now threaded through dispatch.

## §66 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.vertical — `DEFAULT` + `VERTICAL` → `VerticalPager` (with correction)

### §66.1 Goal

Bring the rework reader to legacy parity for
`ReadingMode.DEFAULT` and `ReadingMode.VERTICAL`,
which both render `VerticalPager` (paged-
vertical, snap-on-swipe) in the legacy
`:composeApp` reader's
`VerticalReadingMode.kt`. Pre-slice, both
modes were routing to the placeholder
vertical `LazyColumn` — wrong layout shape.

### §66.2 Correction to §64.8 / §65.5 deferral lists

Earlier slice close-outs (§64.8 and §65.5)
listed `CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL` as a future
`VerticalPager` candidate, based on the
enum-name reading the field as "continuous
*vertical paging*". That was wrong. The
legacy `:composeApp` reader (see
`ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt`) renders
`CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL` as a free-scroll
`LazyColumn` of vertically-stitched panels
— effectively a webtoon variant with simpler
placeholders. So:

- `DEFAULT` / `VERTICAL` → `VerticalPager`
  (legacy `VerticalReadingMode.kt`).
- `WEBTOON` / `CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL` →
  `LazyColumn` (legacy
  `WebToonReadingMode.kt` /
  `ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt`).

This slice fixes the routing for the first
pair (the two that were in the wrong bucket).
The second pair was already correctly in the
`LazyColumn` bucket; the deferral note in
§64.8 / §65.5 implying `CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL`
needed a `VerticalPager` is hereby retired.
Reading code, not enum names, is the source
of truth for legacy parity.

### §66.3 Branch table (post-slice, complete)

| Mode | Layout | Composable |
|------|--------|------------|
| `RIGHT_TO_LEFT` | HorizontalPager(reverseLayout=true) | `ReaderHorizontalPager` |
| `LEFT_TO_RIGHT` | HorizontalPager(reverseLayout=false) | `ReaderHorizontalPager` |
| `DEFAULT` | VerticalPager | `ReaderVerticalPager` |
| `VERTICAL` | VerticalPager | `ReaderVerticalPager` |
| `WEBTOON` | LazyColumn | `ReaderVerticalList` |
| `CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL` | LazyColumn | `ReaderVerticalList` |

Three composables, six modes. Every `when`
arm is explicit (no fall-through `else`) so
adding a new enum entry triggers a compile
error at the dispatch site.

### §66.4 `ReaderVerticalPager` design

Mirrors `ReaderHorizontalPager` on the
vertical axis:

- Owns its own `PagerState` via
  `rememberPagerState(pageCount = { pages.size })`.
- Installs its own `snapshotFlow { pagerState.currentPage }`
  effect that emits to the parent's
  `onPageChanged` lambda.
- Uses `Modifier.fillMaxSize()` +
  `ContentScale.Fit` so each page fills the
  viewport without cropping (matching the
  horizontal-pager rationale from §64.4).
- No `reverseLayout` parameter: legacy
  doesn't expose a bottom-to-top vertical
  reading mode, so adding the flag would be
  unused complexity. If a use case appears
  later, the flag can be added without
  changing any caller.

### §66.5 Build gates

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`
  green in 26 s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` green
  in 59 s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
  green in 1 m 1 s.

### §66.6 Remaining deferrals (post-slice)

The six-row table in §66.3 is layout-complete
vs legacy. What remains is polish, not
missing layouts:

- **`DEFAULT` per-source resolution.** Legacy
  treats `DEFAULT` as "use the source/manga's
  preferred mode"; until the rework has a
  sources-metadata story, `DEFAULT` is a
  synonym for `VERTICAL`.
- **`WEBTOON` vs `CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL`
  placeholder ergonomics.** Both render
  `LazyColumn` today. Legacy differentiates
  by spinner/placeholder treatment per item;
  a future polish slice can branch on the
  mode inside `ReaderVerticalList` or
  introduce a paired body composable.
- **Gapless `WEBTOON` spacing.** ~~Legacy
  renders webtoon panels with zero inter-page
  spacing for true vertically-stitched
  reading; current placeholder uses
  `LazyColumn`'s natural item layout.~~
  **Retired by §68 (Phase
  7.x.reader.modelayout.webtoongap).** The
  rework's `LazyColumn` was already gapless;
  the actual legacy parity item was a
  `.background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)`
  modifier on the LazyColumn (now applied).
- **Zoomable modifier across all layouts.**
  ~~Legacy wraps each layout in
  `zoomable(rememberZoomState())` so users
  can pinch-zoom. The rework layouts don't
  yet.~~ **Retired by §67 (Phase
  7.x.reader.modelayout.zoom).** All three
  layout composables now wrap their outermost
  modifier with `.zoomable(rememberZoomState())`.
- **Mode-toggle scroll-position
  preservation.** ~~See §64.5.~~ **Retired by §69
  (Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.scrollpos)** —
  `state.currentPageIndex` is now threaded
  through `ReaderPageLayout` to each layout's
  `remember*State` `initial*` parameter.

## §67 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.zoom — pinch-to-zoom across all three reader layouts

### §67.1 Goal

Bring the rework reader to legacy parity for
pinch-to-zoom + pan. Legacy
`composeApp/.../reader/ui/reading_modes/*.kt`
wraps each of its three layout composables
(`HorizontalReadingMode`,
`VerticalReadingMode`, `WebToonReadingMode`,
`ContinuousVerticalReadingMode`) with
`.zoomable(rememberZoomState())` so users can
pinch-zoom into pages and pan around them.
Pre-slice the rework layouts had no
pinch-handling — a tap-to-toggle was the
only registered gesture.

### §67.2 Library choice — `net.engawapg.lib:zoomable` 2.8.0

The legacy `:composeApp` classpath already
carries `libs.zoomable` (see
`composeApp/build.gradle.kts:97` —
`implementation(libs.zoomable)`). The library
is Kotlin Multiplatform-capable (Android +
Desktop + iOS via Compose Multiplatform);
nothing about its `Modifier.zoomable(ZoomState)`
extension is JVM-specific.

So this slice adds
`implementation(libs.zoomable)` to
`:ui/build.gradle.kts`'s `commonMain`
dependency block alongside the existing Coil
deps. No expect/actual shim is needed; no
`:platform` SPI is introduced. The library
sits on the `:ui` classpath the same way
`coil-compose` and `coil-network-core`
already do.

`:ui` taking a third-party Compose-modifier
dependency is consistent with the established
pattern (the module already takes
`coil-compose` for `AsyncImage` and
`coil-network-core` for per-request
`NetworkHeaders`). The layer-boundary rule
(§4) forbids `:ui` from importing
`:platform` / `:data` / `:shared` — not from
taking external Compose libraries that are
themselves multiplatform-pure.

### §67.3 Modifier ordering — `.zoomable` outer, `.fillMaxSize` inner

All three layout composables apply the
modifier as:

```kotlin
modifier = Modifier
    .zoomable(rememberZoomState())
    .fillMaxSize(),
```

The outermost modifier processes pointer
events first. Putting `.zoomable` outer means
pinch is recognized at the layout root before
the inner `HorizontalPager` /
`VerticalPager` / `LazyColumn` pointer
handlers (page-swipe, scroll) claim the
pointer slot. The pager / list pointer
handlers continue to receive single-pointer
drags (swipe-to-page-change for pagers,
free-scroll for the LazyColumn); `.zoomable`
only consumes the gesture once a second
pointer arrives.

This mirrors the legacy modifier ordering in
`HorizontalReadingMode.kt`. See the inline
comment block on each modifier addition for
the per-layout rationale.

### §67.4 Tap-detector + zoomable coexistence

The outer `Box` in `ReaderScreen` already
hosts a `detectTapGestures` modifier for the
chrome-toggle (Phase 7.x.reader.chrome §62).
This slice registers `.zoomable(...)` with
no `onTap` callback, so single taps pass
through the zoomable modifier to the outer
Box's tap-detector unchanged. The outer
Box's tap detection covers the loading
spinner and error states (not just the
page-list body), so keeping it as the
single tap source is intentional.

Future polish slice can adjust if pinch-zoom
swallows single-tap-to-toggle in practice
(would route taps through the layout's own
`onTap` parameter); current decision is to
trust the library's gesture disambiguation
and validate at the route-swap (Phase
9.x.routeswap, when the rework Reader
becomes user-facing).

### §67.5 Layout-by-layout placement

| Composable | Modifier site | Why |
|------------|---------------|-----|
| `ReaderHorizontalPager` | `HorizontalPager(modifier = …)` | Pager-level pinch matches legacy `HorizontalReadingMode.kt`. The pager owns viewport; zoom origin is the visible page. |
| `ReaderVerticalPager` | `VerticalPager(modifier = …)` | Same rationale as horizontal pager; pinch at pager-level avoids fighting the pager's vertical-swipe-for-page-change. |
| `ReaderVerticalListBody` | `LazyColumn(modifier = …)` | List-level (not outer Box) so zoom origin is the list contents — same convention as legacy `WebToonReadingMode.kt`. The outer Box's tap-detector for chrome-toggle still receives single taps. |

Three composables × one modifier each = three
modifier additions, all to the existing
outermost layout modifier of each composable.
No new composables, no parameter changes, no
state lifted up or down.

### §67.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- **Gapless `WEBTOON` spacing.** Still
  deferred. `ReaderVerticalList` renders
  `LazyColumn` with default item layout for
  both `WEBTOON` and `CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL`;
  legacy webtoon renders with zero inter-page
  spacing for true vertically-stitched
  reading. Cross-cutting follow-up slice.
- **Mode-toggle scroll-position
  preservation.** See §64.5; still deferred.
- **Zoom-state mode-toggle preservation.**
  Each layout composable owns its own
  `ZoomState` via `rememberZoomState()`. A
  mode switch destroys the old layout's
  composition + its `ZoomState`, so the next
  layout's zoom resets to identity. Legacy
  behaves the same way (each
  reading-mode composable has its own
  `rememberZoomState()`). No change required.
- **`onTap` parameter on `.zoomable`.** The
  library exposes an `onTap: (Offset) -> Unit`
  parameter; this slice doesn't wire it so
  single taps pass through to the outer
  Box's `detectTapGestures` chrome-toggle.
  If validation at Phase 9.x.routeswap finds
  pinch swallowing single taps, the polish
  is a one-line `onTap = { onTap() }` add per
  layout — out of slice today.
- **Double-tap to zoom.** Library supports
  this via `onDoubleTap`. Legacy doesn't
  wire it. Out of slice; out of legacy parity.
- **Phase 9.x.routeswap.** Block-and-ask per

  Reader user-facing despite missing features
  (bookmark / share / gapless-webtoon /
  decoder-hints), which is an observable
  user-behavior change. Owner decision

## §68 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.webtoongap — `LazyColumn` theme background (legacy WebToon parity)

### §68.1 Goal

Close out the §66.6 "Gapless `WEBTOON`
spacing" deferral with a definitive code +
documentation answer: the rework reader is
already gapless on inter-item spacing. The
only true legacy parity item turned out to
be a `.background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)`
modifier painted at the LazyColumn level,
which legacy `WebToonReadingMode.kt` line
134 and `ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt`
line 118 both apply.

### §68.2 The deferral was misidentified

The §66.6 deferral said:

> Legacy renders webtoon panels with zero
> inter-page spacing for true vertically-
> stitched reading; current placeholder uses
> `LazyColumn`'s natural item layout.

That implied `LazyColumn`'s natural item
layout introduces a gap. It doesn't:

- `LazyColumn` with no `verticalArrangement`
  parameter defaults to `Arrangement.Top` —
  zero inter-item spacing.
- `ReaderPageItem`'s default modifier is
  `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` with no `padding`
  applied; `AsyncImage` under
  `ContentScale.FillWidth` produces a
  natural-height item with no margin.
- The rework's `ReaderVerticalListBody`
  doesn't call `.padding` / `spacedBy` /
  any height-affecting modifier between
  items.

So the rework's WEBTOON / CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL
layouts were already gapless when the
deferral was written. The deferral note was
based on a misreading of the layout, not on a
real gap.

### §68.3 What the actual legacy parity item is

Grepping `.background(` across the legacy
reader's reading-mode composables shows:

| Layout | Background paint at LazyColumn/Pager? |
|--------|----------------------------------------|
| `WebToonReadingMode.kt` | ✓ `.background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)` |
| `ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt` | ✓ `.background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)` |
| `VerticalReadingMode.kt` | ✗ (none) |
| `HorizontalReadingMode.kt` | ✗ (none) |

Only the LazyColumn-backed reading modes
paint a theme background; the pagers don't.
That asymmetry follows from the layout's
own behaviour:

- A LazyColumn item is sized to its own
  content (`wrapContentHeight` or natural
  bitmap height) — it can be shorter than
  the viewport. The background paints any
  void below / above an item that the row
  doesn't fill.
- A pager page fills the entire viewport
  (each `Pager` content slot is exactly
  `viewport` × `viewport`). There's no void
  for a background to fill.

### §68.4 Change applied

Single modifier addition on
`ReaderVerticalListBody`'s LazyColumn:

```kotlin
LazyColumn(
    state = listState,
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxSize()
        .zoomable(rememberZoomState())
        .background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background),  // ← new
) { ... }
```

Ordering rationale: `.background` after
`.zoomable` is intentional — the background
paints behind the LazyColumn content, but it
*should not* extend behind the `.zoomable`
gesture handler's transformed area. Putting
`.zoomable` first means the gesture handler
operates on the un-coloured modifier chain
(no perf cost from compositing); putting
`.background` second means the colour layer
sits inside the gesture's frame of reference
(it pans with the content during a zoom).

That ordering also matches legacy
`WebToonReadingMode.kt` (lines 130–134):

```kotlin
.fillMaxSize()
.zoomable(zoomState = rememberZoomState(), onTap = { _ -> onTap() })
.background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)
```

## §69 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.scrollpos — mode-toggle scroll-position preservation

Closes the §64.5 / §65.5 / §66.6 deferral
on mode-toggle scroll-position preservation.
Before this slice, swapping `readingMode`
mid-chapter discarded the old layout's
`LazyListState` / `PagerState` and the new
layout mounted at index 0 — even though the
VM's `currentPageIndex` still carried the
user's real position. This slice threads
`state.currentPageIndex` through the
dispatch composable into each layout's
`remember*State` `initial*` parameter.

### §69.1 Goal

A mode toggle mid-chapter must open the new
layout on the same page the user was just
reading. Improves on legacy, which also
resets to page 0 on mode toggles. Pure
UX upside, no contract change.

### §69.2 Design

Single new `initialPageIndex: Int`
parameter added to four composables in
`ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt`:

| Composable             | New parameter         | Used as                                            |
|------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `ReaderPageLayout`     | `initialPageIndex`    | forwarded to each `when`-arm child                 |
| `ReaderHorizontalPager`| `initialPageIndex`    | `rememberPagerState(initialPage = ...)`            |
| `ReaderVerticalPager`  | `initialPageIndex`    | `rememberPagerState(initialPage = ...)`            |
| `ReaderVerticalList`   | `initialPageIndex`    | `rememberLazyListState(initialFirstVisibleItemIndex = ...)` |

Caller (`ReaderScreenContent`) passes
`state.currentPageIndex`. The dispatch
composable owns the parameter once; each
leaf reads it exactly once.

### §69.3 Why the §64.5 streaming-anchor concern was a non-issue

The original §64.5 deferral note flagged
that the LazyColumn side might need
anchor logic — "which item-index
corresponds to `currentPageIndex` when items
are streaming in?" That concern turned out
to not apply:

- **Reducer-side clamping.** The VM's
  `OnPageChanged` reducer (in
  `:presentation/.../reader/ReaderViewModel`)
  clamps `currentPageIndex` into
  `0..pages.lastIndex` on every update.
  The VM never holds a stale-with-respect-to-
  current-`pages.size` index, so the
  initial value handed to the new layout is
  always a legal index.
- **Streaming is settled by the time
  the user toggles modes.** Mode toggle is
  a deliberate, low-frequency user action
  (top-bar control). By the time the user
  decides to toggle, they've been on the
  page long enough that any streaming-Success
  emissions for already-visible pages have
  long landed. The list isn't actively
  growing under the gesture.
- **The LazyColumn key is the page URL,
  not the index.** Streaming-driven Success
  emissions that append new pages don't
  cause reorderings — they only extend the
  tail. So an item at index N before a
  Success emission is still at index N
  after.

The "anchor" mental model would only matter
if the page list could re-index existing
items (e.g. a re-fetch that returned a
different ordering). The rework's streaming
contract is append-only on URL identity,
so index-based anchors are sufficient.

### §69.4 Why `remember*State`'s `initial*` parameter is safe across recompositions

Both `rememberPagerState` and
`rememberLazyListState` consult their
`initial*` parameters only on the **first**
composition of that composable instance.
Subsequent recompositions return the same
state holder; the live `currentPage` /
`firstVisibleItemIndex` is the source of
truth from then on, and the `initial*`
parameter is ignored.

Practical effect:

- **Mode toggle** creates a fresh composable
  instance (`when` selects a different child)
  → fresh state → `initial*` is honoured →
  layout lands on the user's current page.
- **Same-layout recomposition** (e.g. a new
  page streams in, the VM emits a fresh
  `ReaderState` with a higher `pages.size`)
  → same composable instance → same state
  holder → `initial*` is ignored → live
  scroll position survives untouched.

Inline comments on lines 461–466 (the
LazyColumn) and 547–549 / 597 (the pagers)
document this contract at the leaves so a
future maintainer doesn't try to "fix" the
parameter being seemingly-unused after the
first frame.

    parameters reshuffled — preserves OCP
    on call shape).
  - 1 caller pass-through
    (`state.currentPageIndex →
    ReaderPageLayout`).
  - 3 leaf `rememberPagerState` /
    `rememberLazyListState` calls now consult
    the parameter (`initialPage = ...` /
    `initialFirstVisibleItemIndex = ...`).
  - File-level KDoc and the
    `ReaderPageLayout` KDoc updated:
    the stale §394 "deferred polish: mode-

    reference now points to §69, and the

## §70 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.placeholder — loading + error placeholder reserved height

Closes the §68.8 / §69.8 deferral on
collapse-to-0 during streaming. Before this
slice, the rework's `ReaderPageItem`
rendered a plain `AsyncImage`, which during
the bitmap-in-flight window has intrinsic
size 0 — a streaming LazyColumn item would
collapse to 0 height until the decoded
bitmap landed, then snap to its real
height, visibly jolting the scroll position.
This slice replaces `AsyncImage` with
`SubcomposeAsyncImage` and gives the
`loading` + `error` slots a reserved-height
modifier that mirrors legacy
`WebToonReadingMode.kt` lines 200–211 and
`ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt` lines
200–211.

### §70.1 Goal

A streaming LazyColumn item must occupy
the full viewport height during loading and
error states. Eliminates the visible scroll-
jolt as decoded bitmaps land. Pure UX
polish, no behaviour or state change.

### §70.2 Design

Two parts:

1. **Viewport height harvest.** The Scaffold
   content's outer `Box` was switched to a
   `BoxWithConstraints` so `maxHeight: Dp`
   is available as a local. The local is
   captured as `screenHeightDb` (matching
   legacy naming) and threaded through
   `ReaderPageLayout` to every layout.
2. **`SubcomposeAsyncImage` slots.**
   `ReaderPageItem` switched from `AsyncImage`
   to `SubcomposeAsyncImage`. The `loading`
   slot renders a `CircularProgressIndicator`
   centered in a `Box` modifier-chained
   with `.fillMaxWidth().defaultMinSize(minHeight = screenHeightDb)`.
   The `error` slot renders a centered "Failed
   to load page" `Text` in the same box.

Parameter plumbing matches the §69 scrollpos
pattern — single `Dp` parameter threaded
through the five composables in the layout
family.

### §70.3 Pager vs LazyColumn asymmetry (it's symmetric this time)

Unlike §68 (`background` modifier — applied
only to the LazyColumn because the pagers
already fill viewport with no inter-item
void), `screenHeightDb` is threaded
uniformly through all three layouts. For
the pagers it's a no-op inside the page
because the page's outer modifier
(`Modifier.fillMaxSize()`) already
constrains height to the viewport — but
since `defaultMinSize` only acts when the
parent's min constraint is less than its
argument, a no-op modifier is harmless.
Uniform plumbing keeps `ReaderPageItem`'s
contract single-shape and avoids two
divergent call sites for the same composable.

### §70.4 Files

- `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt`
  - Imports: `+BoxWithConstraints`,
    `+defaultMinSize`, `+Dp`,
    `+SubcomposeAsyncImage`,
    `−AsyncImage`.
  - Outer `Box` → `BoxWithConstraints`;
    `val screenHeightDb = maxHeight` near
    the top of its scope.
  - 5 composable signatures gained
    `screenHeightDb: Dp`: `ReaderPageLayout`,
    `ReaderHorizontalPager`,
    `ReaderVerticalPager`,
    `ReaderVerticalList`,
    `ReaderVerticalListBody`,
    `ReaderPageItem`.
  - `ReaderPageItem` body rewritten:
    `AsyncImage` → `SubcomposeAsyncImage`
    with `loading` + `error` slots that each
    apply `.defaultMinSize(minHeight = screenHeightDb)`.
  - File-level KDoc bullet rewritten —
    the "placeholder ergonomics" gap now
    correctly identifies what *still*
    differs (legacy's download-% indicator).

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid`
  — green (6 s post-cache).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +

## §71 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.pageretry — per-page retry button in error placeholder

Closes the §70.7 retry-button half of the
per-page error placeholder deferral. The
rework's `ReaderPageItem` error slot now
renders a Retry button below the "Failed to
load page" text; tapping it re-issues just
this page's `ImageRequest` via Coil's
`AsyncImagePainter.restart()`. Legacy parity
for three readers
(`WebToonReadingMode.kt` line 211,
`PagerImageItem.kt` line 83,
`ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt` line 212
— all use `onRetry = { painter.restart() }`).

### §71.1 Goal

Recovery from a single-page network blip
without reloading the whole chapter. Before
this slice, the only retry surface was the
top-bar refresh action (chapter-level
`ReaderIntent.OnRetry`), which re-fetches the
entire page list — costly when only one
page failed to decode. Legacy users have a
per-page button; the rework's error
placeholder lacked one until now.

### §71.2 Design

UI-only — no MVI plumbing.

`AsyncImagePainter.restart()` (Coil 3) is
the primitive: it re-issues the painter's
current `ImageRequest` against the singleton
`ImageLoader`. Cache behaviour is governed by
the loader's policy
(memory + disk caches are consulted; a
permanent network failure won't be papered
over by a cached error if the request didn't
write one).

`SubcomposeAsyncImageScope` (the receiver of
the `error` lambda) exposes `painter:
AsyncImagePainter`, so the retry is
accessible without reaching past Coil's
surface. The only wrinkle: the inner `Box` /
`Column` lambdas introduce their own scopes
that *shadow* the outer scope's implicit
receiver, so we capture `painter` to a
local (`val errorPainter = painter`) at the
top of the `error` slot before entering the
nested scopes. Without the capture, the
compiler emits "cannot be called in this
context with an implicit receiver" — caught
on the first build attempt.

The retry button is a plain `Button` (matches
`ReaderErrorPane`'s chapter-level retry
button shape) wrapped in a `Column` with
`Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.md)` between
the "Failed to load page" text and the
button. The whole `Column` is centered
inside the existing reserved-height `Box`
from §70.

### §71.3 Why open-in-WebView half is deferred

Legacy's `ImageLoadError` exposes a second
button: "Open in WebView", which launches a
browser pointed at the chapter URL so the
user can verify the source is up. Three
moving parts the rework doesn't yet have:

1. A new `ReaderEffect` variant —
   `OpenChapterInWebView(url: String)`. The
   current `ReaderEffect` is
   `NavigateBack | ShowError`. The MVI
   contract is a `sealed interface`, so
   adding the variant is additive but
   requires a reducer-side dispatch path.
2. The route adapter
   (`ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute`) needs
   to collect the new effect and route it
   to the platform's intent launcher.
3. The `:platform` facade
   `IntentLauncher.openUrl(url)` is already
   in place
   (`platform/.../intent/IntentLauncher.kt`),
   so the platform side has no work. The
   route adapter needs to inject it.

Net: a 3-file slice across `:presentation` /
`:composeApp` (route adapter) / nothing in
`:ui` proper. Scoped as a separate
auto-continuable micro-slice
(§71.7 carries it forward).

### §71.4 Files

- `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt`
  - `ReaderPageItem`'s `error` slot body
    rewritten from a single `Text` to a
    `Box` containing a `Column` of
    `Text + Button`.
  - Local `val errorPainter = painter`
    captured at the top of the `error`
    lambda so `Button.onClick` (a non-
    composable scope) can call
    `errorPainter.restart()`.
  - Local `val errorSpacing = LocalSpacing.current`
    captured for the `Column`'s
    `Arrangement.spacedBy(errorSpacing.md)`.
  - No new imports — `Button`, `Column`,
    `Arrangement`, `LocalSpacing` are all
    already in scope from prior slices.

### §71.5 Build gates

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` —
  green (combined 39 s on second attempt
  after the implicit-receiver compile error
  was fixed on first attempt by capturing
  `painter` to a local).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +
  `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
  — green (combined 39 s).
- Desktop compile not explicitly re-run;
  `SubcomposeAsyncImageScope.painter` is a
  `commonMain` Coil 3 symbol.
- iOS framework linking + on-device
  verification — Windows-impossible,
  deferred to user's Mac.
- Compile error encountered + fixed during
  the slice: "'val painter:
  AsyncImagePainter' cannot be called in
  this context with an implicit receiver."
  Root cause: nested `BoxScope` / `ColumnScope`
  shadow `SubcomposeAsyncImageScope`'s
  implicit receiver. Fix: capture
  `val errorPainter = painter` at the top
  of the `error` lambda. Logged as a
  reminder for future slices that touch
  Coil's scope-receiver-based slots.

### §71.6 SOLID verdict pointer

`SOLID_AUDIT.md` → "Phase
7.x.reader.modelayout.pageretry" for the
per-file 10-point checklist. The file
passes.

  `ReaderEffect.OpenChapterInWebView(url)`,

  adjacent intent (or a new
  `OnOpenInWebView` intent), and route-
  adapter wiring to the existing
  `IntentLauncher.openUrl`. Auto-continuable
  micro-slice; carried forward from §70.7.~~

  shipped as a 5-file MVI slice: new

  + `ReaderIntent.OnOpenInWebView(url, api)`
  + reducer dispatch + `:ui` Row of two

  (strangler-fig nav target sharing). The
  in-app WebView screen ended up the right

  the in-app browser so the rework matches.
  See §72 for the full slice writeup.
- **Per-page retry analytics / telemetry.**

  (verified via grep — no
  `Analytics.logEvent("page_retry")` or

## §72 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.openwebview — Open-in-WebView button + ReaderEffect routing through MVI

Closes the Open-in-WebView half of the
§70.7 / §71.7 per-page error placeholder
deferral. The rework's `ReaderPageItem`
error slot now renders a `Row` of two
`Button`s: Retry (Coil-level
`AsyncImagePainter.restart()` from §71) and
Open in WebView (new — routes through
strict MVI to the in-app browser at
`Screen.WebView(url, api)`).

Legacy parity for three readers
(`WebToonReadingMode.kt` lines 206–214,
`PagerImageItem.kt`, and
`ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt`) — all
expose the same Retry + Open-in-WebView
button pair via `ImageLoadError`. With this
slice the rework matches.

### §72.1 Goal

Recover from a page that won't decode even
on retry — typical when the source domain
requires a cookie consent flow or a
Cloudflare challenge that Coil's headless
HTTP client can't navigate. The user opens
the chapter URL in the in-app WebView,
solves the challenge, and the next retry
(or the next chapter open) succeeds because
the cookies persisted to the source's
cookie jar.

### §72.2 Design

Strict MVI — additive to the existing
sealed `ReaderEffect` / `ReaderIntent`
contracts.

1. **`:presentation`** adds
   `ReaderEffect.OpenChapterInWebView(url: String, api: String)` and
   `ReaderIntent.OnOpenInWebView(url: String, api: String)`.
   The reducer's `handle(intent)` gains a
   single branch:
   `is ReaderIntent.OnOpenInWebView -> emit(ReaderEffect.OpenChapterInWebView(intent.url, intent.api))`.
   No state mutation — pure side-effect
   dispatch. The page stays in error state
   when the user returns from the WebView;
   that's a Coil cache-policy concern, not
   an MVI one.
2. **`:ui`** adds
   `onOpenInWebView: (url: String, api: String) -> Unit`
   to `ReaderScreen`'s parameter list,
   collects the new effect into that
   callback in the existing `LaunchedEffect`
   that consumes `viewModel.effect`, and
   pre-binds a `() -> Unit` closure at
   `ReaderScreenContent` where `manga` and
   `chapter` are non-null by signature:
   `val openInWebView: () -> Unit = { onIntent(ReaderIntent.OnOpenInWebView(chapter.url, manga.api)) }`.
   The closure threads down through five
   composable layers
   (`ReaderPageLayout` →
   `ReaderHorizontalPager` /
   `ReaderVerticalPager` /
   `ReaderVerticalList` →
   `ReaderVerticalListBody` →
   `ReaderPageItem`).
3. **`:composeApp`** route adapter
   (`ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute`)
   passes `onOpenInWebView = { url, api -> navController.safeNavigate(Screen.WebView(url, api)) }`
   into `ReaderScreen`. Reuses the legacy
   `Screen.WebView` nav target —
   strangler-fig nav target sharing: the
   in-app WebView screen is a stable piece
   of infrastructure that the rework
   reuses without porting. Phase 9.x
   route-swap reconciles ownership of
   `Screen.WebView` if/when the rework
   gains its own WebView composable.

The leaf `ReaderPageItem` swaps the §71
single `Button` in the `error` slot's
`Column` for a `Row` of two `Button`s
(`Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.sm)`,
`verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically`).
Same receiver-shadowing workaround from
§71 (`val errorPainter = painter`)
remains — the new "Open in WebView"
button just calls the threaded
`onOpenInWebView` parameter.

### §72.3 Callback closure pattern — why threaded `() -> Unit`, not `(ReaderIntent) -> Unit`

Three options were on the table for
getting `url + api` from
`ReaderScreenContent` (where `manga` and
`chapter` are non-null parameters) to the
leaf `ReaderPageItem` (which doesn't know
about either):

- **(A)** Add `chapterUrl: String` +
  `sourceApi: String` parameters to every
  layout composable on the path —
  parameter-list pollution; the leaf only
  needs them to call the closure.
- **(B)** Thread
  `onIntent: (ReaderIntent) -> Unit` all
  the way down — leaks the MVI Intent
  type into leaf composables that
  otherwise stay framework-agnostic.
  Violates ISP for the leaf (it gets a
  fat callback when it only needs the
  one).
- **(C)** Pre-bind a `() -> Unit` closure
  at `ReaderScreenContent` (where `manga`
  + `chapter` are in scope by signature)
  and thread the bound closure down —
  the leaf receives a parameterless
  callback. Closure captures handle the
  `manga.api` + `chapter.url` bind.

Chose (C). Matches legacy's posture (the
legacy `ImageLoadError` parameter is also
a parameterless `onOpenInWebView: () -> Unit`
— legacy `ReadingMode`s pre-bind the
URL+api at the same level the rework
does, see
`composeApp/.../reader/ui/reading_modes/WebToonReadingMode.kt`
line 211). The leaf composable stays
agnostic to where the WebView lives.

### §72.4 Files

5 files (at the per-commit cap), single
commit because exhaustive-`when` on the
sealed `ReaderEffect` forced
contract + consumer to land together
(see §72.5):

- `presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderEffect.kt`
  - New variant
    `data class OpenChapterInWebView(val url: String, val api: String) : ReaderEffect`.
  - 17-line KDoc on the variant explains
    legacy parity, why effect (not direct
    nav from the VM), why `(url, api)` (not
    just `url`).
- `presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderIntent.kt`
  - New variant
    `data class OnOpenInWebView(val url: String, val api: String) : ReaderIntent`.
  - 15-line KDoc explains MVI routing
    rationale vs §71's UI-only Retry.
- `presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderViewModel.kt`
  - Reducer's `handle(intent)` gains the
    single branch
    `is ReaderIntent.OnOpenInWebView -> emit(ReaderEffect.OpenChapterInWebView(intent.url, intent.api))`.
    No state mutation, no fetch trigger,
    no concurrency concerns — pure
    intent-to-effect translation.
- `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt`
  - New import
    `me.manga.kira.navigation.safeNavigate`.
  - New parameter passed to `ReaderScreen`:
    `onOpenInWebView = { url, api -> navController.safeNavigate(Screen.WebView(url, api)) }`.
  - 9-line KDoc on the lambda documents
    strangler-fig nav target sharing.
- `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt`
  - New import
    `androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row`.
  - New parameter
    `onOpenInWebView: (url: String, api: String) -> Unit`
    on `ReaderScreen` (the public entry
    point) and `ReaderScreenContent`.
  - Effect-collector `when` gains
    `is ReaderEffect.OpenChapterInWebView -> onOpenInWebView(effect.url, effect.api)`.
  - Pre-bound closure at
    `ReaderScreenContent`:
    `val openInWebView: () -> Unit = { onIntent(ReaderIntent.OnOpenInWebView(chapter.url, manga.api)) }`.
  - Five layout composable signatures
    gain `onOpenInWebView: () -> Unit`
    (`ReaderPageLayout`,
    `ReaderHorizontalPager`,
    `ReaderVerticalPager`,
    `ReaderVerticalList`,
    `ReaderVerticalListBody`,
    `ReaderPageItem`).
  - `error` slot's single `Button` becomes
    a `Row { Button(Retry); Button(Open in WebView) }`.
    Same `Arrangement.spacedBy(errorSpacing.sm)`
    pattern as the chapter-level
    `ReaderErrorPane`.

### §72.5 Build gates

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` —
  green (combined 32 s on the final
  attempt).
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` +
  `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64`
  — green (combined 32 s).
- Desktop compile not explicitly re-run;
  all symbols touched are `commonMain`.
- iOS framework linking + on-device
  verification — Windows-impossible,
  deferred to user's Mac.
- Compile error encountered + resolution
  during the slice: first staging
  attempted to land the `:presentation`
  contract files in one commit and the
  `:ui` consumer in a second commit; the
  first commit failed `compileDebugKotlinAndroid`
  with "'when' expression must be
  exhaustive. Add the 'is OpenChapterInWebView'
  branch or an 'else' branch." Root
  cause: the strict-MVI sealed interface
  `ReaderEffect` makes the
  effect-collector `when` exhaustive,
  so adding a variant in `:presentation`

  combine contract + consumer into one
  5-file commit (at the per-commit cap).
  Logged as a SOLID-friendly side effect:
  the exhaustive-`when` is the OCP
  compile-time guard catching us — it
  worked exactly as intended.

  Legacy users come back to the page
  still in error state and tap Retry
  themselves. Rework matches. An

  which the cross-platform shim doesn't

- **Telemetry on Open-in-WebView taps.**
  Legacy doesn't log this event (verified
  via grep — no
  `Analytics.logEvent("open_in_webview")`
  in `composeApp/.../reading_modes/`).
  Rework matches.
- **Progress-percentage indicator on the
  loading placeholder.** Still deferred
  per §70.7 — needs `ProgressManager`-
  equivalent in `:platform`.
- **Next-chapter inline-loading background.**
  Still deferred per §70.7.
- **Per-source `DEFAULT` resolution.**
  Still pending sources-metadata story
  (§64 / §66).
- **Bookmark / share / settings actions.**
  Block-and-ask on chapter-identity strategy
  (Task #217).
- **`onTap` on `.zoomable`.** Pinch vs tap

  currently reuses the legacy `Screen.WebView`
  nav target during the strangler-fig

  either gets ported or stays as shared
