## §73 Phase 7.x.reader.next — multi-chapter navigation (Prev / Next chapter)

Reader top bar gains two new affordances —
`‹` Prev chapter and `›` Next chapter —
backed by `ListChaptersUseCase`,
`ReaderState.chapters`, two new sealed
`ReaderIntent` cases (`OnNextChapter`,
`OnPrevChapter`), and an in-place state
mutation strategy that reuses the existing
`onEnter` reducer path. Legacy parity with
the in-app reader's chapter-stepper:
`goToNextChapter` / `goToPreviousChapter`
in `shared/.../reader/ui/viewmodel/ReaderViewModel.kt`
lines 480 / 515.

### §73.1 Goal

Close the "no next / previous chapter
within the Reader" gap that has stood
since Phase 7.x.reader landed the
single-chapter shell (§59). The rework
reader previously required the user to
back out to Details, scroll the chapter
list, and tap a different chapter — three
taps for what should be one.

### §73.2 Design — in-place state mutation, not pop+push

Two nav strategies were on the table:

- **(A) pop+push.** Each Next / Prev pops
  the current `Screen.ChapterImagesRework`
  off the back stack and pushes a fresh
  one with the new chapter args. The VM is
  recreated; the chapter list refetches
  for each chapter; pop+push animation
  flashes between chapters.
- **(B) in-place state mutation.** Next /
  Prev dispatches `OnNextChapter` /
  `OnPrevChapter` intents to the same VM
  instance, which routes through the
  existing `onEnter` reducer path. No nav
  destination change; the chapter list
  stays populated across intra-manga
  navigation; no animation flicker.

Picked (B). Rationale:
- **Matches legacy posture.** Legacy
  reader's `goToNextChapter` mutates a
  `currentChapterIndex` StateFlow in place
  on the same VM. The rework can do the
  same with less ceremony.
- **No new `ReaderEffect`.** A pop+push
  approach would need
  `ReaderEffect.NavigateToChapter` plus
  route-adapter consumption; in-place
  needs neither.
- **Chapter list cached.** Same-manga
  intra-chapter nav reuses
  `state.chapters` — only the page fetch
  is re-issued. Pop+push would refetch
  the chapter list per chapter (the new
  VM has no in-memory state).
- **UX.** No nav flicker; the top bar's
  reading-mode picker selection and the
  `isUiVisible` toggle survive
  intra-chapter nav (modulo `isUiVisible`
  which we explicitly reset to `true` on
  every `onEnter` per legacy parity).

### §73.3 Design — `ListChaptersUseCase` reuses `MangaDetailsRepository`

Two repository strategies were on the
table:

- **(A) new `ChaptersRepository`** with a
  `fun list(manga: Manga): AppResult<List<Chapter>>`
  method that calls the source.
- **(B) reuse `MangaDetailsRepository`**
  and project `MangaDetails.chapters`.

Picked (B). Rationale:
- **Legacy has one endpoint.**
  `BaseMangaRepository.fetchMangaChaptersF(url)`
  returns a `MangaInfo` containing both
  metadata and chapters. There is no
  "chapters-only" endpoint on the source
  contract.
- **(A) would either duplicate the fetch
  or delegate.** A standalone
  `ChaptersRepository.list` impl would
  either call the same legacy method
  (duplicating
  `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl`'s fetch
  logic) or delegate to the existing
  `MangaDetailsRepository` (at which point
  the new interface is dead weight).
- **Projection is presentation-friendly.**
  `ListChaptersUseCase` extracts just
  `chapters` from the `AppResult<MangaDetails>`
  so the Reader VM gets
  `AppResult<List<Chapter>>` directly —
  no field-by-field threading of
  `MangaDetails` through state for one
  field.
- **SRP contract §6 single source of
  truth.** `MangaDetails.chapters` is the
  source of truth for the chapter list;
  Reader's chapter list IS Details'
  chapter list. No field-by-field
  divergence to manage.

Cost: each first OnEnter per manga
refetches the full `MangaDetails` (cover /
genres / description / chapters). The
description and friends are discarded by
the use case projection. Acceptable
because the Reader VM caches
`state.chapters` after the first
successful fetch — subsequent intra-manga
Next / Prev does NOT re-invoke the use
case (preserved by the `mangaChanged`
branch in `onEnter`).

### §73.4 Design — fire-and-forget `runFetch` with tracked `Job`

Pre-this-slice, `runFetch` was a `suspend
fun` that the reducer awaited inline. For
streaming sources (Prochan) the flow never
completes until cancellation, so `onEnter`
parked on the collector indefinitely. This
was fine when each OnEnter created a new
VM (route-level nav). With in-place Next /
Prev, a new OnEnter on the same VM would
launch a SECOND collector in parallel with
the first — `MviViewModel.submit()` runs
each intent in its own
`viewModelScope.launch`, so the prior
intent's coroutine is still alive when the
next one starts.

Two concurrent collectors race on
`updateState`. The OLD chapter's emissions
(still flowing from the streaming source)
would overwrite the NEW chapter's pages
after the new fetch's first emission
lands.

Fix: `runFetch` becomes a non-suspend
`fun` that launches the collector in a
tracked `fetchJob: Job?`. The first line
of `runFetch` cancels the prior job before
starting the new one. Same pattern
applied to `runListChapters` /
`chaptersJob` so a slow chapter-list
fetch for the previous manga can't land
on the new manga's state.

Side benefit: `onEnter` no longer parks
on the collector, so the StateFlow reader
sees `isLoading = true` immediately after
the `updateState` call (before the first
flow emission lands). This shifts
`isLoading` from "synchronized with the
fetch's first emission" to "synchronized
with the intent dispatch" — closer to the
user's mental model.

### §73.5 Design — chapter-list failure is silent

The page fetch and the chapter-list fetch
are independent: a page fetch can succeed
while the chapter list fails (and vice
versa). Surfacing chapter-list failure as
a `ReaderEffect.ShowError` snackbar would
mask a successfully-rendered page —
strictly worse UX than silent disablement.

So `runListChapters` swallows
`AppResult.Failure` without emitting an
effect. The Next / Prev buttons stay
disabled (via
`state.canGoPrev` / `state.canGoNext`,
which evaluate to `false` when
`chapters.isEmpty()`), and the user can
back out to Details and retry there if
they need the chapter list. The page
fetch's error path (separate, MVI-routed)
is unchanged.

### §73.6 Files

foundation + VM consumption):
- `domain/.../domain/usecase/reader/ListChaptersUseCase.kt` (new)
- `presentation/.../presentation/reader/ReaderState.kt` (modified — adds `chapters` + convenience props)
- `presentation/.../presentation/reader/ReaderIntent.kt` (modified — adds `OnNextChapter` / `OnPrevChapter`)
- `presentation/.../presentation/reader/ReaderViewModel.kt` (modified — injects `ListChaptersUseCase`, fire-and-forget `runFetch` / `runListChapters`, Next / Prev handlers, KDoc)
- `composeApp/.../di/ReaderReworkModule.kt` (modified — adds factory + VM 4-arg)

UI commit (`f3682bb`, 1 file):

### §73.8 SOLID

Full 10-point checklist per touched file
in `SOLID_AUDIT.md` "Phase 7.x.reader.next"
entry. Highlights:
- **SRP** — `ListChaptersUseCase` projects
  ONE field; `ReaderViewModel` gains TWO
  intent branches that delegate to the
  existing `onEnter`.
- **OCP** — `ReaderIntent` sealed
  hierarchy extended by data objects, no
  existing branches modified.
- **LSP** — N/A (no inheritance changes).
- **ISP** — `ReaderTopBar` gains 4 params

  no fat-interface widening.

  constructor takes the `MangaDetailsRepository`

### §73.9 What this slice deliberately defers

- ~~**Chapter-position label in the top bar
  ("23 / 156").** Legacy reader shows the
  position. Rework defers — a pure
  presentation polish that doesn't gate
  navigation.~~ **Retired by §74** —
  Phase 7.x.reader.pageindicator landed
  the label between the Prev / Next
  chevrons in `ReaderTopBar`.
- **Long-press / hold-to-jump-N-chapters.**
  Legacy doesn't have it; not needed for
  parity.
- **Preserve `currentPageIndex` on
  intra-chapter nav.** Currently the
  reducer resets `currentPageIndex = 0`
  on every `onEnter` (since pages are
  reset, the index has no meaning yet).
  This matches the user-tested legacy
  behaviour — the new chapter opens at
  page 1.
- **Pre-fetching the next chapter's pages
  in the background.** Legacy reader has
  a multi-chapter feed that pre-loads
  N+1 / N-1 pages while reading. Rework
  defers — that's the `FetchChapterFeedUseCase`
  +
  `loadedChapterIndexes` / `allReaderItems`
  state shape from the legacy VM's
  multi-chapter slice, NOT this slice.
  See `ReaderState` KDoc "Deferred state
  fields" bullet on `loadedChapterIndexes`.
- **Chapter-bookmark / progress-percentage
  indicators on Next / Prev chevrons.**
  Need bookmark slice (Task #217 — still
  block-and-asked on chapter-identity).
- **Per-source-specific Next / Prev
  ordering.** Some sources (rare) list
  chapters in the wrong order. Legacy
  uses the source's natural order;
  rework matches. A future polish slice
  could expose an "Invert order" toggle —
  not in scope here.

## §74 Phase 7.x.reader.pageindicator — chapter-position label in top bar

Closes the §73.9 deferral. The
`ReaderTopBar` now shows a 1-based "N /
total" text label between the Prev and
Next chevrons (e.g. "23 / 156"). Pure
presentation polish — no MVI surface
change, no VM change, no new effect; the
data was already plumbed by Phase
7.x.reader.next via
`ReaderState.currentChapterIndex` +
`ReaderState.chapters.size`.

### §74.1 Goal

Surface visual feedback for "where I am
in the chapter list" right next to the
Next / Prev chevrons. The user clicks
Next without knowing whether they're at
chapter 1, chapter 50, or the end — the
chevrons disable at the ends (via the
§73-shipped `canGo*` flags) but the
position itself is invisible. Legacy
reader shows the same label in the same
place.

### §74.2 Design — render inline between the chevrons, not as a dedicated `Box`

Two layout strategies were on the table:

- **(A) Wrap Prev + label + Next in a
  `Row` inside `actions`.** Forces the
  three elements to align as a tight
  group; gives explicit control over the
  spacing between them; matches the
  legacy reader's pill-style
  presentation.
- **(B) Inline the label between the
  chevrons.** Lets the `TopAppBar`'s
  `actions` slot's own `Row` (the
  Material3 default) lay them out with
  the standard `8.dp` action-spacing.
  No new `Row`; no new modifier;
  one fewer composable in the tree.

Picked (B). Rationale:
- Material3's `TopAppBar.actions` is
  itself a `Row` with `Arrangement.End`,
  so inlining is the same shape with
  one less wrapper.
- The label fits naturally as a sibling
  `Text` — `IconButton` parents already
  pad their children, the label gets
  its baseline-aligned look for free.
- Spacing matches the existing back ←
  / overflow ⋯ pattern in the same
  file (no bespoke spacing values).
- Future variant (e.g. icon swap or
  badge) can replace just the `Text`
  without touching the chevrons —
  open to refinement.

### §74.3 Design — conditional render, not always-visible with sentinel text

Two visibility strategies:

- **(A) Always render** with a
  `chaptersCount > 0` guard inside the
  `Text` itself (e.g. show "—" or "?"
  when the list is unloaded).
- **(B) Conditional render** with an
  `if (chaptersCount > 0 &&
  currentChapterIndex >= 0)` block —
  no sentinel text, the label simply
  disappears.

Picked (B). Rationale:
- Mirrors the Prev / Next chevrons'
  `canGo*` disabled posture for the
  same window. The user sees the
  whole nav cluster fade in together
  once the list lands rather than a
  half-state ("—" with a disabled
  chevron) that invites questions.
- Defensive guard on
  `currentChapterIndex >= 0` covers
  the rare "chapter not in list"
  case (e.g. source returns an
  inconsistent URL between Details
  and Reader). The chevron `canGo*`
  flags evaluate to `false` in this
  case too; consistent posture.
- The `TopAppBar.actions` `Row`'s
  `Arrangement.End` automatically
  reflows when the label disappears
  — no layout flicker.

### §74.7 What this slice deliberately defers

## §75 — Phase 6.4.x.statistics: reading-session timer port

### §75.1 Goal

Close the load-bearing "the user's
read-minutes total stops growing while
they use the rework Reader" gap. Legacy
`ReaderViewModel.onScreenResume()` and
`onScreenPause()` bracket a session via
`StatisticsRepository.startReadingSession`
/ `endReadingSession`; the elapsed
minutes accumulate into a single on-disk
counter (`StorageKeys.READ_MINUTES`)
that the Statistics screen reads.
Without this slice, time spent in the
rework Reader is invisible to those
totals, so any user who already uses
the (debug-route-gated) rework Reader
sees their lifetime-read-minutes
counter freeze.

### §75.2 Design — strangler-fig delegate, not a parallel persistence path

Two ways to land the session timer:

- **(A) Port the legacy persistence
  graph.** Move `sessionStartMillis`
  into a new rework state holder,
  write to a new on-disk key (or
  factor out a shared `:platform`
  facade over `DataStoreHelper.addReadMinutes`).
- **(B) Strangler-fig delegate.**
  Define a new `:domain`
  `ReadingSessionRepository` with two
  verbs (`begin` / `end`); the `:data`
  impl forwards both calls verbatim to
  the legacy `:shared`
  `StatisticsRepository` (which is
  already bound as a Koin `single`).
  Both the legacy and the rework
  Reader call the same legacy
  singleton; both contribute to the
  same on-disk counter.

Picked (B). Rationale:
- **Crossover correctness.** The user's
  read-minutes total must remain
  monotonic across the strangler-fig
  transition. If (A) wrote to a new
  on-disk cell, the user's lifetime
  total would visibly drop the moment
  the rework Reader took over the
  route (Phase 9.x) — every minute
  written under the old key would
  vanish from the new key's
  perspective. (B) keeps a single
  source of truth.
- **Layer discipline.** The `:data`
  impl reaches into `:shared` exactly
  the way `ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl`
  already reaches into
  `SourcesRepository` and the way the
  Details slice's repository reaches
  into legacy fetchers — the same
  pattern, not a new one.
- **Retire path is obvious.** Phase
  9.x flips the user-facing route to
  the rework Reader; the legacy
  `StatisticsRepository.startReadingSession`
  / `endReadingSession` methods can be
  deleted at that point (or kept as a
  thin alias). The
  `ReadingSessionRepository` interface
  in `:domain` doesn't change either
  way.

### §75.3 Design — DisposableEffect(Unit), not LaunchedEffect, not keyed on (manga, chapter)

Three lifecycle hooks were on the
table:

- **(A) `LaunchedEffect(Unit)`**:
  enters once, but no exit hook —
  pause never fires.
- **(B) `LaunchedEffect(manga.api,
  manga.language, manga.title,
  chapter.url)`**: re-keyed on the
  same four-tuple `OnEnter` uses. An
  intra-manga Next / Prev would
  re-key, restarting the timer
  mid-session — double-billing the
  user's minutes.
- **(C) `DisposableEffect(Unit)`** with
  enter dispatching `OnScreenResumed`
  and `onDispose` dispatching
  `OnScreenPaused`.

Picked (C). Rationale:
- `onDispose` is the only Compose
  primitive that **always** fires on
  composition tear-down — including
  the path where Compose tears the
  composition down before the host
  reaches its resumed state. That
  path is exactly where the
  `StatisticsRepository.end`
  no-op-on-no-session guard becomes
  load-bearing.
- The session must span the WHOLE
  Reader visit, not a single chapter.
  Keying on `Unit` (not on chapter)
  means intra-manga Next / Prev is
  one continuous session — same
  posture as legacy
  `ReaderActivity.onResume/onPause`,
  same posture as a user who reads
  ten chapters in a row sees one
  contiguous minute-count.

### §75.6 SOLID

Full 10-point checklist for each
touched file in `SOLID_AUDIT.md`
"Phase 6.4.x.statistics" entry.
Highlights:
- **SRP** — each new file owns ONE rule.
  Interface: "bracket a session";
  use cases: "delegate to repository";
  impl: "delegate to legacy
  StatisticsRepository"; module: "Koin
  bindings"; VM branches: "route the
  two new intents". No file gains a
  second responsibility.
- **OCP** — `ReaderIntent` sealed
  hierarchy extended additively
  (two `data object`s); reducer's
  exhaustive-`when` catches the
  extension at compile time.
- **ISP** — both intents are payload-
  free `data object`s. The
  repository interface is two
  methods (the minimum to bracket).
  The two use cases are
  single-method classes. No
  fat-interface anywhere.
- **DIP** — the VM depends on the use
  cases; the use cases depend on the
  `:domain` interface; the `:data`
  impl depends on the legacy `:shared`
  type (strangler-fig boundary,
  documented). Koin binds the impl at
  the composition root. The UI's
  `DisposableEffect` dispatches via
  the `(ReaderIntent) -> Unit` lambda
  it already received from
  `ReaderScreen` — no new dependency
  on the VM.

- **Per-chapter session minutes.**
  Legacy bracket-once-per-screen is
  preserved; per-chapter granularity
  isn't visible in the Statistics

- **Resume-on-last-page persistence.**
  `OnPageChanged` already updates

  `ReadProgressRepository` or an

- **Total-time HUD in the Reader.**
  Some readers show "you've been

  rework has no consumer for the

  later means adding a `Flow<Long>`
  to the repository interface — an
  additive extension, no
  compatibility-breaking change.
- **Read-streak / daily-target
  tracking.** Belongs in a future
  Statistics-screen rework, not in
  the Reader's bracket pair.
- **Disable timer on long pauses
  (e.g. >5 minutes idle).** Legacy
  doesn't do this either — out of
  scope.

## §76 — Phase 7.x.reader.resumeposition: per-chapter last-read-page persistence

### §76.1 Goal

Land a UX the legacy reader never
delivered: when the user closes the
rework Reader mid-chapter, the page
they were on should be restored on
re-entry. Today the rework starts
every chapter at page 0; for any
chapter the user opens twice within
a session, they have to manually
re-find their place.

### §76.2 Design — net-new persistence, not strangler-fig

Two ways to land a resume-position
slice:

- **(A) Populate the legacy on-disk
  cell.** `HistoryItemD.lastReadPage`
  is a Room column on the existing
  `history_items` table; a
  strangler-fig `:data` impl could
  reach into the legacy
  `HistoryRepository` (mirrors
  Phase 6.4.x.statistics' delegation
  over `StatisticsRepository`) and
  start writing real page indices
  there.
- **(B) Fresh ObservableSettings
  cell.** Skip the legacy Room graph
  entirely; write a new key under
  the platform's settings store.

Picked (B). Rationale:

- **The legacy column is dead-write.**
  Every legacy call site of
  `HistoryViewModel.updateHistoryItem`
  passes `lastReadPage = 0` — the
  field exists in the schema but
  the legacy reader never populates
  it with a real page index, and
  never reads it back. So unlike
  the statistics slice, there is
  **no on-disk state to preserve**:
  no risk of user-visible value
  loss at the Phase 9.x route swap,
  no crossover-correctness
  requirement.
- **Layer cleanliness.** (A) would
  pull the rework `:data` layer
  into a dependency on the legacy
  `:shared` `HistoryRepository`
  AND the Room DAO. Phase 6.4.x.
  statistics had to accept that
  coupling because the legacy
  store was live; here, the same
  coupling buys nothing.
- **Per-chapter granularity for
  free.** `HistoryItemD` is keyed
  by `mangaUrl` (one row per
  manga), so its `lastReadPage`
  semantic would be "last position
  of most recently opened chapter
  in this manga" — losing the
  prior chapter's position whenever
  the user opens a different one.
  A fresh ObservableSettings cell
  keyed per chapter URL gives
  per-chapter granularity at no
  extra cost.
- **Same template as
  Phase 6.4.x.mode.** Both slices
  wrap `ObservableSettings`. Same
  factory Koin binding, same
  `:data` `single`, same `:domain`
  interface shape. Less context
  to learn, less surface to
  maintain.

### §76.3 Design — storage layout (hash key + URL collision guard)

The naive design — `putInt(
"reader.last_page.${chapter.url}",
pageIndex)` — fails on Desktop:
multiplatform-settings's
`PreferencesSettings` wraps
`java.util.prefs.Preferences`,
whose `MAX_KEY_LENGTH` is 80 chars.
Real chapter URLs routinely exceed
that (100-200+ characters for typical
sources).

The impl derives a bounded-length
key from the URL:
`"reader.last_page." +
chapter.url.hashCode().toUInt()
.toString(36)` — a 17-char prefix
plus a 1-7 char alphanumeric suffix,
total ≤ 24 chars, well under the
Desktop limit. Same shape on every
platform (no per-target branching).

`String.hashCode` is not injective.
A naive `putInt(hashedKey, pageIndex)`
would silently restore the wrong
chapter's page on a collision. To
guard, the impl stores a `String`
value of the form
`"${chapterUrl}|${pageIndex}"` under
the hashed key. On [load], the impl
splits on `|`, verifies the stored
URL matches the requested URL, and
returns `null` on mismatch —
converting what would be a
wrong-page-bug into a "start at
page 0" graceful fallback (the
caller's existing null-handling
path).

Separator choice: literal `|`.
Chapter URLs are HTTP(S) URLs per
RFC 3986; `|` is not a valid URL
character, sources URL-encode it
as `%7C` if it appears, so the
separator is reversible.

### §76.4 Design — VM consumption (suspend cascade through `onEnter`)

The current rework `ReaderViewModel`:

- `onEnter(manga, chapter)` was a
  regular `fun`. The new resume-load
  needs to call the suspend
  `loadPagePosition(chapter.url)`
  before the `updateState` block so
  the new chapter's state lands
  with the saved page in one atomic
  transition.
- Pattern: make `onEnter` suspend.
  The call site is the suspend
  `handle` function — no cascade
  beyond `handle` since `onEnter`
  is private. Two intra-VM callers
  (`onNextChapter`, `onPrevChapter`)
  also become suspend; same suspend
  reach since they were already in
  the suspend handle context.
- Why not launch a separate
  coroutine: the load happens once
  per chapter entry, on a
  ms-bounded ObservableSettings
  read. Splitting it into a
  coroutine would split the
  `updateState` into a multi-step
  transition where readers could
  see a "loading old chapter" then
  "seed new page" — defeats the
  atomic state-update contract.

The save side is fire-and-forget:

- `onPageChanged` already clamps
  the page index and short-circuits
  on no-op changes. After the
  `updateState`, the reducer
  launches
  `viewModelScope.launch {
  savePagePosition(chapterUrl,
  clamped) }` — write must not
  block the reducer (every page
  swipe would otherwise pay the
  settings I/O cost), and there's
  no UI surface to expose a write
  failure even if one happened
  (see the repository's
  no-`AppResult` rationale).
- The chapter URL is captured at
  reducer time (not at the
  launched-coroutine's resume),
  so a fast Next/Prev that
  follows a page-change still
  writes against the right
  chapter — the launched
  coroutine carries the captured
  `chapterUrl` value, not the
  evolving `state.chapter`.

### §76.5 Design — bounds clamping (no extra check needed)

Edge case: chapter shrinks on a
re-publish, the saved page index
is past `pages.lastIndex` on
re-entry. Handled by the existing
`runFetch` Success branch:

```kotlin
val nextIndex = when {
    pages.isEmpty() -> 0
    else -> prev.currentPageIndex
        .coerceIn(0, pages.lastIndex)
}
```

The saved seed lands in
`currentPageIndex` before the page
list arrives; when pages finally
land, the existing clamp pulls it
into range. No extra bounds check
in `LoadPagePositionUseCase` or
the repo — clean separation.

### §76.9 Deliberate deferrals

- **No UI surface to clear saved
  positions.** Intentional — kept
  the slice focused on the resume
  happy-path. A future Settings
  screen "Clear reading history"
  toggle could call a new
  `ClearAllProgressUseCase` if
  needed.
- **No incognito-mode parity.**
  Legacy `HistoryViewModel.update
  HistoryItem` short-circuits
  when incognito is enabled; the
  rework's `savePagePosition`
  currently always writes. The
  incognito-mode use case isn't
  ported yet to the rework's
  `:domain`; once it lands, the
  `onPageChanged` save can guard
  on it. Out of scope for this
  slice.
- **No cleanup of stale entries.**
  Settings can grow unbounded
  over many chapters (each gets
  a 24-char key + a ~150-char
  value). For practical reader
  usage (hundreds of chapters)
  this is well within platform
  limits; cleanup could be a
  future slice if telemetry shows
  the Settings dictionary growing
  unreasonably.
- **No streaming observation
  (Flow shape).** The Reader is
  the only producer of these
  values; there's no out-of-band
  editor to observe. Two
  single-shot suspend methods
  are the minimal sufficient
  surface.
- **No telemetry of resume
  events.** Could surface
  "resumed at page N of M" in
  the Statistics view, but the
  Statistics view is itself
  unported and the data is
  inherently sensitive (per-
  manga reading patterns) —
  deferred until the Statistics
  rework slice considers what
  to expose.

## §77 — Phase 7.x.reader.pagecounthud: page X/Y label in top bar

### §77.1 Goal

Pair the §74 chapter-position
label with a parallel page-position
label so a user scanning the top
bar sees BOTH dimensions of
progress (chapter N of M, page
X of Y) in one place. The bottom
HUD pill (Phase 7.x.reader.chrome,
task #218) has shown page X/Y
since the early Reader slice but
only as a bottom-center overlay;
this slice surfaces the same
information alongside the chapter
indicator in the chrome.

### §77.2 Design — additive companion (top bar) + retain bottom HUD

Two ways to land it:

- **(A) Move page X/Y from the
  bottom HUD to the top bar.**
  Consolidates progress in one
  place, less visual noise.
  Removes the bottom HUD pill
  entirely.
- **(B) Add a compact label to
  the top bar; keep the bottom
  HUD pill.** Two indicators,
  same info, different surfaces.

Picked (B). Rationale:

- **Behaviour preservation.**
  The bottom HUD pill has been
  the Reader's progress
  indicator since the chrome
  slice. Removing it counts as
  Rule 8(b) "refactor would
  change observable behavior" —
  block-and-ask. Adding a
  companion in the top bar is a
  purely additive UX win.
- **Surface complementarity.**
  The bottom HUD is positioned
  near the gesture surface
  (users' fingers, while
  reading). The top-bar label
  is positioned near the
  chapter affordances (Prev /
  Next chevrons). Different
  ergonomics for different
  reading postures.
- **Cost is symmetric.** Both
  fade together via the
  `state.isUiVisible` gate
  (top bar wraps in the outer
  AnimatedVisibility around
  ReaderTopBar; HUD has its
  own AnimatedVisibility keyed
  off the same flag). When the
  user taps to hide chrome,
  both disappear — no surface
  for "two indicators clutter
  the screen" complaint
  outside of chrome-visible
  mode.

### §77.3 Design — positional grouping

The actions row reads:

```
‹  chapter N / M  ›  page X / Y  ⋯
```

The chapter-position label sits
BETWEEN Prev / Next chevrons —
chapter affordances cluster
around the chevrons. The new
page-count label follows
AFTER the Next chevron so it
reads as a separate group:
chapter group, then page group,
then overflow.

Alternative: putting the
page-count label IMMEDIATELY
after the chapter-position
label between the chevrons
would visually compact both
into one group but loses the
two-group reading; rejected
for clarity.

### §77.4 Files

Single source commit (`9cdc71c`,
1 file):

- `ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt`
  (modified) — Two new
  ReaderTopBar params:
  `currentPageIndex: Int`,
  `pagesCount: Int`. Three new
  lines at the call site
  (`currentPageIndex =
  state.currentPageIndex`,
  `pagesCount =
  state.pages.size`). A new
  conditional `Text` after the
  Next chevron in the actions
  block, gated on `pagesCount
  > 0`. 12-line inline comment
  documents the parallel with
  the §74 chapter-position
  label, the gate semantics,
  the deliberate retention of
  the bottom HUD pill, and
  the shared isUiVisible fade.

### §77.5 Build gates

The single source commit gated
through the standard trio:

  Android` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIos
  Arm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIos
  SimulatorArm64` — BUILD
  SUCCESSFUL.

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` entry
"Phase 7.x.reader.pagecounthud
— page X/Y label in top bar"
for the full 10-point checklist
across the single touched file.

### §77.7 Deliberate deferrals

- **No HUD vs top-bar mode
  picker.** Some users may
  prefer one or the other; a
  settings toggle could surface
  this. Out of scope — kept
  the slice focused.
- **No page-scrubber slider.**
  A horizontal slider to drag
  through pages would be a
  natural next slice — single-

  here for the auto-continue
  Next-recommended block.
- **No icon for the kebab

  needs an icon-system slice
  of its own).

## §78 Phase 7.x.reader.pagescrubber — horizontal slider for jump-to-page

Closes the page-scrubber
deferral from §77.7 with a
single-file `:ui` slice.

### §78.1 Goal

Give the user a horizontal
slider at the bottom of the
Reader screen so they can drag
to jump to any page in the
current chapter. The slider
sits below the bottom HUD pill,
inside the same `isUiVisible`
chrome gate — both fade
together when the user taps to
hide chrome.

The slider IS a real jump-to-
page affordance, not a read-
only progress indicator —
dragging actually moves the
layout to the target page in
all four layout shapes
(vertical-list webtoon, paged
vertical, paged horizontal
RTL, paged horizontal LTR).

### §78.2 Design — MVI re-use

The scrubber dispatches the
SAME `ReaderIntent.OnPageChanged
(Int)` that the layout's own
`snapshotFlow`-driven scroll
effects already emit. No new
MVI surface:

- No `OnScrubToPage` intent.
- No `ReaderEffect.ScrollToPage`
  effect.
- No new use case.
- No new `:domain` type.

The VM's reducer is identity-
drop on duplicate page indices,
so the scrubber's potentially
high-frequency drag tick stream
is absorbed cheaply. From the
VM's perspective the scrubber
is indistinguishable from
organic scrolling — both arrive
as `OnPageChanged(Int)` and
update the same
`state.currentPageIndex`.

This MVI re-use posture
mirrors the earlier slices in
this phase (§70 `OnRetry`
reuse for per-page Coil retry,
§75 `OnPageChanged` reuse for
the pagecounthud label).

### §78.3 Design — closing the layout loop

The harder design question:
how does the scrubber's drag
actually move the LazyColumn
/ Pager? Layouts currently
DRIVE `currentPageIndex`
(scroll → snapshotFlow →
OnPageChanged → VM state).
They don't REACT to
`currentPageIndex` changes
from other sources.

The chosen fix: each layout
composable
(`ReaderVerticalList`,
`ReaderHorizontalPager`,
`ReaderVerticalPager`)
installs a new
`LaunchedEffect(currentPage
Index)` that calls
`scrollToItem` /
`scrollToPage` when the
param changes AND the
layout's own scroll/pager
state lags behind. The
if-guard makes the inverse
direction (scroll-driven
update) a no-op: by the time
the param recomposes from
the snapshotFlow → state
round-trip, the layout's own
state already matches, so
the if-guard skips the
redundant scroll call.

This closes the loop:
scrubber drag → VM →
recompose → layout
LaunchedEffect → scroll →
snapshotFlow eventually
emits same index →
distinctUntilChanged drops
it → no further emission.
Stable.

Side benefit: any future
non-scroll source of
page-index updates
(deeplink-to-page,
prev/next-chapter resume
on a specific page) reuses
the same plumbing without
additional wiring.

### §78.4 Design — `initialPageIndex` → `currentPageIndex` rename

`ReaderPageLayout` (and the
three child layouts) had a
parameter named
`initialPageIndex`, used
only as `initialFirstVisible
ItemIndex` /
`initialPage` for the
respective remember*State.
With the new LaunchedEffect
that reacts to live changes
to this param, the name
became misleading — it's no
longer purely "initial".

Renamed to
`currentPageIndex` across
the layout call site, the
`ReaderPageLayout`
signature, and the three
child layout signatures.
KDoc updated to reflect the
dual role:

1. Initial value for the
   layout's
   `remember*State` (so a
   mode-toggle mid-chapter
   opens the new layout on
   the same page) — same
   §69 behaviour.
2. Drive scroll-on-change
   for the scrubber (new
   §78 behaviour).

Same value drives both
roles. The rename plus a
new "Scrubber-driven
scroll" paragraph in
`ReaderPageLayout`'s KDoc
document the change.

### §78.5 Design — Slider config

Material3 `Slider` config:

- `value =
  currentPageIndex.toFloat
  ().coerceIn(0f,
  lastIndex.toFloat())`
  — thumb reflects the
  current page; coerce
  guards a narrow window
  where state outraces a
  chapter swap.
- `valueRange = 0f..
  lastIndex.toFloat()` —
  spans the page list.
- `steps = (pagesCount -
  2).coerceAtLeast(0)` —
  Material3 counts steps
  BETWEEN endpoints, so
  N-2 internal + 2
  endpoints = N discrete
  positions, one per
  page. The slider snaps
  to integer positions
  during drag.
- `onValueChange` toInt-
  rounds the new value
  and dispatches
  `onPageChanged(newIndex)`
  only when the integer
  changed — cheaper than
  relying on VM identity-
  drop, skips intent
  allocation.

For very long chapters
(say >50 pages) the
rendered tick marks get
visually dense — a
density-polish concern,
not a correctness issue.
Tracked as a deferral in
§78.7.

### §78.6 Design — bottom-overlay refactor

Before: a single
`AnimatedVisibility(visible
= state.isUiVisible)`
wrapping
`ReaderPageIndicatorHud(text
= hudText)` at
`BottomCenter`.

After: a single
`AnimatedVisibility`
wrapping a `Column` that
holds the HUD pill (when
`hudText != null`) followed
by `ReaderPageScrubber`
(when `state.pages.size >
1`). The Column has
`Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`
so the Slider's
`fillMaxWidth()` has a
fixed parent width.

HUD pill renders FIRST in
the Column (visually
upper); scrubber renders
SECOND (visually lower —
closer to the screen bottom
edge for easier thumb reach
during one-handed reading).
HUD's existing
`Modifier.padding(bottom =
spacing.lg)` provides
natural separation between
the pill and the slider; no
additional padding needed
between them.

The scrubber's own
`Modifier.padding(
horizontal = spacing.lg,
vertical = spacing.sm)`
keeps it off the screen
side edges and adds a
buffer between the slider
thumb and the screen
bottom.

### §78.7 Files

Single source commit
(`76a7174`, 1 file,
+162/-35 lines):

- `ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen
  .kt` (modified) — Added
  `Slider` import. New
  `ReaderPageScrubber`
  composable. Bottom-
  center overlay
  refactored to wrap HUD +
  scrubber in a single
  Column inside one
  AnimatedVisibility.
  Renamed
  `initialPageIndex`
  → `currentPageIndex`
  on `ReaderPageLayout`
  signature + call site +
  all three child layouts.
  Added a new
  `LaunchedEffect(current
  PageIndex)` in each
  child layout calling
  `scrollToItem` /
  `scrollToPage` with an
  if-guard. KDoc updated
  on `ReaderPageLayout` to
  document the dual role
  and the scrubber loop.

### §78.8 Build gates

The single source commit
gated through the standard
trio:

- `:composeApp:compileDebug
  KotlinAndroid` — BUILD
  SUCCESSFUL in 13s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlin
  IosArm64` — BUILD
  SUCCESSFUL in 42s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlin
  IosSimulatorArm64` —
  BUILD SUCCESSFUL,
  bundled in the same
  42s task graph.

Only baseline deprecation
warnings (all pre-existing,
all in `:composeApp`
legacy tree, none in the
rework `:ui` module).
Skiko version-mismatch
warning persists — pre-
existing Coil 3.4 / Skiko
incompatibility carried
since the initial port.

### §78.9 SOLID pointer

See `SOLID_AUDIT.md` entry
"Phase 7.x.reader.pagescrubber
— horizontal slider for
jump-to-page" for the full
10-point checklist across
the single touched file.

### §78.10 Deliberate deferrals

- **No tick-density polish
  for long chapters.** With
  `steps = pagesCount - 2`,
  a 100-page chapter renders
  98 tick marks visibly.
  Material3 currently has no
  "render endpoints only"
  variant. A future polish
  slice could swap to
  `steps = 0` (continuous,
  no ticks, no snap) with a
  local mutableStateOf to
  preserve smooth thumb
  movement. Out of scope —
  functional correctness
  ships first.
- **No drag-driven HUD/page-
  count update during drag.**
  The current design
  dispatches `onPageChanged`
  on every drag tick, but
  the integer-only update
  means the HUD/page-count
  label updates in step with
  the slider's integer
  snaps. If a future slice
  switches to continuous
  `steps = 0`, mid-drag HUD
  updates would need a
  rethink to avoid thumb-
  snap-back. Tracked here
  for that future slice.
- **No animated scroll on
  scrubber-drive.**
  `scrollToItem` /
  `scrollToPage` are
  instant. For a 1-page
  jump that's the right
  call (snappy); for a
  50-page jump an animated
  scroll might feel less
  jarring. Material3
  exposes `animateScrollTo
  Item` /
  `animateScrollToPage`
  variants — a future
  polish slice could swap
  in animated scrolling
  conditional on the jump
  magnitude. Out of scope.
- **No bookmark / chapter-
  resume callers.** The
  scroll-on-change
  LaunchedEffect is now
  ready to serve any
  caller that mutates
  `state.currentPageIndex`,
  but no other slice
  currently does this from
  a non-scroll source. The
  resumeposition slice
  (§76) DOES — but the
  read happens before the
  initial composition of
  the layout, so it's
  honoured via the
  `remember*State`
  initial-* parameter and
  the LaunchedEffect's
  if-guard makes the post-
  init no-op the right
  thing. So no behavioural
  change there.

## §79 Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.pageprogress — download-% indicator on loading placeholder

Closes the `pageprogress`
deferral floated in §78.10
(implicitly) and the
`SOLID_AUDIT.md` Phase
7.x.reader.pagescrubber
"Next" block — gives the
Reader's loading placeholder
a real download-% indicator
backed by per-byte progress
on Android, with iOS /
Desktop on coarse 3-stage
parity. Multi-commit, plan-
mode-driven slice — see
`PLAN_pageprogress.md` for
the original 8-step roadmap.

### §79.1 Goal

Replace the loading
placeholder's plain
indeterminate spinner with a
determinate
`CircularProgressIndicator
(progress = { fraction })`
when a per-byte fraction is
available, falling back to
an indeterminate spinner
when it isn't.

The slice covers three
independent surfaces:

1. **Lifecycle progress**
   from Coil per-request
   `listener(...)` —
   `Started` / `Complete` /
   `Failed` / `Idle` (on
   cancel). Works on all
   three platforms unchanged.
2. **Per-byte fraction**
   from a custom Android
   OkHttp interceptor that
   wraps the response body
   with a `ForwardingSource`
   byte counter. Android-
   only this slice; iOS /
   Desktop ktor3 byte-
   progress is a follow-on.
3. **Decoder-hint parity**
   audit for the rework
   Reader's inline
   `ImageRequest`. Lifted
   `applyReaderDecoderHints
   ()` (Android: RGB_565 +
   allowHardware(false))
   into `:ui/reader/internal
   /` via expect/actual so
   the rework matches legacy
   native parity without
   reaching back into
   `:composeApp`.

### §79.2 Design — `:domain` types

`PageDownloadProgress` is a
sealed interface with six
variants:

- `Idle` — no download
  attempted yet
- `Started` — request
  issued, bytes not yet
  flowing
- `InProgress(fraction:
  Float?)` — bytes flowing;
  fraction is 0f..1f when
  `Content-Length` is known,
  `null` when chunked /
  unknown
- `Decoding` — bytes
  received, decode in
  flight (reserved for
  future use; not emitted
  in this slice)
- `Complete` — decode done
- `Failed` — download or
  decode error; Coil's
  existing `error` slot
  takes over

`PageProgressRepository` is
the `:domain` interface:

```kotlin
fun observe(url: String):
    Flow<PageDownloadProgress>
fun report(url: String,
    status: PageDownloadProgress)
```

Cold flow per URL with
`distinctUntilChanged()`
projection so duplicate
ticks don't churn
collectors. `report` is the
write-side, called by Coil
listeners + the Android
OkHttp interceptor.

### §79.3 Design — `:data` impl

`PageProgressRepositoryImpl`
is backed by a
`MutableStateFlow<Map
<String, PageDownloadProgress>>`.
`observe(url)` maps the
state to the per-URL value
with `it[url] ?:
PageDownloadProgress.Idle`
and applies
`distinctUntilChanged()`.
`report(url, status)` does
an atomic `.update { it +
(url to status) }`. Pure-
in-memory, no `:platform`
reach, no on-disk cell.
Single Koin `single<>`
binding in
`readerReworkModule` so
reporter (Coil listener +
OkHttp interceptor) and
observer (VM) share state
exactly.

### §79.4 Design — VM extension

`ReaderState` gains a
`pageProgress: Map<String,
PageDownloadProgress>`
field, defaulting to an
empty map. `ReaderViewModel`
gains a
`PageProgressRepository`
constructor dep + an
`onEnter` cascade:
`startObservingProgress()`
launches one collector per
page URL in the chapter,
each running
`repository.observe(url)
.collect { state.update {
it.copy(pageProgress =
it.pageProgress + (url to
status)) } }`.

A tracked `Job?` field
(`progressCollectorsJob`)
gets cancelled in the
re-entry guard so a chapter
swap mid-fetch cleanly
tears down the previous
chapter's collectors before
starting the new ones.
Mirrors the §73 fire-and-
forget `Job?` posture for
`runFetch` / `runListChapters`.

### §79.5 Design — `:ui` listener + placeholder

`ReaderPageItem`'s inline
`ImageRequest.Builder`
gains a `.listener(...)`
block that maps the four
Coil callbacks to the
`PageProgressRepository`:

- `onStart` →
  `report(url, Started)`
- `onCancel` →
  `report(url, Idle)` —
  chapter swap mid-fetch
  returns the slot to the
  placeholder default
- `onSuccess` →
  `report(url, Complete)`
- `onError` →
  `report(url, Failed)`

The callback shape that
crosses the `:ui` boundary
is `(url: String, status:
PageDownloadProgress) ->
Unit` — `:ui` only knows
the `:domain` type, not
the repository. The route
adapter (
`ChapterImagesReworkScreen
Route.kt`) binds it to
`pageProgressRepo::report`,
keeping `:ui` decoupled
from `:data`.

`rememberUpdatedState`
wraps the callback so the
`remember`-cached
ImageRequest's captured
listener always invokes
the latest lambda — even
if the parent passes an
unmemoized closure.
Defensive against future
call sites.

The `loading` slot
dispatches on the per-URL
progress map entry:

```kotlin
val fraction = (progress
    as? PageDownloadProgress
    .InProgress)?.fraction
if (fraction != null) {
    CircularProgressIndicator
    (progress = {
        fraction.coerceIn(
            0f, 1f) })
} else {
    CircularProgressIndicator
    ()
}
```

`coerceIn(0f, 1f)` is a
defensive guard against
malformed `Content-Length`
headers from misbehaving
CDNs (per
`PageDownloadProgress
.InProgress` KDoc). Idle /
Started / Decoding /
Complete / Failed all stay
indeterminate — the
determinate ring is only
shown when there's an
actual fraction.

The `pageProgress` map +
`onReportProgress` callback
thread through:
`ReaderVerticalList` →
`ReaderVerticalListBody`,
`ReaderHorizontalPager`,
`ReaderVerticalPager` →
`ReaderPageItem`. The
per-page map lookup
(`pageProgress[page.url] ?:
PageDownloadProgress.Idle`)
happens at the call site
so `ReaderPageItem` sees a
resolved
`PageDownloadProgress`
value, minimizing
recompositions on
unrelated map changes.

### §79.6 Design — Android OkHttp byte interceptor

`OkHttpProgressInterceptor`
is an application-level
`okhttp3.Interceptor` (NOT
network-level — see KDoc
for why: `chain.request()
.url` reflects the ORIGINAL
caller URL, matching
`page.url` in the progress
map). It wraps every
response body in
`ProgressResponseBody`, an
`okhttp3.ResponseBody`
subclass that interposes
an `okio.ForwardingSource`
over the upstream source.
Each `read(sink,
byteCount)` increments a
`bytesRead` counter, then
calls `maybeReport(
totalBytes)`.

Throttling: at most 1 tick
per 50ms OR per 1% advance,
whichever fires first.
Without it, the read loop
emits a tick per ~8KB
buffer fill — drowns the
MVI reducer in ~1000
updates per 8MB page. The
fraction comparison uses
`Int` tenThousandths to
dodge `Float` equality fuzz
(a jump of ≥100 = 1%
counts).

When `totalBytes <= 0`
(server omitted
`Content-Length` or chunked
encoding without one), the
interceptor emits
`InProgress(fraction =
null)` purely as a "bytes
are flowing" signal — still
rate-limited to one per
50ms.

The interceptor emits ONLY
`InProgress` ticks. The
Coil per-request listener
in `:ui` (§79.5) emits the
lifecycle bookends
(Started / Complete /
Failed / Idle). Splitting
the responsibility avoids
double-edging.

Wiring: `PlatformNetwork
Fetcher.android.kt`'s
actual:

```kotlin
val repository =
    GlobalContext.get()
    .get<PageProgress
        Repository>()
val client = OkHttpClient
    .Builder()
    .addInterceptor(
        OkHttpProgressInterceptor
        (reporter =
            repository::report))
    .build()
return OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory(
    callFactory = { client })
```

The repository is resolved
via `org.koin.core.context
.GlobalContext.get()`
rather than threading a
Koin scope through `App()`
or growing the expect/actual
signature. The repository
is bound `single` in
`readerReworkModule`,
aggregated by
`allReworkModules()`,
started in every entry
point — always graph-
reachable by the time
`App()` composes.

Block-and-ask trigger #1
("default carries load-
bearing config we can't
replicate"): NOT met. Coil
3.4.0's default OkHttpClient
is a vanilla `OkHttpClient()`
with no cache, no custom
timeouts, no pool tuning,
no auth. Observationally
equivalent to our
`Builder().addInterceptor
().build()`.

### §79.7 Design — Reader decoder-hint lift

The rework Reader's inline
`ImageRequest.Builder` did
not call any analog of the
legacy `applyPlatformDecoder
Hints` (which sits today in
`:composeApp/.../images/
PlatformDecoderHints.kt`
and is used by both the
legacy reader and the
legacy library / details
covers via `rememberSource
ImageRequest`).

Step 7 lifts the hints into
`:ui/reader/internal/` via
expect/actual:

- `:ui/commonMain/.../reader
  /internal/ReaderDecoder
  Hints.kt` — internal
  expect
  `Builder.applyReaderDecoder
  Hints(): Builder`
- `:ui/androidMain/.../reader
  /internal/ReaderDecoder
  Hints.android.kt` —
  applies `.allowHardware
  (false).bitmapConfig
  (Bitmap.Config.RGB_565)`
- `:ui/desktopMain/...` —
  no-op
- `:ui/iosMain/...` —
  no-op

Why this matters (project
memory: "Mirror native
buildImageRequest for
reader pages"): without
RGB_565, Android decodes
manga pages at ARGB_8888 —
twice the memory per
bitmap. Coil's memory
cache fills ~2× faster,
evicted pages re-decode at
sample sizes >1, producing
visibly blurry mid-scroll
output. The "image quality
so bad I can't read it"
regression cited in the
project's image-quality
memory was exactly this.

Skiko (iOS / Desktop) has
no `Bitmap.Config` analog;
pixel format is implicit
in the Skia surface
backend. Quality on those
targets is supplied by
`HighQualitySkiaImage
Decoder` (Catmull-Rom
cubic resampling)
registered on the
singleton ImageLoader in
`:composeApp/App.kt`. The
actuals there are no-ops.

Reader-scoped (under
`reader/internal/`)
because manga-page low-
color → RGB_565
assumptions don't
generalize to library /
details covers. Those keep
ARGB_8888 through the
singleton loader's
defaults. The legacy
helper serves both
reader + covers; the
rework's covers don't yet
use a builder-level helper
(they use `AsyncImage(model
= url)` directly), so
reader-scoping the new
helper is the minimum-
blast-radius change.

### §79.8 Files

Eight source commits, all
≤5 files. Plan + roadmap
in `PLAN_pageprogress.md`.

### §79.11 Deliberate deferrals

- **iOS / Desktop per-byte
  progress.** The ktor3
  byte-progress wrap is a
  follow-on slice
  (working name "Phase
  7.x.reader.modelayout
  .pageprogress.ktor3").
  Today on those targets,
  the placeholder shows
  an indeterminate spinner
  during the entire fetch.
  Visually equivalent to
  pre-slice; the slice's
  differentiator on iOS /
  Desktop is that the
  same `:domain` plumbing
  is ready for the
  follow-on without any
  `:ui` / `:presentation`
  reshuffling.
- **No estimated time
  remaining ("47s left").**
  Would need a
  smoothing / rate
  calculation atop
  `fraction`. Out of
  scope — functional
  correctness ships
  first.
- **No per-page failed-
  state user message
  (e.g., "404 not
  found").** Coil's
  existing `error` slot
  + the per-page retry
  button (§71) already
  cover the failure UX.
  This slice doesn't
  extend it.
- **No `Decoding` emission
  in this slice.** The
  `PageDownloadProgress
  .Decoding` variant is
  defined in `:domain`
  but no surface emits
  it today — Coil's
  `onSuccess` lands
  almost immediately
  after the bytes arrive,
  so a brief flicker
  through a final
  spinner is the right
  ergonomics (matches
  legacy `WebToonReading
  Mode.kt` page
  placeholder). The
  variant is kept in
  `:domain` so a future
  decoder-stage progress
  slice can emit it
  without a sealed-
  hierarchy extension.
- **No `PageProgressReporter
  Attacher` expect/actual
  facade.** The original
  plan (`PLAN_pageprogress
  .md` §design) floated
  a `:platform`-side
  attacher facade that
  installs the platform-
  appropriate hooks on an
  `ImageRequest.Builder`.
  We landed instead on
  per-request listener
  attachment at the
  `:ui` site (zero
  platform reach) + an
  Android-only OkHttp
  interceptor wired into
  `PlatformNetworkFetcher
  .android.kt`. Smaller
  blast radius, no
  expect/actual surface.
  If iOS / Desktop ktor3
  per-byte progress
  arrives, the same
  posture (per-platform
  wiring of the
  underlying client) is
  the natural fit — no
  attacher facade needed.

## §80 — Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.pageprogress.ktor3 — per-byte progress on iOS + Desktop

Follow-on to §79.
Where the parent slice
landed per-byte fraction
on Android via OkHttp
interceptor + per-request
Coil listener (Started /
Complete / Failed
everywhere else), this
slice closes the iOS +
Desktop gap by porting
the same byte-counting
posture to the ktor3
client used by `coil-
network-ktor3`. The
`:domain`, `:data`,
`:presentation`, and `:ui`
plumbing from §79 carries
through unchanged — this
slice only adds emitters.

### §80.1 Strategy — ktor3 responsePipeline interceptor

Three observation seams
were considered:

1. **Per-request
   `onDownload`**: Coil
   constructs the ktor
   `HttpRequestBuilder`
   internally; there is no
   Coil hook to inject a
   per-request progress
   callback. Not viable.
2. **`createClientPlugin
   { onResponse }`** (ktor
   3.x plugin DSL): fires
   AFTER the body is fully
   read — useful for "got
   a response, here's the
   content" but useless
   for incremental byte
   counting.
3. **`responsePipeline.
   intercept(HttpResponse
   Pipeline.Receive)`**:
   client-level pipeline
   interceptor at the
   structurally-equivalent
   seam to OkHttp's
   `addInterceptor`. Fires
   after the engine has
   produced an
   `HttpResponse` but
   before downstream
   phases parse the body.
   The subject is
   `HttpResponseContainer
   (info, body)`; replace
   `body` (a
   `ByteReadChannel`) with
   a counting bridge
   channel and
   `proceedWith` the new
   subject.

Strategy 3 wins on the
same architectural
grounds the Android side
chose `addInterceptor`:
fires per logical
request, sees the
ORIGINAL request URL
(matching `page.url` in
the progress map), and
observes the final body
the decoder will actually
consume.

### §80.2 Byte counting via writer channel bridge

The interceptor wraps the
upstream `ByteReadChannel`
in a `writer(context.
coroutineContext) { ... }`
-built bridge channel.
The writer's coroutine
pumps bytes from the
upstream channel to the
downstream channel in a
fixed 8KB buffer loop:
each `readAvailable` →
`writeFully` round
increments `bytesRead`,
recomputes the fraction
(when `contentLength > 0`)
or sets it to `null` (when
unknown), and gate-checks
the throttle before
emitting.

`writer(...)` is from
`io.ktor.utils.io`,
called on the `HttpClient`
itself (which extends
`CoroutineScope`); the
captured `context.
coroutineContext` is the
`HttpClientCall`'s
context, so cancellation
of the call (Coil
swiping past a page mid-
fetch) cooperatively
cancels the writer
coroutine — no leaked
coroutines, no zombie
progress emissions.

### §80.3 Throttle parity with Android

`THROTTLE_MS = 50L` and
`THROTTLE_TENTHOUSANDTHS =
100` (= 1%) — identical
to `OkHttpProgressInter
ceptor`'s gate. The
ktor3 helper uses
`TimeSource.Monotonic.
markNow()` for the
wall-clock gate (KMP-
portable; the Android
side uses
`System.currentTimeMillis
()` because OkHttp's
interceptor body
synchronously runs on
the JVM). Both gate
shapes emit at most ~20
ticks per second per
page — sufficient for a
smooth determinate ring,
negligible churn for the
MVI reducer.

When `contentLength <= 0`
(unknown length / chunked
encoding without
Content-Length), the
fraction stays `null` and
the gate fires only on
the 50ms timer — matching
Android's `InProgress
(null)` "bytes flowing"
signal. The UI placeholder
treats `null` fraction
as an indeterminate
spinner, so visual
behaviour is identical to
pre-slice on these
responses.

### §80.4 No-engine `HttpClient { }` form

`HttpClient { }` with no
explicit engine argument
delegates engine
resolution to:

- **JVM (Desktop)**:
  ServiceLoader on the
  runtime classpath. The
  `:shared/desktopMain`
  module declares
  `implementation(libs.
  ktor.client.cio)` which
  transitively reaches
  `:composeApp`'s
  desktop runtime classpath.
- **K/N (iOS)**: link-time
  engine selection.
  `:shared/iosMain`
  declares `implementation
  (libs.ktor.client.
  darwin)`, transitively
  reaching `:composeApp`'s
  iOS link classpath.

No engine dep needs to be
declared in `:composeApp`
itself — the standing
"`:platform` module owns
its own dep graph"
project memory applies
to `:platform`, not
`:composeApp`, which
participates in a single
shared compile classpath
with `:shared` via the
`api`/`implementation`
transitive aggregation
that Gradle performs at
the source-set graph
level for KMP projects.

### §80.5 Koin resolution — KoinPlatform.getKoin()

The Android actual uses
`org.koin.core.context.
GlobalContext.get()` to
resolve the
`PageProgressRepository`
singleton. That object is
JVM-only — the
`koin-core-jvm` artifact
declares `object
GlobalContext : Koin
Context`, but
`koin-core` (KMP umbrella)
publishes only
`internal class
MutableGlobalContext`
plus an `internal fun
globalContextByMemoryModel
()` factory on K/N.

The KMP-portable
accessor is `org.koin.mp.
KoinPlatform.getKoin()`,
which calls
`KoinPlatformTools.
defaultContext().get()`
and returns the same
singleton on every target.
iOS and Desktop actuals
both use this path. The
repository remains a
`single` declared in
`readerReworkModule`,
graph-reachable at
`App()` composition time
when `remember {
platformNetworkFetcherFac
tory() }` runs.

### §80.6 Block-and-ask trigger #1 audit (preserved-config-on-default)

Coil 3.4.0's default
ktor3 `HttpClient()`
(constructed internally
by `coil-network-ktor3`
when our actuals
previously returned
`null`) is vanilla — no
plugins installed, no
custom timeouts, no
User-Agent, no
authentication. Trigger
NOT met.

Load-bearing fixes
preserved verbatim:

- `HighQualitySkiaImage
  Decoder` (singleton
  ImageLoader, registered
  in `:composeApp/App.kt`
  for iOS + Desktop) —
  lives at the Coil
  `decoderFactories`
  layer, NOT the HTTP-
  client layer. Untouched.
- `maxBitmapSize(Size.
  ORIGINAL)` (singleton
  ImageLoader baseline) —
  ImageLoader-component
  layer. Untouched.
- `CoilSourceHeader
  Interceptor` (singleton
  ImageLoader, `.
  components { add(...) }`)
  — a Coil `Interceptor`
  (not a ktor3 plugin).
  Runs on the Coil
  interceptor chain
  AHEAD of the network
  fetcher. Orthogonal to
  the ktor3 client
  swap; untouched.
- Android `OkHttp
  NetworkFetcherFactory
  (callFactory = {
  client })` explicit
  ServiceLoader pin (§79.5
  refinement) — Android
  path; untouched by this

- `AvifDecoderCoil.

  — untouched.
- Per-request `RGB_565 +

### §80.8 Deferrals carried forward + slice-specific

Carried forward from
§79.11 (unchanged by this
slice):

- No time-remaining
  smoothing.
- No per-page failed-
  state user message.
- No `Decoding` emission.

Slice-specific:

- **No Darwin-engine
  streaming-aggregation
  polish.** ktor's Darwin
  engine has known
  HTTP/2 chunked-response
  aggregation quirks (the
  same engine has WebSocket
  single-frame buffering).
  If iOS smoke testing on
  the user's Mac reveals
  visible "0% jumps to
  100%" behaviour, the
  follow-on slice would
  either (a) fall back to
  indeterminate on Darwin
  via a runtime engine
  probe, or (b) pin the
  Darwin engine to a more
  streaming-friendly
  config. Out of scope —
  ship the functional
  baseline first.
- **No engine swap to
  OkHttp on Desktop.**
  `:shared/desktopMain`
  uses CIO; if per-byte
  streaming is comparable
  to Darwin (visible
  buffering rather than
  smooth fraction
  ticking), a follow-on
  slice swaps Desktop to
  `ktor-client-okhttp`.
  Out of scope.

## §81 — Phase 7.x.statistics — Statistics screen rework

First post-Reader feature
slice. End-to-end port of
the legacy Statistics
screen (`composeApp/.../
features/statistics/ui/
screens/StatisticsScreen
.kt`, 8 reading-stats
aggregates) into the new
layer stack: pure-domain
`ReadingStatistics` data
class + one observer
interface + one use case
+ strangler-fig `:data`
impl + MVI surface +
`:ui` composable +
debug-guarded nav route.

### §81.1 Strategy — strangler-fig over the legacy aggregates

The legacy
`StatisticsRepository`
(`shared/.../features/
statistics/domain/`) is
the cell of truth for
the 8 numbers: it owns
8 named flows
(`inLibraryFlow`,
`chaptersTotalFlow`,
`chaptersDownloadedFlow`,
`chaptersReadFlow`,
`chaptersBookmarkedFlow`,
`completedEntriesFlow`,
`startedEntriesFlow`,
`readDurationFlow`)
each backed by
`MutableStateFlow` that
mirrors a Room
aggregate or the read-
minutes DataStore key.
The reader's per-page
read-mark and the
session-timer port
(Phase 6.4.x.statistics)
both write through
this repository; the
rework's `:data` impl
therefore reads-only —
delegates to the same
flows the legacy reader
populates, so a chapter
the user reads in
EITHER reader updates
the numbers on BOTH
screens (legacy and
rework). This is the
same strangler-fig
posture as
`ReadingSessionRepository
Impl` (§70 / Phase
6.4.x.statistics) — but
on the read-side this
time.

### §81.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

`:domain` (3 new files,
zero deps):

- `model/statistics/
  ReadingStatistics.kt` —
  data class with 8
  named fields (`inLibrary
  : Int`, `readDuration:
  String`, `entriesStarted
  : Int`, `entriesCompleted
  : Int`, `chaptersTotal:
  Int`, `chaptersRead:
  Int`, `chaptersDownloaded
  : Int`,
  `chaptersBookmarked:
  Int`). `readDuration`
  is a pre-formatted
  String ("Xh Ym") — see
  §81.5 for the formatting
  posture choice.
- `repository/
  ReadingStatisticsRepository
  .kt` — interface with
  `fun observe(): Flow<
  ReadingStatistics>`.
- `usecase/statistics/
  ObserveReadingStatistics
  UseCase.kt` — `operator
  fun invoke(): Flow<...>`
  pass-through.

`:data` (1 new file):

- `repository/
  ReadingStatisticsRepository
  Impl.kt` —
  constructor-takes the
  legacy `:shared`
  `StatisticsRepository`;
  `observe()` combines
  the 7 Int flows via
  `combine(vararg)` →
  `Flow<Array<Int>>`,
  then chains a 2-arity
  combine with the
  String `readDurationFlow`
  to assemble the
  `ReadingStatistics`
  data class. Two-stage
  combine avoids the
  `Any`-typed mixed
  `combine(*flows: Flow<*>)`
  shape (which would
  require an `as Int` cast
  inside the transform —
  banned).

`:presentation` (4 new
files):

- `statistics/
  StatisticsState.kt` —
  data class with the 8
  fields + `isLoading:
  Boolean = true`
  (initial-emission gap).
- `statistics/
  StatisticsIntent.kt` —
  empty sealed interface.
  OCP-friendly: future
  `OnClearReadTime` /
  `OnExportCsv` /
  `OnTapEntriesCard`
  variants slot in
  without rewiring the
  VM's superclass
  parameterisation.
- `statistics/
  StatisticsEffect.kt` —
  empty sealed interface.
  Today: no error toasts
  (Room flows don't
  throw at observe), no
  outbound nav
  (Statistics is
  terminal).
- `statistics/
  StatisticsViewModel.kt`
  — extends
  `MviViewModel<State,
  Intent, Effect>`;
  subscribes in `init {}`
  (not on `OnEnter` —
  there's no user-action
  to gate observation
  by; matches the
  `ReaderViewModel`
  observers pattern).
  `handle(intent)` is a
  no-op `when {}` over
  the empty sealed
  hierarchy.

`:ui` (1 new file):

- `statistics/
  StatisticsScreen.kt` —
  stateless inner
  `StatisticsScreenContent`
  + `StatisticsScreen`
  wrapper that resolves
  `state` via
  `viewModel.state.
  collectAsState()`.
  Layout mirrors the
  legacy: StatsOverview
  Card at the top (3
  big numbers in a Row),
  then two ItemsGroup
  sections (Entries: 3
  rows, Chapters: 4
  rows) with dividers.

`:composeApp` (1 new
module + 1 new route + 3
modified files):

- `di/StatisticsRework
  Module.kt` — `single`
  binds `ReadingStatistics
  Repository` →
  `ReadingStatisticsRepository
  Impl`, `factory` for
  the use case,
  `viewModel` for the
  VM.
- `navigation/routes/
  StatisticsReworkScreen
  Route.kt` — resolves
  VM via `koinViewModel()`
  and renders the
  composable. No nav
  callbacks (Statistics
  is terminal).
- Append to `di/
  ReworkModules.kt`
  (one-line append to
  `allReworkModules()`).
- Add `Screen.
  StatisticsRework`
  object to
  `navigation/Screen.kt`.
- Add `composable<Screen.
  StatisticsRework>`
  block to `App.kt`
  alongside the existing
  `composable<Screen.
  Statistics>`.

### §81.3 MVI shape rationale — empty intent/effect sealed interfaces

`StatisticsIntent` and
`StatisticsEffect` are
declared as empty sealed
interfaces (no variants).
Two alternatives
considered:

1. **Don't declare
   them.** Parameterise
   the VM as
   `MviViewModel<State,
   Nothing, Nothing>`.
   Compiles, but uglier
   signature, no clearer
   semantics, and any
   future user action
   (e.g., a "Clear read
   time" button) would
   force a base-class
   parameter swap.
2. **Declare empty
   sealed interfaces.**
   `MviViewModel.submit(
   intent: StatisticsIntent)`
   compiles — there's
   just no way for a
   caller to construct an
   instance to pass.
   `submit` is
   unreachable until a
   variant is added. No
   runtime cost,
   documents the slice's
   extensibility hook.

Strategy 2 wins on OCP
grounds: adding
`object OnClearReadTime
: StatisticsIntent` in a
future settings-screen
rework is a pure
addition; no
parameterisation
churn.

The `handle(intent:
StatisticsIntent)`
override is a no-op
`when {}` over the
empty sealed hierarchy.
The Kotlin compiler
proves it exhaustive
(sealed-with-zero-
subtypes is trivially
exhaustive), so no
`else` branch is needed.

### §81.4 Why `init {}` collector — no `OnEnter`

`LibraryViewModel` uses
`OnEnter` because (a)
the screen has explicit
lifecycle moments
(search filter,
selection mode) that
mediate the observation,
and (b) lazy-starting
keeps unused VMs from
subscribing. Statistics
has neither: no
toggles, no per-screen
state to gate
observation on. The
`init {}` collector
matches the
`ReaderViewModel`
observers pattern: the
flow auto-subscribes
on VM construction and
stays hot until
`viewModelScope`
cancellation cancels
the collector at host
destruction.

`viewModelScope`
ensures the collector
cancels on VM cleared
(no leaks); the
upstream `combine`'s
coroutines auto-cancel
via structured
concurrency.

### §81.5 Read-duration formatting — pre-formatted String, deferred i18n

The legacy
`readDurationFlow`
formats `"Xh Ym"`
directly in the
`:shared` repository
(with an existing
`TODO Phase 10:
stringResource(R.string.
h_m)` note). The rework
reuses the pre-formatted
String verbatim:
`ReadingStatistics.
readDuration: String`,
not `readMinutes: Int`.

Two reasons:

- **Crossover
  correctness.** Both
  routes (legacy and
  rework) consume the
  same flow; both must
  show the same string
  for the same user. If
  the rework formatted
  separately, drift
  would appear at the
  next h/m boundary.
- **Don't duplicate
  the i18n TODO.** Phase
  10's i18n lift will
  swap the legacy
  formatter to
  `stringResource(...)`
  at the same time it
  swaps the rework
  labels (StatsItem
  titles "In Library" /
  "Started" / etc. are
  also inlined as
  literal Strings
  awaiting Phase 10
  resources).

### §81.6 `:ui` minimal-dep posture — icons omitted

The legacy
`StatisticsScreen`
decorates each
StatsItem row with an
icon from
`androidx.compose.
material.icons.outlined
.*` (LibraryBooks,
Schedule,
TaskAlt, etc.). These
require the
`compose.materialIcons
Extended` artifact —
a ~6 MB resource dep.

The `:ui` module
deliberately omits
that dep (its
`build.gradle.kts`
wires only
`compose.runtime` /
`foundation` /
`material3` / `ui`).
This matches the
existing `:ui`
screens
(`LibraryScreen`,
`DetailsScreen`,
`ReaderScreen`) which
all render icon-free.
Pulling the extended
icon set in for one
screen would balloon
the binary
disproportionately for
the visual benefit.

The rework Statistics
rows are text-only:
the title-Text
(`bodyMedium`) on the
left and the value-Text
(`titleMedium
SemiBold`) on the
right. Same 8 numbers,
no information loss.

### §81.7 Loading-state branch

The VM defaults to
`StatisticsState(isLoading
= true, ...)` on
construction. Between
subscription and the
first `combine`
emission the screen
renders a centered
`CircularProgressIndicator`
(matching the existing
`:ui` Library/Details
loading idiom). On the
first upstream
emission the collector
sets `isLoading = false`
and populates the 8
fields.

The gap is sub-frame
in practice (Room's
`Flow<Int>` for
`COUNT(*)` queries
emits the current
value immediately on
subscription; the
DataStore-backed
`readMinutesFlow`
emits its
already-decoded value
immediately too). The
spinner avoids a
one-frame "all zeros"
flash on cold start.

## §82 — Phase 7.x.history — History screen rework

Second post-Reader feature
slice. End-to-end port of
the legacy History screen
(`composeApp/.../features/
history/ui/screens/
HistoryScreen.kt`, a
date-grouped reading-history
list with per-row cover +
title + chapter + relative
date + delete) into the new
layer stack: pure-domain
`HistoryEntry` model + one
read interface with three
methods + three use cases +
strangler-fig `:data` impl
+ MVI surface + `:ui`
composable + nav route.
Mirrors the Phase 7.x.
statistics shape (§81) on
the read-side, with the
addition of two mutating
intents (delete-entry,
delete-all) and two
navigational intents
(manga-click, chapter-
click) — slightly more
interactive than Statistics
but still smaller than
Library/Reader.

### §82.1 Strategy — strangler-fig over the legacy `HistoryRepository`

The legacy `:shared`
`HistoryRepository` (at
`shared/.../features/
history/domain/
HistoryRepository.kt`) is
the cell of truth for the
`history_items` Room table.
It wraps the legacy
`HistoryDao` and exposes
`getAllHistory(): Flow<
List<HistoryItemD>>`,
`deleteHistory(HistoryItemD)
`, and `deleteAllHistory()
`. The legacy Reader writes
through it on chapter-open
(via the legacy reader VM);
both the legacy History
screen and the rework
History screen subscribe to
the SAME `getAllHistory()`
flow.

The rework `:data` impl
(`HistoryRepositoryImpl`)
takes the legacy facade as
a constructor dep,
strangler-fig style — same
posture as
`ReadingStatisticsRepository
Impl` (§81.1) and
`ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl
` (§70). Reads are a pure
`map { it.toDomain() }`
flow operator; writes
(delete-entry, delete-all)
forward through the legacy
facade after the rework
`HistoryEntry` round-trips
through `toEntity()` to the
legacy `HistoryItemD`
shape. A chapter the user
reads in EITHER legacy or
rework reader updates the
SAME Room row, so the
history list on EITHER
History screen stays
synchronized — the primary
smoke-test invariant.

### §82.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

`:domain` (5 new files, zero
deps beyond `kotlinx.
coroutines.flow.Flow` and
`kotlinx.datetime.
LocalDateTime`):

- `model/history/
  HistoryEntry.kt` — data
  class with 14 fields
  carrying the full

  the row's two
  navigation targets
  (`Screen.MangaDetails`
  cover-tap + legacy
  `Screen.
  ChapterImagesFragment`
  row-tap). 14 fields is
  the maximum the legacy
  reader nav arg requires;
  carrying them on the

- `repository/

  HistoryEntry)`,
  `suspend fun deleteAll()
  `. The interface is

  (ISP) because the

- `usecase/history/

  ` — `operator fun invoke

### §82.3 Date-grouping algorithm — commonMain-portable

The legacy
`HistoryScreen.
groupItemsByDate()`
algorithm groups entries
by their `lastReadDate.
date` (drop the time-of-
day component), sorts the
group keys descending, and
emits a label per group
using a "Today /
Yesterday / N days ago /
MMM d, yyyy" formatter
(via `daysUntil(today)`).

The rework reproduces the
exact same algorithm with
one KMP-portability
adjustment: legacy uses
JVM-only `toSortedMap(
compareByDescending { it
})`; the rework substitutes
`groupBy { entry ->
entry.lastReadDate.date }`
+ `entries.sortedByDescending
{ it.key }` + `associate {
it.key to it.value }` into
a `LinkedHashMap` (the
sort-then-associate
preserves insertion order
in `LinkedHashMap`, which
`LazyColumn` then iterates
deterministically).

`MMM` (the month
abbreviation for older
dates) is computed by an
inline `monthAbbrev(month:
Int)` `when {}` over the
12 months — no
`java.text.DateFormat`,
no `Locale`, no platform-
specific calls. The
labels stay in English
inline literals; Phase 10
i18n lift will swap to
`stringResource(...)`.

### §82.4 MVI shape rationale — four intents, two effects

Unlike Statistics (§81)
where intents and effects
are empty sealed
interfaces, History has
real user actions:

- **Two mutating intents**
  (`OnDeleteEntry`,
  `OnDeleteAll`) reduce to
  `viewModelScope.launch
  { useCase(...) }`. The
  use case is `suspend`
  but `handle()` returns
  before await — the
  upstream Room flow
  re-emits with the
  mutation reflected, so
  the screen updates
  reactively without
  needing the VM to
  imperatively mutate
  `items`. `submit(intent)
  ` doesn't block.
- **Two navigational
  intents** (`OnMangaClick
  `, `OnChapterClick`)
  reduce to `emit(effect)
  `. The route adapter
  collects `effects` in a
  `LaunchedEffect` and
  translates each into a
  `safeNavigate(...)`
  call. Same posture as
  `LibraryViewModel.
  onItemClick` emitting
  `LibraryEffect.
  NavigateToDetails`.

This is the **canonical
shape** for a list screen
with per-row CRUD +
navigation: mutating
intents fire-and-forget
to use cases (upstream
re-emission updates the
view); click intents emit
effects (the route
adapter owns the nav
graph). No reducer logic
mutates `items` directly —
state is flow-driven.

### §82.5 The 14-field `HistoryEntry` payload

`HistoryEntry` carries
**14 fields** — far more
than the History screen's
4 visible elements (cover,
title, chapter, relative
date). Why:

The row's chapter-click
callback navigates to
the legacy reader
(`Screen.
ChapterImagesFragment`),
which takes a 12-argument
identity tuple (api,
language, mangaId,
chapterId, mangaTitle,
mangaUrl, mangaImageUrl,
chapterNumber, chapterUrl,
paths, isDownload,
isHome). The route
adapter needs every
field at click time.

Three options were
considered:

1. **Carry only the
   visible fields on
   `HistoryEntry`,
   re-query the DAO at
   click time.** Costs an
   extra Room round-trip
   per click, and risks
   races (the entry could
   be deleted between
   list render and click).
2. **Carry the 12 reader-
   nav fields on
   `HistoryEntry`, NOT on
   `HistoryState`.**
   Forces a side-channel
   from VM to route
   adapter for the click
   payload. Adds
   complexity.
3. **Carry all 14 fields
   on `HistoryEntry`.**
   The legacy entity
   already has them all;
   the mapper is a 14-
   field copy. The state
   already holds
   `List<HistoryEntry>`,
   so the click handler
   has the full tuple
   in-hand. Phase 9.x
   route-swap to a
   redesigned reader nav
   surface can shrink
   `HistoryEntry`
   field-by-field as the
   reader's identity tuple
   simplifies.

Option 3 wins on
simplicity and crash-
safety grounds; the 14-
field domain model is the
established shape until
the reader nav redesign
in Phase 9.x.

### §82.6 Cover-thumbnail rendering

Each row renders the
cover via plain
`AsyncImage(model = entry.
mangaImageUrl)`. The
singleton `ImageLoader`
(set in `:composeApp/
App.kt` via
`setSingletonImageLoader
Factory`) carries the
AVIF decoder, OkHttp
fetcher, max-bitmap-size
override,
HighQualitySkiaImage
Decoder, and the
`CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor
` that transparently
attaches per-source
headers (cf. memory
`project_yami_okhttp_
fetcher` /
`project_yami_desktop_
skia_size_cap` /
`project_yami_image_
quality_buildrequest`).
No per-screen
`ImageRequest.Builder` is
needed — the same posture
as `LibraryScreen`'s
`LibraryCardCover` and
`DetailsScreen`'s
`DetailsCover`. The load-
bearing image-quality
fixes apply to the
History thumbnails by
inheritance.
