## §83 — Phase 7.x.updates — Updates screen rework

Third post-Reader feature slice. End-to-end port of the legacy Updates / chapter-notifications screen (`composeApp/.../features/notifications/ui/screens/UpdatesScreen.kt`, a date-grouped chapter-update feed with per-row mark-read + delete + bulk top-bar actions + cover/title/chapter/relative-date row) into the new layer stack: pure-domain `UpdateEntry` model + one read+mutate interface with five methods + five use cases + strangler-fig `:data` impl (with mapper) + MVI surface + `:ui` composable + nav route. Mirrors the Phase 7.x.history shape (§82) on the read+CRUD+nav side but adds two more mutating intents (mark-read per-entry, mark-all-read) reflecting the screen's read-state surface — six intents total, two more than History.

### §83.1 Strategy — strangler-fig over the legacy `NotificationRepository`

The legacy `:shared` `NotificationRepository` (at `shared/.../features/notifications/domain/NotificationRepository.kt`) is the cell of truth for the `notifications` Room table. It wraps the legacy `NotificationDao` (+ the legacy `LibraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead` cross-table consistency helper) and exposes six methods: `getGroupedNotifications(): Flow<List<Pair<String, List<ChapterNotification>>>>` (pre-grouped by 4 English date buckets), `markAsRead(id: Long)` (misleadingly named — the `id` parameter is actually the `chapterId`; see §83.7), `markAllAsRead()`, `delete(notification: ChapterNotification)`, `deleteAll()`, and a `LiveNotifications` helper used only by the legacy widgets. The legacy `LibraryRefreshWorker` writes through it on chapter discovery (via the legacy notification scheduling path); both the legacy Updates screen and the rework Updates screen subscribe to the SAME `notifications` table flow.

The rework `:data` impl (`UpdatesRepositoryImpl`) takes the legacy facade as a constructor dep, strangler-fig style — same posture as `HistoryRepositoryImpl` (§82.1), `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl` (§81.1), and `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (§70). Reads flatten the legacy's pre-grouped flow (`flatMap { (_, entries) -> entries }`) and map per-entry into `UpdateEntry` — the rework converges Updates and History on a single `:ui`-side date-grouping algorithm rather than carrying the legacy's 4-tier English-literal buckets across the layer boundary (§83.3). Mark-read forwards `entry.chapterId` (NOT `entry.id`) because the legacy facade's `id` parameter is misleadingly named (§83.7). Delete forwards through the legacy `delete(entity)` after round-tripping `UpdateEntry` to `ChapterNotification` via the mapper. A chapter update added by the legacy `LibraryRefreshWorker` appears identically on BOTH Updates screens; mark-read / delete actions from EITHER route propagate to the other — the primary smoke-test invariant.

### §83.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

`:domain` (7 new files, zero deps beyond `kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow` and `kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate`):

- `model/updates/UpdateEntry.kt` — data class with 14 fields carrying the full identity tuple needed by the row's two navigation targets (`Screen.MangaDetails` cover-tap + legacy `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment` row-tap). The 12-field reader nav arg shape (api / language / mangaId / chapterId / mangaTitle / mangaUrl / mangaImageUrl / chapterUrl / chapterNumber / localImagePaths / isDownloaded) plus `id` (the primary key — used as the Compose list-key only, NOT as the chapterId arg) and `notificationDate: LocalDate` (date-only — the legacy entity stores day granularity, no time-of-day; see §83.4 for the `LocalDate` vs `LocalDateTime` choice). Plus the `isRead: Boolean` for the per-row read-state styling.
- `repository/UpdatesRepository.kt` — interface with five methods: `observeUpdates(): Flow<List<UpdateEntry>>` + four `suspend` mutators (`markAsRead(entry)`, `markAllAsRead()`, `deleteEntry(entry)`, `deleteAll()`). KDoc justifies the entry-vs-id parameter for `markAsRead` (the impl forwards `entry.chapterId`, NOT `entry.id` — §83.7) and the entity-based shape of `deleteEntry`.
- `usecase/updates/ObserveUpdatesUseCase.kt` — `operator fun invoke(): Flow<List<UpdateEntry>>` pass-through.
- `usecase/updates/MarkUpdateAsReadUseCase.kt` — `suspend operator fun invoke(entry: UpdateEntry)` pass-through. KDoc cross-references §83.7 about the legacy facade's misleading naming.
- `usecase/updates/MarkAllUpdatesAsReadUseCase.kt` — `suspend operator fun invoke()` pass-through.
- `usecase/updates/DeleteUpdateEntryUseCase.kt` — `suspend operator fun invoke(entry: UpdateEntry)` pass-through.
- `usecase/updates/DeleteAllUpdatesUseCase.kt` — `suspend operator fun invoke()` pass-through.

`:data` (2 new files):

- `mapper/UpdateMappers.kt` — `internal fun ChapterNotification.toDomain(): UpdateEntry` + `internal fun UpdateEntry.toEntity(): ChapterNotification`. Field-for-field copies; trivial transform.
- `repository/UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt` — class with one constructor dep (the legacy `NotificationRepository` aliased as `LegacyNotificationRepository`). `observeUpdates()` flattens the legacy's pre-grouped flow + maps to domain; `markAsRead(entry)` forwards `entry.chapterId` to the legacy `markAsRead(id)`; `markAllAsRead` + `deleteAll` forward verbatim; `deleteEntry(entry)` round-trips through `toEntity()` then forwards to the legacy entity-based `delete`.

`:presentation` (4 new files):

- `updates/UpdatesState.kt` — data class with `isLoading: Boolean = true`, `items: List<UpdateEntry> = emptyList()`, plus two derived getters: `isEmpty: Boolean` (true when not loading + items empty) and `hasUnreadItems: Boolean` (true when any item has `isRead == false` — drives the "Mark all read" enablement). No `error` field — Room's `getAllNotifications()` doesn't throw at observe site; mutations are structurally infallible `UPDATE`/`DELETE` SQL.
- `updates/UpdatesIntent.kt` — sealed interface, six variants: `OnMarkAsRead(entry)` + `OnMarkAllAsRead` (data object) + `OnDeleteEntry(entry)` + `OnDeleteAll` (data object) + `OnMangaClick(entry)` + `OnChapterClick(entry)`. Two more than History because Updates exposes per-entry + bulk read toggles in addition to delete actions.
- `updates/UpdatesEffect.kt` — sealed interface, two nav variants: `NavigateToDetails(api, mangaUrl)` + `NavigateToReader(entry)`. The `entry`-carrying reader effect mirrors History's posture (§82.5) — the legacy reader nav arg expects the full identity tuple.
- `updates/UpdatesViewModel.kt` — extends `MviViewModel<State, Intent, Effect>`; constructor takes 5 use cases (one observe + four mutating). `init {}` collector subscribes via `launchIn(viewModelScope)`; `handle()` dispatches the six-branch `when` — mutating intents launch fire-and-forget so the upstream Room re-emission updates state reactively without imperative mutation; click intents emit one-shot effects for the route adapter to translate into `navController.navigate(...)` calls. §83.5 documents the canonical "list screen with CRUD + nav" MVI shape this slice adopts.

`:ui` (1 new file):

- `updates/UpdatesScreen.kt` — Compose entry point. `UpdatesScreen(viewModel, onNavigateToDetails, onNavigateToReader)` stateful wrapper + stateless `UpdatesScreenContent` inner (same posture as `HistoryScreen` — separates VM wiring from rendering). Top bar with title + two top-bar actions ("Mark all read" / "Clear all"). Date-grouped `LazyColumn` with `stickyHeader` per date group. Per-row `Card` with `AsyncImage` cover + 3-line text column (title / chapter / relative date) + 2-button action column ("Mark read" disabled when entry already read / "Delete"). Read-state visual signal: unread rows render the title at `FontWeight.SemiBold`; read rows render at `FontWeight.Normal` with content at 60% alpha — KMP-portable expression of the legacy's opacity-based unread cue. Date grouping algorithm matches the History screen verbatim (4-tier "Today / Yesterday / N days ago / MMM d, yyyy"), converging the two list screens on one date-label idiom in `:ui` (§83.3).

`:composeApp` (2 new files + 3 modified):

- New `composeApp/.../di/UpdatesReworkModule.kt` — Koin module declaring `single<UpdatesRepository> { UpdatesRepositoryImpl(legacy = get()) }` + five `factory { ... }` use case bindings + `viewModel { UpdatesViewModel(get(), get(), get(), get(), get()) }`.
- New `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt` — route adapter that resolves the VM via `koinViewModel()` and forwards the two nav callbacks: `onNavigateToDetails(api, mangaUrl)` → legacy `Screen.MangaDetails`; `onNavigateToReader(entry)` → legacy `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment` with the full 12-field identity tuple (uses `entry.chapterId` directly — no History-style "id doubles as chapterId" quirk because `UpdateEntry` carries `chapterId` as a dedicated field — see §83.6 + KDoc).
- Modified `composeApp/.../di/ReworkModules.kt` — one-line append: `updatesReworkModule` joins `allReworkModules()`.
- Modified `composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt` — append `object UpdatesRework : Screen("...Screen.UpdatesRework")` with KDoc cross-referencing the legacy `Updates` route as the coexisting partner.
- Modified `composeApp/.../App.kt` — import the new route + add `composable<Screen.UpdatesRework> { ... }` block alongside the existing `composable<Screen.Updates>` legacy entry and the rework siblings. Bottom-bar visibility true to mirror the legacy Updates experience.

### §83.3 Date-grouping convergence — flat-domain + ui-regroup

The legacy `NotificationRepository.getGroupedNotifications()` returns `Flow<List<Pair<String, List<ChapterNotification>>>>` with four English-literal date buckets ("Today" / "Yesterday" / "Last Week" / "Older"). The rework `:data` impl deliberately FLATTENS this into `Flow<List<UpdateEntry>>` (`flatMap { (_, entries) -> entries }.map { it.toDomain() }`) and the `:ui` regroups by `UpdateEntry.notificationDate` using the same algorithm History uses.

Rationale:

1. **One idiom across list screens** — the `:ui` date-grouping algorithm (`groupBy + sortedByDescending + associate` into `LinkedHashMap` + the 4-tier "Today / Yesterday / N days ago / MMM d, yyyy" formatter) already lives in `HistoryScreen.kt`. Reusing it for Updates means one date-label idiom across both list screens. The legacy's 4 English buckets ("Today" / "Yesterday" / "Last Week" / "Older") would have created divergence (History: per-day; Updates: 4-bucket) for no domain reason.
2. **i18n lift convergence** — when Phase 10 i18n lift swaps inline literals for `stringResource(...)`, ONE formatter and ONE set of date-label keys cover both screens. The legacy's bucket labels are pre-formatted English in the `:shared` repository — they'd need to be unwound first.
3. **`:domain` purity** — the rework `:domain` model carries `notificationDate: LocalDate` (the raw timestamp), NOT pre-bucketed strings. Pre-bucketing in the legacy facade is presentation logic leaking into persistence; the rework hoists it back to `:ui` where it belongs.
4. **Sort order preservation** — `flatMap { (_, entries) -> entries }` over the legacy's bucket-ordered list preserves `notificationDate DESC + chapterNumber DESC` (the legacy buckets are date-bucket-ordered Today→Yesterday→LastWeek→Older). The `:ui` regroup is a stable resort that gives the same visual ordering.

The `:ui`'s `formatRelativeDate(date: LocalDate)` works on a `LocalDate` directly (no `.date` projection needed) — diverges from `HistoryScreen.formatRelativeDate(date: LocalDateTime)` by one signature char because Updates carries day-granularity timestamps and History carries minute-granularity timestamps (§83.4).

### §83.4 `LocalDate` (not `LocalDateTime`) for `notificationDate`

The legacy `ChapterNotification` entity stores `notificationDate` as `LocalDate` — chapter updates are reported at day granularity by the `LibraryRefreshWorker`. There is no time-of-day per row to preserve. The rework preserves the same wire shape: `UpdateEntry.notificationDate: LocalDate`. This diverges from `HistoryEntry.lastReadDate: LocalDateTime` (§82) because the legacy `HistoryItemD` entity DOES store minute-granularity timestamps (reading events happen at specific moments).

Consequence: the `:ui` `formatRelativeDate(date: LocalDate)` consumes `LocalDate` directly. There's no `date.date` projection step (unlike History's `LocalDateTime.date`). The 4-tier formatter is otherwise identical.

### §83.5 MVI shape rationale — canonical list-screen-with-CRUD-and-nav

The Updates MVI surface uses the same canonical shape introduced in Phase 7.x.history (§82.4):

- **State is flow-driven, not intent-driven**: the `init {}` collector subscribes to `ObserveUpdatesUseCase` at construction time and projects each emission into a fresh `UpdatesState`. No `OnEnter` intent — there are no per-screen toggles (search, selection mode) gating observation. Same posture as `HistoryViewModel` and `StatisticsViewModel`.
- **Mutating intents fire-and-forget**: `OnMarkAsRead` / `OnMarkAllAsRead` / `OnDeleteEntry` / `OnDeleteAll` each launch the use case in `viewModelScope.launch { useCase() }`. The Room flow re-emits with the mutation reflected, the VM's collector updates state — no imperative state mutation in the reducer. The `launch {}` lets the `handle` suspend return immediately so the view's `submit(intent)` doesn't block; the mutation itself completes on the use case's coroutine. `UPDATE notifications SET isRead = ...` and `DELETE FROM notifications` SQL are structurally infallible — no `.onFailure` is needed.
- **Navigational intents emit effects**: `OnMangaClick` / `OnChapterClick` emit one-shot `UpdatesEffect`s; the route adapter collects them via `LaunchedEffect` and translates each into a `navController.navigate(...)` call. Tapping a row doesn't change what Updates renders — it navigates away.

OCP for the slice: adding e.g. an `OnMarkAsUnread` variant or an `OnEnterUnreadFilter` is an append to `UpdatesIntent`; the VM's exhaustive `when` flags the missing branch at compile time. Adding a `ShowUndoSnackbar` to `UpdatesEffect` (a legacy UX the rework deliberately omits — see §83.8) is similarly additive.

### §83.6 14-field `UpdateEntry` payload — same crash-safety + nav-arg rationale as History (§82.5)

`UpdateEntry` carries all 14 fields the legacy `ChapterNotification` entity carries: `id` (Room primary key), `api`, `language`, `mangaId`, `mangaTitle`, `mangaImageUrl`, `mangaUrl`, `chapterId`, `chapterNumber`, `chapterUrl`, `notificationDate` (`LocalDate`), `isRead`, `isDownloaded`, `localImagePaths`. The 12-field reader nav arg shape (`Screen.ChapterImagesFragment`) needs api / language / mangaId / chapterId / mangaTitle / mangaUrl / mangaImageUrl / chapterUrl / chapterNumber / localImagePaths / isDownloaded — eleven of the entry's fields, missing only `id` / `isRead` / `notificationDate`. The full payload lets the route adapter build the legacy nav arg without an extra DAO round-trip + survives mid-tap deletions (a `getById` lookup from a click handler could race against a `DELETE FROM notifications` and crash; carrying the data on the click eliminates the race).

Differences vs `HistoryEntry`:

- `UpdateEntry.chapterId` is a DEDICATED field (the legacy `ChapterNotification` entity stores it as `chapterId`, separate from the primary-key `id`). `HistoryEntry.id` doubles as the legacy nav arg `chapterId` (a quirk of `HistoryItemD` where the primary key IS the chapterId). The rework Updates route adapter passes `entry.chapterId` directly; the rework History route adapter passes `entry.id`. Both mirror their respective legacy adapters verbatim.
- `UpdateEntry.chapterNumber` is the chapter label string (the legacy nav arg's `chapterNumber` field). `HistoryEntry.chapterTitle` mirrors a legacy quirk where the history row's "chapter title" is reused as the nav arg's `chapterNumber`. The rework Updates avoids that quirk because the legacy `ChapterNotification` entity has a properly-named `chapterNumber` column.

### §83.7 Misleading legacy facade naming — `markAsRead(id: Long)` actually takes `chapterId`

The legacy `NotificationRepository.markAsRead(id: Long)` parameter is named "id" but is actually the **chapterId**, NOT the notification row's primary key. The legacy method body delegates to `LibraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead(id)`, which runs:

```sql
UPDATE notifications SET isRead = NOT isRead WHERE chapterId = :chapterId;
UPDATE saved_chapters SET isRead = ... WHERE id = :chapterId;
```

— i.e., a cross-table flip keyed on `chapterId`. The legacy `UpdatesScreen.kt:151` / `:233` call sites verify this: they invoke `onMarkAsRead(notification.chapterId)`. The rework `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.markAsRead(entry: UpdateEntry)` forwards `entry.chapterId` (NOT `entry.id`). Forwarding `entry.id` would target the wrong `chapterId` column and silently no-op (if `entry.id` happens not to collide with any chapter row) or flip the wrong row (if it does).

This is captured verbatim in:
- `UpdateMappers.kt` (mapper preserves both columns)
- `UpdatesRepository.markAsRead`'s KDoc (`entry`-shaped parameter rationale)
- `MarkUpdateAsReadUseCase.kt`'s KDoc (cross-references this §83.7)
- `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.markAsRead`'s KDoc (deep legacy facade analysis)

Future Phase 9.x cleanup can rename the legacy facade parameter to `chapterId: Long` once the rework route-swap retires the legacy route adapter — until then the misleading name stays in `:shared` for legacy call-site stability.

### §83.9 Deferrals

- **No i18n lift** — inline literal strings ("Updates" / "Mark all read" / "Clear all" / "Mark read" / "Delete" / "No updates yet" + the date labels). Phase 10's i18n lift swaps both legacy and rework consumers in one pass.
- **No icons** — the legacy uses `Icons.Outlined.Done` / `.DeleteForever` / `.Delete` etc. from `compose.materialIconsExtended`; `:ui` deliberately omits that ~6 MB icon-resource dep. Substitute labelled `TextButton`s.
- **No undo-snackbar UX** — the legacy `UpdatesScreen` wires a `SnackbarHost` for undo-delete after each row dismiss. The rework slice deliberately omits this — adding a `UpdatesEffect.ShowUndoSnackbar(entry)` variant is an OCP append for a future slice.
- **No swipe-to-dismiss** — the legacy uses `rememberSwipeToDismissBoxState` + `SwipeToDismissBox` for per-row dismiss (with the deprecated `confirmValueChange` callback). The rework's per-row "Delete" button replaces it; swipe-to-dismiss can be a follow-on gesture slice without touching the existing intent surface.
- **No per-row download button** — the legacy threads `DownloadViewModelv2` through the route adapter for per-row download triggers + queued/running spinners. The rework's per-row download surface is deferred to a future `Phase 7.x.updates.download` slice once the `DownloadRepository`'s Android-only Koin binding is lifted to commonMain (per `migration/pending-work.md` Phase 11).
- **No notification grouping by manga** — the legacy already shows a flat-by-date list; the rework preserves that. Grouping by manga (e.g., "Chapter 12, 13, 14 of MangaTitle") would be an OCP `:ui`-only change without touching the state.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.Updates` stays bound to the legacy route. Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice; this slice only adds the parallel `Screen.UpdatesRework` route.

## §84 — Phase 7.x.sources — Sources screen rework

Fourth post-Reader feature slice. End-to-end port of the legacy onboarding-flavoured Sources screen (`composeApp/.../features/onboarding/sources/SourcesScreen.kt`, a language-bucketed source list with per-source + per-language `Switch`es) into the new layer stack: pure-domain `Source` model + one read+toggle interface with three methods + three use cases + strangler-fig `:data` impl (with mapper) + MVI surface + `:ui` composable + nav route. Smallest list-screen slice so far — no date grouping, no delete, no nav out, no `error` state — but the FIRST slice with a bulk-fan-out mutator (`setLanguageEnabled` snapshots the upstream and fans out per-source writes inside the `:data` layer, lifting that fan-out from the legacy onboarding VM).

### §84.1 Strategy — strangler-fig over the legacy `SourcesRepository`

The legacy `:shared` `SourcesRepository` (at `shared/.../features/repo_settings/domain/SourcesRepository.kt`) is the cell of truth for the `sources` Room table AND for the in-memory `repoMap: Map<String, BaseMangaRepository>` registry that powers `findRepoByHost` / `activeRepoFlow` / `repoTaps` / `getUrl` / `getEnabledRepos` — the LOAD-BEARING entry points consumed by Home / Search / MangaDetails / Reader / the Coil header interceptor (MEMORY: `project_yami_okhttp_fetcher`). The legacy facade exposes ~20 methods; the rework slice deliberately depends on ONLY two (`allSources: Flow<List<SourcesEntity>>` and `enableDisAbleSource(name: String, enabled: Boolean)`) and leaves the rest UNTOUCHED.

The rework `:data` impl (`SourcesRepositoryImpl`) takes the legacy facade as a constructor dep, strangler-fig style — same posture as `UpdatesRepositoryImpl` (§83.1), `HistoryRepositoryImpl` (§82.1), `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl` (§81.1), and `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (§70). `observeSources()` maps the legacy `allSources` flow into the domain `Source` model via the new `SourcesMappers.kt`. `setSourceEnabled(api, enabled)` forwards verbatim — the entity's `name` column equals the domain `Source.api` (the legacy `saveSources` seeds rows with `name = repo.API`). `setLanguageEnabled(language, enabled)` snapshots the upstream via `.first()` and fan-outs per-source `setSourceEnabled` calls — lifting that fan-out from the legacy onboarding VM (`RepoSettingsViewModel.toggleLanguage` does the same iteration on the VM side) into the `:data` layer so the rework VM stays free of repository-shape leakage. Toggling a source in EITHER route flips the same `sources` Room row; both screens converge via the upstream `allSources` flow re-emit.

### §84.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

`:domain` (5 new files, zero deps beyond `kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow`):

- `model/sources/Source.kt` — data class with 4 fields: `api: String` (the source identifier — equal to the entity's `name` column), `language: String`, `priority: Int`, `isEnabled: Boolean`. Drops 5 legacy fields (`siteState`, `baseUrl`, `baseVersion`, `imageBaseUrl`, `imageUrlVersion`) that the screen never renders and the slice never mutates — the rework deliberately avoids falsely advertising mutability of fields the load-bearing legacy facade still owns. The legacy in-memory `BaseMangaRepository` registry (consumed by Home / Search / MangaDetails / Reader / Coil) still owns these; the rework table view is intentionally a narrow read+toggle subset.
- `repository/SourcesRepository.kt` — interface with three methods: `observeSources(): Flow<List<Source>>` + two `suspend` mutators (`setSourceEnabled(api, enabled)`, `setLanguageEnabled(language, enabled)`). KDoc explicitly justifies the ISP-narrow surface — adding the routing methods (`findRepoByHost`, `activeRepoFlow`, etc.) here would couple this interface to the still-legacy in-memory registry path.
- `usecase/sources/ObserveSourcesUseCase.kt` — `operator fun invoke(): Flow<List<Source>>` pass-through.
- `usecase/sources/SetSourceEnabledUseCase.kt` — `suspend operator fun invoke(api: String, enabled: Boolean)` pass-through.
- `usecase/sources/SetLanguageEnabledUseCase.kt` — `suspend operator fun invoke(language: String, enabled: Boolean)` pass-through. KDoc cross-references the `:data` impl's fan-out posture.

`:data` (2 new files):

- `mapper/SourcesMappers.kt` — `internal fun SourcesEntity.toDomain(): Source = Source(api = name, language = language, priority = priority, isEnabled = isEnabled)`. Entity → domain only (NO reverse). The rework never writes a full row — `enableDisAbleSource(name, enabled)` takes the name + the target flag, not an entity, so a `Source.toEntity()` would be dead code.
- `repository/SourcesRepositoryImpl.kt` — class with one constructor dep (the legacy `SourcesRepository` aliased as `LegacySourcesRepository`). `observeSources()` is `legacy.allSources.map { entities -> entities.map { it.toDomain() } }`; `setSourceEnabled` forwards verbatim; `setLanguageEnabled` is `val snapshot = legacy.allSources.first(); snapshot.filter { it.language == language }.forEach { legacy.enableDisAbleSource(it.name, enabled) }`.

`:presentation` (4 new files):

- `sources/SourcesState.kt` — data class with `isLoading: Boolean = true`, `items: List<Source> = emptyList()`, plus three derived getters: `isEmpty` (true when not loading + empty), `groupedByLanguage: Map<String, List<Source>>` (insertion-ordered `groupBy` for the `:ui` regroup — §84.3), and `enabledCount: Int` (count of enabled sources — surfaced for a future "X of N enabled" header line). No `error` field — Room flow doesn't throw at observe; the toggle `UPDATE sources SET isEnabled` SQL is structurally infallible.
- `sources/SourcesIntent.kt` — sealed interface, two variants: `OnToggleSource(source, enabled)` + `OnToggleLanguage(language, enabled)`. No nav intents (Sources is terminal — no outbound links). No bulk delete / clear intent (sources are a fixed seed; the rework cannot delete them).
- `sources/SourcesEffect.kt` — sealed interface, EMPTY. No effects today — same posture as `StatisticsEffect`. OCP placeholder: a future `Phase 7.x.sources.complaint` slice can add `ShowComplaintDialog(api)` or `ShowError(error)` without touching the VM's base-class signature.
- `sources/SourcesViewModel.kt` — extends `MviViewModel<State, Intent, Effect>`; constructor takes 3 use cases. `init {}` collector subscribes via `launchIn(viewModelScope)`; `handle()` dispatches the two-branch `when` — mutating intents launch fire-and-forget so the upstream Room re-emission updates state reactively without imperative mutation. §84.4 documents the simplest possible "list screen with toggles" MVI shape.

`:ui` (1 new file):

- `sources/SourcesScreen.kt` — Compose entry point. `SourcesScreen(viewModel, modifier)` stateful wrapper + stateless `SourcesScreenContent` inner (same posture as `UpdatesScreen` / `HistoryScreen`). Top bar with title ("Sources") + `LazyColumn` with one section per language. Each section starts with a `LanguageHeader` row showing the language name + a "X of Y enabled" subtitle + a Material 3 `Switch` (`checked = sources.any { it.isEnabled }` per the legacy `LanguageToggle` predicate); per-source rows follow, each with the API label + a per-source `Switch`. `HorizontalDivider` between rows. Reads `groupedByLanguage` directly off state — the regroup lives in `:presentation`, not in the composable. Centered `CircularProgressIndicator` for `isLoading`; centered "No sources available" for `isEmpty`.

`:composeApp` (2 new files + 3 modified):

- New `composeApp/.../di/SourcesReworkModule.kt` — Koin module declaring `single<SourcesRepository> { SourcesRepositoryImpl(legacy = get()) }` + three `factory { ... }` use case bindings + `viewModel { SourcesViewModel(get(), get(), get()) }`.
- New `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/SourcesReworkScreenRoute.kt` — route adapter that resolves the VM via `koinViewModel()` and renders `SourcesScreen`. No nav callbacks (Sources is terminal). KDoc explicitly notes that the legacy onboarding's `onFinish` callback is NOT ported — the rework is a standalone source-list-with-toggles surface, not an onboarding wizard step.
- Modified `composeApp/.../di/ReworkModules.kt` — one-line append: `sourcesReworkModule` joins `allReworkModules()`.
- Modified `composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt` — append `object SourcesRework : Screen("...Screen.SourcesRework")` with KDoc cross-referencing the legacy `Sources` onboarding step as the coexisting partner.
- Modified `composeApp/.../App.kt` — import the new route + add `composable<Screen.SourcesRework> { ... }` block alongside the existing rework siblings. Bottom-bar visibility false to mirror the legacy onboarding Sources step's chrome.

### §84.3 Language grouping convergence — flat-domain + ui-regroup (via `:presentation` derived getter)

The legacy `RepoSettingsScreen` accepts an already-grouped `LinkedHashMap<String, List<SourcesEntity>>` from its onboarding VM. The rework deliberately FLATTENS the upstream into `Flow<List<Source>>` and the `:presentation` derived getter `SourcesState.groupedByLanguage = items.groupBy { it.language }` regroups for the `:ui` LazyColumn.

This mirrors §82.3 (History) and §83.3 (Updates) — convergence on one "flat-domain + regroup-at-render" idiom across all rework list screens. The variation here is that the regroup lives in `:presentation` (as a derived getter on `SourcesState`) rather than in `:ui` directly. Rationale: the regroup is purely structural (no date-format logic, no i18n string-formatter call), it's stable across renders, and surfacing it as a state-derived map keeps the composable a pure render function. History / Updates regroup in `:ui` because their date formatters are render-time concerns (the relative-date threshold "Today / Yesterday / N days ago" depends on `Clock.System.now()` at the moment of formatting); Sources has no such formatter, so the derived-getter posture is cleaner.

Sort order: `items.groupBy { it.language }` is `LinkedHashMap`-backed via the stdlib, which preserves the upstream's natural row order. The legacy `allSources` flow is the raw `SELECT * FROM sources` with no explicit `ORDER BY`; rows come out in insertion order from the legacy `saveSources` seed which iterates `repoMap.values`. This stable-but-arbitrary order is fine for the rework (the legacy onboarding screen iterates the same way); a future slice can sort languages by endonym if UX requires.

### §84.4 MVI shape rationale — simplest list-screen-with-toggles

The Sources MVI surface uses the simplest possible list-screen-with-toggles shape — the lightest in the slice catalog so far:

- **State is flow-driven**: the `init {}` collector subscribes to `ObserveSourcesUseCase` and projects each emission into a fresh `SourcesState`. No `OnEnter` intent — no per-screen toggles gate observation. Matches `HistoryViewModel`, `UpdatesViewModel`, `StatisticsViewModel`.
- **Two mutating intents fire-and-forget**: `OnToggleSource` / `OnToggleLanguage` each launch the use case in `viewModelScope.launch { useCase(...) }`. The Room `UPDATE sources SET isEnabled` write re-emits via the `allSources` flow; the VM's collector updates state. No imperative mutation in the reducer. `UPDATE` SQL is structurally infallible — no `.onFailure` needed.
- **No nav intents**: Sources is terminal. No effects, no `LaunchedEffect` collector in the route adapter.
- **`SourcesEffect` is an empty sealed interface**: same OCP-placeholder posture as `StatisticsEffect`. Future `Phase 7.x.sources.complaint` slice can add `ShowComplaintDialog(api)` without touching the VM's base-class signature.

This is the minimum viable MVI surface for a flow-driven list with toggle mutators. The `handle(intent)` reducer is a 2-branch `when` — sealed-with-2-subtypes is exhaustive; no `else` needed.

### §84.5 4-field `Source` payload — narrower than History (§82.5) / Updates (§83.6) on purpose

`Source` carries 4 fields, vs `UpdateEntry`'s 14 and `HistoryEntry`'s 12. Rationale:

- **No nav out** — Sources has zero outbound links. The 14-field reader nav arg shape that History / Updates carry is unnecessary here.
- **No mutability advertising for fields the slice can't write** — `siteState` (last-known-availability), `baseUrl` / `baseVersion` / `imageBaseUrl` / `imageUrlVersion` (Coil + fetch routing) are owned by the LOAD-BEARING in-memory `BaseMangaRepository` registry on the legacy facade. The rework `:data` impl forwards ONLY `enableDisAbleSource` writes — no method to mutate `baseUrl` exists in the legacy facade either (those are populated by the source seed code + the WebView capture flow). Carrying these fields on `Source` would falsely advertise mutability the rework cannot honour.
- **ISP-correctness for the screen** — the `:ui` screen renders 2 fields per source row (`api` label + `isEnabled` Switch state) and groups by 1 field (`language`). `priority` is the upstream's natural sort key (already baked into the row order via the legacy seed iteration) — carried for completeness but not visually surfaced.
- **Future expansion is OCP-additive** — when a future slice (e.g., a "show site status indicator" UX) needs `siteState`, the field appends to `Source` with a default value; existing call sites stay working.

This is the leanest the slice could be while preserving correctness. The legacy `SourcesEntity` 9-field shape is presentation-leaks-into-persistence in reverse: it carries fields nobody on the legacy onboarding screen reads either; the rework `:domain` deliberately narrows.

### §84.6 Load-bearing legacy paths UNTOUCHED — explicitly enumerated

The legacy `SourcesRepository` facade exposes ~20 methods/properties. The rework slice consumes ONLY two (`allSources` flow + `enableDisAbleSource(name, enabled)`). The following load-bearing legacy paths are NOT touched by this slice and continue to serve their existing consumers verbatim:

- `findRepoByHost(host)` — consumed by the Coil `CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor` in `App.kt` for per-source header injection (Cookie + User-Agent on Cloudflare-protected hosts). MEMORY: `project_yami_okhttp_fetcher`. Without this, image fetches 403 even after Layer 2's WebView session capture.
- `activeRepoFlow` / `repoTaps` / `getActiveRepo()` — consumed by Home / Search / MangaDetails / Reader to identify the currently-active source for the user's flow.
- `getUrl(api)` / `updateActiveByApi(api)` — consumed by source-page fetches + the source-picker UX.
- `getEnabledRepos()` — consumed by Home's per-source carousel population.
- `saveSources()` — the seed write the legacy onboarding's `RepoSettingsViewModel` calls to populate the `sources` Room table from the in-memory `repoMap` on first launch.

The rework reads + writes through ONLY the two methods listed above. The strangler-fig boundary is captured in `SourcesRepositoryImpl`'s class-level KDoc.

- **No i18n lift** — inline literal strings ("Sources" / "No sources available" / "X of Y enabled"). Phase 10's i18n lift swaps both legacy and rework consumers in one pass.
- **No complaint dialog** — the legacy `SourcesScreen` wires a `ComplaintViewModel` for the "request new source" feature. The rework's empty `SourcesEffect` sealed interface is the OCP placeholder; a future `Phase 7.x.sources.complaint` slice adds `ShowComplaintDialog(api)` + the per-row complaint trigger.
- **No "Finish" button / onboarding chain** — the legacy onboarding screen has a "Finish" button that flips `first_launch` to false. The rework is a standalone surface; the legacy `Screen.Sources` route stays bound to the onboarding flow's `SourcesScreenRoute` verbatim.
- **No `AnimatedBackground` / gradient overlay** — the legacy uses an onboarding-flavour gradient backdrop. The rework uses plain Material 3 `Scaffold` chrome.
- **No "Languages coming soon" info card** — legacy onboarding marketing surface; not part of the rework.
- **No siteState indicator** — the legacy entity carries `siteState` ("ok" / "broken" / etc.); the rework `Source` deliberately drops it (§84.5) until a future slice ports the per-source health surface.
- **No sort-by-endonym / language-name lookup** — sources display in upstream natural order (§84.3).
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.Sources` stays bound to the onboarding route. Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice; this slice only adds the parallel `Screen.SourcesRework` route.


## §85 — Phase 7.x.theme — Theme picker screen rework

The Theme picker is the smallest viable settings-sub-screen rework: a 3-tab
Material 3 `TabRow` (Light / Dark / System) backed by a tri-state ADT in the
new architecture, strangler-fig-delegating to the legacy `:shared`
`SettingsRepository`'s two-boolean `SharedPreferences` storage shape
(`darkMode` + `followSystem`). It is the first rework slice that targets a
*pref-flow-driven* picker (vs the prior list-driven slices for Library /
Statistics / History / Updates / Sources), establishing the canonical settings-
sub-screen rework pattern for the remaining settings-screen lifts to come.

### §85.1 Strategy

The legacy theme picker lives in `composeApp/.../onboarding/theme_selection/ThemeSelectionScreen.kt` + `ThemeSelector.kt` as an *onboarding-flavoured* surface (animated-background overlay, notification-permission grant button + auto-requester, "Continue" wizard advance), with a separate route adapter at `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt` that performs a boolean -> `AppTheme` translation inline and dispatches back through `OnboardingViewModel.setTheme(...)` which calls `SettingsRepository.setDarkMode` + `setFollowSystem` directly.

The rework slice extracts ONLY the *picker* surface — three tabs, current selection highlighted, tap dispatches an MVI intent — and leaves the onboarding chrome (animated background, gradient overlay, permission grant, wizard "Continue") on the legacy onboarding route. Both routes (`Screen.Theme` legacy + `Screen.ThemeRework`) coexist; both consume the SAME `darkMode` + `followSystem` `SharedPreferences` booleans through the legacy `SettingsRepository` facade, so toggling the theme on EITHER route flips the same two booleans and the change propagates to the other screen via the upstream `darkModeFlow` / `followSystemFlow` flow re-emit.

### §85.2 Why this slice was picked next

- The Reader stack (Phases 6.4.x + 7.x.reader.*) is exhausted. The list-screen catalog (Library / Statistics / History / Updates / Sources) is consolidated.
- Block-and-ask triggers (a)-(d) all NOT met: no contract library blocker; no observable behaviour change (legacy onboarding route preserved verbatim; rework route is parallel + debug-guarded); no compile risk (the `SettingsRepository` facade dep is already declared on `:data` from prior slices); no SOLID violation.
- The Theme slice depends ONLY on `SettingsRepository` (two boolean flows + two setter methods) — no `BaseMangaRepository` entanglement, no Coil image loading, no nav graph re-routing complexity. Smallest viable surface for establishing the settings-sub-screen rework canon.
- One state field on the screen (`AppTheme` selection) + one user-driven intent (`OnSelectTheme(theme)`). Pure flow-driven UI: the VM does not imperatively mutate `theme` — the `SetAppThemeUseCase` writes propagate through the pref flow round-trip. Reactive without a `OnRefresh` intent.

### §85.3 `:domain` layer

Three new files, all in `:domain/commonMain`:

- `domain/.../model/theme/AppTheme.kt` — pure enum ADT with three variants: `Light`, `Dark`, `System`. NOT Compose-aware (no `ImageVector` or `material.icons.*` import — those live in `:ui`'s `AppTheme.icon` extension property, see §85.6). The ADT collapses the legacy's two-boolean shape into a single tri-state value; the picker can render it as a 3-tab segmented control, a radio list, or any future shape without changing the domain contract.
- `domain/.../repository/ThemeRepository.kt` — interface with two methods:
  - `fun observeAppTheme(): Flow<AppTheme>` — pure observer, no fallibility.
  - `suspend fun setAppTheme(theme: AppTheme)` — write returns Unit, no fallibility (the legacy facade's `setDarkMode` / `setFollowSystem` calls are sync `SharedPreferences` writes that complete in microseconds; no `Result`-wrapping needed).
- `domain/.../usecase/theme/ObserveAppThemeUseCase.kt` — single-line pass-through (`operator fun invoke() = repository.observeAppTheme()`).
- `domain/.../usecase/theme/SetAppThemeUseCase.kt` — single-line pass-through (`suspend operator fun invoke(theme: AppTheme) = repository.setAppTheme(theme)`).

### §85.4 `:data` strangler-fig impl

One new file: `data/.../repository/ThemeRepositoryImpl.kt`. Reaches into the legacy `:shared` `SettingsRepository` via constructor injection (aliased as `LegacySettingsRepository` per the prior strangler-fig posture established by `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` / `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl` / `HistoryRepositoryImpl` / `UpdatesRepositoryImpl` / `SourcesRepositoryImpl`).

The impl `combine`s the legacy's two boolean flows into the tri-state `AppTheme` ADT:

```kotlin
override fun observeAppTheme(): Flow<AppTheme> =
    combine(legacy.darkModeFlow, legacy.followSystemFlow) { dark, system ->
        when {
            system -> AppTheme.System
            dark -> AppTheme.Dark
            else -> AppTheme.Light
        }
    }
```

The setter translates back:

```kotlin
override suspend fun setAppTheme(theme: AppTheme) {
    when (theme) {
        AppTheme.Light -> {
            legacy.setFollowSystem(false)
            legacy.setDarkMode(false)
        }
        AppTheme.Dark -> {
            legacy.setFollowSystem(false)
            legacy.setDarkMode(true)
        }
        AppTheme.System -> {
            legacy.setFollowSystem(true)
        }
    }
}
```

The "System leaves `darkMode` unchanged" quirk is preserved verbatim from the legacy `ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt`'s boolean translation (the legacy onboarding route only sets `followSystem = true` and does NOT reset `darkMode` — when the user later toggles back to Light or Dark, the `darkMode` value at that point is the explicit choice they made, not a stale System-induced value). This means System -> Dark -> System -> Light sequences round-trip through the upstream flows correctly.

### §85.5 `:presentation` MVI surface

Four new files in `presentation/.../theme/`:

- `ThemeState.kt` — `data class ThemeState(val isLoading: Boolean = true, val theme: AppTheme = AppTheme.System)`. The default `theme = System` matches the legacy `SettingsRepository.followSystemFlow`'s `true` default — if the upstream takes a tick to emit the first value, the picker initially renders System highlighted with `isLoading = true`; the user can't perceive the gap.
- `ThemeIntent.kt` — sealed interface with one variant: `OnSelectTheme(val theme: AppTheme)`. No `OnEnter` (the VM's `init {}` collector handles subscription).
- `ThemeEffect.kt` — empty sealed interface (OCP placeholder for future `Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack` slice's `ShowError` or a follow-on `OnThemeApplied` snackbar trigger).
- `ThemeViewModel.kt` — extends `MviViewModel<ThemeState, ThemeIntent, ThemeEffect>`; constructor takes two use cases; `init {}` launches `observeAppTheme()` collector that updates state on each emission; `handle(OnSelectTheme)` fires-and-forgets `setAppTheme(intent.theme)` on `viewModelScope` (the upstream flow re-emit drives the UI update — no imperative state mutation here).

### §85.6 `:ui` composable

One new file: `ui/.../themepicker/ThemeScreen.kt`. The package is `me.manga.kira.ui.themepicker` (NOT `ui.theme`) to avoid colliding with the existing `ui.theme` design-token package (`YamiColors`, `YamiShapes`, `Spacing`, `YamiTheme`).

The composable renders a Material 3 `Scaffold` with a `TopAppBar` titled "Theme" and a `TabRow` with three text-only tabs (Light / Dark / System). The loading branch shows a centered `CircularProgressIndicator` — same posture as Sources / History / Updates / Statistics loading branches.

**Icon-free posture**: the legacy onboarding picker shows `Icons.Default.LightMode` / `.DarkMode` / `.SettingsBrightness` icons. The rework drops them for classpath consistency — the rework `:ui` module does NOT depend on `material-icons-extended` (the existing `HistoryScreen`, `StatisticsScreen`, `UpdatesScreen`, `SourcesScreen` all avoid Material icons too). Accepted as a minor visual divergence per the rework's design-token discipline. A future slice can lift the `material-icons-extended` dep across all rework `:ui` screens in one pass if desired.

The screen has TWO `:ui`-local extension properties on `AppTheme`:

- `AppTheme.indexInPicker: Int` — maps Light/Dark/System to 0/1/2 for the `TabRow`'s `selectedTabIndex`. Defined here (not on `:domain`'s enum) because tab order is a UI-only concern.
- `AppTheme.label: String` — inline literal "Light" / "Dark" / "System" (Phase 10 i18n lift will route through `Res.string.*`).

The legacy onboarding's `AppTheme.icon` extension was deliberately omitted (see "Icon-free posture" above).

The composable splits stateful (`ThemeScreen(viewModel)`) and stateless (`ThemeScreenContent(state, onIntent)`) per the established preview / test convention.

### §85.7 `:composeApp` Koin + nav wiring

Five files at the standing cap:

- NEW `composeApp/.../di/ThemeReworkModule.kt` — binds `ThemeRepository -> ThemeRepositoryImpl(legacy = get())` as `single`, `ObserveAppThemeUseCase` + `SetAppThemeUseCase` as `factory`, and `ThemeViewModel(get(), get())` as `viewModel`.
- MODIFIED `composeApp/.../di/ReworkModules.kt` — appends `themeReworkModule` to `allReworkModules()`. Hosts already thread the full list through `initKoin { modules(*allReworkModules()...) }` from prior slices.
- NEW `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ThemeReworkScreenRoute.kt` — resolves `ThemeViewModel` via `koinViewModel()` and calls `ThemeScreen(viewModel = viewModel)`. `navController` + `backStackEntry` accepted for parity with sibling adapters; both unused (Theme is terminal, no outbound nav).
- MODIFIED `composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt` — adds `object ThemeRework : Screen("me.manga.kira.navigation.Screen.ThemeRework")` with KDoc documenting the strangler-fig coexistence (same prefs as the legacy `Theme` route).
- MODIFIED `composeApp/.../App.kt` — adds the `composable<Screen.ThemeRework>` entry alongside the existing rework routes + the import. Bottom bar visibility false to mirror the legacy onboarding `Theme` step's chrome posture.

### §85.8 Legacy `SettingsRepository` surface — what the rework touches vs leaves

The legacy `SettingsRepository` (at `shared/.../settings/domain/SettingsRepository.kt`) is a large facade carrying every app-wide pref. The rework reads + writes through ONLY four of its members:

- `darkModeFlow: Flow<Boolean>` — read by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.observeAppTheme`.
- `followSystemFlow: Flow<Boolean>` — read by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.observeAppTheme`.
- `setDarkMode(value: Boolean)` — sync, called by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.setAppTheme`.
- `setFollowSystem(value: Boolean)` — sync, called by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.setAppTheme`.

The remaining surface — `firstLaunchFlow` + `firstLaunchToFalse()`, `languageFlow` + `setLanguage()`, `notificationsEnabledFlow` + `setNotificationsEnabled()`, `adultContentEnabledFlow` + `setAdultContentEnabled()`, plus every other pref accessor — stays on the legacy facade verbatim for `OnboardingViewModel`, `SettingsViewModel`, `MainActivity`'s theme observer, and any other legacy consumer.

The rework reads + writes through ONLY the four members listed above. The strangler-fig boundary is captured in `ThemeRepositoryImpl`'s class-level KDoc.

### §85.9 Files

Six source commits (plus the plan commit and this close-out), all <=5 files per commit:

- `a1e2a02` — plan + commit roadmap (1 file: new `PLAN_theme.md`).
- `4ac0100` — `:domain` foundation (4 files: new `AppTheme.kt` + `ThemeRepository.kt` interface + `ObserveAppThemeUseCase.kt` + `SetAppThemeUseCase.kt`).
- `86a7687` — `:data` strangler-fig impl (1 file: new `ThemeRepositoryImpl.kt`).
- `13828e9` — `:presentation` MVI surface (4 files: new `ThemeState.kt` + `ThemeIntent.kt` + `ThemeEffect.kt` + `ThemeViewModel.kt`).
- `cff1e2c` — `:ui` composable (1 file: new `ThemeScreen.kt`).
- `adcd36b` — `:composeApp` Koin + nav (5 files at the cap: new `ThemeReworkModule.kt` + new `ThemeReworkScreenRoute.kt` + modified `ReworkModules.kt` + modified `Screen.kt` + modified `App.kt`).

### §85.10 Deferrals

- **No i18n lift** — inline literal strings ("Theme" / "Light" / "Dark" / "System" / "Choose your theme"). Phase 10's i18n lift swaps both legacy and rework consumers in one pass.
- **No Material icons** — the rework `:ui` module does not depend on `material-icons-extended`. The legacy onboarding picker's icons (`LightMode`, `DarkMode`, `SettingsBrightness`) are deliberately omitted to preserve classpath consistency across all rework `:ui` screens.
- **No `AnimatedBackground` overlay** — legacy onboarding marketing surface; not part of the rework.
- **No notification-permission grant section** — the legacy onboarding's Theme step also wires a notification-permission grant button + auto-requester. The rework doesn't model permissions at all; that surface is an onboarding concern, not a theme-picker concern.
- **No "Continue" button** — the rework is a standalone surface, not part of a wizard chain.
- **No PureBlack / OLED theme variant** — the legacy app has no such variant today. A future `Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack` slice would add a fourth `AppTheme` variant + a fourth `Tab` + a new pref flow on the legacy `SettingsRepository`. The empty `ThemeEffect` sealed interface is the OCP placeholder for a `ShowError` variant if the future write becomes fallible (e.g., after a DataStore migration).
- **No system uiMode fallback** — `AppTheme.System` defers to the legacy's `followSystem` Boolean; the rework does not query Compose's `isSystemInDarkTheme()` directly. Future Compose-aware theming is a separate slice.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.Theme` stays bound to the onboarding route. Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice; this slice only adds the parallel `Screen.ThemeRework` route.

## §86 — Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack — PureBlack/OLED variant extension on the Theme slice

Follow-on to §85. Where the parent slice landed the Light/Dark/System tri-state picker against the legacy `SettingsRepository`'s `darkModeFlow` + `followSystemFlow` boolean pair, this slice adds the orthogonal **PureBlack/OLED variant** flag — a single Boolean preference that the legacy `SettingsScreen`'s "Pure Black for dark mode" toggle already drove against `SettingsRepository.pureBlackFlow` / `setPureBlack()`. The rework picker now exposes the same toggle inline under the TabRow, sharing the same underlying `SharedPreferences` key.

The slice validates the §85 close-out's prediction that `Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack` would slot in as a small follow-on via the empty `ThemeEffect` sealed interface (OCP placeholder) without ripping out any of the existing MVI surface. In practice the slice landed in 5 commits, not the originally-scoped 7, because two pairs of files collapsed under build-coupling — interface changes force impl changes in the same commit (commit 2 = `:domain` + `:data`), and VM constructor arity changes force the Koin DSL update in the same commit (commit 3 = `:presentation` + Koin module).

### §86.1 What changed

- `:domain` `ThemeRepository` interface grew from 2 methods → 4 methods. The two new members (`observePureBlack(): Flow<Boolean>` + `suspend fun setPureBlack(enabled: Boolean)`) are orthogonal to the existing tri-state pair — they pass through the legacy `SettingsRepository`'s `pureBlackFlow` + `setPureBlack()` verbatim with no Boolean-pair translation.
- `:domain` gains two new use cases: `ObservePureBlackUseCase` (read) + `SetPureBlackUseCase` (write). Both are thin `operator fun invoke()` pass-throughs, mirroring `ObserveAppThemeUseCase` + `SetAppThemeUseCase` from §85.
- `:data` `ThemeRepositoryImpl` overrides the two new methods, each as a one-line delegate to the legacy `SettingsRepository`. The strangler-fig reach into the legacy facade grows from 2-of-13 members → 4-of-13.
- `:presentation` `ThemeState` grows a `pureBlack: Boolean = true` field (first-run default matches `SettingsRepository.isPureBlack()`'s `true` default — existing users see no behaviour change after the rework picker ships).
- `:presentation` `ThemeIntent` grows a new variant `OnTogglePureBlack(val enabled: Boolean) : ThemeIntent`.
- `:presentation` `ThemeViewModel` constructor expands from 2 use cases → 4 use cases. The `init {}` block now launches **two independent** `launchIn` collectors (one per upstream flow) rather than collapsing into a `combine` — see §86.3 for the rationale.
- `:composeApp` `ThemeReworkModule` binds the two new use cases as `factory` and updates the `viewModel { ... }` invocation to the 4-arg VM constructor.
- `:ui` `ThemeScreen` adds a `PureBlackRow` composable under the `TabRow` — a Material 3 `Switch` in a `Row` with the label "Pure Black for dark mode" on the left and the switch on the right. The switch is always interactive (no enabled-state gate on the theme tri-state) — a user can pre-set their PureBlack preference while in Light mode and it persists for the next Dark resolution.

### §86.2 Legacy `SettingsRepository` surface — updated rework reach

The rework now reads + writes through **four** of the legacy facade's ~13 members (up from two in §85):

- `darkModeFlow: Flow<Boolean>` — read by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.observeAppTheme`.
- `followSystemFlow: Flow<Boolean>` — read by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.observeAppTheme`.
- `setDarkMode(value: Boolean)` — sync, called by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.setAppTheme`.
- `setFollowSystem(value: Boolean)` — sync, called by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.setAppTheme`.
- `pureBlackFlow: Flow<Boolean>` (NEW reach) — read by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.observePureBlack`.
- `setPureBlack(value: Boolean)` (NEW reach) — sync, called by `ThemeRepositoryImpl.setPureBlack`.

The remaining ~7 members (firstLaunch, language, notifications, adult-content, etc.) stay on the legacy facade verbatim for OnboardingViewModel, SettingsViewModel, MainActivity's theme observer, and every other legacy consumer.

### §86.3 Why two independent `launchIn` collectors (NOT a `combine`)

The two upstream flows (`observeAppTheme()` returning `Flow<AppTheme>` and `observePureBlack()` returning `Flow<Boolean>`) are **orthogonal**: toggling PureBlack does not affect the theme tri-state, and vice versa. A `combine` would couple them — every PureBlack toggle would re-trigger the theme projection on the downstream, and every theme tap would re-emit the PureBlack value. Two independent `onEach` collectors update only the field they own (`it.copy(theme = ...)` vs `it.copy(pureBlack = ...)`), keeping recompositions minimal and the projection logic trivial.

The `isLoading` flag clears on the FIRST emission from EITHER upstream — once any field has a real value, the screen can render. The remaining default field renders against its initial value until its own upstream emits (which is sub-millisecond after subscription for `SharedPreferences.booleanPrefFlow`, so the user does not perceive a half-loaded state).

### §86.4 Why `OnTogglePureBlack` carries `enabled` (not a "toggle" verb)

The intent variant is `data class OnTogglePureBlack(val enabled: Boolean) : ThemeIntent` — it carries the post-toggle value, not a "flip the current value" verb. The reducer is idempotent regardless of state-vs-intent ordering: a `false → false` write is a no-op at the `SharedPreferences` level (Android's `putBoolean` short-circuits on equal values). Same posture as `OnSelectTheme(theme: AppTheme)` from §85 — both intents are pure "set to value X" verbs.

If the user rapidly double-taps the Switch (off-on-off in <100 ms), the three `viewModelScope.launch { setPureBlack(...) }` calls fire in sequence and the upstream flow re-emits the final value after all three writes settle — the displayed Switch state converges to the final value. No queue-coalescing needed.

### §86.5 PureBlack and the Theme tri-state — interaction rules

The PureBlack flag is **orthogonal** to the theme tri-state at the data layer but has different visual effects depending on the resolved theme at render time:

- **Theme = Dark, PureBlack = true** → dark color scheme uses pure-black (#000000) background. The current YamiTheme already routes through `if (pureBlack) BlackColorScheme else DarkColorScheme` (or the equivalent in the legacy YamiTheme) — the rework picker only **sets the pref**; the actual color-scheme resolution stays in the existing Compose theme code.
- **Theme = Dark, PureBlack = false** → dark color scheme uses standard Material 3 dark variant.
- **Theme = Light, PureBlack = (either)** → light color scheme renders; the PureBlack value persists for the next dark resolution. The Switch remains interactive in Light mode — a user can pre-set their PureBlack preference without first switching to Dark.
- **Theme = System, PureBlack = (either)** → the resolved scheme depends on the system uiMode; if dark, PureBlack drives the dark variant; if light, the PureBlack value persists.

The legacy `SettingsScreen`'s PureBlack toggle has the same always-interactive posture — the rework matches it byte-for-byte.

### §86.6 `:ui` Switch placement and Row shape

The PureBlack toggle lives inside `ThemePickerColumn`, directly below the `TabRow` and above the column's bottom padding. The row shape mirrors the legacy `SettingsScreen`'s PureBlack row:

```kotlin
Row(
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
) {
    Text(
        text = "Pure Black for dark mode",
        style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge,
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
    )
    Switch(
        checked = checked,
        onCheckedChange = onCheckedChange,
    )
}
```

Differences vs the legacy `SettingsScreen`'s row:

- **No leading icon** — the rework `:ui` module does not depend on `material-icons-extended` (same posture as the §85 picker's icon-free tabs and every other rework `:ui` screen).
- **Inline literal label** — `"Pure Black for dark mode"` (no `stringResource` lookup). Phase 10 i18n lift swaps both legacy and rework consumers in one pass.
- **`Modifier.weight(1f)`** on the label so the Switch right-aligns under any container width.

The `ThemePickerColumn`'s `verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.md)` provides the vertical gap between the TabRow and the Switch row — no per-row padding override.

### §86.7 Files

Five commits (plus this close-out), all ≤5 files per commit:

- `1d5ab36` — plan + commit roadmap (1 file: new `PLAN_theme_pureblack.md`).
- `50a4cba` — `:domain` interface extension + `:data` strangler-fig override (4 files: modified `ThemeRepository.kt` + new `ObservePureBlackUseCase.kt` + new `SetPureBlackUseCase.kt` + modified `ThemeRepositoryImpl.kt`). Combined under the same commit because the interface and its impl must move together — every commit must be green.
- `0357582` — `:presentation` MVI extension + Koin DSL update (4 files: modified `ThemeState.kt` + modified `ThemeIntent.kt` + modified `ThemeViewModel.kt` + modified `ThemeReworkModule.kt`). Combined under the same commit because the VM constructor arity change forces the Koin DSL `viewModel { ThemeViewModel(get(), get(), get(), get()) }` update — every commit must be green.
- `70b0532` — `:ui` Switch row addition (1 file: modified `ThemeScreen.kt`).
- This commit — ARCHITECTURE.md §86 + SOLID_AUDIT.md Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack entry.

### §86.8 Deferrals

- **No "PureBlack" tab in the TabRow** — PureBlack is a Boolean variant orthogonal to the tri-state, NOT a fourth tab. Modelling it as a fourth `AppTheme` variant would require the legacy `SettingsRepository` to carry a tri-state OR introduce a sealed PureBlack-aware variant, both of which break the orthogonality. The Switch under the TabRow is the natural shape.
- **No system-uiMode-aware Switch enabled-state gate** — the Switch stays interactive even when the resolved theme is Light. Matches the legacy `SettingsScreen`'s always-interactive posture.
- **No animated transition between standard-dark and pure-black** — toggling the Switch triggers a recomposition through the existing YamiTheme color-scheme selector; Compose's default cross-fade between color schemes handles the visual transition. No additional `AnimatedContent` wrap is introduced.
- **No `ThemeEffect.ShowError` variant added** — the empty `ThemeEffect` sealed interface stays empty. The PureBlack write is a sync `SharedPreferences.putBoolean` whose runtime-failure modes are vanishingly small (same posture as the §85 theme writes). If a future DataStore migration makes either write fallible, a `ShowError` variant slots in via the same OCP placeholder.
- **No i18n lift** — the inline literal "Pure Black for dark mode" string mirrors the legacy `SettingsScreen`'s deferred i18n. Phase 10's i18n lift handles both consumers in one pass.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — both the legacy `SettingsScreen`'s PureBlack toggle and the rework `ThemeScreen`'s Switch are wired against the SAME `pureBlackFlow` + `setPureBlack()` legacy facade calls. Toggling on EITHER surface flips the same `SharedPreferences` key and propagates to the other via upstream flow re-emit. Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice; this slice only extends the existing rework picker.


## §87 — Phase 7.x.about — About screen rework

### §87.1 Strategy

Port the legacy `composeApp/.../features/about/screen/AboutScreen.kt` (the version + actionable-rows screen — Check for update, Rate our app, Whats-new, Source-code, Privacy policy, SocialMediaRow) to the rework Clean Architecture stack (`:domain` → `:data` → `:presentation` → `:ui` → `:composeApp` Koin/nav). The slice ships the four most load-bearing rows (Version, Check for update, Rate our app, Privacy policy) and defers Whats-new, Source-code, the app-icon image, and the SocialMediaRow to follow-on slices — each has a dependency the rework `:ui` module doesn't carry today (`Screen.WhatsNewRework` doesn't exist; Source-code is no-op in the legacy; the app icon needs a `:ui/commonMain/composeResources` binding; SocialMediaRow needs `material-icons-extended` which the rework `:ui` `build.gradle.kts` deliberately omits — same posture as Statistics / History / Updates / Sources / Theme rework screens).

Strangler-fig posture inherited from prior rework slices: `:data` reaches into the legacy `:shared` `core.platform.AppVersionProvider` expect class to read `versionName` + `packageName`. The `:platform/.../version/AppVersionProvider.kt` SPI exists (Phase 5.3 + 5.z.cleanup relocated it) but is not yet Koin-bound; rewiring the `:platform` SPI's Koin graph is a separate `Phase 8.z.platform-rewire` slice that lifts the `IntentLauncher` + `AppVersionProvider` + `ToastShower` triumvirate together once their actuals are confirmed binding-compatible with every existing call site.

### §87.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (3 new files):
- `domain/.../model/about/AppMetadata.kt` — pure value type with two fields (`versionName: String`, `packageName: String`). Non-null per the legacy provider's structural infallibility contract ("unknown" substitution on read failure passes through).
- `domain/.../repository/AboutRepository.kt` — interface with `suspend fun getMetadata(): AppMetadata`. The `suspend` declaration is forward-compatibility for a hypothetical async metadata source (remote build channel lookup); the current legacy provider is synchronous so `:data`'s impl runs without `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`.
- `domain/.../usecase/about/GetAppMetadataUseCase.kt` — `class GetAppMetadataUseCase(private val repository: AboutRepository) { suspend operator fun invoke(): AppMetadata = repository.getMetadata() }`. Thin pass-through, no orchestration today.

**`:data`** (1 new file):
- `data/.../repository/AboutRepositoryImpl.kt` — class takes `legacy: LegacyAppVersionProvider` constructor arg (alias for the legacy `:shared` provider, for the same readability reason as `ThemeRepositoryImpl`'s `as LegacySettingsRepository` alias); `getMetadata()` returns `AppMetadata(versionName = legacy.versionName, packageName = legacy.packageName)`. Body is synchronous despite the `suspend` declaration on the interface — no blocking call happens.

**`:presentation`** (4 new files):
- `presentation/.../about/AboutState.kt` — `data class AboutState(val isLoading: Boolean = true, val versionName: String = "", val packageName: String = "")`. `isLoading` flag exists for forward-compat with a future async metadata source; on the current synchronous provider the loading window is effectively zero frames.
- `presentation/.../about/AboutIntent.kt` — sealed interface with two variants: `OnOpenPlayStore` (data object) and `OnOpenUrl(val url: String)`. The two Play-Store-targeted rows (Check for update + Rate our app) share the same intent because the action is identical; the row label is a pure-display concern owned by `:ui`. The `OnOpenUrl(url)` intent generalises across all URL-launching rows (Privacy policy in this slice; future source-code / changelog rows extend without growing the hierarchy).
- `presentation/.../about/AboutEffect.kt` — sealed interface with two variants: `OpenPlayStorePage(val packageName: String)` and `OpenUrl(val url: String)`. Effects carry only the bare params the platform call needs — strict-MVI Contract §17.
- `presentation/.../about/AboutViewModel.kt` — extends `MviViewModel<AboutState, AboutIntent, AboutEffect>`; constructor takes one dep (`getAppMetadata: GetAppMetadataUseCase`). `init {}` block dispatches `viewModelScope.launch { ... }` that calls the suspend use case once and updates state — same posture as `StatisticsViewModel` and Reader's resume-position pre-load. `handle()` switches on `AboutIntent` and emits the corresponding effect with the param plucked from current state (`OnOpenPlayStore` → `OpenPlayStorePage(state.value.packageName)`) or carried verbatim (`OnOpenUrl(url)` → `OpenUrl(url)`).

**`:ui`** (1 new file):
- `ui/.../about/AboutScreen.kt` — `@Composable` taking `viewModel: AboutViewModel` + `onEffect: (AboutEffect) -> Unit`. `EffectBridge` internal composable collects `viewModel.effects` and forwards each emission to `onEffect`. Renders a Material 3 Card with 4 rows (Version display + 3 actionable rows) inside a Scaffold + TopAppBar. Uses `LocalSpacing` design tokens, MaterialTheme color/typography. NO icons (no `compose.materialIconsExtended` dep — matches Statistics / History / Updates / Sources / Theme). NO app-icon image (no `:ui/commonMain/composeResources` binding for `Res.drawable.ic_launcher_foreground`).

**`:composeApp`** (1 new module + 1 new route + 3 modifications):
- `composeApp/.../di/AboutReworkModule.kt` — declares `single<AboutRepository> { AboutRepositoryImpl(legacy = get()) }` + `factory { GetAppMetadataUseCase(get()) }` + `viewModel { AboutViewModel(get()) }`. The `legacy = get()` resolves to the legacy `:shared` `AppVersionProvider` already bound `single` by `PlatformModule.{android,ios,desktop}.kt`.
- `composeApp/.../di/ReworkModules.kt` — `aboutReworkModule` appended to `allReworkModules()` (9th rework module).
- `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/AboutReworkScreenRoute.kt` — `@Composable` taking `NavController` + `NavBackStackEntry` (both unused — terminal screen). Resolves `AboutViewModel` via `koinViewModel()` + `IntentLauncher` (the legacy `:shared` facade) via `koinInject()`. Bridges effects to the launcher: `OpenPlayStorePage(packageName) → launcher.openPlayStorePage(packageName)`, `OpenUrl(url) → launcher.openUrl(url)`. Both launcher methods are fire-and-forget (failures logged via Kermit, no exceptions propagate) — same posture as every other launcher call site.
- `composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt` — `@Serializable object AboutRework : Screen("...AboutRework")` appended alongside the existing `ThemeRework`, `SourcesRework`, etc. The name diverges from the legacy `AboutScreen` (which already exists at line 52) to avoid collision; the rework convention `<Feature>Rework` matches all prior slices.
- `composeApp/.../App.kt` — `composable<Screen.AboutRework> { AboutReworkScreenRoute(navController, it) }` registered alongside the existing `composable<Screen.AboutScreen>` block. Bottom bar hidden via `SideEffect { onBottomBarVisibleChange(false) }` to mirror the legacy About route.

### §87.3 MVI shape rationale

**Why `init {}`-driven state load (not `OnEnter` intent)**: the metadata is needed unconditionally the moment the screen mounts; an `OnEnter` would just push the trigger to the `:ui`'s `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` for no behavioural gain (the metadata is stable for the running process — re-reads on screen re-entry produce identical values). Same posture as `StatisticsViewModel` / Reader resume-position pre-load.

**Why `viewModelScope.launch { ... }` not `useCase().onEach {...}.launchIn(viewModelScope)`**: `GetAppMetadataUseCase` is a `suspend fun invoke()` returning a single `AppMetadata`, not a `Flow`. A `launch { ... }` captures the result once and updates state once. Same shape as `DetailsViewModel`'s init `loadDetails()` call.

**Why `OnOpenUrl(url: String)` instead of per-target intents like `OnOpenPrivacy` / `OnOpenSourceCode` / `OnOpenChangelog`**: URL-launching is a single side-effect class with a single parameter shape. Splitting into per-target intents would just push the URL string to a `when (intent)` block in `handle()` — same dispatch, more code. Same posture as the Reader's `OnOpenInWebView(url: String)` from Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.openwebview.

**Why no `ShowError` effect**: the legacy `IntentLauncher` actuals are structurally infallible (no exceptions from `openUrl` / `openPlayStorePage` — Android catches `ActivityNotFoundException` internally; iOS / Desktop ignore failures). The rework matches that posture. If a future actual changes its failure contract (remote-URL validation throws on malformed input), `AboutEffect` gains a `ShowError(error: AppError)` variant — strict-MVI OCP §6.

**Why a single `onEffect: (AboutEffect) -> Unit` (not per-effect callbacks like Reader)**: the two AboutEffect variants share the same shape (a String param) and the same target (the legacy `IntentLauncher`). Per-effect callbacks would force the route adapter to plumb two near-identical lambdas (`onOpenPlayStore` + `onOpenUrl`). The single-callback pattern keeps the `AboutScreen` signature stable as new effects are added — adding `OpenSourceCode` etc. doesn't change the function signature, just adds a new `when` arm at the route-adapter call site.

**Why `state.value.packageName` read at emit-time, not captured at intent submission**: if the use case is still in flight when the user taps "Check for update" (effectively impossible given the synchronous nature of the legacy provider, but defensible forward-compat for an async metadata source), `AboutState.packageName` is the empty string and `AboutEffect.OpenPlayStorePage` receives `""`. The legacy `IntentLauncher.openPlayStorePage` actuals tolerate an empty package id (Android builds a malformed Play Store URI and the system launcher refuses; iOS / Desktop fall through to a no-op).

### §87.4 Strangler-fig boundary

The `:data` impl reaches into `:shared`'s legacy `AppVersionProvider` — SAME posture as `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl`, `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl`, `HistoryRepositoryImpl`, `UpdatesRepositoryImpl`, `SourcesRepositoryImpl`, `ThemeRepositoryImpl`. The existing `:data/build.gradle.kts` dependency on `:shared` is already in place; no new build-config changes.

The route adapter (`AboutReworkScreenRoute`) also reaches into `:shared` for the legacy `IntentLauncher` facade via `koinInject()`. Each Phase 5.x SPI relocation (Phase 5.3 for `IntentLauncher`) ports the facade into `:platform` as an interface but does NOT yet bind it to Koin — the rework consumers reach into the legacy facade until `Phase 8.z.platform-rewire` retires the entire legacy facade triumvirate (`IntentLauncher` + `AppVersionProvider` + `ToastShower`) in one pass.
