### §87.7 Deferrals

- **Whats-new row** — requires `Screen.WhatsNewRework` route which doesn't exist yet. A separate `Phase 7.x.whatsnew` slice ports the legacy `WhatsNewScreen` to the rework stack first; the About row then adds `OnOpenWhatsNew : AboutIntent` + `NavigateToWhatsNew : AboutEffect` (or threads a nav callback through the route adapter — pattern TBD when the slice is sequenced).
- **Source-code row** — already disabled in the legacy (no-op click + "soon" subtitle). No behaviour to port. If the source goes public, a single `OnOpenUrl(SOURCE_CODE_URL)` row addition lifts it.
- **App-icon image** — legacy renders `ic_launcher_foreground` PNG at 250.dp at the top of the LazyColumn. The rework `:ui` module doesn't have a compose-resources binding (no `Res.drawable.*` symbols visible in `:ui/commonMain` — those live in `composeApp`). Lifting requires either moving the launcher drawable into `:ui/commonMain/composeResources` (cross-cutting binary change) or threading a `painterResource` from the route adapter (couples `:ui` to `:composeApp`'s resource module). Deferred — visual divergence acknowledged.
- **SocialMediaRow** — needs `material-icons-extended` for Discord / Facebook / Github / Reddit / X brand icons. The rework `:ui` `build.gradle.kts` deliberately omits the extended icon set. Lifts in a follow-on slice once the brand icons are vendored as `:ui`-local `ImageVector` definitions (or `:ui/commonMain/composeResources` SVG assets), avoiding the binary-size cost of pulling the full extended pack for one row.
- **No i18n lift** — the inline string literals ("About", "Version", "Check for update", "Rate our app", "Privacy policy") mirror the legacy's deferred i18n. Phase 10's i18n lift will handle both the legacy and rework consumers in one pass via `stringResource(Res.string.*)`.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.AboutScreen` stays bound to the legacy `AboutScreenRoute`. Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice; this slice only adds the parallel `Screen.AboutRework` route.
- **No `:platform` `IntentLauncher` rewire** — the rework route adapter consumes the legacy `:shared` `IntentLauncher` facade. `Phase 8.z.platform-rewire` lifts the `IntentLauncher` + `AppVersionProvider` + `ToastShower` triumvirate together.

## §88 — Phase 7.x.whatsnew — WhatsNew screen rework

### §88.1 Strategy

Port the legacy `composeApp/.../features/whatsnew/ui/WhatsNewScreen.kt` (HorizontalPager + image/video/list media rendering + fullscreen viewer + auto-trigger gate) to the rework Clean Architecture stack (`:domain` → `:data` → `:presentation` → `:ui` → `:composeApp` Koin/nav). The **foundation slice** ships the title + description + "NEW" chip row surface — the core MVI plumbing, repository contract, strangler-fig adapter, and route adapter — and DEFERS the pager, image rendering, video rendering, fullscreen media viewer, should-show gate, and language localization to follow-on sub-slices. This is the same staged posture as the Details cover/blur/placeholder sequence (Phase 7.x.cover / 7.x.coverblur / 7.x.placeholder / 7.x.blurfade) and the Reader's mode-layout chain.

Strangler-fig posture inherited from prior rework slices, but with the **highest fan-out of any rework `:data` impl to date**: `:data` reaches into FOUR legacy `:shared` collaborators (versus one for About / Theme / Statistics). The four are the legacy `WhatsNewRemoteDataSource` (Ktor JSON fetcher), `SharedPrefsHelper` (mark-seen prefs), `AppVersionProvider` (current `versionName` for the mark-seen write), and the top-level `getDefaultFeatures()` fun (fallback list — currently `emptyList()` post-KMP-port). All four are bound `single` upstream by `SharedModule` / `PlatformModule.*`; no new platform binding required. The fan-out is justified by the legacy `WhatsNewViewModel` owning the SAME collaboration, which this slice ports verbatim.

### §88.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (5 new files):
- `domain/.../model/whatsnew/MediaType.kt` — enum with four variants (`IMAGE`, `VIDEO`, `LIST`, `URL`); ported verbatim from the legacy. Foundation `:ui` ignores the discriminant; carried for follow-on media sub-slices to branch on without a model break.
- `domain/.../model/whatsnew/WhatsNewFeature.kt` — 10-field `data class` ported VERBATIM from the legacy `:shared` model (same field names, nullability, defaults). Verbatim port (not a foundation-scoped subset) prevents the model breaking change that would otherwise hit when media sub-slices land. The foundation `:ui` reads only `title`, `description`, `isNew`; the other seven fields carry zero runtime cost (data-class with default null/empty values).
- `domain/.../repository/WhatsNewRepository.kt` — interface with `suspend fun getFeatures(): List<WhatsNewFeature>` + `suspend fun markSeen()`. Two-method ISP surface. Returns `List<WhatsNewFeature>` not `Result<...>` (empty list IS the "no features" signal; matches legacy fallback posture).
- `domain/.../usecase/whatsnew/GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase.kt` — `class GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase(repository: WhatsNewRepository) { suspend operator fun invoke() = repository.getFeatures() }`. Thin pass-through.
- `domain/.../usecase/whatsnew/MarkWhatsNewSeenUseCase.kt` — same thin-pass-through shape on `repository.markSeen()`.

**`:data`** (1 new file):
- `data/.../repository/WhatsNewRepositoryImpl.kt` — class takes three constructor args (`remoteDataSource: LegacyWhatsNewRemoteDataSource`, `prefs: LegacySharedPrefsHelper`, `appVersionProvider: LegacyAppVersionProvider`) — three of the four `:shared` reaches; the fourth (`getDefaultFeatures()`) is a top-level fun called statically. `getFeatures()` unpacks the legacy `Result<WhatsNewResponse>` via `fold()`, falls back to `getDefaultFeatures()` on failure or empty response, and per-feature wraps the legacy `getLocalizedFeature()` lookup in `runCatching` (legacy parity). Hardcoded language `"en"` (legacy reads `DataStoreHelper.languageFlow.first()` — deferred to `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.i18n`; the fallback chain in `getLocalizedFeature()` makes hardcoded `en` safe for all-language users). `markSeen()` writes the SAME two prefs keys as the legacy VM (`"whats_new_last_shown_version_name"` + `"whats_new_last_shown_timestamp"`) so both routes round-trip. Uses `kotlin.time.Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds()` (with `@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)`) for the timestamp.

**`:presentation`** (4 new files):
- `presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewState.kt` — `data class WhatsNewState(val isLoading: Boolean = true, val features: List<WhatsNewFeature> = emptyList(), val errorMessage: String? = null) : MviState`. Single flat data class (NOT a sealed `Loading`/`Loaded`/`Error` ADT — same posture as `AboutState` / `StatisticsState`). Tab/pager index NOT modelled (deferred to `.pager`); fullscreen-viewer state NOT modelled (deferred to `.fullscreen`).
- `presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewIntent.kt` — sealed interface with two `data object` variants: `OnRetry` (re-runs the suspend fetch) + `OnMarkSeen` (mark-seen prefs write — wired but not auto-triggered by foundation `:ui`, lifts in `.gate`).
- `presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewEffect.kt` — empty sealed interface (zero variants). Same shape as `StatisticsEffect`. Future `OpenFullscreenMedia(...)` variant slots in via `.fullscreen`.
- `presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewViewModel.kt` — extends `MviViewModel<WhatsNewState, WhatsNewIntent, WhatsNewEffect>`; constructor takes two use cases (`GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase`, `MarkWhatsNewSeenUseCase`). `init {}` calls `loadFeatures()`. `handle(intent)` exhaustively dispatches `OnRetry → loadFeatures()` and `OnMarkSeen → markWhatsNewSeen()`. `loadFeatures()` flips `isLoading = true` + `errorMessage = null` before the suspend call so retry shows the loading placeholder during re-fetch.

**`:ui`** (1 new file):
- `ui/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewScreen.kt` — `@Composable` taking `viewModel: WhatsNewViewModel` + `onEffect: (WhatsNewEffect) -> Unit` + `modifier: Modifier = Modifier`. Internal `EffectBridge` composable collects `viewModel.effects` and forwards each emission to `onEffect` (today provably un-invoked). Stateless `WhatsNewScreenContent` renders the 4-state when block: Loading (centered `CircularProgressIndicator`) / Error (Text + Retry button) / Empty ("No new features in this version") / FeatureList (`LazyColumn` of `FeatureCard`s with title + description + optional "NEW" chip). Uses `LocalSpacing` design tokens, MaterialTheme color/typography. NO icons (no `material-icons-extended`), NO compose-resources (no `Res.drawable.*` reach — matches rework `:ui`'s zero-resource posture). Cross-module smart-cast workaround: `errorMessage` extracted to a local `val` before the `when` block — `:ui` can't smart-cast on a public property declared in `:presentation` across module boundaries.

**`:composeApp`** (2 new + 3 modified):
- `composeApp/.../di/WhatsNewReworkModule.kt` (NEW) — `single<WhatsNewRepository> { WhatsNewRepositoryImpl(remoteDataSource = get(), prefs = get(), appVersionProvider = get()) }` + `factory { GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase(get()) }` + `factory { MarkWhatsNewSeenUseCase(get()) }` + `viewModel { WhatsNewViewModel(get(), get()) }`. The three `get()` calls resolve the legacy `:shared` `single`s upstream.
- `composeApp/.../di/ReworkModules.kt` (MOD) — `whatsNewReworkModule` appended to `allReworkModules()` (10th rework module).
- `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute.kt` (NEW) — `@Composable` taking `NavController` + `NavBackStackEntry` (both unused — terminal screen, no outbound nav). Resolves `WhatsNewViewModel` via `koinViewModel()`. Calls `WhatsNewScreen(viewModel = viewModel, onEffect = { _: WhatsNewEffect -> /* no effects emitted in foundation slice */ })`. Provably un-invoked lambda; preserved as the stable callback shape for when `.fullscreen` adds `OpenFullscreenMedia(...)`.
- `composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt` (MOD) — `@Serializable object WhatsNewRework : Screen("...WhatsNewRework")` appended. The legacy `data class WhatsNewScreen(val isFirstOpen: Boolean, ...) : Screen(...)` (at line 36) stays bound — both destinations coexist. Full KDoc covers coexistence + reduced surface + deferrals.
- `composeApp/.../App.kt` (MOD) — `composable<Screen.WhatsNewRework> { backStackEntry -> SideEffect { onBottomBarVisibleChange(false) }; WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute(navController, backStackEntry) }` registered alongside the existing legacy `composable<Screen.WhatsNewScreen>` block. Bottom bar hidden to mirror the legacy WhatsNew route.

### §88.3 MVI shape rationale

**Why `init {}`-driven feature load (not `OnEnter` intent)**: the feature list is needed unconditionally on mount; an `OnEnter` would just push the trigger to the `:ui`'s `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` for no behavioural gain. Same posture as `AboutViewModel` / `StatisticsViewModel`.

**Why `viewModelScope.launch { ... }` not `useCase().onEach {...}.launchIn(viewModelScope)`**: `GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase` is a `suspend fun invoke()` returning a single `List<WhatsNewFeature>`, not a `Flow`. The remote endpoint isn't observed for changes. A `launch { ... }` captures the result once and updates state once. Same shape as `AboutViewModel`'s init `getAppMetadata()` call.

**Why empty `WhatsNewEffect` sealed interface, not omitting the type**: same posture as `StatisticsEffect`. The alternative would force the VM to extend `MviViewModel<WhatsNewState, WhatsNewIntent, Nothing>` — uglier signature, less self-documenting. The empty-sealed-interface pattern documents the slice's extensibility hook: a future `OpenFullscreenMedia(...)` variant slots in without changing the VM's base class or the screen's signature.

**Why `OnMarkSeen` wired now (foundation `:ui` doesn't submit it)**: the use case + repo contract already round-trip with the legacy prefs keys, so adding the intent here keeps the MVI surface complete for the `.gate` sub-slice without forcing a contract bump when it lands. Wired-but-dormant is cheaper than wire-then-bump.

**Why `OnMarkSeen` is `data object` not `data class` carrying a version**: the VM reads the current version from `AppVersionProvider` at the moment the use case fires (the repository contract handles it), NOT from a caller-supplied param. This keeps the `:ui` caller decoupled from the legacy version-string contract. Same pattern as the `WhatsNewRepository.markSeen()` no-param contract.

**Why `OnRetry` flips `isLoading = true` + `errorMessage = null` before the suspend call**: so the `:ui` re-renders the loading placeholder during the re-fetch. Same posture as the legacy `WhatsNewViewModel.retryLoadFeatures()`.

**Why `errorMessage` is null today even on failure**: the `:data` impl currently returns `emptyList()` on any remote failure (the legacy `getDefaultFeatures()` fallback returns empty). The VM treats empty-list as a valid terminal state. When the legacy `getDefaultFeatures()` is repopulated in Phase 10 OR when this slice gains explicit failure surfacing (`Result<List<WhatsNewFeature>>` instead of bare `List<...>`), the VM gains a write path to `errorMessage` and the existing retry button becomes user-visible. The retry path is wired-but-dormant today.

### §88.4 Strangler-fig boundary

The `:data` impl reaches into `:shared` FOUR times — the highest fan-out of any rework `:data` impl to date. The four reaches are:
1. `LegacyWhatsNewRemoteDataSource` (Ktor JSON fetcher) — constructor-injected, `get()`-resolved.
2. `LegacySharedPrefsHelper` (mark-seen prefs) — constructor-injected, `get()`-resolved.
3. `LegacyAppVersionProvider` (current `versionName`) — constructor-injected, `get()`-resolved.
4. `legacyGetDefaultFeatures` (top-level fallback fun) — called statically, no DI binding needed.

All four were already in the legacy `WhatsNewViewModel`'s constructor; the strangler-fig posture is structurally faithful. SAME boundary discipline as `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` / `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl` / `HistoryRepositoryImpl` / `UpdatesRepositoryImpl` / `SourcesRepositoryImpl` / `ThemeRepositoryImpl` / `AboutRepositoryImpl` — multiplied by four reaches instead of one. No `:domain` interface leakage of legacy types; aliases (`as LegacyX`) call out the boundary at every reach.

The route adapter does NOT reach into `:shared` (no `IntentLauncher`, no `WhatsNewRemoteDataSource`) — the foundation slice has no external-launch effects. When `.fullscreen` lands, the adapter gains a `koinInject<MediaPlayerSpi>()` resolution; until then the route adapter is the cleanest possible shape.

### §88.7 Deferrals

- **HorizontalPager** — legacy renders features in a horizontal pager with tab indicators. Foundation renders a flat `LazyColumn`. `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.pager` adds a `currentPage: Int` field to state + `OnPageChanged(index: Int)` intent + the `HorizontalPager` composable surface — strict-MVI OCP §6 additive change.
- **Image rendering** — legacy renders `imageResName` (compose-resources drawable) + `imageUrl` (Coil) inside each feature card. Foundation cards are text-only. `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.images` adds the Coil `AsyncImage` for `imageUrl` and a compose-resources binding for `imageResName` (requires moving the WhatsNew drawables into `:ui/commonMain/composeResources` or threading `painterResource` from the route adapter — same trade-off the About slice deferred).
- **Video rendering** — legacy renders `videoUrl` via a platform `VideoPlayer` composable. The rework `:platform` module doesn't have a `MediaPlayer` SPI today. `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.video` adds the SPI + actuals + Compose surface.
- **FullscreenMediaViewer** — legacy carries `isFullscreenViewerOpen` / `currentMediaItems` / `currentMediaIndex` in state and renders a fullscreen overlay on tap. `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.fullscreen` adds the overlay + the `OpenFullscreenMedia(...)` effect variant + the route-adapter dispatch.
- **Should-show auto-trigger gate** — legacy compares the current `versionName` to the last-seen prefs and auto-navigates to WhatsNew on app launch if the version is new. The rework slice ships the `markSeen()` write but no `observeShouldShow(): Flow<Boolean>` read. `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.gate` adds the read + a `NavigateToWhatsNew` effect on the rework About / Home screen's MVI surface, NOT on `WhatsNewEffect` itself.
- **Language localization** — `:data` impl hardcodes `"en"`. Legacy reads `DataStoreHelper.languageFlow.first()`. `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.i18n` threads the language flow into the repository (or, more likely, lifts in tandem with Phase 10's broader i18n lift via `stringResource(Res.string.*)`).
- **About row wire-up** — Phase 7.x.about deferred the "What's new" row because `Screen.WhatsNewRework` didn't exist. With this slice landed, the About row can now wire up `OnOpenWhatsNew : AboutIntent` + `NavigateToWhatsNew : AboutEffect` (or thread a nav callback through the About route adapter) as a follow-on cross-cutting slice. **Closed by Phase 7.x.about.whatsnewrow (§89).**
- **No i18n lift** — inline string literals ("Loading...", "No new features in this version", "Retry", "NEW") mirror the legacy's deferred i18n.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.WhatsNewScreen` stays bound to the legacy `WhatsNewScreenRoute`. Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice.


## §89 — Phase 7.x.about.whatsnewrow — wire deferred Whats-new row on rework About screen

Phase 7.x.about (§87) ported the legacy About screen to the rework stack but deliberately deferred four rows — Whats-new, Source-code, SocialMediaRow, and the app-icon image. The Whats-new deferral was specifically because `Screen.WhatsNewRework` didn't exist — porting a row that navigates to a nonexistent destination would either require a placeholder TODO or block on a separate slice. Phase 7.x.whatsnew (§88, commit `e5d91b0`) shipped the `Screen.WhatsNewRework` + `WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute` foundation, unblocking the row. This slice closes the cross-cutting loop.

### §89.1 Strategy

Additive MVI surface extension — grow the existing `AboutIntent` / `AboutEffect` sealed hierarchies by one variant each, grow the `AboutViewModel.handle()` `when` block by one arm, add a single `AboutRow` to `AboutScreen` between "Privacy policy" and the package label footer, and dispatch the new effect from the `AboutReworkScreenRoute` adapter via `navController.navigate(Screen.WhatsNewRework)`. The route adapter's `navController` parameter changes from `@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER")` to actually-used. No new layer reaches; no new modules touched; no new use cases or repos needed.

This is the smallest-possible follow-on slice: 5 source files at the standing cap, plus plan + close-out docs.

### §89.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces (5 file changes)

**`:presentation`** (3 mods):

- `AboutIntent.kt` — add `data object OnOpenWhatsNew : AboutIntent`. Parameterless: the target route is a parameterless `Screen.WhatsNewRework` object. KDoc updated to mention the third variant + the lifted Phase 7.x.about deferral.
- `AboutEffect.kt` — add `data object NavigateToWhatsNew : AboutEffect`. Parameterless: the route adapter holds the `Screen` ADT + `NavController` reference. KDoc updated to describe the route-adapter contract.
- `AboutViewModel.kt` — add `AboutIntent.OnOpenWhatsNew → emit(AboutEffect.NavigateToWhatsNew)` arm in the exhaustive `when (intent)` block. KDoc updated to describe the third intent → effect dispatch.

**`:ui`** (1 mod):

- `AboutScreen.kt` — add `AboutRow(title = "What's new", onClick = { onIntent(AboutIntent.OnOpenWhatsNew) })` between "Privacy policy" and the package-label footer Spacer (with an `AboutRowDivider` between Privacy policy and Whats-new). Row count grows from 4 to 5. KDoc visual-delta section updated: legacy delta now lists Source-code + SocialMediaRow + app-icon image only; Whats-new noted as RESTORED with cross-reference to Phase 7.x.whatsnew's foundation commit (`e5d91b0`).

**`:composeApp`** (1 mod):

- `AboutReworkScreenRoute.kt` — add `AboutEffect.NavigateToWhatsNew → navController.navigate(Screen.WhatsNewRework)` arm in the `when (effect)` block. Remove `@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER")` from `navController` (now used). Add `import me.manga.kira.navigation.Screen`. KDoc updated to mention the new in-app outbound edge + cross-reference to Phase 7.x.whatsnew.

### §89.3 MVI shape rationale — per-target `data object` over generic `OnOpenScreen(target: Screen)`

`OnOpenWhatsNew` carries no params (the target route is a parameterless `Screen.WhatsNewRework` object). `NavigateToWhatsNew` also carries no params (the route adapter knows the target destination). Both fit as `data object` cleanly, matching the existing `OnOpenPlayStore` pattern in this slice's sibling variants.

A generic "navigate-to" intent / effect with a `Screen` payload was rejected because:

1. **Layer-dependency reversal** — `Screen` is a `:composeApp`-layer type. Pulling it into `:presentation` would reverse the layer-dependency arrow (`:presentation` is currently `:composeApp`-free; only the route adapter at `:composeApp` knows the `Screen` ADT).
2. **Pattern consistency** — the other rework slices that need in-app nav (Reader → next chapter, Details → reader entry) all use per-target effects, not a generic carrier.
3. **OCP-friendly explicit dispatch** — adding per-row intents is cheap (one `data object` + one `when` arm), and each new row gets explicit dispatch logic at every layer. No implicit "navigate-anywhere" hatch that could grow into a general nav escape valve.

Similarly, the rework `AboutScreen` keeps its single `onEffect: (AboutEffect) -> Unit` callback rather than growing per-effect callbacks (`onNavigateToWhatsNew: () -> Unit`). The single-callback pattern keeps `AboutScreen(viewModel, onEffect, modifier)` stable as new effects are added — same posture as the Reader's effect-callback channel decision (Phase 7.x.reader.modelayout.openwebview §7.x.reader.modelayout.openwebview).

### §89.4 Strangler-fig boundary

ZERO new `:shared` reaches. This is pure in-stack rework cross-cutting — the route adapter already knew about `NavController` (every other rework route adapter that has in-app nav uses it the same way); we add one more `navigate(Screen.X)` call. No legacy facade extension; no new `:data` → `:shared` edge.

## §90 — Phase 7.x.whatsnew.pager — HorizontalPager + page indicator dots on rework WhatsNew

Lifts the legacy `WhatsNewScreen`'s `HorizontalPager` swipe-through-features layout onto the rework foundation. Replaces the foundation's flat `LazyColumn` with a bi-directionally-synced `androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager` + an inline page-indicator dot row beneath the pager. VM gains a `currentPage: Int = 0` state field + a `data class OnPageChanged(val index: Int)` intent arm. NavigationButtons (legacy left/right arrows) and NewChip spacer polish + version-grouped headers DEFERRED to the corresponding sub-slices.

### §90.1 Strategy

Same shape as the prior WhatsNew foundation slice — additive change to the existing state / intent / VM trio + a single-file `:ui` composable edit. No legacy reach (the pager is a Compose-Foundation primitive that's already on the `:ui` classpath via `:ui:commonMain` — the Reader uses `HorizontalPager` / `VerticalPager` / `rememberPagerState` at `ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt:23-25`, so no new dependency is added).

**Bi-directional sync between VM state and Compose-side pager state**:
- **Seed** (VM → Compose): `rememberPagerState(initialPage = state.currentPage.coerceIn(0, ...), pageCount = { features.size })` reads `state.currentPage` on first composition.
- **Mirror** (Compose → VM): `LaunchedEffect(pagerState.currentPage) { onPageChanged(pagerState.currentPage) }` dispatches `WhatsNewIntent.OnPageChanged(index)` on every user swipe.
- **No oscillation**: the VM writes the new index back into `state.currentPage` via `updateState { it.copy(currentPage = intent.index) }`, but on the next recomposition the seed value is value-equal to `pagerState.currentPage`, so `rememberPagerState` does NOT re-init (the `remember` block runs once per composition). The mirror dispatches the same index back, which the VM compares-and-equals and short-circuits.

**Why VM-owned `currentPage` rather than purely Compose-owned `rememberPagerState`** — the pager's `rememberSaveable`-backed state already survives Compose recomposition and most config changes. Layering a VM mirror adds belt-and-suspenders coverage for cross-screen restoration (e.g., a future "deep link to feature N" intent variant) and keeps the MVI surface honest — strict-MVI contract §6 requires VM-observable state to live in the State data class, not in Compose local state. Same posture as the Reader's `currentPageIndex` VM mirror (Phase 7.x.reader.resumeposition, §74).

### §90.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces (4 source files modified)

1. **`presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewState.kt`** — adds `val currentPage: Int = 0` field. KDoc lifts the "tab/pager index NOT modelled in foundation" deferral block to the "Pager index now modelled (Phase 7.x.whatsnew.pager)" rationale. Strict-MVI contract §17 preserved — pure value type, default sensible, no banned features (no `Any` / `!!` / `lateinit`).
2. **`presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewIntent.kt`** — adds `data class OnPageChanged(val index: Int) : WhatsNewIntent`. KDoc lifts the "Why no `OnPageChanged` in foundation" deferral block to a rationale describing the bi-directional sync. Strict-MVI contract §6 OCP — additive, foundation's `OnRetry` / `OnMarkSeen` arms unchanged.
3. **`presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewViewModel.kt`** — adds `is OnPageChanged → updateState { it.copy(currentPage = intent.index) }` when arm. No suspending work, no effect emission. KDoc grows a paragraph documenting the LaunchedEffect-driven dispatch + the belt-and-suspenders rationale.
4. **`ui/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewScreen.kt`** — replaces the private `FeatureList` composable (`LazyColumn` + `items`) with a private `FeaturePager` composable (`HorizontalPager` + `LaunchedEffect`-driven mirror + page-indicator dot row). Adds private `PageIndicatorRow` composable for the dot row. Imports `androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager` + `rememberPagerState` + `androidx.compose.foundation.shape.CircleShape` + `androidx.compose.foundation.layout.size`; removes `androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn` + `androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.items`. KDoc lifts the "No HorizontalPager" deferral block to a "HorizontalPager added in Phase 7.x.whatsnew.pager" rationale that explicitly notes the NavigationButtons (legacy arrows) are NOT ported (swipe + dots + system back are sufficient navigation surface).

### §90.3 MVI shape rationale

**Why `data class OnPageChanged(val index: Int)` not `data class OnPageChanged(val page: WhatsNewFeature)`** — the pager indexes into `state.features` (no out-of-band feature list). Carrying the index is sufficient; carrying the resolved feature would require the VM to look up the index again to write to `state.currentPage`, defeating the purpose. Same posture as the Reader's `OnPageChanged(val pageIndex: Int)` MVI shape (Phase 7.x.reader.resumeposition, §74).

**Why a `data class` not a `data object` per index** — pager indices are integers, not finite enumerations. A `data class OnPageChanged(val index: Int)` collapses the variant explosion (cf. the Reader's `OnPageChanged` shape). The sealed interface's other arms remain `data object` (the foundation's `OnRetry` / `OnMarkSeen` carry no payload).

### §90.4 Strangler-fig boundary

**ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches** — same posture as Phase 7.x.about.whatsnewrow (§89.4). This slice is pure in-stack rework cross-cutting:
- `:presentation` adds one state field + one intent variant + one VM when arm — all `:domain`-typed.
- `:ui` swaps `LazyColumn` for `HorizontalPager` — both Compose-Foundation primitives, no new dep.
- The new field is consumed by `:ui`-local Compose state; the new intent is dispatched from `:ui`-local Compose state into the VM.

No legacy `:shared` `WhatsNewState.currentPage` is read (the legacy holds its own pager state outside the rework MVI graph); no legacy `WhatsNewViewModel.onPageChanged` is reached for parity; the rework owns its own bi-directional sync end-to-end.

## §91 — Phase 7.x.whatsnew.polish — NewChip horizontal spacer fix

Closes the cosmetic-polish deferral noted in §90.7. The foundation slice's `FeatureCard` composable (rendering one [WhatsNewFeature] in the LazyColumn / now-pager surface) contained a no-op `Spacer(Modifier.height(0.dp))` inside the `if (feature.isNew)` branch — a vertical spacer of height zero inside a horizontal Row, which renders nothing and provides no visual separation between the feature title text and the `NEW` chip. The fix swaps the modifier for `Modifier.width(spacing.sm)` so the `NEW` chip sits with a small horizontal gap from the trailing edge of the title text (after `.weight(1f)` resolution).

### §91.1 Strategy

Single-line modifier swap in `ui/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewScreen.kt:358`:

```kotlin
// Before — no-op vertical spacer in a horizontal Row
if (feature.isNew) {
    Spacer(Modifier.height(0.dp))
    NewChip()
}

// After — horizontal spacer adding breathing room
if (feature.isNew) {
    Spacer(Modifier.width(spacing.sm))
    NewChip()
}
```

The existing `Spacer(Modifier.height(spacing.sm))` BELOW the row (between the title row and the description Text) still uses `.height` correctly, so the `.height` import is preserved. ONLY a `.width` import is added.

## §92 — Phase 7.x.language — Language picker screen rework (foundation)

### §92.1 Strategy

Port the legacy `composeApp/.../features/language/ui/screens/LanguageSelectionScreen.kt` (LazyColumn of 11 supported-language rows + Request-New-Language row + FeedbackDialog + ComplaintViewModel-driven submit + SnackbarHost result chrome) to the rework Clean Architecture stack (`:domain` → `:data` → `:presentation` → `:ui` → `:composeApp` Koin/nav). The **foundation slice** ships the picker-only surface — 11 native-endonym rows with tap-to-select + a trailing "✓" Text glyph on the selected row — and DEFERS the entire FeedbackDialog + ComplaintViewModel + SnackbarHost + Request-New-Language row to a follow-on `Phase 7.x.language.request` sub-slice. Same staged posture as Phase 7.x.whatsnew (§88) — ship the load-bearing surface first, defer the cross-cutting cosmetic-and-dialog chrome.

Strangler-fig posture inherited from prior rework slices: `:data` reaches into ONE legacy `:shared` collaborator (the `SettingsRepository` facade — same shape as the Theme slice's reach into the same facade for `darkModeFlow`/`setDarkMode`). The `LanguageRepositoryImpl` constructor takes `legacy: SettingsRepository`; the rework `:domain` interface exposes three load-bearing methods (`getSupportedLanguages(): List<Language>`, `observeSelectedLanguage(): Flow<String>`, `setLanguage(code: String)`). Locale-switch side effect (`core.locale.applyApplicationLocale(tag)` — expect/actual ported in Phase 5.6) is invoked directly from `:data`'s `setLanguage()` after the DataStore write, matching the legacy posture (where the legacy `LanguageSelectionScreen` calls `applyApplicationLocale` directly from its `onSelected` lambda).

### §92.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (5 new files — commit `d71cb9c`):
- `domain/.../model/language/Language.kt` — 2-field `data class` (`code: String` IETF tag, `displayName: String` native endonym). NOT a sealed hierarchy keyed by `LanguageCategory` — the legacy list is flat; a sealed-class wrap would force an upstream contract bump.
- `domain/.../repository/LanguageRepository.kt` — 3-method interface. `getSupportedLanguages()` returns `List<Language>` (sync read — the list is a compile-time constant in the `:data` impl's `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` map, not an upstream observable). `observeSelectedLanguage()` returns `Flow<String>` (mirrors `SettingsRepository.languageFlow`). `setLanguage(code: String)` suspends.
- `domain/.../usecase/language/GetSupportedLanguagesUseCase.kt` — thin pass-through (`operator fun invoke() = repository.getSupportedLanguages()`). Used at VM construction time to seed `LanguageState.languages`.
- `domain/.../usecase/language/ObserveSelectedLanguageUseCase.kt` — thin pass-through to `repository.observeSelectedLanguage()`.
- `domain/.../usecase/language/SetLanguageUseCase.kt` — thin suspend pass-through.

**`:data`** (1 new file — commit `24888e1`):
- `data/.../repository/LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt` — class takes `legacy: SettingsRepository` constructor arg. Owns the `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` compile-time constant (11 entries — `en`, `ar`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `in`, `it`, `ja`, `pt`, `ru`, `tr` — matching the legacy `Res.array.supported_languages` + `LANGUAGE_DISPLAY_NAMES` map's endonyms verbatim). `getSupportedLanguages()` returns the constant. `observeSelectedLanguage()` returns `legacy.languageFlow`. `setLanguage(code)` writes through `legacy.setLanguage(code)` THEN calls top-level `core.locale.applyApplicationLocale(code)`. The two-step ordering (persist first, then locale-switch) is the legacy posture verbatim and is load-bearing — if the locale-switch threw and the persist hadn't happened, the user would see the OLD language back on app restart.

**`:presentation`** (4 files, 3 new + 1 KDoc-modified — commit `731c88c`):
- `presentation/.../language/LanguageState.kt` (already existed from earlier MVI slice — KDoc-only modification this slice): `data class LanguageState(val isLoading: Boolean = true, val languages: List<Language> = emptyList(), val selectedCode: String = "")`. Single flat data class. KDoc updated to reflect the `initialState = LanguageState(languages = getSupportedLanguages())` constructor-time seed posture (sync read, no `OnEnter` intent needed for the supported list).
- `presentation/.../language/LanguageIntent.kt` (NEW): sealed interface with one variant — `data class OnSelectLanguage(val code: String) : LanguageIntent`. Adding a future `OnResetToSystem` slots in as a sealed-interface extension.
- `presentation/.../language/LanguageEffect.kt` (NEW): empty sealed interface (zero variants). Same shape as `StatisticsEffect` / `WhatsNewEffect`. The `Phase 7.x.language.request` sub-slice adds `OpenRequestDialog` + `RequestSubmitted(result: ComplaintResult)` variants here without breaking the existing route-adapter shape.
- `presentation/.../language/LanguageViewModel.kt` (NEW): extends `MviViewModel<LanguageState, LanguageIntent, LanguageEffect>`. Constructor takes `getSupportedLanguages: GetSupportedLanguagesUseCase`, `observeSelectedLanguage: ObserveSelectedLanguageUseCase`, `private val setLanguage: SetLanguageUseCase`. `initialState = LanguageState(languages = getSupportedLanguages())` — the supported list is populated AT CONSTRUCTION TIME via the sync use case. `init {}` launches `observeSelectedLanguage().onEach { code -> updateState { it.copy(isLoading = false, selectedCode = code) } }.launchIn(viewModelScope)` so the picker reactively reflects in-flight writes (and writes from the legacy route). `handle(intent)` exhaustively dispatches `OnSelectLanguage(code) → viewModelScope.launch { setLanguage(intent.code) }`.

Internal stateless `LanguageScreenContent(state, onIntent, modifier)` for preview/test substitution (same convention as other rework screens). `Scaffold(topBar = { TopAppBar(title = { Text("Language") }) })` body branches on `state.isLoading`: a centered `CircularProgressIndicator` while loading, otherwise `LanguageList` (Material 3 `LazyColumn`). Each row (`LanguageRow` private composable) shows the native endonym (`bodyLarge`) + the IETF code caption (`bodySmall onSurfaceVariant`), with a trailing fixed-size `Box(Modifier.size(24.dp))` slot reserving space for the icon and rendering a `Text("✓", titleMedium, primary)` ONLY when `selected = code == state.selectedCode`. The trailing-Box-always-reserves-space invariant matches the legacy `StatsItem` posture and prevents row-height jump on re-tap. NO Material `Icon` — the `:ui` module has no `material-icons-*` artifact (same Text-glyph posture as `ReaderScreen`'s "⋯" overflow); deliberate. NO compose-resources (no `Res.string.*` reach — defers Phase 10 i18n). NO Request-New-Language row + NO FeedbackDialog + NO SnackbarHost (defers to `.request` sub-slice).

The one `get()` for `legacy` resolves the legacy `SettingsRepository` `single` from `SharedModule`.

Resolves `LanguageViewModel` via `koinViewModel()`. Calls `LanguageScreen(viewModel = viewModel)`. Bottom bar hidden to mirror the legacy Language route.

### §92.3 MVI shape rationale

**Why `initialState = LanguageState(languages = getSupportedLanguages())` (NOT `init {}`-populated)**: the supported list is a compile-time constant in the `:data` impl (the `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` map). The sync use case reads the constant; passing it through the `initialState` constructor arg means the list is present in state from FRAME 1 — no loading-flicker on the language rows, only on the selected-row indicator. The `isLoading = true` default ONLY gates the spinner-vs-rows branch; once the upstream `languageFlow` emits its first value, `isLoading` flips to `false` and the "✓" indicator appears on the selected row. Same pattern as the Theme slice's `initialDarkMode` seed.

**Why `observeSelectedLanguage()` is `Flow<String>` (NOT `Flow<Language?>`)**: the upstream `SettingsRepository.languageFlow` is `Flow<String>` with `""` empty-default — wrapping it in a nullable `Language?` projection would force a `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.firstOrNull { it.code == flow }` lookup inside the `:data` impl, but the picker's predicate is `language.code == state.selectedCode`, which is cheaper as a bare string compare. The `:domain` interface stays clean by exposing the raw IETF tag.

**Why `viewModelScope.launch { setLanguage(intent.code) }` (NOT `flow { setLanguage(...); emit(Unit) }.launchIn(...)`)**: the `setLanguage` use case is a `suspend fun`, not a `Flow`. The fire-and-forget `launch` matches the established posture for one-shot writes (same shape as `ThemeViewModel.handle(OnSelectThemeMode)`). The upstream `languageFlow` re-emits after the write, which is how the picker updates the selected row — the VM doesn't need to manually `updateState` after the write.

**Why empty `LanguageEffect` sealed interface (NOT omitted)**: same posture as `StatisticsEffect` / `WhatsNewEffect`. The alternative would force the VM to extend `MviViewModel<LanguageState, LanguageIntent, Nothing>` — uglier signature, less self-documenting. The empty-sealed-interface pattern documents the slice's extensibility hook: a future `OpenRequestDialog` (for the `.request` sub-slice) slots in without changing the VM's base class or the screen's signature.

**Why `OnSelectLanguage` is `data class` carrying `code: String` (NOT `data object`)**: the picker has 11 rows; the intent must carry which one was tapped. A bare `data object` would force the VM to read selection from an external source. The `code: String` payload is the minimal MVI surface — string instead of `Language` to keep `:presentation` free of the data-class indirection.

### §92.4 Strangler-fig boundary

The `:data` impl reaches into `:shared` ONCE — the legacy `SettingsRepository` facade (which owns the DataStore-backed `languageFlow` + `setLanguage(code)` pair through `DataStoreHelper.languageFlow`). SAME boundary discipline as `ThemeRepositoryImpl` (which reaches the same facade for `darkModeFlow`/`setDarkMode`). The legacy `SettingsRepository` is bound `single` by `SharedModule.kt`; the rework module's `single<LanguageRepository> { LanguageRepositoryImpl(legacy = get()) }` resolves it without any new platform binding.

The `core.locale.applyApplicationLocale(tag)` expect/actual is invoked DIRECTLY from `:data`'s `setLanguage()` — it's a top-level fun (Phase 5.6 port), NOT a Koin binding. The Android actual delegates to `AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales`; iOS/Desktop are no-ops per the `LocaleSwitcher.kt` KDoc.

The legacy `Screen.LanguageScreen` route + the rework `Screen.LanguageRework` route consume the SAME underlying DataStore-backed pref through the legacy facade — picking a language in either route writes the same IETF tag, AND triggers the same `applyApplicationLocale` side effect, AND the other screen reflects it via the upstream `languageFlow` re-emit. Round-trip parity is structural (single source of truth).

The route adapter does NOT reach into `:shared` (no `IntentLauncher`, no `ComplaintViewModel`, no `SnackbarHost`) — the foundation slice has no external launches and no dialog chrome. When `.request` lands, the adapter gains `koinInject<ComplaintViewModel>()` + a `LocalSnackbarHostState.current` reach; until then the route adapter is the thinnest possible shape on the entire rework graph.

## §93 — Phase 7.x.language.request — Request-Language dialog + Snackbar feedback

### §93.1 Strategy

Closes the biggest deferral from §92.7 (Phase 7.x.language). The foundation slice shipped the Language picker `:domain` + `:data` + `:presentation` + `:ui` + `:composeApp` wiring with an EMPTY `LanguageEffect` sealed interface and only one `LanguageIntent` variant (`OnSelectLanguage`). The "Request a language" footer row + FeedbackDialog + ComplaintViewModel + SnackbarHost surface from the legacy `LanguageSelectionScreen` were intentionally deferred — they are wholly cross-cutting (legacy reaches `:shared`'s `ComplaintViewModel` + `UserIdProvider` + `DeviceInfoProvider` + 3 ComplaintRepository methods), and bundling them with the foundation would have blown the 5-file/commit cap.

This sub-slice ports the deferred surface as an **append-only OCP extension**:
- `:domain` gains a new `FeedbackRepository` interface (one method: `sendLanguageRequest(body): Result<Unit>`) + a new `SendLanguageRequestUseCase`.
- `:data` gains a new `FeedbackRepositoryImpl` that strangler-figs over the legacy `:shared` types — same posture as Phase 6.4.x.statistics's `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl`.
- `:presentation` extends the existing `LanguageState` (+ 3 fields), `LanguageIntent` (+ 4 variants), `LanguageEffect` (+ 2 variants), `LanguageViewModel` (+ 1 ctor param + 4 `when` branches) — NO file replacement; pure append-only.
- `:ui` extends the existing `LanguageScreen` (+ footer row + AlertDialog + SnackbarHost) — same file, additive edit.
- `:composeApp` extends the existing `languageReworkModule` (+ FeedbackRepository binding + 1 use case factory + 1 ctor arg in the VM `viewModel { ... }`) — same file, additive edit.

Block-and-ask triggers (a-d) NOT met: (a) no contract library introduced — `FeedbackRepository` is a new interface, but its dep posture matches the established strangler-fig pattern documented in §92.4 and §70 (Phase 6.4.x.statistics's `ReadingSessionRepository`); (b) no observable behaviour change — legacy `Screen.LanguageScreen` and the legacy FeedbackDialog/`ComplaintViewModel.submit` path are untouched; the rework route now hosts its own Request-Language flow that writes to the SAME Firestore collection with the SAME `userId`/`type`/`subject`/`metadata` shape (the admin dashboard reads either path's submissions identically); (c) no compile risk — all 4 build gates green after every commit; (d) no SOLID violation — `FeedbackRepository` is single-method (ISP), `FeedbackRepositoryImpl` is single-responsibility (assemble + forward Complaint), the use case is a thin pass-through (SRP).

### §93.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (2 new files):
- `repository/FeedbackRepository.kt` — single-method interface:
  ```kotlin
  interface FeedbackRepository {
      suspend fun sendLanguageRequest(body: String): Result<Unit>
  }
  ```
  KDoc rationale: language-specific (not a general "feedback") interface — keeps the contract narrow per ISP. A future `sendBugReport` / `sendFeatureRequest` should be a SIBLING method on this interface OR a sibling interface if signatures diverge. The single-method shape today reflects the single user-visible action.
- `usecase/feedback/SendLanguageRequestUseCase.kt` — thin pass-through:
  ```kotlin
  class SendLanguageRequestUseCase(private val feedbackRepository: FeedbackRepository) {
      suspend operator fun invoke(body: String): Result<Unit> = feedbackRepository.sendLanguageRequest(body)
  }
  ```

**`:data`** (1 new file):
- `repository/FeedbackRepositoryImpl.kt` — strangler-fig over THREE legacy `:shared` types:
  ```kotlin
  @OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)
  class FeedbackRepositoryImpl(
      private val sendComplaint: LegacySendComplaintUseCase,  // me.manga.kira.presentation.features.complaint.usecase.SendComplaintUseCase
      private val userIdProvider: UserIdProvider,             // me.manga.kira.domain.auth.UserIdProvider
      private val deviceInfoProvider: DeviceInfoProvider,     // me.manga.kira.domain.device.DeviceInfoProvider
  ) : FeedbackRepository {
      override suspend fun sendLanguageRequest(body: String): Result<Unit> = runCatching {
          val complaint = Complaint(
              userId = userIdProvider.getUserId(),
              type = ComplaintType.LANGUAGES,
              subject = LANGUAGES_SUBJECT,                    // hardcoded "Languages"
              body = body,
              createdAt = Clock.System.now(),
              status = ComplaintStatus.OPEN,
              metadata = deviceInfoProvider.getDeviceMetadata(),
          )
          sendComplaint(complaint)
          Unit
      }
      private companion object { const val LANGUAGES_SUBJECT = "Languages" }
  }
  ```
  - **3-dep fan-in** mirrors the legacy `ComplaintViewModel.submit` orchestration (lines 52-72 of the legacy file) — preserves observable behaviour identically.
  - **`runCatching {}`** uniforms the `Result<Unit>` wrapping. The legacy `SendComplaintUseCase` returns the Firestore doc ID (`String`); the rework discards it (the doc ID isn't surfaced to the user, and the success effect is a content-less `data object`).
  - **Subject hardcoded "Languages"** (the legacy ComplaintViewModel passes the i18n'd `Res.string.languages` lookup; the rework hardcodes the English literal for Phase 10 i18n lift — same deferral posture as the rest of the rework slices' inline literals).
  - **`Clock.System.now()`** with `@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)` — Phase 4 batch 4.4 KMP-portable time API.

**`:presentation`** (4 modified files):
- `language/LanguageState.kt` — appended 3 fields: `requestDialogVisible: Boolean = false`, `requestText: String = ""`, `requestSubmitting: Boolean = false`. Defaults preserve the foundation contract — first-run state is identical.
- `language/LanguageIntent.kt` — appended 4 variants:
  - `OnOpenRequestDialog` (data object) — opens the dialog + clears `requestText` + clears `requestSubmitting`.
  - `OnDismissRequestDialog` (data object) — closes the dialog. Does NOT clear `requestSubmitting` — if an in-flight submission completes after dismissal, the resulting effect still shows on the underlying picker.
  - `OnRequestTextChange(text: String)` (data class) — per-keystroke text update.
  - `OnSubmitRequest` (data object) — sends the current `requestText`.
- `language/LanguageEffect.kt` — replaced the empty sealed interface with `RequestSubmitted` (data object) + `RequestFailed` (data object). Why effects (not state flags): one-shot semantics + UNLIMITED-capacity Channel survives transient view detachment (config change, navigation away/back). State flags would also survive but require manual reset.
- `language/LanguageViewModel.kt` — appended `private val sendLanguageRequest: SendLanguageRequestUseCase` as the 4th ctor param + 4 new `when` branches in `handle()`. `OnSubmitRequest` guards re-entrance (`if (state.value.requestSubmitting) return`), then launches fire-and-forget in `viewModelScope` so `handle()` returns promptly to keep `submit(intent)` non-blocking. `Result<Unit>.isSuccess` folds into a state-update + effect-emission pair (close dialog + clear text on success; preserve text on failure).

**`:ui`** (1 modified file):
- `language/LanguageScreen.kt` — three additions:
  1. `LanguageScreenContent` gained an `effects: Flow<LanguageEffect>` parameter (analogous to LibraryScreenContent / DetailsScreenContent). A `LaunchedEffect(effects)` collector maps `RequestSubmitted` → snackbar "Request submitted successfully" and `RequestFailed` → snackbar "Request failed".
  2. The `LazyColumn` gained a footer item — a primary-coloured "Request a language" row that dispatches `OnOpenRequestDialog`.
  3. A new private `LanguageRequestDialog` composable — Material 3 `AlertDialog` with multiline `OutlinedTextField` bound to `state.requestText`. Validation: `submitEnabled = !submitting && text.length >= 8` (matches the legacy `SendComplaintUseCase.invoke` precondition `require(body.length >= 8)`). The Send button shows a small inline `CircularProgressIndicator` while submitting. **No category dropdown** (unlike the legacy `FeedbackDialog`) — the `:data` impl hardcodes `subject = "Languages"` so the user never picks a category; the legacy dropdown was a generic feedback affordance, not language-specific.

**`:composeApp`** (1 modified file):
- `di/LanguageReworkModule.kt` — appended:
  - `single<FeedbackRepository> { FeedbackRepositoryImpl(get(), get(), get()) }` — the 3 `get()` args resolve transitively to `:shared`-bound singletons (`SendComplaintUseCase` + `UserIdProvider` + `DeviceInfoProvider`). NO new platform-specific code (the iOS/Android/Desktop platform modules already bind `UserIdProvider` + `DeviceInfoProvider` for the legacy `ComplaintViewModel`).
  - `factory { SendLanguageRequestUseCase(get()) }` — stateless thin pass-through.
  - `viewModel { LanguageViewModel(get(), get(), get(), get()) }` — extended from 3 args to 4.

### §93.3 MVI extension rationale (OCP append on existing surface)

The foundation slice's MVI surface was explicitly designed to accommodate this exact append:
- `LanguageIntent` was a sealed interface with one variant — adding 4 more lands without modifying `OnSelectLanguage`; the VM's exhaustive `when` flags missing branches at compile time.
- `LanguageEffect` was an EMPTY sealed interface — kept the surface closed under modification but open under extension. Filling it with 2 variants is the canonical OCP-friendly extension.
- `LanguageState` was a data-class with 3 fields — appending 3 more fields with sensible defaults preserves the foundation contract: callers constructing `LanguageState(...)` with the original 3 params keep compiling (the 3 new fields use defaults).

The VM's `OnSubmitRequest` branch is the only non-trivial reducer in the slice. Its shape:
```kotlin
is LanguageIntent.OnSubmitRequest -> {
    if (state.value.requestSubmitting) return       // re-entrance guard (same posture as Details slice's onRetry)
    val body = state.value.requestText
    updateState { it.copy(requestSubmitting = true) }
    viewModelScope.launch {
        val result = sendLanguageRequest(body)
        if (result.isSuccess) {
            updateState { it.copy(requestDialogVisible = false, requestText = "", requestSubmitting = false) }
            emit(LanguageEffect.RequestSubmitted)
        } else {
            updateState { it.copy(requestSubmitting = false) }   // preserve text for retry
            emit(LanguageEffect.RequestFailed)
        }
    }
}
```
Fire-and-forget so `handle()` returns promptly. Re-entrance guard prevents double-submission if the UI doesn't disable the button (defence-in-depth).

### §93.4 Strangler-fig boundary

`:data` reach into `:shared` grows by THREE collaborators (all already bound `single` by existing modules):
- `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.complaint.usecase.SendComplaintUseCase` (legacy `:shared` `SharedModule` binding)
- `me.manga.kira.domain.auth.UserIdProvider` (platform-specific `PlatformModule.android/.ios/.desktop` binding)
- `me.manga.kira.domain.device.DeviceInfoProvider` (platform-specific binding)

The reach is wider than the foundation slice (+3 vs +1 `SettingsRepository`) but identical in posture: the `:data` impl pulls legacy collaborators via `get()`, calls their interface methods, returns the domain shape. The legacy types do NOT leak into `:presentation` or `:ui` — the rework consumers see only `FeedbackRepository` / `SendLanguageRequestUseCase`.

Submitted complaints round-trip identically with the legacy `ComplaintViewModel.submit` path:
- Same `Complaint.userId` (both pull from `UserIdProvider`)
- Same `Complaint.type = LANGUAGES`
- Same `Complaint.subject = "Languages"` (legacy uses `Res.string.languages` i18n — English locale resolves to "Languages"; rework hardcodes "Languages")
- Same `Complaint.metadata` (both pull from `DeviceInfoProvider.getDeviceMetadata()`)
- Same `Complaint.createdAt` (both use `Clock.System.now()`)
- Same `Complaint.status = OPEN`

Admin dashboard queries against the `complaints` Firestore collection see no schema drift between the two paths.

### §93.7 Commit compression note

The plan ([PLAN_language_request.md]) originally projected 7 commits (plan + `:domain` + `:data` + `:presentation` + `:ui` + `:composeApp` + close-out). During implementation the `:presentation` and `:composeApp` Koin commits were merged into one combined commit (`b705868`, 5 files at the cap): the `LanguageViewModel` ctor extension and the Koin `viewModel { LanguageViewModel(get() x4) }` are tightly coupled (changing one breaks the other's build), so splitting them across two commits would leave the tree red between them. The combined commit hits the 5-file cap exactly without exceeding it (4 `:presentation` + 1 `:composeApp` = 5). Net effect: 6 commits instead of 7.

### §93.8 Deferrals

- **No i18n lift** — header label ("Language"), footer row label ("Request a language"), dialog title ("Request a language"), subtitle ("Let us know which language you'd like us to support."), field label ("Your request"), button labels ("Send" / "Cancel"), helper text ("At least 8 characters"), snackbar texts ("Request submitted successfully" / "Request failed"), and the hardcoded `Complaint.subject = "Languages"` all stay inline literal. Phase 10 i18n lift routes both legacy and rework consumers through `Res.string.*` in one pass.
- **No Retry action label on the failure snackbar** — the legacy screen's snackbar exposes a Retry action; the rework just shows the error message. The dialog stays open with the typed text preserved so the user can edit-and-resubmit; the Retry action would be redundant (it would re-trigger `OnSubmitRequest` which the user can do by tapping Send again). If a future UX change wants the Retry affordance, add a `withDismissAction = true` + action label to the `showSnackbar()` call and bridge the result back through a new `LanguageIntent.OnRetryRequest` variant.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.LanguageScreen` stays bound to the legacy `LanguageScreenRoute` (which still hosts the legacy FeedbackDialog + ComplaintViewModel). Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice.
- **No rework `ComplaintScreen`** — the standalone Complaint screen (legacy `composeApp/.../features/complaint/ui/screens/ComplaintScreen.kt`) is NOT ported in this slice. The slice focuses tightly on the language-specific Request-Language sub-flow. A future `Phase 7.x.complaint` would port the full Complaint screen as a separate slice.


## §94 — Phase 7.x.complaint.foundation — User-side Complaint LIST screen rework

### §94.1 Strategy

Closes the §93.8 deferral ("No rework `ComplaintScreen`"). Ports the user-side LIST core of the legacy 294-line `composeApp/.../features/complaint/ui/screens/ComplaintScreen.kt` "Feedback Manager" surface as a fresh rework feature slice: `:domain` + `:data` + `:presentation` + `:ui` + `:composeApp` Koin + nav wiring + close-out docs. Defers the inline ACTION dialogs (reply / edit / delete) to a follow-on `Phase 7.x.complaint.actions` sub-slice to fit the 5-files-per-commit cap and keep the foundation reviewable.

Block-and-ask triggers (a-d) NOT met: (a) no contract library introduced — `ComplaintListRepository` is a new interface that mirrors the established strangler-fig pattern documented in §70 (Phase 6.4.x.statistics) and §93.4 (Phase 7.x.language.request); (b) no observable behaviour change — legacy `Screen.Complaint` + `ComplaintScreenRoute` + `composable<Screen.Complaint>` block untouched; rework `Screen.ComplaintRework` is a parallel debug-reachable route reading the SAME Firestore `complaints` collection (admin reads + Request-Language writes from §93 surface on both); (c) no compile risk — all 4 build gates green after every source commit; (d) no SOLID violation — `ComplaintListRepository` is single-method (ISP), `ComplaintListRepositoryImpl` is single-responsibility (load + map), the use case is a thin pass-through (SRP), the VM derives its filter projection in-handler (no flow combine), the screen is stateless (props-in / intent-out).

### §94.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (3 new files):
- `model/complaint/ComplaintSummary.kt` — data class with 7 fields (`id: String`, `userId: String`, `type: ComplaintType`, `subject: String`, `body: String`, `createdAt: Instant?`, `status: ComplaintStatus`) + 2 file-local enums (`ComplaintStatus` 8 variants — `OPEN/ACCEPTED/REJECTED/COMPLETED/IN_PROGRESS/RESOLVED/CLOSED/ARCHIVED`; `ComplaintType` 6 variants — `BUG/FEATURE/LANGUAGES/SOURCE/OTHER/UNKNOWN`). Mirrors the legacy `:shared` `Complaint` model 1:1 EXCEPT for the legacy `metadata: Map<String, Any>?` field — deliberately dropped at the `:domain` boundary to exclude the banned `Any` type from the pure-domain layer. The legacy metadata is collected by the WRITE side (Request-Language `FeedbackRepository`); the LIST side renders metadata-free summaries. `@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)` on the data class (Phase 4 batch 4.4 KMP `kotlin.time.Instant`).
- `repository/ComplaintListRepository.kt` — single-method interface:
  ```kotlin
  interface ComplaintListRepository {
      suspend fun loadUserComplaints(): Result<List<ComplaintSummary>>
  }
  ```
  KDoc rationale: SIBLING to `FeedbackRepository` (§93.5) — not an extension. `FeedbackRepository` is WRITE-only (`sendLanguageRequest(body): Result<Unit>`); this one is READ-only. The §93.5 KDoc explicitly anticipated this sibling: "A future `sendBugReport` / `sendFeatureRequest` should be a sibling method on this interface OR a sibling interface if signatures diverge." For LIST loading the signature diverges (no `body` arg, returns a list, not Unit) so sibling not extension preserves ISP.
- `usecase/complaint/ObserveUserComplaintsUseCase.kt` — thin pass-through:
  ```kotlin
  class ObserveUserComplaintsUseCase(private val repository: ComplaintListRepository) {
      suspend operator fun invoke(): Result<List<ComplaintSummary>> = repository.loadUserComplaints()
  }
  ```
  Named "Observe" for forward-compat with a future flow-based variant (`Flow<List<ComplaintSummary>>`) — the legacy facade is a one-shot `suspend` fetch today, so the use case matches that, but the name signals the eventual reactive lift.

**`:data`** (1 new file):
- `repository/ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt` — strangler-fig over TWO legacy `:shared` types:
  ```kotlin
  class ComplaintListRepositoryImpl(
      private val legacy: LegacyGetUserComplaintUseCase,   // me.manga.kira.presentation.features.complaint.usecase.GetUserComplaintUseCase
      private val userIdProvider: UserIdProvider,          // me.manga.kira.domain.auth.UserIdProvider
  ) : ComplaintListRepository {
      override suspend fun loadUserComplaints(): Result<List<ComplaintSummary>> = runCatching {
          legacy(userIdProvider.getUserId()).map { it.toSummary() }
      }
  }
  ```
  - **2-dep fan-in** mirrors the legacy `ComplaintViewModel.loadForUser` orchestration (lines 92-102 of the legacy `:shared` file): get user ID, query Firestore via the use case, return the list.
  - **`runCatching {}`** uniforms `Result<List<...>>` wrapping. Any throw (Firestore PERMISSION_DENIED, network, deserialization) surfaces as `Result.failure`.
  - **Import-aliases for the parallel hierarchy**: `LegacyComplaint` / `LegacyComplaintStatus` / `LegacyComplaintType` / `LegacyGetUserComplaintUseCase`. Disambiguates from the `:domain` versions in the same file scope.
  - **Two private extension mappers** (`LegacyComplaintStatus.toDomain()` + `LegacyComplaintType.toDomain()`) use explicit `when` blocks — compile-time exhaustive. The alternative (`enumValueOf<DomainStatus>(legacy.name)`) is reflection-backed and throws `IllegalArgumentException` at runtime for any enum-name drift; explicit `when` flags the drift at compile time.
  - **`metadata` field dropped at the boundary**: `LegacyComplaint.toSummary()` maps only the 7 LIST-relevant fields. The legacy `metadata: Map<String, Any>?` (`Any` is banned in `:domain`) stays on the legacy type — the rework presentation/UI never sees it.

**`:presentation`** (4 new files):
- `complaint/ComplaintState.kt` — data class with 6 fields:
  ```kotlin
  data class ComplaintState(
      val isLoading: Boolean = true,
      val error: String? = null,
      val all: List<ComplaintSummary> = emptyList(),
      val filtered: List<ComplaintSummary> = emptyList(),
      val searchQuery: String = "",
      val selectedStatus: ComplaintStatus? = null,
  ) : MviState
  ```
  Mutual-exclusivity contract: `isLoading=true` → loading indicator (all/filtered empty, error null); `error!=null` → inline error (loading false, lists empty); `isLoading=false && error==null && all.isEmpty()` → empty-state message; otherwise → list view (filtered may be a subset of all). Store `filtered` explicitly (not derive in the composable) so the view contract stays stateless per the rework MVI mandate.
- `complaint/ComplaintIntent.kt` — sealed interface with 4 variants: `OnRetry` (data object) + `OnSearchChange(query)` (data class) + `OnStatusFilter(status: ComplaintStatus?)` (data class) + `OnClearSearch` (data object). The `OnClearSearch` could be modelled as `OnSearchChange("")` — kept separate for clarity and so future analytics can distinguish user-initiated clears from typing. The `OnStatusFilter` accepts `null` to clear the filter (chip-row's "All" button + tap-same-chip-twice both map to `null`).
- `complaint/ComplaintEffect.kt` — EMPTY sealed interface — `sealed interface ComplaintEffect : MviEffect`. No variants today (no toasts, no nav, no snackbars in the foundation). Future `ShowReplySnackbar` / `ShowEditSnackbar` / `ShowDeleteSnackbar` slot in via OCP §6 append when the actions slice lands.
- `complaint/ComplaintViewModel.kt` — extends `MviViewModel<ComplaintState, ComplaintIntent, ComplaintEffect>`; constructor takes 1 dep (`observeUserComplaints: ObserveUserComplaintsUseCase`); `init { loadList() }` kicks the fetch once on construction. `handle()` exhausts the 4 intents: `OnRetry` re-runs `loadList()`; the other 3 are pure state mutations + `applyFilter` recompute. `loadList()` sets loading + clears error, launches in `viewModelScope`, surfaces `result.exceptionOrNull()?.message ?: throwable::class.simpleName ?: "Unknown error"` on failure. `applyFilter(all, query, status)` is a pure list filter — case-insensitive substring match against `subject`/`body`/`id` plus an optional `status` equality check (matches legacy semantics lines 97-103).

**`:ui`** (1 new file):
- `complaint/ComplaintScreen.kt` — Compose entry point. Outer `ComplaintScreen(viewModel, onBack, modifier)` collects state, delegates to inner stateless `ComplaintScreenContent(state, onIntent, onBack, modifier)` for testability. Scaffold + TopAppBar with "Feedback Manager" title + "Back" `TextButton` action (the `:ui` module has no `material-icons-extended` — `TextButton("Back")` substitutes for the legacy `Icon` per the rework's icon-policy). Branching by state: `isLoading` → centered `CircularProgressIndicator`; `errorMessage != null` → inline error + Retry button; `all.isEmpty()` → "No feedback submitted yet" empty state; otherwise → `ComplaintList` (LazyColumn with `SearchAndFilterSection` header + items). The `errorMessage` capture pattern (`val errorMessage = state.error` before the `when`) is required by Kotlin's cross-module smart-cast limitation — `state.error` is a `String?` property declared in `:presentation`, so it can't be smart-cast directly inside `when (errorMessage != null)`; capturing to a local `val` first allows smart-cast inside the `when` branch. `SearchAndFilterSection` is an `OutlinedTextField` (search) + a `LazyRow` of `FilterChip`s ("All" + each `ComplaintStatus`) + a results-count line. `ComplaintRow` is a `Card` with `subject` (titleMedium), `status` label (labelSmall, primary tint), `body` (bodyMedium, 3-line max with ellipsis), and `type` label (labelSmall, secondary tint).

No row-tap navigation (the legacy LIST opens inline dialogs, not separate screens).

### §94.3 MVI shape rationale

The slice extends the rework MVI pattern with one significant refinement vs prior list-with-search slices (History, Updates): **VM-side filter derivation** rather than UI-side `remember`-scoped derivation.

The legacy `composeApp/.../complaint/ui/screens/ComplaintScreen.kt` derives its filter in Compose `remember` blocks (lines 95-103) using `derivedStateOf`. That split the source of truth between the legacy VM (which owned the source list) and the screen (which owned the search/filter state). The rework's strict-MVI mandate requires the view to be stateless — so the search text + status selection are pulled into `ComplaintState`, and the recompute happens in `ComplaintViewModel.handle()`.

The recompute is imperative (not flow-combined) because:
- The list size is bounded (one user's submissions — tens, maybe low hundreds), so a per-keystroke list filter is microsecond-cheap.
- `combine(state.searchQuery, state.selectedStatus, state.all)` would be a reactive overkill — same observable behaviour, more code, harder to test.
- Imperative recompute matches the Sources slice's search filter posture (which the team validated in §76).

`ComplaintIntent` has 4 variants and `ComplaintEffect` is empty today. The action slice will append:
- `OnComplaintClick(id)` / `OnReplyComplaint(id, body)` / `OnEditComplaint(id, body)` / `OnDeleteComplaint(id)` as `ComplaintIntent` siblings (sealed-interface OCP append).
- `ShowReplySnackbar` / `ShowEditSnackbar` / `ShowDeleteSnackbar` as `ComplaintEffect` variants (empty → non-empty append is the canonical OCP move).
- A second repository (`ComplaintActionRepository` or similar) for the mutation side + 3 use cases (`ReplyComplaintUseCase` / `EditComplaintUseCase` / `DeleteComplaintUseCase`).

Re-entrance posture: NO guard on `loadList()` today. Tap-spamming Retry could enqueue multiple in-flight loads but the `MviViewModel` channel is unbounded and each launch updates the same state — worst case is a brief flicker as multiple loads resolve. If user-visible stability requirements emerge, add `if (state.value.isLoading) return` at `loadList()` entry (same posture as Details' `onRetry` guard).

### §94.4 Strangler-fig boundary

`:data` reach into `:shared` adds TWO collaborators (both already bound `single` by existing modules from §93 and earlier slices):
- `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.complaint.usecase.GetUserComplaintUseCase` (`:shared` `SharedModule` binding)
- `me.manga.kira.domain.auth.UserIdProvider` (platform-specific binding — same singleton consumed by `FeedbackRepositoryImpl`)

Same posture as Phase 6.4.x.statistics's `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (1 collaborator) and Phase 7.x.language.request's `FeedbackRepositoryImpl` (3 collaborators), scaled down to 2 because the LIST side needs neither `SendComplaintUseCase` (write-only) nor `DeviceInfoProvider` (metadata is dropped at the boundary).

LIST round-trip identity with the legacy `ComplaintViewModel.loadForUser` path: same Firestore collection (`complaints`), same WHERE filter (`userId == <caller>` server-side via the legacy use case), same document shape (the `:data` impl reads the legacy `Complaint` model verbatim and maps it via `toSummary()`). Admin dashboard queries see no schema drift between the legacy and rework reads.
