### §94.7 Deferrals

- **No i18n lift** — top bar title ("Feedback Manager"), Retry button ("Retry"), empty-state ("No feedback submitted yet"), search placeholder ("Search submissions…"), filter chip "All", per-status chip labels (humanised from the enum constant — "OPEN" → "Open" etc.), results count ("N matching"), no-matches message, type label prefix ("Type: …"), Back button label all stay inline literal. Phase 10 i18n lift routes both legacy and rework consumers through `Res.string.*` in one pass.
- **No row-tap action surface** — the legacy screen's row tap opens an inline reply/edit/delete dialog. The rework foundation row is non-interactive (the Card has no `clickable` modifier). Action slice (`Phase 7.x.complaint.actions`) adds: 3 new intents (`OnReplyComplaint`/`OnEditComplaint`/`OnDeleteComplaint` — each carries the complaint id + a body string for reply/edit), 3 new effects (`ShowReplySnackbar`/`ShowEditSnackbar`/`ShowDeleteSnackbar` — payload-less data objects, snackbar text owned in `:ui`), a second `:domain` repository interface for the action side (writes/updates/deletes on the same Firestore collection — likely sharing the existing `FeedbackRepository` if signatures line up, otherwise a sibling `ComplaintActionRepository`), and 3 corresponding use cases. The action slice extends `ComplaintReworkScreenRoute` to host the SnackbarHost + effect collector.
- **No pull-to-refresh** — the legacy screen has no PTR either; both rely on the inline Retry button. If user-visible requirements emerge, `OnRetry` already doubles as the manual-refresh intent — a `PullToRefreshContainer` wrapper in `:ui` plus an `isRefreshing` field on the state would land additively.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.Complaint` stays bound to the legacy `ComplaintScreenRoute` (which still hosts the reply/edit/delete dialog surface). Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice; this slice only adds the parallel `Screen.ComplaintRework` route.
- **No admin-side rework** — the admin LIST/triage route (`Screen.ComplaintAdmin` + `AdminComplaintScreenRoute`) is COMPLETELY untouched. The admin surface is a separate user role and a separate set of mutation actions (Accept/Reject/Mark Complete); a future `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin` slice would be its own port.
- **No `metadata` exposure** — the legacy `Complaint.metadata: Map<String, Any>?` field is dropped at the `:data → :domain` boundary because `Any` is banned in `:domain` (contract §6). The LIST view doesn't render metadata. The WRITE side (§93's `FeedbackRepositoryImpl`) collects metadata into the legacy type at the boundary; the LIST side discards it on the way out. If a future feature needs to display metadata (e.g., admin diagnostics), the lift would replace `Map<String, Any>?` with a typed `ComplaintDeviceInfo` data class in `:domain` and add a Phase 4-style migration use case to map between the typed shape and the legacy `Map<String, Any>?` representation that remains on the Firestore wire.

## §95 — Phase 7.x.complaint.actions — Reply / Edit / Delete action dialog rework

The natural follow-on to §94's user-side LIST foundation. §94's `ComplaintEffect` was deliberately declared as an empty sealed interface — the OCP extensibility hook for exactly this slice. The legacy `composeApp/.../ComplaintActionDialog.kt` (696 lines, 4 dialog sub-screens: Menu / Reply / Edit / Delete) lifts into a `:ui` composable driven by the MVI state-machine instead of the legacy's local `var currentAction by remember { mutableStateOf(DialogAction.NONE) }`.

### §95.1 Strategy

OCP append everywhere: §94's MVI surface accepts 6 new intents (`OnRowClick`, `OnDismissActionDialog`, `OnSelectAction`, `OnSubmitReply`, `OnSubmitEdit`, `OnConfirmDelete`); state grows 3 fields (`actionDialogMode`, `activeComplaint`, `isSubmittingAction`) plus a new `ActionDialogMode` enum (NONE / MENU / REPLY / EDIT / DELETE — the legacy collapses MENU into NONE with a `currentAction == NONE` shortcut, the rework adds an explicit MENU variant for state-machine clarity); effect surface adds 2 snackbar variants (`ShowSuccessMessage` / `ShowErrorMessage`). No foundation entries modified; only added.

Strangler-fig posture mirrors §93's `FeedbackRepositoryImpl` + §94's `ComplaintListRepositoryImpl` — a new `:data` impl reaches into legacy `:shared`'s 3 mutation use cases (`SendComplaintUseCase` / `UpdateComplaintUseCase` / `DeleteComplaintUseCase`). The new `:domain` repository interface `ComplaintActionRepository` is a sibling to §94's READ-only `ComplaintListRepository`, splitting the legacy `ComplaintRepository`'s 5 methods along ISP lines (READ vs WRITE).

### §95.2 `:domain` surface

`ComplaintActionRepository` (`:domain/repository/`): three suspend methods returning `Result<Unit>`:
- `replyToComplaint(parent: ComplaintSummary, body: String)` — creates a child record with `metadata = mapOf("replyto" to parent.id)`.
- `editComplaint(original: ComplaintSummary, subject: String, body: String)` — overwrites the parent's `subject` + `body`, preserves `userId` / `type` / `createdAt` / `status`.
- `deleteComplaint(id: String)` — pure identity-based delete.

Three use case classes (`:domain/usecase/complaint/`): `ReplyToComplaintUseCase`, `EditComplaintUseCase`, `DeleteComplaintUseCase`. Each is a thin pass-through over the action repository. `DeleteComplaintUseCase` shares its short class name with the legacy `:shared` `DeleteComplaintUseCase` (different packages — no compile clash); the `:data` impl uses an `as LegacyDeleteComplaintUseCase` import alias for unambiguous IDE/tooling references.

### §95.3 `:data` strangler-fig impl

`ComplaintActionRepositoryImpl` (`:data/repository/`): constructor takes 3 legacy use cases (`LegacySendComplaintUseCase`, `LegacyUpdateComplaintUseCase`, `LegacyDeleteComplaintUseCase` — all `Legacy*` import aliases). Each method wraps a single legacy invocation in `runCatching {}` so any throw (network failure, Firestore permission denial, legacy `SendComplaintUseCase.require()` validation) surfaces as `Result.failure`.

Reply construction synthesises a fresh `LegacyComplaint(id = "", userId = parent.userId, type = parent.type.toLegacyType(), subject = parent.subject, body = body, createdAt = null, status = OPEN, metadata = mapOf("replyto" to parent.id))`. Intentional behaviour delta vs legacy: the rework does NOT inherit `parent.metadata` into the reply — only the `{replyto: parent.id}` thread anchor is attached. Rationale: (a) excludes `Map<String, Any>` banned `Any` exposure from the `:domain → :data` boundary (the rework `ComplaintSummary` has no `metadata` field — see §94.7's banned-`Any` containment); (b) avoids misattributing stale device-info from the parent's submission onto a fresh reply; (c) admin diagnostics still see the parent record's own metadata via separate Firestore reads if needed.

Edit reconstruction builds a full `LegacyComplaint(id = original.id, userId = original.userId, type = original.type.toLegacyType(), subject = subject, body = body, createdAt = original.createdAt, status = original.status.toLegacyStatus(), metadata = null)`. Legacy `updateComplaint(complaint)` overwrites the entire document; the reconstruction preserves the parent's non-edited fields. `metadata = null` — the legacy `UpdateComplaintUseCase` doesn't preserve metadata across edits either (the source caller passed a synthesised record with `metadata = null` for the same reason).

Two reverse-direction enum mappers (`ComplaintStatus.toLegacyStatus()` + `ComplaintType.toLegacyType()`) are the inverse of §94's forward mappers — same posture, exhaustive `when` branches (not `enumValueOf`-style reflection) so a new variant on either side becomes a compile-time error here.

### §95.4 `:presentation` MVI append

`ComplaintState` gains 3 fields + a sibling `ActionDialogMode` enum (same file — tightly-coupled, no consumers outside the slice). The enum's 5 variants are NONE / MENU / REPLY / EDIT / DELETE. Field semantics:
- `actionDialogMode` — which dialog sub-screen is rendered. NONE means no dialog mounted; the others map to the legacy `DialogAction` enum.
- `activeComplaint` — the row the user tapped to open the action dialog. Required for every sub-mode. Null when `actionDialogMode == NONE`.
- `isSubmittingAction` — `true` while a Reply / Edit / Delete request is in-flight. Drives the dialog's submit-button `enabled = false` + loading spinner. Cleared on success (alongside dialog dismissal) or on failure (dialog stays open at current mode).

Dialog mount precondition: the `:ui` composable mounts `ComplaintActionDialog` only when `actionDialogMode != NONE && activeComplaint != null`. Both are set together by `OnRowClick` and cleared together by `OnDismissActionDialog`; the precondition protects against the (currently unreachable) invariant violation.

`ComplaintIntent` gains 6 variants (1 data object — `OnDismissActionDialog`; 1 data object — `OnConfirmDelete`; 4 data classes — `OnRowClick(complaint)` / `OnSelectAction(mode)` / `OnSubmitReply(body)` / `OnSubmitEdit(subject, body)`). All carry `data` modifiers per the rework MVI contract. `OnSelectAction` consolidates 4 payload-free transitions (MENU↔REPLY/EDIT/DELETE) into a single enum-payload intent — keeps the surface compact.

`ComplaintEffect` gains 2 data class variants (`ShowSuccessMessage(message)` / `ShowErrorMessage(message)`). The foundation's empty surface was specifically declared as the OCP hook for this addition. Two distinct variants rather than `ShowMessage(text, isError)` so the failure path is a compile-time-distinct branch (separate snackbar styling possible).

`ComplaintViewModel` constructor expands from 1 to 4 args (foundation's `observeUserComplaints` + the 3 new mutation use cases). The `handle()` over the now-10-variant `ComplaintIntent` adds 6 new branches:
- `OnRowClick(complaint)` → set `actionDialogMode = MENU` + `activeComplaint = complaint`.
- `OnDismissActionDialog` → clear both back to NONE / null.
- `OnSelectAction(mode)` → update `actionDialogMode = mode` (guards: ignore `NONE` — that's `OnDismissActionDialog`'s job; ignore when `activeComplaint == null`).
- `OnSubmitReply(body)` / `OnSubmitEdit(subject, body)` / `OnConfirmDelete` → each sets `isSubmittingAction = true`, launches a `viewModelScope` coroutine that calls the matching use case, then routes the `Result` through the private `completeAction(result, successMessage)` helper:
  - Success: dismiss dialog (mode → NONE, activeComplaint → null, isSubmittingAction → false) + emit `ShowSuccessMessage(successMessage)` + refire `loadList()` to reflect the post-mutation truth.
  - Failure: keep dialog open at current mode (only clear `isSubmittingAction`) + emit `ShowErrorMessage(message)` with the throwable's message + class-name + literal fallback chain.

In-flight re-entrance guards: every action handler short-circuits when `state.isSubmittingAction == true`. The `:ui` dialog also disables its submit buttons while the flag is set, but the VM-side guard is defence-in-depth against intent re-entry from the unbounded `MviViewModel` intent channel (a tap-spam queues intents).

### §95.5 `:ui` composable

`ComplaintActionDialog.kt` (NEW) is a single composable that renders the 4-mode action dialog inside a `Dialog { Card { when (mode) { ... } } }` block — same outer chrome across modes, no flash when the inner branch swaps. 4 private inner composables (`ActionSelectionContent` / `ReplyContent` / `EditContent` / `DeleteConfirmationContent`) + 1 shared `ComplaintPreviewCard`. Validation parity: Reply caps at 500 chars, Edit caps at 1000 chars body + non-blank subject. Status-gated affordances: Edit + Delete buttons are hidden when `complaint.status == ComplaintStatus.PINNED` (parity with legacy lines 206-241 — admin-pinned FAQ entries are reply-only on the user side).

Form input state (`replyText` / `editedSubject` / `editedBody`) uses `rememberSaveable(complaint.id) { ... }` — transient typed-input state surviving config changes but resetting when a different parent record is opened. The `:ui` is otherwise stateless; the loading spinner on submit buttons comes from `state.isSubmittingAction` (single source of truth in VM; legacy used a local `var isLoading by remember` that's redundant here).

Icon-free posture: legacy `IconButton(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack)` / `IconButton(Icons.Default.Close)` / `Icon(... Reply / Edit / Delete / Info / Warning ...)` all swap to labelled `TextButton`s ("Back", "Close", "Cancel") or are dropped (action-button icons + Info/Warning info-card icons — the card colour + heading convey severity). Same posture as the rest of the rework `:ui` (`HistoryScreen`, `StatisticsScreen`, `ComplaintScreen`'s foundation top bar).

`ComplaintScreen.kt` (MODIFIED) gains 3 things: (a) `ComplaintRow` is now `clickable` and fires `OnRowClick(complaint)`; (b) the `ComplaintActionDialog` mounts under the precondition `mode != NONE && activeComplaint != null` inside the same outer Box that hosts the list; (c) a `SnackbarHost` is added to the Scaffold and a `LaunchedEffect(viewModel)` collects `ComplaintEffect` emissions via `collectLatest`, routing `ShowSuccessMessage` / `ShowErrorMessage` to a `SnackbarHostState` (default Material 3 `SnackbarDuration.Short`).

### §95.9 Deferrals

- **No i18n lift** — dialog labels ("Actions", "Reply to complaint", "Edit complaint", "Delete complaint", "Send", "Save", "Delete forever", "Cancel", "Back", "Close", "Warning", "This action cannot be undone…", "Subject", "Body", "Your reply", "Type your reply…", "Edit your complaint…", character-count "N/M", success messages "Reply sent" / "Complaint updated" / "Complaint deleted") all stay inline literal. Phase 10 i18n lift routes both legacy and rework consumers through `Res.string.*` in one pass.
- **No status-display polish** — the rework `ComplaintPreviewCard` shows `complaint.status.name` (raw enum constant) where the legacy uses `complaint.status.displayName()` (humanised) + a colour-coded background pill from `getColorWithContrast()`. Phase 10 humanisation lift handles both surfaces.
- **No optimistic UI** — the rework refires `loadList()` on every successful mutation, accepting a brief `isLoading = true` flicker between dialog-dismissal and the new list arriving. Legacy does the same. Optimistic update would split the source of truth between VM's projection of the mutation and the Firestore-bound truth — fragile. Refire keeps both consistent.
- **No retry-from-snackbar action** — the rework's `ShowErrorMessage` snackbar is action-less (just the error text). User retries by tapping the affected sub-mode's submit button again (the dialog stays open at the current mode on failure, exactly so this is possible). Future "Retry" snackbar action would be additive.
- **No parent-thread display** — the rework reply attaches `metadata = {replyto: parent.id}` to the child record, same as legacy. But the LIST view doesn't render the thread (no "↳ reply to #parent" affordance). Phase 7.x.complaint.thread (or admin-side) would add a thread-folding LIST projection if user-visible requirements emerge.
- **No nav graph route-swap** — legacy `Screen.Complaint` stays bound to the legacy `ComplaintScreenRoute` (which still hosts its own reply/edit/delete dialog surface). Phase 9.x route-swap is its own slice.
- **No admin-side action rework** — the admin LIST/triage route's mutation set (Accept/Reject/Mark Complete) is a separate surface; this slice ONLY ports the user-side actions.

## §96 — Phase 7.x.settings.foundation — Settings hub screen rework

The Settings hub is the most-trafficked screen of the legacy app and the biggest deferred user-facing surface. The legacy `composeApp/.../features/settings/ui/screens/SettingsScreen.kt` (407 lines) is a fused composable that owns: 5 boolean toggle rows, 9 navigation rows, dark-mode conditional visibility, the ReadingMode dialog, the Feedback dialog, the CBZ-progress dialog, an admin testing-mode switch, the Clear-cache action with okio cache-folder file walk, and the app-header image. The foundation slice ports only the load-bearing subset (5 toggles + 6 nav rows + clear-cache) and defers the dialog-heavy surfaces (ReadingMode / Feedback / CBZ progress) and the admin / Downloads / Help / themegating extras to sibling sub-slices via OCP-additive sealed-interface variants.

### §96.1 Strategy

Same strangler-fig posture as §85 (Theme) / §92 (Language) / §87 (About) — a single new `:data` impl over the legacy `:shared` `SettingsRepository` facade (the same facade Theme and Language already strangler-fig over). The legacy facade exposes 5 boolean pref flows (`downloadedOnlyFlow`, `incognitoFlow`, `followSystemFlow`, `darkModeFlow`, `pureBlackFlow`), their 5 matching setters, the okio cache-folder file walk (`getCacheFolderSize()`), and the cache-clear action (`clearFilesLargerThan1MB()`). The rework's `SettingsRepositoryImpl` projects these into a single `Flow<SettingsSnapshot>` via `combine(...)` and exposes ONE WRITE method per toggle via an exhaustive `when` over the rework `SettingsToggle` enum + a one-shot `clearCache(): Result<Unit>` action that gates a `MutableSharedFlow<Unit>` refresh trigger to re-emit the cache-size string after the legacy delete completes.

The 5 pref flows + the cache-size flow are wired through `combine(...)` — the upstream `Flow<SettingsSnapshot>` only emits once ALL 6 sources have emitted at least once. `isLoading` clears on the first joint emission (standard `combine` semantics). The cache-size flow runs the okio file walk on `dispatchers.io` (KMP-safe IO dispatcher from `:core`) via `flowOn(dispatchers.io)`; failure of the walk degrades gracefully (legacy `getCacheFolderSize()` returns 0 for missing dirs, `formatSize(0)` returns `"0 B"`).

### §96.2 `:domain` surface

`domain/.../model/settings/SettingsSnapshot.kt` (NEW) — pure value type with 6 fields: `downloadedOnly: Boolean`, `incognito: Boolean`, `followSystemTheme: Boolean`, `darkMode: Boolean`, `pureBlack: Boolean`, `cacheSize: String`. Co-located in the same file (per the SRP-cluster pattern §94 used for `ComplaintStatus`/`ComplaintType`/`ComplaintSummary`) is the `SettingsToggle` enum — 5 variants matching the 5 boolean fields exactly: `DOWNLOADED_ONLY`, `INCOGNITO`, `FOLLOW_SYSTEM_THEME`, `DARK_MODE`, `PURE_BLACK`. The enum is the parameter to the single `UpdateSettingsToggleUseCase`; the exhaustive `when` on it in the `:data` impl translates each variant to the matching legacy setter.

`domain/.../repository/SettingsRepository.kt` (NEW) — interface with 3 methods: `observe(): Flow<SettingsSnapshot>`, `suspend fun setToggle(toggle: SettingsToggle, value: Boolean)`, `suspend fun clearCache(): Result<Unit>`. The `clearCache()` returns `Result<Unit>` because the legacy `clearFilesLargerThan1MB()` is fire-and-forget; the rework adds a failure path for snackbar surfacing (legacy's posture is to not surface failures).

Three use case classes (`:domain/usecase/settings/`): `ObserveSettingsUseCase` (operator-invoke pass-through over `observe()`), `UpdateSettingsToggleUseCase` (operator-invoke pass-through over `setToggle()`), `ClearCacheUseCase` (operator-invoke pass-through over `clearCache()`).

### §96.3 `:data` strangler-fig impl

`SettingsRepositoryImpl` (`:data/repository/`): constructor takes 2 args — `legacy: me.manga.kira.presentation.features.settings.domain.SettingsRepository` (the `:shared` facade, kept distinct from the rework `SettingsRepository` interface name via fully-qualified import alias to avoid ambiguity) + `dispatchers: DispatcherProvider` (KMP-safe IO dispatcher from `:core`). The class is `single`-scoped because it holds the `MutableSharedFlow<Unit>(replay = 1).also { tryEmit(Unit) }` refresh trigger for the cache-size flow — multiple resolutions would fragment the trigger across independent flow instances, breaking the "clear cache → cache-size re-emits" contract.

The `observe()` impl uses `combine(downloadedOnlyFlow, incognitoFlow, followSystemFlow, darkModeFlow, pureBlackFlow, cacheSizeFlow) { d, i, fs, dm, pb, cs -> SettingsSnapshot(d, i, fs, dm, pb, cs) }`. The 6-arg `combine` overload is provided by kotlinx.coroutines.flow (vararg with typed lambda receiver — no `Array<Any>` unpacking needed at this arity).

The `cacheSizeFlow` is built as `refreshTrigger.flatMapLatest { flow { emit(formatSize(legacy.getCacheFolderSize())) } }.flowOn(dispatchers.io)`. `flatMapLatest` (annotated `@OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)`) ensures only the most-recent walk's result emits when the trigger refires (defence against rapid back-to-back `clearCache()` calls during in-flight walks). `formatSize` is a private helper that mirrors the legacy's bytes-to-string logic (e.g., `"12.3 MB"`).

The `setToggle(toggle, value)` impl is an exhaustive `when` over `SettingsToggle` — each branch dispatches to the matching legacy setter (`legacy.setDownloadedOnly(value)` / `legacy.setIncognito(value)` / `legacy.setFollowSystem(value)` / `legacy.setDarkMode(value)` / `legacy.setPureBlack(value)`). The legacy setters are themselves suspend over `SharedPreferences.putBoolean` / `DataStore.edit`.

The `clearCache()` impl runs `runCatching { legacy.clearFilesLargerThan1MB() }` then on success fires `refreshTrigger.tryEmit(Unit)` to re-trigger the cache-size walk. On failure, the `Result<Unit>` propagates back to the VM for snackbar surfacing.

### §96.4 `:presentation` MVI

4 sibling files in `:presentation/commonMain/.../settings/`:

`SettingsState.kt` — data class with 8 fields: 5 booleans matching the snapshot + `cacheSize: String` + `isLoading: Boolean` (initial-emission gap, cleared on first `combine` emission) + `isClearingCache: Boolean` (in-flight protection for the clear-cache action). Defaults `isLoading = true`, `isClearingCache = false`, booleans `false`, `cacheSize = ""`.

`SettingsIntent.kt` — sealed interface with 3 variants: `OnToggle(toggle, value)` data class, `OnClearCache` data object, `OnNavigate(destination)` data class.

`SettingsDestination.kt` — enum with 6 variants: `THEME`, `STATISTICS`, `LANGUAGE`, `ABOUT`, `COMPLAINT`, `WHATSNEW`. These are abstract identifiers — the `:composeApp` route adapter maps each to the concrete `Screen.<X>Rework` route. `COMPLAINT` is special-cased at the adapter (consults `Admin.isAdmin`); the `:presentation` layer doesn't know about Admin state.

`SettingsEffect.kt` — sealed interface with 2 variants: `NavigateTo(destination)` data class + `ShowSnackbar(message)` data class. The `NavigateTo` carries the same `SettingsDestination` payload as the `OnNavigate` intent — the VM's `OnNavigate` handler is a pure pass-through to the effect channel, because the `:presentation` layer can't construct a `NavController`.

`SettingsViewModel.kt` — extends `MviViewModel<SettingsState, SettingsIntent, SettingsEffect>`; constructor takes the 3 use cases (NOT impls — strict DIP). `init {}` launches a `observeSettings().onEach { snapshot -> updateState { ... } }.launchIn(viewModelScope)` collector that maps each emission's 6 fields into state + clears `isLoading`. The `handle()` over `SettingsIntent` has 3 branches: `OnToggle` → `viewModelScope.launch { updateToggle(toggle, value) }` (fire-and-forget; upstream pref flows re-emit on write commit); `OnClearCache` → re-entry-guarded `handleClearCache()` (set `isClearingCache = true`, launch coroutine that runs `clearCache()`, on completion clear flag + emit `ShowSnackbar` with success or failure-fallback message — `e.message ?: e::class.simpleName ?: "Unknown error"` chain mirrors §95's `completeAction()` posture); `OnNavigate(dest)` → `emit(SettingsEffect.NavigateTo(dest))` (pure pass-through; nav is a side effect, not state).

### §96.5 `:ui` composable

`SettingsScreen.kt` (NEW): outer `SettingsScreen(viewModel, onNavigate, modifier)` resolves `state` via `collectAsState()` and forwards `viewModel.effects` + `viewModel::submit` to the stateless inner `SettingsScreenContent(state, effects, onIntent, onNavigate, modifier)`. The inner owns the Material 3 Scaffold + TopAppBar "Settings" + SnackbarHost + LazyColumn.

**Effect-as-callback-bridge** — the `LaunchedEffect(effects) { effects.collect { ... } }` collector inside the screen routes the 2 effect variants to their sinks: `NavigateTo(dest)` → `onNavigate(dest)` callback (the `:composeApp` route adapter provides this); `ShowSnackbar(message)` → `snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message)`. This pattern matches the established `:ui` posture for nav-emitting screens (`LanguageScreen`, `ComplaintScreen`'s back callback, `DetailsScreen`'s `onOpenReader`). Reconciles the design contract (the route adapter consumes the effect per `SettingsIntent.kt` KDoc) with the single-receiver `Channel.receiveAsFlow()` semantics — the screen owns the one collector and forwards the nav variant through the callback.

The LazyColumn has 4 section Cards: **General** (Downloaded only + Incognito mode toggles), **Theme** (Follow system theme + Dark mode + Pure Black for dark mode toggles — all 3 always visible; legacy's `if (!state.followSystemTheme)` gating defers to a sibling sub-slice), **Navigation** (6 rows mapping to the 6 `SettingsDestination` variants, each `clickable { onIntent(OnNavigate(dest)) }`), **Storage** (Clear cache row showing `state.cacheSize` + an enabled-while-not-clearing button; tapping fires `OnClearCache`). Each toggle row is a `Switch` whose `onCheckedChange = { value -> onIntent(OnToggle(toggle, value)) }`. The `isLoading` flag drives a top-of-screen `CircularProgressIndicator` overlay until the first `combine` emission arrives.

Helper extension props at file bottom — `private val SettingsToggle.label: String` exhaustive `when` for the 5 toggles + `private val SettingsDestination.label: String` exhaustive `when` for the 6 destinations. Inline hardcoded English strings (i18n lift deferred to Phase 10 — matches the rest of the rework `:ui` posture).

Icon-free posture: standard `Switch` for toggles + a "›" Text glyph trailing each nav row (no Material `Icon` — `:ui` module deliberately omits `compose.materialIconsExtended`; same posture as §85 Theme / §82 History / §83 Updates / §94 Complaint).

### §96.6 `:composeApp` Koin + nav wire

`SettingsReworkModule.kt` (NEW) — Koin module:
- `single<SettingsRepository> { SettingsRepositoryImpl(legacy = get(), dispatchers = get<DispatcherProvider>()) }` — `single` because of the refresh-trigger SSoT (see §96.3).
- `factory { ObserveSettingsUseCase(get()) }` + `factory { UpdateSettingsToggleUseCase(get()) }` + `factory { ClearCacheUseCase(get()) }` — `factory` lifecycle, stateless pass-throughs.
- `viewModel { SettingsViewModel(get(), get(), get()) }` — Koin's ViewModelStore-aware binding.

The legacy `:shared` `SettingsRepository` is already `single`-bound by `SharedModule` (since prior Theme + Language slices); zero new `:shared` modifications. `DispatcherProvider` is already `single`-bound by `CoreModule`.

`ReworkModules.kt` (MOD) — one-line append of `settingsReworkModule` to the `allReworkModules()` list. Hosts unchanged (`MyApp.kt` Android, `KoinHelper.doInitKoin()` iOS, `Main.kt` Desktop all call `initKoin { modules(*allReworkModules().toTypedArray()) }`).

`Screen.kt` (MOD) — adds `@Serializable object SettingsRework : Screen("me.manga.kira.navigation.Screen.SettingsRework")` with extensive KDoc covering strangler-fig parity, the 8 deferrals (dark-mode gating / ReadingMode dialog / Feedback dialog / Downloads / Help / CBZ progress / admin testing mode / i18n), and the Admin-routing branch on `COMPLAINT`.

`SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt` (NEW) — thin adapter that resolves `SettingsViewModel` via `koinViewModel()` and provides the `onNavigate: (SettingsDestination) -> Unit` callback. Exhaustive `when` over `SettingsDestination`:
- `THEME` → `Screen.ThemeRework`
- `STATISTICS` → `Screen.StatisticsRework`
- `LANGUAGE` → `Screen.LanguageRework`
- `ABOUT` → `Screen.AboutRework`
- `COMPLAINT` → `if (Admin.isAdmin) Screen.ComplaintAdmin else Screen.ComplaintRework` (same as legacy `SettingsScreen.kt:272-278`)
- `WHATSNEW` → `Screen.WhatsNewRework`

The `:ui` module stays nav-agnostic; the route adapter is the FIRST layer that knows about the `Screen` sealed type. No back callback (the legacy `SettingsRoute` also leaves system back as the only back affordance).

`App.kt` (MOD) — adds `import me.manga.kira.navigation.routes.SettingsReworkScreenRoute` (alphabetical, before `SettingsRoute`) and the `composable<Screen.SettingsRework> { backStackEntry -> SideEffect { onBottomBarVisibleChange(false) }; SettingsReworkScreenRoute(navController, backStackEntry) }` block alongside the existing rework Screen.X blocks, after the `Screen.ComplaintRework` block.

## §97 — Phase 7.x.settings.themegating — gate Dark mode row on `!followSystemTheme`

The smallest sibling sub-slice on top of §96 — closes the first deferral from §96.9 ("No dark-mode gating"). UI-only change in the rework `:ui/.../settings/SettingsScreen.kt`: wrap the Dark mode `ToggleRow` + its preceding `HorizontalDivider` in `if (!state.followSystemTheme) { ... }`. The Pure Black row + its preceding `HorizontalDivider` remain unconditional — exactly matches legacy `composeApp/.../presentation/features/settings/ui/screens/SettingsScreen.kt:228-241` (legacy's `if (!isFollowSystem)` wraps only the dark/light `SwitchItem`; Pure Black's row stays always-visible after the conditional block).

### §97.1 Strategy

Strictly additive. The `state.followSystemTheme` field is already in `SettingsState` from §96; the wrap reads it directly. No new intents, effects, state fields, or use cases. No new dependencies. No layer-boundary changes.

The visual rule: there is always a divider before Pure Black; the divider before Dark mode only renders when Dark mode is visible. Toggling Follow system theme on now hides Dark mode mid-section cleanly (no orphan divider); toggling off shows it again. The `Switch`'s `onCheckedChange` routes through the same single-source-of-truth `followSystemFlow` that both legacy and rework consume, so toggling on either screen reflects on the other.

## §98 — Phase 7.x.settings.feedback — Feedback dialog on rework Settings hub

Closes the second deferral from §96.9 ("No Feedback dialog"). Adds the "Request feature / bug" entry row + the inline modal Feedback dialog (category dropdown + body field + Submit / Cancel) to the rework Settings hub. The submission re-uses §93's already-bound `FeedbackRepository` `single` via a new generic `submit(type, subject, body)` surface (the original `sendLanguageRequest(body)` becomes a default-impl wrapper that pins the type + subject and delegates to `submit`).

### §98.1 Strategy

Strangler-fig posture preserved. ZERO new collaborators in `:data` — the §93 `FeedbackRepositoryImpl` already orchestrates the 3 `:shared` deps (`SendComplaintUseCase` + `UserIdProvider` + `DeviceInfoProvider`); this slice generalises its `sendLanguageRequest(body)` into `submit(type, subject, body)` and keeps the language-request entry working via an interface default-impl wrapper.

Three approaches considered for the interface evolution: (A) fatten the interface to two methods, (B) sibling repository (the original §93 KDoc forecast), (C) default-impl wrapper. Chose (C) because: (1) preserves backwards-compat with the language-picker call site under ISP — the picker continues to depend on the narrow `sendLanguageRequest(body)` signature; (2) avoids `:data` duplication that (B) would have introduced (both impls would have orchestrated the same 3 `:shared` deps); (3) keeps the impl as one cohesive class. The KDoc forecast in §93's `FeedbackRepository` is formally retired.

MVI surface additions narrow: 2 new state fields (`feedbackDialogOpen` + `isSubmittingFeedback`) + 3 new intent variants (`OnOpenFeedbackDialog` / `OnDismissFeedbackDialog` / `OnSubmitFeedback(type, body)`); the existing `SettingsEffect.ShowSnackbar` carries success + failure messages. Dropdown selection + body text live LOCAL to the `:ui` composable (`remember { mutableStateOf(...) }`) — same posture as §95 OnSubmitReply / OnSubmitEdit; payload rides along with `OnSubmitFeedback` rather than being mirrored into state. Keeps the state surface narrow (2 fields, not 4) and avoids per-keystroke intents.

### §98.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:domain` (MOD + NEW):
  - `domain/.../repository/FeedbackRepository.kt` (MOD) — adds `suspend fun submit(type, subject, body): Result<Unit>` (the generic surface); the existing `sendLanguageRequest(body)` becomes a default-impl wrapper that pins `type=LANGUAGES + subject="Languages"` (lifted to `companion object const val LANGUAGE_REQUEST_SUBJECT`) and delegates to `submit`. KDoc retires the original "sibling repository" forecast.
  - `domain/.../usecase/feedback/SubmitFeedbackUseCase.kt` (NEW) — thin pass-through to `FeedbackRepository.submit`. Same OCP-friendly decoration-hook rationale as §93's `SendLanguageRequestUseCase`.
- `:data` (MOD):
  - `data/.../repository/FeedbackRepositoryImpl.kt` (MOD) — removes the old `sendLanguageRequest(body)` override (inherits the new default impl) + removes the `LANGUAGES_SUBJECT` companion (lifted to the interface). Adds the generic `submit` override that maps the `:domain` `ComplaintType` to the legacy `:shared` `ComplaintType` by name (`enumValueOf(type.name)` — the two enums share identity + order per `ComplaintSummary.kt` KDoc), passes through subject/body verbatim, and re-uses the existing 3-`:shared`-dep orchestration. `runCatching {}` wrapper carries through unchanged. Import alias `LegacyComplaintType` avoids ambiguity with the `:domain` enum.
- `:presentation` (MOD):
  - `presentation/.../settings/SettingsState.kt` (MOD) — 2 new fields: `feedbackDialogOpen` (open/closed) + `isSubmittingFeedback` (in-flight).
  - `presentation/.../settings/SettingsIntent.kt` (MOD) — 3 new variants: `OnOpenFeedbackDialog` / `OnDismissFeedbackDialog` (both `data object`) + `OnSubmitFeedback(type: ComplaintType, body: String)` (`data class`). KDoc adds the "Phase 7.x.settings.feedback variants" section.
  - `presentation/.../settings/SettingsViewModel.kt` (MOD) — new `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` constructor dep + 3 new `when` branches + `handleSubmitFeedback(type, body)` private method with the established re-entry guard pattern (`isSubmittingFeedback` flag). On `Result.success` the dialog closes + confirmation snackbar fires; on `Result.failure` the dialog stays open (user retains typed text) + error snackbar fires. Subject derived as `type.name` pre-Phase 10 (mirroring legacy `SettingsScreen.kt:374-376`'s `complaintViewModel.submit(it, it.name, body, ...)` pattern).
- `:ui` (MOD):
  - `ui/.../settings/SettingsScreen.kt` (MOD) — new "Feedback" `SectionCard` at the bottom of the `LazyColumn` with one `NavRow` ("Request feature / bug") that fires `OnOpenFeedbackDialog`. Inline private `@Composable FeedbackDialog` rendered conditionally on `state.feedbackDialogOpen`. Mirrors legacy `composeApp/.../dialogs/FeedbackDialog.kt` structure (dropdown + body field + Submit / Cancel) but drops the decorative SocialMediaRow footer (the rework `:ui` deliberately doesn't depend on that composeApp component; the core function is type+body+submit). Dropdown selection + body text are LOCAL `remember { mutableStateOf(...) }`. Submit gating matches legacy (`selectedType != null && body.length >= 5 && !isSubmitting`). Dismissal gating during submission via `DialogProperties` (disables back-press + outside-tap dismissal). Inline `ComplaintType.label` extension property (matches the `SettingsToggle.label` / `SettingsDestination.label` posture in the same file).
- `:composeApp` (MOD):
  - `composeApp/.../di/SettingsReworkModule.kt` (MOD) — `factory { SubmitFeedbackUseCase(get()) }` binding + 4th `get()` arg to the `viewModel { SettingsViewModel(...) }` binding. `FeedbackRepository` is already bound `single` by `languageReworkModule` (§93) — settings resolves the SAME singleton transitively via `get()`, no re-bind needed. KDoc extended to call out the transitive resolution.

### §98.3 MVI shape rationale

Why a single combined "OnSubmitFeedback(type, body)" intent instead of per-keystroke `OnFeedbackTypeChange` / `OnFeedbackBodyChange` intents that mirror the dialog inputs into MVI state?

- Local state is sufficient for the user-resume-typing experience (the dialog stays open while user types; the `remember { mutableStateOf(...) }` survives recomposition; if the dialog dismisses, the inputs reset — same UX as the legacy dialog).
- Per-keystroke intents would route every typed char through the VM's intent channel (unbounded flow), inflating event traffic without any state-driven side effect.
- Matches the §95 OnSubmitReply / OnSubmitEdit posture (legacy `ComplaintViewModel.submit` also reads `subject` + `body` from local fields, not from a mirrored state field).

Why `data object` for the open/dismiss intents (no payload) but `data class` for `OnSubmitFeedback`?

- Open/dismiss carry no caller-side variation — they're verbs that toggle a single state field. `data object` is the established posture for payload-free intents (matches `OnClearCache`).
- Submit carries the dropdown + body payload — these vary per-submission and the VM needs both to invoke the use case. `data class` carries them as constructor args.

### §98.4 Strangler-fig boundary

ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches. The §93 `FeedbackRepositoryImpl`'s existing 3-`:shared`-dep orchestration (`SendComplaintUseCase` + `UserIdProvider` + `DeviceInfoProvider`) carries both flows (language-request + generic feedback) unchanged. Same posture as the foundation slice's existing `SettingsRepositoryImpl` strangler-fig (1 reach — legacy `:shared` `SettingsRepository`, unchanged from §96).

The legacy ComplaintViewModel's submission path remains untouched on the legacy Settings screen — the legacy `Screen.Setting` route still uses `complaintViewModel.submit(...)`. The rework `Screen.SettingsRework` route uses the new `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` → `FeedbackRepository.submit` → `FeedbackRepositoryImpl` → same orchestration. Both paths write to the SAME Firestore collection with the SAME payload shape (userId + type + subject + body + metadata + createdAt + status); the admin-side complaint feed reads either path's submissions identically.

## §99 — Phase 7.x.settings.readingmode — Reading-mode picker dialog on rework Settings hub

Closes the third deferral from §96.9 ("No ReadingMode dialog"). Adds a "Reading" SectionCard with a single "Reading mode" row + the modal Reading-mode picker dialog to the rework Settings hub. The dialog uses single-tap-commits UX (tapping a row both persists the choice and closes the dialog) — matches the rework Theme picker's established `OnSelectTheme` posture, NOT the legacy two-step Apply/Revert. ZERO new `:domain` or `:data` files — both halves were already landed by Phase 6.4.x.mode; this slice is pure consumer wiring.

### §99.1 Strategy

Strangler-fig posture preserved. The Phase 6.4.x.mode slice (§44 / Task #219) already landed `ReadingModeRepository` (`:domain`) + `ReadingModeRepositoryImpl` (`:data`, over `ObservableSettings.getStringFlow("reading_mode")` — the SAME cell the legacy `:shared` `DataStoreHelper.readingModeFlow` reads from) + `ObserveReadingModeUseCase` + `SetReadingModeUseCase` + the `readerReworkModule` Koin bindings. The Settings hub slice only needs to consume them — no new types, no new bindings beyond the VM's constructor growth.

Three approaches considered for the dialog UX: (A) single-tap-commits (Theme picker posture — tap a row → persist + close); (B) two-step Apply/Revert (legacy `ReadingModeDialog.kt`'s posture — radio list + Apply button that commits + Cancel that reverts); (C) inline dropdown (no modal — selectedRow opens a dropdown anchored to the row). Chose (A) because: (1) matches the rework's established picker pattern (Theme picker landed in Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack); (2) cleaner MVI shape — no "pending selection" mirror in MVI state (the displayed mode comes directly from `state.readingMode`, which re-emits when the upstream `ObserveReadingModeUseCase` flow updates after the write commits); (3) `ObservableSettings.putString` is sub-microsecond synchronous on every platform — there's no in-flight window worth modeling, so the Apply step adds friction without any safety benefit.

MVI surface additions narrow: 2 new state fields (`readingMode: ReadingMode` + `readingModeDialogOpen: Boolean`) + 3 new intent variants (`OnOpenReadingModeDialog` / `OnDismissReadingModeDialog` — both `data object` — + `OnSelectReadingMode(mode)` `data class`). NO new effects (the picker is self-contained; no navigation, no snackbar feedback — the row's subtitle re-renders on the upstream re-emit, which is sufficient feedback). NO new use cases — the existing `ObserveReadingModeUseCase` + `SetReadingModeUseCase` from §44 are reused verbatim.

### §99.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:domain` (UNCHANGED) — `ReadingMode` enum, `ReadingModeRepository` interface, `ObserveReadingModeUseCase`, `SetReadingModeUseCase` all already landed by §44. No new types.
- `:data` (UNCHANGED) — `ReadingModeRepositoryImpl` already landed by §44 (over `ObservableSettings.getStringFlow("reading_mode", "DEFAULT")`, falling back to `DEFAULT` on unknown disk value). No new impl.
- `:presentation` (MOD):
  - `presentation/.../settings/SettingsState.kt` (MOD) — 2 new fields: `readingMode: ReadingMode = ReadingMode.DEFAULT` (driven by the new `init {}` collector) + `readingModeDialogOpen: Boolean = false` (dialog open/closed flag). Default `ReadingMode.DEFAULT` matches the repository's unset-disk fallback — the row shows a sensible label before the first emission (sub-millisecond gap on the same cold-start as the existing toggle defaults).
  - `presentation/.../settings/SettingsIntent.kt` (MOD) — 3 new variants: `OnOpenReadingModeDialog` (tap the row) / `OnDismissReadingModeDialog` (back-press / outside-tap / Cancel) / `OnSelectReadingMode(mode: ReadingMode)` (tap a dialog entry — persists + closes from the same code path).
  - `presentation/.../settings/SettingsViewModel.kt` (MOD) — constructor grows from 4 → 6 use case deps (the 2 reader use cases added). New 2nd `init {}` collector subscribes to `ObserveReadingModeUseCase` and projects each emission into `state.readingMode`. 3 new `when` branches in `handle(intent)` — the Open/Dismiss handlers are pure state mutations; the Select handler closes the dialog + fires `viewModelScope.launch { setReadingMode(mode) }` fire-and-forget (sub-microsecond `ObservableSettings.putString` write; no in-flight window). The upstream flow re-emits and the row's subtitle updates reactively.
- `:ui` (MOD):
  - `ui/.../settings/SettingsScreen.kt` (MOD) — new "Reading" `SectionCard` inserted between Theme and Navigation, hosting a single `ReadingModeRow` that shows "Reading mode" as the row title + the current mode's label as the subtitle. New conditional `ReadingModeDialog(...)` invocation alongside `FeedbackDialog`. New private `ReadingModeRow(mode, onClick)` composable. New private `ReadingModeDialog(currentMode, onSelect, onDismiss)` composable — `AlertDialog` with `RoundedCornerShape(20.dp)` + tonalElevation, hosting a `Column` of 6 rows (one per `ReadingMode.entries`); each row has a `RadioButton(selected = mode == currentMode, onClick = null)` + the label `Text`; tapping the row's `clickable` invokes `onSelect(mode)` (radio is `onClick = null` — the row owns the click). New inline `ReadingMode.label` extension property (matches `SettingsToggle.label` / `SettingsDestination.label` / `ComplaintType.label` posture in the same file).
- `:composeApp` (MOD):
  - `composeApp/.../di/SettingsReworkModule.kt` (MOD) — 6th `get()` arg to the `viewModel { SettingsViewModel(...) }` binding. NO new bindings — both reader use cases + the `ReadingModeRepository` `single` are already bound by `readerReworkModule` (§44); the settings slice resolves the SAME instances transitively via `get()`, no re-bind. KDoc extended to document the cross-module transitive resolution (same shape as the existing `FeedbackRepository` transitive note from §98).

### §99.3 MVI shape rationale

Why a separate `OnSelectReadingMode(mode)` intent instead of mirroring the dialog's selection into a transient `pendingReadingMode` state field?

- Single-tap-commits means there IS no "pending" state — selecting a row commits immediately. The dialog's RadioButton draws its selected indicator from `currentMode` directly (which equals `state.readingMode`); on `onSelect`, the dialog closes and the VM dispatches the write; the upstream flow re-emits and `state.readingMode` updates; the dialog (if still rendered for a frame) sees the new selection — but it's already dismissed.
- Mirroring into state would require a separate `pendingReadingMode` field + a synchronization point to clear it when the dialog dismisses — strictly more code with no observable difference.
- Matches the rework Theme picker's `OnSelectTheme(theme)` intent shape verbatim.

Why `viewModelScope.launch { setReadingMode(mode) }` fire-and-forget instead of a `suspend` collect + state update?

- The `ObservableSettings.putString` write is synchronous on every platform (in-memory hash-map mutate + commit to disk; sub-microsecond). There's no failure mode to handle — the call returns `Unit`, not `Result<Unit>` (unlike the cache-clear's okio file walk which can fail on missing dirs).
- The upstream `ObserveReadingModeUseCase` flow re-emits as soon as the put commits, so the state-update path is the existing `init {}` collector — no imperative VM-side mutation needed.
- Matches the existing `OnToggle` handler's posture (also fire-and-forget; the upstream pref flow re-emits and the toggle row's `Switch` updates reactively).

Why a separate `init {}` collector for `ObserveReadingModeUseCase` instead of extending the existing `combine(...)`-of-five over `SettingsRepository.observe()`?

- `ReadingMode` lives in a different `:domain` model (`reader.ReadingMode`) than the 5 `SettingsSnapshot` booleans + cache size — wiring it through `SettingsRepository.observe()` would require either widening that interface (violates SRP — `SettingsRepository` is the 5-toggle facade, not the everything-reactive facade) OR introducing a `SettingsSnapshot.readingMode` field that the existing `:data` impl would have to source from a different collaborator (couples the two repositories where they were independent).
- Two `init {}` collectors with their own `.launchIn(viewModelScope)` is the established multi-source projection pattern (the rework Reader VM does this with 3 collectors for chapters/pages/bookmarks; the rework Library VM does this with 2 collectors for library entries + filters).

### §99.4 Strangler-fig boundary

ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches in THIS slice. The §44 `ReadingModeRepositoryImpl` already taps the SAME `ObservableSettings` cell (`"reading_mode"`) the legacy `:shared` `DataStoreHelper.readingModeFlow` reads from and writes to (verified — legacy `DataStoreHelper.kt` calls `settings.getStringFlow(StorageKeys.READING_MODE, defaultValue = "DEFAULT")` and `settings.putString(StorageKeys.READING_MODE, mode)` where `StorageKeys.READING_MODE = "reading_mode"`). Toggling the mode on the rework Settings hub propagates to:
1. The legacy Reader VM via the legacy `DataStoreHelper.readingModeFlow` (which observes the SAME cell);
2. The rework Reader VM via the `:data` `ReadingModeRepositoryImpl.observe()` flow (which also observes the SAME cell);
3. The rework Settings hub's own row subtitle (re-renders on the upstream re-emit).

Three consumers, one cell of truth, no coordination needed — the cleanest possible strangler-fig posture. Phase 9.x route-swap retirement of the legacy `DataStoreHelper.readingModeFlow` happens when the legacy Reader retires; until then, both flows reactively converge on the same value on every write.

## §100 — Phase 7.x.settings.downloads — Downloads nav row bridging to legacy Screen.DownloadsScreen

### §100.1 Strategy

The §96.9 deferral list left "Downloads nav row" outstanding on the rework Settings hub. Investigation showed the rework codebase has no Downloads screen counterpart — there is no `Screen.DownloadsRework`, no `:ui/.../downloads/` package, no `:presentation/.../downloads/` MVI surface, no `:data/.../DownloadsRepositoryImpl`. The legacy Downloads screen at `composeApp/.../features/download/ui/screens/DownloadsScreen.kt` is the only working surface.

Two options were available:
1. **Defer the Downloads nav row until a full `Phase 7.x.downloads` slice lands** — would require the entire MVI stack (domain interface + use cases + data impl + presentation VM + UI composable + Koin module + nav route) for a screen the user already has a working legacy version of. Multiple commits, 5-files-per-commit cap means 3-4 sub-commits.
2. **Bridge the rework Settings hub's "Downloads" row to the existing legacy `Screen.DownloadsScreen` route** — three-file slice (one enum case + one when-arm + one label). Honours the strangler-fig posture (legacy route stays put; rework hub points to it). The Settings hub's `OnNavigate(DOWNLOADS)` intent fires the same generic effect every other nav row does — no new VM logic.

Option 2 was chosen. The Settings hub now offers the same 7 nav rows the legacy `composeApp/.../features/settings/ui/screens/SettingsScreen.kt` offers (minus the dead `Help` placeholder), parity-restored.

### §100.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`**: zero new files. The destination set is named in `:presentation`, not `:domain` — destinations are a presentation-layer concept (the nav-routing intent payload), not a business-model concept.

**`:data`**: zero new files. The Settings hub VM dispatches a fire-and-forget `SettingsEffect.NavigateTo` effect that flows through the existing `:ui` `onNavigate` callback. No new persistence, no new flow, no new repository binding.

**`:presentation`**: `SettingsDestination` enum (existing file at `presentation/.../settings/SettingsDestination.kt`) gets a new `DOWNLOADS` variant appended. The Settings hub VM is unchanged — `OnNavigate(intent.destination)` blindly emits `SettingsEffect.NavigateTo(destination)` regardless of which variant lands; adding a destination is pure surface-extension. The `SettingsState`, `SettingsIntent`, `SettingsEffect`, and `SettingsViewModel` files are all UNTOUCHED — this is the minimum-surface MVI extension.

**`:ui`**: `SettingsScreen.kt`'s `SettingsDestination.label` extension property (existing) gets a new `DOWNLOADS -> "Downloads"` arm appended. The `SectionCard("Navigation") { ... }` block already iterates `SettingsDestination.entries.forEachIndexed { ... }` — adding an enum variant automatically renders the new row without any composable change. The exhaustive-`when` on labels at `:466-491` enforces compile-time completeness.

**`:composeApp`**: `SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt`'s exhaustive `when (destination) { ... }` block gets a new `SettingsDestination.DOWNLOADS -> Screen.DownloadsScreen` arm appended. The adapter forwards to the LEGACY `Screen.DownloadsScreen` route (no rework counterpart exists). The legacy `App.kt` nav graph already binds `Screen.DownloadsScreen` to the legacy `DownloadsScreen` composable; no change there.

### §100.3 MVI shape rationale

The new destination doesn't require new intents, new effects, or new state — the existing `SettingsIntent.OnNavigate(destination: SettingsDestination)` variant accepts the new enum value transparently. The existing `SettingsEffect.NavigateTo(destination: SettingsDestination)` variant carries it through to the `:ui` `LaunchedEffect` collector, which forwards to the `onNavigate` callback wired by the route adapter. From the VM's perspective, the new destination is indistinguishable from any of the original six.

This is the OCP §6 contract working as designed: the sealed `SettingsIntent` / `SettingsEffect` interfaces accept new variants (or, in this case, the existing variant's payload accepts new enum values) without forcing any existing variant to change. The Settings hub VM compiled unchanged against the new enum — no behavioural change for any of the other six destinations.

### §100.4 Strangler-fig boundary

ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches in this slice. The reach is on the nav-graph side — the rework Settings hub navigates to a LEGACY route (`Screen.DownloadsScreen`), which the existing legacy `App.kt` nav graph binds to the legacy `DownloadsScreen` composable. From the rework's perspective:
1. The rework Settings hub fires `OnNavigate(DOWNLOADS)`.
2. The route adapter maps `DOWNLOADS -> Screen.DownloadsScreen`.
3. `navController.navigate(Screen.DownloadsScreen)` lands in the legacy `App.kt` `composable<Screen.DownloadsScreen> { ... }` block, which renders the legacy `DownloadsScreen` composable.

This is the inverse of the standard rework→legacy reach (which has rework `:data` impls reaching into `:shared` repositories). Here, the rework `:composeApp` nav adapter points to a legacy nav route — same strangler-fig posture, inverted direction. Phase 9.x route-swap retirement of the legacy `Screen.DownloadsScreen` binding happens when a `Phase 7.x.downloads` slice lands a `Screen.DownloadsRework` counterpart; until then, the rework hub points to the legacy screen and both routes stay reachable.

§96.9's remaining 6 deferrals (Help / CBZ progress / admin testing-mode / app-header image / i18n / nav graph route-swap) remain open. Help is a no-op `onClick = null` placeholder in the legacy too — porting it would change observable behaviour (the row becomes functional in the rework but is dead in the legacy) and is therefore better deferred until a Help URL actually exists in the `:platform` `IntentLauncher` target set. CBZ progress depends on a Chapters VM rework that has no foundation slice yet. Admin testing-mode is a `:composeApp`-level concern (depends on `Admin.testingMode` Compose state) not a Settings-hub MVI concern. App-header image needs a `:ui` compose-resources binding lift (cross-cutting; better as its own dedicated slice). i18n lifts in Phase 10 alongside every other rework consumer. Nav graph route-swap is Phase 9.x.

Recommended next: **Phase 7.x.complaint.admin** — admin counterpart to the user-side complaint surface; reuses sibling repository pattern from §94/§95 (`GetUserComplaintUseCase` posture inverted to fetch ALL complaints rather than just the current user's). Alternatively: **Phase 7.x.settings.appheader** — surface the app header image on the rework Settings hub via a `:ui` compose-resources binding lift; closes the §96.9 app-header deferral. Both are tractable slices ≤5 files; admin is the larger and more strategic; appheader is the smaller and more aesthetic.

## §101 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin — admin Complaint dashboard screen rework (foundation)

### §101.1 Strategy

§100's next-candidate block recommended **Phase 7.x.complaint.admin** as the strategic next step — admin counterpart to the user-side complaint surface (§94 / §95), inverting the user-side's `GetUserComplaintUseCase` posture to fetch ALL complaints rather than just the current user's. This slice lands the foundation surface (load + display + search + 2-axis filter) of the legacy admin Complaint dashboard, deferring the 6 admin mutations + statistics aggregation + sort options + app-version filter + long-press body-copy to a future `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.actions` sub-slice via OCP §6.

The user-side `ComplaintListRepository` KDoc lines 27-32 explicitly anticipated this admin slice as a SIBLING interface, not an extension — the user-side interface's `loadComplaints()` takes no `userId` arg (the impl pulls it from `UserIdProvider`), so making the admin "all complaints" load a second method on the same interface would force every non-admin consumer to depend on a method they can't use without elevated privileges. Two sibling interfaces with one method each is the ISP-clean split (contract §6 ISP).

Scope decision: the legacy `AdminComplaintViewModel` has 7 action methods (status change, edit, closure-reason, delete, bulk-update, bulk-delete, statistics aggregation). Determined this is too much for one slice. Scoped foundation to LOAD + DISPLAY + SEARCH + 2-axis FILTER only — exactly the surface the legacy admin screen renders on first view before any user interaction.

 - `domain/.../usecase/complaint/ObserveAllComplaintsUseCase.kt` — pass-through use case, `suspend operator fun invoke(): Result<List<ComplaintSummary>> = repository.loadAllComplaints()`.

Non-admin branch unchanged. Kept atomic so the route flip is reviewable in isolation.

### §101.3 MVI shape rationale

The admin foundation surface has TWO filter dimensions (status + type) where the user-side foundation (§94) had ONE (status only). Parity intent, parity surface — legacy admin filters by both axes (`AdminComplaintScreen.kt:140-141`), legacy user-side filters by status only.

Search dimension matches legacy admin semantics — `subject` + `body` + `id` + `userId` (4 fields, case-insensitive), vs the user-side's 3 fields (no `userId` — the user knows who they are). Admin searches userId too (legacy lines 184-189), so the admin foundation surface reuses the same posture.

`AdminComplaintEffect` is declared as an empty sealed interface. They CAN compile (sealed interfaces with no variants are valid Kotlin) and they document the slice's extensibility hook. The alternative ("don't declare them") would force `AdminComplaintViewModel` to extend `MviViewModel<AdminComplaintState, AdminComplaintIntent, Nothing>` — uglier signature, loss of OCP §6 extension hook. The empty-sealed-interface pattern is the rework convention for "no effects today; reserved for tomorrow" (same posture as the user-side foundation §94's effect declaration before §95 added the snackbar variants).

VM-side derivation of `state.filtered` from `state.all` + `state.searchQuery` + `state.selectedStatus` + `state.selectedType` matches the user-side foundation's posture — the `:ui` layer is contractually stateless; storing search/filter selections in Compose `remember` (as the legacy admin screen does, lines 139-144) would split the source of truth between VM and view. Recomputing in the VM on each intent keeps the composable stateless and lets future tests assert on `state.filtered` directly.

### §101.4 Strangler-fig boundary

ONE new `:data` → `:shared` reach in this slice — `AdminComplaintListRepositoryImpl(private val legacy: GetAllComplaintUseCase)`. Same posture as the user-side foundation (§94 — `ComplaintListRepositoryImpl(legacy = GetUserComplaintUseCase, ...)`) and the Reading-session timer port (Phase 6.4.x.statistics — `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl(legacy = ...)`). The `:data` impl maps `LegacyComplaint` → `ComplaintSummary` via private file-local extension functions; the domain model and the legacy model both coexist in the same module until Phase 9.x retirement of the legacy facade.

**Mapper duplication decision**: the user-side `ComplaintListRepositoryImpl` KDoc explicitly anticipated this admin slice as the trigger for lifting mappers to a shared `ComplaintMappers.kt`. Decided to defer the lift because it would: (a) require modifying the existing working user-side impl, (b) push commit 2 toward the 5-file cap, (c) mix structurally-distinct concerns (admin-foundation slice + DRY refactor). Duplication is bounded to two file-local 12-line blocks, all `:data`-internal, no exposed API surface. The lift is a candidate for a separate `Phase 7.x.complaint.mappers.lift` slice when/if a third complaint-consumer impl emerges.

### §101.5 Sibling repository pattern (ISP §6)

This slice exemplifies the ISP-clean split predicted by the user-side `ComplaintListRepository` KDoc lines 27-32. The two repositories are SIBLINGS, not an extension:

 - `:domain/.../repository/ComplaintListRepository.kt` — `suspend fun loadComplaints(): Result<List<ComplaintSummary>>` (user-scoped via `UserIdProvider` in the impl).
 - `:domain/.../repository/AdminComplaintListRepository.kt` — `suspend fun loadAllComplaints(): Result<List<ComplaintSummary>>` (collection-wide, no userId filter).

Each consumer depends only on what it uses. The user-side `ComplaintViewModel` never sees `loadAllComplaints()`; the admin-side `AdminComplaintViewModel` never sees `loadComplaints()`. The Settings hub adapter is the FIRST layer that knows both exist — and it routes via `Admin.isAdmin` (a `:composeApp`-level concern), not via a repository abstraction.

If a future requirement emerges to expose admin "all complaints" to non-admin contexts (e.g., a public statistics board), it would be a third sibling repository (`PublicComplaintStatsRepository`), not an extension of either existing interface. The ISP §6 contract scales by sibling proliferation, not interface widening.

### §101.6 Admin gate posture

Admin-only access is enforced at the Settings hub adapter — `SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt` consults `Admin.isAdmin` to decide between `Screen.ComplaintAdminRework` and `Screen.ComplaintRework`. The `AdminComplaintReworkScreenRoute` itself does NOT re-check `Admin.isAdmin` — same posture as the legacy `AdminComplaintScreenRoute`. If a non-admin somehow lands here (e.g., via a deep link in a debug build), the underlying Firestore query will surface a 403-permission-denied error which the screen's inline-error-with-Retry pattern handles gracefully.

The `:presentation` and `:ui` modules don't know about Admin state — that's a `:composeApp`-level concern. The `:domain` repository signature also doesn't gate on admin status; the Firestore security rules are the load-bearing access control (the legacy `GetAllComplaintUseCase` reaches Firestore directly, which enforces the admin-only `complaints` collection scan permission).

## §102 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.actions — admin mutations slice (status-change / closure-reason / delete)

### §102.1 Strategy

§101's next-candidate block recommended **Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.actions** as the strategic next step — admin WRITE counterpart to the foundation's READ slice, mirroring the user-side §94 → §95 progression. This slice ports the three per-row admin mutations that are the legacy admin's primary daily workflow:

1. **Status change** — the quintessential admin action. Legacy `AdminComplaintViewModel.updateComplaintStatus` (lines 65-98).
2. **Closure reason** — admin-specific specialization of "set status to CLOSED + provide a reason". Legacy `AdminComplaintViewModel.addClosureReason` (lines 139-190) — auto-CLOSEs the complaint when its current status is OPEN or IN_PROGRESS, leaves the status alone otherwise.
3. **Delete** — admin-side parity with the legacy admin's `DeleteConfirmationDialog`. Legacy `AdminComplaintViewModel.deleteComplaint` (lines 195-224).

Edit / Bulk-update / Bulk-delete / Statistics / Sort / App-version filter / Long-press copy intentionally deferred (the 3-action size matches the user-side §95's 3 actions exactly).

### §102.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — 4 new files (commit 2, `52e8bb0`):
 - `domain/.../repository/AdminComplaintActionRepository.kt` — interface with 3 methods: `suspend fun changeStatus(complaint, newStatus): Result<Unit>`, `suspend fun addClosureReason(complaint, reason): Result<Unit>`, `suspend fun deleteComplaint(id): Result<Unit>`. Sibling to `ComplaintActionRepository` (§95), not an extension — two separate WRITE-side scopes (user-side vs admin-side).
 - `domain/.../usecase/complaint/ChangeComplaintStatusUseCase.kt` — pass-through.
 - `domain/.../usecase/complaint/AddClosureReasonUseCase.kt` — pass-through.
 - `domain/.../usecase/complaint/AdminDeleteComplaintUseCase.kt` — pass-through. The `Admin`-prefix disambiguates from user-side `DeleteComplaintUseCase`; both bind to the legacy `DeleteComplaintUseCase` but depend on different repository interfaces.

**`:data`** — 1 new file (commit 3, `2cfaff3`):
 - `data/.../repository/AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt` — class takes 4 legacy collaborators (`LegacyGetAllComplaintUseCase`, `LegacyUpdateComplaintUseCase`, `LegacyDeleteComplaintUseCase`, `UserIdProvider`). Implements `changeStatus` by re-fetching the legacy `Complaint` by id (via `legacyGetAll().firstOrNull { it.id == id }`), `copy`-ing the new status into it, and writing it back. Implements `addClosureReason` by re-fetching, then merging `reason` / `reasonAddedBy` / `reasonAddedAt` into legacy `metadata`, then auto-CLOSEing on OPEN/IN_PROGRESS, then writing back. Implements `deleteComplaint` as a direct pass-through to `legacyDelete(id)`. KDoc covers the metadata-preservation strategy + `@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)` rationale.

**`:presentation`** — 5 modified files at the commit cap (commit 4, `5c8236b`):
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintState.kt` — appends 3 fields: `actionDialogMode: AdminActionDialogMode = NONE`, `activeComplaint: ComplaintSummary? = null`, `isSubmittingAction: Boolean = false`. Adds the `AdminActionDialogMode` enum (5 variants: `NONE`, `MENU`, `STATUS_CHANGE`, `CLOSURE_REASON`, `DELETE_CONFIRM`).
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintIntent.kt` — appends 6 new variants under the actions-slice section: `OnRowClick(complaint)`, `OnDismissActionDialog`, `OnSelectAction(mode)`, `OnSubmitStatusChange(newStatus)`, `OnSubmitClosureReason(reason)`, `OnConfirmDelete`.
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintEffect.kt` — appends `ShowSuccessMessage(message: String)` + `ShowErrorMessage(message: String)`. Same posture as user-side `ComplaintEffect`'s 2 effects — one snackbar variant per outcome, message text carries the action-specific copy.
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintViewModel.kt` — constructor signature widens to 4 use cases (added `changeStatus`, `addClosureReason`, `adminDeleteComplaint`). `handle()` `when` arm exhaustively covers the 6 new intents via 6 new private handlers (`handleRowClick`, `handleDismissDialog`, `handleSelectAction`, `handleSubmitStatusChange`, `handleSubmitClosureReason`, `handleConfirmDelete`) + 1 shared helper `completeAction(result, successMessage)` — same shape as user-side §95's `completeAction()`.
 - MOD `composeApp/.../di/ComplaintAdminReworkModule.kt` — bundled into this commit (5-file cap). Adds `single<AdminComplaintActionRepository> { ... }` binding constructor-injecting the 4 legacy collaborators, plus 3 `factory` bindings for the use cases, plus extends the `viewModel { AdminComplaintViewModel(...) }` block with the 3 new ctor args. Bundling rationale: the VM's new constructor args would break the existing Koin binding if separated.

**`:ui`** — 1 new + 1 modified file (commit 5, `db05068`):
 - NEW `ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt` — single composable, 4 sub-modes (Menu / StatusChange / ClosureReason / DeleteConfirm) like user-side `ComplaintActionDialog`'s 4 sub-modes (Menu / Reply / Edit / Delete). Sub-mode contents: 3 admin-action buttons in MENU (Delete uses error contentColor); status candidate buttons in STATUS_CHANGE (excludes the complaint's current status); 500-char-capped `OutlinedTextField` with non-blank Add button in CLOSURE_REASON; warning + destructive Button in DELETE_CONFIRM. Submit-button loading state comes from `isSubmittingAction` (single source of truth). All affordances gated by `isSubmitting`.
 - MOD `ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` — adds `snackbarHostState` + `LaunchedEffect(viewModel)` effects collector routing `ShowSuccessMessage` / `ShowErrorMessage` to the host. `Scaffold`'s `snackbarHost` slot wired. Conditionally mounts `AdminComplaintActionDialog` when `actionDialogMode != NONE && activeComplaint != null`. `AdminComplaintRow` Card is now `clickable` and fires `OnRowClick(complaint)`.

### §102.3 MVI shape rationale

The MVI surface evolved from foundation (5 intents, 0 effects, 7-field state) to actions (11 intents, 2 effects, 10-field state). The OCP §6 anticipation from foundation slice §101 materialised exactly as predicted — `AdminComplaintEffect` was an empty sealed interface specifically for this addition, and `AdminComplaintIntent` was a sealed interface so the new variants are exhaustively checked in the VM `when`.

**`completeAction()` helper** — shared post-mutation flow: on success, clear `isSubmittingAction` / `actionDialogMode` / `activeComplaint`, emit `ShowSuccessMessage`, then refire `loadList()` to refresh the table. On failure, clear `isSubmittingAction` only (keep dialog open with the user's input preserved), emit `ShowErrorMessage`. Matches user-side §95's `completeAction()` shape.

**In-flight guard via `isSubmittingAction`** — every handler short-circuits when `state.value.isSubmittingAction` is true, preventing concurrent mutations on the same complaint. Defence-in-depth: the MVI base class already serialises intents through a single channel, but the guard catches races introduced by future channel changes.

**Dialog-state-overlap with list `isLoading`** — same posture as user-side §95: the VM sets `isSubmittingAction = true` (not `isLoading`) during the write; after success, `completeAction()` clears the dialog substate first, emits the effect, then refires `loadList()` which sets `isLoading = true` briefly. The list-loading flicker happens with the dialog gone.

### §102.4 Strangler-fig boundary

3 new `:data` → `:shared` reaches in this slice — `AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl` constructor-injects `LegacyGetAllComplaintUseCase`, `LegacyUpdateComplaintUseCase`, `LegacyDeleteComplaintUseCase` (plus `UserIdProvider` for the closure-reason metadata `reasonAddedBy` field). Same posture as the user-side §95 (which constructor-injects `SendComplaintUseCase` / `UpdateComplaintUseCase` / `DeleteComplaintUseCase`) and the foundation §101 (which constructor-injects `GetAllComplaintUseCase`). All four legacy use cases are pre-bound `single` in `SharedModule` from prior phases; no new boundaries.

**Metadata preservation strategy**: `ComplaintSummary` (domain) deliberately omits `metadata: Map<String, Any>?` per Contract §6 banned-`Any` rule. Solved by re-fetching the full legacy `Complaint` by id (via `legacyGetAll().firstOrNull { it.id == id }`) inside the `:data` impl before each write, then preserving / extending its metadata. Cost: 1 extra Firestore READ per admin action — acceptable for admin frequency (admins act on individual complaints, not in tight loops), retired by Phase 9.x route-swap when the rework owns Firestore directly. The `Any` containment is confined to `:data`'s mutableMap; `:domain` sees only `String reason`.

### §102.5 Closure-reason auto-CLOSE semantics

Legacy `AdminComplaintViewModel.addClosureReason` lines 156-163 auto-CLOSEs the complaint when its current status is OPEN or IN_PROGRESS, and leaves other statuses (CLOSED / RESOLVED / etc.) alone. Ported verbatim in `AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.addClosureReason`:

```kotlin
val newStatus = when (legacy.status) {
    LegacyComplaintStatus.OPEN, LegacyComplaintStatus.IN_PROGRESS -> LegacyComplaintStatus.CLOSED
    else -> legacy.status
}
```

Two metadata fields are merged on top of legacy's existing `metadata`:
 - `reason` — the admin-provided closure rationale.
 - `reasonAddedBy` — the admin's `userId` from `UserIdProvider`.
 - `reasonAddedAt` — `kotlin.time.Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds().toString()` (NOT `kotlinx.datetime.Clock` — `:data` module convention is `kotlin.time.Clock` with `@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)`).

### §102.6 Sibling repository pattern (ISP §6)

Both new repos in this complaint-rework family (`ComplaintActionRepository` §95 and `AdminComplaintActionRepository` §102) are SIBLINGS, not an extension hierarchy. Three reasons documented in the impl KDoc:

1. **Different write scope semantics**: user-side WRITES are "act on MY complaint" (auth-gated by Firestore rules to the caller's userId). Admin WRITES are "act on ANY complaint" (admin-gated client-side, with Firestore rules enforcing the admin-collection permission).
2. **Different mutation methods**: user-side has reply/edit/delete; admin has status-change/closure-reason/delete. Only `delete` overlaps; the legacy `:shared` `DeleteComplaintUseCase` doesn't care who calls it.
3. **ISP §6**: fattening either interface to include the other's methods would force consumers to depend on methods they never call. Two clean siblings.
