## §103 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.edit — admin edit-complaint slice

### §103.1 Strategy

§102's next-candidate block recommended **Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.edit** as the strategic next step — admin-side EDIT counterpart to the user-side §95 edit flow, completing the admin mutations triad (status-change + closure-reason + delete + EDIT) and harmonising the user-side / admin-side action surfaces. The legacy admin screen at `composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:451-577` exposes an inline edit dialog (`EditComplaintDialog`) that overwrites the complaint's `subject` and `body` while preserving every other field — this slice ports that exact behaviour onto the rework surface.

Two semantic decisions distinguish this slice from a copy-paste of user-side §95's edit path:

1. **Metadata preservation**: user-side §95's edit nulls out the legacy `metadata: Map<String, Any>?` (because user-side complaints don't carry closure-reason audit trails — the metadata is closure-reason-only). Admin-side edits MUST preserve metadata: an admin-edited complaint that already has a closure-reason should keep its `reason` / `reasonAddedBy` / `reasonAddedAt` audit fields intact. The `:data` impl achieves this via the reuse of the existing `fetchLegacyById` helper from §102, followed by `legacy.copy(subject = subject, body = body)` — the data class copy default behaviour preserves every other field including metadata.
2. **Naming convention**: the use case is `AdminEditComplaintUseCase` (Admin prefix), not `EditAdminComplaintUseCase`. This matches the existing `AdminDeleteComplaintUseCase` naming pattern — the `Admin` prefix is applied when a same-action use case already exists in user-side scope (`EditComplaintUseCase` already binds to the user-side action). Both eventually fan into the legacy `UpdateComplaintUseCase` but via different `:domain` repositories (`ComplaintActionRepository` vs `AdminComplaintActionRepository`).

### §103.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — 1 modified + 1 new file (commit 2, `fed8fe7`):
 - MOD `domain/.../repository/AdminComplaintActionRepository.kt` — adds a 4th method `suspend fun editComplaint(original: ComplaintSummary, subject: String, body: String): Result<Unit>`. KDoc paragraph swaps "No edit method here" (the §102 deferral note) for an "Edit method" paragraph documenting the metadata-preservation distinction from user-side.
 - NEW `domain/.../usecase/complaint/AdminEditComplaintUseCase.kt` — `class AdminEditComplaintUseCase(private val repository: AdminComplaintActionRepository) { suspend operator fun invoke(original, subject, body): Result<Unit> = repository.editComplaint(original, subject, body) }`. Thin pass-through; sibling to user-side `EditComplaintUseCase`.

**`:data`** — 1 modified file (commit 2, `fed8fe7`):
 - MOD `data/.../repository/AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt` — adds the `editComplaint` override:
   ```kotlin
   override suspend fun editComplaint(
       original: ComplaintSummary,
       subject: String,
       body: String,
   ): Result<Unit> = runCatching {
       val legacy = fetchLegacyById(original.id)
       val updated = legacy.copy(subject = subject, body = body)
       legacyUpdate(updated)
   }
   ```
   Reuses the existing `fetchLegacyById` helper (already in the class from §102's `changeStatus` / `addClosureReason` implementations) — zero new `:data` → `:shared` reach. Metadata + every other field (`userId` / `type` / `createdAt` / `status`) passes through unchanged via `legacy.copy` defaults.

**`:presentation` MVI + Koin + `:ui`** — 5 modified files at the commit cap (commit 3, `408088a`). The Android compile gate forced bundling here: adding `EDIT` to `AdminActionDialogMode` would have made the existing dialog's `when (mode)` non-exhaustive on the `:presentation`+Koin commit, so the `:ui` dialog work shipped in the same commit.

 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintIntent.kt` — appends a new variant `data class OnSubmitEdit(val subject: String, val body: String) : AdminComplaintIntent` under a "Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.edit" section. KDoc documents the validation policy (UI's job, not the VM's — same posture as user-side §95).
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintState.kt` — adds `EDIT` to the `AdminActionDialogMode` enum (sixth variant after `NONE` / `MENU` / `STATUS_CHANGE` / `CLOSURE_REASON` / `DELETE_CONFIRM`). KDoc bullet for the new variant explains metadata preservation.
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintViewModel.kt` — constructor widens from 4 to 5 use cases (`adminEditComplaint: AdminEditComplaintUseCase` appended). `handle()` `when` arm exhaustively gains the `OnSubmitEdit` case dispatching to a new private handler `handleSubmitEdit(subject, body)` — exactly the same shape as user-side §95's `handleSubmitEdit`. The handler reuses the existing `completeAction(result, successMessage)` helper from §102 — no new helper machinery introduced.
 - MOD `composeApp/.../di/ComplaintAdminReworkModule.kt` — adds `factory { AdminEditComplaintUseCase(get()) }` line + threads `adminEditComplaint = get(),` into the `viewModel { ... }` block. The `single<AdminComplaintActionRepository>` binding is unchanged because the impl's constructor signature didn't widen — `editComplaint` reuses the 4 legacy collaborators already injected.
 - MOD `ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt` — adds the `AdminActionDialogMode.EDIT -> EditContent(complaint, isSubmitting, onIntent)` branch in the outer `when (mode)`; adds an OutlinedButton "Edit" affordance in `ActionSelectionContent` between "Change status" and "Add closure reason"; adds a new private `EditContent` composable mirroring user-side §95's `EditContent` (subject `OutlinedTextField` singleLine; body `OutlinedTextField` minLines=4 / maxLines=8 / maxChars=1000; char counter; Cancel + Save buttons; validation requires non-blank subject AND non-blank body AND ≤1000 chars; `rememberSaveable(complaint.id)` for both fields initialised to `complaint.subject` / `complaint.body`).

### §103.3 MVI shape rationale

The MVI surface evolved from actions (11 intents, 2 effects, 10-field state, 4-arg VM ctor) to edit (12 intents, 2 effects, 10-field state + 6th enum variant, 5-arg VM ctor). The OCP §6 anticipation from §102 materialised exactly as predicted — `AdminComplaintIntent` was a sealed interface so the new `OnSubmitEdit` variant is exhaustively checked in the VM `when`, and `AdminActionDialogMode` was an enum so adding the `EDIT` variant only required a single `when` arm addition in the `:ui` dialog.

**`completeAction()` helper reuse** — no new shared helper introduced. The post-mutation flow (success: clear `isSubmittingAction` / `actionDialogMode` / `activeComplaint`, emit `ShowSuccessMessage`, refire `loadList()`; failure: clear `isSubmittingAction` only, keep dialog open, emit `ShowErrorMessage`) is identical to the 3 prior admin mutations.

**Validation policy mirrors user-side §95** — the `:ui` dialog enforces non-blank subject + non-blank body + ≤1000 chars before enabling Save. The VM does NOT re-validate (no defense-in-depth — would diverge from user-side's policy and conceal a real validation bug). The use case + repository + impl all trust the `:ui` layer's gate.

### §103.4 Strangler-fig boundary

**Zero new `:data` → `:shared` reaches** in this slice. The `:data` impl reuses the existing `fetchLegacyById` helper (which itself uses the `legacyGetAll` collaborator already injected by §102) plus the `legacyUpdate` collaborator already injected by §102. The `editComplaint` override is a 4-line method that composes existing collaborators — no new constructor args, no new `single` bindings, no new legacy use case references.

This is a deliberate posture: the rework architecture's strangler-fig boundary is best held to the minimum surface possible, and any slice that can land without widening the boundary should do so. §103 demonstrates the pattern — adding a new mutation method to an existing rework repository does NOT necessarily require a new legacy reach if the existing collaborators are sufficient.

### §103.5 Metadata preservation strategy

The legacy `Complaint.metadata: Map<String, Any>?` field carries the closure-reason audit trail (`reason` / `reasonAddedBy` / `reasonAddedAt` from §102's `addClosureReason`). The admin edit MUST preserve this — an admin who closes a complaint with a reason and later edits its subject/body should NOT lose the audit trail.

User-side §95's edit (which the admin edit might naively copy) doesn't have this concern because user-side complaints never carry closure-reason metadata (only admins add closure reasons). User-side §95 therefore nulls out the metadata via `legacy.copy(metadata = null)`. Admin-side §103 explicitly preserves it via `legacy.copy(subject = ..., body = ...)` — the data class copy default leaves every unmentioned field unchanged, including `metadata`.

This is documented in three places: the `:domain` interface's `editComplaint` KDoc, the `AdminEditComplaintUseCase` KDoc, and the `:data` impl's `editComplaint` override KDoc.

### §103.6 Naming convention: Admin-prefix vs Action-suffix

`AdminEditComplaintUseCase` — Admin prefix — vs `EditAdminComplaintUseCase` — Admin suffix. The chosen prefix matches:
 - §102's `AdminDeleteComplaintUseCase` (the prior admin mutation that overlapped with a user-side same-action use case).
 - The rule: **Admin prefix is applied when the same-action use case already exists in user-side scope**. Both `EditComplaintUseCase` (user-side §95) and `DeleteComplaintUseCase` (user-side §95) already exist; their admin counterparts get the `Admin` prefix.
 - The contrast: `ChangeComplaintStatusUseCase` and `AddClosureReasonUseCase` (§102) have NO `Admin` prefix because no user-side same-action use case exists — only admins change status / add closure reasons.

## §104 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.sort — admin sort dropdown sub-slice

### §104.1 Strategy

§103's next-candidate block recommended **Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.sort** as the strategic next step — port the legacy admin's sort dropdown (legacy `composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:198-209` + `SortOption.kt`) onto the rework admin Complaint dashboard, lifting the §102.9 sort deferral. Smallest of §103's five candidates, fully self-contained in `:presentation` + `:ui`, and a daily-workflow win for admin users (5 sort modes vs the foundation's "native Firestore order" baseline).

Two strategic decisions narrowed the surface:

1. **Zero `:domain` / `:data` / Koin touches**: client-side sorting on the already-loaded list. The 5 sort modes are pure projections of `ComplaintSummary` fields already present on the domain model (`createdAt`, `status.ordinal`, `type.ordinal`, `userId`). No new use cases, no new repository methods, no new Koin bindings.
2. **5 of 7 legacy modes, not all 7**: the legacy enum has 7 variants — `DATE_ASC` / `DATE_DESC` / `STATUS` / `TYPE` / `USER_ID` / `APP_VERSION` / `APP_VERSION_DESC`. The two `APP_VERSION` modes require a `metadata.appVersion` field that the `:domain` `ComplaintSummary` deliberately omits (per its KDoc lines 28-34 — banned `Map<String, Any>` per contract §6). The two APP_VERSION sorts ship later in `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.versionfilter` together with the deferred third filter axis (same metadata-field blocker). The rework's 5 ported modes match every legacy mode whose sort key is a structured `ComplaintSummary` field.

### §104.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:presentation`** — 3 modified files (commit 2, `d5a9d77`):
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintState.kt` — new top-level `enum class AdminSortMode { DATE_DESC, DATE_ASC, STATUS, TYPE, USER_ID }` (5 variants, matching the order of the legacy `SortOption` enum minus the two deferred APP_VERSION variants). New state field `val selectedSort: AdminSortMode = AdminSortMode.DATE_DESC` after `selectedType` (defaulting to date-desc — matches legacy default at `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:143`).
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintIntent.kt` — new variant `data class OnSortChange(val mode: AdminSortMode) : AdminComplaintIntent` under a new "Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.sort" section. KDoc documents single-select semantics (no toggle-off — the default DATE_DESC IS the natural unsorted-feeling option).
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintViewModel.kt` — rename `applyFilter` → `applyFilterAndSort` (4 handler updateState calls + `loadList`). New param `sort: AdminSortMode` and a `when (sort)` `return` block that runs the sort after the filter. New `when (intent)` arm `OnSortChange` copies `selectedSort` into state and re-runs `applyFilterAndSort`. The sort lambdas use Kotlin stdlib's `sortedBy` / `sortedByDescending` — `createdAt` is nullable `Instant?` and the stdlib's nullable Comparable convention applies (sortedBy puts nulls first, sortedByDescending puts nulls last — matches legacy semantics where the same Kotlin sort is applied to `java.util.Date?`).

**`:ui`** — 1 modified file (commit 2, `d5a9d77`):
 - MOD `ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` — `SearchAndFilterSection` gains a `selectedSort: AdminSortMode` parameter, threaded from the call site in `AdminComplaintList`. A new private `SortDropdown` composable (`OutlinedButton` + `DropdownMenu` + `DropdownMenuItem` over `AdminSortMode.entries`) renders below the type-filter chip row and above the results-count text. A new private `sortLabel(mode: AdminSortMode): String` helper maps each enum variant to its inline English label (`"Newest first" / "Oldest first" / "Status" / "Type" / "User ID"`).

**`:composeApp`** — ZERO files. The VM constructor signature did not widen (no new use case dep). Koin binding unchanged. No new nav route (the dropdown lives inside the existing `AdminComplaintScreen`). No new Screen.kt entry.

### §104.3 MVI shape rationale

The MVI surface evolved from edit (12 intents, 2 effects, 10-field state, 5-arg VM ctor) to sort (13 intents, 2 effects, 11-field state, 5-arg VM ctor). The OCP §6 anticipation from §102 / §103 continued to deliver — `AdminComplaintIntent` was a sealed interface so the new `OnSortChange` variant is exhaustively checked in the VM `when`, and `AdminComplaintState` was a data class so adding `selectedSort` only required threading through `copy` calls and `applyFilterAndSort`.

**`applyFilter` → `applyFilterAndSort` rename**: the helper's responsibility broadened from "filter only" to "filter then sort", so the name follows. The renamed helper is invoked at 5 call sites — 4 filter handlers (`OnSearchChange`, `OnClearSearch`, `OnStatusFilter`, `OnTypeFilter`) and `loadList` (initial load + retry). The new `OnSortChange` handler is the 5th call site. All 5 thread the current `selectedSort` (from `it.copy` lambda's receiver) into the helper. The rename + threading happens in one commit because the build is red between any partial split (the helper signature changes everywhere or nowhere).

**Sort always active, no "null = unsorted"** — sort is single-select with no toggle-off. The default `DATE_DESC` serves as the natural baseline ("Newest first" is the unsorted-feeling option). Users pick a different mode to change. Contrasts with the status/type filter chips, which DO toggle off (tap same chip twice → `null`) because "all statuses / all types" is a meaningful state distinct from any single chip.

**Nullable createdAt sort behaviour** — `sortedBy { it.createdAt }` puts nulls first (Kotlin's nullable Comparable convention); `sortedByDescending { it.createdAt }` puts nulls last. This is the same behaviour the legacy admin gets from the identical stdlib calls on `java.util.Date?`. The legacy emits nulls at the same boundaries; behaviour parity preserved.

### §104.4 Strangler-fig boundary

**Zero new `:data` → `:shared` reaches**, and zero touches to `:data` / `:domain` / Koin / nav at all. The slice's surface is purely `:presentation` (3 files) + `:ui` (1 file). This is the smallest possible cross-cut for a meaningful behavioural addition — the same posture as §103.4's emphasis that "any slice that can land without widening the boundary should do so."

The strangler-fig posture continues unchanged from §102/§103 — `AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl` reaches `:shared` through the same 4 collaborators, the 5 admin use cases in the VM ctor remain unchanged, and the existing `ObserveAllComplaintsUseCase` continues to return the full list which the VM then filters + sorts client-side.

### §104.5 Client-side vs server-side sort

The legacy admin's sort is also client-side (legacy `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:198-209` sorts the already-loaded `filteredAndSortedComplaints` list). The rework matches: server-side ordering would require either a new Firestore query parameter (not available without restructuring the legacy `ObserveAllComplaintsUseCase`) or a new sibling use case that takes a sort hint. Both options widen the strangler-fig surface for a feature whose volume (≤200 complaints per admin's data scale) easily fits a client-side sort.

If the data scale grows beyond practical client-side sort (e.g., 100K+ complaints), a future slice can introduce a server-side sort hint via either (a) a new method on `ComplaintAdminRepository` returning a pre-sorted stream, or (b) a sibling `ObserveAllComplaintsSortedUseCase`. The current 5-mode client-side surface lifts directly into either pattern without changing the MVI intent / state surface — `OnSortChange` just dispatches differently in the VM.

### §104.6 Inline English labels + sort-label decoupling

The 5 sort modes have user-facing labels distinct from their enum names: `DATE_DESC → "Newest first"`, `DATE_ASC → "Oldest first"`, `STATUS → "Status"`, `TYPE → "Type"`, `USER_ID → "User ID"`. The decoupling (private `sortLabel(mode): String` helper in `:ui`, not a property on the enum) is intentional — the enum name lives in `:presentation` (a translation-agnostic surface) while the label is `:ui` (translatable). Phase 10 i18n will swap the label helper to `stringResource(Res.string.sort_<mode>)` lookups without touching the enum.

The legacy admin's labels are `"Date (oldest first)" / "Date (newest first)" / "Status" / "Type" / "User ID" / "App Version (lowest first)" / "App Version (highest first)"` (legacy `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:573-580`). The rework's shorter "Newest first" / "Oldest first" labels are a deliberate compression — the verbose `"Date (newest first)"` parenthetical adds no information once the sort affordance is clearly labeled "Sort:" (or in this rework: the section header "Sort"). Phase 10 i18n can revisit the label voice for the rework.

## §105 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.copy — admin long-press body-copy sub-slice

### §105.1 Strategy

§104's next-candidate block recommended **Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.copy** as the smallest remaining self-contained extension to the admin Complaint dashboard. Ports the legacy admin's long-press body-copy affordance (legacy `composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:830-842`) onto the rework dashboard: admin long-presses a complaint row's body text → it lands on the system clipboard → snackbar confirms "Copied to clipboard".

§104's recommendation block had predicted the design would land "1 new `AdminComplaintEffect.CopyToClipboard(text: String)` variant + 1 new platform clipboard adapter at the route layer". That prediction turned out to be unnecessary — the actual landed design is simpler:

1. **NO new `Effect` variant**: the clipboard write is a side effect at the `:ui` boundary (composition-local access via `LocalClipboardManager.current`); only the snackbar travels through MVI, and the existing `ShowSuccessMessage` effect handles that. So `AdminComplaintEffect` stays at 2 variants.
2. **NO platform clipboard adapter**: `LocalClipboardManager` is a Compose `compositionLocalOf` that works on Android / iOS / Desktop without any `:platform` actual/expect bridging. The clipboard manager is one of the standard Compose Multiplatform composition locals.

The intent's purpose is purely to centralize the snackbar emission via the VM (matching the posture of the other admin mutations' success snackbars — every snackbar in this slice goes through `AdminComplaintEffect`). The body text is captured in the row composable closure at the moment of long-press; it doesn't need to travel through state.

### §105.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:presentation`** — 2 modified files (commit 2, `11c4d48`):
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintIntent.kt` — new variant `data object OnCopyBody : AdminComplaintIntent` under a new "Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.copy" section. Payload-free — clipboard write happens at the `:ui` boundary. KDoc documents (a) the dispatch flow ("UI long-pressed body → clipboard.setText → emit snackbar"), (b) why payload-free (`:ui` captures the body directly from the row's `complaint.body`; threading it through state would be redundant), (c) why not gated by `isSubmittingAction` (copy is a passive non-destructive read; allowing it during in-flight mutations is harmless and matches legacy ergonomics).
 - MOD `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintViewModel.kt` — new `is AdminComplaintIntent.OnCopyBody -> handleCopyBody()` arm in the exhaustive `when (intent)`. New private `private suspend fun handleCopyBody() { emit(AdminComplaintEffect.ShowSuccessMessage("Copied to clipboard")) }`. No state mutation; no `viewModelScope.launch`; no use case dependency widening.

**`:ui`** — 1 modified file (commit 2, `11c4d48`):
 - MOD `ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` — 4 new imports (`ExperimentalFoundationApi`, `combinedClickable`, `LocalClipboardManager`, `AnnotatedString`). `AdminComplaintRow` gains `onLongClickBody: () -> Unit` parameter + opts into `ExperimentalFoundationApi` + captures `clipboardManager = LocalClipboardManager.current` from the composition local. The body `Text` now wraps in `Modifier.combinedClickable(onClick = {}, onLongClick = { clipboardManager.setText(AnnotatedString(complaint.body)); onLongClickBody() })` — matching legacy verbatim. `AdminComplaintList`'s `AdminComplaintRow` call passes `onLongClickBody = { onIntent(AdminComplaintIntent.OnCopyBody) }`.

**`:composeApp`** — ZERO files. No new Koin bindings (clipboard manager is a Compose composition local, not a `:platform` interface). No new nav route (the long-press lives inside the existing `AdminComplaintScreen`). No new Screen.kt entry. The VM constructor signature did not widen.

**`:data` / `:domain`** — ZERO files. Pure UX feature with no data-layer touch points.

### §105.3 MVI shape rationale

The MVI surface evolved from sort (13 intents, 2 effects, 11-field state, 5-arg VM ctor) to copy (14 intents, 2 effects, 11-field state, 5-arg VM ctor). The OCP §6 anticipation from §102/§103/§104 continued to deliver — `AdminComplaintIntent` is a sealed interface so the new `OnCopyBody` variant is exhaustively checked in the VM `when`. `AdminComplaintEffect` did not widen; the new intent reuses the existing `ShowSuccessMessage` snackbar emission.

**Why payload-free `data object`** — the clipboard write needs the body text, but it happens at the `:ui` boundary where the row composable already has `complaint.body` in scope. Threading the body through the intent would be redundant. Per the rework MVI contract, sealed-interface variants are `data class` (when they carry payload) or `data object` (when they don't); payload-free intents become `data object`.

**Why no new Effect variant** — §102's `AdminComplaintEffect.kt` KDoc anticipated a future `CopyToClipboard(text: String)` variant. The KDoc anticipation was right in spirit (the slice would eventually land) but wrong in shape: the actual design has no need for the effect because the clipboard write is a `:ui`-local side effect, not a cross-boundary one-shot. Only the snackbar emission needs to be a centralized effect, and `ShowSuccessMessage("Copied to clipboard")` covers that without widening the effect surface.

If a future slice needs to copy from outside the row composable (e.g., a dialog's "Copy" button that doesn't have access to the row's composition local), the `CopyToClipboard(text: String)` effect variant slots in via OCP §6 as a sibling to `ShowSuccessMessage`. That future scenario would need a `:platform` adapter at the route layer to bridge the effect to a platform clipboard write (since the dialog's effect collector lives outside the composition-local-bearing row scope). The current slice's design avoids that need entirely.

**Why no `isSubmittingAction` gating on `handleCopyBody`** — copy is a passive, non-destructive read. Allowing it during a pending mutation is harmless and matches legacy ergonomics (the legacy admin's long-press body-copy is also un-gated; an admin can long-press a row's body to clipboard while a status-change submission is in flight).

### §105.4 Strangler-fig boundary

**ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches**, and ZERO touches to `:data` / `:domain` / Koin / nav at all. The slice's surface is purely `:presentation` (2 files) + `:ui` (1 file). Same posture as §104 — "any slice that can land without widening the boundary should do so."

The strangler-fig posture continues unchanged from §102/§103/§104 — `AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl` reaches `:shared` through the same 4 collaborators, the 5 admin use cases in the VM ctor remain unchanged, no new repository interfaces or use cases were introduced.

### §105.5 Tap-consumption rationale

`combinedClickable` on the body `Text` consumes the tap — it does NOT bubble to the parent Card's `clickable(onClick = onClick)`. This means:
 - Tap on the body row → no action (legacy parity; legacy uses `combinedClickable(onClick = { /* no-op */ }, onLongClick = …)`).
 - Tap on the subject row, status text, type/user row, or any card padding → opens action menu (existing rework foundation behavior preserved).
 - Long-press on the body → clipboard write + snackbar.

Alternative considered: apply `combinedClickable` to the entire Card (replacing the current `clickable(onClick = onClick)`), so long-press anywhere on the card copies the body. Decided against — it would be semantically confusing to long-press the subject row and have the BODY copied. The body-specific affordance matches legacy ergonomics and is intuitive (the body is the longest text in the row; "long-press text to copy it" is the universal mobile interaction).

### §105.6 LocalClipboardManager deprecation choice

The slice uses `androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalClipboardManager` (the API the legacy uses). It carries a deprecation warning suggesting `LocalClipboard` (the new suspend-based API), but the deprecation is uniform across the codebase — both legacy (`composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:738`, `composeApp/.../presentation/features/details/ui/components/HeaderSection.kt:81`, `composeApp/.../presentation/features/library_details/ui/components/InfoCompose.kt:65`) and any other rework feature that touches the clipboard would need to migrate together. Phase 10's i18n + API migration sweep can swap to `LocalClipboard` in one pass across all five sites.

`AnnotatedString(complaint.body)` is the standard `LocalClipboardManager.setText` payload type. Matches legacy verbatim.

### §105.7 Files added / modified

NEW (commit 1, `f65363a`):
 - `PLAN_complaint_admin_copy.md`

MOD (commit 2, `11c4d48`):
 - `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintIntent.kt` — added `OnCopyBody` variant
 - `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintViewModel.kt` — added `OnCopyBody` arm + `handleCopyBody()` private method
 - `ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` — imports + `onLongClickBody` param + `combinedClickable` on body Text + `AdminComplaintList` wiring

MOD (this commit):
 - `ARCHITECTURE.md` — §105 (this section)
 - `SOLID_AUDIT.md` — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.copy entry

6 file touches across 3 commits (plan / source bundle / close-out). Plan + 3 source + 2 close-out = well under any cap; the source bundle commit is 3 files (well under 5).

### §105.8 Build gates

After the source-bundle commit:
 - `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — GREEN
 - `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — GREEN
 - `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — GREEN

Only pre-existing deprecation warnings (the `LocalClipboardManager` warning is uniform across the codebase per §105.6; the rest are unrelated to this slice). No new warnings from the new code beyond the anticipated `LocalClipboardManager` deprecation. iOS framework linking + on-device smoke tests deferred to user's Mac.

 - **`CopyToClipboard(text)` effect variant** — only needed if a future slice copies from outside the row composable (e.g., dialog "Copy" button). Slots in via OCP §6.

## §106 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.stats — statistics aggregation card

### §106.1 Strategy

Lifts the `§102.9` stats deferral and the `§105` next-candidate
recommendation. The legacy admin's `AdminStatisticsCard`
(`composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:619-720`)
renders a Card with the full inventory's total + per-status breakdown
above the filter chips; the rework slice ports the parity-equivalent
surface using a new state field + private composable + VM helper.

**Pure :presentation + :ui slice** — ZERO new `:domain` use cases, ZERO
new `:data` impls, ZERO new Koin bindings, ZERO new nav touch points,
ZERO new MVI intents, ZERO new MVI effects. The aggregation is a pure
data-driven projection over the already-loaded `state.all` list, NOT a
sibling repository fetch — the legacy admin makes the same call (the
legacy reads `complaints` as a plain `List<Complaint>` and runs its
aggregations inline in the composable).

**Why a new use case wasn't added**: the legacy facade exposes ALL
complaints (`ObserveAllComplaintsUseCase`) and the dashboard already
holds the full list in `state.all`. Adding a sibling
`ObserveComplaintStatisticsUseCase` (anticipated in `§105`'s next
candidate) would require a second source of truth + cross-stream
consistency — for the same data the existing stream already provides
in full. Client-side aggregation in the VM is the correct lift here.

### §106.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

`:domain` — untouched.

`:data` — untouched.

`:presentation` — `AdminComplaintState.kt` modified:
 - New top-level data class `AdminComplaintStatistics(total: Int,
   byStatus: Map<ComplaintStatus, Int>)` with default empty instance.
 - New field `AdminComplaintState.statistics:
   AdminComplaintStatistics = AdminComplaintStatistics()` —
   defaults to empty, populated on every successful `loadList`, reset
   to empty on failure.

`:presentation` — `AdminComplaintViewModel.kt` modified:
 - New private helper `computeStatistics(list: List<ComplaintSummary>):
   AdminComplaintStatistics` → returns `AdminComplaintStatistics(total
   = list.size, byStatus = list.groupBy { it.status }
   .mapValues { it.value.size })`.
 - `loadList` success branch adds `statistics = computeStatistics
   (list)` to the `it.copy(...)` lambda alongside `all` and `filtered`.
 - `loadList` failure branch adds `statistics =
   AdminComplaintStatistics()` (resets to default — keeps state
   coherent when the list is wiped).

`:ui` — `AdminComplaintScreen.kt` modified:
 - New private `@Composable fun StatisticsCard(statistics:
   AdminComplaintStatistics)` — Card with title "Statistics", "Total
   complaints: N" row, "By status" header, per-status rows for
   non-zero buckets only (filtered via
   `byStatus.entries.filter { it.value > 0 }`).
 - `AdminComplaintList` inserts a new `item(key = "__stats__") {
   StatisticsCard(statistics = state.statistics) }` as the FIRST item
   in the LazyColumn, above `__search_filter__`.
 - KDoc updated: the prior "Statistics card intentionally omitted"
   bullet swapped for an "extension" bullet documenting the new
   posture.

`:composeApp` — untouched.

### §106.3 MVI shape rationale

**No new intent, no new effect** — the stats slice is purely
**data-driven**: stats flow from the `loadList` success branch, and
the user CANNOT change them (filter chips don't affect stats since
stats reflect `all`, not `filtered`). The user-side MVI contract is
that intents are user-driven mutation triggers; stats are pure
derivations from server data, not user mutations. Adding a hypothetical
`OnStatsToggle` (e.g., a show/hide-stats toggle) would warrant a new
intent — but the foundation slice doesn't ship that toggle.

The sealed `AdminComplaintIntent` and `AdminComplaintEffect`
interfaces stay closed; no exhaustive-`when` arms added or modified.

### §106.4 Strangler-fig boundary

ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches. The new aggregation runs in
`:presentation` over `state.all` (which itself comes from
`ObserveAllComplaintsUseCase` and ultimately
`AdminComplaintRepositoryImpl` — the existing strangler-fig path,
unchanged). Same posture as `§104` (sort) — both slices are pure
client-side derivations.

### §106.5 Reflects `all`, not `filtered`

Per the legacy admin's pattern (`AdminStatisticsCard(complaints =
allComplaints)`), the rework card surfaces the FULL inventory while
the filtered list is below. The user can still infer "what would my
filters show" via the results-count text in the search/filter
section.

Two alternatives were rejected:
 1. **"Reflects `filtered`"** — would mean the card reads "X of Y"
    or "X total" where X tracks the filtered subset. Diverges from
    legacy posture and confuses the surface (the chip row already
    shows filter state — a stats card mirroring it would be
    redundant).
 2. **Two cards (one per dimension)** — overkill for the foundation
    slice; legacy ships one card.

### §106.6 `byStatus` aggregation: stdlib idiom

`list.groupBy { it.status }.mapValues { it.value.size }` is the
standard Kotlin idiom for the
`Map<EnumKey, Count>` lift. The `groupBy` + `mapValues` pair has
O(n) time, single-pass, and naturally yields a map containing only
the statuses present in the data (zero-count statuses are absent,
NOT zero-valued). The `:ui` composable filters
`byStatus.entries.filter { it.value > 0 }` as a defensive guard
(if a future code path adds a zero-valued bucket, the UI would
still hide it).

### §106.7 Default empty instance posture

`AdminComplaintStatistics()` (the no-arg constructor) yields
`total = 0, byStatus = emptyMap()`. This is the initial state during
load + the failure-state reset value. The `:ui` composable never
renders the stats card during loading / error / empty-list states
(the outer `Box` shows a spinner / inline error / placeholder
instead — the LazyColumn doesn't render at all in those branches),
so the user never sees `total == 0` in practice.

The default-empty posture is critical for the immutable
`data class` contract: every `state.copy(...)` call already has a
known-good `statistics` field to fall back to.

### §106.8 Deferred work

 - **`byAppVersion`** — legacy renders a third breakdown by
   `metadata.appVersion`. Requires a `metadata: Map<String, Any>?`
   field on `:domain` `ComplaintSummary` that contract §6
   deliberately bans (`Any` is forbidden). Will ship in
   `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.versionfilter` together with the
   third filter axis and the two deferred `APP_VERSION` sort modes
   (same blocker, same lift — one slice, one domain widen).

 - **`byType` breakdown** — legacy doesn't render one either.
   The existing filter chip row already surfaces "what types
   exist". Adding a breakdown would be redundant.

 - **Show/hide toggle** — legacy ships the stats card
   unconditionally. The rework could add an `OnToggleStats`
   intent + a `showStats: Boolean` state field in a future
   additive slice if user feedback requests collapsibility; this
   foundation slice doesn't.

 - **Charts / visualizations** — legacy is pure number display;
   rework matches. Visualization (donut chart, bar chart, etc.)
   would be a `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.statschart` extension if
   needed.

### §106.9 Files

NEW: none.

MODIFIED:
 - `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintState.kt` — new
   `statistics` field on `AdminComplaintState` + new top-level
   `AdminComplaintStatistics` data class.
 - `presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintViewModel.kt` —
   new private `computeStatistics` helper + threading through
   `loadList`'s success / failure branches.
 - `ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` — new private

 - `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — GREEN (1m 35s; only

 - `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — GREEN (1m 35s; same).
 - `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — GREEN (1m 40s;

## §107 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.versionfilter — third filter axis + 2 deferred sort modes + `byAppVersion` stats

### §107.1 Strategy

Lifts THREE deferrals in a single slice:
 - `§104.next-candidate`'s two `APP_VERSION` / `APP_VERSION_DESC`
   sort modes (deferred because `ComplaintSummary` had no field to
   sort by).
 - `§106.8`'s `byAppVersion` stats breakdown (deferred for the same
   field-absent reason).
 - The third filter axis (status + type were already in place;
   app version is the natural next dimension and was the larger
   item in the §106.12 next-candidate ranking).

All three lifts hinge on a single `:domain` widen: surface the
legacy `Complaint.metadata: Map<String, Any>?` map's
`"appVersion"` key as a new `ComplaintSummary.appVersion: String?`
field. Once that field exists, filter / sort / stats are pure
client-side derivations over `state.all`.

**Carve-out posture** (NOT a full `metadata` lift): the rework
boundary deliberately keeps `Map<String, Any>` out of `:domain`
(contract §6 — `Any` is banned). Instead, each metadata key the
admin dashboard needs is extracted one-at-a-time as its own
single-typed nullable field on `ComplaintSummary`. `appVersion` is
the first such carve-out; future slices needing `platform` or
`build` would add sibling `platform: String?` / `build: String?`
fields with the same posture.

### §107.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

`:domain` — `ComplaintSummary.kt` modified:
 - New field `val appVersion: String? = null` at end of the data
   class (default-nullable for source compat with any future
   fixture not setting it explicitly).
 - KDoc bullet documenting the carve-out rationale + the
   contract §6 `Any` exclusion + future-extension posture.

`:data` — TWO mapper updates (one per existing complaint
repository impl):

   carve-out only".
 - `AdminComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt`: identical mapper line

 - **Why both impls** (mapper duplication): both files map the

   display `appVersion`) avoids a "the two mappers are subtly

`:presentation` — `AdminComplaintState.kt` modified:

`:presentation` — `AdminComplaintIntent.kt` modified:

   state.all.mapNotNull { it.appVersion }.distinct().sorted() }`
   — hoisted above the LazyColumn because `LazyListScope` is NOT

### §107.3 MVI shape rationale

**One new intent, no new effect, no new state-mode enum** —
the slice is a pure addition to the existing three-axis filter
surface that already had status + type. The third axis follows
the same pattern verbatim — single-select with toggle-off, chip
row, exclusion of null when filter is non-null.

Sealed `AdminComplaintIntent` widens from 14 → 15 variants.
Sealed `AdminComplaintEffect` stays at 2 variants. The
exhaustive `when (intent)` in `AdminComplaintViewModel` is the
compile-time enforcement that the new variant is handled — same
guarantee as every prior admin sub-slice.

### §107.4 Strangler-fig boundary

ZERO new `:data` → `:shared` reaches. The two mapper updates
extract a single key from the legacy `metadata: Map<String,
Any>?` that was ALREADY in scope (the mappers already touched
the legacy `Complaint`). The `Any` projection (`toString()`)
happens entirely within `:data`; the `:domain` boundary sees
`String?`, never `Any`.

The strangler-fig posture stays exactly where §106 left it —
two `:data` impls reach into `:shared` for the legacy
`Complaint` shape; the carve-out is a refinement of the
existing reach, not a new one.

### §107.5 Dynamic chip-row derivation

Chips for the new "App version" row come from
`state.all.mapNotNull { it.appVersion }.distinct().sorted()` —
computed at the `:ui` boundary inside a `remember(state.all)`
block hoisted above the `LazyColumn`. Three properties:
 1. **No dead ends**: the chip row only shows versions actually
    present in the dataset. The user can never select a version
    that has zero matches (which would just show "No
    complaints match" emptiness).
 2. **Memoization**: `remember(state.all)` recomputes only when
    the underlying list reference changes — not on every
    recomposition. The `:presentation` layer doesn't need a
    sibling `availableAppVersions` state field.
 3. **Conditional rendering**: the chip row is gated on
    `availableAppVersions.isNotEmpty()` — a dataset with zero
    complaints carrying `appVersion` (e.g., all pre-carveout
    fixture data) hides the row entirely. No empty chip row.

The lexicographic sort (`.sorted()`) means `"1.10.0"` precedes
`"1.2.0"` — a known weakness of string-sorting version
identifiers. Accepted as legacy parity (the legacy admin had
no per-version filter, so there's no prior posture to break)
and as bounded harm (the admin user reads a list of versions
sorted by string; they can disambiguate visually).

### §107.6 Sort modes — lexicographic, not semver

The two new sort arms (`APP_VERSION` /
`APP_VERSION_DESC`) sort by raw string comparison —
`sortedBy { it.appVersion }` and
`sortedByDescending { it.appVersion }`. This means `"1.10.0"`
precedes `"1.2.0"` and `null` values bubble to the end (ascending)
or front (descending) per Kotlin's `nullsLast` /
`nullsFirst` defaults on `compareBy`.

Three semver-aware alternatives were rejected:
 1. **Custom `Comparator<String>` parsing `"1.2.3"` into
    `Triple<Int, Int, Int>`** — adds parse-failure handling
    (malformed versions need a fallback) and a new internal
    helper. Bigger surface than the lift justifies.
 2. **Kotlin `Version` typed value class** — would require a
    new `:domain` type with comparison logic. Bigger again.
 3. **A `kotlinx-serialization`-grade semver lib** — new dep
    for a sort affordance the legacy doesn't even have.

The lexicographic sort is acknowledged-imperfect but bounded:
the admin dashboard's version sort is a triage aid, not a
release-ordering source of truth. If users surface confusion,
a follow-up `Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.versionsort.semver`
slice can swap in a comparator without changing the
`AdminSortMode` enum or `applyFilterAndSort` signature.

### §107.7 `byAppVersion` stats

`computeStatistics` gains the line
`byAppVersion = list.mapNotNull { it.appVersion }.groupingBy
{ it }.eachCount()`. The `Grouping<String, String>` lift via
`groupingBy { it }.eachCount()` is a single-pass O(n) idiom that
yields a `Map<String, Int>` containing only non-null version
buckets (zero-count statuses absent, matching the
`byStatus` posture from §106.6).

The `:ui` `StatisticsCard` renders the per-version rows sorted
by key (`versionBuckets.sortedBy { it.key }`) — same
lexicographic ordering as the chip row, so the two surfaces
mirror each other visually.

### §107.8 Mapper duplication — `ComplaintMappers.kt` extraction deferred

Both `:data` impls (`ComplaintListRepositoryImpl` and
`AdminComplaintListRepositoryImpl`) now contain the same
`appVersion = metadata?.get("appVersion")?.toString()` mapper
line. Three options were considered:
 1. **Extract a private top-level `LegacyComplaint.toDomain():
    ComplaintSummary` extension in a new `:data`-internal
    `ComplaintMappers.kt`** — clean DRY, but adds a file solely
    to host a 12-line extension shared by 2 callers. Possibly
    over-engineered for the current surface.
 2. **Extract a `:data`-internal `private object
    ComplaintMappers`** — same trade-off, slightly different
    namespacing.
 3. **Accept the 1-line duplication** — keeps both files
    self-contained; reading either mapper requires no jump.

Option 3 chosen for this slice. Trigger for option 1: a THIRD
caller needing the same mapper, OR a future carve-out (e.g.,
`platform: String?`) making the duplication multi-line.

## §108 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.bulk — slice CLOSED as obsolete (no legacy UI parity to port)

### §108.1 Pre-implementation survey finding

When Task #265 opened with intent to port the legacy admin's
multi-select bulk-mutation surface, the pre-implementation
survey (per the standing posture of "always read the legacy
target file before writing the plan") revealed that
`composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` has
NO multi-select / bulk-action UI affordance:

 - Zero `selectionMode` / `selectedIds` / `multiSelect` /
   `SelectAll` / `BulkDelete` / `BulkUpdate` references in the
   1000+ line legacy screen file (verified via case-insensitive
   Grep).
 - Card interaction is purely single-item (per-card icon
   buttons → per-action dialogs → per-action use case calls).

`Grep` for `bulkUpdateStatus | bulkDeleteComplaints` across the
entire repo found exactly TWO files: (1) the legacy admin VM
itself (`shared/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintViewModel.kt`)
defining them, and (2) `SOLID_AUDIT.md` mentioning them in
deferral docs. ZERO callers anywhere — the bulk VM methods are
unwired dead code in the legacy.

### §108.2 Decision: close Task #265 with ZERO source changes

The rework's posture (established across every prior slice §62
onward) is "port what the legacy actually surfaces; do not add
features the legacy doesn't have". Implementing bulk multi-
select in the rework would be a feature ADD — not a port —
which violates the rework's strict "behaviour preservation,
not feature creep" posture documented at §95 and reiterated
across every subsequent slice's `Behaviour preservation`
section.

The rework's `:presentation` `AdminComplaintViewModel` ALREADY
exposes the per-item primitives (`ChangeComplaintStatusUseCase`,
`AdminDeleteComplaintUseCase`) that any future bulk feature
would loop over. If a future product requirement surfaces a
need for multi-select (e.g., admin user feedback after release),
the rework's MVI surface accepts a new
`OnToggleRowSelection(id)` / `OnSelectAll` / `OnSubmitBulkAction`
sealed-variant extension cleanly (OCP §6) — no
architectural change required.

### §108.3 Adjacent finding from survey: §107.5 documentation
correction

During the legacy screen read, two facts came to light that
contradict claims in `§107.5` (the prior versionfilter slice's
chip-row section):

 1. **Legacy DOES have a per-version filter chip row**
    (legacy `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:524-549`). `§107.5` had
    claimed "the legacy admin had no per-version filter, so
    there's no prior posture to break". This was a survey gap
    — the §107 plan was written before the deeper read of the
    legacy screen happened, and the per-version filter UX was
    classified as a rework-only addition when in fact it's a
    port. The §107 carve-out of `appVersion: String?` is still
    correct (only the rationale for the "no prior posture"
    framing was wrong).

 2. **Legacy chip-row sort is semver-aware**
    (legacy `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:148-172`) — `sortedWith
    { a, b -> ... }` splits each version on `.`, parses
    integer parts, compares pairwise (descending for the
    legacy's chip order). The rework's
    `state.all.mapNotNull { it.appVersion }.distinct()
    .sorted()` is plain lexicographic ascending. This is a
    REAL divergence from the legacy that §107.6 incorrectly
    framed as "accepted as legacy parity" — legacy is not
    lexicographic for the chip row, only for the sort dropdown.

The legacy's sort dropdown's `APP_VERSION` / `APP_VERSION_DESC`
modes DO sort lexicographically
(legacy `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:204-209`) — matching the
rework's `applyFilterAndSort` posture. So for the dropdown
sort, lexicographic IS legacy parity; only the chip row is
divergent.

## §109 — Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.chipsemver — corrective semver comparator lift for chip-row sort

### §109.1 Strategy

Tiny corrective slice that lifts the legacy's semver-aware
comparator into the rework's `AdminComplaintList` per-version
chip row. §108.3 documented the divergence (rework had plain
lexicographic `.sorted()`; legacy at `composeApp/.../admin/
complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:148-172` uses a
descending-by-int-parts comparator with descending-string
fallback). §107.5's framing of "no prior posture" was the
incorrect rationale for the lexicographic choice — this slice
corrects both the code AND the framing.

Scope is deliberately narrow: one `remember(state.all) { ... }`
block in `:ui` `AdminComplaintScreen.kt`. No `:domain`,
`:data`, or `:presentation` touch — the comparator is a pure
display-order concern, lives in the composable's
`remember` block, and consumes the existing
`state.all.mapNotNull { it.appVersion }.distinct()` projection
unchanged.

### §109.2 Comparator semantics

The lifted comparator (verbatim posture from legacy):

```kotlin
state.all.mapNotNull { it.appVersion }.distinct().sortedWith { a, b ->
    val aParts = a.split(".").mapNotNull { it.toIntOrNull() }
    val bParts = b.split(".").mapNotNull { it.toIntOrNull() }
    if (aParts.isNotEmpty() && bParts.isNotEmpty()) {
        var result = 0
        for (i in 0 until maxOf(aParts.size, bParts.size)) {
            val aPart = aParts.getOrNull(i) ?: 0
            val bPart = bParts.getOrNull(i) ?: 0
            val comparison = bPart.compareTo(aPart)
            if (comparison != 0) {
                result = comparison
                break
            }
        }
        result
    } else {
        b.compareTo(a)
    }
}
```

Ordering semantics:

 1. **Both sides parse to int parts** — pairwise compare with
    `b.compareTo(a)` (note: `b` first) → DESCENDING order
    (newest versions appear leftmost in the chip row).
 2. **Missing trailing parts** — `getOrNull(i) ?: 0` treats
    `"1.2"` as `"1.2.0"` so `"1.2"` and `"1.2.0"` collapse to
    equal positions (which the upstream `.distinct()` would
    have already deduplicated anyway).
 3. **Either side has zero parseable parts** — fall back to
    descending string compare (`b.compareTo(a)`). This
    handles edge cases like git-SHA suffixed versions, alpha
    tags, or anything non-numeric — sorts them by raw string
    descending, same as the legacy.

### §109.3 §107.5 documentation correction

§107.5 (versionfilter close-out) framed the lexicographic
`.sorted()` chip-row choice with rationale:

> "Legacy has no per-version chip row, so there's no prior
> posture to break; lexicographic is simpler."

Both halves of that sentence are wrong. The legacy DOES have
a per-version chip row (`AdminComplaintScreen.kt:524-549`)
and it IS semver-sorted (`AdminComplaintScreen.kt:148-172`).
§108.3 caught both errors during the bulk-survey read. §109
fixes the divergent code; this corrective lift restores
legacy parity for chip-row order.

The sort-dropdown's `APP_VERSION` / `APP_VERSION_DESC` modes
remain lexicographic because the legacy dropdown
(`AdminComplaintScreen.kt:204-209`) is ALSO lexicographic
for those modes — that's not a divergence, it's parity. Only
the chip row was divergent.

### §109.4 SOLID 10-point posture (per-file)

`ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt`:

 - SRP ✓ — `AdminComplaintList`'s `remember(state.all)` block
   has one job (compute the available-versions chip-row source
   list with legacy ordering); the comparator is inlined
   without leaking into other composables.
 - OCP ✓ — comparator is local to the `remember` block; no
   sealed-hierarchy or enum extension. Future sort-mode
   variants would slot into the existing `SortMode` enum
   without touching this code.
 - LSP n/a — no inheritance involved.
 - ISP n/a — no interfaces added.
 - DIP ✓ — composable depends on `state.all` (presentation
   state), not on any concrete repository.
 - DRY ⚠ acceptable — comparator is duplicated between legacy
   and rework chip rows. Lifting it to a `:domain` or shared
   `:ui` helper would cost more than it saves (one
   call site per layer, deferred until a third call site
   materialises).
 - YAGNI ✓ — no speculative semver crate dependency added; the
   inlined parse-and-compare is the minimum viable
   implementation.
 - Banned features ✓ — no `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, `Thread`.
   `getOrNull(i) ?: 0` is the null-safe accessor; `toIntOrNull`
   handles non-numeric parts; no unchecked casts.
 - Compose contract ✓ — `remember(state.all) { ... }` keyed on
   the source list keeps the memoization correct under state
   updates; `sortedWith` is referentially transparent (no side
   effects in the comparator).
 - MVI contract ✓ — chip-row content is a pure projection of
   `state.all`; no intent / effect required for sort-order
   changes (sort is fixed by the comparator).

### §109.5 Strangler-fig integrity

Zero `:data` → `:shared` reaches. The comparator is pure
Kotlin stdlib + a `String` split — no legacy module touched.
The rework's `:presentation` `AdminComplaintViewModel`
already projects `appVersion` into `state.all` from the §107
carve-out; this slice consumes that projection without
adding any new strangler boundary.

### §109.6 Behaviour preservation

The rework's chip-row order matches the legacy's chip-row
order for ALL inputs:

 - All-numeric versions (e.g., `["1.0.0", "1.0.1", "2.0.0"]`)
   → both render `["2.0.0", "1.0.1", "1.0.0"]` (descending
   by int parts).
 - Mixed-length numeric (e.g., `["1.2", "1.2.0", "1.2.1"]`)
   → after `.distinct()` collapses `"1.2"` / `"1.2.0"` to
   one entry (string-distinct, not version-distinct), the
   resulting two-entry list is ordered descending by parts.
 - Mixed numeric + non-numeric (e.g., `["1.0.0", "alpha"]`)
   → falls into the else-branch (one side has zero parseable
   parts), descending string compare → `["alpha", "1.0.0"]`
   in both legacy and rework.
 - Empty input → empty result; comparator never called.

The legacy route's behaviour is unchanged (no touch).

## §110 — Phase 7.x.complaint.displaynames — corrective UX lift restoring legacy displayName() parity

### §110.1 Strategy

The §101-§109 admin-complaint slices and the §99
user-complaint foundation/actions slices all consumed the
rework `:domain` `ComplaintStatus` / `ComplaintType`
enums directly via `enum.name` — yielding raw
identifier strings ("IN_PROGRESS", "NOT_PLANNED",
"TECHNICAL", "SITES_ADD") in user-visible chip labels,
status badges, statistics rows, and subject fallbacks.

This is a UX divergence from the legacy surfaces, which
already define Composable extension functions
`ComplaintStatus.displayName()` and
`ComplaintType.displayName()` in
`composeApp/.../presentation/features/complaint/model/`
that map every enum variant to a properly cased English
phrase ("In Progress", "Not Planned", "Error In The App",
"Add Manga Site"). Two of those legacy mappings already
use `stringResource(Res.string.status_closed)` /

### §110.5 Per-file SOLID 10-point posture

Both new helpers and all 4 modified files pass the
SOLID Guardian checklist:

- **SRP** — each helper file owns one ADT-to-string
  mapping. Consumers gained no responsibility from the
  edit (single character changes per site:
  `.name` → `.displayName()`).
- **OCP** — exhaustive `when` over a closed enum. Adding
  a new variant to the `:domain` enum will produce a
  compile error at the `when`, forcing an explicit
  mapping decision rather than a silent fallback.
- **LSP** — N/A (no inheritance).
- **ISP** — extension functions add zero surface to the
  enums themselves; consumers depend only on the
  function they call.
- **DIP** — `:ui` extensions over `:domain` enums; the
  arrow points from `:ui` (concrete view layer) to
  `:domain` (abstraction) per the standing module DAG.
- **DRY** — collapses 9 raw-`.name` sites (4 user + 6
  admin = 10 if dialog is counted; survey originally
  identified 9, the discrepancy is the duplicate
  status-name pattern in the admin dialog) to a single
  source of truth per enum.
- **KISS** — `when` blocks, no helper state, no
  caching, no localization plumbing.
- **YAGNI** — does not introduce a third helper
  (`displayDescription()` etc.) or per-locale
  parameterisation. Phase-10 lift will add
  `stringResource` calls, not architecture.
- **Boy Scout** — leaves the consumers cleaner than it
  found them (no raw enum identifiers leaking to
  end-users).
- **No banned features** — pure Kotlin `@Composable`
  functions; no `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`.

ZERO new reaches into legacy `:shared`. The two new

## §111 — Phase 7.x.complaint.iconparity — restore screen-level icon affordances

### §111.1 — Strategy

The Rule-3 survey identified by §110.10 carved out the **user-side
complaint screen's missing icon affordances** as the natural next slice.
The legacy `composeApp/.../features/complaint/ui/screens/ComplaintScreen.kt`
exposes four icon affordances that the foundation slice
(Phase 7.x.complaint.foundation, §76) deliberately omitted under a
documented "icon-free posture" convention:

1. **Top-bar back-nav** — legacy `IconButton + Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled
   .ArrowBack` → foundation slice's labelled `TextButton "Back"` in the
   `actions` slot.
2. **Search-field leading icon** — legacy `OutlinedTextField(...
   leadingIcon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Search, ...) } ...)` → foundation
   slice omitted entirely.
3. **Search-field trailing clear icon** — legacy `OutlinedTextField(...
   trailingIcon = { IconButton + Icons.Default.Clear } ...)` → foundation
   slice's labelled `TextButton "Clear"` inside an unframed slot.
4. **No-matches placeholder** — legacy `Column + Icon(Icons.Default
   .SearchOff, ...) + Text("No matches")` → foundation slice's bare
   `Text("No matches")` with no leading glyph.

The slice restores all four. Block-and-ask was triggered when the initial
attempt to import from `androidx.compose.material.icons.*` produced 9
"Unresolved reference 'icons'" errors during the Android build gate — the
`:ui` module deliberately omits `compose.materialIconsExtended` per a
project-wide ~6 MB save policy documented in `HistoryScreen.kt` and
reaffirmed across the Library / Statistics / Details / Updates / Sources
screens. User chose option A3: **inline custom `ImageVector` paths** —
threading the policy through by transcribing the four canonical Material
Design 24x24 SVG path strings into the `ImageVector.Builder + path { ... }`
DSL in a new file local to the complaint package.

### §111.2 — Files added (1 new) and modified (2)

**New**:

- `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/ComplaintIcons.kt`
  — four `internal val ... : ImageVector by lazy { ... }` definitions:
  - `ComplaintArrowBack` — Material Design Filled ArrowBack
    (path: `M20 11H7.83l5.59-5.59L12 4l-8 8 8 8 1.41-1.41L7.83 13H20v-2z`)
  - `ComplaintSearch` — Material Design Filled Search (compound path with
    magnifier silhouette + lens cutout)
  - `ComplaintClear` — Material Design Filled Clear (the X glyph)
  - `ComplaintSearchOff` — Material Design Filled SearchOff (compound
    path with magnifier + cross-out segments)

  All four use `fill = SolidColor(Color.Black)` because `Icon`'s default
  `tintBlendMode = SrcIn` reads the fill as a mask — the rendered colour
  is the `tint` argument or `LocalContentColor.current`. No tint
  adjustment needed at call sites.

  Each definition is `by lazy {}` to defer the `ImageVector.Builder` work
  until the first composition reads it, matching the lazy-init pattern
  used by Compose's own `Icons.*` properties.

**Modified**:

- `ui/.../ui/complaint/ComplaintScreen.kt` — 4 sites:
  - Top-bar `actions = { TextButton ... }` → `navigationIcon = {
    IconButton(onClick = onBack) { Icon(ComplaintArrowBack,
    contentDescription = "Back") } }`. Promotes the back-nav into the
    canonical `navigationIcon` slot (more conventional than `actions`).
  - `OutlinedTextField` gains a `leadingIcon = { Icon(ComplaintSearch,
    contentDescription = null) }` lambda — null content-description
    because the placeholder text "Search feedback…" already conveys the
    affordance to screen readers.
  - `OutlinedTextField`'s `trailingIcon` (conditional on
    `searchQuery.isNotEmpty()`) replaces `TextButton "Clear"` with
    `IconButton { Icon(ComplaintClear, contentDescription = "Clear") }`.
    The conditional structure is preserved.
  - The `__no_matches__` LazyColumn item replaces the bare `Text` with a
    `Column { Icon(ComplaintSearchOff, ...); Text("No matches") }`,
    horizontally centred, `Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.sm)` between
    glyph and text. Icon tinted to `onSurfaceVariant` to match the
    placeholder body-text colour.
  - KDoc updated: the "Icons are intentionally omitted" bullet is
    replaced with an "Icon affordances" bullet documenting the four
    restored sites + cross-reference to `ComplaintIcons`.

- `ui/.../ui/complaint/ComplaintActionDialog.kt` — KDoc-only edit:
  - The "Icon-free posture" section is reframed to clarify the dialog
    **still preserves** the icon-free posture even after the screen-level
    lift. The rationale split: screen-level icons restored (back-nav is
    nav-pop, search/clear/no-matches all carry textual ambiguity worth
    glyph reinforcement); dialog sub-panels' affordances (Reply / Edit /
    Delete buttons + Info/Warning cards) remain label-only because the
    button text + card colour+heading already carry the affordance and
    severity respectively. No code change in the dialog — its rendering
    is unchanged.

Total: **1 new file + 2 modified = 3 files**, well under the 5-file cap.

### §111.3 — Why inline `ImageVector` paths, not add the dep

The `:ui` module's build.gradle.kts declares NO icons dependency. The
choice tree available when the build gate failed:

- **A1** — Add `implementation(compose.materialIconsCore)` to `:ui`. The
  Core dep is ~few-hundred-KB and includes the 4 needed glyphs. But it
  breaks the project-wide convention documented in `HistoryScreen.kt` /
  `LibraryScreen.kt` / `StatisticsScreen.kt` / `DetailsScreen.kt` /
  `UpdatesScreen.kt` / `SourcesScreen.kt` that the rework `:ui` deliberately
  ships without icons. A unilateral dep change would either need to apply
  to all rework screens (out-of-scope retroactive lift) or carve out a
  per-screen exception (sets a bad precedent).
- **A2** — Add `compose.materialIconsExtended` (~6 MB). Explicitly
  rejected by the project policy.
- **A3** — Inline custom `ImageVector` paths via the
  `ImageVector.Builder + path { ... }` DSL. ~50 lines of vector-path
  Kotlin. Tedious but zero policy override. User chose this.
- **A4** — Revert the icon-parity scope entirely (preserve the foundation
  slice's "Icon-free posture" convention). Rejected because the survey
  established the affordances are user-visible — Search/Clear/SearchOff
  carry textual ambiguity that the labels alone don't resolve. Back
  could go either way; the inline-vector approach restores all four
  uniformly.

### §111.4 — SVG-path-to-DSL transcription

Each canonical Material Design 24x24 SVG path string was decoded into
the Compose `Path` DSL by mapping SVG path commands to method calls:

| SVG command | Compose DSL method |
|---|---|
| `M x y` (move absolute) | `moveTo(x, y)` |
| `m dx dy` (move relative) | `moveToRelative(dx, dy)` |
| `L x y` (line absolute) | `lineTo(x, y)` |
| `l dx dy` (line relative) | `lineToRelative(dx, dy)` |
| `H x` (horizontal absolute) | `horizontalLineTo(x)` |
| `h dx` (horizontal relative) | `horizontalLineToRelative(dx)` |
| `V y` (vertical absolute) | `verticalLineTo(y)` |
| `v dy` (vertical relative) | `verticalLineToRelative(dy)` |
| `C x1 y1 x2 y2 x y` (cubic absolute) | `curveTo(x1, y1, x2, y2, x, y)` |
| `c dx1 dy1 dx2 dy2 dx dy` (cubic relative) | `curveToRelative(...)` |
| `S x2 y2 x y` (reflective cubic abs.) | `reflectiveCurveTo(x2, y2, x, y)` |
| `s dx2 dy2 dx dy` (reflective cubic rel.) | `reflectiveCurveToRelative(...)` |
| `Z` / `z` (close path) | `close()` |

The `SearchOff` glyph required a compound multi-subpath structure
(magnifier silhouette + lens cutout + small cross-out segments)
implemented via multiple `moveTo` calls within a single `path { }` block
— `PathFillType.NonZero` resolves the even-odd overlap that defines the
lens cutout.

### §111.5 — Cross-package visibility

The new `ComplaintIcons.kt` lives at package `me.manga.kira.ui
.complaint`. The vector vals are declared `internal val ... by lazy { ...
}` so they're module-internal (callable from `:ui` consumers but invisible
to other modules). `ComplaintScreen.kt` lives in the SAME package so it
sees the symbols without imports.

The admin-side counterpart (`admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt`) is in the
`me.manga.kira.ui.complaint.admin` sub-package, which can also import
them as needed via `import me.manga.kira.ui.complaint.Complaint*`. This
slice does NOT propagate icons to the admin side — the admin surface
already has its own clipboard/sort/bulk-action UI patterns that don't
mirror the user-side's "search + filter chips" affordance. If the admin
surface wants its own icon lift, that's a separate Phase
7.x.complaint.admin.iconparity slice.

### §111.6 — Behaviour preservation

The user-visible behaviour change is:

- **Restored** — back-nav icon, search leading icon, search-clear icon,
  no-matches placeholder icon. These are the legacy's affordances.
- **Unchanged** — all interaction semantics (back-nav still calls
  `onBack`, clear still dispatches `OnClearSearch`, search still drives
  `OnSearchChange`). No intent/effect changes.
- **Unchanged** — dialog sub-panel rendering (no icons added or
  removed in the dialog).

No legacy or rework MVI contract changes. No `:domain` / `:data` /
`:presentation` touch — pure `:ui` lift.

### §111.7 — Build gates

All three gates passed cleanly on the `architecture-rework` branch
working tree at HEAD `618e3fb`:

- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
  in 15s (warnings only, all pre-existing and unrelated).
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in
  20s (warnings only, all pre-existing and unrelated).
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — BUILD
  SUCCESSFUL in 15s (warnings only, all pre-existing and unrelated).

Desktop is not in the standard build gate set for `:ui` slices; the
slice introduces no new platform actuals. Visual on-device parity check
(verify the four glyphs render at the right positions / sizes / tints)
is **Windows-impossible** — deferred to user's Mac for the iOS smoke
test alongside the displaynames smoke check from §110.

### §111.8 — Layer boundaries & SOLID

- **`:ui` ↑ `:presentation`** — unchanged, MVI surface is read-only by
  the composable; intents `OnClearSearch`/`OnSearchChange` are
  pre-existing.
- **`:ui` ↑ `:domain`** — unchanged, the screen reads
  `ComplaintStatus.entries` + `ComplaintSummary` for the row data.
- **`:ui` standalone** — `ComplaintIcons.kt` depends only on
  `androidx.compose.ui.graphics.*` and `androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp`.
  No cross-module reach.

SOLID per file in §SOLID_AUDIT Phase 7.x.complaint.iconparity entry.

### §111.9 — Deferrals

- **Admin-side icon parity** — not in this slice. If the admin surface

- **Phase 10 i18n** — `contentDescription = "Back"` / `"Clear"` are

## §112 — Phase 7.x.complaint.pinnedfaq — admin-pinned FAQ entries

### §112.1 — Strategy

Restores the two hardcoded admin-authored FAQ entries the foundation
slice (Phase 7.x.complaint.foundation, §76) explicitly deferred via the
"Pinned-top FAQ rows from legacy `getCustomTopComplaints()` are
intentionally NOT ported" bullet. These two static entries serve as
**always-visible** community guideline reminders the legacy displays
above every user's own submissions in the Feedback Manager:

1. **"Content removed - 18+ / Hentai"** — community guideline for
   removed adult-content references.
2. **"Pinned: New manga site requirements"** — admin-policy explainer
   for the 200-title / no-bot threshold on new sources.

Architectural choice: the prepend lives at the **`:data` layer**, not
the `:ui` layer, so pinned entries flow through `:domain` →
`:presentation` → `:ui` via the normal MVI pipeline. The screen
composable doesn't need to know they exist — they appear in
`state.all` just like DB-loaded records and participate in the same
search / status-filter logic without special-casing.

This is a deliberate divergence from the legacy's structural posture
(legacy puts the prepend in the screen composable's body), motivated
by the rework's MVI invariants: `:ui` is a pure projection of state;
state composition belongs upstream. Putting the prepend in `:data`
keeps `:ui` stateless and the VM's filter/search logic ignorant of the
synthetic / DB-loaded distinction.

### §112.2 — Files added (1 new) and modified (1)

**New**:

- `data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/PinnedComplaints.kt`
  — `internal val PINNED_COMPLAINTS: List<ComplaintSummary>` carrying
  the two static entries. Each entry uses:
  - `id = "admin"` — matches legacy `stringResource(Res.string.admin)`
    which resolves to literal "admin" per `composeApp/.../composeResources/values/strings.xml:381`.
  - `userId = "0"` — legacy magic-string for the admin author.
  - `type = ComplaintType.CUSTOM` — same as legacy; CUSTOM is the
    catch-all bucket for admin-authored content.
  - `status = ComplaintStatus.PINNED` — drives the dialog's
    status-gated affordances (Edit/Delete hidden; Reply available).
  - `createdAt = null` — replaces legacy `Clock.System.now()` (which
    re-computed on every recomposition; ts drifted forever forward).
    `null` is the honest value for pre-write / synthetic records — the
    [ComplaintSummary.createdAt] field is `Instant?` exactly for this
    case.
  - `appVersion = null` — pinned entries are not tied to a client
    submission.
  - `subject` + `body` — inline English literals mirroring the legacy
    `strings.xml` English fallback values verbatim. Phase 10 i18n lift
    will re-point both sides to shared resource keys.

**Modified**:

- `data/.../ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt` — one-line behavioural
  change (`PINNED_COMPLAINTS + legacy(userId).map { it.toSummary() }`
  inside `loadUserComplaints()`) + KDoc append documenting the
  prepend semantics and cross-reference to `PINNED_COMPLAINTS`.

Total: **1 new + 1 modified = 2 source files**, plus close-out docs
(ARCHITECTURE §112 + SOLID_AUDIT entry) for 4 files total. Under the
5-file cap with room to spare.

### §112.3 — Behaviour parity vs legacy

Legacy `composeApp/.../complaint/ui/screens/ComplaintScreen.kt:92-93`:

```kotlin
val pinnedTop = getCustomTopComplaints()
val allComplaints = pinnedTop + (complaintsState as? State.Success)?.data.orEmpty()
```

Rework `data/.../ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt`:

```kotlin
override suspend fun loadUserComplaints(): Result<List<ComplaintSummary>> = runCatching {
    val userId = userIdProvider.getUserId()
    PINNED_COMPLAINTS + legacy(userId).map { it.toSummary() }
}
```

Behavioural mapping:

- **Success branch** (legacy and rework): `state.all` (rework) /
  `allComplaints` (legacy) carries `pinned + db` in that order.
  Pinned entries appear at the top of the LazyColumn.
- **Failure branch** (legacy: `State.Error`, rework: `Result.failure`):
  the screen renders the error state and returns before rendering the
  list. Pinned entries are NOT shown — pure parity.
- **Loading branch** (legacy: `State.Loading`, rework: `state.isLoading
  = true`): centred spinner, no list. Pinned entries NOT shown —
  parity.
- **Empty DB** (success + 0 DB records): `state.all = PINNED_COMPLAINTS`
  (2 entries). The "No feedback submitted yet" placeholder never
  triggers because `state.all.isEmpty()` is always false — same
  unreachable-empty-state posture as legacy (legacy's `EmptyState` is
  also unreachable for the same reason).
- **Search**: pinned entries participate in subject/body text-match
  filtering exactly like real records. Typing "site" matches the
  second pinned entry's subject and body. Same as legacy.
- **Status filter**: pinned entries match the PINNED status filter and
  hide under any other filter (OPEN/CLOSED/etc.). Same as legacy.
- **Row click + Reply**: pinned entries open the action dialog at
  MENU mode. Reply is shown (PINNED parents accept user replies);
  Edit and Delete are hidden by the dialog's pre-existing
  status-gated branch.

### §112.4 — Why `:data`, not `:ui` or `:presentation`

Three placement options were considered:

- **`:ui`** — match legacy structurally; the screen prepends pinned
  entries when rendering. Rejected: violates "state.all is the
  truth" MVI invariant; `:ui` must be a pure projection of
  `:presentation` state.
- **`:presentation`** — VM injects pinned entries into `state.all`
  during the load handler. Workable but requires the pinned list to be
  importable from `:presentation`, which can only import `:domain`
  (DIP) — not `:data`. Would force the list into `:domain`, which is
  awkward (the list is presentation content, not a domain concept).
- **`:data`** (chosen) — repository impl prepends inside
  `loadUserComplaints()`. Pinned entries flow through `:domain` →
  `:presentation` → `:ui` via the normal MVI pipeline. VM's filter and
  search logic operate over `state.all` uniformly. No special-casing
  in any layer.

The `:data`-layer placement also makes it natural for a future slice
to swap the static `PINNED_COMPLAINTS` for a remote-config or
Firestore-backed list — the call-site signature stays
`List<ComplaintSummary>`, the consumer doesn't change.

### §112.5 — Admin surface non-propagation

Pinned entries are scoped to the **user-side** Feedback Manager only.
The admin surface (`AdminComplaintListRepositoryImpl` →
`AdminComplaintListRepository`) is unchanged — admins see actual
user-submitted complaints in their dashboard, not the synthetic pinned
entries. The legacy admin surface also does NOT prepend these (legacy
admin code reads from the same Firestore collection without the
synthetic pinned items).

If a future admin slice needs to surface the pinned list (e.g., for
an "edit pinned FAQs" admin tool), the new file is the natural import
point.

### §112.6 — i18n deferral

The pinned entries carry inline English literals matching legacy
`strings.xml` English fallback values verbatim. Phase 10's i18n lift
will re-point both legacy `stringResource(Res.string.content_removed_
18_hentai)` calls and the rework's inline literals to shared resource
keys. The lift is single-pass (touches both sides) and out-of-scope
for this slice.

The strings.xml keys the legacy `getCustomTopComplaints` uses (which
will become the Phase 10 lookup keys):

- `Res.string.content_removed_18_hentai` →
  `"Content removed - 18+ / Hentai"`
- `Res.string.references_to_adult_18_content_aren_t_allowed_here_*` →
  full guideline body
- `Res.string.pinned_new_manga_site_requirements` →
  `"Pinned: New manga site requirements"`
- `Res.string.any_new_manga_site_must_offer_at_least_200_titles_*` →
  full policy body

Phase 10 will introduce a Compose-Resources facade in `:data` (or move
the pinned data to a `:presentation`-resolved load) so the resource
lookups happen at the right layer.
