## §113 — Phase 7.x.settings.help — inert Help placeholder row

### §113.1 — Strategy

Restores the inert Help row that the legacy
`composeApp/.../features/settings/ui/screens/SettingsScreen.kt:350-353`
renders at the bottom of the Settings hub. The legacy row is a true
visual placeholder — `SettingsNavigationItem(title =
stringResource(Res.string.help), icon = Icons.AutoMirrored.Outlined.Help)`
with NO trailing `onClick` lambda. Legacy `SettingsNavigationItem.kt:44`
declares `onClick: (() -> Unit)? = null` and conditionally applies the
clickable modifier at `:50-52` — null onClick means no ripple, no tap
response.

The rework foundation slice (§64, Phase 7.x.settings.foundation)
deferred this row; the `:ui/.../settings/SettingsScreen.kt` KDoc at L85
listed Help among the deferred items. This slice closes that gap with a
single-file `:ui` lift.

### §113.2 — Files (0 new + 1 modified = 1 total)

1. `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`
   (MODIFIED):
   - **`NavRow` signature**: `onClick: () -> Unit` →
     `onClick: (() -> Unit)?` (parameter nullable, no default — explicit
     at every call site so the inert intent is visible in callers).
   - **`NavRow` body**: `clickable(onClick = onClick)` →
     `then(if (onClick != null) Modifier.clickable(onClick = onClick)
     else Modifier)`. Conditional clickable modifier, identical pattern
     to the legacy `SettingsNavigationItem.kt:50-52`.
   - **Navigation section append**: after the
     `SettingsDestination.entries.forEachIndexed` loop, a
     `HorizontalDivider()` and a final `NavRow(label = "Help",
     onClick = null)` for the inert placeholder.
   - **KDoc**: the "Three sections" bullet updated — Navigation is now
     "6 rows + an inert Help placeholder added by Phase 7.x.settings.help",
     and the legacy-parity note ("but adds a header image + additional
     rows (ReadingMode dialog / Feedback dialog / Downloads / Help)")
     is trimmed to "but adds a header image (still deferred — purely
     decorative)" since Help / Downloads / ReadingMode / Feedback are
     all now closed.

### §113.3 — Behaviour parity vs legacy

| Trait                            | Legacy             | Rework (after)       |
|----------------------------------|--------------------|----------------------|
| Row visible                      | Yes                | Yes (now)            |
| Row label                        | "Help"             | "Help" (now)         |
| Row clickable / ripple           | No (onClick=null)  | No (onClick=null)    |
| Row position                     | Bottom of Settings | Bottom of Navigation |
| Row icon (auto-mirrored Help)    | Yes                | No (`:ui` no-icon)   |
| Row description                  | None               | None                 |

The single intentional divergence is the absent leading icon — the
`:ui` module's project-wide no-icons-dep policy (`compose.materialIcons
Extended` ~6 MB omission, documented at §111.3 and reaffirmed at the
KDoc of `HistoryScreen.kt`, `StatisticsScreen.kt`, `ThemeScreen.kt`).
The text label is unambiguous; the visual rhythm matches the other
text-only rows in the rework Settings.

### §113.4 — Why nullable `onClick` over a new "PlaceholderRow"
composable

Three options considered:
1. **Inline `Row { Text("Help") }`** inside the LazyColumn — simplest,
   but loses the visual consistency: the inline row wouldn't share
   `NavRow`'s `LocalSpacing` / `MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge` /
   `colorScheme.onSurface` / padding values.
2. **New `private fun PlaceholderRow(label)` composable** — keeps
   `NavRow` signature stable, but introduces a duplicate composable
   that differs from `NavRow` only by the absent clickable modifier.
   Maintenance cost: any future styling change to nav rows would need
   to be applied to both.
3. **`NavRow.onClick` nullable** (chosen) — single composable handles
   both cases. Mirrors the legacy `SettingsNavigationItem`'s same
   pattern (also nullable onClick). One callsite passes null. SOLID:
   OCP-friendly extension (the row now accepts the closed set of "real
   nav row" and "inert placeholder" without further changes).

The change is one line in the signature plus the `then(...)` branch in
the body. No default value on the nullable param — every existing
caller has been updated to pass an explicit lambda (which they all
already did), the new Help caller passes explicit `null`. Forces
callers to make the inert-vs-active decision at the call site.

### §113.5 — Why "Help" inline literal, not `stringResource`

Same Phase-10-deferred-i18n posture as the rest of `:ui/.../settings/`
(§64.4) and the broader rework (§107.5, §109.4, §110.1, §111.10,
§112.6). Legacy uses `stringResource(Res.string.help)` →
`composeApp/.../composeResources/values/strings.xml` `help` key.
Phase 10's i18n lift will re-point both consumers in one pass.

## §114 — Phase 7.x.complaint.date — restore createdAt timestamp on ComplaintRow

### §114.1 — Strategy

Restores the absolute-format complaint timestamp display
("MMM dd, yyyy HH:mm") in the rework ComplaintRow, mirroring the legacy
`composeApp/.../features/complaint/ui/components/ComplaintCard.kt:150`
which renders `formatTimestamp(complaint.createdAt?.toEpochMilliseconds()
?: 0L)` at the row footer. The rework foundation slice (§76) omitted
this display; this slice closes the parity gap.

Pattern: new `:ui`-internal formatter file + 1-line append to the
existing `ComplaintRow` composable. No domain/data/presentation/Koin/
nav touch.

### §114.2 — Files (1 new + 1 modified = 2 total)

1. `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/ComplaintDateFormat.kt`
   (NEW):
   - File-private `val formatter: DateTimeFormat<LocalDateTime>` using
     the `kotlinx.datetime` `LocalDateTime.Format { ... }` DSL. Pattern
     is identical to the legacy `shared/.../complaint/utils/formatTime
     stamp.kt`: monthName(ENGLISH_ABBREVIATED), day(ZERO), year(),
     hour(ZERO), minute(ZERO) — produces e.g. "May 22, 2026 14:30".
   - `internal fun formatComplaintTimestamp(instant: Instant): String`
     resolving against `TimeZone.currentSystemDefault()` and returning
     the formatted string. Takes `Instant` directly (no `Long`-with-
     sentinel pattern from legacy) because the rework's domain field
     `ComplaintSummary.createdAt` is already `Instant?` — null handled
     at the call site, not via a `0L` magic value. SRP / OCP / DIP
     rationale documented in the file's KDoc.

2. `ui/.../ui/complaint/ComplaintScreen.kt` (MODIFIED):
   - `ComplaintRow` composable: after the existing `Text("Type: ${...}")`
     row, append `complaint.createdAt?.let { createdAt -> Text(text =
     formatComplaintTimestamp(createdAt), style = bodySmall, color =
     onSurfaceVariant) }`. Same typography + color tokens as the Type
     line — visually a paired row footer.
   - Inline comment cross-references the legacy `ComplaintCard.kt:150`
     and `PinnedComplaints.kt` for the null-createdAt handling.

### §114.3 — Behaviour parity vs legacy

| Trait                            | Legacy                      | Rework (after)             |
|----------------------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------------|
| Date display                     | "MMM dd, yyyy HH:mm"        | "MMM dd, yyyy HH:mm"       |
| Timezone                         | TimeZone.currentSystemDefault | TimeZone.currentSystemDefault |
| Month name locale                | English abbreviated         | English abbreviated        |
| Null/missing createdAt handling  | `formatTimestamp(0L) == ""` → blank Text | `?.let { ... }` → no Text  |

The single difference is structural — legacy renders an empty Text for
null/zero createdAt (taking up a row's vertical baseline of space);
rework omits the Text entirely (collapses to nothing). Both surface as
"no visible date for this row" to the user.

Pinned-FAQ entries from `PinnedComplaints.kt` (the 2 static admin
entries from §112) have `createdAt = null` by design, so they render
without a date in the rework — the more honest semantic for static
entries with no real timestamp. The legacy uses `Clock.System.now()`
for these entries (drifting timestamp bug); the rework's null-omission
is a quality improvement over legacy.

### §114.4 — Why `Instant` parameter, not `Long`

Three options considered:
1. **Match legacy literally** — `fun formatComplaintTimestamp(epochMs:
   Long): String` with `if (epochMs == 0L) return ""` sentinel.
2. **`Instant?` nullable param** — `fun formatComplaintTimestamp(instant:
   Instant?): String` returning "" for null.
3. **`Instant` non-null param + caller-side null check** (chosen) —
   `fun formatComplaintTimestamp(instant: Instant): String`; caller does
   `?.let { ... }` and omits the Text for null.

Option 1: matches legacy but propagates the magic `0L` value, which
the rework's `:domain` boundary deliberately replaces with `Instant?`
(§107 / §76).

Option 2: clean type signature but moves the null-rendering decision
out of the call site. Less SRP-clean: the formatter has two
responsibilities (format + null-handling).

Option 3: the formatter has one rule ("format an Instant"). The caller
(`ComplaintRow`) decides what to render for null — naturally aligns
with the Compose `?.let { ... }` idiom and lets the caller choose
between "no Text", "fallback Text", or future "Pinned" label as
requirements evolve.

### §114.5 — Why `:ui`, not `:presentation` or `:domain`

- **`:domain`** — value types only; formatting is platform-locale
  concern, not invariant business logic.
- **`:presentation`** — would mean either (a) eagerly format in the VM
  on every emission (re-formats per row per emission — wasteful for
  scroll), or (b) expose formatter to `:ui` (DIP-clean but no
  benefit). Same posture as `ComplaintStatus.displayName()` /
  `ComplaintType.displayName()` which live in `:ui` per §107 / §110.
- **`:ui`** (chosen) — formatting is a render-time presentation
  concern. Pure projection from `Instant` to `String`, runs once per
  visible row on recomposition.

### §114.6 — Build gates

All three green at HEAD `9f52510`:

  SUCCESSFUL in 10s.
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL
  in 16s.
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — BUILD
  SUCCESSFUL in 16s.

14:30"-style timestamps below the Type line; pinned entries render
without a date): Windows-impossible, deferred to user's Mac.

### §114.7 — Layer boundaries & SOLID

- `:ui` self-contained. ZERO touches on `:domain` / `:data` /
  `:presentation` / `:composeApp` / `:shared` / Koin / nav.
- The new formatter takes only `kotlinx.datetime` + `kotlin.time`
  dependencies, both already on `:ui`'s classpath (used by
  HistoryScreen / UpdatesScreen).
- **SRP** — formatter file has one rule: format an Instant as the
  complaint-row absolute timestamp.
- **OCP** — closed under absolute format; if a relative format is
  ever needed, slot in a separate function in the same file without
  modifying this one.
- **DIP** — pure `kotlinx.datetime` dependency; no cross-module
  reach.

SOLID per-file in SOLID_AUDIT Phase 7.x.complaint.date entry.

- **Phase 10 i18n** — month names hardcoded English; lifted in the
  coordinated pass.
- **Admin-side date display** — `AdminComplaintScreen.kt` doesn't
  display createdAt either; lifting it would be a separate slice

- **Dialog date display** — `ComplaintActionDialog` doesn't currently

### §115.7 — Layer boundaries & SOLID

- **`:ui` only** — single touch in `ui/.../complaint/admin/

  the `kotlinx.datetime` alias, both in commonMain) and the

## §116 — Phase 7.x.complaint.statuschip — per-status colored pill parity

### §116.1 — Strategy

Closes §115.9's next-candidate #6 ("per-status colour tint on the
status pill"). Legacy verification first: the legacy
`composeApp/.../features/complaint/ui/components/ComplaintComponents.kt:55`
declares a full `StatusChip(status: ComplaintStatus)` composable that
wraps `Text(status.displayName())` in a `Surface(shape =
RoundedCornerShape(16.dp), color = containerColor)` with
`horizontal=12.dp / vertical=6.dp` text padding,
`labelMedium`/`FontWeight.Medium` typography, and a per-status
`(containerColor, contentColor)` pair selected by an exhaustive
`when` over the 8 `ComplaintStatus` variants. The rework's
pre-statuschip posture diverged on TWO axes — no pill chrome (bare
`Text`), and no per-status colour (uniform
`MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary`). This slice ports both axes in
a single composable, restoring full legacy visual parity.

The decision NOT to ship a bare `ComplaintStatus.displayColor()`
extension (the original §115.9 #6 hypothesis) is documented in the
new `ComplaintStatusChip.kt` KDoc — a bare colour extension would
only fix the per-status axis and leave the Surface-pill axis
diverged; porting the legacy widget shape verbatim is the correct
parity restoration.

### §116.2 — Files added/modified

NEW:

- `ui/.../complaint/ComplaintStatusChip.kt` (NEW; same package as
  `ComplaintScreen.kt` and `ComplaintActionDialog.kt`; sub-package
  reach from `admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt` covered by Kotlin's
  module-wide `internal`):
  - `@Composable @ReadOnlyComposable internal fun chipColors(status:
    ComplaintStatus): Pair<Color, Color>` — pure resolver, one rule
    per status. `@ReadOnlyComposable` because the function only
    reads `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` without writing composition
    slot state — matches the established `:ui` posture for theme-
    derived colour resolvers.
  - `@Composable internal fun ComplaintStatusChip(status:
    ComplaintStatus, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)` — pill
    composable. Internal `chipColors` destructure → `Surface(shape =
    RoundedCornerShape(16.dp), color = container, modifier =
    modifier)` wrapping a `Text(status.displayName(),
    modifier.padding(horizontal = 12.dp, vertical = 6.dp), style =
    labelMedium, color = content, fontWeight = Medium)`.

MODIFIED:

- `SOLID_AUDIT.md` (Phase 7.x.complaint.statuschip entry)

files in 1 docs commit (this commit). 4 files in the source commit,
under the 5-file cap.

### §116.3 — Behaviour parity matrix

The 7 `complaint.status.displayName()` call sites across the 3
complaint surfaces split into TWO contexts:

- **Status-pill contexts** (3 sites, ALL swapped to
  `ComplaintStatusChip`):
  - `ComplaintScreen.kt:411-417` — user-side `ComplaintRow` Type +
    Status row right cell.
  - `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:623-628` — admin-side
    `AdminComplaintRow` Type + Status row right cell.
  - `ComplaintActionDialog.kt:613-619` — `ComplaintPreviewCard`
    Type + Status row right cell (the row that previews the
    complaint being acted upon — e.g. the Reply / Edit / Delete
    confirmation dialogs).
- **Non-pill contexts** (4 sites, INTENTIONALLY left as bare Text
  — these are sentences, filter chips, or statistics labels, NOT
  status badges):
  - `ComplaintScreen.kt:362` — `FilterChip(label = { Text(...)
    })` label text.
  - `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:379` — `FilterChip(label = { Text(...)
    })` label text.
  - `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:539` — `"By status"` statistics card
    bucket row label (the number-prefixed text on the left side of
    the bucket row, not a pill).
  - `AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt:265` — `"Current: ${complaint.
    status.displayName()}"` sentence inside the admin status-change
    confirmation dialog body.

The 4 non-pill sites correctly stay as plain `Text` — wrapping a
filter-chip label in a Surface-pill would visually duplicate the
chip chrome, and wrapping a sentence fragment would create a
mid-line pill that breaks reading flow. The slice's scope is
strictly status-pill parity, not "every site that calls
`displayName()`".

### §116.4 — Per-status colour rationale

The 8-variant mapping in `chipColors` matches legacy
`ComplaintComponents.kt:56-65` verbatim:

| `ComplaintStatus` | `containerColor` | `contentColor` | Legacy line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OPEN` | `primaryContainer` | `onPrimaryContainer` | 57-58 |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | `tertiaryContainer` | `onTertiaryContainer` | 58-59 |
| `RESOLVED` | `secondaryContainer` | `onSecondaryContainer` | 59-60 |
| `CLOSED` | `errorContainer` | `onErrorContainer` | 60-61 |
| `PLANNED` | `surfaceVariant` | `onSurfaceVariant` | 61-62 |
| `PINNED` | `Color.Black` | `Color.White` | 62-63 |
| `UNKNOWN` | `Color.Black` | `Color.White` | 63-64 |
| `NOT_PLANNED` | `Color.Gray` | `Color.White` | 64-65 |

The theme-independent `Color.Black` / `Color.White` for
`PINNED` / `UNKNOWN` and `Color.Gray` / `Color.White` for
`NOT_PLANNED` are a deliberate parity preservation — the legacy
uses these exact constants, so the rework's dark-mode appearance
matches the legacy's dark-mode appearance. Phase 10 i18n / theme-
token lift may revisit these as `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.
inverseSurface` / `inverseOnSurface` if dark-mode contrast becomes
a UX bug, but only as a joint legacy + rework change.

## §117 — Phase 7.x.complaint.usercopy — long-press body-copy on user-side `ComplaintRow`

### §117.1 — Strategy

Closes §116.10's next-candidate #1. Adds usability parity with the
admin surface (§104 Phase 7.x.complaint.admin.copy) — the user-side
`ComplaintRow` body text is now long-press-copyable to the
clipboard, with a `"Copied to clipboard"` Snackbar confirmation.

This is a usability IMPROVEMENT atop the legacy posture, not a
legacy-parity restoration: the legacy user-side does NOT long-press-
copy bodies (verified by grep — only the legacy admin's
`AdminComplaintScreen.kt` has `combinedClickable(onLongClick = ...)`
on body text). The rework now achieves user-admin parity, which is
strictly additive over what the legacy ships. Documented as a
deliberate addition rather than a regression-fix in this slice's
KDoc.

The MVI surface is mirrored 1:1 from the admin side:
- New `ComplaintIntent.OnCopyBody` data object — payload-free
  (clipboard write happens at the `:ui` boundary).
- New `ComplaintViewModel.handleCopyBody()` private suspend handler
  that emits the existing `ComplaintEffect.ShowSuccessMessage(
  "Copied to clipboard")`. Reuses the existing effect — no new
  variant.
- `:ui` `ComplaintRow` gains an `onLongClickBody: () -> Unit` param
  + `LocalClipboardManager.current` capture + `Modifier.combined
  Clickable(onClick = {}, onLongClick = { clipboardManager.setText
  (AnnotatedString(complaint.body)); onLongClickBody() })` on the
  body Text. Call site at the LazyColumn dispatches `Complaint
  Intent.OnCopyBody`.

## §118 — Phase 7.x.downloads.foundation — Downloads screen rework (foundation)

The Downloads queue is the next un-reworked feature surface after the complaint-rework reached feature-completion in §117.10. The legacy `composeApp/.../features/download/ui/screens/DownloadsScreen.kt` (legacy ~580 lines) renders a 3-tab queue (Running / Queued / Failed plus an implicit Completed bucket) over the `:shared` `DownloadRepository.observeAllDownloads()` flow, with per-row mutation affordances (Retry / Cancel / Delete / CancelRunning). The foundation slice ports the READ surface only — list rendering, tab bucketing, per-row card chrome — and defers mutations to §119 (`Phase 7.x.downloads.actions`).

### §118.1 Strategy

Same strangler-fig posture as §75 (`ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl`) / §94 (`ComplaintListRepositoryImpl`) — a new `:data` impl reaches into the legacy `:shared` `DownloadRepository` facade for the source flow. Five sub-slices land in five commits (`d05bd45` :domain → `f93640b` :data → `6716659` :presentation → `8f2965b` :ui → `ca690dd` wire), each at-or-under the 5-file cap. Tabs and bucketing are driven by `DownloadStatus` enum branching in `:presentation`; the foundation slice's `DownloadsIntent` has exactly ONE variant (`OnTabSelect(index: Int)`) and `DownloadsEffect` is declared as an empty sealed interface — explicit OCP hook for §119 to extend with mutation variants without modifying the foundation surface.

### §118.2 `:domain` surface

`DownloadStatus` enum (`:domain/model/downloads/`): five variants — `RUNNING`, `QUEUED`, `COMPRESSING`, `FAILED`, `SUCCESS` — covering the legacy `:shared` `DownloadStatus`'s observable states. `DownloadedChapter` data class (`:domain/model/downloads/`): row-level projection with 9 fields (`chapterId: Long`, `mangaId: Long`, `chapterTitle: String`, `mangaTitle: String?`, `api: String`, `status: DownloadStatus`, `progress: Float?`, `pageCount: Int?`, `errorMessage: String?`). The Float-based `progress` allows the rework to render a determinate progress bar where the legacy uses an integer `currentPage` / `totalPages` pair — same semantic content, `:ui`-friendlier projection. Null `progress` means "no progress signal yet" (QUEUED, FAILED, SUCCESS); non-null means the running download has surfaced a fraction.

`DownloadsRepository` interface (`:domain/repository/`): single READ method `observeAllDownloads(): Flow<List<DownloadedChapter>>`. `ObserveDownloadsUseCase` (`:domain/usecase/downloads/`) is a thin pass-through `operator fun invoke()` delegating to the repository.

### §118.3 `:data` strangler-fig impl

`DownloadsRepositoryImpl` (`:data/repository/`): constructor takes the legacy `:shared` `DownloadRepository`; `observeAllDownloads()` maps each legacy `ChapterDownloadEntity` to a `DownloadedChapter` via a private `ChapterDownloadEntity.toDownloadedChapter()` extension. The mapper exhaustively `when`s over the legacy `DownloadStatus` to populate the rework's 5-variant enum + computes `progress` from the legacy `currentPage / totalPages` ratio (null when `totalPages == 0` or status doesn't make a progress signal meaningful).

Sibling enum `DownloadStatus.toDomain()` mapper (private file-local extension) — exhaustive `when` so a future legacy-side enum variant (e.g., a hypothetical `PAUSED`) is a compile-time error here. Mirrors the `ComplaintStatus.toDomain()` posture from §94.

### §118.4 `:presentation` MVI

`DownloadsState` (`:presentation/downloads/`): 4 fields — `selectedTab: Int` (0..3), `downloads: List<DownloadedChapter>`, `isLoading: Boolean`, `error: String?`. Computed properties expose 4 bucket lists (`running`, `queued`, `failed`, `completed`) derived from `downloads` filtered by status. `COMPRESSING` rows route into the `running` bucket (legacy parity — both are in-flight states the user perceives as "running").

`DownloadsIntent` sealed interface: ONE variant `OnTabSelect(val index: Int)`. Declared as a sealed interface (not a single data class) so §119 can extend with siblings without modifying the foundation. `DownloadsEffect` sealed interface: empty — explicit OCP hook for §119's `ShowError` variant.

`DownloadsViewModel`: extends `MviViewModel<DownloadsState, DownloadsIntent, DownloadsEffect>`. Constructor takes 1 dep (`observeDownloads: ObserveDownloadsUseCase`). `init {}` launches `observeDownloads().onEach { downloads -> updateState { it.copy(downloads = downloads, isLoading = false, error = null) } }.catch { e -> updateState { it.copy(isLoading = false, error = e.message) } }.launchIn(viewModelScope)`. `handle()` over `DownloadsIntent`: single branch `OnTabSelect -> updateState { it.copy(selectedTab = intent.index) }`.

No `OnRefresh` intent — Room's `Flow<List<...>>` re-emits on every transaction; refresh is implicit. No `OnRetry` for the initial-load `error` field — the error surface is a defensive degradation indicator, not a recoverable failure state (Room flows don't fail in practice; if they do, restarting the screen restarts the collector).

### §118.5 `:ui` composable

`DownloadsScreen.kt` (`:ui/downloads/`): top-bar with back-arrow `TextButton("Back")` (icon-free `:ui` posture, same as History / Statistics / Library), `TabRow` over 4 bucket labels ("Running" / "Queued" / "Failed" / "Completed"), `LazyColumn` rendering the selected bucket's rows. Two private composables — `DownloadCard(chapter: DownloadedChapter)` for the QUEUED / COMPRESSING / FAILED / SUCCESS buckets and `RunningDownloadCard(chapter: DownloadedChapter)` for the RUNNING bucket (the latter renders a determinate `LinearProgressIndicator(progress = chapter.progress ?: 0f)` when progress is non-null, indeterminate otherwise).

`DownloadBucketList(rows: List<DownloadedChapter>)` is a stateless renderer; the wrapper composable owns the state-shape and forwards `rows = state.runningBucket` (etc.) to it. Empty buckets render an `EmptyBucket("No downloads")` placeholder rather than collapsing the screen — same UX as the legacy.

No mutation buttons in the foundation slice — `:ui` is pure render of the READ surface. §119 retrofits the per-row `TextButton("Retry") / ("Cancel") / ("Delete")` affordances.

### §118.6 `:composeApp` wire

`downloadsReworkModule` (NEW): three Koin bindings — `single<DownloadsRepository> { DownloadsRepositoryImpl(legacy = get()) }` (legacy `DownloadRepository` is already `single` in `SharedModule`) + `factory { ObserveDownloadsUseCase(get()) }` + `viewModel { DownloadsViewModel(get()) }`. Appended to `allReworkModules()` aggregator. `DownloadsReworkScreenRoute.kt` (NEW): the standard adapter shape (`koinViewModel<DownloadsViewModel>()` → `DownloadsScreen(viewModel = viewModel)` + an `onBack` callback wired to `navController.safePopBackStack()`).

`Screen.kt` adds `DownloadsRework` route object. `App.kt` adds a `composable<Screen.DownloadsRework> { ... }` block; the existing `composable<Screen.DownloadsScreen> { ... }` (legacy) stays bound — both routes coexist until §119's swap redirects the Settings hub's Downloads row from the legacy to the rework target.

### §118.7 Files added/modified

NEW (10):
- `domain/.../model/downloads/DownloadStatus.kt`
- `domain/.../model/downloads/DownloadedChapter.kt`
- `domain/.../repository/DownloadsRepository.kt`
- `domain/.../usecase/downloads/ObserveDownloadsUseCase.kt`
- `data/.../repository/DownloadsRepositoryImpl.kt`
- `presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsState.kt`
- `presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsIntent.kt`
- `presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsEffect.kt`
- `presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsViewModel.kt`
- `ui/.../downloads/DownloadsScreen.kt`
- `composeApp/.../di/DownloadsReworkModule.kt`
- `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/DownloadsReworkScreenRoute.kt`

MODIFIED (3):
- `composeApp/.../di/ReworkModules.kt` — append `downloadsReworkModule`.
- `composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt` — add `DownloadsRework` route object.
- `composeApp/.../App.kt` — add `composable<Screen.DownloadsRework>` block.

### §118.8 Build gates

After every source commit (`d05bd45`, `f93640b`, `6716659`, `8f2965b`, `ca690dd`):
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green (verified on the `:ui` + wire commits; pre-`:ui` commits don't link into the Desktop entry point but were green there too)

iOS framework linking + on-device smoke tests deferred to user's Mac.

### §118.9 Deferrals

- **Mutations** — Retry / Cancel / Delete / CancelRunning lift to §119 (`Phase 7.x.downloads.actions`). The foundation slice's empty `DownloadsEffect` + single-variant `DownloadsIntent` are the documented OCP extension points.
- **i18n** — Tab labels ("Running" / "Queued" / "Failed" / "Completed"), placeholder strings ("No downloads"), error fallback text all stay inline literal. Phase 10 i18n lift handles all consumers in one pass.
- **No optimistic UI** — list re-emits from Room on every transaction; no VM-side projection of in-flight mutations. §119 maintains this — failure surfaces as a snackbar, success is visually self-evident through the next Room emission.
- **Settings row swap** — the rework Settings hub's Downloads row still points at the LEGACY `Screen.DownloadsScreen` at the end of foundation; swapping early would have user-reached the rework route before mutations were re-wired (forbidden observable behaviour regression). The swap lands in §119 once the mutation surface is complete.

## §119 — Phase 7.x.downloads.actions — Downloads mutation slice + Settings row swap

The foundation slice (§118) deliberately deferred the legacy's 4 per-row mutation affordances (Retry / Cancel / Delete / CancelRunning) — landing them required ISP-splitting the rework's READ repo from a sibling WRITE repo, expanding the `:presentation` MVI surface with 4 intent variants + a `ShowError` effect, and threading per-row buttons through the `:ui` layer. Once the mutation surface was complete, the Settings hub's Downloads row swapped from the legacy `Screen.DownloadsScreen` to the rework `Screen.DownloadsRework` — completing the rework Downloads stack as the user-reachable path.

### §119.1 Strategy

Four sub-slices, four commits (`dc009da` :domain WRITE → `ac1d4dd` data+Koin+presentation → `e08f0ec` :ui → `94987b5` swap), each at-or-under the 5-file cap. ISP-split posture: the foundation's `DownloadsRepository` stays READ-only (one method, `observeAllDownloads()`); a sibling `DownloadsActionRepository` houses the 4 WRITE methods. Mirrors §95's `ComplaintListRepository` (READ) + `ComplaintActionRepository` (WRITE) split — a consumer that only needs reads doesn't pull a write dep through the type system.

### §119.2 `:domain` WRITE surface

`DownloadsActionRepository` (`:domain/repository/`): four suspend methods returning `Result<Unit>`:
- `retryDownload(chapterId: Long)` — re-enqueues a FAILED row by reading the persisted chapter entity and calling the legacy `enqueueChapterDownload(chapter, title, mangaApi)`.
- `cancelDownload(chapterId: Long)` — calls legacy `onCancel(chapterId)`; applies to QUEUED + COMPRESSING rows (status removal from the queue without process-kill).
- `cancelRunningDownload(chapterId: Long, mangaId: Long)` — calls legacy `cancelARunningChapter(chapterId, mangaId)`; the 2-arg signature is load-bearing for the legacy implementation (the running coroutine is keyed by both ids).
- `deleteDownload(chapterId: Long)` — calls legacy `deleteDownload(chapterId)`; applies to FAILED + SUCCESS rows.

Four use case classes (`:domain/usecase/downloads/`): `RetryDownloadUseCase`, `CancelDownloadUseCase`, `CancelRunningDownloadUseCase`, `DeleteDownloadUseCase`. Each is a thin pass-through `suspend operator fun invoke(...)` over the action repo.

### §119.3 `:data` strangler-fig impl

`DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl` (`:data/repository/`): constructor takes 2 deps — the legacy `:shared` `DownloadRepository` (for the 4 mutation methods) + the `:shared` `ChapterDownloadDao` (for the retry path's persisted-entity reload). Each method wraps a single legacy invocation in `runCatching {}` so any throw (Room failure, Coil cache eviction during retry's entity-rehydration, queue-state-mismatch from the legacy) surfaces as `Result.failure`.

Retry reconstruction: `dao.getDownloadByChapter(chapterId)` returns the persisted `ChapterDownloadEntity` (null if absent — surfaced as `error("download row not found")`); the entity's `toChapterEntity()` extension (already on the legacy classpath) rehydrates the upstream `Chapter` model the legacy enqueuer expects. `mangaTitle` is read from the row directly (the legacy enqueuer takes `title: String`, denormalised on the row), and `api` (denormalised from the row) carries the source-tag the legacy uses to route the download to the correct fetcher.

Strangler-fig reach grows by ONE legacy reference (`ChapterDownloadDao` — already `single` in `SharedModule`). The legacy `DownloadRepository` was already injected via the foundation's `DownloadsRepositoryImpl`; the actions impl reuses the same singleton.

### §119.4 `:presentation` MVI append

`DownloadsIntent` grows from 1 variant to 5 (sealed-interface OCP extension; existing `OnTabSelect` untouched). The 4 new variants are all `data class` (per the rework MVI contract):
- `OnRetry(val chapter: DownloadedChapter)`
- `OnCancel(val chapter: DownloadedChapter)`
- `OnCancelRunning(val chapter: DownloadedChapter)`
- `OnDelete(val chapter: DownloadedChapter)`

Variants carry the full `DownloadedChapter` (not just `chapterId`) so a future "Undo" snackbar can rehydrate the row's UI state without a second Room round-trip. `OnCancelRunning` extracts both `chapterId` AND `mangaId` from the chapter (the legacy `cancelARunningChapter` takes both; passing only `chapterId` would re-introduce a `0L` placeholder, a known legacy footgun).

`DownloadsEffect` grows from empty to 1 variant: `data class ShowError(val message: String)`. Mirror of §95's `ShowErrorMessage` — drives a snackbar on failure. No `ShowSuccessMessage` variant: Room re-emits on every write, so successful retry (FAILED → QUEUED transition), delete (row vanishing), and cancel (status flip) are visually self-evident. A success snackbar would be redundant chrome.

`DownloadsViewModel` constructor expands from 1 dep to 5 (foundation's `observeDownloads` + the 4 new use cases). `handle()` over the now-5-variant `DownloadsIntent` adds 4 new branches; each launches a `viewModelScope` coroutine, awaits the suspend use case, routes the `Result` through a private `emitOnFailure(result: Result<Unit>)` helper that emits `DownloadsEffect.ShowError(message)` only when the `Result` is a failure. The error-message extraction chain is `result.exceptionOrNull()?.let { e -> e.message ?: e::class.simpleName } ?: "Unknown error"` — same posture as §95's failure-text fallback.

No in-flight gating — Downloads mutations don't conflict with each other across rows, and a tap-spam on the same row's button at worst no-ops on the second attempt (Room transaction idempotency).

### §119.5 `:ui` composable

`DownloadsScreen.kt` (MODIFIED) grows three surfaces:
- `SnackbarHostState` hoisted into the wrapper composable; threaded into the stateless content composable as a positional param. `Scaffold` gains `snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }`.
- `LaunchedEffect(viewModel) { viewModel.effects.collectLatest { effect -> when (effect) { is DownloadsEffect.ShowError -> snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(effect.message) } } }` — same posture as §95's `ComplaintEffect` collector.
- `DownloadCard` + `RunningDownloadCard` both gain an `onIntent: (DownloadsIntent) -> Unit` callback param (threaded through `DownloadBucketList`); per-row buttons render exactly the legacy's affordances:
  - QUEUED, COMPRESSING → "Cancel" (`OnCancel`)
  - RUNNING → "Cancel" (`OnCancelRunning` — 2-arg legacy call)
  - FAILED → "Retry" + "Delete" (`OnRetry` + `OnDelete`)
  - SUCCESS → "Delete" (`OnDelete`)

`DownloadCardActions` private composable owns the per-status button-row branching — exhaustive `when (chapter.status)` so a future enum variant is compile-time-flagged here. Buttons are `TextButton`s with literal labels (no icons) — same icon-free `:ui` posture as the foundation. The eventual icon-parity lift (cross-references `Phase 7.x.complaint.iconparity` / §111) is a separate slice that touches all `:ui` modules' button labels at once.

### §119.6 `:composeApp` Koin rewire + Settings swap

`downloadsReworkModule` appends:
- `single<DownloadsActionRepository> { DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl(legacy = get(), dao = get()) }` — both deps already `single` in `SharedModule`.
- `factory { RetryDownloadUseCase(get()) }` + `factory { CancelDownloadUseCase(get()) }` + `factory { CancelRunningDownloadUseCase(get()) }` + `factory { DeleteDownloadUseCase(get()) }`.
- `viewModel { DownloadsViewModel(get(), get(), get(), get(), get()) }` — replaces the foundation's 1-arg `viewModel { DownloadsViewModel(get()) }` binding with the 5-arg expansion. `DownloadsReworkScreenRoute.kt` is untouched — it consumes the VM via `koinViewModel()` and Koin resolves the new constructor signature transparently.

**Settings hub swap** — `SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt:98`: the `when` arm `SettingsDestination.DOWNLOADS -> Screen.DownloadsScreen` (foundation pointed at legacy) becomes `SettingsDestination.DOWNLOADS -> Screen.DownloadsRework` (now points at rework). The legacy `composable<Screen.DownloadsScreen>` binding in `App.kt` stays in place for parity testing but is no longer reachable from any user-facing entry. Phase 9.x route-swap retires the legacy binding completely once on-device parity is verified.

KDocs on `Screen.DownloadsRework` (Screen.kt) and the `composable<Screen.DownloadsRework>` block (App.kt) updated to reflect the swap — both previously said "not surfaced in any user-facing entry yet" (foundation-era) and now describe the user-reachable path through Settings hub.

### §119.7 Files added/modified

NEW (5):
- `domain/.../repository/DownloadsActionRepository.kt`
- `domain/.../usecase/downloads/RetryDownloadUseCase.kt`
- `domain/.../usecase/downloads/CancelDownloadUseCase.kt`
- `domain/.../usecase/downloads/CancelRunningDownloadUseCase.kt`
- `domain/.../usecase/downloads/DeleteDownloadUseCase.kt`
- `data/.../repository/DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.kt`

- `presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsEffect.kt` — 1 new `ShowError` variant
- `presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsViewModel.kt` — 5-arg ctor + 4 new handlers + `emitOnFailure` helper
- `ui/.../downloads/DownloadsScreen.kt` — snackbar + per-row buttons + `DownloadCardActions`
- `composeApp/.../di/DownloadsReworkModule.kt` — appended action repo + 4 use case factories + 5-arg VM binding
- `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt` — `when` arm swap + KDoc update

All ≤5 files per commit per the standing cap. The data+Koin+presentation bundle was at-cap atomic — splitting it would have broken the build between commits (the Koin module's 5-arg `viewModel` resolution requires the VM's 5-arg constructor, which is in the same commit).

### §119.8 Build gates

After every source commit (`dc009da`, `ac1d4dd`, `e08f0ec`, `94987b5`):
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green (verified on the :ui and swap commits; pre-:ui commits don't link into Desktop entry point but were green there too)

iOS framework linking + on-device smoke tests deferred to user's Mac.

### §119.9 Deferrals

- **i18n** — Button labels ("Retry" / "Cancel" / "Delete"), snackbar error fallback ("Unknown error") all stay inline literal. Phase 10 i18n lift handles all consumers in one pass.
- **Icon parity** — buttons are labelled `TextButton`s, no icons. Same icon-free posture as the foundation (§118) and as History / Statistics / Library. The eventual icon-parity lift (`Phase 7.x.complaint.iconparity` / §111 model) is a separate cross-`:ui` slice.
- **Undo snackbar** — Cancel + Delete are immediate; no "Undo" affordance. Legacy doesn't have one either. Future addition would build on the existing `DownloadsEffect.ShowError`-style snackbar surface + a `ShowAction(message, onAction)` variant.
- **Retry-from-snackbar action** — failure snackbar is action-less, same as §95's posture. Retry by tapping the row's Retry button again.
- **No optimistic UI** — Room re-emits on every transaction; VM doesn't project in-flight mutation state onto the list. Same posture as §95. Optimistic updates would split the source of truth between VM's projection and Room — fragile.
- **No nav graph route retirement** — the legacy `composable<Screen.DownloadsScreen>` binding in `App.kt` stays bound but is no longer user-reachable. Phase 9.x route-swap retires it completely after on-device parity verification.

### §119.10 Block-and-ask check (a)-(d)

- **(a)** Contract library blocker: none.
- **(b)** Observable behaviour change: yes — the Settings hub's Downloads row now lands on the rework screen instead of the legacy. The rework's mutation set was deliberately wired to legacy parity (`Retry / Cancel / Delete / CancelRunning` all dispatch to the same legacy methods the legacy `DownloadsScreen` invokes), so the user-visible outcome of every button press is identical to pre-swap; only the rendering chrome differs. Documented as a deliberate route-swap, not a regression.
- **(c)** Compile fail: no — all 4 build gates green after the swap.
- **(d)** Unresolvable SOLID violation: no.

Slice complete. Downloads-surface rework reaches feature-completion against the legacy counterpart's user-visible surface. Phase 7 advances to the next un-reworked feature; legacy route inventory shows `Screen.Welcome`, `Screen.Home`, `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails`, `Screen.WebView`, `Screen.RepoSettings` remaining without rework counterparts. Among these, **`Screen.RepoSettings`** is the next obvious candidate — it's the only one without significant cross-screen interaction (Welcome is bootstrap-only; Home / LibraryMangaDetails / WebView are large feature surfaces with significant deferral risk), and it is a settings-hub leaf so the strangler-fig posture is well-established.

## §120 — Phase 7.x.sources.complaint — Request-Source dialog on rework Sources screen

Targeted extension of §84's Sources rework (Task #282). Rather than building a parallel `RepoSettings` rework that duplicates the source list, this slice extends the existing rework Sources screen with the "Request adding source" affordance the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt` carries — surfacing the same `FeedbackDialog`-backed pipeline the legacy uses (pinned `ComplaintType.SITES_ADD`, header "we_will_add_it_as_soon_it_possible", URL body field). Same posture as §95's Settings hub feedback dialog (Phase 7.x.settings.feedback), but with a fixed complaint type (no dropdown — the row label "Request adding source" pins the category). §84.8 explicitly named this slice as the deferred OCP-extension hook for the empty `SourcesEffect` foundation.

### §120.1 Strategy

The legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt:215-248` carries two distinct affordances: (1) the per-source on/off list (already ported in §84) and (2) the "Request adding source" row that opens a `FeedbackDialog` with `ComplaintType.SITES_ADD` pinned. The rework Sources screen already covers (1); this slice ports (2) onto the same screen so a future `RepoSettings` route swap can retire the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt` entirely without losing the request affordance. The complaint submission flows through the SAME `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` the rework Settings hub uses (Phase 7.x.settings.feedback) — Koin's global container resolves the use case across modules, so no new `:domain` / `:data` plumbing is needed.

The choice of "extend Sources" over "build parallel RepoSettings rework" is deliberate. A parallel rework would (a) duplicate the source list (already a 200+-LOC composable + the bucketed-by-language regroup logic in `SourcesState`), (b) require nav-graph wiring for a second route that shows the same data, and (c) confuse the eventual route-swap (legacy `Screen.RepoSettings` would have to pick between two rework counterparts). Extending Sources keeps the rework surface one-screen-per-concept and uses the OCP hook §84.8 already named.

### §120.2 Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:domain` — **untouched**. `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` already exists (Phase 7.x.settings.feedback / §95.2); `ComplaintType.SITES_ADD` already exists in the `ComplaintSummary` model from Phase 7.x.complaint.foundation. No new files.
- `:data` — **untouched**. The Complaint repository impl already plumbs `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` through to the same `:shared` complaint endpoint the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen` invokes via `SendComplaintUseCase`.
- `:presentation` — **3 modified files** (`SourcesIntent.kt`, `SourcesEffect.kt`, `SourcesState.kt`) **+ 1 modified VM** (`SourcesViewModel.kt`). `SourcesIntent` grows by 3 variants (`OnOpenComplaintDialog`, `OnDismissComplaintDialog`, `OnSubmitComplaint(body)`); `SourcesEffect` gains its first variant (`ShowSnackbar(message)`); `SourcesState` gains 2 fields (`complaintDialogOpen`, `isSubmittingComplaint`); `SourcesViewModel` grows by 1 ctor dep (`SubmitFeedbackUseCase`) + 1 handler method (`handleSubmitComplaint`).
- `:ui` — **1 modified file** (`SourcesScreen.kt`). New `SnackbarHost` on the `Scaffold`, new `LaunchedEffect(effects)` collector routing `ShowSnackbar` to the host, new private `RequestSourceRow` LazyColumn item above the language list, new private `RequestSourceDialog` composable.
- `:composeApp` — **1 modified file** (`SourcesReworkModule.kt`). The `viewModel { SourcesViewModel(get(), get(), get()) }` binding expands to `viewModel { SourcesViewModel(get(), get(), get(), get()) }` (4th arg resolves the pre-existing `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` from `settingsReworkModule`'s `factory` binding).

### §120.3 MVI shape — pinned-type complaint dialog

`SourcesIntent` grows by 3 variants:

- `data object OnOpenComplaintDialog` — flips `complaintDialogOpen = true`.
- `data object OnDismissComplaintDialog` — flips `complaintDialogOpen = false`, but ONLY if `!state.isSubmittingComplaint`. The VM-side guard is defence-in-depth — the `:ui` `DialogProperties` also disables back-press / outside-tap dismissal during submission.
- `data class OnSubmitComplaint(val body: String)` — triggers `handleSubmitComplaint(body)`.

The complaint type is NOT in the intent payload — `ComplaintType.SITES_ADD` is pinned VM-internal because the row label "Request adding source" fixes the category. This differs from the Settings hub's `FeedbackDialog`, which carries a `complaintType: ComplaintType` field on its intent because the hub's dialog DOES show a dropdown for the user to pick the category.

`SourcesEffect.ShowSnackbar(message)` — fills the foundation's empty `SourcesEffect`. Same `data class` shape as `SettingsEffect.ShowSnackbar` (§95) and `LanguageEffect.RequestLanguageSubmitted` (Phase 7.x.language.request).

`SourcesState` grows by 2 fields:

- `complaintDialogOpen: Boolean = false` — drives the `if (state.complaintDialogOpen) RequestSourceDialog(...)` branch.
- `isSubmittingComplaint: Boolean = false` — gates the Submit button's enabled state, the Cancel button's enabled state, and the `DialogProperties` dismissal flags. Re-entry-protects `handleSubmitComplaint` (the VM short-circuits if `state.value.isSubmittingComplaint == true`).

The body text field is NOT in `SourcesState` — it's local to the `:ui` composable (`remember { mutableStateOf("") }`) and rides along with the `OnSubmitComplaint(body)` intent. Same posture as the Settings hub's feedback dialog field — keeps the state surface narrow (2 fields, not 3) and preserves "user can resume typing mid-edit" behaviour without OnComplaintBodyChange intents firing per-keystroke.

### §120.4 VM submission posture

`handleSubmitComplaint(body)`:

1. Short-circuit if `state.value.isSubmittingComplaint` (re-entry guard).
2. Set `isSubmittingComplaint = true` synchronously.
3. `viewModelScope.launch { ... }` — kicks off the submit on the VM coroutine so `handle` returns immediately (view's `submit(intent)` doesn't block).
4. Invoke `submitFeedback(type = ComplaintType.SITES_ADD, subject = type.name, body = body)`.
5. On `Result.success`: clear `isSubmittingComplaint`, close the dialog (`complaintDialogOpen = false`), emit `ShowSnackbar("Thanks! Your request was submitted.")`.
6. On `Result.failure`: clear `isSubmittingComplaint` (dialog stays open with the user's typed text preserved), emit `ShowSnackbar("Failed to submit request: <cause>")`. Cause construction mirrors `SettingsViewModel.handleSubmitFeedback` / `handleClearCache` — `exceptionOrNull()?.message ?: simpleName ?: "Unknown error"`.

The choice of "dialog stays open on failure" matches the Settings hub's feedback dialog (§95.4) — the user just typed potentially 100s of chars; closing on failure would force re-typing.

### §120.5 `:ui` surface

`SourcesScreenContent` gains a `effects: Flow<SourcesEffect>` parameter and a `SnackbarHostState`. The `LaunchedEffect(effects)` collector routes `ShowSnackbar` to the host. `Scaffold(snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(hostState = snackbarHostState) })` plumbs the host onto the screen.

New private `RequestSourceRow(onClick, paddingHorizontal, paddingVertical)` composable — a `Row` with title "Request adding source" + subtitle "Enter the URL of a site you'd like us to add", wrapped in `.clickable(onClick = onClick)`. Added to the `LazyColumn` as `item(key = "request-source")` above the per-language fold. A `HorizontalDivider` separates it from the first language section.

New private `RequestSourceDialog(isSubmitting, onSubmit, onDismiss)` composable — `AlertDialog` with:
- Title "Request adding source"
- Body text "We will add it as soon as possible." + OutlinedTextField (label "Enter the site URL") with 5/500 char validation matching the Settings hub's `FeedbackDialog`
- Submit button labeled "Submit" / "Submitting…" (enabled when `body.length >= 5 && !isSubmitting`)
- Cancel button (disabled when `isSubmitting`)
- `DialogProperties(dismissOnBackPress = !isSubmitting, dismissOnClickOutside = !isSubmitting)` — UI-side gate; the VM's `OnDismissComplaintDialog` guard is defence-in-depth.

The dialog composable is NOT extracted into a shared `:ui` component (e.g., a hypothetical `:ui/feedback/FeedbackDialog.kt`). The Settings hub has its own private `FeedbackDialog`; Sources has its own private `RequestSourceDialog`. The two share ~80% of layout shape but differ in three places: (a) Sources omits the type-dropdown, (b) the labels differ (URL vs free-form feedback), (c) the supporting text differs. Per "three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction" (CLAUDE-MD §rules), the second occurrence does not yet justify an abstraction; a third consumer would.

### §120.6 Koin rewire

`sourcesReworkModule` updates the `viewModel { SourcesViewModel(get(), get(), get()) }` binding to `viewModel { SourcesViewModel(get(), get(), get(), get()) }`. The 4th `get()` resolves `SubmitFeedbackUseCase` — already bound `factory` by `settingsReworkModule` (§95) / `feedbackReworkModule`. Koin's container is global across all `:composeApp` rework modules; cross-module resolution is the established pattern (§79.8 hover-only pattern for cross-slice deps).

KDoc on the `viewModel` binding explicitly notes the cross-module resolution and the Phase 7.x.sources.complaint origin of the 4th arg.

## §122 — Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingfinish — onboarding "Finish" button on rework Sources

### §122.1 Strategy

Closes the last §84.8 deferral. The legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt:125-153` renders a Finish bottom-bar button when `isFirstOpen == true` (the onboarding entry). With this slice landed, the rework Sources screen reaches feature-parity with the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt`, unblocking the upcoming **Phase 7.x.reposettings.swap**.

### §122.2 API shape — collapse legacy's flag+callback pair into one nullable callback

The legacy uses TWO parameters: `isFirstOpen: Boolean` (gate) + `onFinish: () -> Unit` (callback). This slice collapses both into a single nullable parameter:

```kotlin
fun SourcesScreen(
    viewModel: SourcesViewModel,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    onFinish: (() -> Unit)? = null,
)

internal fun SourcesScreenContent(
    state: SourcesState,
    effects: Flow<SourcesEffect>,
    onIntent: (SourcesIntent) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    onFinish: (() -> Unit)? = null,
)
```

The Scaffold's `bottomBar` slot is `onFinish?.let { FinishButton(onClick = it) }`. Non-null signal IS the gate. This removes the legacy's footgun where `isFirstOpen=true` could pair with a no-op `onFinish={}`.

### §122.3 Visual parity

`FinishButton` private composable:
- Full-width `Button` inside a `Box` with 24.dp horizontal / 12.dp vertical padding (matches legacy).
- 50.dp tall, `RoundedCornerShape(26.dp)` — pill shape matching legacy's explicit `.clip(RoundedCornerShape(26.dp))` post-`shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.medium` override.
- Default Material 3 button colors (primary container + on-primary content) — matches legacy's explicit `containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary`. No need to override; M3 defaults already match.
- Text "Finish" with `MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge` — legacy uses `labelLarge.copy(fontSize = 16.sp, color = onPrimary)`; the rework drops the explicit `16.sp` override because M3's `labelLarge` is already `14.sp`-ish and the typography token is the canonical choice (slight visual delta acceptable — legacy was carrying a one-off override the design system has since normalized).

### §122.4 Layer-by-layer surfaces

ZERO new files; ONE `:ui` file modified (`SourcesScreen.kt`). The Finish button is a UI-only concern that depends on a single callback — no `:domain`/`:data`/`:presentation` changes, no state, no intents, no effects. The route adapter doesn't change in this slice either; it implicitly passes `onFinish = null` via the parameter default, so existing callers stay working.

When the upcoming **Phase 7.x.reposettings.swap** wires the rework route into the onboarding chain, it will:
- Either add an `isFirstOpen` route arg to `Screen.SourcesRework`, OR
- Add a second route variant `Screen.SourcesReworkOnboarding`, OR
- Modify `SourcesReworkScreenRoute` to read a route arg and pass `onFinish = { navController.popBackStack() }` (or whatever the onboarding chain's next-step navigation requires).

### §122.5 i18n posture

"Finish" stays an inline string literal — Phase 10 i18n lift will swap it for `stringResource(Res.string.finish)` on both legacy + rework consumers in one pass. Legacy already has the resource key (`Res.string.finish`); rework will reuse it.

### §122.6 Files added/modified

NEW (0):
- _none_ — entire slice extends an existing file.

MODIFIED (1):
- `ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen.kt`:
  - New `onFinish: (() -> Unit)? = null` parameter on `SourcesScreen` + `SourcesScreenContent`.
  - New `bottomBar = { onFinish?.let { FinishButton(onClick = it) } }` slot on the Scaffold.
  - New private `FinishButton` composable.
  - New import: `androidx.compose.foundation.layout.height`.
  - Screen-level KDoc updated — onboarding-flavour UI restoration is now COMPLETE (all §84.8 deferrals closed).

2 commits: source-only (1 file) + close-out docs (2 files). Within the ≤5-files-per-commit cap.

## §123 — Phase 7.x.reposettings.swap — `Screen.RepoSettings` adapter renders rework `SourcesScreen`

The route-swap arrived as the **smallest possible change** to flip the legacy `Screen.RepoSettings` nav entry from the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen` render to the rework `:ui` `SourcesScreen`. The route-shape and both callers stay literally byte-identical. The swap lives entirely in the route adapter file `RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt` — `App.kt`'s `composable<Screen.RepoSettings>` block is unchanged.

### §123.1 Strategy

Three options were live going in:
- **A** — modify `App.kt`'s `composable<Screen.RepoSettings>` block to call `SourcesScreenRoute` directly. Cleanest in caller-graph terms (one fewer indirection), but spreads the swap rationale across multiple files (the route adapter file `RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt` would become dead but stay on disk, confusing).
- **B** — rewrite the route adapter file `RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt` itself: drop legacy imports, swap the render body, preserve the function signature. Same caller-graph behaviour (App.kt still calls `RepoSettingsScreenRoute(navController, backStackEntry)`), but all swap context lives in one file's KDoc + diff.
- **C** — delete the route adapter file and inline the rework render into `App.kt`. Most aggressive; bundles the deletion sweep with the swap. Defers cleanest to Phase 9.x where all retired legacy adapters get retired together.

**Chosen: B.** Single-file source commit (1/5 of the cap), all rationale co-located in the route file's KDoc, function signature unchanged means App.kt + Screen.kt + both callers (`SourcesScreenRoute.kt:59`, `HomeScreenRoute.kt:193`) need ZERO modification.

### §123.2 What changed in `RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt`

**Imports dropped:**
- `me.manga.kira.features.repo_settings.ui.screens.RepoSettingsScreen` (legacy composable)
- `me.manga.kira.features.repo_settings.presentation.RepoSettingsViewModel` (legacy VM)
- `me.manga.kira.navigation.safePopBackStack` (defensive back-pop helper — see §123.5)

**Imports added:**
- `me.manga.kira.presentation.sources.SourcesViewModel` (rework MVI VM)
- `me.manga.kira.ui.sources.SourcesScreen` (rework composable)

**Render body** — legacy `RepoSettingsScreen(viewModel = legacyVM, onBackPress = { navController.safePopBackStack() }, isFirstOpen = args.isFirstOpen, onFinish = …)` becomes:

```kotlin
SourcesScreen(
    viewModel = viewModel,
    onFinish = if (args.isFirstOpen) {
        {
            prefs.putBoolean("first_launch", false)
            navController.navigate(Screen.Library) {
                popUpTo(navController.graph.startDestinationId) {
                    inclusive = true
                }
                launchSingleTop = true
            }
        }
    } else {
        null
    },
)
```

VM resolution swaps from `koinViewModel<RepoSettingsViewModel>()` to `koinViewModel<SourcesViewModel>()`. Koin binding for `SourcesViewModel` lives in `sourcesReworkModule` (see [`SourcesReworkModule.kt`](./composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/SourcesReworkModule.kt) and §82). The VM is scoped to the `NavBackStackEntry` `ViewModelStoreOwner` per `androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose`'s `koinViewModel()` integration, so each route's VM instance is independent — even though `SourcesReworkScreenRoute` resolves the same Koin binding.

### §123.3 Preserved verbatim from the legacy adapter

Onboarding-chain `onFinish` semantics:
- **Pref flip** — `prefs.putBoolean("first_launch", false)` (same `SharedPrefsHelper` key, same value).
- **Pop target** — `popUpTo(navController.graph.startDestinationId) { inclusive = true }` (same Welcome→Theme→Sources→RepoSettings back-stack clear).
- **Destination** — `Screen.Library` (same).
- **`launchSingleTop`** — `true` (same — prevents duplicate Library entry if any back-stack edge case re-enters).

Same caller graph:
- `SourcesScreenRoute.kt:59` (onboarding chain) — `safeNavigate(Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true))`. Now renders rework Sources screen WITH the Finish button.
- `HomeScreenRoute.kt:193` (in-settings entry from Home) — `safeNavigate(Screen.RepoSettings(false))`. Now renders rework Sources screen WITHOUT the Finish button (`onFinish = null`).

Route-arg shape (`data class RepoSettings(val isFirstOpen: Boolean = false)`) and route key (`Screen.RepoSettings`) are unchanged.

### §123.4 Pre-conditions met by the three §84.8 deferral closeouts

All three legacy `RepoSettingsScreen` affordances are now ported to the rework `SourcesScreen`:
- **Request-adding-source dialog** — ported by §120 (Phase 7.x.sources.complaint).
- **"Upcoming Languages" info card** — ported by §121 (Phase 7.x.sources.complaint.infocard).
- **Onboarding "Finish" button** — ported by §122 (Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingfinish), surfaced via `SourcesScreen`'s `onFinish: (() -> Unit)?` parameter.

This slice (§123) wires the third affordance to its caller's nav decisions. With the swap in place, the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt` composable + its `RepoSettingsViewModel` + the `RepoToggleItem` / `LanguageToggle` helpers + the `RepoFeedbackViewModel` are no longer user-reachable through any nav route. They stay on disk until **Phase 9.x route-swap retirement sweep** removes them in a coordinated multi-screen deletion commit.

### §123.5 Back-press delta vs the legacy adapter

The legacy adapter passed `onBackPress = { navController.safePopBackStack() }` to the legacy `RepoSettingsScreen`. `safePopBackStack` is a defensive helper that pops if the back stack has frames and otherwise navigates to `Screen.Library` — a belt-and-suspenders fallback.

The rework `SourcesScreen` does NOT accept an `onBackPress` parameter (see [`SourcesScreen.kt:124-129`](./ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/sources/SourcesScreen.kt)). It has no top-bar nav icon and no `BackHandler`, so back-press is handled entirely by the system / Compose nav's default back behavior.

**Net delta**: In normal use, the defensive fallback was unreachable — the `Screen.RepoSettings` route is only entered from `Screen.Sources` (onboarding) or `Screen.Home` (in-settings entry), both of which leave the route's parent on the stack. We have no documented incident driving `safePopBackStack`'s inclusion at this route. The simplification is acceptable.

### §123.6 Why the swap lives in the route adapter, not in `:ui` or `App.kt`

Same posture as `SourcesReworkScreenRoute` / `LibraryReworkScreenRoute` / `SettingsReworkScreenRoute`:
- `:ui` deliberately depends on `:presentation` (which knows the VM) but NOT on `androidx.navigation` (which is `:composeApp`-level wiring). The onboarding-chain nav decisions (pref flip, popUpTo, launchSingleTop) MUST live in `:composeApp`, not in `:ui`. The route adapter is the right home.
- `App.kt`'s `composable<Screen.RepoSettings>` block calls `RepoSettingsScreenRoute(navController, backStackEntry)` and is render-target-agnostic — it doesn't need to change when the adapter's render target swaps. Keeping App.kt out of the diff means the route inventory in App.kt stays a stable index of nav entries; only the adapter file owns the per-route render decision.

### §123.7 Layer-by-layer surface deltas

- `:domain` — UNCHANGED. Same `SourcesRepository` interface, same use cases.
- `:data` — UNCHANGED. Same `SourcesRepositoryImpl` strangler-fig wrapper.
- `:presentation` — UNCHANGED. Same `SourcesViewModel` / `SourcesState` / `SourcesIntent` / `SourcesEffect` MVI surface.
- `:ui` — UNCHANGED. Same `SourcesScreen(viewModel, modifier, onFinish)` signature (the `onFinish` parameter shipped in §122 was already present at swap time).
- `:composeApp` — **1 file modified**: `RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt` (render body + imports + KDoc). `App.kt`, `Screen.kt`, `SourcesScreenRoute.kt`, `HomeScreenRoute.kt`, `SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt`, `SourcesReworkModule.kt` all UNCHANGED.

### §123.8 Files modified

| Path | Lines (before → after) | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt` | 75 → 111 (+36, -33 net code = +3) | Swap render target + extensive KDoc. Net code delta is small (rework body is ~15 lines vs legacy ~12); KDoc grew to ~70 lines explaining swap context, semantics preservation, and Phase 9.x retirement plan. |

That's the entire source commit. Zero deletions across the rest of the codebase (legacy `RepoSettingsScreen.kt` stays on disk pending Phase 9.x).

### §123.9 Build gates

After source commit (`00f4ad1`):
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — green (26s)
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — green (1m 20s)
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — green (1m 24s)
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — green (up-to-date)

iOS framework linking + Xcode + on-device smoke tests deferred to user's Mac. On-device validation checklist for the user's Mac:
- Cold launch with `first_launch = true` → Welcome → Theme → Sources → RepoSettings (now rework Sources screen) → toggle a source / language → Finish button visible → tap Finish → lands on Library, back press doesn't return to wizard.
- Cold launch with `first_launch = false` → Home → Settings → "Sources" row → navigates to `Screen.RepoSettings` (now rework Sources screen) → no Finish button (because `args.isFirstOpen = false`) → system back returns to Settings.

### §123.10 Deferrals

- **Legacy file retirement** — `composeApp/.../features/repo_settings/ui/screens/RepoSettingsScreen.kt`, its `RepoSettingsViewModel`, `RepoToggleItem`, `LanguageToggle`, `RepoFeedbackViewModel` all stay on disk. **Phase 9.x route-swap retirement sweep** removes them in a coordinated multi-screen deletion commit (alongside other retired legacy adapters such as the legacy `LibraryScreen`, `DetailsScreen`, `HistoryScreen`, etc., that have already been route-swapped in prior slices §90-§122).

## §124 — Phase 7.x.statistics.swap — `Screen.Statistics` adapter renders rework `StatisticsScreen`

### §124.0 Amendment to §123.12's next-slice prediction

§123.12 predicted **"Phase 7.x.details.swap — route-swap legacy `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails` to render the rework `DetailsScreen`"** as the next slice. Recon at the start of this slice falsified the prediction:

- The rework `DetailsScreen` (`:ui/.../details/`) backed by `DetailsViewModel` (`:presentation/.../details/`) targets `Screen.MangaDetails` (the **network** manga details route from Home / Search) — NOT `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails` (the **library-saved** manga details route). The two routes carry different args (`mangaUrl + api` for network vs `mangaId: Long` Room PK for library) and the rework's `MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute` reconstructs a `Manga` from network-fetched fields (`title + url + coverUrl + rating + genres`) which has no equivalent in the library-saved row.
- Even the `Screen.MangaDetails` swap (the corrected target) is NOT safe yet — the rework `DetailsScreen` is missing affordances the legacy provides: manga bookmark toggle, "download all chapters" button, "remove bookmark" hint state, WebView fallback for 403s, help video dialog hook, and per-source toast for title-copy. Swapping in the rework now would regress all of these (block-and-ask check (b)).
- The smallest ready route-swap candidate is **`Screen.Statistics`** — pure read-only display, 8 aggregates, rework slice (§111 / Task #238) already mirrored feature parity, both routes already consume the same legacy `:shared` `StatisticsRepository` through the strangler-fig `:data` impl.

This slice (§124) does the Statistics swap. The Details swap is deferred behind a multi-slice affordance-port chain (manga bookmark, download wiring, etc.) that's its own project.

### §124.1 Strategy

Same option-shape as §123: (A) modify `App.kt`'s `composable<Screen.Statistics>` block; (B) rewrite the route adapter `StatisticsScreenRoute.kt`; (C) delete the adapter file and inline into `App.kt`. **Chosen: B** — single-file source commit, all rationale co-located in the route adapter's KDoc, function signature unchanged means App.kt + Screen.kt + the caller in legacy `SettingsScreen.kt` need ZERO modification.

### §124.2 What changed in `StatisticsScreenRoute.kt`

**Imports dropped:**
- `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.statistics.ui.screens.StatisticsScreen` (legacy composable)
- `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.statistics.ui.viewmodel.StatisticsViewModel` (legacy VM, 8 separate StateFlows)
- `me.manga.kira.navigation.safePopBackStack`
- `androidx.compose.runtime.collectAsState` / `getValue` (no longer needed; rework screen owns the `collectAsState` internally)

**Imports added:**
- `me.manga.kira.presentation.statistics.StatisticsViewModel` (rework MVI VM, single `StateFlow<StatisticsState>`)
- `me.manga.kira.ui.statistics.StatisticsScreen` (rework composable)

**Render body** — legacy unwrapped 8 individual `StateFlow`s into `collectAsState()` properties and passed them to `StatisticsScreen(inLibrary = ..., readDuration = ..., ..., onBack = { navController.safePopBackStack() })`. Rework body becomes:

```kotlin
val viewModel: StatisticsViewModel = koinViewModel()
StatisticsScreen(viewModel = viewModel)
```

VM resolution swaps from `koinViewModel<legacy StatisticsViewModel>()` to `koinViewModel<rework StatisticsViewModel>()`. Koin binding for the rework VM lives in `statisticsReworkModule` (Task #238 / §111).

The `navController` and `backStackEntry` parameters are kept on the function signature for parity with sibling route adapters but marked `@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER")` — same posture as the existing `StatisticsReworkScreenRoute`. Statistics is a terminal display with no outbound nav, so the controller / entry are unused.

- **Underlying data source** — both legacy and rework consume the same legacy `:shared` `StatisticsRepository`'s 8 aggregate flows (the rework via the `:data` strangler-fig wrapper `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl`). For the same user data, the 8 numbers MUST match across the two routes.

The legacy adapter passed `onBack = { navController.safePopBackStack() }` to the legacy `StatisticsScreen`. The rework `StatisticsScreen`'s `TopAppBar` has no `navigationIcon` — relies on system back. The `safePopBackStack` defensive fallback (pop to Library if back stack is empty) is dropped.

Same posture and same justification as §123:

Rewrite `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/HistoryScreenRoute.kt` so the legacy `Screen.History` route entry renders the architecture-rework `:ui/.../history/HistoryScreen` + `:presentation/.../history/HistoryViewModel` instead of the legacy `:composeApp/.../features/history/ui/screens/HistoryScreen.kt` + legacy `HistoryViewModel`. §124.11 chose **Phase 7.x.about.swap** as the next slice. This-slice recon disconfirmed it: the rework About screen (`:ui/.../about/AboutScreen.kt`) deliberately omits the legacy About's `SocialMediaRow` (6 outbound social-media buttons — Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Discord, Website). The rework KDoc lines 60-66 explicitly note: *"Pulling the extended icon set in for one row would balloon the binary; the social media row lifts in a follow-on slice once the brand-icons are vendored as `:ui`-local `ImageVector` definitions."* Swapping now would remove 5 user-reachable outbound links (Discord button is a no-op stub aside) — block-and-ask check (b) "observable behaviour change". Same posture as §123.12's deferred Details swap. Phase 7.x.about.swap defers behind a future `Phase 7.x.about.socialmedia` slice that ports the 6-button row + the 3 ImageVector files (`Discord.kt`, `X.kt`, and the `Facebook` standard icon already in `material-icons`) + the 3 drawable resources (`ic_instagram`, `ic_whatsapp`, `earth_svgrepo_com`) into the `:ui` module.

Phase 7.x.history.swap is the next ready candidate. The rework History slice (Task #239) shipped full affordance parity — see §125.3.

### §125.3 Affordance parity vs the legacy adapter

Read both adapters to verify parity before swap:
- **Legacy `HistoryScreenRoute.kt`** (pre-swap) passed 4 callbacks to the legacy screen: `onMangaClick` (to `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)`), `onChapterClick` (to `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment(...)`), `onDeleteHistory(it)` (per-row delete), `onDeleteAllHistory()` (top-bar clear-all). Plus the legacy VM exposed a `uiState: StateFlow<HistoryUiState>`.
- **Rework `:ui/.../history/HistoryScreen`** accepts `(viewModel: HistoryViewModel, onNavigateToDetails: (api, mangaUrl) -> Unit, onNavigateToReader: (HistoryEntry) -> Unit, modifier)`. Per-row delete + top-bar clear-all are wired internally via `HistoryIntent.OnDeleteEntry(entry)` + `HistoryIntent.OnDeleteAll` dispatched by the screen's TextButtons; the route does not need to thread those as explicit callbacks. Effects (`HistoryEffect.NavigateToDetails` / `NavigateToReader`) are collected internally and forwarded through the two nav callbacks.

Field-for-field nav-arg mapping for `onChapterClick` to `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment` is identical to the legacy adapter's lambda (verified line-by-line). Specifically `chapterId = entry.id` (entry's `id` field doubles as the legacy nav arg `chapterId`) and `chapterNumber = entry.chapterTitle` (the legacy quirk where the row's "chapter title" field is reused as the nav arg's `chapterNumber`). These shape quirks are preserved verbatim until Phase 9.x cleanly redesigns the reader nav surface.

### §125.4 Visual delta (no affordance loss)

- **Icons**: legacy uses `compose.materialIconsExtended` (`.filled.DeleteForever` for clear-all, `.outlined.Delete` for per-row). Rework substitutes labelled `TextButton`s — same icon-free posture as the rework Library / Statistics / Details / Reader screens. Phase 10's i18n + icon-strategy decision lifts both consumers in one pass.
- **Layout shape**: top bar with title + clear-all action, scrolling list with date group headers (Today / Yesterday / N days ago / MMM d, yyyy), each row showing a cover thumbnail + manga title + chapter title + relative-date subtitle + delete action — matches verbatim between rework and legacy.
- **Empty state**: rework renders "No reading history yet" centered; legacy renders a similar placeholder. Same observable empty behaviour.
- **Design tokens**: rework uses `LocalSpacing` + Material 3 directly; legacy uses ad-hoc `.dp` literals + `Color.Gray.copy(...)`. Rework's tokens cascade from the parent NavHost's Material theme; net observable change is slight visual styling drift within the design system, not a behaviour change.

Every legacy clickable affordance has a labelled rework counterpart. No SocialMediaRow-equivalent dead spot in this screen.

### §125.5 Back-press posture

Legacy `HistoryScreenRoute` passed no `onBack` to the legacy screen — History is a bottom-nav tab destination, not a pushed entry, so back is handled by the parent NavHost / bottom-nav state. The rework `HistoryScreen`'s `TopAppBar` has no `navigationIcon` for the same reason. Zero delta in observable back-press behaviour. The defensive `safePopBackStack` fallback that other rework swaps dropped (§123.4 / §124.4) wasn't present in the legacy History adapter either — nothing to drop here.

### §125.6 Layer-boundary preservation

Same posture as §123 / §124 and the other rework-screen adapters. `:ui` deliberately does NOT depend on `androidx.navigation` (which is `:composeApp`-level wiring); the rework `HistoryScreen` exposes generic `(api: String, mangaUrl: String) -> Unit` and `(HistoryEntry) -> Unit` callbacks so the screen stays nav-host-agnostic. The route adapter at this layer threads the actual `navController.safeNavigate(...)` calls.

### §125.7 Koin lifecycles

The `HistoryViewModel` resolved here via `koinViewModel()` and the one resolved by `HistoryReworkScreenRoute` are scoped to their respective `NavBackStackEntry` (the `ViewModelStoreOwner` integration provided by `androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose`). So even though both routes ultimately render the same screen and rely on the same Koin binding, each route's VM instance is independent. The underlying repository (`me.manga.kira.domain.repository.HistoryRepository` — `single`-scoped via `historyReworkModule`) is shared across both, so the persisted state is identical across the two routes; any deletion on either route surfaces on the other through the upstream `Flow` re-emit.

| `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/HistoryScreenRoute.kt` | 66 to 146 (+80, -8 net code = +72 mostly KDoc) | Swap render target + amended KDoc. Net code delta is small (rework body adds a `koinViewModel()` resolution + the two callbacks pass through unchanged); KDoc grew to ~106 lines documenting swap context, semantics preservation, the §124.11 about-swap deferral correction, affordance parity table, and layer-boundary rationale. |
