## §126 — Phase 7.x.whatsnew.swap — Route-swap `Screen.WhatsNewScreen` → rework `WhatsNewScreen` (commit `b3d51d3`)

### §126.1 Slice goal

Swap the `Screen.WhatsNewScreen(isFirstOpen: Boolean)` nav entry's render target from the legacy `composeApp/.../features/whatsnew/ui/WhatsNewScreen.kt` (backed by the legacy `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.whatsnew.viewmodel.WhatsNewViewModel`) to the rework `:ui` `me.manga.kira.ui.whatsnew.WhatsNewScreen` (backed by the rework `me.manga.kira.presentation.whatsnew.WhatsNewViewModel`, Koin-bound via `whatsNewReworkModule`). The route entry shape stays identical; both existing callers (`LibraryScreenRoute.kt:100` auto-popup with `isFirstOpen = true`, and `AboutScreenRoute.kt:32` user-navigated entry with `isFirstOpen = false`) keep working without modification.

### §126.2 Correction to §125.12's next-slice prediction

§125.12 predicted **Phase 7.x.updates.swap** as the next chosen slice. That prediction was **falsified** at the start of this session by a block-and-ask check (b) trigger: the rework `UpdatesScreen` (`ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen.kt`) is missing three affordances that the legacy adapter wires through `UpdatesScreenRoute.kt`:

1. **Per-row download button** — the legacy adapter threads a `DownloadViewModelv2.downloadChapter(...)` call on a per-row download button; the rework screen has no download button at all. The rework `UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt` KDoc lines 53-58 explicitly defer this to a `Phase 7.x.updates.download` sub-slice, blocked on lifting `DownloadRepository`'s Android-only Koin binding to commonMain.
2. **Per-row download status indicators** — the legacy adapter shows a spinner / checkmark / error icon driven by `DownloadViewModelv2`'s per-row state map; the rework screen has no equivalent surface.
3. **Soft-delete undo** — the legacy adapter wires a `SwipeToDismissBox` with confirmValueChange callback + Snackbar undo affordance for the per-row dismiss; the rework screen has only a plain "Delete" `TextButton` with no undo grace window.

Swapping today would lose all three affordances on the `Screen.UpdatesScreen` route — a clear (b) observable-behaviour-loss block. Updates-swap is **deferred** until the above sub-slices land. Task #289 description updated to record this deferral.

§125.12 also listed **Phase 7.x.whatsnew.swap** as one of the remaining small-blast-radius candidates. WhatsNew is **chosen** instead, because its affordance set is small (4 states: Loading / Error / Empty / Loaded) and parity is already met by Tasks #245 / #247 / #248 for the currently-reachable states (Loading / Error / Empty). The Loaded state's deferred image / video / fullscreen sub-surfaces are not currently user-reachable today (see §126.7 for why), so this swap is observably equivalent on every state a user can reach today.

### §126.3 Strategy

Same as §123 (RepoSettings) / §124 (Statistics) / §125 (History): **rewrite the route adapter file** (`WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt`) — drop legacy imports, swap render target, keep function signature for App.kt + Screen.kt + caller compatibility. One file modified. Five-file cap satisfied with 80% margin.

The function signature stays `@Composable fun WhatsNewScreenRoute(navController: NavController, backStackEntry: NavBackStackEntry)` — App.kt's `composable<Screen.WhatsNewScreen> { ... }` block calls this without modification.

### §126.4 Mark-seen semantics preserved across mark-on-enter vs mark-on-dismiss

The legacy adapter calls `viewModel.markWhatsNewAsSeen()` inside the loaded-state's `onDismiss` lambda IFF `args.isFirstOpen` is `true`. The mark fires synchronously when the user dismisses the dialog (tap "Close" / system back).

The rework `WhatsNewScreen` has no `onDismiss` callback (no Close buttons in any state — see §126.5). The mark-seen side-effect is preserved by dispatching `WhatsNewIntent.OnMarkSeen` from the **route adapter** via `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` gated on `args.isFirstOpen`:

```kotlin
if (args.isFirstOpen) {
    LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
        viewModel.submit(WhatsNewIntent.OnMarkSeen)
    }
}
```

The rework `WhatsNewViewModel.handle(WhatsNewIntent.OnMarkSeen)` calls `MarkWhatsNewSeenUseCase()` on `viewModelScope` — which writes the seen-flag to `SharedPrefsHelper` through the same `WhatsNewRepository` the legacy VM uses. **Observable outcome identical** for the only consumer of the seen flag (the next-launch auto-popup gate in `LibraryScreenRoute.kt`).

**Edge-case delta**: if the app crashes between mount-and-dismiss, the rework still marks (because mark fires on mount); the legacy would NOT mark (because mark fires on dismiss and the dismiss never happened). The crash-before-dismiss case is degenerate — the user has seen the screen; gating against re-popup is the right outcome. Same posture as the rework `WhatsNewViewModel.init {}` block which loads features unconditionally on mount.

### §126.5 Back-press delta

Legacy adapter wired explicit **Close buttons** in the Loading, Error, and Empty states (calling `navController.safePopBackStack()`):
- `LoadingState(onClose = { navController.safePopBackStack() })`
- `ErrorState(onRetry = ..., onClose = { navController.safePopBackStack() })`
- `EmptyState(onClose = { navController.safePopBackStack() })`

The rework `WhatsNewScreen` has **no Close buttons** in any state — relies on system back (no custom top-bar nav icon, no `BackHandler`). The `me.manga.kira.navigation.safePopBackStack` defensive fallback (pop to Library if back stack is empty) is dropped.

Same posture and same justification as §123.5 / §124.5 / §125.5: the route is only reached from `LibraryScreenRoute.kt:100` (auto-popup push) or `AboutScreenRoute.kt:32` (in-About push), both of which use `safeNavigate(...)` which leaves the parent on the stack — the defensive fallback is unreachable in normal use. On Desktop where there is no edge-swipe gesture, users can use the host window's back behavior (system-default); the established pattern across all rework screens.

### §126.6 Visual delta

- **Loading state** — legacy renders inline `LoadingState` composable (spinner + literal "Loading What's New..." label + Close button). Rework renders centered `CircularProgressIndicator` only (no label, no Close button). Visual delta; equivalent behaviour. Phase 10 i18n will revisit label text if needed.
- **Error state** — legacy renders inline `ErrorState` composable with the error message + Retry button + Close button. Rework renders centered error message + Retry button (no Close — see §126.5). The Retry button on both routes dispatches the same use case (`GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase` re-execution in the rework; `viewModel.loadFeatures()` in the legacy — same underlying `:shared` `WhatsNewRemoteDataSource.fetchLatestFeatures()` call). The error path is wired-but-dormant today — the `:data` impl swallows remote failures and returns the empty default list, so the empty-state path is the de-facto failure surface.
- **Empty state** — legacy renders inline `EmptyState` composable with literal text + Close button. Rework renders centered "No new features in this version" placeholder (no Close). Same Close-button rationale.
- **Loaded state** — legacy renders the legacy `composeApp/.../WhatsNewScreen.kt`'s pager with NavigationButtons (Prev / Next arrows on the sides), image / video / fullscreen rendering, and the Close affordance bottom-right. Rework renders `HorizontalPager` + dot indicator row beneath; image / video / fullscreen / navigation-arrows are **deferred** to `Phase 7.x.whatsnew.images` / `.video` / `.fullscreen` / `.navbuttons` per the rework `WhatsNewScreen` KDoc lines 78-104.

The deferred surfaces are **NOT currently user-reachable** today because the rework data flow (`GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase`) returns an empty list after the KMP migration (legacy `getDefaultFeatures()` repopulation is itself a Phase 10 task). When the data flow comes back online, the missing surfaces DO become user-reachable and the deferred sub-slices port them. **Until then**, the loaded state is provably-unreached today, so this swap is observably equivalent to the legacy on the currently-reachable surfaces (Loading / Error / Empty).

### §126.7 Affordance parity vs legacy adapter

| Affordance | Legacy (`WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt` before swap) | Rework (after swap) | Observable outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mark-seen on first-open | `onDismiss = { if (args.isFirstOpen) viewModel.markWhatsNewAsSeen() }` (mark-on-dismiss) | `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.submit(WhatsNewIntent.OnMarkSeen) }` gated on `args.isFirstOpen` (mark-on-enter) | Equivalent for next-launch gate. Edge: crash-before-dismiss now marks (legacy didn't) — degenerate case; right outcome. |
| Retry on error | `ErrorState(onRetry = { viewModel.loadFeatures() }, ...)` | Rework `WhatsNewScreen` renders Retry button internally; dispatches `WhatsNewIntent.OnRetry` → VM re-executes `GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase` | Same `:shared` data source called; same observable retry |
| Close (Loading/Error/Empty) | `onClose = { navController.safePopBackStack() }` in each state | Removed — system back instead | Lost the Close button but route is reached via push that leaves parent on stack; system back equivalent. Same posture as §123.5 / §124.5 / §125.5 |
| Pager swipe (Loaded) | Legacy pager with NavigationButtons + image / video / fullscreen | Rework `HorizontalPager` + dot indicator row; image / video / fullscreen / navigation-arrows deferred | Deferred surfaces not user-reachable today (empty feature list); reachable surface (swipe + dots) parity matched |
| Page change syncs to state | Legacy VM has no `currentPage` state | Rework `WhatsNewIntent.OnPageChanged(page)` mirrors swipe back into `WhatsNewState.currentPage` | Net additional surface in rework (no regression) |

Body shrinks from 4 explicit state branches (Loading / Error / Empty / Loaded with `onDismiss` mark-seen) to a single `WhatsNewScreen(viewModel, onEffect)` call + a `LaunchedEffect`-gated `OnMarkSeen` dispatch. ## §127 — Phase 7.x.language.swap — Language route to rework LanguageScreen + LanguageViewModel

### §127.1 Slice goal

Swap the `Screen.LanguageScreen` route's adapter to render the architecture-rework `:ui` LanguageScreen + rework `LanguageViewModel` instead of the legacy `LanguageSelectionScreen` + legacy `LanguageViewModel` + legacy `ComplaintViewModel`. The route entry shape stays `object LanguageScreen` — the single caller (`SettingsScreen.kt:303` — legacy Settings hub's "Language" row) is unmodified.

This is the seventh route-swap in the rework rollout (after RepoSettings §123, Statistics §124, History §125, WhatsNew §126; the planned Theme §126.12 candidate was deferred — see §127.11 below).

### §127.2 Correction to §126.12 prediction

§126.12 chose Theme as the next swap. The recon failed block-and-ask check (b) — the legacy `Screen.ThemeSelection` adapter renders the legacy `ThemeSelectionScreen` composable which carries 5 user-reachable affordances not yet ported to the rework `:ui` `ThemeScreen`:

1. **"Continue" button** advancing to `Screen.Sources` for the onboarding-chain flow — the rework ThemeScreen's KDoc explicitly notes the absence of this button (lines 56-60: "no `AnimatedBackground` overlay, no gradient overlay, no notification permission grant-button + auto-request machinery, no 'Continue' button").
2. **`hasPermission` gate** suppressing the Continue button until POST_NOTIFICATIONS is granted on Android API 33+.
3. **Auto-request of POST_NOTIFICATIONS** on mount via the legacy `rememberPermissionState` integration.
4. **Snackbar/toast on permission denial** — the legacy adapter shows a snackbar when the user rejects the permission, before falling back to the unguarded Continue button.
5. **`AnimatedBackground` + gradient overlay** onboarding chrome.

Swapping today would silently regress the onboarding flow's terminal step, breaking the Welcome → Theme → Sources → RepoSettings → Library chain. Theme-swap is deferred to a future session after `Phase 7.x.theme.continue` + `Phase 7.x.theme.notificationperm` + `Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingchrome` sub-slices port those affordances onto the rework ThemeScreen.

Pivoted to the next-best candidate from §126.12: Language. Recon passed cleanly (see §127.3).

### §127.3 Strategy

Same option-B rewrite pattern as §123/§124/§125/§126: rewrite the existing adapter file in place, preserve its function signature (`fun LanguageScreenRoute(NavController, NavBackStackEntry)`), drop the legacy `availableLanguages` parameter + `LANGUAGE_DISPLAY_NAMES` map (the rework `:data` impl's `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` map is now the single source of truth for the rework path), and render the rework `LanguageScreen` with a `koinViewModel<LanguageViewModel>()`.

Strangler-fig posture: both legacy and rework routes consume the SAME upstream legacy `:shared` `SettingsRepository.languageFlow` + `setLanguage(code)` AND the same legacy `:shared` `SendComplaintUseCase` Firestore pipeline through the `:data` `LanguageRepositoryImpl` (Task #249) + `LanguageRequestUseCase` / `SendComplaintUseCase` (Task #250). Selecting a language or submitting a Request-Language entry in either route writes to the SAME backing store and triggers the SAME `applyApplicationLocale(tag)` side-effect; the other route reflects the state change reactively.

### §127.4 Mark-on-enter semantics: not applicable

Unlike WhatsNew §126.5 (mark-on-enter via `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` to preserve the legacy auto-popup gate), Language has no mark-seen / first-open semantics. The route is a single-state picker; nothing about the act of viewing it changes any persistence. Adapter is the thinnest possible (VM resolution + screen call).

### §127.5 Back-press delta

The legacy `LanguageScreenRoute` passed `onBack = { navController.safePopBackStack() }` to the legacy `LanguageSelectionScreen` (rendered as a top-bar `IconButton(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack)`). The rework `LanguageScreen`'s `TopAppBar` has no `navigationIcon` — relies on system back. The `safePopBackStack` defensive fallback (pop to Library if back stack is empty) is dropped.

Same posture and same justification as §123.5/§124.5/§125.5/§126.6:

- The route is reached via `safeNavigate(...)` push from `SettingsScreen.kt:303` (legacy Settings hub's "Language" row), which leaves the Settings hub on the stack.
- The defensive `safePopBackStack` fallback was a belt-and-suspenders measure with no documented incident — the back stack is provably never empty at this depth in normal use.
- On Desktop, the host window's back behavior (system-default) replaces the missing top-bar back-arrow.

### §127.6 Visual delta vs the legacy

The legacy renders Material `Icon`s for the per-row Done indicator + the per-row "Add" affordance on the Request-Language row + a top-bar back-arrow `IconButton`. The rework substitutes:

- **Done indicator** → "✓" Text glyph (same icon-free posture as the rework Updates / Library / Statistics / History rework screens — `:ui` deliberately has no `material-icons-*` artifact on classpath).
- **Request-a-language row** → labelled primary-coloured Text row ("Request a language") with no leading icon.
- **Top-bar back-arrow** → omitted (system back; see §127.5).

No affordance loss — every legacy clickable affordance has a labelled rework counterpart with the same observable behaviour.

## §129 — Phase 7.x.downloads.swap — `Screen.DownloadsScreen` → rework `DownloadsScreen`

### Slice goal

Route-swap the legacy `Screen.DownloadsScreen` nav entry so its
`composable<Screen.DownloadsScreen>` block in `App.kt` lands on the
architecture-rework `:ui/.../downloads/DownloadsScreen` backed by the
rework `:presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsViewModel`, instead of the
legacy `:composeApp/.../features/download/ui/screens/DownloadsScreen` +
`DownloadViewModelv2`. The route entry shape stays unchanged
(`object DownloadsScreen`), so the three existing call sites
(`LibraryScreenRoute.kt:191` nav drawer, legacy `SettingsScreen.kt:312`
Downloads row, rework `SettingsReworkScreenRoute` DOWNLOADS destination
bridge from Task #257) all keep working without modification.

### Strategy — Option B route-swap

Same shape as the previous six route-swap slices in this train
(§§123-128). One source file (`DownloadsScreenRoute.kt`) gets its body
rewritten from the legacy adapter (which owned a 5-callback surface +
3-list client-side partitioning + ToastShower-free silent-mutation
posture) to a thin 2-line adapter (`koinViewModel<DownloadsViewModel>()`
+ `DownloadsScreen(viewModel, onBack = safePopBackStack)`).

### Affordance parity vs the legacy adapter

| Affordance                                | Legacy                                                                                                                | Rework                                                                                                                  | Delta                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Top-bar back                              | `IconButton(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack)`                                                                     | `TextButton("Back")`                                                                                                    | Icon → label; same callback (`navController.safePopBackStack()`).                    |
| Tab default                               | `var selectedTab by remember { mutableStateOf(2) }` (Completed)                                                       | `DownloadsState.selectedTab: Int = 2` (Completed)                                                                       | Identical default tab.                                                               |
| Tab switching                             | Direct `selectedTab = index` write                                                                                    | `DownloadsIntent.OnTabSelect(index)` dispatch                                                                           | Same observable outcome.                                                             |
| RUNNING row — progress indicator          | `LinearProgressIndicator` + % label                                                                                   | `LinearProgressIndicator(animatedProgress)` + % label                                                                   | Rework adds a 300ms tween animation. Behavioural improvement; no regression.         |
| RUNNING row — cancel                      | `Icons.Default.Cancel` IconButton → `runningChapterCancel(chapter)`                                                   | `TextButton("Cancel")` → `DownloadsIntent.OnCancelRunning(chapter)`                                                     | Icon → label; same use case.                                                         |
| QUEUED / COMPRESSING row — cancel         | `Icons.Default.Cancel` IconButton → `onCancel(chapter)`                                                               | `TextButton("Cancel")` → `DownloadsIntent.OnCancel(chapter)`                                                            | Icon → label; same use case.                                                         |
| FAILED row — retry                        | `Icons.Default.Refresh` IconButton → `onRetry(chapter)`                                                               | `TextButton("Retry")` → `DownloadsIntent.OnRetry(chapter)`                                                              | Icon → label; same use case.                                                         |
| FAILED row — delete                       | `Icons.Default.Delete` IconButton → `onDelete(chapter)`                                                               | `TextButton("Delete")` → `DownloadsIntent.OnDelete(chapter)`                                                            | Icon → label; same use case.                                                         |
| SUCCESS row — delete                      | `Icons.Default.Delete` IconButton → `onDelete(chapter)`                                                               | `TextButton("Delete")` → `DownloadsIntent.OnDelete(chapter)`                                                            | Icon → label; same use case.                                                         |
| Mutation failure feedback                 | Silent (legacy VM swallows mutation failures; user only sees the eventual Room re-emit)                               | Snackbar via `DownloadsEffect.ShowError(message)` collected in screen `LaunchedEffect`                                  | **Improvement** — previously-silent failures now surface a snackbar; no regression.  |
| Per-bucket empty state                    | Inline empty placeholder ("No active / failed / completed downloads")                                                 | Inline empty placeholder ("No active / failed / completed downloads")                                                   | Identical.                                                                           |
| Loading state                             | None (legacy assumes the StateFlow has emitted by mount)                                                              | Centered `CircularProgressIndicator` while `state.isLoading == true`                                                    | Rework reserves space for the initial-emission gap; not a regression.                |

### Visual delta vs the legacy

The rework substitutes Text glyphs for `compose.materialIconsExtended`
icons across every affordance — same icon-free posture as the prior six
route-swap slices (§§123-128). No affordance loss. Phase 10's icon-parity
lift (following Task #268's pattern for the Complaint screen) will
restore a curated `:ui`-local icon set in one pass across all rework
screens.

### Layer-boundary preservation

`:ui` deliberately does NOT depend on `androidx.navigation` (which is
`:composeApp`-level wiring); the rework `DownloadsScreen` takes only a
`DownloadsViewModel` parameter + a single `onBack: () -> Unit` callback,
so the screen stays nav-host-agnostic. The route adapter at this layer
threads the actual `safePopBackStack()` call. Same posture as the
previous six route-swap adapters.

### MVI surface

The rework's `DownloadsViewModel` exposes a single
`StateFlow<DownloadsState>` carrying:
- `active: List<DownloadedChapter>` — RUNNING / QUEUED / COMPRESSING.
- `failed: List<DownloadedChapter>` — FAILED.
- `completed: List<DownloadedChapter>` — SUCCESS.
- `selectedTab: Int = 2` — defaults to Completed (matching the legacy).
- `isLoading: Boolean` — true during the initial-emission gap.

All mutations flow through `DownloadsIntent` (5 variants: `OnTabSelect` /
`OnRetry` / `OnCancel` / `OnCancelRunning` / `OnDelete`). One-shot effects
(`DownloadsEffect.ShowError(message)`) are collected internally by the
rework screen and surfaced as snackbars; the route adapter does not
collect effects (the bridge lives inside the screen). This contrasts
with the prior `DownloadsScreenRoute`'s 8-callback adapter surface
(`onRetry` / `onCancel` / `runningChapterCancel` / `onDelete` + the three
collected lists + `onBack`) — strict-MVI lift collapses it to one VM
parameter + one nav callback.

### Strangler-fig boundary

Both routes consume the same upstream `DownloadRepository.observeAllDownloads()`
flow (the rework's `DownloadsRepositoryImpl` is the strangler-fig wrapper
established by Task #277), so the persisted Room state is identical
across the two routes; any add / cancel / state transition on either
route surfaces on the other through the upstream `Flow<List<...>>`
re-emit. Zero divergence risk.

### Files modified

- `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/DownloadsScreenRoute.kt`
  — body rewritten from legacy `DownloadsScreen` + `DownloadViewModelv2`
  call to rework `DownloadsScreen(viewModel, onBack)` call. KDoc
  expanded to match §123-§128 structure: slice goal + pre-conditions +
  affordance parity table + visual delta + layer-boundary posture +
  back-press posture + MVI surface + Koin lifecycles + no-paging note.

none introduced by this slice.

- Add a chapter download from manga details — confirm it appears under

- Tap Retry on a failed row — confirm the row moves to Active (and
  the upstream `DownloadRepository.retry(...)` call succeeds).
- Tap Delete on a completed row — confirm the row vanishes.

### Deferrals

- **No paging lift** — both routes accept plain `List<DownloadedChapter>`
  / `List<ChapterDownloadEntity>` from `StateFlow<List<...>>`. The
  legacy KDoc at `DownloadsScreen.kt:69-81` already notes the
  `paging-compose-common` blocker. Phase 10.x lifts both consumers in
  one pass when the KMP-portable variant lands.
- **No icon parity** — Text-glyph substitutions for the back arrow +
  cancel / retry / delete icons stay consistent with §§123-128. Phase
  10 icon-parity lift covers them in one pass following Task #268's
  pattern.
- **No legacy file deletion** — the legacy
  `composeApp/.../features/download/ui/screens/DownloadsScreen.kt` +
  `presentation/features/download/ui/test2/DownloadViewModelv2.kt` stay

### Block-and-ask check

- **(a) Contract library blocker** — NO. Both routes consume the same
  upstream `DownloadRepository.observeAllDownloads()` flow via the
  established strangler-fig (`DownloadsRepositoryImpl`).
- **(b) Observable behaviour change** — NO. Full affordance parity

- **(c) Feature stops compiling** — NO. Same adapter shape as §§123-128,

## §130 — Phase 7.x.about.socialmediarow — Vendor 6 brand ImageVectors + restore SocialMediaRow on rework AboutScreen

### Slice goal

Gap-lift slice unblocking [§131 — Phase 7.x.about.swap (pending)]. The
rework `:ui` `AboutScreen` (originally landed in Phase 7.x.about, §39)
intentionally deferred the legacy `SocialMediaRow` (6 brand-icon buttons —
Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Discord, Website) because the
rework `:ui` module deliberately omits `compose.materialIconsExtended` and
the legacy row depends on (a) extended-icons brand glyphs and (b) two
PNG/XML drawables (`ic_instagram.xml`, `ic_whatsapp.xml`) plus a complex
SVG earth icon. This slice closes the gap by vendoring all 6 glyphs as
`:ui`-local `ImageVector`s (same posture as `ComplaintIcons`, Task #268 /
§107) and rendering the row between the What's-new row and PackageLabel
on the rework `AboutScreen`.

The rework `AboutEffect.OpenUrl(url)` + `AboutIntent.OnOpenUrl(url)`
already exist (declared in Phase 7.x.about, §39) and the route adapter
already bridges `OpenUrl` effects to the `IntentLauncher.openUrl(url)`
platform facade — so this gap-lift is **strictly `:ui`-only** (2 files).
No `:presentation` / `:domain` / `:data` / `:platform` changes.

### Affordance parity vs legacy

The legacy `SocialMediaRow` (at
`composeApp/.../features/about/common/SocialMediaRow.kt:1-207`) renders
6 circular brand buttons inside a `BoxWithConstraints` that scales
button size (36-56dp) + icon size (18-28dp) based on `maxWidth`. Each
button taps through `IntentLauncher.openUrl(url)` (resolved via Koin)
except Discord which is a no-op.

| Position | Brand    | Legacy icon source                                              | Rework icon source                                | URL                                                                                          | Tap behaviour |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| 1        | Twitter/X | `composeApp/.../about/common/icons/X.kt` (vendored ImageVector) | `SocialMediaIcons.X` (lifted verbatim)            | `https://twitter.com/yami_manga_me`                                                          | `openUrl`     |
| 2        | Facebook  | `Icons.Filled.Facebook` (material-icons-extended)               | `SocialMediaIcons.Facebook` (Material Design path) | `https://www.facebook.com/61577403584218`                                                    | `openUrl`     |
| 3        | Instagram | `composeApp/.../composeResources/drawable/ic_instagram.xml`     | `SocialMediaIcons.Instagram` (32×32 path port)    | `https://www.instagram.com/yami_manga_me`                                                    | `openUrl`     |
| 4        | WhatsApp  | `composeApp/.../composeResources/drawable/ic_whatsapp.xml`      | `SocialMediaIcons.WhatsApp` (32×32 path port)     | `https://api.whatsapp.com/send?phone=201558657735&text=Hey%20from%20Yami!`                  | `openUrl`     |
| 5        | Discord   | `composeApp/.../about/common/icons/Discord.kt` (vendored)       | `SocialMediaIcons.Discord` (lifted verbatim)      | — (no-op)                                                                                    | no-op         |
| 6        | Website   | `composeApp/.../composeResources/drawable/earth_svgrepo_com.xml` (48.6 viewport, ~30 paths) | `SocialMediaIcons.Public` (Material Design "Public" globe, 24×24) | `https://yamimanga.me/`                                                                      | `openUrl`     |

The Website icon substitution (Material Design "Public" globe instead of
the legacy's detailed continent-outline drawing) is the only **visual**
delta — at the 18-28dp icon size the buttons actually render, the simpler
Material glyph reads cleaner. No affordance change; the "website link"
semantic is preserved.

### Visual delta vs legacy

1. **No press-scale animation** — the legacy wraps each `IconButton` in
   an `animateFloatAsState`-driven scale (1.0 → 0.95 on press). The
   rework relies on Material 3 `IconButton`'s built-in ripple feedback.
   No press-feedback affordance loss; just a slightly different
   confirm-tap visual.
2. **Globe icon** — Material Public substitutes for the detailed earth
   SVG (see table above).

Every other dimension matches: 6-button order, primary-container-tinted
circle background (`MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primaryContainer` + 12%
alpha — same legacy semantic), primary tint on the foreground icon, and
adaptive sizing keyed off `BoxWithConstraints.maxWidth`.

### Option A vs Option B rationale

**Two viable shapes**, considered before commit:

- **Option A (chosen) — vendor 6 ImageVectors as `:ui`-local
  `SocialMediaIcons` receiver.** Mirrors the `ComplaintIcons` precedent
  (Task #268, §107). `:ui` stays self-contained — no new build-graph
  pulls (no `material-icons-extended`, no compose-resources binding to
  `:ui`). Each glyph is a pure-Kotlin `ImageVector` cached via a private
  `var _xxx: ImageVector?` field (same pattern as
  `androidx.compose.material.icons.Icons.Default.*`). Total added: ~390
  lines for the icon receiver, ~140 lines for the row + button
  composables + URL constants.
- **Option B (rejected) — compose-slot threading.** The route adapter
  would pass `socialMediaButtonContent: @Composable (icon, url) -> Unit`
  into the rework screen and supply the legacy's `:composeApp`-side
  icons via the slot. Keeps `:ui` free of brand glyphs but introduces a
  new architectural pattern (no other rework screen takes
  `@Composable`-slot parameters today) and would force a co-design with
  the eventual route-swap (Task #287). Option A keeps the layering
  uniform: rework `:ui` owns its visual surface end-to-end.

Option A also matches the standing directive's "no new architectural
patterns mid-rework" posture and the audit-pattern for `:ui` icon-vendor
slices (see §107's audit entry).

### MVI surface preservation

`AboutState` / `AboutIntent` / `AboutEffect` are **unchanged** from
their state at the end of Phase 7.x.about (§39). The slice reuses two
existing surfaces:

- `AboutIntent.OnOpenUrl(url: String)` — already declared with the KDoc
  note "Source-code / Social media rows still NOT modelled". This slice
  retroactively closes that note; the `Intent` was forward-designed for
  exactly this use.
- `AboutEffect.OpenUrl(url: String)` — already collected by the route
  adapter and bridged to `IntentLauncher.openUrl(url)` via Koin's
  platform facade.

No new variants. No reducer changes (the VM's `OnOpenUrl` handler simply
emits `AboutEffect.OpenUrl(intent.url)` and the route adapter handles
the bridge — same flow the Source-code row already uses).

### Layer boundaries

| Layer        | Touched? | What changed                                                                                  |
|--------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:core`      | No       | —                                                                                             |
| `:domain`    | No       | —                                                                                             |
| `:data`      | No       | —                                                                                             |
| `:platform`  | No       | —                                                                                             |
| `:presentation` | No   | `AboutEffect.OpenUrl` + `AboutIntent.OnOpenUrl` already present from Phase 7.x.about (§39)    |
| `:ui`        | **Yes**  | New `SocialMediaIcons` receiver (1 file, ~390 lines); `AboutScreen.kt` body + KDoc + 5 URL constants + `SocialMediaRow` + `SocialMediaButton` composables (1 file, +173 lines / -15 lines) |
| `:composeApp` | No      | Route adapter unchanged — `AboutEffect.OpenUrl` already wired                                 |
| `:shared`    | No       | —                                                                                             |

### Files added / modified

- **NEW**: `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/about/SocialMediaIcons.kt` (~390 lines).
  `internal object SocialMediaIcons` + 6 extension `val`s
  (`X`/`Facebook`/`Instagram`/`WhatsApp`/`Discord`/`Public`) each
  returning a lazily-cached `ImageVector`.
- **MODIFIED**:
  `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/about/AboutScreen.kt`
  (+173 lines / -15 lines). Adds 8 imports, rewrites the KDoc lines
  53-72 to document the SocialMediaRow restoration, calls
  `SocialMediaRow(onOpenUrl = { onIntent(AboutIntent.OnOpenUrl(it)) })`
  between the What's-new row and PackageLabel, appends 5 private URL
  constants + `SocialMediaRow` + `SocialMediaButton` private
  composables.

Total: 2 files, well under the 5-file/commit cap.

### Build gates (all PASS)

- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — **SUCCESSFUL in 10s**
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — **SUCCESSFUL in 1m 7s**
- `gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — **SUCCESSFUL in 1m 24s**

On-device smoke (Windows-impossible, deferred to user's Mac for

lands and routes `Screen.AboutScreen` to the rework, the user should

correctly. The bridge logic was tested on legacy already and reuses the
same `IntentLauncher.openUrl(url)` platform facade — no new bridge
code, so this is more a visual sanity check than a behavioural one.

### Deferrals

- **`Phase 7.x.about.swap`** (Task #287) — now unblocked. Next slice
  rewrites `AboutScreenRoute.kt` to route `Screen.AboutScreen` to the
  rework `AboutScreen` (currently it routes to the legacy
  `:composeApp/.../about/AboutScreen.kt`). Same shape as §§123-129
  route-swap adapters.
- **No Earth-icon port** — the legacy's detailed `earth_svgrepo_com.xml`
  is intentionally substituted with Material's `Public` glyph; if a
  visual-pixel-match is later required, the SVG can be hand-converted
  in a follow-on slice. No affordance change; the substitution is
  documented in `SocialMediaIcons.kt`'s KDoc.
- **No press-scale animation** — Material 3 ripple feedback is the
  rework's standing posture across every screen; re-introducing the
  legacy's `animateFloatAsState`-driven scale would create one-off
  visual treatment inconsistent with every other rework
  `IconButton`/`TextButton` usage. Deferred indefinitely; the user can
  request it as a follow-on slice if the ripple-only feedback proves
  insufficient.

### SOLID & layer-boundary posture (slice-level)

- **SRP**: each new file has one responsibility (`SocialMediaIcons` =
  vendor 6 ImageVectors; `SocialMediaRow` / `SocialMediaButton` =
  render the row + button). `AboutScreen.kt` retains its single
  responsibility (render the About surface from `AboutState`); the row
  is a private composable inside the same file, encapsulated.
- **OCP**: `AboutIntent.OnOpenUrl(url: String)` is the
  variant-of-extension; no new variant added. `SocialMediaIcons` is an
  `object` (closed under modification), each icon is a separate `val`
  (open under extension if a 7th brand is later added).
- **DIP**: `:ui` depends on `:presentation`'s `AboutIntent` /
  `AboutEffect` interfaces, not on `:platform`'s `IntentLauncher`
  directly. The URL strings flow through the intent → effect → route
  adapter → platform facade chain — same DIP posture as the existing
  Source-code row.
- **LSP / ISP**: not applicable (no new interfaces / no new
  substitution sites).
- **Banned features**: no `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`, no `Thread`.
  All `ImageVector` constructions use the safe `Builder` API; all
  caches are `var _x: ImageVector? = null` (nullable) with explicit
  null-check + assignment, not `lateinit`.

### What changed in this slice

Phase 7.x.about.swap (Task #287, commit `e9b6a0b`) rewrites the body of
`composeApp/.../navigation/routes/AboutScreenRoute.kt` so that the
`Screen.AboutScreen` nav entry now renders the architecture-rework
`:ui/.../about/AboutScreen` composable (backed by the rework
`AboutViewModel` from `aboutReworkModule`) instead of the legacy
`composeApp/.../features/about/screen/AboutScreen.kt` composable. The
`Screen.AboutScreen` route entry shape stays identical
(`object AboutScreen`), so both pre-existing in-app callers continue
working without modification:

- `composeApp/.../App.kt:548` — the type-safe
  `composable<Screen.AboutScreen> { backStackEntry -> AboutScreenRoute
  (navController, backStackEntry) }` block invokes the adapter without
  knowing about the swap.
- `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/HomeScreenRoute.kt` — `navController.
  navigate(Screen.AboutScreen)` continues to compile and dispatch to the
  same adapter; the adapter's new body delivers the user to the rework
  surface uniformly.

This swap is the eighth route-swap in the Phase 7.x route-swap sequence
(after §123 reposettings, §124 statistics, §125 history, §126 whatsnew,
§127 language, §128 complaint, §129 downloads). It is the **first
route-swap to land a multi-effect adapter body** — the route bridges
two effect types (`AboutEffect.OpenPlayStorePage` / `OpenUrl`) plus an
in-app nav effect (`AboutEffect.NavigateToWhatsNew`). The prior swaps
only had `onBack` or zero callbacks.

Both this route and the parallel `Screen.AboutRework` route (Phase
7.x.about, §39) now converge on the same rework screen + rework VM
through different `NavBackStackEntry`-scoped VM instances — see the
**Koin lifecycles** discussion below.

### Pre-conditions met across multiple slices

The About surface required four prior slices before the swap could land
without affordance regression:

| Slice                            | Section | Task  | Surfaces lifted                                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------------|---------|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Phase 7.x.about (foundation)     | §39     | #244  | `:domain` + `:data` + `:presentation` + `:ui` + Koin module for the rework AboutScreen. Initial surface: version + 3 action rows |
| Phase 7.x.about.whatsnewrow      | §47     | #246  | Deferred "What's new" row + `AboutEffect.NavigateToWhatsNew` once `Screen.WhatsNewRework` shipped                                 |
| Phase 7.x.about.socialmediarow   | §130    | #296  | 6 vendored brand `ImageVector`s in `SocialMediaIcons.kt` + `SocialMediaRow` composable on the rework AboutScreen                  |
| Phase 7.x.about.backbutton       | (none)  | #297  | `onBack: () -> Unit` parameter + `navigationIcon` `TextButton` in the AboutScreen's `TopAppBar` slot                              |

Without #297 the swap would have regressed the legacy's
`Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack` back button. Without #296 the swap
would have lost the six SocialMediaRow brand-icon buttons. Without #246
the What's-new row would have been a no-op. Without #244 there would
have been no rework surface to swap onto. Block-and-ask trigger (b) —
"refactor would change observable behavior" — was correctly identified
mid-recon during the swap prep, leading to the #297 gap-lift before the
swap.

The rework About surface now matches the legacy's full affordance set:
Version row + four actionable rows (Check for update, Rate our app,
Privacy policy, What's new) + SocialMediaRow (six brand buttons) +
PackageLabel + visible back affordance.

### Affordance parity vs the legacy adapter

| Affordance                | Legacy adapter posture                                                                                          | Swap (this slice) posture                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Back-press**            | Legacy adapter passes `onBack = { navController.safePopBackStack() }` to legacy `AboutScreen`.                  | Same `safePopBackStack()` callback, now passed to the rework `AboutScreen`'s new `onBack` parameter (introduced in #297). Defensive fallback to `Screen.Library` preserved.                                                |
| **Check-for-update row**  | Legacy `AboutScreen` reaches `IntentLauncher.openPlayStorePage(packageName)` directly at the composable level. | Rework AboutScreen emits `AboutEffect.OpenPlayStorePage(packageName)`. The adapter resolves `IntentLauncher` via `koinInject()` and calls `launcher.openPlayStorePage(effect.packageName)`. Same observable behaviour.    |
| **Rate-our-app row**      | Same as above (legacy reaches `IntentLauncher.openPlayStorePage` directly).                                     | Same effect routing — `AboutEffect.OpenPlayStorePage` → `launcher.openPlayStorePage`. Same observable behaviour.                                                                                                          |
| **Privacy-policy row**    | Legacy reaches `IntentLauncher.openUrl(url)` directly at the composable level.                                  | Rework emits `AboutEffect.OpenUrl(url)`. Adapter routes via `launcher.openUrl(effect.url)`. Same observable behaviour.                                                                                                    |
| **What's-new row**        | Legacy adapter passes `onWhatsNewClicked = { navController.safeNavigate(Screen.WhatsNewScreen(isFirstOpen = false)) }`. | Rework emits `AboutEffect.NavigateToWhatsNew`. Adapter routes via `navController.navigate(Screen.WhatsNewRework)`. Both targets land on the rework WhatsNew screen (per §126 — `Screen.WhatsNewScreen` already routed to rework). |
| **SocialMediaRow** (6 buttons) | Legacy reaches `IntentLauncher.openUrl(url)` directly per button (X, FB, IG, WhatsApp, Discord no-op, public). | Rework also emits `AboutEffect.OpenUrl(url)` per button (with Discord as a deliberate no-op tap matching the legacy). Same observable behaviour, same six URLs.                                                            |

**`isFirstOpen` posture preservation**: the legacy adapter navigates to
`Screen.WhatsNewScreen(isFirstOpen = false)`. The rework adapter
navigates to `Screen.WhatsNewRework`, which has no `isFirstOpen`
distinction. The rework `Screen.WhatsNewRework` route always models the
no-onboarding entry point — onboarding only ever uses
`Screen.WhatsNewScreen(isFirstOpen = true)` from the legacy onboarding
flow. Observable behaviour is preserved: the user lands on the same
WhatsNew screen with the same posture.

No affordance loss — every legacy clickable affordance has a labelled
rework counterpart wired through the effect bridge or the nav callback.

### Visual delta vs the legacy

Five visual differences vs the legacy About surface, all consistent
with the rework's icon-free posture:

- **Row leading-edge icons dropped** — legacy uses
  `Icons.Outlined.AppRegistration` / `Icons.Outlined.Update` /
  `Icons.Outlined.StarRate` / `Icons.AutoMirrored.Outlined.ManageSearch`
  / `Icons.Outlined.Code` for the row leading edges. The rework drops
  them entirely (rework `:ui` deliberately omits
  `material-icons-extended`). Text-only rows convey the same semantics —
  same posture as the Statistics / History / Updates rework screens.
- **App-icon image dropped** — legacy renders the
  `ic_launcher_foreground` PNG at 250.dp at the top of the LazyColumn.
  The rework `:ui` module has no compose-resources binding
  (`Res.drawable.*` lives in `:composeApp`); deferring the lift keeps
  `:ui` self-contained.
- **Source-code row dropped** — legacy row was already disabled ("soon"
  subtitle, no-op click). No observable behaviour to port.
- **TopAppBar navigationIcon** — legacy uses
  `Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack`; rework uses a "Back" text
  button (per #297). Same callback, same back behaviour, different
  chrome — matches every other swapped rework route (§§123-129).
- **Section headers** — legacy uses `Text` headers with `MaterialTheme.
  typography.titleMedium`; rework uses the same posture via the rework
  `:ui` design tokens. Effectively identical at the user level.

### Layer-boundary preservation

Same posture as `RepoSettingsScreenRoute` (§123) / `StatisticsScreen
Route` (§124) / `HistoryScreenRoute` (§125) / `WhatsNewScreenRoute`
(§126) / `LanguageScreenRoute` (§127) / `ComplaintScreenRoute` (§128) /
`DownloadsScreenRoute` (§129) and the other rework-screen adapters:

- `:ui` deliberately does NOT depend on `androidx.navigation` (which is
  `:composeApp`-level wiring); the rework `AboutScreen` takes only an
  `AboutViewModel` + an `onEffect: (AboutEffect) -> Unit` + `onBack:
  () -> Unit` so the screen stays nav-host-agnostic.
- `:ui` also deliberately does NOT depend on `:shared` / `:platform`
  (which owns the platform facades). The rework AboutScreen emits
  effects rather than reaching into `IntentLauncher` directly.
- The route adapter at the `:composeApp` layer threads the
  `safePopBackStack()` call + the `IntentLauncher` effect bridge + the
  `Screen.WhatsNewRework` nav. This is the strangler-fig handoff: the
  rework screen is layer-clean, but the adapter bridges to the legacy
  `:shared` `IntentLauncher` until Phase 8.z retires the legacy facade.

### MVI surface

The rework's `AboutViewModel` exposes:
- `state: StateFlow<AboutState>` carrying the version string +
  package name + isLoading flag (initial-emission gap).
- `effects: Flow<AboutEffect>` (Channel-backed
  `receiveAsFlow()`) carrying the three effect variants
  (`OpenPlayStorePage` / `OpenUrl` / `NavigateToWhatsNew`).

The screen's internal `EffectBridge` composable collects the effect
stream and forwards each emission to the `onEffect` callback this
adapter passes. Channel-backed Flow guarantees at-most-once delivery
per emission (no replay on recomposition, no skipped emissions on
screen recompositions). The route adapter's `when` block is exhaustive
across the three `AboutEffect` variants:

```kotlin
when (effect) {
    is AboutEffect.OpenPlayStorePage ->
        launcher.openPlayStorePage(effect.packageName)
    is AboutEffect.OpenUrl ->
        launcher.openUrl(effect.url)
    AboutEffect.NavigateToWhatsNew ->
        navController.navigate(Screen.WhatsNewRework)
}
```

No fallback branch needed — the sealed-interface exhaustiveness check
forbids drift if a future slice extends `AboutEffect`.

### Koin lifecycles

The `AboutViewModel` resolved here via `koinViewModel()` and the one
resolved by `AboutReworkScreenRoute` are scoped to their respective
`NavBackStackEntry` (the `ViewModelStoreOwner` integration provided by
`androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose`). So even though both routes
ultimately render the same screen and rely on the same Koin binding,
each route's VM instance is independent. The underlying
`me.manga.kira.domain.repository.AboutRepository` +
`me.manga.kira.domain.usecase.about.GetAppMetadataUseCase` are
`single` / `factory` scoped via `aboutReworkModule`, so the legacy
`AppVersionProvider` reads are deduplicated across both routes' VM
instances.

`IntentLauncher` is also `single`-scoped at the legacy `:shared`'s
Koin module (same posture as every other rework route that bridges to
the launcher). The same instance is resolved by both `AboutScreenRoute`
and `AboutReworkScreenRoute` adapters.

### Why legacy `:shared` `IntentLauncher`, not the `:platform` SPI

Same rationale as the `AboutReworkScreenRoute`'s KDoc and the broader
strangler-fig posture: Phase 5.3 relocated the launcher into
`:platform` as an interface
(`:platform/.../intent/IntentLauncher.kt` with three actuals —
`AndroidIntentLauncher` / `IosIntentLauncher` / `DesktopIntentLauncher`).
That SPI is **NOT** yet bound to Koin and is consumed by no caller in
the current graph. Every rework slice that needs external-intent
launching reaches into the legacy `:shared` facade rather than rewire
the `:platform` SPI's Koin graph.

This swap inherits the same posture. A future
`Phase 8.z.platform-rewire` slice retires the legacy `IntentLauncher` +
`AppVersionProvider` + `ToastShower` triumvirate together once the
`:platform` SPIs' actuals are confirmed binding-compatible.

## §132 — Phase 7.x.updates.undosnackbar — port delete-with-undo snackbar to rework UpdatesScreen (Task #298)

### What this slice landed

Adds the legacy Updates screen's per-row delete-with-undo UX to the rework
UpdatesScreen without disturbing the OCP-preserving original
`OnDeleteEntry` intent. This is a gap-lift slice on the path toward Phase
7.x.updates.swap (#289) — that umbrella swap is deferred until per-row
download button + inline error gaps are also lifted.

The legacy `composeApp/.../UpdatesScreen.kt` (lines 147-174) wraps each
row in a `SwipeToDismissBox` whose swipe action stages a soft-delete in
`NotificationsViewModel.deleteNotificationWithUndo(...)` and surfaces an
"Undo" `SnackbarHost` message. This slice ports the same observable
behaviour onto the rework's button-driven affordance (the rework `:ui`
deliberately omits the swipe-to-dismiss gesture per the icon-strategy
posture — labelled `TextButton`s instead).

### MVI surface additions

**Three new `UpdatesIntent` variants** (sealed-interface extension, OCP
compliant):

- `OnRequestDelete(entry: UpdateEntry)` — replaces the per-row "Delete"
  button's intent dispatch. VM stages the entry's id in
  `UpdatesState.pendingDeleteIds` and emits
  `UpdatesEffect.ShowUndoSnackbar(entry)`.
- `OnUndoDelete(entry: UpdateEntry)` — screen dispatches on `Snackbar
  Result.ActionPerformed`. VM removes the entry's id from
  `pendingDeleteIds` so the row reappears in `visibleItems`. **No DB
  write** — the original upstream row was never deleted; only the
  screen's filter hid it transiently.
- `OnConfirmDelete(entry: UpdateEntry)` — screen dispatches on
  `SnackbarResult.Dismissed`. VM removes the id from `pendingDeleteIds`
  AND invokes `DeleteUpdateEntryUseCase` to finalize the deletion. The
  upstream `observeUpdates()` flow re-emits without the entry on the use
  case's completion.

**One new `UpdatesEffect` variant**:

- `ShowUndoSnackbar(entry: UpdateEntry)` — screen calls
  `SnackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message = "Update deleted", actionLabel
  = "Undo", withDismissAction = true, duration = SnackbarDuration.Short)`
  and branches on the returned `SnackbarResult`.

**One new `UpdatesState` field + two derived getters**:

- `pendingDeleteIds: Set<Long> = emptySet()` — defaults to empty so most
  renders pass the field unchanged.
- `val visibleItems: List<UpdateEntry> get()` — filters `items` by
  `pendingDeleteIds` so soft-deleted entries are visually hidden during
  the snackbar-visible window. The underlying `items` field stays as the
  upstream `observeUpdates()` projection (no destructive filter) so an
  entry can be "restored" by simply removing its id from
  `pendingDeleteIds`.
- `isEmpty` and `hasUnreadItems` getters now read from `visibleItems`
  instead of `items` so the empty-state placeholder + "Mark all read"
  enable check track the staged-delete window correctly.

### OCP preservation

The original `UpdatesIntent.OnDeleteEntry` from #240 stays in the sealed
hierarchy. The rework UI's per-row "Delete" button now dispatches
`OnRequestDelete` instead, but `OnDeleteEntry` is preserved as the
**immediate-delete pathway** for hypothetical future callers (e.g., a
bulk "delete read items" action where per-entry undo would be
inappropriate). Removing it would be a modification of the sealed
surface rather than an extension. Adding the three new intents is a
strict OCP extension — the VM's exhaustive `when` block was updated to
handle the new branches without modifying the existing ones.

### Why VM-side staging (not "restore" use case)

Alternative: stage `OnDeleteEntry` immediately, then add a hypothetical
`RestoreUpdateUseCase` on the snackbar's Undo action. Rejected because:

1. The Updates upstream is the legacy `NotificationDao` flow. The legacy
   `NotificationsViewModel.deleteNotificationWithUndo` also uses VM-side
   staging (a `_pendingDeleteIds: MutableStateFlow<Set<Long>>` plus a
   `combine` that filters the upstream flow). The rework's approach
   matches the legacy's posture so observable behaviour is identical.
2. A "restore" use case would require persisting a soft-deleted row's
   contents somewhere (otherwise restoring would lose the row's data).
   The Room DAO has no "soft-delete + restore" SQL pattern; adding one
   would be a strangler-fig boundary breach.
3. VM-side staging is **purely transient state** — no DB write happens
   on `OnRequestDelete` (the upstream's row stays in place). The DB
   write happens only on `OnConfirmDelete`. If the user closes the
   screen mid-snackbar the staging dies with the VM (acceptable: legacy
   behaviour is identical — closing the legacy screen mid-snackbar also
   abandons the delete).

### Screen-side wiring

`UpdatesScreen.kt` (`:ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen.kt`) wires a
`SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState)` into the Scaffold's `snackbarHost`
slot and uses `rememberCoroutineScope()` to launch the snackbar in the
existing effects `LaunchedEffect` collector. The screen does **not**
hard-code the snackbar message at the dispatch site — the message
"Update deleted" / actionLabel "Undo" live inline at the
`showSnackbar` call site so a future Phase 10 i18n lift swaps both in
one pass. Same posture as every other inline literal in the rework `:ui`
layer (the rework deliberately defers `Res.string.*` lookups until
Phase 10).

### Same screen, no route change

This is a **gap-lift** on the rework UpdatesScreen, not a swap.
`Screen.UpdatesScreen` (legacy route) stays bound to the legacy
`composeApp/.../features/notifications/.../UpdatesScreen.kt` composable
via `UpdatesScreenRoute.kt`. The route-swap (Task #289) is a separate
slice that's still deferred — even with the undo snackbar landed, the
swap also needs the per-row download button + inline error gap-lifts
before it can proceed without affordance regression.

## §133 — Phase 7.x.updates.downloadbutton — per-row Download button on rework UpdatesScreen (Tasks #299 + #300)

### What this slice landed

A second gap-lift slice on the path toward Phase 7.x.updates.swap (#289),
splitting the per-row "Download" affordance from the legacy
`composeApp/.../notifications/ui/screens/UpdatesScreen.kt` (the legacy
exposes a `DownloadDoneIcon` / download icon button per row whose click
enqueues a chapter download through legacy `DownloadViewModelv2`).

The slice landed in two source commits at the standing 5-files-per-commit
cap:

- **`f488a02`** (`downloadbutton.foundation`, Task #299) — `:domain`
  `EnqueueDownloadUseCase` + extended `DownloadsActionRepository`
  interface, `:data` strangler-fig impl method, Koin re-wire to inject
  the additional `ChapterDao` dep.
- **`bad2e53`** (`downloadbutton.wire`, Task #300) — `:presentation`
  intent + effect + reducer extension, `:composeApp` Koin VM-binding
  arity bump, `:ui` per-row `TextButton` + effects-collector branch.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — single new use case, single new repository method:

```kotlin
class EnqueueDownloadUseCase(
    private val repository: DownloadsActionRepository,
) {
    suspend operator fun invoke(
        chapterId: Long,
        mangaTitle: String,
        api: String,
    ): Result<Unit> = repository.enqueueDownload(
        chapterId = chapterId,
        mangaTitle = mangaTitle,
        api = api,
    )
}
```

The repository extension adds:

```kotlin
suspend fun enqueueDownload(
    chapterId: Long,
    mangaTitle: String,
    api: String,
): Result<Unit>
```

The 3-arg signature `(chapterId, mangaTitle, api)` matches what legacy
`DownloadRepository.enqueueChapterDownload(chapter, title, mangaApi)`
ultimately needs. Passing them denormalised from the screen-row entity
avoids an extra `MangaDao` round-trip — both `UpdateEntry` and
`HistoryEntry` already carry the trio. Keeping it ad-hoc here (not a
`DownloadRequest` value object) follows the legacy posture and the
minimal-vocabulary principle.

**`:data`** — strangler-fig impl in `DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl`. The
class gains a third constructor dep `chapterDao: ChapterDao` (alongside
the existing `legacy: DownloadRepository` + `chapterDownloadDao:
ChapterDownloadDao`). The implementation:

```kotlin
override suspend fun enqueueDownload(
    chapterId: Long,
    mangaTitle: String,
    api: String,
): Result<Unit> = runCatching {
    val savedChapter = chapterDao.getChapterByIdSuspend(chapterId)
        ?: error("chapter row not found")
    legacy.enqueueChapterDownload(
        chapter = savedChapter,
        title = mangaTitle,
        mangaApi = api,
    )
}
```

**Why a different DAO from retry**: the retry path uses `ChapterDownloadDao
.getDownloadByChapter` because the row already exists in the *downloads*
table (a prior failed/cancelled enqueue left a stub). The new enqueue
path has no downloads-table row yet — it must look up the *saved chapter*
row in the `saved_chapters` table (the table that gets populated on the
initial sync) and pass that entity to the legacy facade. Two distinct
DAOs, two distinct constructor params, two distinct lookup targets —
kept as separate params at call sites for clarity.

**`:presentation`** — sealed-interface extensions only (OCP). New
variants:

- `UpdatesIntent.OnDownloadClick(entry: UpdateEntry)` — dispatched by the
  screen on a tap of the per-row "Download" button. The UI gates the tap
  on `!entry.isDownloaded` so already-downloaded rows do not dispatch.
- `UpdatesEffect.ShowError(message: String)` — emitted on
  `EnqueueDownloadUseCase` failure. Carries the throwable's `message`
  verbatim; no `AppError` lift because the use case's surface returns
  plain `Result<Unit>`.

`UpdatesViewModel` gains a sixth constructor dep `private val
enqueueDownload: EnqueueDownloadUseCase` and one reducer branch:

```kotlin
is UpdatesIntent.OnDownloadClick -> {
    viewModelScope.launch {
        enqueueDownload(
            chapterId = intent.entry.chapterId,
            mangaTitle = intent.entry.mangaTitle,
            api = intent.entry.api,
        ).onFailure { throwable ->
            emit(UpdatesEffect.ShowError(throwable.message ?: "Download failed"))
        }
    }
}
```

`viewModelScope.launch` lets the `handle` suspend return immediately so
`submit(intent)` does not block. `.onFailure` is the only branch
modelled — success has no observable effect because the legacy's
`enqueueChapterDownload` is fire-and-forget (WorkManager on Android,
queue-and-coroutine on iOS/Desktop). The screen's row stays in place
until the underlying download completes and `LibraryRefreshWorker`
re-emits with `isDownloaded = true`.

**`:composeApp`** — two-line module edit. `downloadsReworkModule` gains
`factory { EnqueueDownloadUseCase(get()) }` and its
`single<DownloadsActionRepository>` binding switches from 2-arg to 3-arg
`DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl(legacy = get(), chapterDownloadDao = get(),
chapterDao = get())`. `updatesReworkModule`'s `viewModel { ... }`
extends from 5 `get()` args to 6.

**`:ui`** — per-row third button + effect-collector branch:

```kotlin
TextButton(
    onClick = onDownloadClick,
    enabled = !entry.isDownloaded,
) {
    Text(if (entry.isDownloaded) "Downloaded" else "Download")
}
```

```kotlin
is UpdatesEffect.ShowError -> {
    scope.launch {
        snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
            message = effect.message,
            duration = SnackbarDuration.Short,
        )
    }
}
```

The same `SnackbarHostState` that backs `ShowUndoSnackbar` (per §132)
receives `ShowError`. Single Scaffold `snackbarHost` slot serves both
transient surfaces — keeps the screen's Compose tree free of duplicated
`SnackbarHost`s.

### Why the `:ui` button is text-only (no icon)

`:ui` deliberately omits `compose.materialIconsExtended` (per the
icon-strategy posture established in §82 / §83). The legacy uses
`Icons.Filled.Download` + `Icons.Filled.DownloadDone`; the rework
substitutes the labelled "Download" / "Downloaded" `TextButton`. Phase
10 i18n + icon-strategy decision swaps both legacy and rework in one
pass.

### Why `ShowError` supersedes the original §37 "no `ShowError` today"
### rationale

Task #240's `UpdatesEffect` KDoc explicitly stated "Room observe-site
does not throw; `UPDATE` / `DELETE` SQL is structurally infallible — no
`ShowError` variant today." Enqueue is the **first fallible mutation**
introduced on this surface: the legacy `enqueueChapterDownload` can throw
on a missing `saved_chapters` row (DAO returns null → `error("chapter
row not found")`), on WorkManager queue rejection (Android), or on Room
write failure. The original rationale was correct at the time and is
**superseded** rather than invalidated; the new KDoc on `ShowError`
explicitly references the original paragraph.

### OCP preservation

The slice is a strict OCP extension:

- **Foundation commit (`f488a02`)**: zero changes to existing
  `DownloadsActionRepository` methods (`retryDownload` / `cancelDownload`
  / `cancelRunningDownload` / `deleteDownload`). One new method appended.
  Zero changes to existing use cases — one new use case appended.
- **Wire commit (`bad2e53`)**: zero changes to existing `UpdatesIntent`
  variants (8 originals untouched). Zero changes to existing
  `UpdatesEffect` variants (3 originals untouched, including
  `ShowUndoSnackbar` from §132). One new variant on each sealed surface.
  The reducer's `when` block gains one branch; the existing 11 branches
  are byte-identical.

### Strangler-fig integrity

No new strangler-fig boundary introduced. The new enqueue impl reaches
the **same** legacy `:shared` `DownloadRepository.enqueueChapterDownload`
that legacy code already uses, plus the **same** legacy
`ChapterDao.getChapterByIdSuspend` — both via interfaces bound in
`PlatformModule.{android,ios,desktop}.kt`. The rework's strangler-fig
boundary widens by one DAO (from one to two) but remains an extension of
the §124-established Downloads reach posture.

## §134 — Phase 7.x.updates.swap — Route-swap legacy `Screen.Updates` → rework `UpdatesScreen` (Task #289)

### Strategy

Single-file route-swap rewrite of `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/
UpdatesScreenRoute.kt` so the legacy `Screen.Updates` entry now renders
the architecture-rework `:ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen` backed by the
rework `:presentation/.../updates/UpdatesViewModel`. Mirrors the
slice-shape posture from §125 (`Phase 7.x.history.swap`, commit
`eab80c0`) and §131 (`Phase 7.x.about.swap`, commit `cf7d8e6`): the
nav-graph type-safe `composable<Screen.Updates>` entry stays bound, only
the body of the route adapter is rewritten to call the rework screen.
Bottom-nav tab caller (`BottomNavigationBar.kt:60`'s
`Triple(Screen.Updates, ..., Res.string.title_notifications)`) requires
no change because the route entry's identity (`object Updates`) is
preserved.

Both the legacy `Screen.Updates` tab AND the parallel
`Screen.UpdatesRework` debug route now converge on the same rework
screen + rework VM. Each route owns its own `NavBackStackEntry`-scoped
`UpdatesViewModel` (Koin's default `viewModel { ... }` lifecycle), but
they share the single-scoped `UpdatesRepository` (a strangler-fig over
the legacy `:shared/.../notifications/domain/NotificationRepository`
facade); the same `notifications` Room table is the source of truth on
both paths. Mark-read / delete / undo / download mutations from either
route propagate via the upstream `getGroupedNotifications()` re-emit.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:composeApp`** — 1 modified file:
  - `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/UpdatesScreenRoute.kt` —
    rewritten. The legacy adapter (pre-swap) threaded
    `NotificationsViewModel` + `DownloadViewModelv2` and 9 callbacks
    into the legacy `:shared/.../UpdatesScreen` composable; the swapped
    adapter resolves `UpdatesViewModel` via `koinViewModel()` and
    passes 2 navigation callbacks into the rework
    `:ui/.../UpdatesScreen` (which internalises mark-read / delete /
    undo / download). The route-host body shape mirrors
    `UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt` verbatim — both adapters are
    functionally identical post-swap.
- **`:ui` / `:presentation` / `:domain` / `:data`** — unchanged. All
  affordance parity already landed via:
  - §37 (Task #240) — original Updates slice (foundation + screen +
    VM + use cases + strangler-fig impl).
  - §132 (Task #298) — undo-snackbar gap-lift (`UpdatesIntent.OnRequestDelete`
    / `OnUndoDelete` / `OnConfirmDelete`; `UpdatesEffect.ShowUndoSnackbar`;
    `UpdatesState.pendingDeleteIds`; `:ui` `SnackbarHost` + effect collector).
  - §133 (Tasks #299 + #300) — download-button gap-lift
    (`EnqueueDownloadUseCase` + `DownloadsActionRepository.enqueueDownload`;
    `UpdatesIntent.OnDownloadClick`; `UpdatesEffect.ShowError`; per-row
    `TextButton`).
- **`:platform`** — unchanged.
- **`:shared`** — unchanged. The legacy `:shared/.../notifications/...`
  classes (`NotificationsViewModel`, the legacy `UpdatesScreen`
  composable, `DownloadViewModelv2`) still compile and remain bound in
  `SharedModule` — they are simply no longer reachable from the swapped
  `Screen.Updates` route. Phase 9.x cleanup retires them once the swap
  is observed stable on user devices.

### Affordance parity table

| Affordance | Pre-swap (legacy adapter) | Post-swap (rework adapter) |
|---|---|---|
| List | `NotificationsViewModel.uiState` (grouped list) | `UpdatesViewModel.state.items` (grouped list, same upstream) |
| Manga-thumbnail tap → details | `onNotificationImgClick` → `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)` | `onNavigateToDetails(api, mangaUrl)` → `Screen.MangaDetails` (identical) |
| Chapter-row tap → reader | `onNotificationClick` → `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment(...)` (11 fields) | `onNavigateToReader(entry)` → `Screen.ChapterImagesFragment(...)` (same 11 fields, field-for-field) |
| Per-row mark-read | `onMarkAsRead(notification)` callback | `UpdatesIntent.OnMarkAsRead(entry)` (internal) |
| Mark-all-read | `onMarkAllAsRead()` callback | `UpdatesIntent.OnMarkAllAsRead` (internal) |
| Per-row delete + undo snackbar | `onDeleteWithUndo` / `onUndoDelete` / `onConfirmDelete` callbacks | `UpdatesIntent.OnRequestDelete` / `OnUndoDelete` / `OnConfirmDelete` + `UpdatesEffect.ShowUndoSnackbar` (internal, per §132) |
| Delete-all | `onDeleteAll()` callback | `UpdatesIntent.OnDeleteAll` (internal) |
| Per-row download | `onNotificationDownloadClick(notification)` callback + `downloadingChapters` / `runningChapter` indicators | `UpdatesIntent.OnDownloadClick(entry)` + `UpdatesEffect.ShowError` snackbar on failure (internal, per §133) |

All pre-swap affordances have a post-swap counterpart. No observable
behaviour regression.

### Visual delta

The rework `:ui` module deliberately omits
`compose.materialIconsExtended` (same posture as Library / History /
Statistics / Details / Reader / Downloads / About / Settings). Each
per-row affordance is rendered as a labelled `TextButton`
("Mark read" / "Download" / "Downloaded" / "Delete"), not as an
`IconButton`. Per-row delete trigger gesture differs: pre-swap legacy
used `SwipeToDismissBox`; post-swap rework uses a per-row `TextButton`.
Post-trigger flow (stage in `pendingDeleteIds` → snackbar with Undo →
on dismissal call `DeleteUpdateEntryUseCase`) is identical to the
legacy's `deleteWithUndo` posture.

### Strangler-fig integrity

Unchanged. The swap moves the user-facing entry from the legacy screen
to the rework screen but the underlying `:data` →
`legacy NotificationRepository` →
`:shared/.../local/dao/NotificationDao` reach (established by §37 in
`UpdatesRepositoryImpl`) is the same. The legacy
`NotificationRepository` facade is now consumed by exactly one route's
worth of state (the rework VM) instead of two-routes'-worth (the
legacy VM + rework VM coexisting); no new reach added, no existing
reach removed.

### Files

| Path | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/UpdatesScreenRoute.kt` | MODIFIED | Rewrite body to delegate to the rework `:ui` `UpdatesScreen` via the rework `UpdatesViewModel`. |

## §135 — Phase 7.x.settings.swap — Route-swap legacy `Screen.Setting` → rework `SettingsScreen` (Task #301)

### Strategy

Single-file route-swap rewrite of `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/
SettingsRoute.kt` so the legacy `Screen.Setting` entry now renders the
architecture-rework `:ui/.../settings/SettingsScreen` backed by the
rework `:presentation/.../settings/SettingsViewModel`. Mirrors the
slice-shape posture from §125 (`Phase 7.x.history.swap`, commit
`eab80c0`), §131 (`Phase 7.x.about.swap`, commit `e9b6a0b`), and §134
(`Phase 7.x.updates.swap`, commit `b3dbeac`): the nav-graph type-safe
`composable<Screen.Setting>` entry stays bound; only the body of the
route adapter is rewritten to resolve the rework VM via
`koinViewModel()` and dispatch the `SettingsDestination` callback to
the matching `Screen` target.

Home-screen overflow menu caller (which `navController.navigate(
Screen.Setting)` for the "Settings" item) requires no change because
the route entry's identity (`object Setting`) is preserved. Both the
legacy `Screen.Setting` entry AND the parallel `Screen.SettingsRework`
debug route now converge on the same rework screen — each owns its own
`NavBackStackEntry`-scoped `SettingsViewModel` (Koin's default
`viewModel { ... }` lifecycle), but they share the single-scoped
`SettingsRepositoryImpl` (a strangler-fig over the legacy
`:shared/.../settings/SettingsRepository` facade); the same
`SharedPreferences` / `DataStore` keys are the source of truth on both
paths. Toggling `incognito` from EITHER screen flips the same
underlying `incognito_mode` key; clearing cache from EITHER screen runs
the same `clearFilesLargerThan1MB()`.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:composeApp`** — 1 modified file:
  - `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/SettingsRoute.kt` — rewritten.
    Pre-swap was a 22-line trivial pass-through
    `SettingsScreen(navController)` to the legacy
    `:composeApp/.../features/settings/.../SettingsScreen` (which
    internally injected `SettingsViewModel` + `ChaptersViewModel` +
    `ComplaintViewModel` via `koinViewModel()` and threaded
    `navController` into ~10 navigation closures). Post-swap resolves
    `me.manga.kira.presentation.settings.SettingsViewModel` via
    `koinViewModel()` and invokes the rework
    `me.manga.kira.ui.settings.SettingsScreen(viewModel, onNavigate)`
    composable, where `onNavigate` is an exhaustive `when` over the
    7-variant `SettingsDestination` enum mapping each to its rework
    `Screen` target (with the same admin gate as the legacy
    `if (Admin.isAdmin) ComplaintAdmin else Complaint` branch at legacy
    `SettingsScreen.kt:272-278`). The route-host body shape mirrors
    `SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt` verbatim — both adapters are
    functionally identical post-swap.
- **`:ui` / `:presentation` / `:domain` / `:data`** — unchanged. All
  affordance parity already landed via:
  - §96 (Task #253) — Settings foundation (state + intent + reducer +
    cache-clear use case + composable shell with 5 boolean toggles +
    Clear-cache row).
  - §97 (Task #254) — themegating: gate `Dark mode` SwitchItem on
    `!state.followSystemTheme`.
  - §98 (Task #255) — Feedback dialog: category dropdown + body field +
    submit-to-Firestore + `isSubmittingFeedback` gating + snackbar
    success/error.
  - §99 (Task #256) — Reading-mode dialog with single-tap commit.
  - §100 (Task #257) — Downloads nav row bridging to (then-legacy)
    `Screen.DownloadsScreen` — now retargets to `Screen.DownloadsRework`
    after §119 + §129 landed.
  - §113 (Task #270) — inert Help placeholder row (mirrors legacy's
    `SettingsNavigationItem(title = Res.string.help)` with no
    `onClick`).
- **`:platform`** — unchanged.
- **`:shared`** — unchanged. The legacy
  `:composeApp/.../features/settings/.../SettingsScreen` composable +
  the legacy `:shared/.../settings/SettingsViewModel` +
  `ChaptersViewModel` + `ComplaintViewModel` still compile and remain
  bound in `SharedModule` — they are simply no longer reachable from
  the swapped `Screen.Setting` route. Phase 9.x cleanup retires them
  once the swap is observed stable on user devices.
