## §136 — Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingcontinue — optional `onContinue` callback + Continue button on rework `ThemeScreen` (Task #302)

### §136.1 Strategy

First of three gap-lifts that together unblock the deferred **Phase
7.x.theme.swap** (Task #291). The legacy `ThemeSelectionScreen.kt`'s three
onboarding-only affordances are:

1. **Continue button** (advances Welcome → Theme → Sources → RepoSettings →
   Library wizard) — closed by this slice (§136).
2. **Notification permission requester** (calls
   `rememberNotificationPermissionRequester()`, auto-requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS
   on first composition, renders a grant-button row if denied) — still
   deferred (separate `Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingpermission` gap-lift).
3. **`AnimatedBackground` overlay** (gradient sweep behind the picker) — still
   deferred (separate `Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingbackground` gap-lift).

This slice ports affordance (1). Mirrors the established §122
`sources.onboardingfinish` pattern: rather than carrying a legacy-style
`isFirstOpen: Boolean` gate + `onContinue: () -> Unit` callback pair, the
rework collapses both into a single nullable callback. Non-null IS the
gate.

### §136.2 API shape — single nullable callback (mirroring §122)

```kotlin
@Composable
fun ThemeScreen(
    viewModel: ThemeViewModel,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    onContinue: (() -> Unit)? = null,
)

@Composable
internal fun ThemeScreenContent(
    state: ThemeState,
    onIntent: (ThemeIntent) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    onContinue: (() -> Unit)? = null,
)

@Composable
private fun ThemePickerColumn(
    selected: AppTheme,
    pureBlack: Boolean,
    onSelect: (AppTheme) -> Unit,
    onTogglePureBlack: (Boolean) -> Unit,
    contentPadding: PaddingValues,
    paddingHorizontal: Dp,
    paddingVertical: Dp,
    onContinue: (() -> Unit)?,
)
```

The Continue button renders as the last child of `ThemePickerColumn` under
the `PureBlackRow` only when `onContinue != null`. Existing call sites
(only `ThemeReworkScreenRoute.kt` today) implicitly pass `null` via the
`= null` default — Screen.ThemeRework behaviour is bit-for-bit unchanged.

### §136.3 Visual posture

- Material 3 `Button` (not `OutlinedButton` or `TextButton`) — the legacy
  uses an outlined button styled as full-width primary; the rework uses
  the default M3 `Button` for primary-container coloring without explicit
  overrides (same posture as §122 `FinishButton` — let the M3 theme
  defaults carry the styling).
- `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` — full-width to match the legacy's emphasis
  posture and to read as a clear "next" call-to-action at the bottom of
  the picker.
- Label "Continue" — inline string literal. Phase 10 i18n lift will route
  both legacy + rework consumers through `Res.string.continueText` (or
  whatever the existing legacy key is) in one pass.
- Vertical spacing comes free from the parent Column's
  `verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(paddingVertical)` — no
  explicit padding modifier on the button.
- No icon — same icon-free posture as the rest of the rework `:ui`
  module (`compose.materialIconsExtended` is deliberately not on the
  `:ui` classpath).

### §136.4 Layer-by-layer surfaces

ZERO new files; TWO modified files (`:ui` + `:composeApp`). The Continue
button is a UI-only concern; no `:domain`/`:data`/`:presentation` changes,
no new state, no new intents/effects.

**`ui/.../themepicker/ThemeScreen.kt`** (modified):
- New `import androidx.compose.material3.Button`.
- New `onContinue: (() -> Unit)? = null` parameter on `ThemeScreen` +
  `ThemeScreenContent`.
- New `onContinue: (() -> Unit)?` parameter on `ThemePickerColumn`
  (non-default — internal helper).
- Threaded through both surfaces.
- New conditional `Button` rendering at the bottom of `ThemePickerColumn`.
- KDoc bullet rewritten: "Onboarding-flavour UI omitted" → "Onboarding-
  flavour UI partially restored" — documents the `[onContinue]` callback
  semantics + forward-references the two still-deferred gap-lifts.

**`composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ThemeReworkScreenRoute.kt`** (modified):
- No call-site change (the default `onContinue = null` keeps Screen.
  ThemeRework's standalone-picker behaviour).
- KDoc paragraph updated from "Onboarding chain is NOT touched" to
  "Onboarding chain not consumed here" — accurate now that the rework
  ThemeScreen DOES support the callback shape, even though THIS route
  doesn't pass one.

### §136.5 Why route adapter isn't touched call-site-wise

The `ThemeReworkScreenRoute` is the standalone-picker entry from the
rework Settings hub (Phase 7.x.settings.swap §135 wires
`SettingsDestination.THEME` to `Screen.ThemeRework`). At that entry, the
screen is terminal — there's no next-step destination to navigate to.
Passing `onContinue = null` is correct.

The wiring with `onContinue = { navController.navigate(Screen.Sources) }`
is the job of **Phase 7.x.theme.swap** — when the legacy `Screen.Theme`
route adapter (currently `ThemeSelectionScreenRoute`) gets swapped to
render the rework screen, IT passes the navigation callback. Two
different route adapters, two different `onContinue` values — the
optional parameter cleanly separates the two consumption modes.

## §137 — Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingpermission — opt-in notification permission grant row + permission-gated Continue button on rework `ThemeScreen` (Task #303)

### §137.1 Strategy

Second of three gap-lifts toward the deferred **Phase 7.x.theme.swap**
(Task #291). The legacy `ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:71-95` carries two
notification-related concerns that the rework needs to host before swap
can fire:

1. **Notification permission grant UI** — when the user lacks
   POST_NOTIFICATIONS, the legacy renders an "Enable Notifications"
   row (header + descriptive copy + Grant Permission button) above the
   Continue button, and gates the Continue button on
   `enabled = hasPermission`.
2. **Auto-request lifecycle** — a `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` fires the
   permission request on first composition (gated by a local
   `autoRequested` `rememberSaveable` flag so it doesn't re-fire across
   recompositions); a denial triggers a toast.

This slice ports **only concern (1)** — the visible grant row + the
permission-gated Continue button. Concern (2) — the auto-request
lifecycle — is deferred to the route adapter (see §137.5). The split
keeps `:ui` free of `LaunchedEffect`-based side effects on platform APIs
and keeps the `expect`/`actual` `NotificationPermissionRequester` facade
in `composeApp/.../core/platform/` rather than pulling it into `:ui`.

Mirrors the established §122 `sources.onboardingfinish` +
§136 `theme.onboardingcontinue` pattern: each onboarding affordance is
gated on whether the caller supplied the corresponding optional
parameter. Non-null IS the gate.

### §137.2 API shape — Boolean state input + nullable callback (mirroring §122/§136)

```kotlin
@Composable
fun ThemeScreen(
    viewModel: ThemeViewModel,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    onContinue: (() -> Unit)? = null,                      // §136
    hasNotificationPermission: Boolean = true,             // §137 new
    onRequestNotificationPermission: (() -> Unit)? = null, // §137 new
)

@Composable
internal fun ThemeScreenContent(
    state: ThemeState,
    onIntent: (ThemeIntent) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    onContinue: (() -> Unit)? = null,
    hasNotificationPermission: Boolean = true,
    onRequestNotificationPermission: (() -> Unit)? = null,
)

@Composable
private fun ThemePickerColumn(
    selected: AppTheme,
    pureBlack: Boolean,
    onSelect: (AppTheme) -> Unit,
    onTogglePureBlack: (Boolean) -> Unit,
    contentPadding: PaddingValues,
    paddingHorizontal: Dp,
    paddingVertical: Dp,
    onContinue: (() -> Unit)?,
    hasNotificationPermission: Boolean,
    onRequestNotificationPermission: (() -> Unit)?,
)
```

Two new optional parameters: a `Boolean` state input (defaults `true` —
"no gating") and a nullable callback (defaults `null` — "no grant row").
This shape keeps the screen a pure projection — Compose state flows in
via parameters, side effects flow out via callbacks. No
`rememberNotificationPermissionRequester()` call from inside `:ui`.

### §137.3 Conditional rendering logic

```kotlin
if (onRequestNotificationPermission != null && !hasNotificationPermission) {
    NotificationPermissionRow(onRequest = onRequestNotificationPermission)
}
if (onContinue != null) {
    Button(
        onClick = onContinue,
        enabled = onRequestNotificationPermission == null || hasNotificationPermission,
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    ) {
        Text("Continue")
    }
}
```

Two independent guards:
- **Grant row visibility**: shown only when the caller wired a permission
  callback AND permission is currently denied. When permission is
  granted, the row disappears entirely (no stale "Grant Permission"
  button taking up vertical space). Matches the legacy's behavior.
- **Continue button enablement**: gated only when the caller wired a
  permission callback. Callers that don't supply
  `onRequestNotificationPermission` (today: every caller, including
  `Screen.ThemeRework`) get the §136 unconditional-enablement behavior
  preserved bit-for-bit. Callers that supply both (future Phase
  7.x.theme.swap) get the wizard-style gating: the user can't advance
  through the onboarding flow without granting notifications.

### §137.4 Visual posture (NotificationPermissionRow)

- **Title** "Enable Notifications" — `MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge`,
  same weight as the `PureBlackRow` sibling row title.
- **Body** descriptive copy explaining notifications are used for
  chapter updates + download progress —
  `MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall` softened via
  `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant`. Copy verbatim from the
  legacy `Res.string.notification_permission` resource literal at
  `shared/.../composeResources/values/strings.xml:294`. Phase 10 i18n
  lift will route both legacy + rework consumers through the same
  resource key.
- **Grant button** in a trailing `Row` with
  `horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.End` — right-aligned, Material 3
  `Button` with primary-container coloring (default M3 styling, no
  explicit overrides), label "Grant Permission". Same M3-defaults
  posture as the §136 Continue button + §122 FinishButton.
- **No icon** — same icon-free posture as the rest of the rework `:ui`
  module.
- Layout container: an outer `Column(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth())`
  letting the parent's `verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(...)`
  carry the row's vertical spacing free.

### §137.5 Why the route adapter (not `:ui`) owns the auto-request lifecycle

The Compose-aware `NotificationPermissionRequester` facade is an
`expect`/`actual` declared at
`composeApp/.../core/platform/RememberNotificationPermissionRequester.kt`,
NOT in `:platform` and NOT in `:ui`. The `:ui` module deliberately has
no `androidx.activity.compose` dependency (which the Android `actual`
needs for the launcher), so reaching into the requester from `:ui`
would either drag the dep into `:ui` or require a multiplatform shim —
neither is justified for a side-effect that fundamentally belongs at
the route-adapter layer (where lifecycle, route arguments, and
nav-callback wiring already live).

Splitting like this also makes the `:ui` Theme screen unit-testable
in `commonTest` without mocking platform-specific permission APIs.
A test can pass `hasNotificationPermission = false` +
`onRequestNotificationPermission = { /* assert called */ }` and verify
the rendering + button enablement entirely in commonMain.

### §137.6 Layer-by-layer surfaces

ZERO new files; TWO modified files (`:ui` + `:composeApp`). Same shape
as §136 — the permission-related state + callback are UI-only concerns;
no `:domain`/`:data`/`:presentation` changes, no new state, no new
intents/effects (the permission state lives in Compose state at the
caller, not in `ThemeState`).

**`ui/.../themepicker/ThemeScreen.kt`** (modified):
- New `hasNotificationPermission: Boolean = true` +
  `onRequestNotificationPermission: (() -> Unit)? = null` parameters on
  `ThemeScreen` + `ThemeScreenContent`.
- Non-default versions of the same two parameters on the internal
  `ThemePickerColumn` helper.
- Threaded through all three surfaces.
- New conditional `NotificationPermissionRow` render in
  `ThemePickerColumn`, above the conditional Continue button render
  from §136.
- New `enabled = ...` gating expression on the existing §136 Continue
  button.
- New private composable `NotificationPermissionRow` with the
  bodyLarge title + bodySmall description + right-aligned Grant
  Permission button.
- KDoc bullet rewritten: documents all three onboarding parameters
  (`onContinue`, `hasNotificationPermission`,
  `onRequestNotificationPermission`), the gating semantics, the
  defaults-preserve-behavior posture, the §122 idiom reuse, and the
  still-deferred `AnimatedBackground` + auto-request lifecycle.

**`composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ThemeReworkScreenRoute.kt`**
(modified):
- No call-site change. `Screen.ThemeRework` continues to pass NONE of
  the three onboarding parameters; defaults preserve the
  standalone-picker terminal-screen behavior bit-for-bit.
- KDoc paragraph rewritten to document the expanded onboarding API
  surface (3 parameters now), explain why this route still doesn't
  pass any (terminal entry from the rework Settings hub), and update
  the deferral list (the `AnimatedBackground` overlay AND the
  auto-request lifecycle are still pending — see §137.8 status table).

  (commit `d24d07e`)

## §138 — Phase 7.x.theme.swap — Route-swap legacy `Screen.Theme` → rework `ThemeScreen` (Task #291)

### Strategy

Single-file route-swap rewrite of
`composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt` so the
legacy `Screen.Theme` onboarding-step entry now renders the
architecture-rework `:ui/.../themepicker/ThemeScreen` backed by the
rework `:presentation/.../theme/ThemeViewModel`. Mirrors the
single-file route-swap posture from §125 (`history.swap`), §131
(`about.swap`), §134 (`updates.swap`), and §135 (`settings.swap`):
the nav-graph type-safe `composable<Screen.Theme>` entry stays bound;
only the body of the route adapter is rewritten.

This swap was previously deferred (see §135 cross-reference) pending
three gap-lifts to bring the rework `ThemeScreen` to onboarding-step
parity:
1. **`onContinue` callback + Continue button** — closed by §136
   (`Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingcontinue`).
2. **Notification permission grant row + permission-gated Continue
   button** — closed by §137 (`Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingpermission`).
3. **Auto-request `LaunchedEffect` lifecycle + toast-on-denial** —
   addressed here at the route-adapter layer (NOT a screen-level gap-
   lift). The expect/actual `NotificationPermissionRequester` facade
   lives in `composeApp/.../core/platform/`, NOT in `:ui`; reaching
   into it from `:ui` would violate the layer boundary. The route
   adapter is the right owner.

The legacy `AnimatedBackground` gradient overlay is intentionally
NOT ported — matches the §122 `sources.onboardingfinish` precedent
which also skipped the equivalent legacy decorative background.
Purely cosmetic, no semantic value.

Welcome screen caller
(`WelcomeScreenRoute.kt:23 → navController.navigate(Screen.Theme)`)
requires no change because the route entry's identity (`object Theme`)
is preserved. Both the legacy `Screen.Theme` onboarding entry AND
the parallel `Screen.ThemeRework` debug route (added in §85) now
converge on the same rework screen — each owns its own
`NavBackStackEntry`-scoped `ThemeViewModel` (Koin's default
`viewModel { ... }` lifecycle), but they share the single-scoped
`ThemeRepositoryImpl` (strangler-fig over `:shared/.../settings/
SettingsRepository`'s `darkModeFlow` + `followSystemFlow` +
`pureBlackFlow` + setters); the same `SharedPreferences` booleans are
the source of truth on both paths. Setting theme from EITHER screen
flips the same underlying booleans; a user mid-onboarding before the
swap, restarted after the swap, sees their theme + pureBlack
preference preserved.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:composeApp`** — 1 modified file:
  - `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt`
    — rewritten. Pre-swap was a 71-line route adapter that resolved
    `OnboardingViewModel` via `koinViewModel()`, projected its two
    `StateFlow<Boolean>`s (`darkMode` + `followSystem`) into an
    `AppTheme` tri-state, and dispatched theme selection back through
    three `toggleFollowSystem` / `toggleDarkMode` setters on the
    legacy VM. Post-swap is a 130-line route adapter that resolves
    `me.manga.kira.presentation.theme.ThemeViewModel` via
    `koinViewModel()` plus `ToastShower` via `koinInject()` plus the
    Compose-aware `rememberNotificationPermissionRequester()`, hosts
    the auto-request `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` lifecycle + the
    toast-on-denial `LaunchedEffect(hasPermission, autoRequested.value)`,
    and invokes the rework `ThemeScreen` with all three §136/§137
    onboarding parameters wired:
    - `onContinue = { navController.navigate(Screen.Sources) }` —
      advances the onboarding wizard.
    - `hasNotificationPermission = hasPermission` — reactive Compose
      state collected from the platform requester.
    - `onRequestNotificationPermission = { permissionRequester.request() }`
      — re-launches the platform permission request from the screen's
      "Grant Permission" tap.
- **`:ui` / `:presentation` / `:domain` / `:data` / `:platform` /
  `:shared`** — unchanged. All affordance parity already landed via
  §85 (`Phase 7.x.theme` foundation), §86 (`Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack`),
  §136 (`Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingcontinue`), and §137
  (`Phase 7.x.theme.onboardingpermission`).
- **Legacy `:composeApp/.../presentation/features/onboarding/theme_
  selection/`** files (`ThemeSelectionScreen.kt`, `ThemeSelector.kt`,
  `AppTheme.kt`) still compile and remain on the classpath — they
  are simply no longer reachable from the swapped `Screen.Theme`
  route. Phase 9.x cleanup retires them once the swap is observed
  stable on user devices. The `OnboardingViewModel` itself stays
  Koin-bound in `SharedModule` because other onboarding steps
  (Welcome → Sources → RepoSettings) still consume it.

### Affordance parity table

| Affordance | Pre-swap (legacy adapter) | Post-swap (rework adapter) |
|---|---|---|
| Theme tri-state picker (Light / Dark / System) | Legacy `ThemeSelector` vertical list with custom Box backgrounds + `selected` highlight | Rework Material 3 `TabRow` with three text tabs; same persisted state (`SettingsRepository.darkModeFlow` + `followSystemFlow`); same translation rules (System → followSystem=true; Dark/Light → followSystem=false + darkMode=true/false) |
| Continue button | Legacy custom-styled `Button` (50.dp height + `RoundedCornerShape(26.dp)` + `shapes.medium` + primary `containerColor` + onPrimary label) gated on `hasPermission` | Rework Material 3 default `Button` with primary-container coloring + inline literal "Continue"; gated on `hasNotificationPermission` (per §137 enabled expression) |
| Auto-request POST_NOTIFICATIONS on screen entry | Legacy `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` in `ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:85-90` gated by `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` flag; calls `permissionRequester.request()` once | Identical lifecycle preserved verbatim in route adapter (same `LaunchedEffect(Unit)`, same `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` guard, same `.request()` call) |
| Toast on denial | Legacy `LaunchedEffect(hasPermission, autoRequested.value)` in `ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:78-82` calling `toastShower.showLong(...)` | Identical lifecycle preserved verbatim in route adapter (same keys, same condition, same toast string `Res.string.you_need_to_enable_notifications` via `stringResource`) |

All pre-swap legacy affordances have a post-swap counterpart. No
observable behaviour regression on theme selection, continue-button
navigation, auto-request lifecycle, toast-on-denial, or the grant
button.

Additive affordance (rework-only — not in pre-swap legacy onboarding):

| Affordance | Source |
|---|---|
| `PureBlackRow` Switch toggle visible during onboarding | Pure addition (§86 `Phase 7.x.theme.pureblack`). Legacy onboarding does NOT expose the PureBlack/OLED preference at this step — it's only in the legacy Settings screen. The rework treats the toggle as part of the canonical theme-picker surface, so it appears in BOTH onboarding AND Settings-hub entry. Default value `true` (from `SettingsRepository.isPureBlack()`) matches the legacy initial state; un-toggled behaviour is identical to pre-swap. Acceptable enrichment — earlier access to a useful preference without imposing it on the user. |

### Visual delta

Four intentional visual deltas vs the legacy
`ThemeSelectionScreen.kt`:

- **TopAppBar with "Theme" title** (rework, unconditional, no

## §139 — Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingseed — default-language source auto-seed gap-lift (Task #304)

### Strategy

Lift the legacy onboarding step 3 default-language seed mechanism
(`LaunchedEffect(userLanguageCode) { repoSettingsViewModel.
setLanguageEnabledDefault("(${tag.uppercase()})", true) }` at
`composeApp/.../onboarding/sources/SourcesScreen.kt:124-127`,
implemented in `RepoSettingsViewModel.setLanguageEnabledDefault` at
lines 80-123) onto the rework `:domain` + `:data` + `:presentation`
+ `:ui` stack so a future `Phase 7.x.sources.swap` can route the
legacy onboarding `Screen.Sources` to the rework screen without
losing the auto-seed behavior. The seed enables every source whose
parenthesised language tag matches the user-selected locale (e.g.
`"(EN)"` for `"en"`, `"(FR)"` for `"fr"`), falling back to `"(EN)"`
when no native sources exist for the chosen locale.

This is the third gap-lift in the onboarding-sources stack —
following §121 (Phase 7.x.sources.complaint), §122 (Phase 7.x.
sources.onboardingfinish), and §123 (Phase 7.x.sources.infocard).
With this slice landed, the rework Sources screen reaches full
feature parity with the legacy onboarding `SourcesScreen.kt` and
unblocks `Phase 7.x.sources.swap` (route Screen.Sources → rework).

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — interface + use case.

- `SourcesRepository.setLanguageEnabledWithFallback(primary:
  String, fallback: String, enabled: Boolean)` — new fourth method
  on the existing repository interface. Case-sensitive `==` match
  against the persisted `language` column; fallback fires only
  when `primary` yields zero matches. Mechanism-only — neither the
  tag-formatting policy nor the fallback policy (defaulting to EN)
  lives on the repository.
- `EnableDefaultLanguageSourcesUseCase(languageTag: String)` — new
  use case. Owns the policy: blank locale coerces to `"en"`, tag
  uppercases + wraps in parens (`"(EN)"`, `"(FR)"`), fallback pins
  to `"(EN)"`. Mirrors `RepoSettingsViewModel.
  setLanguageEnabledDefault` semantics verbatim.

**`:data`** — strangler-fig impl extension.

- `SourcesRepositoryImpl.setLanguageEnabledWithFallback(...)` —
  one-shot `legacy.allSources.first()` snapshot, filter by
  `primary`, then (if empty) filter by `fallback`, fan out
  `legacy.enableDisAbleSource(name, enabled)` over each match. Same
  legacy-facade reach as the existing `setLanguageEnabled` impl;
  no new build-config changes.

**`:presentation`** — MVI surface extension.

- `SourcesIntent.OnSeedDefaultLanguage(languageTag: String)` — new
  6th intent variant. Transient "fire-and-forget seed" command
  intent (no corresponding state field). The dedup (one-fire per
  locale change) lives in the `:ui` composable's
  `LaunchedEffect(onboardingLanguageTag)` key, NOT in the VM —
  matches the legacy `LaunchedEffect(userLanguageCode)` posture
  verbatim.
- `SourcesViewModel` — gains a 5th ctor dep
  (`EnableDefaultLanguageSourcesUseCase`) and a single handler
  branch that `viewModelScope.launch`es the use case. VM stays a
  thin dispatcher (no state mutation, no flag-flipping).

**`:ui`** — param + LaunchedEffect.

- `SourcesScreen(viewModel, modifier, onFinish, onboardingLanguage
  Tag: String? = null)` — new optional param. Defaulted to `null`
  so existing callers (`SourcesReworkScreenRoute` from the
  settings entry, the `Screen.RepoSettings` swap entry from
  §124) compile unchanged. The `LaunchedEffect(onboardingLanguage
  Tag)` dispatches `OnSeedDefaultLanguage(tag)` only when
  non-null — non-onboarding callers see no behavior change.

**`:composeApp`** — Koin binding.

- `sourcesReworkModule` — new `factory` binding for
  `EnableDefaultLanguageSourcesUseCase`; `viewModel` resolution
  bumped from 4 to 5 `get()` args.

### MVI shape rationale

- **Why a 6th intent variant** vs. extending an existing one — OCP.
  `OnToggleLanguage(language, enabled)` is the per-language Switch
  intent; widening it with a fallback param would silently change
  every existing call site. The new intent is additive at the type
  level.
- **Why a "command intent" with no state field** — the legacy seed
  is a transient `LaunchedEffect` action, not a UI affordance.
  Adding a `seedFired: Boolean` state field would only re-introduce
  a second dedup layer on top of the `LaunchedEffect` key — pure
  duplication. The screen-level key is the dedup.
- **Why the raw locale code (not the formatted tag) as payload** —
  DIP / SRP. The format ("(EN)") is a policy choice owned by the
  use case; the intent payload is the raw user-selected locale.
  A future onboarding revision (e.g., different tag format,
  device-region fallback) becomes a use-case-only change with no
  intent-shape impact.

### Strangler-fig boundary

The new `setLanguageEnabledWithFallback` impl method reaches into
the legacy `:shared` `SourcesRepository` via the existing
`SourcesRepositoryImpl` constructor injection (same posture as
§84.6's existing `setLanguageEnabled` impl). The legacy facade
keeps owning the cell-of-truth Room queries, the routing surface
(`findRepoByHost`, `activeRepoFlow`, `repoTaps`, `getUrl`,
`getEnabledRepos`), and the on-disk seed (`saveSources`). The
rework `:data` impl reaches in for ONLY `allSources` +
`enableDisAbleSource` — same narrow boundary as before this slice.

The legacy `RepoSettingsViewModel.setLanguageEnabledDefault` and
the legacy `SourcesScreen.kt:124-127` `LaunchedEffect` remain
in place and continue to serve the legacy onboarding route until
the future `Phase 7.x.sources.swap` retires `Screen.Sources` in
favor of the rework screen.

- `domain/.../usecase/sources/EnableDefaultLanguageSourcesUseCase.
  kt` (NEW)

### Files modified

- `domain/.../repository/SourcesRepository.kt` — add 4th method +
  KDoc covering Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingseed rationale.

  method + KDoc.

- `composeApp/.../di/SourcesReworkModule.kt` — add factory
  binding + bump `viewModel { ... }` to 5 args.
- `ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen.kt` — add `onboardingLanguageTag:
  String? = null` param + LaunchedEffect + KDoc subsection.

### Deferrals

- **No swap of legacy `Screen.Sources` onboarding route** — that
  becomes the next sibling slice (`Phase 7.x.sources.swap`). The
  rework screen now has the seed mechanism, the Finish button
  (§122), the InfoCard (§123), and the Request-Source dialog
  (§121) — full parity. The swap is a follow-on, NOT this slice.
- **No tag-format change** — the legacy uses parenthesised
  uppercase tags ("(EN)", "(FR)"); the rework matches verbatim
  because the Room rows are seeded that way (`saveSources`).
  Changing the format would require a Room migration (out of
  scope).
- **No i18n lift** — the new use case's tag-formatting is locale-
  code based, not human-readable string based; Phase 10 i18n lift

## §140 — Phase 7.x.sources.swap — Route-swap legacy onboarding `Screen.Sources` → rework `SourcesScreen` (Task #305)

### Strategy

Single-file route-swap rewrite of
`composeApp/.../navigation/routes/SourcesScreenRoute.kt` so the legacy
`Screen.Sources` onboarding-step-3 entry now renders the architecture-
rework `:ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen` backed by the rework
`:presentation/.../sources/SourcesViewModel`. Mirrors the single-file
route-swap posture from §125 (`history.swap`), §131 (`about.swap`),
§134 (`updates.swap`), §135 (`settings.swap`), and §138 (`theme.swap`):
the nav-graph type-safe `composable<Screen.Sources>` entry stays
bound; only the body of the route adapter is rewritten.

This swap was previously deferred (see §124 cross-reference) pending
four gap-lifts to bring the rework `SourcesScreen` to onboarding-step
parity:
1. **Request-Source dialog** — closed by §121
   (`Phase 7.x.sources.complaint`).
2. **Finish button surface** — closed by §122
   (`Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingfinish`).
3. **"Upcoming Languages" info card** — closed by §123
   (`Phase 7.x.sources.infocard`).
4. **Default-language source auto-seed** — closed by §139
   (`Phase 7.x.sources.onboardingseed`).

All four affordances are now ported. The swap rewrites the route
adapter to:
- Resolve the rework `me.manga.kira.presentation.sources.
  SourcesViewModel` via `koinViewModel()` (replacing the legacy
  `RepoSettingsViewModel`-backed onboarding adapter).
- Snapshot the user-selected language via
  `DataStoreHelper.languageFlow.collectAsState(initial = "")` and
  thread it as `onboardingLanguageTag = userLanguageCode` (the §139
  `LaunchedEffect(onboardingLanguageTag)` fires
  `SourcesIntent.OnSeedDefaultLanguage` on every non-null tag change,
  mirroring legacy `SourcesScreen.kt:124-127`'s
  `LaunchedEffect(userLanguageCode)` posture verbatim).
- Preserve the `onFinish = { navController.safeNavigate(Screen.
  RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true)) }` nav target verbatim — same
  next-step target as the pre-swap adapter.

### Onboarding chain — preserved verbatim, 4 steps

```
Welcome
  → Theme (rework via §138)
  → Sources (rework via THIS slice; §140)
  → RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true) (rework via §124)
  → Library
```

The 4-step structure is preserved deliberately. The §124 swap already
rewired step 4 (`Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true)`) to render
the SAME rework `SourcesScreen` with a Finish button that flips
`first_launch = false` + navigates to Library + clears the back-stack
through Welcome. This slice rewires step 3 (`Screen.Sources`) to also
render the rework `SourcesScreen` with a Finish button that advances
to step 4.

Step 3 / step 4 both rendering the rework `SourcesScreen` with a
Finish button is a pre-existing condition that §124's KDoc
explicitly anticipated. A future `Phase 9.x.onboarding.cleanup` can
collapse to 3 steps (advancing directly from step 3 to Library) if
desired — collapsing here would be a structural onboarding-chain
change beyond the scope of a route-swap slice.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:composeApp`** — 1 modified file:
  - `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/SourcesScreenRoute.kt` —
    rewritten. Pre-swap was a 36-line route adapter that resolved the
    legacy `RepoSettingsViewModel` via `koinViewModel()`, snapshotted
    its `repos` / `enabledLanguages` / `enabledExtensions` / `repoUrl`
    StateFlows, passed them as the 8 plain parameters to the legacy
    `composeApp/.../presentation/features/onboarding/sources/
    SourcesScreen.kt` composable, and dispatched mutations back
    through the legacy VM's setters. Post-swap is a 17-line adapter
    body (plus a 100+ line KDoc documenting the swap rationale) that
    resolves the rework `SourcesViewModel` via `koinViewModel()`,
    snapshots `DataStoreHelper.languageFlow` via `collectAsState`,
    and renders `me.manga.kira.ui.sources.SourcesScreen` with the
    three explicit params: `viewModel`, `onboardingLanguageTag =
    userLanguageCode`, `onFinish = { safeNavigate(Screen.
    RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true)) }`.
- **`:ui` / `:presentation` / `:domain` / `:data`** — unchanged. All
  affordance parity already landed via §84 (`Phase 7.x.sources`
  foundation), §121 (complaint), §122 (onboardingfinish), §123
  (infocard), and §139 (onboardingseed).
- **Legacy `:composeApp/.../presentation/features/onboarding/sources/
  SourcesScreen.kt`** still compiles and remains on the classpath —
  no longer reachable from the swapped `Screen.Sources` route. Phase
  9.x cleanup retires it once the swap is observed stable on user
  devices. The legacy `RepoSettingsViewModel` itself stays Koin-
  bound in `SharedModule` because other call sites still reference
  some of its methods (the legacy adapter was the last user-
  reachable consumer of `setLanguageEnabledDefault` specifically;
  the rest is a Phase 9.x concern).

### Affordance parity table

| Affordance | Pre-swap (legacy adapter) | Post-swap (rework adapter) |
|---|---|---|
| Per-language toggles | Legacy `SourcesScreen.kt` rendered a list of `LanguageRow` widgets with `Switch` + label per language | Rework `SourcesScreen` renders the equivalent `LanguageGroup` cards with Switch + label, same persisted state (`SourcesRepository.allSources.languages` via the legacy facade) |
| Per-source toggles | Legacy rendered a `SourceRow` per source with `Switch` + name + description | Rework renders the equivalent per-source list under each LanguageGroup with the same Switch + name + description |
| Request-Source dialog | Legacy invoked a `RepoUrlDialog` composable opened by an "Add repo URL" button | Rework `RequestSourceDialog` (§121) — same posture, same submission target |
| Finish button (if first-open) | Legacy gated a `if (isFirstOpen) FinishButton(onFinish)` block at the bottom | Rework `SourcesScreen` accepts `onFinish: (() -> Unit)?` and renders the Finish button iff non-null (§122). Adapter passes the same lambda (advance to `Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true)`) |
| Upcoming Languages info card | Legacy rendered an `InfoCard` with deferred-language copy | Rework `UpcomingLanguagesInfoCard` (§123) — always rendered |
| Default-language source auto-seed | Legacy `LaunchedEffect(userLanguageCode)` (legacy SourcesScreen.kt:124-127) called `vm.setLanguageEnabledDefault("(${tag.uppercase()})", true)` on every non-null tag change | Rework `LaunchedEffect(onboardingLanguageTag)` (§139) fires `SourcesIntent.OnSeedDefaultLanguage` on every non-null tag change. Adapter passes `onboardingLanguageTag = userLanguageCode` from the same `DataStoreHelper.languageFlow` source. Posture preserved verbatim |
| Onboarding advance | Legacy `onFinish = { navController.safeNavigate(Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true)) }` | Identical lambda, identical target, now passed into rework `SourcesScreen.onFinish` |

All pre-swap legacy affordances have a post-swap counterpart. No
observable behaviour regression on the per-language toggle, per-
source toggle, Request-Source dialog, Finish button, info card,
auto-seed, or onboarding-advance navigation.

### Visual delta

Material 3 default `Surface`/`Card`/`Switch` primitives on the
rework path vs the legacy's hand-styled wrappers on the pre-swap
path. Same semantic content, same controls, same persisted state.
The visual deltas are the canonical rework posture matching every
other route-swap that landed in §§286-290, §292, §293, §295, §301,
§138.

### Strangler-fig integrity

Unchanged. The swap moves the user-facing entry from the legacy
screen to the rework screen but the underlying `:data`
`SourcesRepositoryImpl` → legacy `:shared/.../sources/
SourcesRepository` facade reach (established by §84, extended by
§139 with the narrow `setLanguageEnabledWithFallback` method) is the
same. The legacy `SourcesRepository` facade is now consumed by
exactly one route's worth of sources-state per onboarding step (the
rework VM) at each entry instead of two-routes'-worth coexisting.

The `RepoSettingsViewModel`'s remaining surface still subscribes in
`SharedModule`'s `viewModel { ... }` factory for other call sites —
its remaining methods continue to consume the same underlying Room
rows the rework consumes, so the persisted state stays synchronized.

Both routes (`Screen.Sources` after this swap + `Screen.
RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = ...)` after §124) share the same
`SourcesRepository` `single` Koin lifecycle; toggle made on step 3
surfaces on step 4 via the upstream `allSources` flow re-emit.

### Koin lifecycle

Each route's `SourcesViewModel` is scoped to its own `NavBackStackEntry`
(the `ViewModelStoreOwner` integration provided by `androidx.lifecycle.
viewmodel.compose`). Step 3 (`Screen.Sources` after this swap) and
step 4 (`Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true)` after §124) resolve
DIFFERENT VM instances scoped to their own back-stack entries — each
route's VM is independent. The underlying `:domain` `SourcesRepository`
(and its `:data` impl over the legacy `:shared` facade) is shared
`single` across both routes, so the persisted state is identical and
changes flow through the upstream re-emission.

## §141 — Phase 7.x.welcome — Welcome screen rework + route-swap (Task #306)

### Strategy

Two-file slice (one new `:ui` composable + one route-adapter rewrite)
that moves the onboarding-step-1 Welcome screen onto the architecture-
rework stack. The new `:ui` composable is a verbatim stateless port of
the legacy `composeApp/.../presentation/features/onboarding/welcome/
WelcomeScreen.kt` minus the cosmetic `AnimatedBackground` gradient
sweep (matches §122 / §138 precedent — purely cosmetic, no semantic
value, skipped on rework consistently across the onboarding flow).

This is the **simplest** route-swap slice landed to date: Welcome is
genuinely stateless. There is no state, no business logic, no
persisted preference reads, no domain entities, no use cases, no MVI
surface, no Koin module needed. The legacy composable was already a
75-line pure-Compose display with a single `onGetStarted: () -> Unit`
callback. Adding empty `:domain`/`:data`/`:presentation` layers would
be premature abstraction — the rework Welcome is what an architecturally
ideal "pure display" screen looks like, and the slice is structured
to match.

### Onboarding chain — preserved verbatim, 4 steps end-to-end-rework

With this swap landing, the entire onboarding wizard now consumes the
rework stack at every step:

```
Welcome  (rework via THIS slice; §141)
  → Theme (rework via §138)
  → Sources (rework via §140 — onboarding step 3)
  → RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true) (rework via §124 — onboarding step 4)
  → Library
```

The 4-step chain is preserved verbatim — same step count, same nav
targets, same Finish-on-step-4 destination (Library) + same
`first_launch = false` flip semantics (lives inside `RepoSettings
ScreenRoute.onFinish` per §124). The deliberate decision NOT to
collapse step 3 / step 4 into a single step (carried over from §140)
is unchanged here; a future `Phase 9.x.onboarding.cleanup` can revisit
the chain shape now that every step renders the rework stack.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:domain`** — unchanged. Welcome has no domain entities, no use
  cases, no repository interfaces. Stateless display.
- **`:data`** — unchanged. Welcome reads nothing persisted, mutates
  nothing.
- **`:presentation`** — unchanged. No MVI surface, no `WelcomeState`,
  no `WelcomeIntent`, no `WelcomeEffect`, no `WelcomeViewModel`.
  Adding any of these would be premature abstraction for a stateless
  display.
- **`:ui`** — 1 NEW file:
  - `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/welcome/Welcome
    Screen.kt` — stateless `@Composable fun WelcomeScreen(onGet
    Started: () -> Unit)`. Surface → Box → (vertical-gradient
    legibility overlay Box) → Column with Title Text ("Welcome to
    Yami Manga", 36sp ExtraBold primary), Subtitle Text ("Explore,
    read and collect manga with ease.", 18sp onBackground 0.9
    alpha), Spacer 24.dp, Material 3 Button (52.dp height, Rounded
    CornerShape(26.dp) clip, primary container, onPrimary "Get
    Started" label). The visible strings preserved VERBATIM from
    legacy `values/strings.xml: welcome_title / welcome_suptitle /
    get_started`. Inline literal strings (consistent with every
    other rework `:ui` screen — Phase 10 i18n lift unifies both
    consumers in one pass).
- **`:composeApp`** — 1 MODIFIED file:
  - `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/
    routes/WelcomeScreenRoute.kt` — body rewritten. Pre-swap rendered
    the legacy `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.onboarding.
    welcome.WelcomeScreen` composable; post-swap renders the new
    `me.manga.kira.ui.welcome.WelcomeScreen` composable. Nav
    target unchanged — `onGetStarted = { navController.navigate
    (Screen.Theme) }`. The `backStackEntry` parameter is preserved
    with `@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER")` for nav-graph signature
    parity (same posture as the pre-swap adapter — Compose-MP's
    `composable<Screen.Welcome>(...)` block always hands one to its
    content lambda even when the route is parameter-less).

- **Koin** — unchanged. No new module, no `welcomeReworkModule`. The
  rework Welcome composable takes its single `onGetStarted` lambda
  from the route adapter directly — there is nothing to inject. The
  `allReworkModules()` aggregate is unchanged.

### Affordance parity table

| Affordance | Pre-swap (legacy adapter) | Post-swap (rework adapter) |
|---|---|---|
| Title text | "Welcome to Yami Manga" (legacy `R.string.welcome_title`) | "Welcome to Yami Manga" (inline literal on rework — same string, Phase 10 unifies via `stringResource`) |
| Subtitle text | "Explore, read and collect manga with ease." (legacy `R.string.welcome_suptitle`) | "Explore, read and collect manga with ease." (inline literal on rework — same string) |
| Get-Started button | Material 3 Button, 52.dp height, RoundedCornerShape(26.dp) clip, primary container, onPrimary "Get Started" label | Identical Material 3 Button — same height, same clip, same colors, same label text |
| Get-Started button label | "Get Started" (legacy `R.string.get_started`) | "Get Started" (inline literal on rework — same string) |
| Get-Started nav target | `navController.navigate(Screen.Theme)` | Identical nav target — same `Screen.Theme` destination (rework via §138) |
| Vertical-gradient legibility overlay | `Brush.verticalGradient` from `background.copy(alpha = 0.1f)` to opaque `background` | Identical overlay — same colors, same alphas, same brush stops. **Preserved as legibility shim, not decoration** |
| `animateContentSize(tween(600))` | Applied to the bottom-aligned content column | Identical — same modifier, same tween duration |
| `AnimatedBackground` gradient sweep (`me.manga.kira.presentation.features.onboarding.components.AnimatedBackground`) | Rendered behind the content column | **Intentionally omitted** — matches §122 / §138 precedent. Purely cosmetic, no semantic value. Welcome is the third (and final) onboarding screen to omit it on rework |

All semantic content + the legibility shim + the content-animation
spec are preserved verbatim. Only the cosmetic animated background
sweep is omitted (intentionally, consistent with the rest of the
rework onboarding chain).

### Visual delta

Three intentional visual deltas vs the legacy `WelcomeScreen.kt`,
all consistent with §122 / §138 precedent:

1. **AnimatedBackground omission** — see Affordance parity table
   above. Purely cosmetic, no semantic value. Matches §122
   (Sources onboarding-finish) + §138 (Theme swap) precedent — the
   three onboarding screens all skip the equivalent legacy
   decorative background on rework.
2. **Inline literal strings** — same approach as every other
   rework `:ui` screen (SourcesScreen, SettingsScreen, etc.).
   Phase 10 i18n lift unifies legacy + rework consumers in one
   pass through a shared `stringResource` lookup.
3. **Material 3 default `Surface`/`Box`/`Column`/`Button` primitives**
   used directly — no `LocalSpacing` design tokens added because
   Welcome doesn't have a multi-section layout that benefits from
   them. The single Column padding (24.dp) is inline.

Net: same screen minus the animated gradient sweep. The bottom-
aligned content column (title + subtitle + button), the vertical-
gradient legibility overlay, the 600ms animateContentSize, the
button styling, and the nav target are all preserved verbatim.

### Strangler-fig integrity

N/A — Welcome reads nothing persisted, reaches into nothing in
`:shared`. This slice does NOT extend any strangler-fig boundary;
the `:data` → `:shared` reach surface stays exactly as it was
before this slice landed.

### Koin lifecycle

N/A — no VM bound, no module registered. The rework Welcome
composable is stateless and takes its single `onGetStarted: () ->
Unit` callback from the route adapter directly. The `allRework
Modules()` aggregate is unchanged.

KDoc refreshed to document the swap rationale, the 4-step onboarding chain (now end-to-end rework), the stateless-no-VM rationale, the legacy file disposition. |

## §143 — Phase 9.y.onboardingvm_retire — Retire :shared OnboardingViewModel

### Strategy

First Phase 9.y cleanup slice. Pure-retirement sweep retiring the
now-unreachable `:shared` `OnboardingViewModel` class + its
`SharedModule.kt` Koin binding. Identified as the next non-blocked
candidate immediately after §142 (Phase 9.x.onboarding.legacy_retire,
Task #307) landed.

With §142 having deleted the 5 legacy onboarding UI files from
`composeApp/.../presentation/features/onboarding/`, the
`OnboardingViewModel` they consumed via `koinViewModel()` had no
remaining resolution call sites in production code. The class +
binding became dead weight in the strangler-fig boundary — bound but
never resolved.

This slice retires the dead weight in a 2-file sweep: delete the VM
class, remove its `import` line + `viewModel { ... }` binding from
`SharedModule.kt`. No replacements, no behaviour change.

### Reachability verification

Performed via Grep before deletion:

- `OnboardingViewModel` symbol-grep across `**/*.kt`:
  - `shared/.../OnboardingViewModel.kt:10` — class declaration itself.
  - `shared/.../SharedModule.kt:23` — import.
  - `shared/.../SharedModule.kt:326` — `viewModel { OnboardingViewModel(
    get()) }` Koin binding.
  - `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:
    31, 52, 104, 107` — KDoc comment text only.
  - `composeApp/.../di/ThemeReworkModule.kt:39` — KDoc comment text
    only.
  - `data/.../ThemeRepositoryImpl.kt:25` — KDoc comment text only.
  - `data/.../LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:26` — KDoc comment text only.
  - `domain/.../ThemeRepository.kt:26` — KDoc comment text only.
- `OnboardingViewModel` symbol-grep across `**/*.{swift,h,m,kts,gradle,
  xml}`: NO MATCHES.
- `koinViewModel|getViewModel|get\(\).*OnboardingViewModel|
  OnboardingViewModel\(\)` symbol-grep across `**/*.kt`: only the
  binding line at `SharedModule.kt:326`. No resolution call sites
  in production code.

Empirically confirmed by all 4 build gates returning green AFTER the
sweep — if any production consumer existed, compile would have
broken.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:core` — unchanged.
- `:domain` — unchanged. `ThemeRepository.kt:26` KDoc comment text
  referencing the retired VM becomes a stale comment; harmless, not
  load-bearing.
- `:data` — unchanged. KDoc comment text in `ThemeRepositoryImpl.kt:
  25` + `LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:26` referencing the retired VM
  becomes stale comments; harmless.
- `:presentation` — unchanged.
- `:ui` — unchanged.
- `:platform` — unchanged.
- `:composeApp` — unchanged. KDoc comment text in `ThemeReworkModule.
  kt:39` + `ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:31, 52, 104, 107` referencing
  the retired VM becomes stale comments; harmless.
- `:shared` — 1 file DELETED + 1 file MODIFIED (the only module
  touched):
  - `shared/.../presentation/features/onboarding/viewmodel/Onboarding
    ViewModel.kt` — DELETED. 28 lines (Compose-Multiplatform `ViewModel`
    exposing `darkMode: StateFlow<Boolean>` + `followSystem: StateFlow<
    Boolean>` + `toggleDarkMode(on)` + `toggleFollowSystem(on)`, all
    backed by `SettingsRepository`).
  - `shared/.../di/SharedModule.kt` — `import …OnboardingViewModel`
    line removed; `viewModel { OnboardingViewModel(get()) }` binding
    removed inside the Phase 9.6 ports VM block.

### Strangler-fig boundary

This retirement shrinks the `:shared` surface by one VM binding. The
remaining `:shared` VMs (`NotificationsViewModel`, `WebViewViewModel`,
`HomeViewModel`, `DownloadViewModelv2`, etc.) + the legacy repositories
they consume continue to participate in the boundary until their own
retirement slices land. The `SettingsRepository` dep that
`OnboardingViewModel` had previously consumed remains bound (consumed
by other VMs including `SettingsViewModel`).

### Visual delta

None. The retired VM was no-longer-resolved-anywhere before this slice
landed — no user sees its output today. The sweep is invisible to end-
users; it only cleans the codebase.

### Behaviour preservation

## §144 — Phase 9.z.dead_vm_retire — Retire :shared NotificationsViewModel + TextViewModel

### Strategy

Second Phase 9.y/z cleanup slice. Pure-retirement sweep retiring two
now-unreachable `:shared` ViewModels in a single batched commit:

1. `NotificationsViewModel` (99 lines) — the legacy notifications-feed
   VM consumed by the pre-`5b44b9c` legacy `UpdatesScreen`. After Phase
   7.x.updates.swap (Task #289, commit `5b44b9c`) rewired
   `Screen.Updates` to the rework `:ui` `UpdatesScreen` backed by the
   rework `:presentation` `UpdatesViewModel`, the legacy VM had zero
   resolution call sites in production code.
2. `TextViewModel` (28 lines) — a legacy counter stub
   (`number: StateFlow<Int>` + `increase()` backed by a
   `SavedStateHandle`-stored `"counter"` key). Has no resolution call
   sites anywhere in the codebase — never consumed.

Both VMs identified as the next non-blocked Rule 3 candidates after
§143 (Phase 9.y.onboardingvm_retire, Task #308) landed. Batched into
one slice per §142 precedent (which retired 5 legacy onboarding UI
files together) — 3 files affected total, well within the 5-file cap.

### Reachability verification

Performed via Grep before deletion. The two VMs and their resolution
patterns were checked exhaustively:

**`NotificationsViewModel`** symbol-grep across `**/*.kt`:

- `shared/.../NotificationsViewModel.kt` — class declaration itself.
- `shared/.../SharedModule.kt:22` — import.
- `shared/.../SharedModule.kt:324` — `viewModel { NotificationsViewModel(get()) }`.
- `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/UpdatesScreenRoute.kt:18-20, 25` —
  KDoc comment text only (post-swap historical reference, not a
  resolution site).
- No other matches anywhere.

`koinViewModel<NotificationsViewModel>|: NotificationsViewModel = koinViewModel`
symbol-grep: ZERO matches in production code. The rework
`UpdatesScreenRoute.kt` resolves `UpdatesViewModel`, not the legacy VM.

**`TextViewModel`** symbol-grep across `**/*.kt`:

- `shared/.../TextViewModel.kt` — class declaration itself.
- `shared/.../SharedModule.kt:27` — import.
- `shared/.../SharedModule.kt:343-344` — orphan comment + `viewModel
  { TextViewModel(get()) }` binding.
- `shared/.../SharedModule.kt:345` — adjacent KDoc text mentioning
  "same pattern as TextViewModel" (comment-only reference to the
  retiring VM's pattern).
- No other matches anywhere.

`koinViewModel<TextViewModel>|: TextViewModel = koinViewModel`
symbol-grep: ZERO matches anywhere in the codebase. TextViewModel was
a never-consumed legacy stub.

Cross-platform check (`**/*.{swift,h,m,kts,gradle,xml}`): ZERO matches
for either VM.

Empirically confirmed by all 4 build gates returning green AFTER the
sweep — if any production consumer existed for either VM, compile
would have broken.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:core` — unchanged.
- `:domain` — unchanged.
- `:data` — unchanged.
- `:presentation` — unchanged. The rework `:presentation/.../updates/
  UpdatesViewModel` (a Phase 7.x.updates port) continues to serve the
  notifications-feed surface via the same `NotificationRepository`
  strangler-fig over the same legacy `notifications` Room table.
- `:ui` — unchanged. The rework `:ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen` is the
  ONLY screen rendered for `Screen.Updates` post-§129 (Phase
  7.x.updates.swap).
- `:platform` — unchanged.
- `:composeApp` — unchanged. KDoc comment text in `UpdatesScreenRoute.
  kt:18-20, 25` referencing the retired `NotificationsViewModel` as
  historical context becomes a stale comment; harmless, not load-
  bearing.
- `:shared` — 2 files DELETED + 1 file MODIFIED (the only module
  touched):
  - `shared/.../presentation/features/notifications/ui/viewmodel/
    NotificationsViewModel.kt` — DELETED. 99 lines (class taking
    `NotificationRepository` dep + exposing `uiState: StateFlow<
    NotificationsUiState>` + `markAsRead` / `markAllAsRead` /
    `deleteAll` / `delete` / `deleteWithUndo` / `undoDelete` /
    `confirmDelete` mutations).
  - `shared/.../presentation/features/text/viewmodel/TextViewModel.kt`
    — DELETED. 28 lines (a `SavedStateHandle`-backed counter VM
    exposing `number: StateFlow<Int>` + `increase()`).
  - `shared/.../di/SharedModule.kt` — 2 imports + 2 binding lines + 1
    orphan comment removed (5 lines total). Surrounding bindings
    untouched.

### Strangler-fig boundary

This retirement shrinks the `:shared` surface by two VM bindings. The
remaining 19 `:shared` VMs (`WebViewViewModel`, `HomeViewModel`,
`DownloadViewModelv2`, `ComplaintViewModel`, `AdminComplaintViewModel`,
`StatisticsViewModel`, `HistoryViewModel`, `LanguageViewModel`,
`UpdateSourcesViewModel`, etc.) + the legacy repositories they consume
continue to participate in the boundary until their own retirement
slices land. The `NotificationRepository` dep that
`NotificationsViewModel` had consumed remains bound (the rework
`:data` `UpdatesRepositoryImpl` continues to bridge across it — see
§129's strangler-fig description).

### Visual delta

None. Both retired VMs were no-longer-resolved-anywhere before this
slice landed — no user sees their output today. The sweep is invisible
to end-users; it only cleans the codebase.

### Behaviour preservation

ZERO observable behaviour delta. Specifically:

- The Updates feed (bottom-nav tab → `Screen.Updates`) continues to
  render via the rework `:ui` `UpdatesScreen` backed by the rework
  `:presentation` `UpdatesViewModel`. All affordances
  (mark-read/mark-all-read/delete/delete-with-undo/per-row-download)
  flow through the rework VM's reducer + the rework `:data`
  `UpdatesRepositoryImpl` strangler-fig over the same legacy
  `notifications` Room table. Source of truth preserved verbatim.
- `TextViewModel` had no user-visible surface — it was a never-
  consumed stub. Its retirement is a no-op for users.

## §146 — Phase 9.ab.stale_kdoc.sweep — Refresh stale KDoc references to retired symbols

Task #311. Source commits: `eae48ba` (sweep A), `cf9f170` (sweep B),
`a3b5847` (sweep C). Plan commit: `6195383`.

### Strategy

A pure doc-text sweep refreshing 13 KDoc text references across 11
files that mention symbols retired in §142–§145. The retired-symbol
references were classified as "acceptable per §142 policy" (KDoc text
is not load-bearing; doesn't affect compilation or IDE autocomplete)
during each retirement slice's close-out. This slice elevates them
from "accepted" to "refreshed" — finer state of the same policy.

The §145 close-out enumerated this doc-sweep as the top non-blocked
candidate. After §145 erroneously also listed "Statistics screen
rework" as the next candidate (a stale carry-over from a
pre-completion plan file in `~/.claude/plans/`; the Statistics rework
landed as Task #238 in commits `fdc9c8a`–`5eae2c8` and was swapped in
as `Screen.Statistics` via Task #286 commit `9faa4b7`), pre-flight
recon for this slice confirmed the Statistics rework is fully
complete and corrected the next-candidate to the doc-sweep — the
single zero-recon, ≤5-files-per-commit, no-build-gate-risk candidate.

### Edit semantics

For each stale reference, the edit follows one of three patterns:

1. **Drop the retired-symbol mention, keep live consumers.** Used
   when the comment lists multiple consumers and only one is retired:
   `(SettingsViewModel, OnboardingViewModel)` → `SettingsViewModel`
   plus an annotation noting `OnboardingViewModel` was retired in
   §143.

2. **Replace the retired-symbol mention with its rework equivalent.**
   Used when the comment describes the current consumption pattern:
   `NotificationsUiState / UI layer` → `UpdatesState / UpdatesScreen`.

3. **Leave the historical past-tense reference, add a retirement
   annotation.** Used when the comment describes the pre-swap state
   as accurate history: "this file previously hosted the legacy
   `UpdatesScreen` backed by `NotificationsViewModel`" → same plus
   "(legacy screen retired in §145, legacy VM retired in §144)".

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

| Layer | Touch | Surface |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `:core` | none | n/a |
| `:domain` | MODIFY | `ThemeRepository.kt:26`, `EnqueueDownloadUseCase.kt:26` |
| `:data` | MODIFY | `ThemeRepositoryImpl.kt:25`, `LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:26` |
| `:presentation` | MODIFY | `UpdatesIntent.kt:74` |
| `:shared` | MODIFY | `SharedModule.kt:345`, `NotificationRepository.kt:26` |
| `:ui` | none | n/a |
| `:composeApp` | MODIFY | `ThemeReworkModule.kt:39`, `UpdatesReworkModule.kt:22/34`, `ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:104`, `UpdatesScreenRoute.kt:17` |

Eleven files across five layers. Each commit ≤5 files (Sweep A: 4
files in `:domain` + `:data`; Sweep B: 3 files in `:presentation` +
`:shared`; Sweep C: 4 files in `:composeApp`).

### Strangler-fig boundary

Unchanged. The KDoc edits update prose accuracy; they don't change
which interfaces or impls are bound, who consumes them, or which
direction the dependencies flow. The same strangler-fig boundaries
that existed before the sweep exist after.

### Visual delta

None. KDoc comments do not affect compiled output, IDE autocomplete,
or end-user behaviour. The slice's only effect is to source-code
readers reading KDoc prose.

### Behaviour preservation

Verified empirically: all four build gates GREEN. KDoc text edits
cannot introduce a behaviour change because the Kotlin compiler
treats comment content as opaque — only comment-block boundaries
(`/**` `*/`) are parsed. No malformed boundaries were introduced
(empirically: the gates compile cleanly).

`LibraryIntent.OnDeleteSelected` which immediately invoked
`BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` — no safety affordance, an accidental
tap permanently destroyed all selected manga plus their progress,
read status, bookmarks, and downloaded chapters.

The legacy `LibraryScreenRoute.kt:111-172` already shipped an
`AlertDialog` for the single-manga delete flow; this slice ports that
posture, adapted to the rework's bulk-delete (multi-select) shape.

The slice was selected via the §146 close-out's Rule 3 ladder. Of the
non-blocked candidates (Home screen rework, Library route-swap,
MangaDetails route-swap, further VM retirements), Home rework
required a planning round, route-swaps were multi-slice undertakings,
and Reader-side candidates remain blocked on Task #217. A single-file
intent rename plus a single-file dialog composable is the smallest
zero-recon slice that genuinely improves the rework's user-facing
posture.

### MVI shape decision: state-driven dialog visibility

Two viable patterns for dialog visibility:

1. **Composition-local `mutableStateOf`** — the dialog's open/closed
   flag lives in the screen's `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }`,
   set true by an onClick and false on dismiss.
2. **State-driven** — the open/closed flag lives in the MVI `State`;
   the screen renders the dialog when `state.isDeleteDialogVisible`
   is true; transitions are intent-driven.

The legacy uses pattern (1) — composition-local `mangaToDelete:
Manga?` captured by the route file. The rework uses pattern (2):
`isDeleteDialogVisible: Boolean` lives in `LibraryState`. Three
reasons:

- **Configuration changes** — pattern (1) loses state on rotation
  unless the screen wraps it in `rememberSaveable` (which the legacy
  doesn't). Pattern (2) survives because `LibraryViewModel`'s
  `ViewModelScope` outlives the activity recreation.
- **MVI purity** — the rework's "every visible UI state lives in
  `State`" invariant means there is exactly one source of truth for
  what the screen is displaying.
- **Future bulk-actions extensibility** — if Phase 7.x.* later adds
  bulk-archive or bulk-export, the same MVI shape extends with
  `isArchiveDialogVisible` / `isExportDialogVisible` without
  recourse to composition-local hacks.

### Intent surface changes

The existing `LibraryIntent.OnDeleteSelected` is renamed semantically
(call-site name preserved):

- **Before:** `OnDeleteSelected` → VM immediately calls
  `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`.
- **After:** `OnDeleteSelected` → VM stages
  `isDeleteDialogVisible = true` (no mutation).

Two new variants added:

- `OnDeleteSelectedConfirm` → VM clears selection + dismisses dialog
  + invokes `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase`.
- `OnDeleteSelectedDismiss` → VM clears dialog flag (selection
  stays).

The UI call site (`Delete` button) still dispatches
`OnDeleteSelected` — no churn on the existing button click handler.
Only the VM's interpretation of that intent changed.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

| Layer | Touch | Surface |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `:core` | none | n/a |
| `:domain` | none | n/a (use case unchanged) |
| `:data` | none | n/a |
| `:presentation` | MODIFY | `LibraryState.kt` (+1 field), `LibraryIntent.kt` (+2 variants, rewrite KDoc), `LibraryViewModel.kt` (split handler) |
| `:ui` | MODIFY | `LibraryScreen.kt` (+`DeleteSelectedDialog` composable + render branch) |
| `:composeApp` | none | n/a (route adapter untouched) |

Four files, two layers. One commit.

### Strangler-fig boundary

Unchanged. The slice is entirely above the use-case interface —
`BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` is invoked from the same VM with the
same call site (the use-case interface, its `:data` impl, and its
strangler-fig reach into `:shared` are all untouched). The
confirmation gate sits above the use case, not around it.

### Visual delta

- **Before:** "Delete" button tap permanently removes selected
  manga immediately.
- **After:** "Delete" button tap opens a Material 3 `AlertDialog`
  with title "Delete *N* manga?", a body warning that progress /
  read status / bookmarks / downloaded chapters will be
  permanently lost, an error-coloured "Delete" confirm button,
  and a neutral "Cancel" dismiss button. Tapping confirm performs
  the deletion; tapping cancel / tapping outside / system-back
  closes the dialog with selection mode still active.

### Behaviour preservation

Bulk-delete still works end-to-end; only the user-interaction shape
changed. The success path (selection cleared + snackbar shown via
`LibraryEffect.ShowBulkRemoveSuccess`) is identical to before — the
new confirmation step is purely additive in the dispatch chain.

Empirical verification: all four build gates GREEN. The rework
Library route is debug-guarded, so the change is reachable only via
the debug nav entry; the legacy `Screen.Library` route still
renders the legacy `LibraryScreen` with the unmodified per-manga
delete flow.

| `presentation/.../library/LibraryIntent.kt` | :presentation | MODIFIED | +2 variants, KDoc rewrite |

| `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` | :ui | MODIFIED | +`DeleteSelectedDialog`, +render branch, +`AlertDialog` import |

Total: +124 / −5 lines.

All four ran cleanly AFTER the source commit (`99aaecf`). Warnings

introduced by this slice.

### Deferrals

- **Per-manga delete on rework Library** — out of scope. The rework
