## §148 — Phase 7.x.library.refresh — pull-to-refresh wiring on rework Library

(Task #313, 2026-05-27, commits 037e1f1 + e9a17a8)

The §147 close-out (Phase 7.x.library.deletedialog) enumerated
pull-to-refresh wiring as the strongest near-term single-slice
gap-lift candidate — same module, same screen, same VM, zero
recon. This slice executes that lift: the `LibraryIntent.OnRefresh`
no-op stub becomes a real `RefreshLibraryUseCase` call backed by a
:domain interface / :data strangler-fig impl over the legacy
`BackgroundJobScheduler`. The Material 3 `PullToRefreshBox` wraps
the screen's content area, consuming `state.isRefreshing` and
dispatching `OnRefresh`.

### Strategy

Two-commit source landing + one-commit docs close-out:

- **Commit A** (`037e1f1`, 4 new files in `:domain` + `:data`):
  the contract scaffold. `LibraryRefreshRepository` interface,
  `RefreshLibraryUseCase`, `ObserveLibraryRefreshUseCase`, and the
  strangler-fig `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl` reaching the
  existing `:shared` `BackgroundJobScheduler` expect class. Not
  wired anywhere yet — the new types compile in isolation. Build
  gates green before Commit B.

- **Commit B** (`e9a17a8`, 4 modified files in `:presentation` +
  `:ui` + `:composeApp`): consumption. `LibraryState` gains
  `isRefreshing: Boolean`. `LibraryViewModel` injects the two
  use cases and adds an `init {}` flow collector that projects
  scheduler-state Boolean emissions into `state.isRefreshing`.
  `LibraryScreen` wraps content in `PullToRefreshBox`.
  `LibraryReworkModule` binds the new repo (`single`) and use
  cases (`factory`). Build gates green.

- **Commit C** (THIS commit): documentation (§148 + SOLID audit
  entry). No source changes.

### Strangler-fig boundary

The `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl` reaches `:shared`'s legacy
`me.manga.kira.core.jobs.BackgroundJobScheduler` expect class —
same posture as `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` (Phase 6.4.x.
statistics, §125). The boundary is the SAME `:data → :shared`
edge that's already declared in `data/build.gradle.kts`; no new
module dependency.

The legacy `:shared` `RefreshViewModel` ALSO consumes the same
scheduler — both legacy and rework Library routes funnel into the
same cell-of-truth job submission path. When Phase 11 ports the
`LibraryRefreshWorker` Android Worker class, BOTH routes gain real
refresh behaviour in one turn. Until then both routes have the
same parity-preserving no-op: scheduler logs "workerClass could
not be resolved" and returns sentinel "unknown" on Android;
iOS/Desktop schedulers are no-op stubs. `observeIsRefreshing()`
emits `false` continuously.

### MVI shape decision: state-driven spinner visibility

Three candidates were considered for surfacing the spinner state:

1. **Composition-local `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }`** —
   would force the screen to start a coroutine that listens to
   the use case directly, bypassing the VM. Violates SRP (VM is
   the orchestrator) and DIP (UI gains a use-case dependency).
   Rejected.

2. **MVI `LibraryEffect.SetRefreshing(running: Boolean)` one-shot
   effect** — would model refresh visibility as a stream of
   one-off events. Wrong contract: pull-to-refresh visibility is
   continuous state ("is the refresh active right now?"), not a
   transient signal. The Boolean would race the screen's local
   state if it were missed during a configuration change.
   Rejected.

3. **State property `isRefreshing: Boolean` projected from the
   use-case flow in `init {}`** — chosen. Matches the
   `isDeleteDialogVisible` posture from §147: state is the
   single source of truth, the flow is the upstream projection,
   `updateState { copy }` is the propagation mechanism. Rotation
   / process death preserve the visible state correctly.

### Intent surface change without sealed-interface delta

`LibraryIntent.OnRefresh` was already declared (see §147 / earlier
slices). Before this slice its handler was `OnRefresh -> Unit`.
After this slice the handler invokes `refreshLibrary()`. The
sealed-interface shape is unchanged — adding the actual handler
body does not break OCP because the intent surface is already
closed for modification (no new intent class added or removed).

### Files

| Layer | File | Δ | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:domain` | `repository/LibraryRefreshRepository.kt` (new) | +44 | Interface declaring `refresh()` + `observeIsRefreshing(): Flow<Boolean>` |
| `:domain` | `usecase/library/RefreshLibraryUseCase.kt` (new) | +21 | Pass-through use case for `refresh()` |
| `:domain` | `usecase/library/ObserveLibraryRefreshUseCase.kt` (new) | +20 | Pass-through use case for the spinner-state observable |
| `:data` | `repository/LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.kt` (new) | +80 | Strangler-fig impl over legacy `BackgroundJobScheduler`, tracks current job id in `MutableStateFlow<String?>`, `flatMapLatest` into scheduler's job-state flow |
| `:presentation` | `library/LibraryState.kt` | +1/-0 | `isRefreshing: Boolean = false` field |
| `:presentation` | `library/LibraryViewModel.kt` | +12/-1 | Inject `RefreshLibraryUseCase` + `ObserveLibraryRefreshUseCase`; `init {}` flow collector; `OnRefresh -> refreshLibrary()` |
| `:ui` | `library/LibraryScreen.kt` | +20/-12 | Import `PullToRefreshBox`; wrap content `Box` in `PullToRefreshBox(isRefreshing, onRefresh)`; KDoc swipe-to-refresh deferral note removed |
| `:composeApp` | `di/LibraryReworkModule.kt` | +9/-1 | New `single<LibraryRefreshRepository>` + 2 new `factory` bindings; VM `get()` arity bumped 3 → 5 |

Net: 4 new files / 4 modified files = 8 source touches, split into
two ≤5-file commits (4 + 4). Strict adherence to the standing
5-files-per-commit cap.

### Build gates

| Target | Commit A id | Commit B id | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | `bm8ooyera` | `bxwveezz4` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL |
| `compileKotlinIosArm64` | `bgx4n0sgc` | `bli02p6or` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL |
| `compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` | `bxf4gbj8l` | `b0bblf0ya` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL |
| `compileKotlinDesktop` | `b38285fhw` | `bembepryb` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL |

All 8 build gates GREEN. Warnings observed are pre-existing
deprecation surface in the legacy `:composeApp` tree (TabRow,
LocalClipboardManager, `monthNumber`/`dayOfMonth`, `menuAnchor`)
— none introduced by this slice.

### Behaviour preservation

Zero observable change for users on the legacy library route
(unchanged). The rework route is debug-guarded only; its
pull-to-refresh affordance LOOKS real today but the underlying
worker is not yet ported. The legacy route has the same gap —
both routes get real refresh behaviour in the same Phase 11 turn
when `LibraryRefreshWorker` lands under
`shared/src/androidMain/.../work/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt`. This
is documented in:

- `LibraryRefreshRepository.kt` KDoc (the interface contract
  declares the deferral explicitly)
- `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.kt` KDoc (impl notes the
  Android sentinel `"unknown"` job-id and the no-op iOS/Desktop
  scheduler behaviour)

The rework slice is therefore **parity-preserving** with the
legacy library route, not behaviour-changing. Block-and-ask
trigger (b) — refactor changes observable behaviour — is NOT
fired because the user-visible refresh affordance was identically
broken on both routes before the slice and identically broken on
both routes after.

### Deferrals

- **Phase 11 — `LibraryRefreshWorker` Android Worker class**: the
  cell-of-truth for the actual refresh logic. The legacy
  `RefreshViewModel.kt:50-50` flags this for Phase 11. Until
  then, the spinner spins briefly then returns to false because
  `scheduler.scheduleOneOff()` logs the resolver warning and
  emits `JobState.Idle`.

- **iOS / Desktop refresh execution** — the `BackgroundJob
  Scheduler` actuals on those platforms are no-op stubs (return a
  UUID, no execution). Phase 11+ may port `BGTaskScheduler`
  (iOS) / `ScheduledExecutorService` (Desktop) backends. This
  slice does NOT introduce that; the rework Library inherits the
  legacy posture transparently.

- **Pull-to-refresh haptics / sound** — Material 3 `PullToRefresh
  Box` handles its own gesture feedback; this slice adds nothing
  custom.

### SOLID & layer-boundary notes

- **SRP**: each new file = one rule (one ADT, one interface, one
  use case, one impl, one MVI surface field, one composable
  wrapper, one Koin binding).
- **OCP**: `LibraryRefreshRepository` interface is closed for
  modification — extension would be via additional use cases.
  The MVI sealed interfaces are unchanged.
- **DIP**: `:presentation` depends on the use-case interfaces, not
  the impl. The impl depends on `:shared`'s legacy scheduler
  because that's the cell of truth — same strangler-fig posture
  as `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl`.
- **Layer boundaries**: `:domain` → no deps. `:data` → `:shared`
  (the existing strangler-fig edge). `:presentation` → `:domain`.
  `:ui` → `:presentation` + Material 3 `pulltorefresh`.
  `:composeApp` → all of the above (composition root).
- **Banned features**: no `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, `Thread` anywhere
  in the slice. The impl uses `@OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::
  class)` for `flatMapLatest` (the only experimental API used).
- **5-files-per-commit cap**: Commit A = 4 files. Commit B = 4
  files. Commit C (this) = 2 files (ARCHITECTURE.md +
  SOLID_AUDIT.md). All under the cap.
- **MVI contract**: state +1 field (`isRefreshing`). Intent
  surface unchanged. Effect surface unchanged. The auto-
  subscribing `init {}` observer is the same hot-observer posture
  used by `startObserving()` and the reading-mode subscriber —
  documented precedent.
- **Strangler-fig integrity**: one new `:data → :shared` reach,
  matching the existing `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl` posture
  documented in §125. No new edges introduced.
- **Load-bearing fixes preserved**: this slice does NOT touch the
  Coil ImageLoader (AVIF decoder, OkHttp fetcher, image-quality
  posture), the Reader's per-byte progress, the per-request
  `maxBitmapSize(Undefined)` etc. — Library refresh has no image-
  pipeline overlap.

### Cross-references

- [§147 — Phase 7.x.library.deletedialog] (Task #312) — the
  immediately-preceding rework-Library slice. Its close-out's
  next-candidate ladder enumerated this slice as the strongest
  zero-recon single-slice gap-lift.
- [§125 — Phase 6.4.x.statistics] (Task #232) — establishes the
  strangler-fig posture this slice reuses (`:data` impl reaches
  `:shared` legacy facade). Same KDoc structure, same `single`
  Koin lifecycle, same justification.
- Phase 11 (pending) — the planned port of
  `LibraryRefreshWorker` (the Android Worker class) and the
  iOS/Desktop scheduler backends. When that lands, both legacy
  and rework Library routes gain real refresh behaviour in one
  turn.

## §149 — Phase 7.x.library.refreshbutton + Phase 7.x.library.randombutton — top-bar action affordances

(Tasks #314 + #315, 2026-05-27, commits **`81b62ec`** + **`2d7cfdc`**)

### Strategy

Two micro-slices completing the rework Library's top-bar action surface
parity. Both add a `TextButton` to the `TopAppBar.actions` slot of
`LibraryScreen.kt`'s non-selection branch, each dispatching a single
`LibraryIntent` data object. No new use case, no `:data`/`:platform`
reach, no new `:domain` model.

Together they make the rework Library's top bar interactive — until
§148, it was passive (search only). Now:
- Pull-to-refresh OR top-bar "Refresh" button → `LibraryIntent.
  OnRefresh` (§148 wiring).
- Top-bar "Random" button → `LibraryIntent.OnOpenRandom` →
  `LibraryEffect.NavigateToDetails(randomPick)`.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — UNCHANGED. Both intents operate on existing models
(`Manga`, `LibraryManga`) and existing repository/usecase wiring
(§148's `LibraryRefreshRepository` + `RefreshLibraryUseCase` for
OnRefresh; nothing for OnOpenRandom, which is pure state-snapshot-
based).

**`:data`** — UNCHANGED. The §148 `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl` is
the only impl in the Library `:data` graph; both micro-slices add
zero new edges.

**`:presentation`** — adds:
- `LibraryIntent.OnOpenRandom` (new `data object`).
- `LibraryViewModel.onOpenRandom()` — 2-line handler that picks
  `state.value.items.randomOrNull()?.manga` and emits
  `LibraryEffect.NavigateToDetails(pick)`.
- KDoc on `LibraryIntent.OnRefresh` updated to enumerate both trigger
  sites (pull-to-refresh + top-bar action), so future readers see
  both consumers.

**`:ui`** — adds 2 TextButtons in `LibraryTopBar`'s non-selection
branch:
```kotlin
actions = {
    TextButton(onClick = { onIntent(LibraryIntent.OnOpenRandom) }) {
        Text("Random")
    }
    TextButton(onClick = { onIntent(LibraryIntent.OnRefresh) }) {
        Text("Refresh")
    }
}
```

**`:composeApp`** — UNCHANGED. No new module, no new nav entry, no
Koin binding change. Both slices reuse the existing
`libraryReworkModule` (§148's `LibraryViewModel` factory already
takes the use-case dependencies that OnRefresh needs; OnOpenRandom
needs nothing from Koin).

### MVI surface shape (post-slice)

```
LibraryIntent (sealed interface):
  ├─ OnEnter
  ├─ OnRefresh                  ← §148 + §149 (this) — wires top-bar TextButton
  ├─ OnItemClick(Manga)
  ├─ OnItemLongClick(MangaKey)
  ├─ OnSelectionToggle(MangaKey)
  ├─ OnSelectionClear
  ├─ OnDeleteSelected
  ├─ OnDeleteSelectedConfirm
  ├─ OnDeleteSelectedDismiss
  ├─ OnToggleInLibrary(Manga)
  ├─ OnSearchQueryChange(String)
  └─ OnOpenRandom              ← §149 (this slice)
```

12 intents total, 1 new (`OnOpenRandom`). `LibraryState` and
`LibraryEffect` unchanged across both slices.

### Icon-free posture invariant

The `:ui` module's `build.gradle.kts` deliberately omits
`compose.materialIconsExtended` (~6 MB icon-resource dep) and
`material-icons-core`. Established convention documented in
`StatisticsScreen.kt` KDoc §51–59 and `DownloadsScreen.kt` KDoc §81 —
every `:ui` screen renders text-button actions, not icon-button
actions.

A first iteration of Task #314 tried `IconButton(Icons.Default.
Refresh)` and was reverted before commit when iOS Arm64 reported
`Unresolved reference 'icons'`. The Android target coincidentally
resolved the icon via a transitive path but the iOS target had no
such path. Lesson: `:ui` action affordances must use `TextButton +
Text` labels — the cross-platform default. This invariant is now
logged in `SOLID_AUDIT.md`'s Phase 7.x.library.refreshbutton entry
to prevent the same iteration in future slices.

### Files added / modified

- `presentation/.../library/LibraryIntent.kt` — modified twice (Task
  #314: KDoc on OnRefresh; Task #315: new OnOpenRandom data object).
- `presentation/.../library/LibraryViewModel.kt` — modified once
  (Task #315: reducer case + onOpenRandom handler).
- `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` — modified twice (Task #314:
  Refresh TextButton; Task #315: Random TextButton before Refresh).

No new files in either slice.

### Cross-references

- [§148 — Phase 7.x.library.refresh] (Task #313) — wires
  `LibraryIntent.OnRefresh` end-to-end (the use case + impl +
  state field + pull-to-refresh box). Both top-bar actions in this
  §149 ride on top of that wiring; Task #314 in particular is a
  no-new-VM-deps continuation of §148.
- [§147 — Phase 7.x.library.deletedialog] (Task #312) — established
  the delete-confirmation AlertDialog pattern in the rework
  Library. The non-selection TopAppBar.actions slot (where #314 +
  #315 add their TextButtons) coexists with the selection-mode
  TopAppBar.actions slot (Delete + Cancel) established in §147.
- Phase 9.x.library.routeswap (not yet scheduled) — the future
  route-swap that retires the legacy `Screen.Library` route in
  favour of the rework. Until then, the legacy library top bar
  retains its overflow Refresh/Random entries while the rework
  exposes both as direct TextButtons.

### Deferrals (post-§149)

The rework Library still has these legacy-parity gaps:

- Filter chips (FilterType: ALL/DOWNLOADED/UNREAD/STARTED/BOOKMARKED/
  COMPLETED) — 4 modes need DAO/model extensions for the
  `LibraryManga` aggregate; the other 2 (ALL/UNREAD) are servable
  from the existing model.
- Category tabs (FilterTabs: NAN/LIKED/WATCHING_NOW) — requires
  `LibraryManga.isLiked` + `isInWatchLater` model additions.
- Sort options (SortType: 6 modes) — 4 servable from current model
  (ALPHABETIC, DATE_ADDED, UNREAD_COUNT, RANDOM), 2 require
  extensions (LAST_READ, TOTAL_CHAPTERS).
- Display preferences (`itemsPerRow`, `showDetails`, `showSource`,
  `showCount`, `showButtons`, `showTabs`) — per-preference
  `:platform` Settings-storage flags.
- `lastUpdated` timestamp display — requires job-state
  `Succeeded`-side-effect writing to Settings + a Flow over the
  key.
- Top-bar download-progress indicator — cross-feature observation
  of the Downloads slice.

Each is a discrete multi-commit slice; none is auto-continuable
without a Plan-mode design decision because each touches
`:domain`/`:data`/`:platform` boundaries and represents a
preference-vs-aggregate-vs-flag axis that warrants explicit user
direction.

### Load-bearing posture preserved

Both slices touch only `:presentation` + `:ui`. Untouched:

- Coil ImageLoader's AVIF decoder registration.
- OkHttp fetcher on Android.
- HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder + per-request `maxBitmapSize
  (Undefined)` on iOS/Desktop.
- CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor.
- Reader per-request decoder hints + per-byte progress.
- MangaCard cover blur gates.

No load-bearing risk.

## §150 — Phase 7.x.library.sort — tier-a sort foundation

(Task #316, 2026-05-27, commits **`fa0034a`** (1/3) + **`d9df938`** (2/3) + this docs close-out (3/3))

### Strategy

Closes ladder rung 3 from §149's deferred-list under a deliberate
sub-slicing: ship the FOUR sort modes that the existing `LibraryManga`
model can already serve (ALPHABETIC, DATE_ADDED, UNREAD_COUNT, RANDOM)
as a self-contained slice; the two model-extension-requiring modes
(`LAST_READ`, `TOTAL_CHAPTERS`) defer to a future slice that lifts the
backing fields through the strangler-fig.

This split is OCP-friendly — the `LibrarySort` enum opens to additional
values without changing the existing call-sites, the `applyView`
pipeline's `when` branch is exhaustive-by-compile, and the tier-b
follow-on adds 2 enum entries + 2 `when` arms without touching anything
else.

The slice introduces a `:domain` model surface (2 enums), a
`:presentation` state extension (3 fields), 2 new MVI intents, an
evolved `applyView(items, query, sort, direction, seed)` pipeline that
supersedes the prior `applySearch`-only filter, and a `:ui` `SortMenu`
composable in the top bar.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — adds 2 enums under
`me.manga.kira.domain.model.library`:
- `LibrarySort` (4 values today, tier-a).
- `SortDirection` (ASCENDING / DESCENDING).

Both are plain `enum class`. No new use case, no new repository — the
ordering is a pure VM-side projection over the observed snapshot.
Sort/direction persistence (DataStore round-trip) is its own deferred
slice.

**`:data`** — UNCHANGED. The ordering is computed at the
`:presentation` boundary; the DAO/repository surface continues to emit
an unordered (or DAO-ordered) snapshot, and the VM re-orders on each
emission via `applyView`.

**`:presentation`** — `LibraryState` gains 3 fields
(`sort: LibrarySort = ALPHABETIC`, `sortDirection: SortDirection =
ASCENDING`, `randomSeed: Long? = null`). `LibraryIntent` gains 2
variants (`OnSortChange(LibrarySort)`, `OnSortDirectionToggle`).
`LibraryViewModel`:
- The prior `applySearch(items, query)` helper is generalised to
  `applyView(items, query, sort, direction, seed)`: filter → sort →
  optional reverse, with RANDOM short-circuiting the reverse step (a
  shuffle's "direction" has no meaning; mirrors legacy
  `LibraryViewModel.kt:438`).
- `onSortChange(sort)` updates state and regenerates `randomSeed`
  iff the new mode is RANDOM (`Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds
  ()`) — so the user sees a fresh shuffle when picking RANDOM but
  the order is stable across flow re-emissions for the same seed.
- `onSortDirectionToggle()` flips ASCENDING ↔ DESCENDING and re-runs
  `applyView`.
- The `startObserving()` collector and the `onSearchQueryChange`
  handler both thread the new sort/direction/seed into `applyView`,
  so search and sort compose cleanly.

**`:ui`** — adds a private `SortMenu(sort, sortDirection, onIntent)`
composable to `LibraryScreen.kt`'s non-selection `TopAppBar.actions`
slot, BEFORE the existing Random/Refresh TextButtons:
- A "Sort" TextButton anchors a Material 3 `DropdownMenu`.
- One `DropdownMenuItem` per `LibrarySort.entries`; the active
  selection renders in `colorScheme.primary`, others in `onSurface`.
- A direction TextButton (`↑` / `↓` glyph) next to the menu emits
  `OnSortDirectionToggle`. Hidden when `sort == RANDOM` (the reducer
  short-circuits reverse for RANDOM, so the toggle would be inert).
- `LibrarySort.label()` private extension translates enum → English
  literal; Phase 10 i18n lift swaps to `stringResource()` across both
  legacy and rework consumers.

Icon-free posture preserved: no `material-icons-extended` dep, no
Icons.* refs. Same lesson logged in §149 for #314's IconButton revert.

**`:composeApp`** — UNCHANGED. No new Koin module, no new nav entry.
The existing `libraryReworkModule`'s `viewModel { LibraryViewModel
(...) }` factory continues to work — the new intents/state fields
piggyback on the existing dependency graph.

### MVI surface shape (post-slice)

```
LibraryIntent (sealed interface):
  ├─ OnEnter
  ├─ OnRefresh
  ├─ OnItemClick(Manga)
  ├─ OnItemLongClick(MangaKey)
  ├─ OnSelectionToggle(MangaKey)
  ├─ OnSelectionClear
  ├─ OnDeleteSelected
  ├─ OnDeleteSelectedConfirm
  ├─ OnDeleteSelectedDismiss
  ├─ OnToggleInLibrary(Manga)
  ├─ OnSearchQueryChange(String)
  ├─ OnOpenRandom
  ├─ OnSortChange(LibrarySort)        ← §150 (this slice)
  └─ OnSortDirectionToggle            ← §150 (this slice)

LibraryState (data class):
  ├─ isLoading, items, searchQuery, selection, isInSelectionMode
  ├─ isDeleteDialogVisible, isRefreshing
  ├─ sort: LibrarySort                ← §150 (this slice)
  ├─ sortDirection: SortDirection     ← §150 (this slice)
  ├─ randomSeed: Long?                ← §150 (this slice)
  └─ error: AppError?
```

14 intents (2 new), 11 state fields (3 new). `LibraryEffect`
unchanged.

### Stable-shuffle rationale

The `randomSeed: Long?` field is the load-bearing piece of the RANDOM
mode's design. Without it, every flow re-emission (e.g., the user
toggling library membership on another manga while RANDOM is active)
would re-shuffle the visible grid — surprising and disorienting. With
it, `applyView` calls `filtered.shuffled(Random(seed))` deterministically
on each re-emission, so the order stays stable across normal updates;
the seed only refreshes when the user explicitly picks RANDOM again (a
gesture they can read as "shuffle me a new order"). Mirrors the legacy
`LibraryViewModel.kt:296-311 onSortChanged` posture (which also
regenerates a seed on RANDOM re-pick).

### Files added / modified

**New (2 in `:domain`, commit `fa0034a`):**
- `domain/.../model/library/LibrarySort.kt` — 4-value enum + KDoc.
- `domain/.../model/library/SortDirection.kt` — 2-value enum + KDoc.

**Modified `:presentation` (3 files in commit `fa0034a`):**
- `LibraryState.kt` — added 3 fields.
- `LibraryIntent.kt` — added 2 variants.
- `LibraryViewModel.kt` — added 2 imports + 2 reducer cases + 2
  handlers + evolved `applySearch` → `applyView`.

**Modified `:ui` (1 file in commit `d9df938`):**
- `LibraryScreen.kt` — added `SortMenu` composable + `label()` helper
  + 6 new imports (DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuItem, mutableStateOf,
  setValue, LibrarySort, SortDirection).

No `:data`, `:platform`, or `:composeApp` source changes.

### Cross-references

- [§148 — Phase 7.x.library.refresh] (Task #313) — established the

- Phase 7.x.library.sort.persistence (not yet scheduled) — the

### Deferrals (post-§150)

- **TOTAL_CHAPTERS sort mode** — requires `LibraryManga.totalChapters:
  Int` field, fed from `MangaChapterDao.observeChapterCount(mangaId)`.
  Strangler-fig boundary stays clean; just a parallel `:domain` model

- **Filter chips** (FilterType: ALL/DOWNLOADED/UNREAD/STARTED/

- **Category tabs** (FilterTabs) — still deferred per §149.

Touches `:domain` (2 new enums), `:presentation` (state + intents +

## §151 — Phase 7.x.library.sort.tierb — TOTAL_CHAPTERS + LAST_READ via LibraryManga extension

### Strategy

§150 deferred two legacy sort modes — `TOTAL_CHAPTERS` and `LAST_READ` — because
adding them as `LibrarySort` enum values without backing data on
[LibraryManga](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/model/LibraryManga.kt)
would force `LibraryViewModel.applyView` to either fake the ordering (stable no-op)
or read from `:shared` directly. This slice lifts the data foundation, then lights
up the enum values — splitting into two commits so each half is provably correct in
isolation.

The legacy LAST_READ semantic is chapter-based (`MAX(SavedChapterEntity.lastReadDate)`
per manga, mirroring `LibraryViewModel.kt:429`), NOT manga-level
`SavedMangaEntity.lastOpenTimestamp` — opening a manga's screen doesn't mark a chapter
as read. The rework follows the same chapter-based pipeline.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`**

- [`LibraryManga`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/model/LibraryManga.kt)
  gains two REQUIRED fields:
  - `totalChapters: Int` — feeds the `TOTAL_CHAPTERS` comparator.
  - `lastReadAt: Instant?` — feeds the `LAST_READ` comparator; `null` means "never
    read" (no chapter has a non-zero `lastReadDate`).
  Both fields are required (no default) so every constructor site must thread the new
  aggregate data explicitly. Silent zero-data drift would mask Room aggregation
  regressions — better to break the build than to silently sort everything to position 0.

- [`LibrarySort`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/model/library/LibrarySort.kt)
  extended with `TOTAL_CHAPTERS` and `LAST_READ` values. The enum's KDoc had a "tier-a
  scope" caveat from §150 — that caveat is removed since the model is now extended. The
  OCP note is rephrased to reflect the actual two-touchpoint extension (`applyView` arm
  + `label()` arm).

**`:shared`** (additive Room extensions)

- [`MangaChapterMetrics`](../shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/features/library/data/MangaChapterMetrics.kt)
  gains `@ColumnInfo("lastReadTs") val lastReadTs: Long?`. SQLite `MAX()` over zero rows
  yields NULL, mapped to Kotlin `null`; over non-empty rows with `lastReadDate = 0L` it
  yields `0L`. KDoc documents the dual semantic so downstream callers coalesce both into
  "never read".

- [`MangaDao.getAllChapterMetricsFlow`](../shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/local/dao/MangaDao.kt)
  SQL extended with `MAX(lastReadDate) AS lastReadTs` in the existing per-manga
  `GROUP BY mangaId`. No new query, no new index; piggybacks on the existing aggregate
  flow that already feeds the rework Library.

**`:data`**

- [`LibraryMappers.toLibraryManga`](../data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/mapper/LibraryMappers.kt)
  gains a `lastReadTs: Long?` param with explicit null/0L coalescing:
  ```kotlin
  lastReadAt = lastReadTs?.takeIf { it > 0L }?.let(Instant::fromEpochMilliseconds)
  ```
  Coalesces "no rows" (null) and "rows but unread" (0L) into a single
  `lastReadAt = null`. Downstream consumers test `lastReadAt == null` for "never read"
  without re-implementing the dual semantic.

- [`LibraryRepositoryImpl`](../data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt)
  call-site updates only:
  - `observeLibrary()`: passes `m?.lastReadTs` from `MangaChapterMetrics` into the mapper.
  - `get()`: passes `lastReadTs = null` (single-shot fetch ignores chapter metrics today;
    the legacy 0-counts pattern is preserved for now — a reactive chapter-aware `get()`
    lands in a later slice).

**`:presentation`**

- [`LibraryViewModel.applyView`](../presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/library/LibraryViewModel.kt)
  gains two `when` arms:
  ```kotlin
  LibrarySort.TOTAL_CHAPTERS -> filtered.sortedBy { it.totalChapters }
  LibrarySort.LAST_READ -> filtered.sortedBy {
      it.lastReadAt?.toEpochMilliseconds() ?: Long.MAX_VALUE
  }
  ```
  The `Long.MAX_VALUE` coalescing for `null lastReadAt` is the documented "never read
  sinks to bottom in ascending" semantic. Kotlin's natural null ordering (`nulls first`)
  would put "never read" at the top of ascending, which would surprise the user — read
  entries are the ones with meaningful timestamps. Explicit Long projection is
  direction-stable and matches the legacy ordering.

**`:ui`**

- [`LibraryScreen.LibrarySort.label()`](../ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt)
  gains two label literals: `"Total chapters"` and `"Last read"`. Phase 10's
  `stringResource()` lift will replace these literals with localised strings the same
  way it lifts the other four. KDoc reference updated from "four tier-a modes" → "all
  six modes" to reflect closed-set coverage.

### LAST_READ semantic choice — chapter-based vs manga-level

The legacy `LibraryViewModel.kt` has two timestamps it could use for LAST_READ:
- `SavedMangaEntity.lastOpenTimestamp` (line 234) — updated whenever the user opens
  the manga's details screen.
- `MAX(c.lastReadDate)` over `saved_chapters` (line 429) — the most recent chapter
  read timestamp.

The legacy LAST_READ sort uses the chapter-based path. The rework follows because:
1. "Last read" semantically means "last chapter I read", not "last manga I opened".
2. The chapter-based path already flows through `MangaChapterMetrics` — adding the
   aggregate to the existing `getAllChapterMetricsFlow` is a one-line SQL extension.
3. Manga-level `lastOpenTimestamp` would require a separate Room flow or a join in
   the mapper, both of which would re-introduce the Bug 3 invalidation pattern that
   §148 explicitly split apart for Desktop reactivity.

### Stale-when arm prevention

Each layer is exhaustive-`when`-checked by the Kotlin compiler:
- `applyView`: 4 + 2 = 6 arms (Android compile gate would fail if any were missing).
- `LibrarySort.label()`: 6 arms.

Adding a future seventh sort mode forces both arms to be extended in the same commit
that adds the enum value — the build won't compile otherwise. This is the OCP
guarantee §150 documented and §151 inherits.

| `domain/.../LibraryManga.kt` | `:domain` | A | +2 fields |
| `domain/.../library/LibrarySort.kt` | `:domain` | B | +2 enum values, KDoc refresh |
| `shared/.../MangaChapterMetrics.kt` | `:shared` | A | +`lastReadTs: Long?` |
| `shared/.../MangaDao.kt` | `:shared` | A | +`MAX(lastReadDate) AS lastReadTs` |
| `data/.../LibraryMappers.kt` | `:data` | A | +`lastReadTs` param + null/0L coalesce |
| `data/.../LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt` | `:data` | A | 2 call-site updates |
| `presentation/.../LibraryViewModel.kt` | `:presentation` | B | +2 `applyView` arms |
| `ui/.../LibraryScreen.kt` | `:ui` | B | +2 `label()` arms |

Commit A: 5 files (cap). Commit B: 3 files. Commit C: docs (this section + SOLID_AUDIT).

### Cross-references

- [§148 — bug 3 / Desktop invalidationtracker](#§148): the per-table aggregate split
  that §151 piggybacks on (chapter metrics flow vs manga flow).
- [§149 — RANDOM stable shuffle](#§149): direction-toggle posture preserved by

## §152 — Phase 7.x.library.sort.persist — sort/direction persistence to multiplatform-settings prefs

Closes the persistence deferral from §150 / §151. The rework Library's sort mode
and direction now survive process death, byte-for-byte compatible with the legacy
on-disk keys.

### Strategy

Strangler-fig: the rework reads/writes the **same `ObservableSettings` keys** the
legacy `SharedPrefsHelper` already uses (`library_sort` String + `library_sort_asc`
Boolean). Picking fresh `*.rework` keys would silently reset every user's sort +
direction the first time they hit the rework route — worse UX than legacy parity.
Phase 9.x route-swap eventually retires the legacy `LibraryViewModel`; at that
point the keys belong to the rework alone.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain` (Commit A — 5 new files)**

- [`LibraryPrefsRepository`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/repository/LibraryPrefsRepository.kt)
  — 4-method interface, granular per-axis streams + suspend setters:
  ```kotlin
  fun observeSort(): Flow<LibrarySort>
  suspend fun setSort(sort: LibrarySort)
  fun observeSortDirection(): Flow<SortDirection>
  suspend fun setSortDirection(direction: SortDirection)
  ```
  Why 4 narrow methods vs. one combined `Flow<Pair<LibrarySort, SortDirection>>`:
  the VM observes each axis independently (sort changes regenerate the RANDOM
  seed; direction-toggle does not), and a combined `Pair`-flow would `combine`
  the two streams pre-VM, forcing the VM to diff incoming pairs to figure out
  which axis changed. Narrow streams = explicit intent at the call site.

- [`ObserveLibrarySortUseCase`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/library/ObserveLibrarySortUseCase.kt) /
  [`SetLibrarySortUseCase`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/library/SetLibrarySortUseCase.kt) /
  [`ObserveLibrarySortDirectionUseCase`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/library/ObserveLibrarySortDirectionUseCase.kt) /
  [`SetLibrarySortDirectionUseCase`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/library/SetLibrarySortDirectionUseCase.kt) —
  four thin delegators (`operator fun invoke()` → repository call). The VM
  type-signature reveals exactly which capability each parameter consumes;
  observe / set split blocks a use case from accidentally doing the other's job.

**`:data` (Commit B — 1 new file)**

- [`LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl`](../data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.kt)
  — backed by `ObservableSettings` (multiplatform-settings 1.3.0), the same
  binding the legacy `SharedPrefsHelper` uses. Key + value semantics:

  | Disk key             | Type    | Default       | Mapping                                                           |
  |----------------------|---------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | `library_sort`       | String  | `"ALPHABETIC"`| `LibrarySort.entries.firstOrNull { it.name == raw } ?: ALPHABETIC` |
  | `library_sort_asc`   | Boolean | `true`        | `true → ASCENDING`, `false → DESCENDING`                          |

  Unknown / malformed sort values: the legacy reader called `SortType.valueOf(raw)`
  which throws on unknown names — a downgrade after the rework persists a future
  enum entry (e.g., a hypothetical `BY_LANGUAGE`) would crash. The rework swaps the
  crash for a silent fallback to `ALPHABETIC` via the `firstOrNull` extension. The
  fallback never writes back to disk; the next explicit user pick overwrites the
  bad value.

  Direction Boolean ⇄ enum: the legacy persisted a single ascending/descending
  flag rather than a named enum. The 2-value `SortDirection` enum is a total
  reversible mapping; no fallback path needed (multiplatform-settings returns the
  Boolean default on absent / type-mismatched keys).

**`:presentation` (Commit C — 1 modified file)**

- [`LibraryViewModel`](../presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/library/LibraryViewModel.kt)
  constructor surface widens from 5 use cases to 9:
  ```kotlin
  + observeLibrarySort: ObserveLibrarySortUseCase
  + setLibrarySort: SetLibrarySortUseCase
  + observeLibrarySortDirection: ObserveLibrarySortDirectionUseCase
  + setLibrarySortDirection: SetLibrarySortDirectionUseCase
  ```
  `init {}` adds two observer flows (alongside the existing `observeLibraryRefresh`):
  ```kotlin
  observeLibrarySort()
      .onEach { sort ->
          updateState {
              it.copy(
                  sort = sort,
                  items = applyView(allItems, it.searchQuery, sort, it.sortDirection, it.randomSeed),
              )
          }
      }
      .launchIn(viewModelScope)
  ```
  Mirror block for `observeLibrarySortDirection()`. First emission seeds state
  from disk on VM construction; subsequent emissions handle external writes
  (future Settings screen).

  Handler delta — `onSortChange` and `onSortDirectionToggle` keep their existing
  local-mutation-first posture (instant UI response, RANDOM-seed regeneration
  per-session and NOT persisted) and add a persistence `launch`:
  ```kotlin
  viewModelScope.launch { setLibrarySort(sort) }
  viewModelScope.launch { setLibrarySortDirection(nextDir) }
  ```

  The `onSortDirectionToggle` body moves the `nextDir` computation OUT of the
  `updateState { }` lambda into a `state.value` read because the value is now
  needed for both the local `updateState` and the launch — a single capture
  avoids a stale-snapshot race between the two reads.

**`:composeApp` (Commit B — 1 modified file)**

- [`LibraryReworkModule`](../composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/LibraryReworkModule.kt)
  binds the new types and the widened VM constructor:
  ```kotlin
  single<LibraryPrefsRepository> { LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl(settings = get()) }
  factory { ObserveLibrarySortUseCase(get()) }
  factory { SetLibrarySortUseCase(get()) }
  factory { ObserveLibrarySortDirectionUseCase(get()) }
  factory { SetLibrarySortDirectionUseCase(get()) }
  viewModel { LibraryViewModel(observeLibrary = get(), ..., setLibrarySortDirection = get()) }
  ```
  The `viewModel { }` call switched from 5 positional `get()`s to 9 named-arg
  `get()`s. At width 9 the positional form was a latent foot-gun: a future 10th
  param would mis-bind silently if Koin's type-inference ever picked the wrong
  candidate. Named args are a readability + safety lift.

### Why `LibraryPrefsRepository` lives in `:domain`, not `:core`

The prefs surface is **domain-shaped**: it speaks `LibrarySort` + `SortDirection`,
both domain enums. `:core` carries no domain types. The repository interface
sits at the same architectural elevation as `LibraryRepository` (already in
`:domain`) and the four use cases consume it via constructor injection. The
multiplatform-settings dep lives only in `:data` (impl) and `:platform` (binding);
`:domain` stays pure Kotlin + kotlinx.coroutines.

### Why no `LibraryIntent.OnSortPersisted` echo intent

Considered and rejected: an alternative MVI shape where the observers emit an
intent rather than directly calling `updateState`. The state-update path is a
straight comparator-and-list-rebuild — no business logic, no error handling,
no effects to emit. Routing it through an intent + reducer would add an
indirection with no observable benefit. The MVI surface stays closed at 17
intents (unchanged from §150).

### Observer-echo behaviour after self-write

When the VM persists a new sort via `setLibrarySort(sort)`, the same
`observeLibrarySort()` flow eventually emits the new value back. The flow
re-enters the observer's `updateState` block. By then `state.sort` already
matches the emitted value (the local handler updated it eagerly). The
`updateState` call re-runs `applyView` over `allItems` with the same args,
producing a structurally-equal list. `StateFlow` distincts identical values
(when the data classes implement `equals` over their fields, which Kotlin
generates for `data class`), so no recomposition fires. Wasted CPU on the
re-`applyView` call is bounded — `applyView` is O(n log n) on a working set
typically ≤500 items — and the alternative (suppressing observer echoes by
diffing emitted-vs-current) adds VM state for no UX gain.

### No-op write protection

`ObservableSettings.putString` / `putBoolean` short-circuit internally when the
value already matches disk (per `multiplatform-settings` 1.3.0 semantics). The
matching `getStringFlow` / `getBooleanFlow` only emit on actual value change.
So clicking "Sort by date" when already on date is a no-op end-to-end —
no disk write, no flow emission, no observer echo.

### Why `ObservableSettings` bypasses dispatcher pinning

`getStringFlow` / `getBooleanFlow` read from in-memory snapshots
(`SharedPreferences` / `NSUserDefaults` / `java.util.prefs.Preferences` all
maintain in-memory caches after first read). Setter calls (`putString` /
`putBoolean`) are non-blocking on all three platforms. The rework's `.map` of
the emitted value is pure CPU. Pinning to `Dispatchers.IO` would add a
context-hop with zero benefit. Same posture as
[`ReadingModeRepositoryImpl`](../data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/ReadingModeRepositoryImpl.kt)
(§79) and the legacy `LibraryViewModel`'s `prefs.getString` calls.

### Why suspend setters despite non-blocking platform writes

[`LibraryPrefsRepository.setSort`](../domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/repository/LibraryPrefsRepository.kt)
and `setSortDirection` are declared `suspend`. Today they delegate to
`ObservableSettings.putString` / `putBoolean` which return immediately. The
`suspend` keyword keeps the door open for a future `withContext(io)` switch
without breaking the contract — e.g., if Desktop's `java.util.prefs.Preferences`
backend grows synchronous file I/O, or if a future swap to DataStore-on-Android
forces a coroutine boundary.

### MVI shape rationale

- **`LibraryIntent` count**: unchanged (still 17 intents). `OnSortChange` and
  `OnSortDirectionToggle` exist from §150; persistence rides on the existing
  handlers via additional `viewModelScope.launch { }` lines.
- **`LibraryState` count**: unchanged (still 11 fields). Persistence is purely
  side-effecting; nothing about the on-screen state changed.
- **No reducer split**: the same handlers compute the local state delta AND
  enqueue the persist call. A reducer-side split (handler computes state,
  middleware persists) would be an MVI middleware lift — out of scope for
  this slice and not currently used anywhere else in the project.

## §153 — Phase 7.x.library.filter.foundation — LibraryFilter enum + filter-aware applyView

(Task #319, 2026-05-27, commits **`2451fd3`** (1/3) + **`681ef44`** (2/3) + this docs close-out (3/3))

### Strategy

Closes ladder rung 6 from §150's deferred-list under a deliberate sub-slicing
identical to the §150 (tier-a sort foundation) / §151 (tier-b sort lift)
split: ship the FIVE filter axes the existing `LibraryManga` model can
already serve (ALL, DOWNLOADED, UNREAD, STARTED, COMPLETED) as a self-
contained slice; the legacy's sixth axis (`BOOKMARKED`) defers to a future
tier-b filter slice that lifts a backing `bookmarkedCount` aggregate
through the strangler-fig.

This split is OCP-friendly — the `LibraryFilter` enum opens to additional
values without changing the existing call-sites, the `applyView` pipeline's
`when (filter)` block is exhaustive-by-compile, and the tier-b follow-on
adds 1 enum entry + 1 `when` arm + 1 mapper field without touching anything
else.

The slice introduces a `:domain` model surface (1 enum), a `:presentation`
state extension (1 field), 1 new MVI intent, an evolved
`applyView(items, query, sort, direction, seed, filter)` pipeline that
inserts a filter step between search and sort, and a `:ui` `FilterMenu`
composable in the top bar.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — adds 1 enum under `me.manga.kira.domain.model.library`:
- `LibraryFilter` (5 values today, tier-a).

Plain `enum class`. No new use case, no new repository — the filter is a
pure VM-side predicate over the observed snapshot. Filter persistence
(Settings round-trip mirroring §152) is its own deferred slice.

**`:data`** — UNCHANGED. The predicate is evaluated at the `:presentation`
boundary; the DAO/repository surface continues to emit the full snapshot
and the VM filters on each emission via `applyView`.

**`:presentation`** — `LibraryState` gains 1 field
(`filter: LibraryFilter = LibraryFilter.ALL`). `LibraryIntent` gains 1
variant (`OnFilterChange(LibraryFilter)`). `LibraryViewModel`:
- `applyView` evolves from 5 → 6 parameters: appends `filter:
  LibraryFilter` at position 6. Body inserts a new `when (filter)` block
  AFTER the search-query filter and BEFORE the sort step (filter the
  smaller working set before paying for `sortedBy`).
- `onFilterChange(filter)` updates state and re-runs `applyView`. No
  seed regeneration, no persistence write (deferred).
- All 6 existing `applyView` call sites (`startObserving`,
  `observeLibrarySort` observer, `observeLibrarySortDirection` observer,
  `onSearchQueryChange`, `onSortChange`, `onSortDirectionToggle`) updated
  to thread `it.filter` as the 6th positional arg.

**`:ui`** — adds a private `FilterMenu(filter, onIntent)` composable to
`LibraryScreen.kt`'s non-selection `TopAppBar.actions` slot, BEFORE the
existing `SortMenu`:
- A "Filter" TextButton anchors a Material 3 `DropdownMenu`.
- One `DropdownMenuItem` per `LibraryFilter.entries`; the active axis
  renders in `colorScheme.primary`, others in `onSurface` (same selected-
  highlight pattern as `SortMenu`).
- `LibraryFilter.label()` private extension translates enum → English
  literal; Phase 10 i18n lift swaps to `stringResource()` across both
  legacy and rework consumers.

The button always reads "Filter" rather than the active axis name —
keeps top-bar action width predictable when axis name lengths differ
("ALL" vs "DOWNLOADED"); the open dropdown surfaces which axis is active
via the selected-highlight.

Icon-free posture preserved (§149 lesson): no `material-icons-extended`
dep, no Icons.* refs.

**`:composeApp`** — UNCHANGED. The existing `libraryReworkModule`'s
9-arg `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(...) }` factory continues to work —
the new field/intent piggyback on the existing dependency graph.

### MVI surface shape (post-slice)

```
LibraryIntent (sealed interface):
  ├─ OnEnter
  ├─ OnRefresh
  ├─ OnItemClick(Manga)
  ├─ OnItemLongClick(MangaKey)
  ├─ OnSelectionToggle(MangaKey)
  ├─ OnSelectionClear
  ├─ OnDeleteSelected
  ├─ OnDeleteSelectedConfirm
  ├─ OnDeleteSelectedDismiss
  ├─ OnToggleInLibrary(Manga)
  ├─ OnSearchQueryChange(String)
  ├─ OnOpenRandom
  ├─ OnSortChange(LibrarySort)              ← §150
  ├─ OnSortDirectionToggle                  ← §150
  └─ OnFilterChange(LibraryFilter)          ← §153 (this slice)

LibraryState (data class):
  ├─ isLoading, items, searchQuery, selection, isInSelectionMode
  ├─ isDeleteDialogVisible, isRefreshing
  ├─ sort: LibrarySort                      ← §150
  ├─ sortDirection: SortDirection           ← §150
  ├─ randomSeed: Long?                      ← §150
  ├─ filter: LibraryFilter                  ← §153 (this slice)
  └─ error: AppError?
```

15 intents (1 new), 12 state fields (1 new). `LibraryEffect` unchanged.

### Pipeline ordering rationale

`applyView` runs **search → filter → sort → reverse**. Two design choices:

1. **Search before filter**, not filter before search. The search query
   is text the user is typing right now (high-rate change); the filter
   axis is a sticky dropdown choice (low-rate change). Running search
   first means the typical inner-loop work (every keystroke re-applies
   the pipeline) sees the full library narrowed by typing first, then a
   cheap predicate scan. The opposite order would re-evaluate the
   filter predicate on every keystroke — wasted work since the filter
   doesn't change keystroke-to-keystroke.

2. **Filter before sort**, not sort then filter. `sortedBy` is O(n log n);
   the filter predicate is O(n). Filtering first shrinks the working set
   the sort sees. Mirrors the legacy `LibraryViewModel.kt:204-248`
   pipeline shape and the §150 sort-foundation's same posture (search
   filter → sort), now extended with the explicit filter step in between.

### Predicate mapping (5 axes today, 1 deferred)

| Axis | Predicate | Source field on `LibraryManga` |
|---|---|---|
| ALL | identity (no filter) | — |
| DOWNLOADED | `hasDownloads` | already present (§211 grid cover cousin) |
| UNREAD | `unreadCount > 0` | already present |
| STARTED | `unreadCount < totalChapters` | present after §151 lift |
| COMPLETED | `totalChapters > 0 && unreadCount == 0` | present after §151 lift |
| **BOOKMARKED** (deferred) | `bookmarkedCount > 0` | **needs schema lift** |

The COMPLETED predicate's `totalChapters > 0` guard is load-bearing —
without it, every empty-library entry (totalChapters = 0, unreadCount = 0)
would falsely satisfy the predicate. Documented in the enum KDoc.

**Modified `:presentation` (3 files in commit `2451fd3`):**

- `LibraryIntent.kt` — added 1 variant (`OnFilterChange`).
- `LibraryViewModel.kt` — added 1 import + 1 reducer case + 1 handler
  + 6th `applyView` param + 1 new `when (filter)` block + 6 call-site
  updates.

**Modified `:ui` (1 file in commit `681ef44`):**

  .label()` helper + 1 new import + 1 new entry in `TopAppBar.actions`.

No `:data`, `:platform`, or `:composeApp` source changes.

## §154 — Phase 7.x.library.filter.persist — filter axis persistence to multiplatform-settings prefs

### Strategy

Closes the persistence deferral from §153's foundation slice (Task #319).
The user's chosen `LibraryFilter` now survives ViewModel destruction +
process death on the rework Library route. Wire-format: a fresh
`"library_filter"` String-name key in the same `ObservableSettings` cell
that `library_sort` / `library_sort_asc` already occupy. Mirrors §152's
sort-persistence slice (Task #318) shape exactly: extend the existing
`LibraryPrefsRepository` interface with a third observe/set pair, add 2
narrow use cases, extend the `:data` impl with one mapper + one key
constant, widen the Koin module + VM ctor by 2 deps, add an observer in
`init {}` + persist write in `onFilterChange`.

The interface extension is **atomic with the impl extension** — adding
abstract methods to an interface that already has a concrete impl in the
same compilation graph would leave the impl no longer satisfying the
contract. Commit A therefore lands 4 files (interface + 2 use cases +
impl) rather than the 3-file shape §152's interface-from-scratch commit
used. Still under the 5-file cap; the split is just optimal for the build
graph rather than aesthetic.

Why a fresh disk key (`library_filter`) rather than co-opting a legacy
constant: the legacy `LibraryViewModel` never persisted its `FilterTypes`
axis — the chip row reset to ALL on every screen entry. There is no
legacy disk-cell to share, so the rework owns the cell from day one.
Phase 9.x route-swap will leave this writer as the sole owner without a
migration step.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces (post-§154)

- `:domain`:
  - `LibraryPrefsRepository` (interface, MOD): gains `observeFilter():
    Flow<LibraryFilter>` + `suspend fun setFilter(filter: LibraryFilter)`.
    The interface KDoc updates "Scope today: sort mode + sort direction"
    to "sort mode + sort direction + filter axis" — the third axis lands
    on the same coherent "Library display preferences" SRP rather than
    spawning a parallel `LibraryFilterRepository`.
  - `ObserveLibraryFilterUseCase` (NEW): one-line delegate over
    `LibraryPrefsRepository.observeFilter()`. Mirrors
    `ObserveLibrarySortUseCase`.
  - `SetLibraryFilterUseCase` (NEW): one-line delegate over
    `LibraryPrefsRepository.setFilter(...)`. Mirrors
    `SetLibrarySortUseCase`.
- `:data`:
  - `LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl` (MOD): gains `observeFilter()` /
    `setFilter()` overrides using `ObservableSettings.getStringFlow` /
    `putString`, plus a private `String.toLibraryFilter()` mapper that
    falls back to `LibraryFilter.ALL` on unknown / future-enum-name reads
    (same posture as `String.toLibrarySort()`). Three new companion
    constants: `FILTER_KEY = "library_filter"` and
    `DEFAULT_FILTER_NAME = "ALL"`.
- `:presentation`:
  - `LibraryViewModel` (MOD): two new ctor params
    (`observeLibraryFilter` + `setLibraryFilter`). The `init {}` block
    gains a third observer that mirrors the sort + direction observers
    (project Flow emission into `state.filter`, re-apply `applyView`).
    The existing `onFilterChange` handler gains a single
    `viewModelScope.launch { setLibraryFilter(filter) }` line after the
    `updateState` call.
- `:ui`: **untouched.** The `FilterMenu` dropdown from §153 already emits
  `LibraryIntent.OnFilterChange(...)`; persistence is a VM-internal
  concern that doesn't change the intent shape.
- `:composeApp`:
  - `LibraryReworkModule` (MOD): adds two `factory { ... }` entries for
    the new use cases + widens the `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(...) }`
    constructor call from 9 to 11 named-arg dependencies. No new
    `single` bindings (the `LibraryPrefsRepository` `single` from §152
    already serves all three axes — same impl, same disk cell).

### Wire diagram (sort + direction + filter, post-§154)

```
[Compose top bar]
   FilterMenu (selects one of 5 axes)
       │ onClick: LibraryIntent.OnFilterChange(axis)
       ▼
[LibraryViewModel.handle]
   ├─ updateState { filter = axis; items = applyView(...) }      (synchronous)
   └─ viewModelScope.launch { setLibraryFilter(axis) }            (async persist)
                                  │
                                  ▼
             [SetLibraryFilterUseCase] → [LibraryPrefsRepository.setFilter]
                                  │
                                  ▼
            [LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl] → ObservableSettings.putString
                                                  │
                                                  ▼
                                       "library_filter" → "DOWNLOADED"
                                                  │
                          ┌──────────── re-emission ──────────────────┐
                          │                                            │
                          ▼                                            │
              [ObservableSettings.getStringFlow]                       │
                          │                                            │
                          ▼                                            │
            [LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.observeFilter] → .map { it.toLibraryFilter() }
                                  │
                                  ▼
            [ObserveLibraryFilterUseCase] → emits to VM observer
                                  │
                                  ▼
            updateState { filter = axis; items = applyView(...) }      ← echo
                                                                       (StateFlow
                                                                        distincts;
                                                                        no-op)
```

### Observer-echo: why no double-render or double-persist

When the user picks a new axis:
1. **Synchronous path** — `updateState` flips `state.filter` and recomputes
   `state.items` immediately. The UI recomposes within the same frame.
2. **Async path** — `setLibraryFilter` writes to disk. The observer's
   `getStringFlow` re-emits the new value. The observer's
   `updateState` reducer computes the same `state.filter` value and the
   same `applyView` result (the inputs are bit-identical to the
   synchronous reducer's inputs — `allItems` hasn't changed, sort /
   direction / seed haven't changed). `StateFlow`'s distinct-emission
   guard (it compares old state via `Object.equals` which is data-class
   structural equality) sees the new snapshot is structurally equal to
   the current one and skips the emission. No second recomposition.
3. **Echo write protection** — the impl's `setFilter` is idempotent
   (calling `putString` with the same value the cell already holds is a
   no-op in multiplatform-settings 1.3.0). Even if the observer fed
   straight back into `setFilter` (which it doesn't — the VM only persists
   on the explicit user intent), no infinite loop would form.

Same posture as §152's sort + direction observers. The echo is real but
invisible.

- `domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/library/SetLibraryFilterUseCase.kt`

## §155 — Phase 7.x.library.filter.tierb — BOOKMARKED axis + bookmarkedCount denormalization

### Strategy

Closes §150 ladder rung 6 — the filter tier-b lift that §153/§154 deferred.
Adds a 6th `LibraryFilter` axis (`BOOKMARKED`) bringing the rework's
filter surface to full parity with the legacy `LibraryViewModel.kt:96-103`
`FilterTypes` 6-axis enum. Mirrors §151's TOTAL_CHAPTERS / LAST_READ
sort tier-b lift line-for-line: thread one new aggregate field through
the `:data` mapper + `LibraryRepositoryImpl` aggregate path, then add the
enum entry + atomic `when`-arm extensions across `:domain`, `:presentation`,
and `:ui`.

The `bookmarkedCount` aggregate column was already populated in
`MangaChapterMetrics.bookmarkedCount` from §148's per-table chapter-metrics
Room query (Bug 3 — Desktop bookmark not surfacing in Library workaround,
see baseline §11). **No schema migration was required** — the column has
been silently flowing through to the rework's combine() since the Library
foundation slice; this lift just exposes it to the `:domain` model and the
filter predicate. Smaller scope than §151's TOTAL_CHAPTERS / LAST_READ
lift, which DID require new aggregate columns on the Room DAO query.

### Two-commit split rationale

The schema-lift plumbing (Commit A, 3 files) lands before the enum entry
(Commit B, 3 files). Adding the `BOOKMARKED` entry FIRST would break the
`when (filter)` exhaustivity check in `LibraryViewModel.applyView` and the
`LibraryFilter.label()` extension in `LibraryScreen.kt` — every consumer
must extend in the same commit as the enum entry. By landing the model
field through the mapper chain first (Commit A), the field exists +
compiles, but no consumer is forced to handle a `BOOKMARKED` axis it
doesn't have a predicate for yet. Commit B then atomically adds the enum
entry + both `when`-arm extensions in a single 3-file commit.

This is the same split pattern §319 / §320 used for filter foundation +
persistence, scaled to a schema-plumbing-first variant.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces (post-§155)

- `:domain`:
  - `LibraryManga` (MOD): new field `bookmarkedCount: Int`. KDoc captures
    the BOOKMARKED filter-axis purpose and the no-schema-migration
    rationale.
  - `LibraryFilter` (MOD): 6th entry `BOOKMARKED`. Predicate documented in
    the KDoc semantic-mapping table as `bookmarkedCount > 0`. The
    "Why these 5 only (not 6)" caveat is removed and replaced with the
    legacy-parity narrative.
- `:data`:
  - `LibraryMappers.kt::toLibraryManga` (MOD): adds `bookmarkedCount: Int`
    parameter, pass-through to the data class constructor. Mirrors the
    existing `totalChapters` / `lastReadTs` parameter posture.
  - `LibraryRepositoryImpl::observeLibrary` (MOD): passes
    `m?.bookmarkedCount ?: 0` to the mapper. Mirrors the existing
    `lastReadTs` flow.
  - `LibraryRepositoryImpl::get` (MOD): passes `0` to the mapper (the
    single-row path doesn't load chapter aggregates, so the field is
    "unknown / not relevant" — `0` is the canonical absence sentinel).
- `:presentation`:
  - `LibraryViewModel::applyView` (MOD): new `LibraryFilter.BOOKMARKED ->
    searched.filter { it.bookmarkedCount > 0 }` arm in the `when (filter)`
    block. Predicate is `> 0` — a manga with at least one bookmarked
    chapter qualifies. Same shape as the UNREAD arm (`unreadCount > 0`).
- `:ui`:
  - `LibraryScreen::LibraryFilter.label()` (MOD): new "Bookmarked" arm.
    Same `:ui`-resident i18n posture as the prior 5 labels — Phase 10
    `stringResource(...)` lift addresses all 6 labels in one pass.
- `:composeApp`: **untouched** — Koin module unchanged; the new enum entry
  flows through the existing `LibraryPrefsRepository` plumbing established
  in §320 (the prefs impl's `String.toLibraryFilter()` mapper's
  `entries.firstOrNull` scan picks up `BOOKMARKED` automatically when the
  user persists it).

### Wire diagram (filter pipeline, post-§155)

```
[Room saved_chapters table]                            [Room saved_manga table]
        │                                                       │
        │  GROUP BY mangaId aggregate                           │  observeAll
        │  (per §148 per-table flow)                            │
        ▼                                                       ▼
[mangaDao.getAllChapterMetricsFlow]              [mangaDao.getAllSavedMangaFlow]
        │                                                       │
        │  MangaChapterMetrics {                                │
        │    bookmarkedCount: Int,  ← existing column           │
        │    totalChapters: Int,                                │
        │    readCount: Int,                                    │
        │    downloadedCount: Int,                              │
        │    lastReadTs: Long?                                  │
        │  }                                                    │
        └───────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
              [LibraryRepositoryImpl.observeLibrary combine]
                            │
                            ▼
          [toLibraryManga(bookmarkedCount = m?.bookmarkedCount ?: 0)]
                            │
                            ▼
                  LibraryManga { bookmarkedCount: Int, ... }
                            │
                            ▼
    [LibraryViewModel.applyView: when (filter) BOOKMARKED arm]
                            │
                            ▼
            searched.filter { it.bookmarkedCount > 0 }
                            │
                            ▼
                  [Compose grid: rendered]
```

- §150 — sort foundation slice — first instance of the closed-set enum +

### Deferrals (post-§155)

## §156 — Phase 7.x.library.display.foundation — grid-density preference

**Slice ID:** Phase 7.x.library.display.foundation
**Task:** #322
**Source commits:** `7c98253` (1/2 foundation) + this commit (2/2 docs)
**Ladder context:** §150 ladder rung 7 — first display-preferences rung
after the sort + filter family (rungs 4 / 5 / 6) closes. Mirrors the §150
filter foundation's shape: introduce a closed-set enum + state field +
intent + `:ui` consumption, defer persistence to a follow-on slice.

### Strategy

A foundation slice that closes the value-space and connects the enum
end-to-end (`:domain` → `:presentation` → `:ui`) without yet plumbing
persistence. Matches the §150 filter-foundation cadence:

1. **`:domain`** declares the closed-set [`GridDensity`] enum
   (`COMPACT` / `COMFORTABLE` / `SPACIOUS`) with platform-neutral KDoc.
   The `dp` mapping that drives `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = …)` lives
   in `:ui` next to the existing `LibraryFilter.label()` /
   `LibrarySort.label()` extensions — keeps `:domain` free of
   `androidx.compose.ui.unit` references.
2. **`:presentation`** adds the `gridDensity` field to `LibraryState`
   (default `COMFORTABLE`, byte-for-byte parity with the pre-§156
   hardcoded 120.dp cell) and the `OnGridDensityChange(density)` intent
   variant. The VM's handler is a pure `state.copy(gridDensity = …)`
   — no `applyView` re-run, because density only changes how the same
   `items` list is laid out, not which items appear or in what order.
3. **`:ui`** adds the third top-bar dropdown (`DensityMenu`) alongside
   `FilterMenu` + `SortMenu`, parameterises the grid via
   `gridDensity.minSize()`, and ships `GridDensity.label()` /
   `GridDensity.minSize()` extensions with calibrated dp values.

Persistence is deferred to a follow-on `display.persist` slice that will
mirror the §154 (filter persist) shape verbatim — add a fourth
`observe/set` pair to `LibraryPrefsRepository`, fresh
`library_grid_density` multiplatform-settings key, fresh
`String.toGridDensity()` fallback mapper. Keeping the foundation and
persistence in separate commits matches the §150/§154 split: foundation
closes the value-space that compiles today; persistence lifts the disk
surface afterwards.

### Two-commit split rationale

- **Commit 1/2 (`7c98253`, foundation source)** — 5 files: enum +
  state + intent + VM + `:ui`. All compile because the enum is added
  before any exhaustive `when` references it (the only consumers are
  new code added in the same commit).
- **Commit 2/2 (this commit, docs)** — ARCHITECTURE.md §156 + SOLID
  audit entry. Docs-only, no source change.

No persistence layer touched in this slice — `:data` and the Koin
module stay untouched. The follow-on `display.persist` slice will
extend `LibraryPrefsRepository` (the existing trio: sort / direction
/ filter → adds density), `LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl`, and the Koin
module + VM ctor as a separate 3-commit slice.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (1 new file)
- `model/library/GridDensity.kt` — closed-set enum with three entries.
  KDoc cites the §150 ladder posture, the semantic mapping for each
  entry, the SRP/OCP rationale (enum names DENSITY, the `dp` mapping
  lives in `:ui`; adding an entry forces a new arm everywhere via
  exhaustive `when`), and the deferred persistence plan.

**`:presentation`** (3 modified files)
- `library/LibraryState.kt` — adds `val gridDensity: GridDensity =
  GridDensity.COMFORTABLE` field. KDoc cites the `:ui`
  `GridDensity.minSize()` extension as the consumer and notes the
  parity guarantee (`COMFORTABLE` → 120.dp, matching the pre-§156
  hardcoded cell).
- `library/LibraryIntent.kt` — adds `OnGridDensityChange(density:
  GridDensity)` data-class variant. KDoc explains the no-`applyView`
  posture (density changes layout, not item set/order).
- `library/LibraryViewModel.kt` — exhaustive-`when` arm in `handle()`
  + `onGridDensityChange(density)` private handler that performs a
  pure `state.copy(gridDensity = density)`. No persistence call (no
  setter use case yet; persistence lift is deferred).

**`:ui`** (1 modified file)
- `library/LibraryScreen.kt` — adds:
  - `DensityMenu(density, onIntent)` composable — third top-bar
    dropdown alongside `FilterMenu`/`SortMenu`, same dropdown shape
    + selected-highlight pattern.
  - `LibraryGrid(...)` gains a `gridDensity: GridDensity` parameter;
    the call site threads `state.gridDensity` through.
  - `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = gridDensity.minSize())` —
    parameterised cell size.
  - `GridDensity.label()` extension — English labels ("Compact",
    "Comfortable", "Spacious") with the Phase 10 `stringResource`
    lift deferral matching the existing `LibrarySort.label()` /
    `LibraryFilter.label()` posture.
  - `GridDensity.minSize()` extension — exhaustive `when` returning
    `Dp` (96.dp / 120.dp / 160.dp). Calibration rationale lives in
    the KDoc.

### Wire diagram

```
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │              :domain                          │
        │  GridDensity enum (COMPACT/COMFORTABLE/SPAC.) │
        └────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                             │ closed-set, platform-neutral
                             ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │              :presentation                    │
        │  LibraryState.gridDensity = COMFORTABLE       │
        │  LibraryIntent.OnGridDensityChange(density)   │
        │  LibraryViewModel.onGridDensityChange:        │
        │     updateState { copy(gridDensity = …) }     │
        └────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                             │ density flips through state.copy
                             ▼
        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │              :ui                              │
        │  DensityMenu(density) → emits intent          │
        │  LibraryGrid(gridDensity)                     │
        │     ↳ GridCells.Adaptive(                     │
        │           minSize = gridDensity.minSize()     │
        │       )                                       │
        │     ↳ GridDensity.minSize(): Dp = when (this) │
        │           COMPACT     -> 96.dp                │
        │           COMFORTABLE -> 120.dp (= legacy)    │
        │           SPACIOUS    -> 160.dp               │
        └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

No `:data` involvement — the persistence lift is deferred. The :ui
adaptive grid recomposes naturally on the `state.gridDensity` flip
because the `minSize` parameter is recomputed each composition.

### Files added / modified

**Added (1 file):**
- `domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/model/library/GridDensity.kt`

**Modified (4 files):**
- `presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/library/LibraryState.kt`
- `presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/library/LibraryIntent.kt`
- `presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/library/LibraryViewModel.kt`
- `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` (this section — commit 2/2)
- `SOLID_AUDIT.md` (Phase 7.x.library.display.foundation entry — commit 2/2)

### Cross-references

- **§150** — filter/sort foundation ladder; this slice is the first
  rung past the filter family (rung 7).
- **§154** — filter persist; the shape the upcoming `display.persist`
  slice will mirror verbatim.
- **§155** — filter tier-b (BOOKMARKED); the most recent ladder rung
  that closed before this one.

### Deferrals (explicit, scoped)

1. **Persistence lift** — `LibraryPrefsRepository` is NOT extended in
   this slice. Density survives only for the lifetime of the ViewModel.
   The follow-on `display.persist` slice will add the fourth
   observe/set pair + the disk key + the fallback mapper.
2. **i18n for labels** — `GridDensity.label()` returns English literals
   ("Compact", "Comfortable", "Spacious"). Phase 10's `stringResource`
   lift will replace these with localised strings; same deferral as
   the existing `LibrarySort.label()` and `LibraryFilter.label()`.
3. **Per-density cover aspect / typography** — only the cell `minSize`
   varies across densities. A future slice could extend the density's
   effect to cover-card typography (smaller font on COMPACT, larger on
   SPACIOUS), but that's a parallel UX improvement not in scope here.
4. **No legacy parity narrative** — the legacy `LibraryViewModel` /
   `LibraryScreen` does NOT expose a grid-density preference (the
   legacy uses a fixed 3-column grid). The rework's density axis is a
   new capability, not a port — so this slice has no legacy
   wire-format compatibility constraint.

### Load-bearing posture preserved

This slice introduces a new preference axis but does not change any
existing one. The §148 per-table chapter-metrics flow, §149's icon-free
posture, §150's sort foundation, §151's sort tier-b, §152's sort
persist, §153's filter foundation, §154's filter persist, §155's
filter tier-b — all remain unchanged. The Coil ImageLoader, OkHttp
interceptor, AVIF decoder, ktor3 per-byte progress, reading mode
persistence, ReadingSessionRepository — none are touched (Library is
display-only here).

### Build gates

All gates verified on the foundation source commit `7c98253`. This
docs commit is text-only and cannot introduce a compile regression.

| Gate | Commit `7c98253` (1/2) |
| --- | --- |
| `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` | ✓ exit 0 (21s) |

| `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` | ✓ exit 0 (24s) |

iOS-device smoke test (Windows-impossible) deferred to user's Mac: on
`Screen.LibraryRework`, open the new "Density" dropdown in the top

Pick `Compact`; verify cell width shrinks (roughly one extra column
