## §157 — Phase 7.x.library.display.persist — grid-density persistence

**Slice ID:** Phase 7.x.library.display.persist
**Task:** #323
**Source commits:** `3eba6f7` (1/3 :domain + :data) + `6d55792` (2/3 Koin
+ VM wire) + this commit (3/3 docs)
**Ladder context:** §150 ladder rung 8 — the persistence lift for the
grid-density preference introduced in §156's foundation slice. Closes the
"display preferences" pair the same way §154 closes the filter pair after
§153 introduces it.

### Strategy

Mirror §154's filter-persist shape verbatim, one axis over. The `:domain`
gains a 4th observe/set pair on `LibraryPrefsRepository`; the `:data` impl
gains a 4th disk key (`library_grid_density`) and a 4th fallback mapper
(`String.toGridDensity()`); the Koin module gains two factory bindings
and two ctor args on the VM; the VM gains a 4th `init {}` collector and
one extra `viewModelScope.launch { setLibraryGridDensity(density) }` call
inside the existing `onGridDensityChange` handler.

`:ui` is UNTOUCHED — the `DensityMenu` composable from §156 already
dispatches the `LibraryIntent.OnGridDensityChange(option)` intent on
each pick, and the new persistence wire intercepts that intent inside
the VM. No UI change needed.

### Three-commit split rationale

- **Commit 1/3 (`3eba6f7`, :domain + :data)** — 4 files: interface
  extension + 2 use cases + impl wire. Closed under DIP — :domain
  defines, :data implements. The new disk cell exists and is observable
  in isolation; no caller yet.
- **Commit 2/3 (`6d55792`, Koin + VM wire)** — 2 files: Koin module
  widen + VM ctor / collector / persist call. Closes the loop: the
  disk cell now bidirectionally bound to the VM state via the
  observe-collect + setter-launch pair.
- **Commit 3/3 (this commit, docs)** — ARCHITECTURE.md §157 + SOLID
  audit entry. Docs-only, no source change.

Splitting :domain+:data from VM wiring (rather than bundling everything
in one commit) matches the §154 cadence — keeps each commit narrow
enough for the SOLID 10-point audit to verify per-file in the close-out
without the matrix exploding.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (3 files — 1 modified + 2 new)
- `repository/LibraryPrefsRepository.kt` — adds `observeGridDensity():
  Flow<GridDensity>` + `suspend fun setGridDensity(density:
  GridDensity)`. Top-level KDoc's scope-list bullet extended from
  "sort + direction + filter" to "sort + direction + filter + grid
  density" with §156.persist task reference. Per-method KDoc captures
  the fallback (COMFORTABLE on unknown disk values), rework-owned-key
  rationale (legacy has no density preference, so no cross-route
  compatibility constraint applies — same posture as the filter axis
  in §154).
- `usecase/library/ObserveLibraryGridDensityUseCase.kt` NEW — one-line
  delegate (`operator fun invoke() = repository.observeGridDensity()`).
  Mirrors `ObserveLibraryFilterUseCase` byte-for-byte in shape.
- `usecase/library/SetLibraryGridDensityUseCase.kt` NEW — suspend
  delegate (`suspend operator fun invoke(density) =
  repository.setGridDensity(density)`). Mirrors `SetLibraryFilterUseCase`
  byte-for-byte in shape.

**`:data`** (1 modified file)
- `repository/LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.kt` — implements observe via
  `settings.getStringFlow(GRID_DENSITY_KEY, DEFAULT_GRID_DENSITY_NAME)`
  → `map { it.toGridDensity() }`, set via
  `settings.putString(GRID_DENSITY_KEY, density.name)`. Adds the
  `String.toGridDensity()` fallback mapper (`entries.firstOrNull { it.name
  == this } ?: GridDensity.COMFORTABLE`). Companion const additions:
  `GRID_DENSITY_KEY = "library_grid_density"` and
  `DEFAULT_GRID_DENSITY_NAME = "COMFORTABLE"`.

**`:presentation`** (1 modified file)
- `library/LibraryViewModel.kt` — adds two ctor args
  (`observeLibraryGridDensity`, `setLibraryGridDensity`), one new
  `init {}` collector that updates `state.gridDensity` on each
  emission (no `applyView` re-run — same rationale as the foundation
  slice's intent handler), and extends `onGridDensityChange` with a
  `viewModelScope.launch { setLibraryGridDensity(density) }` call
  after the synchronous `state.copy`. KDoc updated to remove the
  transient-posture caveat and explain the observer-echo idempotency
  (StateFlow distinct-emission guard collapses the echo).

**`:composeApp`** (1 modified file)
- `di/LibraryReworkModule.kt` — adds two `factory` bindings (one per
  use case) and two ctor args to the `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(...) }`
  block. The use cases resolve through `single<LibraryPrefsRepository>`
  which was already bound from §154 (this slice extends the existing
  binding, doesn't duplicate it).

**`:ui`** — UNTOUCHED. The §156 `DensityMenu` already dispatches the
correct intent; the persistence is purely a VM concern.

### Wire diagram

```
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                  :ui                                    │
        │  DensityMenu                                            │
        │    onClick(option) → onIntent(                          │
        │      LibraryIntent.OnGridDensityChange(option)          │
        │    )                                                    │
        └─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                              │ intent
                              ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │            :presentation (LibraryViewModel)             │
        │  handle(intent):                                        │
        │    OnGridDensityChange → onGridDensityChange(density)   │
        │      updateState { copy(gridDensity = density) }  ◀ sync│
        │      viewModelScope.launch {                            │
        │        setLibraryGridDensity(density)            ◀ async│
        │      }                                                  │
        │                                                         │
        │  init {} collector:                                     │
        │    observeLibraryGridDensity()                          │
        │      .onEach { updateState { copy(gridDensity = it) } } │
        │      .launchIn(viewModelScope)                          │
        └─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                              │ both deps inject from
                              ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                  :domain                                │
        │  ObserveLibraryGridDensityUseCase()                     │
        │    = repository.observeGridDensity()                    │
        │  SetLibraryGridDensityUseCase(density)                  │
        │    = repository.setGridDensity(density)                 │
        │                                                         │
        │  LibraryPrefsRepository (interface):                    │
        │    fun observeGridDensity(): Flow<GridDensity>          │
        │    suspend fun setGridDensity(density: GridDensity)     │
        └─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                              │ Koin binds to
                              ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │             :data (LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl)          │
        │  observeGridDensity():                                  │
        │    settings.getStringFlow(                              │
        │      "library_grid_density",                            │
        │      defaultValue = "COMFORTABLE"                       │
        │    ).map { it.toGridDensity() }                         │
        │  setGridDensity(density):                               │
        │    settings.putString(                                  │
        │      "library_grid_density", density.name               │
        │    )                                                    │
        │  String.toGridDensity():                                │
        │    GridDensity.entries.firstOrNull { it.name == this }  │
        │      ?: GridDensity.COMFORTABLE                         │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Loop is closed: VM intent → setter → disk → observe flow → VM state →
recomposition. Same shape as the §154 filter loop, one axis over.

## §158 — Phase 7.x.library.category.foundation — Category tabs (NAN / LIKED / WATCHING_NOW)

**Slice ID:** Phase 7.x.library.category.foundation
**Task:** #324
**Source commits:** `5e06f7b` (1/3 :domain + :data) + `ca9f02d` (2/3
:presentation + :ui) + this commit (3/3 docs)
**Ladder context:** §150 ladder rung 9 — the first of the per-manga
**affinity** axis (orthogonal to the §153 per-chapter status axis).
Surfaces the existing `SavedMangaEntity.isLiked` / `isWatchingNow`
columns through the new `LibraryCategory` enum and exposes them as the
three category tabs the user already knows from the legacy
`LibraryScreen`'s `FilterTabs` row.

### Strategy

The two underlying boolean columns (`isLiked`, `isWatchingNow`) have
been on the `saved_manga` table since the original APK — no schema
migration is required. The legacy app already mutates them from the
Details-screen heart toggle and the "Watching now" mark; the rework's
read-only surface picks those flags up via the same Room flow without
disturbing the mutation paths (which remain in `:shared`).

`:domain` gains:
- A new enum `LibraryCategory` (3 entries — `NAN` / `LIKED` /
  `WATCHING_NOW`) modelling the tab axis.
- Two new pass-through fields on `LibraryManga` (`isLiked: Boolean`,
  `isWatchingNow: Boolean`).

`:data` gains a one-line mapper extension: `SavedMangaEntity.toLibraryManga(...)`
now also passes through `isLiked` / `isWatchingNow`. No new `:data` impl class
— the existing one already reads from the legacy entity, this just lifts two
fields that were previously dropped on the floor (because nothing in the
rework consumed them).

`:presentation` gains:
- A new `LibraryState.category: LibraryCategory = NAN` field.
- A new `LibraryIntent.OnCategoryChange(category)` intent.
- A 7th `category` parameter on the `applyView` helper.
- A new category narrowing step that runs BEFORE the existing filter
  step (pipeline order: search → category → filter → sort → reverse).
- A new private `onCategoryChange` reducer that updates `state.category`
  and re-applies the view pipeline against the current unfiltered
  snapshot.

`:ui` gains:
- A new `CategoryTabs` composable (Material 3 `TabRow` with 3 tabs)
  placed below the existing search field in `LibraryTopBar`.
- A new `LibraryCategory.label()` extension mirroring the existing
  `LibrarySort.label()` / `LibraryFilter.label()` / `GridDensity.label()`
  posture. `NAN` renders as "All" because that is the user-facing
  semantic ("no category narrowing applied"); the literal enum name is
  an implementation detail.

### Three-commit split rationale

- **Commit 1/3 (`5e06f7b`, :domain + :data)** — 3 files: enum + lifted
  fields + mapper extension. Closed under DIP — :domain defines the
  enum + the lifted field signatures, :data implements the mapping. The
  fields exist on the domain model but no consumer reads them yet.
- **Commit 2/3 (`ca9f02d`, :presentation + :ui)** — 4 files: state
  field + intent + VM reducer + pipeline extension + UI TabRow. Closes
  the user-visible loop: tab tap → intent → VM state → recomposition.
- **Commit 3/3 (this commit, docs)** — ARCHITECTURE.md §158 + SOLID
  audit entry. Docs-only, no source change.

Splitting :domain+:data from :presentation+:ui (rather than bundling
everything in one commit) follows the §153 / §154 cadence — keeps each
commit narrow enough for the SOLID 10-point audit to verify per-file
in the close-out without the matrix exploding.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (1 new file + 1 modified)
- `model/library/LibraryCategory.kt` NEW — 3-entry enum with KDoc
  covering the §150 ladder rung 9 context, the orthogonality vs
  `LibraryFilter` (per-manga affinity vs per-chapter status), and the
  semantic-mapping table to the underlying `LibraryManga.isLiked` /
  `isWatchingNow` flags.
- `model/LibraryManga.kt` MODIFIED — adds two pass-through `Boolean`
  fields (`isLiked`, `isWatchingNow`) with KDoc explaining they are
  pass-throughs from `SavedMangaEntity` and that the mutation paths
  remain in `:shared` until a later slice ports them.

**`:data`** (1 modified file)
- `mapper/LibraryMappers.kt` — `SavedMangaEntity.toLibraryManga(...)`
  extended with `isLiked = isLiked, isWatchingNow = isWatchingNow`
  pass-throughs. The Phase-4 migration note's "intentionally not
  exposed" bullet list edits to remove `isLiked` and `isWatchingNow`
  (now exposed). `LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt` is UNTOUCHED — the call
  sites invoke `entity.toLibraryManga(...)` and the mapper reads the
  flags off `this`, so no caller signature change is required.

**`:presentation`** (3 modified files)
- `library/LibraryState.kt` — adds `category: LibraryCategory = NAN`
  field with KDoc explaining defaults to identity, the orthogonality
  vs `filter`, and the deferred persistence. Also a stale-KDoc fix on
  `gridDensity` (§157 already landed, KDoc still said deferred).
- `library/LibraryIntent.kt` — adds `OnCategoryChange(category:
  LibraryCategory)` data class with KDoc referencing the legacy
  `LibraryViewModel.kt:296-304` `onFilterTabChanged` parity (legacy's
  separate tab handler, distinct from the filter dropdown handler).
- `library/LibraryViewModel.kt` — `applyView` extended to a 7th
  `category` parameter; threads `it.category` through all 7 existing
  call sites; new `OnCategoryChange` arm + `onCategoryChange()`
  reducer. Pipeline order documented in updated KDoc.

**`:ui`** (1 modified file)
- `library/LibraryScreen.kt` — adds `CategoryTabs` Material 3 `TabRow`
  composable, called inside `LibraryTopBar` below the search field.
  Selected index = `LibraryCategory.entries.indexOf(category)`. Adds
  `LibraryCategory.label()` extension. Tabs (not Dropdown) chosen to
  match the legacy `FilterTabs` posture and the one-tap-toggle UX the
  category axis benefits from (unlike the secondary filter axis,
  which lives in a dropdown).

**`:composeApp`** — UNTOUCHED. The category axis is pure VM state +
in-memory pipeline extension; no new Koin binding, no new use case, no
DI rewire.

### Pipeline order (search → category → filter → sort → reverse)

The two narrowing axes (`category` and `filter`) are orthogonal — they
filter on independent fields (`isLiked`/`isWatchingNow` vs
`hasDownloads`/`unreadCount`/etc.), so either order produces the same
final set. Running category first is a micro-optimisation: it typically
narrows by a larger ratio than filter (most users have a small "Liked"
or "Watching now" subset of their library), so the filter predicate
operates on a smaller working set. Search runs first regardless — the
user's typed query is the most contextually-load-bearing narrowing and
should take precedence over any tab/filter selection.

### Why Tabs, not Dropdown

The category axis is a **view scope** axis ("which subset of my library
am I looking at right now"). View-scope axes benefit from one-tap
toggling and persistent visibility (the user wants to see "I am in
Liked mode" without opening a menu). The secondary filter axis is a
**condition** axis ("show me only entries that satisfy this condition")
— less load-bearing in everyday browsing, so it's hidden behind a
dropdown to save top-bar real estate. The legacy `LibraryScreen` makes
the same call (legacy `FilterTabs` row + legacy `FilterTypes`
bottom-sheet menu).

- **§154** — filter persistence; the shape this slice's deferred

### Deferrals (explicit, scoped)

2. **Mutation paths (heart toggle / "watching now" mark) remain in

4. **No i18n for the category labels** — `LibraryCategory.label()`

5. **No category-aware search posture** — search still operates on

### Load-bearing posture preserved

## §159 — Phase 7.x.library.category.persist — Category tab persistence

**Slice ID:** Phase 7.x.library.category.persist
**Task:** #325
**Source commits:** `7575426` (1/3 :domain + :data) + `21597e6` (2/3
Koin + VM wire) + this commit (3/3 docs)
**Ladder context:** §150 ladder rung 10 — the persistence lift for the
category-tab preference introduced in §158's foundation slice. Closes
the "category" pair the same way §154 closes the filter pair after
§153 introduces it, and the same way §157 closes the display pair
after §156 introduces it.

### Strategy

Mirror §154 / §157's persist shape verbatim, one axis over. The
`:domain` gains a 5th observe/set pair on `LibraryPrefsRepository`;
the `:data` impl gains a 5th disk key (`library_category`) and a 5th
fallback mapper (`String.toLibraryCategory()`); the Koin module gains
two factory bindings and two ctor args on the VM; the VM gains a 5th
`init {}` collector and one extra `viewModelScope.launch {
setLibraryCategory(category) }` call inside the existing
`onCategoryChange` handler.

`:ui` is UNTOUCHED — the `CategoryTabs` composable from §158 already
dispatches the `LibraryIntent.OnCategoryChange(option)` intent on each
tap, and the new persistence wire intercepts that intent inside the
VM. No UI change needed.

### Three-commit split rationale

- **Commit 1/3 (`7575426`, :domain + :data)** — 4 files: interface
  extension + 2 use cases + impl wire. Closed under DIP — :domain
  defines, :data implements. The new disk cell exists and is
  observable in isolation; no caller yet.
- **Commit 2/3 (`21597e6`, Koin + VM wire)** — 2 files: Koin module
  widen + VM ctor / collector / persist call. Closes the loop: the
  disk cell now bidirectionally bound to the VM state via the
  observe-collect + setter-launch pair.
- **Commit 3/3 (this commit, docs)** — ARCHITECTURE.md §159 + SOLID
  audit entry. Docs-only, no source change.

Splitting :domain+:data from VM wiring (rather than bundling
everything in one commit) matches the §154 / §157 cadence — keeps
each commit narrow enough for the SOLID 10-point audit to verify
per-file in the close-out without the matrix exploding.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** (3 files — 1 modified + 2 new)
- `repository/LibraryPrefsRepository.kt` — adds `observeCategory():
  Flow<LibraryCategory>` + `suspend fun setCategory(category:
  LibraryCategory)`. Top-level KDoc's scope-list bullet extended from
  "sort + direction + filter + grid density" to "sort + direction +
  filter + grid density + category tab" with §158.persist task
  reference. Per-method KDoc captures the fallback (NAN on unknown
  disk values), rework-owned-key rationale (legacy
  `LibraryViewModel`'s `FilterTabs` axis was non-persistent — reset
  to "All" on every screen entry — so the disk-key
  `library_category` is rework-owned; same posture as the filter
  axis in §154 and the density axis in §157).
- `usecase/library/ObserveLibraryCategoryUseCase.kt` NEW — one-line
  delegate (`operator fun invoke() = repository.observeCategory()`).
  Mirrors `ObserveLibraryFilterUseCase` / `ObserveLibraryGridDensity
  UseCase` byte-for-byte in shape.
- `usecase/library/SetLibraryCategoryUseCase.kt` NEW — suspend
  delegate (`suspend operator fun invoke(category) =
  repository.setCategory(category)`). Mirrors `SetLibraryFilterUse
  Case` / `SetLibraryGridDensityUseCase` byte-for-byte in shape.

**`:data`** (1 modified file)
- `repository/LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.kt` — implements observe via
  `settings.getStringFlow(CATEGORY_KEY, DEFAULT_CATEGORY_NAME)`
  → `map { it.toLibraryCategory() }`, set via
  `settings.putString(CATEGORY_KEY, category.name)`. Adds the
  `String.toLibraryCategory()` fallback mapper
  (`entries.firstOrNull { it.name == this } ?: LibraryCategory.NAN`).
  Companion const additions: `CATEGORY_KEY = "library_category"` and
  `DEFAULT_CATEGORY_NAME = "NAN"`.

**`:presentation`** (1 modified file)
- `library/LibraryViewModel.kt` — adds two ctor args
  (`observeLibraryCategory`, `setLibraryCategory`), one new
  `init {}` collector that updates `state.category` AND re-runs
  `applyView` on each emission (unlike density, category narrows the
  visible set, so the pipeline must re-run — same posture as the
  filter / sort collectors), and extends `onCategoryChange` with a
  `viewModelScope.launch { setLibraryCategory(category) }` call
  after the synchronous `state.copy`. KDoc updated to remove the
  transient-posture caveat and explain the observer-echo idempotency
  (StateFlow distinct-emission guard collapses the echo).

**`:composeApp`** (1 modified file)
- `di/LibraryReworkModule.kt` — adds two `factory` bindings (one per
  use case) and two ctor args to the `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(...) }`
  block. The use cases resolve through `single<LibraryPrefsRepository>`
  which was already bound from §154 (this slice extends the existing
  binding, doesn't duplicate it).

**`:ui`** — UNTOUCHED. The §158 `CategoryTabs` composable already
dispatches the correct intent; the persistence is purely a VM concern.

### Wire diagram

```
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                  :ui                                    │
        │  CategoryTabs                                           │
        │    onClick(option) → onIntent(                          │
        │      LibraryIntent.OnCategoryChange(option)             │
        │    )                                                    │
        └─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                              │ intent
                              ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │            :presentation (LibraryViewModel)             │
        │  handle(intent):                                        │
        │    OnCategoryChange → onCategoryChange(category)        │
        │      updateState { copy(category = category,           │
        │                        items = applyView(...)) }  ◀ sync│
        │      viewModelScope.launch {                            │
        │        setLibraryCategory(category)              ◀ async│
        │      }                                                  │
        │                                                         │
        │  init {} collector:                                     │
        │    observeLibraryCategory()                             │
        │      .onEach { updateState {                            │
        │        copy(category = it, items = applyView(...)) } } │
        │      .launchIn(viewModelScope)                          │
        └─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                              │ both deps inject from
                              ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                  :domain                                │
        │  ObserveLibraryCategoryUseCase()                        │
        │    = repository.observeCategory()                       │
        │  SetLibraryCategoryUseCase(category)                    │
        │    = repository.setCategory(category)                   │
        │                                                         │
        │  LibraryPrefsRepository (interface):                    │
        │    fun observeCategory(): Flow<LibraryCategory>         │
        │    suspend fun setCategory(category: LibraryCategory)   │
        └─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                              │ Koin binds to
                              ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │             :data (LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl)          │
        │  observeCategory():                                     │
        │    settings.getStringFlow(                              │
        │      "library_category",                                │
        │      defaultValue = "NAN"                               │
        │    ).map { it.toLibraryCategory() }                     │
        │  setCategory(category):                                 │
        │    settings.putString(                                  │
        │      "library_category", category.name                  │
        │    )                                                    │
        │  String.toLibraryCategory():                            │
        │    LibraryCategory.entries.firstOrNull{it.name == this} │
        │      ?: LibraryCategory.NAN                             │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Loop is closed: VM intent → setter → disk → observe flow → VM state
→ recomposition. Same shape as the §154 filter loop and §157 density
loop, one axis over.

### Why the collector re-runs `applyView` (vs. density's collector that doesn't)

Category narrows the visible-item set; density only changes how the
same set is laid out. Therefore:

- `observeLibraryGridDensity` collector (§157): just updates
  `state.gridDensity`. The `:ui` adaptive grid recomposes on the
  density flip because its `minSize` parameter is derived from
  `state.gridDensity`. `applyView` is NOT re-run.
- `observeLibraryCategory` collector (this slice): updates BOTH
  `state.category` AND `state.items` via a fresh `applyView(...,
  category)` call against the latest `allItems` snapshot. The grid
  receives a new item list and recomposes accordingly. Same posture
  as the `observeLibrarySort` / `observeLibrarySortDirection` /
  `observeLibraryFilter` collectors (§152 / §154) — all four of
  those mutate the visible-item set.

### Files added / modified

**Added (2 files):**
- `domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/library/ObserveLibraryCategoryUseCase.kt`
- `domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/usecase/library/SetLibraryCategoryUseCase.kt`

**Modified (4 files):**
- `domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/repository/LibraryPrefsRepository.kt`
- `data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.kt`
- `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/LibraryReworkModule.kt`
- `presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/library/LibraryViewModel.kt`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` (this section — commit 3/3)
- `SOLID_AUDIT.md` (Phase 7.x.library.category.persist entry — commit 3/3)

### Cross-references

- **§150** — filter/sort foundation ladder; this slice closes rung 10.
- **§152** — sort + direction persistence; the original "first persist
  slice" shape this one mirrors at the surface level.
- **§154** — filter persistence; the closest "narrows-the-visible-set"
  analogue — same observe/set pair shape, same fallback-on-unknown
  mapper, same Koin widen + VM collector + persist-call cadence,
  same re-run-applyView posture for the collector.
- **§157** — display persistence; the immediate predecessor by ladder
  position — same persist-pair shape but its collector does NOT
  re-run `applyView` (density-only). This slice's collector re-runs
  `applyView` because category narrows the visible set; see "Why the
  collector re-runs `applyView`" above.
- **§158** — category foundation; the immediate predecessor that
  introduced the `LibraryCategory` enum and the transient state
  field. This slice lifts that transient state to persistent.

### Deferrals (explicit, scoped)

1. **No legacy-key compatibility narrative** — legacy
   `LibraryViewModel`'s `FilterTabs` axis was non-persistent (reset
   to "All" on every screen entry), so the disk-key `library_category`
   is rework-owned. Phase 9.x route-swap inherits it directly.
2. **No tier-b category entries** — the 3-tier surface (NAN / LIKED
   / WATCHING_NOW) ships as-is. A future slice could add a
   `RECENT_PICKS` or `FAVOURITES` tab; the `String.toLibraryCategory()`
   mapper's `entries.firstOrNull` scan would round-trip the new
   entry automatically, same posture as `BOOKMARKED` was round-tripped
   by the §154 filter mapper without code change.
3. **No i18n for the category labels** — labels still live in `:ui`
   as the §158 deferral noted; Phase 10 will lift both label sets.
4. **No per-category default sort** — the persisted choice for sort
   / direction / filter / density carries across category tab
   switches (no per-tab memory). A future slice could persist
   per-category preferences via a composite disk key; deferred to a
   separate UX slice.

### Load-bearing posture preserved

This slice adds one disk cell + one observe/set + one VM collector.
None of the prior load-bearing surfaces are touched:

- §148 — per-table chapter-metrics flow: untouched.
- §149 — stable-shuffle / icon-free top-bar posture: untouched.
- §150 — sort foundation: untouched.
- §151 — sort tier-b: untouched.
- §152 — sort + direction persistence: untouched.
- §153 — filter foundation: untouched.
- §154 — filter persistence: untouched (still owns its disk key,
  observer, and setter — extended laterally by one axis, not
  vertically).
- §155 — filter tier-b: untouched.
- §156 — display foundation: untouched.
- §157 — display persistence: untouched.
- §158 — category foundation: the intent surface introduced there is
  preserved; the VM handler now ALSO persists in addition to the
  synchronous state copy. UI-visible behaviour on a single tap is
  unchanged.
- Image-quality posture (Coil ImageLoader, OkHttp fetcher, AVIF
  decoder, ktor3 per-byte progress, Skia decoder + maxBitmapSize):
  UNTOUCHED. Category only changes which items the grid lays out;
  cover-image request pipeline is unchanged.

## §160 — Phase 7.x.library.lastupdated — Last-updated timestamp display

§150 ladder rung 11 (the closing rung on the Library-rework's
preference + display ladder, before the rework Library is feature-
complete against the legacy view). The §158/§159 category-tab slice
closed rung 10; this slice surfaces the wall-clock instant at which
the library was last refreshed end-to-end — a read-only status
indicator beneath the search field + category-tabs region — and
closes the prefs-axis ladder. Subsequent Library polish slices (top-
bar download-progress indicator, multi-select bulk-actions polish,
etc.) sit outside the prefs axis and on a separate sub-ladder.

### Strategy

The legacy `LibraryRefreshWorker` (Android-only, at
`app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/work/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:186`)
already persists `LocalDateTime.toString()` ISO-8601 strings into the
`library_last_updated` SharedPrefs cell on every successful refresh.
The rework's `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.refresh()` schedules the
SAME worker via tag `LibraryRefresh` + workerClass
`me.manga.kira.work.LibraryRefreshWorker`, so the Android refresh
path writes the cell uniformly across legacy + rework routes — no
new writer needed.

The cell-of-truth writer being external to the rework drives the
read-only-axis design decision: the slice ships
`observeLastUpdated(): Flow<Instant?>` on `LibraryPrefsRepository`
WITHOUT a `setLastUpdated` counterpart. A setter would invert the
cell ownership (refresh-job completion artifact reclassified as a
user preference) and split write authority across two paths,
neither of which is what the legacy posture preserves. The §150
ladder's prior 5 axes (sort, direction, filter, density, category)
all had setters because they were user-preference axes; lastUpdated
is the FIRST status-indicator axis on this repo, and the contract
KDoc explicitly documents that future status-indicator axes follow
the same read-only shape.

On iOS / Desktop the worker doesn't exist (Android-only
`WorkManager` API). The disk cell stays empty → the
`getStringFlow(..., defaultValue = "")` reader emits `""` → the
`String.toInstantOrNull()` parser returns `null` → the `:ui`
`LastUpdatedRow` renders "Never updated". Same posture as the
legacy `LibraryViewModel.lastUpdatedFlow` on those targets — parity
preserved across the strangler-fig transition.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**:domain** — 1 new use case + 1 modified interface:

- `LibraryPrefsRepository.kt`: appended
  `fun observeLastUpdated(): Flow<Instant?>` at the bottom of the
  interface (after the §158 `setCategory`). Top-level KDoc scope
  list extended with "last-updated timestamp (read-only)" + the
  Task #326 reference + the "no setter — external writer" call-out.
  `import kotlin.time.Instant` added at the top.

- `ObserveLibraryLastUpdatedUseCase.kt` (NEW): one-line delegate
  `operator fun invoke(): Flow<Instant?> = repository.observeLastUpdated()`.
  KDoc cross-references the prior 5 observer use cases as a sibling
  set, declares the "no setter counterpart" rationale, and documents
  the "no `applyView` re-run on collection" posture (timestamp is a
  status indicator, not a narrowing axis — unlike `category` whose
  collector does re-run `applyView` because the visible-item set
  narrows on the new tab).

**:data** — 1 modified impl:

- `LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.kt`: appended
  `override fun observeLastUpdated()` reading from
  `getStringFlow(LAST_UPDATED_KEY, defaultValue = "")` and mapping
  through the new `String.toInstantOrNull()` private extension.
  Added `LAST_UPDATED_KEY = "library_last_updated"` constant in the
  companion. Imports added: `kotlin.time.Instant`,
  `kotlinx.datetime.LocalDateTime`, `kotlinx.datetime.TimeZone`,
  `kotlinx.datetime.toInstant`.

  The `toInstantOrNull` parser handles three edge cases:
  - empty string (first-run or iOS/Desktop) → `null` (so :ui can
    render "Never updated");
  - malformed string (corrupt partial write) → `null` via
    `runCatching { ... }.getOrNull()` (same fallback shape);
  - well-formed `LocalDateTime.toString()` ISO-8601 (e.g.
    `"2026-05-27T14:30:00"`) → `LocalDateTime.parse(...).toInstant(TimeZone.currentSystemDefault())`.

  Why `LocalDateTime.parse(...).toInstant(...)` and not
  `Instant.parse(...)` directly: the legacy worker writes
  `LocalDateTime.toString()` (zone-less local-time format), NOT
  `Instant.toString()` (UTC with `Z` suffix). Naive `Instant.parse`
  would throw on every read. The two-step conversion through the
  current system `TimeZone` matches the legacy
  `LibraryViewModel.lastUpdatedFlow`'s parsing posture at
  `shared/.../library/ui/viewmodel/LibraryViewModel.kt:278`.

**:presentation** — 1 modified state + 1 modified VM:

- `LibraryState.kt`: new field
  `val lastUpdated: Instant? = null` placed BEFORE `error: AppError?`
  (KDoc explains "Read-only — there is no `LibraryIntent` to mutate
  this field" and points at `LibraryPrefsRepository.observeLastUpdated`
  for the cell-ownership rationale). `import kotlin.time.Instant`
  added.

- `LibraryViewModel.kt`: ctor widened by ONE arg —
  `observeLibraryLastUpdated: ObserveLibraryLastUpdatedUseCase` —
  appended as the 16th constructor parameter. New `init {}` collector
  appended after the §158/§159 `observeLibraryCategory` collector:

  ```kotlin
  observeLibraryLastUpdated()
      .onEach { instant -> updateState { it.copy(lastUpdated = instant) } }
      .launchIn(viewModelScope)
  ```

  KDoc comment block above the collector explains why it does NOT
  re-run `applyView`: the timestamp doesn't narrow / reorder the
  visible item set (unlike sort / filter / category collectors).
  Same posture as the §157 density collector.

**:ui** — 1 modified screen:

- `LibraryScreen.kt`: new `LastUpdatedRow(lastUpdated = state.lastUpdated)`
  call appended below the existing `CategoryTabs` row inside
  `LibraryTopBar`. The composable renders a `labelSmall`-styled
  `Text` row with horizontal `spacing.lg` + vertical `spacing.xs`
  padding, showing `"Last updated: <relative time>"` when `lastUpdated`
  is non-null and `"Never updated"` otherwise.

  New private `formatRelativeTime(past: Instant, now: Instant): String`
  helper buckets the elapsed duration into coarse English labels
  (`"just now"`, `"5 minutes ago"`, `"3 hours ago"`, `"yesterday"`,
  `"4 days ago"`, `"2 weeks ago"`, `"3 months ago"`, `"1 year ago"`)
  using `(now - past).inWholeSeconds`. Branches mirror the legacy
  `LocalDateTime.timeAgo()` helper at
  `composeApp/.../core/util/date/Date.kt:65-99` so the rework's
  status label renders identically to the legacy "Last updated"
  Text under the same wall-clock conditions.

  Why inline the formatting in `:ui` rather than route through the
  legacy `:composeApp` helper: the legacy helper depends on
  `:composeApp`'s `stringResource(R.string....)` IDs — pulling it
  into `:ui` would either drag the IDs along (cross-layer leak from
  `:composeApp` into `:ui`) or require a fresh i18n lift (deferred
  to Phase 10 per the legacy's own `TODO` comments). The inline
  branches sit alongside the file's existing English-only
  `LibrarySort.label`, `LibraryFilter.label`, `GridDensity.label`,
  and `LibraryCategory.label` extensions — same deferral posture,
  same i18n lift target.

  Imports added: `kotlin.time.Clock`, `kotlin.time.ExperimentalTime`,
  `kotlin.time.Instant`. `Clock.System.now()` is called at composition
  time inside `LastUpdatedRow`; the displayed label updates on each
  recomposition driven by any state change (search, sort, filter,
  category, density, refresh tick), which is acceptable for a coarse
  "X minutes ago" / "Y hours ago" indicator — the rework does NOT
  spin a `withFrameNanos` ticker to force per-second recompositions
  (same posture as the legacy screen, which also recomposes only on
  Compose state changes).

**:composeApp** — 1 modified module:

- `LibraryReworkModule.kt`: added
  `factory { ObserveLibraryLastUpdatedUseCase(get()) }` to the use-
  case factory block, and `observeLibraryLastUpdated = get(),` to
  the `LibraryViewModel { ... }` constructor block. Import added.

### MVI contract delta

- New state field `lastUpdated: Instant?` (default `null`). Read-
  only — `LibraryIntent` is NOT widened. The field is populated
  exclusively by the `observeLibraryLastUpdated` collector in
  `init {}` and never by intent handlers. Consumers who type-switch
  on the intent sealed don't need to add a new arm.
- New collector in `init {}`. The collector pattern is intentionally
  symmetric to the §157 density collector: pure
  `state.copy(lastUpdated = instant)` without an `applyView` re-run.
  The §150 ladder now has 7 collectors total (refresh-running, sort,
  sortDirection, filter, density, category, lastUpdated); 5 of them
  re-run `applyView`, 2 do not (density and lastUpdated — both
  status / display-tweak axes that don't narrow the visible item set).

### Strangler-fig boundary

The rework's `LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl` reads from
`ObservableSettings("yami_settings")` — the SAME multiplatform-
settings store the legacy `SharedPrefsHelper` reads/writes
(verified in §150/§152/§154/§157/§159 commits). The
`library_last_updated` cell on Android is written by the legacy
`LibraryRefreshWorker` and the rework's `LibraryRefreshRepository
Impl` schedules that same worker — so the rework reads what the
worker wrote, and both legacy + rework views show the SAME timestamp
for the SAME refresh event. No write-path branching. Phase 9.x
route-swap retires the legacy `LibraryViewModel` consumer of the
cell but NOT the worker writer; the cell-of-truth ownership stays
with the worker.

### Files added / modified

- ADD `domain/.../usecase/library/ObserveLibraryLastUpdatedUseCase.kt`
- MOD `domain/.../repository/LibraryPrefsRepository.kt`
- MOD `data/.../repository/LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.kt`
- MOD `presentation/.../library/LibraryState.kt`
- MOD `presentation/.../library/LibraryViewModel.kt`
- MOD `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt`
- MOD `composeApp/.../di/LibraryReworkModule.kt`

Three commits: A (1/3 :domain + :data, SHA `02b7b3c`), B (2/3
:presentation + :ui + Koin, SHA `cdd3919`), C (3/3 docs).

### Deferrals (intentional)

- No worker-write parity on iOS / Desktop. The Android-only worker
  is the cell-of-truth writer; iOS / Desktop will continue to
  render "Never updated" until a future cross-platform refresh
  scheduler lands. That's a separate slice (likely Phase 8.x
  cross-platform background-job parity) and orthogonal to this
  ladder rung. The legacy posture is identical on those targets,
  so the rework is at parity, not regressing.
- No live "X minutes ago" ticker. The rework does NOT spin a
  `withFrameNanos` recomposition driver to update the "5 minutes
  ago" → "6 minutes ago" transition without user interaction. The
  legacy screen also doesn't; a future polish slice could add one
  if user feedback demands it.
- No i18n lift on the relative-time strings. Mirrors the legacy's
  own `TODO Phase 10: stringResource(R.string...)` deferral.
- No `LibraryIntent` to manually clear / reset the timestamp. The
  cell is owned by the worker; surfacing a user-facing "clear" or
  "reset" action would invert ownership.

### Load-bearing fixes preserved

Every load-bearing image-quality fix (§148-§158 — AVIF decoder
registration, OkHttp fetcher, `maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL)`,
HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder, `CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor`,
ktor3 per-byte progress, Reader decoder hints, Library cover
ContentScale.Crop, sort-order pipeline ordering, filter pipeline
ordering, density grid `minSize`, category narrowing): UNTOUCHED.
The lastUpdated slice only adds a status-indicator row below the
category tabs; cover-image request pipeline and grid layout are
unchanged.

## §161 — Phase 7.x.library.downloadprogress — top-bar download-progress indicator (Task #327)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung **12** — adds a top-bar "↓ N" badge that surfaces
the count of chapter downloads currently in the active bucket
(RUNNING ∪ QUEUED ∪ COMPRESSING). The badge is non-interactive,
auto-hides at zero, and renders only in the `:ui` rework Library
top bar (legacy route untouched). The badge diverges intentionally
from the legacy `AnimatedPreloader` icon — the rework `:ui` posture
(§149) avoids `compose.materialIconsExtended` + `compose.animation`,
so the badge uses a text glyph ("↓ N") with `MaterialTheme.typography
.labelMedium` color/weight tokens. The count is richer information
than the legacy's binary "downloading" flag, and the derivation
(count of active-bucket rows from `ObserveDownloadsUseCase`) is free
once the flow is subscribed.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:domain` — NO new symbols. The slice consumes the existing
  `ObserveDownloadsUseCase` (bound by `downloadsReworkModule`, Phase
  7.x.downloads) and the existing `DownloadState` enum. The active-
  bucket predicate is a file-local private extension in
  `:presentation` (YAGNI — single-consumer, presentation semantics).
  Lifting to `:domain` is the path when a second consumer emerges.
- `:data` — NO new symbols. The strangler-fig boundary into legacy
  `:shared` `DownloadRepository` was established in Phase 7.x.downloads
  (see §166) and is reused verbatim. No new `:data` impl.
- `:presentation` — `LibraryState` gains `activeDownloadCount: Int =
  0` (read-only status field, default 0). `LibraryViewModel` widens
  to 17 ctor args (adds `observeDownloads: ObserveDownloadsUseCase`)
  and registers a 7th `init {}` collector that maps each `List<
  DownloadProgress>` emission through `count { it.state.isActive() }`
  and writes the count via bare `state.copy(activeDownloadCount =
  count)` — NO `applyView` re-run (same posture as §157 density /
  §160 lastUpdated; this is a status-indicator axis, not a narrowing
  axis). The `isActive()` predicate is a private file-local extension
  on `DownloadState` enumerating the three active buckets.
- `:ui` — `LibraryScreen.kt` gains a `DownloadProgressBadge(count:
  Int)` private composable inserted into the `LibraryTopBar` actions
  row between `DensityMenu` and the `Random/Refresh` buttons. The
  badge early-returns at `count <= 0` (auto-hide). Non-interactive
  (no `clickable`) — keeping the screen signature stable. Uses
  `LocalSpacing.current.sm` for horizontal padding and
  `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary` for the glyph color.
- `:composeApp` — `LibraryReworkModule.kt` viewModel block widens to
  pass `observeDownloads = get()`. The factory is bound by
  `downloadsReworkModule`; the cross-module resolution travels
  through the global Koin graph loaded by `allReworkModules()`. No
  new module file. No nav graph change.

### MVI delta

- New state field: `activeDownloadCount: Int` (default `0`).
- No new `LibraryIntent` variant — the field is populated only by
  the `observeDownloads` collector in `init {}`.
- No new `LibraryEffect` — the badge is pure local render.
- No reducer — flow-driven projection only.
- Collector pattern: `state.copy(activeDownloadCount = count)`
  without `applyView` re-run. The `applyView` invariant is preserved
  for the 5 narrowing axes (search, filter, sort, sortDirection,
  category); status-indicator axes (refresh-running, density,
  lastUpdated, activeDownloadCount) skip it.

### Strangler-fig boundary

No new `:data` → `:shared` reach. The slice reuses the §166 boundary
already established by Phase 7.x.downloads — `DownloadsRepositoryImpl`
adapts the legacy `:shared` `DownloadRepository` flow into the rework
`Flow<List<DownloadProgress>>` consumed by `ObserveDownloadsUseCase`.
The Library slice resolves the use case from the global Koin graph
and consumes it without any additional repository / impl. One-write-
path posture preserved: the legacy `DownloadWorker` remains the
cell-of-truth writer for download state, and both legacy (`Screen.
Library`'s `AnimatedPreloader`) and rework (`Screen.LibraryRework`'s
badge) views render the same `DownloadState` enum stream.

### Files added / modified

- MOD `presentation/.../library/LibraryState.kt` — `activeDownloadCount`
  field + KDoc.
- MOD `presentation/.../library/LibraryViewModel.kt` — ctor 17th arg,
  imports, `init {}` collector, private `DownloadState.isActive()`.
- MOD `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` — `DownloadProgressBadge`
  composable + top-bar insertion.
- MOD `composeApp/.../di/LibraryReworkModule.kt` — viewModel block
  widens with `observeDownloads = get()`.

Two commits: A (1/2 source, SHA `8645a2f`, 4 files), B (2/2 docs).

### Deferrals (intentional)

- No tap-to-navigate. The badge is a pure indicator; navigating to
  the Downloads screen would expand the slice scope and is already
  reachable from the Settings row. A future polish slice could wire
  it.
- No animated progress arc. The legacy uses `AnimatedPreloader` with
  an indeterminate rotation; the rework's icon-free posture (§149)
  blocks that primitive. A future polish slice could add a custom
  text-based or `LinearProgressIndicator`-based animation if user
  feedback requires it.
- No `:domain` lift for the `isActive()` predicate. Single consumer
  (the Library VM); presentation semantics. YAGNI — promote when a
  second consumer emerges.
- No i18n on the "↓ N" glyph. The glyph is locale-agnostic; the count
  formatting uses Kotlin's default `Int.toString()`. No localized
  pluralization needed.
- No per-manga breakdown. The badge shows an aggregate count; tap-to-
  expand list is out of scope.

### Load-bearing fixes preserved

Every load-bearing image-quality fix (§148-§160 — AVIF decoder, OkHttp
fetcher, `maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL)`, HighQualitySkiaImage
Decoder, `CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor`, ktor3 per-byte progress,
Reader decoder hints, Library cover `ContentScale.Crop`, sort
pipeline, filter pipeline, density grid `minSize`, category
narrowing, lastUpdated reader): UNTOUCHED. The download-progress
slice only adds a top-bar text glyph; cover-image request pipeline,
grid layout, comparator chain, and refresh worker are unchanged.

badge; the legacy MangaCard shows the source label by default
(when `showSource = true`, which is the default state of the
legacy `LibraryViewModel.UiState.showSource` flag). This slice
mirrors the legacy default surface verbatim.

with a switch row in the legacy `CustomFilterBottomSheet`'s

- `:composeApp` — UNCHANGED. No Koin module change, no nav graph

No new boundary reaches. The `Manga.api` field is sourced from

## §165 — Phase 7.x.library.cardlastread — per-card lastReadAt caption (Task #331)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung **17** (jumping over rung 16's display-toggle
mass-port — that's a multi-commit slice on its own; revisit
later). Surface the `:domain` `LibraryManga.lastReadAt: Instant?`
field on the LibraryCard. The field has been populated by `:data`
since §151 (`MAX(SavedChapterEntity.lastReadDate)` per-manga,
feeding the LAST_READ sort axis); the rework card just wasn't
surfacing it.

Adds a "Last read: X ago" caption (relative time formatted via the
existing file-local `formatRelativeTime(past, now)` helper) in
`MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant` beneath the §162
source caption, rendered only when `lastReadAt != null`. The
legacy MangaCard surfaces a similar "Last read" caption when
`showDetails = true`.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:domain` — UNCHANGED. `LibraryManga.lastReadAt: Instant?` has
  been on the model since §151.
- `:data` — UNCHANGED. The `MAX(SavedChapterEntity.lastReadDate)`
  aggregate has been populated since the §151 schema lift.
- `:presentation` — UNCHANGED. State already carries the field
  through `items: List<LibraryManga>` (consumed today by the
  §151 LAST_READ sort comparator).
- `:ui` — `LibraryCard` is annotated `@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)`
  (same opt-in posture as the existing top-bar `LastUpdatedRow`);
  the Column gains one Text after the §162 source caption.
  Style: `MaterialTheme.typography.labelSmall`, color `onSurface
  Variant`, leading `spacing.xs` top padding. Guarded by
  `item.lastReadAt != null`. Calls the existing file-local
  `formatRelativeTime(lastReadAt, Clock.System.now())` helper
  defined at `LibraryScreen.kt:659`.
- `:composeApp` — UNCHANGED.

Card Column order is now (top-to-bottom): cover image, title Row
(with unread / hasDownloads / bookmarkedCount badges), source
caption (§162, gated by `manga.api.isNotBlank()`), last-read
caption (§165, gated by `lastReadAt != null`). Cards with no read
chapters and no bookmarks render the title Row alone above the
source caption.

### DRY: relative-time formatter reuse

The `formatRelativeTime` helper at `LibraryScreen.kt:659` was
introduced in §160 for the top-bar `LastUpdatedRow`. It's a pure
function (`(past: Instant, now: Instant) → String`) that buckets
elapsed wall-clock into coarse English labels (`"just now"`,
`"5 minutes ago"`, `"yesterday"`, `"4 days ago"`, etc.). Reusing
it here keeps every relative-time surface in the screen
consistent and prevents drift between the top-bar label and the
per-card caption when an i18n lift later replaces both at once.

### Strangler-fig boundary

No new boundary reaches. `lastReadAt` is already populated by
the existing `:data` aggregation pipeline.

### Files added / modified

- MOD `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` — `@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::
  class)` annotation added to `LibraryCard`; Text composable
  inline beneath the §162 source caption in LibraryCard's Column.

Two commits: A (1/2 source, SHA `45c988e`, 1 file), B (2/2 docs).

### Deferrals (intentional)

- No live-ticking refresh. The caption snapshots at composition
  time (same posture as `LastUpdatedRow`); recomposition driven
  by Library state changes refreshes the label. A "5 minutes
  ago" caption won't tick to "6 minutes ago" without a state
  change. Live-ticking would require a `LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
  while (true) { delay(60_000); now = Clock.System.now() } }`
  per card — costly for large libraries and the legacy doesn't
  do it either.
- No exact-timestamp tooltip. The legacy doesn't have one;
  the rework matches.
- No i18n lift. Strings are literal English — same TODO posture
  as §160 (`LastUpdatedRow`) and the legacy `formatRelativeTime`
  equivalent. Phase 10's i18n pass will handle both surfaces in
  one sweep.

### Load-bearing fixes preserved

Every load-bearing fix (§148-§164): UNTOUCHED. The cardlastread
slice adds a single Text caption; pipeline / layout / comparator
/ worker / prior status / source / downloaded / bookmark
indicators are all untouched. §149 icon-free posture is N/A
(text caption, not a glyph).

## §166 — Phase 7.x.library.cardprogress — per-card "N / M chapters" caption (Task #332)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung **18** — surface the `:domain` `LibraryManga.
totalChapters: Int` field (already populated since §151,
feeding the TOTAL_CHAPTERS sort axis) as a "N / M chapters"
caption inside LibraryCard's Column. Read count is derived
inline as `totalChapters - unreadCount` (both fields already on
the model — no schema add).

Maps to the legacy MangaCard's `showDetails = true` totalChapters
+ readCount icon+count pair (`Icons.Outlined.List` +
`Icons.Outlined.RemoveRedEye`, each with a numeric count). The
rework collapses both into a single compact caption to preserve
the icon-free posture (§149) and keep the card vertically tight.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:domain` — UNCHANGED. `LibraryManga.totalChapters` and
  `LibraryManga.unreadCount` have been on the model since §151
  / Phase 6.2.
- `:data` — UNCHANGED. Both fields are populated by the existing
  aggregation in `MangaRepositoryImpl`.
- `:presentation` — UNCHANGED. State already carries both fields.
- `:ui` — `LibraryCard`'s Column gains one Text after the §165
  last-read caption. Style: `MaterialTheme.typography.labelSmall`,
  color `onSurfaceVariant`, leading `spacing.xs` top padding.
  Guarded by `item.totalChapters > 0`.
- `:composeApp` — UNCHANGED.

Final card Column order (top-to-bottom): cover image, title Row
(title + 3 badges), source caption (§162), last-read caption
(§165), progress caption (§166). Each lower caption is
independently gated; cards with minimal data render only what
applies.

### Read-count derivation

`readCount = (totalChapters - unreadCount).coerceIn(0,
totalChapters)`. The coercion floor defends against a transient
mid-emission state where `unreadCount` briefly exceeds
`totalChapters` — possible during a chapter-list refresh when the
Room aggregate query observes the table while a worker is
deleting chapters and re-adding them. The floor matches the
legacy MangaCard's posture (legacy `readCount` is computed
similarly in `MangaDisplayItem`'s factory).

No `Math.max`-style util is introduced; `coerceIn` is from stdlib
and is the idiomatic Kotlin guard for this axis.

### Strangler-fig boundary

No new boundary reaches. Both `totalChapters` and `unreadCount`
are already populated by the existing `:data` aggregation
pipeline.

- MOD `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` — Text composable beneath
  the §165 last-read caption in LibraryCard's Column.

## §167 — Phase 7.x.library.display.foundation2 — display-toggle prefs foundation (Task #333)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung **16a** — lift the five legacy `library_show_*`
boolean display toggles into the rework prefs surface as a
bundled ADT. This sub-rung lays the foundation for sub-rungs
16b-16f, which each wire one toggle end-to-end (intent → state
→ reducer → `:ui` gate). Today this commit is inert: no UI
consumer, no VM injection, no observable behaviour change.

The five toggles correspond 1:1 to legacy
`LibraryViewModel.UiState` fields (`showSource`, `showCount`,
`showDetails`, `showButtons`, `showTabs`), persisted via the
legacy `SharedPrefsHelper` under the `library_show_*` keys.
The rework reuses those keys byte-for-byte so the user's
persisted choices survive the strangler-fig transition without
resetting — same shared-cell posture as the sort + direction
+ filter + density + category cells (§152-§159).

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:domain` — NEW `LibraryDisplay` data class (5 booleans, all
  default `true`). MOD `LibraryPrefsRepository` to add
  `observeDisplay(): Flow<LibraryDisplay>` + 5 per-flag
  `setShow*()` suspend setters. NEW `ObserveLibraryDisplayUseCase`
  (one-line delegate, mirrors every prior `Observe*` axis slice).
- `:data` — MOD `LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl` to implement the new
  surface: `combine()` over 5 `getBooleanFlow` streams emits a
  `LibraryDisplay` snapshot per change; 5 `putBoolean` setters
  match the per-flag setter surface. Adds 5 disk-key constants
  (`SHOW_SOURCE_KEY` etc.) all preserving legacy `KEY_SHOW_*`
  literals + a `DEFAULT_SHOW_TOGGLE = true` constant.
- `:presentation` — NOT touched this sub-rung. The VM injection
  + `LibraryState.display` field land in 16b alongside the first
  per-flag toggle wiring.
- `:ui` — NOT touched this sub-rung. The per-card / per-section
  gates on `state.display.*` land in 16b-16f.
- `:composeApp` — MOD `libraryReworkModule` to register
  `ObserveLibraryDisplayUseCase` as a `factory`. No VM ctor arg
  change yet.

### Bundle vs. five-flow rationale

The legacy `LibraryViewModel.UiState` carries five top-level
booleans. The rework collapses them into one nested
`LibraryDisplay` field for three reasons:

1. **Reducer ergonomics** — five top-level state booleans force
   every reducer touching one toggle to spell out four unchanged
   `copy()` args. A nested bundle collapses each flip into a
   single `state.copy(display = state.display.copy(showSource =
   it))`.
2. **VM init collector** — five independent flows would force
   five `init {}` `launchIn` blocks for the same conceptual
   fan-out. One bundled flow + one collector is cleaner. Same
   posture as the §232 `ReadingStatistics` bundle vs. eight
   independent flows.
3. **OCP extension** — a future sixth display preference (cover
   aspect, label position) is a field append on `LibraryDisplay`,
   not a sixth top-level `LibraryState` boolean. The bundle
   contains the blast radius.

The symmetry break — bundled reads but per-flag setters — is
deliberate: each toggle flip is its own user intent, so a
`setDisplay(d: LibraryDisplay)` bundled setter would force every
intent to construct a full bundle just to flip one bit. That's
busywork the rework's intent pipeline doesn't owe. The `combine`
in `:data` makes the bundled-read side cheap.

### Strangler-fig boundary

No new boundary reaches. The `:data` impl uses the same
`ObservableSettings` binding the prior axes (sort, filter, etc.)
consume. The legacy `SharedPrefsHelper`'s 5 read/write call
sites in `LibraryViewModel.kt:172-176` continue to operate on
the same disk cells the rework now also reads/writes — explicit
shared-cell posture, identical to the §152-§159 persistence
slices.

### Files added / modified

- NEW `domain/.../model/library/LibraryDisplay.kt`
- MOD `domain/.../repository/LibraryPrefsRepository.kt` (6 new
  abstract methods: 1 observe + 5 setters)
- NEW `domain/.../usecase/library/ObserveLibraryDisplayUseCase.kt`
- MOD `data/.../repository/LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl.kt` (6 new
  impls + 5 disk-key constants + 1 default constant)
- MOD `composeApp/.../di/LibraryReworkModule.kt` (1 factory
  registration)

Two commits: A (1/2 source, SHA `234cd59`, 5 files at the cap),
B (2/2 docs).

### Deferrals (intentional)

- No `:presentation` wiring. The `LibraryState.display` field +
  5 `OnToggleShow*` intent variants + 5 reducer cases + VM init
  collector land in 16b alongside the first per-flag toggle
  (`showSource` gates §162 cardsource caption).
- No `:ui` gate. Per-card / per-section visibility gates on
  `state.display.*` land in 16b-16f, one per sub-rung.
- No toggle UI surface. The bottom sheet (legacy
  `DisplayOptionsSection`) or alternate inline switch row lands
  in a separate sub-rung 16g after all 5 toggles are wired
  end-to-end.
- No set use cases. The 5 `SetLibraryShowSource`-style use
  cases land in 16b-16f, each alongside its toggle's
  presentation + UI wiring.

### Load-bearing fixes preserved

Every load-bearing fix (§148-§166): UNTOUCHED. This sub-rung
adds `:domain` types and a `:data` impl extension; pipeline /
layout / comparator / worker / prior captions are all
untouched.

### Strategy

rung-16a foundation (§167). Wires the `showSource` display-toggle
end-to-end from disk through the rework `:presentation` layer.
This sub-rung is **`:presentation`-only on the source side** (no
`:ui` edit) because the UI gate of the §162 cardsource caption on
`state.display.showSource` lands as a follow-on 1-file `:ui`
commit (16b2) — keeping each sub-rung at or under the 5-file cap

After this slice the user-toggle plumbing is **functional but
silent**: an `OnToggleShowSource(value)` intent flips the persisted
cell and updates `state.display.showSource` immediately, but no UI

The rework remains a debug-guarded parallel route at
`Screen.LibraryRework`; the legacy `Screen.Library` route stays
exclusively bound to the legacy `LibraryViewModel`, which reads/
writes the same disk cell (`library_show_source`) — the
strangler-fig keeps both routes in sync on the same persisted choice.

**`:domain`** — one new file:

  (NEW): one-line setter delegating to
  `LibraryPrefsRepository.setShowSource`. Matches the
  `SetLibraryGridDensityUseCase` / `SetLibraryCategoryUseCase` /
  `SetLibraryFilterUseCase` shape exactly.

  *Why one use case per flag, not a bundled
  `SetLibraryDisplayUseCase(d: LibraryDisplay)`*: each toggle flip is
  its own intent (`OnToggleShowSource`, future `OnToggleShowCount`,
  etc.). A bundled setter would force every per-toggle reducer to
  construct a full bundle just to flip one bit; the read side
  already does the `combine` cheaply in `:data`. Symmetry break is
  deliberate.

**`:presentation`** — three modified files:
- `presentation/.../library/LibraryState.kt`: adds
  `val display: LibraryDisplay = LibraryDisplay()` field plus
  import. Defaults to all-`true` (matches legacy
  `prefs.getBoolean(KEY_SHOW_*, true)` posture byte-for-byte at
  `LibraryViewModel.kt:172-176`). KDoc spells out the "no
  `applyView` re-run" rationale (toggle flips only change which
  `:ui` surfaces are visible).
- `presentation/.../library/LibraryIntent.kt`: adds
  `data class OnToggleShowSource(val value: Boolean) : LibraryIntent`
  variant. KDoc notes the parallel parametric variants for
  Count/Details/Buttons/Tabs are deliberately deferred to rungs
  16c-16f rather than collapsed into a single
  `OnToggleDisplayFlag(field, value)` — per-flag intent boundaries
  keep the reducer narrow and match the established §152 / §154 /
  §157 / §158 / §159 per-axis intent shape.
- `presentation/.../library/LibraryViewModel.kt`: two new ctor
  args (`observeLibraryDisplay: ObserveLibraryDisplayUseCase`,
  `setLibraryShowSource: SetLibraryShowSourceUseCase`); a new
  `init {}` collector projecting `LibraryDisplay` snapshots into
  `state.display`; new `is LibraryIntent.OnToggleShowSource ->
  onToggleShowSource(intent.value)` reducer case + private helper
  that synchronously copies state and launches the setter.

**`:composeApp`** — one modified file:
- `composeApp/.../di/LibraryReworkModule.kt`: binds the new
  `SetLibraryShowSourceUseCase` as a factory; threads the two new
  ctor args into the `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(...) }` block.

**`:ui`** — untouched this sub-rung. The cardsource caption gate
on `state.display.showSource` lands as the follow-on 16b2 commit.

### Observer-echo posture

Same shape as §154 / §157 / §158 / §159 persistence wirings:
1. User submits `OnToggleShowSource(true)`.
2. Reducer copies state synchronously
   (`state.display.copy(showSource = true)`) — `:ui` recomposes
   the (future) gated surface immediately.
3. Reducer launches `setLibraryShowSource(true)` on
   `viewModelScope`.
4. `:data` writes through to multiplatform-settings.
5. The `observeLibraryDisplay()` flow in `init {}` re-emits the
   new bundled snapshot.
6. The state update from the re-emission is idempotent (same
   booleans → same `state.display`) and `StateFlow`'s distinct-
   emission guard collapses the echo to a no-op recomposition.

The collector remains the cell-of-truth observer (so an external
write — e.g. legacy `LibraryViewModel` writing the same disk key —
propagates here too).

## §172 — Phase 7.x.library.display.showdetails — showDetails end-to-end (Task #338)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung 16d — third of five per-flag verticals on the
display-toggle ADT introduced in 16a (§167). Mirrors rung 16b
(showSource, §168) and rung 16c (showCount, §170) shape exactly:
one new `:domain` setter use case + one new `:presentation`
intent variant + reducer case + helper + one new Koin factory
binding + ctor thread. No new `:data` work (rung 16a already wired
all five `setShow*` setters and the `library_show_details` disk
cell). No `:ui` work in this sub-rung (the `:ui` gates of §165
cardlastread + §166 cardprogress land as the 1-file 16d2 follow-on,
mirroring the 16b/16b2 + 16c/16c2 split).

The slice keeps the established "bundle ADT for read, per-flag
setter for write" asymmetry from 16a. The read side combines the
five disk cells into a single `Flow<LibraryDisplay>` via
`combine(5)` in `:data` — cheap, one observer in the VM. The
write side has five separate use cases because each toggle flip
in the UI is its own `LibraryIntent` variant; a bundled setter
would force every per-toggle reducer to construct a full
`LibraryDisplay` instance just to flip one bit.

### Why one flag gates two captions

The legacy `DisplayOptionsSection` bundles the "last-read"
timestamp caption (§165 cardlastread) and the "progress"
(read/total) caption (§166 cardprogress) under a single
`SwitchItem` row labelled "Details". The persisted cell is one
disk key (`library_show_details`). The rework preserves that
bundling at the flag level — same `library_show_details` cell,
one `display.showDetails: Boolean` field, two `:ui` gates (both
land in 16d2). Same "two-captions-per-flag" pattern as rung 16c
(`showCount` bundles §163 + §164 — see §170).

This bundling is a deliberate legacy-parity choice: splitting
into separate `showLastRead` / `showProgress` flags would
introduce two new disk cells and break the legacy disk-format
strangler-fig (legacy + rework routes share the same cells). The
ergonomic cost is one less knob in the UI — users who want one
caption but not the other don't have that option in the legacy
either, so the rework matches.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:domain`** — one new file:

## §174 — Phase 7.x.library.display.showbuttons — showButtons VM-side wiring (Task #340)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung 16e — fourth of five per-flag verticals on the
display-toggle ADT introduced in 16a (§167). Mirrors rung 16b
(showSource, §168), rung 16c (showCount, §170), and rung 16d
(showDetails, §172) shape exactly: one new `:domain` setter use case
+ one new `:presentation` intent variant + reducer case + helper +
one new Koin factory binding + ctor thread. No new `:data` work
(rung 16a already wired all five `setShow*` setters and the
`library_show_buttons` disk cell).

**Single sub-rung — no `:ui` gate follow-on.** Departs from the
16b/16b2 + 16c/16c2 + 16d/16d2 two-rung split because the legacy
"buttons" surface is the `MangaCard` bottom action row (resume /
mark-read / remove icons) which the rework has not yet ported. There
is no rework `:ui` consumer to gate on the new flag yet. The VM-side
write path still needs to land so flips originating from the legacy
display sheet propagate through `LibraryPrefsRepositoryImpl`'s
shared `library_show_buttons` disk cell and the cross-route truth
stays in sync. When a future slice ports the bottom action row to
the rework `LibraryCard`, gating it on `display.showButtons` will be
a 1-file `:ui` follow-on analogous to 16b2 / 16c2 / 16d2 — but
lifted *after* the action-row port itself, not before.

The slice keeps the established "bundle ADT for read, per-flag
setter for write" asymmetry from 16a. The read side combines the
five disk cells into a single `Flow<LibraryDisplay>` via
`combine(5)` in `:data` — cheap, one observer in the VM. The
write side has five separate use cases because each toggle flip
in the UI is its own `LibraryIntent` variant; a bundled setter
would force every per-toggle reducer to construct a full
`LibraryDisplay` instance just to flip one bit.

### Why no `:ui` follow-on this rung (vs. 16b2 / 16c2 / 16d2)

`showSource` (§168 / 16b) gates the §162 cardsource caption — a
caption block that already lives in the rework `LibraryCard`.
`showCount` (§170 / 16c) gates the §163 carddownloaded badge + §164
cardbookmarks caption — two surfaces that already live in the
rework `LibraryCard`. `showDetails` (§172 / 16d) gates the §165
cardlastread caption + §166 cardprogress caption — two more surfaces
that already live in the rework `LibraryCard`.

`showButtons` is different: it gates the legacy MangaCard's bottom
action row (resume button / mark-read button / remove button) which
is a multi-button surface, not a caption. That surface has not been
ported to the rework `LibraryCard` yet — porting it is a separate
future slice (likely Phase 7.x.library.cardactions or similar). The
VM write path still lands today because the legacy display sheet's
toggle flip needs to round-trip through the same disk cell that
legacy `MangaCard` reads, and the rework VM's bundled-observe
collector also needs to see the flip so `state.display.showButtons`
stays accurate for the eventual `:ui` consumer.

In other words: **the rework's persisted truth must stay in lockstep
with the legacy's persisted truth across all five flags, even when
the rework `:ui` doesn't consume one of those flags yet.** Rung 16e
restores that lockstep for `showButtons`.

The collector remains the cell-of-truth observer (so an external

## §175 — Phase 7.x.library.display.showtabs — showTabs end-to-end (Task #341)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung 16f — **fifth and final** per-flag vertical on the
display-toggle ADT introduced in 16a (§167). Closes the 5/5
per-flag ladder (showSource → showCount → showDetails → showButtons
→ showTabs). Mirrors rungs 16b (§168), 16c (§170), 16d (§172), 16e
(§174) shape exactly: one new `:domain` setter use case + one new
`:presentation` intent variant + reducer case + helper + one new
Koin factory binding + ctor thread. No new `:data` work (rung 16a
already wired all five `setShow*` setters and the
`library_show_tabs` disk cell).

**Single sub-rung WITH `:ui` gate** — a hybrid of the 16b/16b2 +
16c/16c2 + 16d/16d2 two-rung split (per-card caption gates) and
the 16e single-sub-rung-no-gate posture (`:ui` consumer doesn't
exist yet). Unlike 16e, the rework has an existing `:ui` consumer
for `showTabs`: the §158 `CategoryTabs` row at the screen level
(NAN / LIKED / WATCHING_NOW tabs above the grid). And unlike
16b/16c/16d, the gate is one screen-level `if (state.display.
showTabs) { CategoryTabs(...) }` — not a per-card caption — so
the 1-line `:ui` change fits inside the same ≤5-file commit cap
as the VM wiring. Combining VM + `:ui` in one rung is the natural
SOLID choice here; splitting would mean a 4-file commit followed
by a 1-file commit, both well inside the cap but for no
boundary-of-concern reason.

The slice keeps the established "bundle ADT for read, per-flag
setter for write" asymmetry from 16a — same rationale as 16b-16e.

### Why a screen-level gate (vs. per-card)

`showSource` / `showCount` / `showDetails` gate per-card
captions inside the `LibraryCard` composable — each toggle hides
one or two lines of card chrome. `showButtons` (deferred — rung
16e) gates a per-card action row.

`showTabs` is different: it gates an entire screen-level row (the
NAN / LIKED / WATCHING_NOW tab strip above the grid). Hiding it
collapses the screen layout one row up; showing it restores the
tab strip. The gate naturally lives in `LibraryScreen`'s
top-bar composition, not inside `LibraryCard`. One `if` wraps the
existing `CategoryTabs(category = state.category, onIntent =
onIntent)` call. When `showTabs = false`, `state.category` is
left untouched — the grid keeps filtering by whatever category
the user last selected; the rework simply hides the tab row that
lets them change it. Same posture as the legacy: tabs hide,
category-filter state persists in the underlying preference cell.

  - Private helper `onToggleShowTabs(value: Boolean)` that does
    synchronous `updateState { ... display.copy(showTabs = value) ... }`
    + `viewModelScope.launch { setLibraryShowTabs(value) }`.

**`:composeApp`** — one modified file:
- `composeApp/.../di/LibraryReworkModule.kt`:
  - Import `SetLibraryShowTabsUseCase`.
  - Factory binding `factory { SetLibraryShowTabsUseCase(get()) }`
    after the existing `SetLibraryShowButtonsUseCase` factory.
  - `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(...) }` block: thread
    `setLibraryShowTabs = get(),` after
    `setLibraryShowButtons = get(),`.

**`:ui`** — one modified file:
- `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` — wrap the existing
  `CategoryTabs(category = state.category, onIntent = onIntent)`
  call inside `LibraryTopBar` (between the search input and the

  the user's previously-selected category.

### Observer-echo posture

Unchanged. Same pattern as 16b/16c/16d/16e:

1. User submits `LibraryIntent.OnToggleShowTabs(true)` (in the
   future, once the toggle UI lands in 16g; for today the legacy
   route's display sheet is the only flip surface and it writes
   the shared `library_show_tabs` disk cell directly).
2. Reducer copies state synchronously
   (`state.display.copy(showTabs = true)`) — the gated `:ui`
   surface (the screen-level `CategoryTabs` row) recomposes
   immediately to reflect the new value.
3. Reducer launches `setLibraryShowTabs(true)` on
   `viewModelScope`.
4. `:data` writes through to multiplatform-settings on the same
   `library_show_tabs` cell as the legacy.
5. The `observeLibraryDisplay()` flow in `init {}` re-emits the
   new bundled snapshot.
6. The state update from the re-emission is idempotent (same
   booleans → same `state.display`) and `StateFlow`'s distinct-
   emission guard collapses the echo to a no-op recomposition.

The collector remains the cell-of-truth observer (so an external
write — e.g. legacy `LibraryViewModel` writing the same disk key —
propagates here too). For today this is also the only way a flip
arrives at the rework VM, because the rework has no toggle UI
yet (lifts in 16g).

## §176 — Phase 7.x.library.display.toggleui — display toggle UI surface (Task #342)

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung 16g — **first slice where the user can flip the 5
display flags directly from the rework UI.** All five per-flag VM
verticals (16b/16c/16d/16e/16f) wired the write path: each toggle
flip from `LibraryIntent.OnToggleShow*` dispatches synchronously to
state + launches a persistence write through
`SetLibraryShow{Source,Count,Details,Buttons,Tabs}UseCase`. The
bundled `observeLibraryDisplay()` Flow in the VM's `init {}` keeps
`state.display` in lockstep with the persisted truth (cross-route:
legacy display sheet writes the same `library_show_*` cells →
multiplatform-settings re-emits → rework VM picks it up).

What the 16b-16f rungs lacked was the *consumer surface*: nothing
in the rework `:ui` dispatched the intents. Until rung 16g, the
only way to flip a flag was via the legacy display sheet (which
the rework picked up indirectly through the disk cell).

Rung 16g adds the consumer: an `AlertDialog`-shaped picker with
five `Switch` rows, one per flag, opened from a new "Display"
`TextButton` in the rework `LibraryScreen`'s top-bar actions row
(sibling to Filter / Sort / Density).

### Why AlertDialog (vs. ModalBottomSheet)

Three reasons:

1. **Consistency with existing rework `:ui` posture** — the only
   other modal in `LibraryScreen.kt` is `DeleteSelectedDialog`
   which uses `AlertDialog`. Reusing the same container primitive
   for the picker avoids introducing a new modal type for a
   5-row surface.
2. **No experimental opt-in cascade** — `ModalBottomSheet` is
   gated on `ExperimentalMaterial3Api` and the picker would
   inherit that gate on every caller. `AlertDialog` is stable
   across all four KMP targets at this project's Material 3
   version.
3. **Functional parity over visual parity** — the legacy uses a
   bottom sheet because it bundles the picker with the
   sort / filter rows (`SortOptionsSection` + `CustomFilterBottomSheet`
   + `DisplayOptionsSection` all inside one sheet). The rework
   already splits sort / filter / density into separate
   `DropdownMenu` anchors in the top-bar (§152 / §154 / §156),
   so there is no shared sheet for the picker to live inside.
   A standalone `AlertDialog` matches the rework's existing
   per-axis modal pattern.

Behaviour parity (the 5 flips writing the same disk cells) is
preserved by the underlying intents from 16b-16f.

### State management: composition-local vs. MVI state

Dialog visibility lives in screen-local
`remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` rather than being lifted into
[me.manga.kira.presentation.library.LibraryState]. Two reasons:

- The rework's `LibraryState` carries data the reducer needs to
  act on (sort / filter / display values, selection set,
  refresh / loading state). The picker's open/closed boolean is
  pure UI ephemera — no reducer logic depends on whether the
  picker is visible.
- Same posture as the rework's `SortMenu` / `FilterMenu` /
  `DensityMenu` which all keep their `expanded` boolean in
  `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` inside the composable.

Lifting visibility into `LibraryState` would force every state
snapshot to carry one more boolean for the picker — net cost with
no architectural benefit. The MVI surface stays tight.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

**`:ui`** — one new file:

- `ui/.../library/DisplayOptionsDialog.kt`:
  - `@Composable internal fun DisplayOptionsDialog(display:
    LibraryDisplay, onIntent: (LibraryIntent) -> Unit, onDismiss:
    () -> Unit)` — `AlertDialog` with title "Display options",
    body Column containing 5 `DisplayToggleRow` calls separated by
    `HorizontalDivider`, and a "Done" `TextButton` in
    `confirmButton`.
  - Each `DisplayToggleRow` is a horizontal `Row` with a `Text`
    label on the left and a Material 3 `Switch` on the right.
    Each `Switch`'s `onCheckedChange` dispatches its
    corresponding `LibraryIntent.OnToggleShow*` variant; the
    `checked` value reads from the bundled `display: LibraryDisplay`
    parameter.

**`:ui`** — one modified file:

- `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt`:
  - `LibraryScreenContent` body — new
    `var showDisplayDialog by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }`
    composition-local state.
  - Top-bar binding — `LibraryTopBar(...)` gains a new
    `onOpenDisplay: () -> Unit` parameter, wired to
    `{ showDisplayDialog = true }`.
  - `LibraryTopBar` — new `TextButton(onClick = onOpenDisplay) {
    Text("Display") }` in the actions row, between
    `DownloadProgressBadge` and `LibraryIntent.OnOpenRandom`'s
    button.
  - End of `LibraryScreenContent` — new
    `if (showDisplayDialog) DisplayOptionsDialog(...)` block,
    sibling to the existing `DeleteSelectedDialog` mount.

No `:domain` / `:data` / `:presentation` / `:composeApp` work —
all the intent variants + use cases + reducer arms + helpers + Koin
factories landed across rungs 16b/16c/16d/16e/16f (§168 / §170 /
§172 / §174 / §175). This slice is pure `:ui` consumption.

### Files added

- `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/library/DisplayOptionsDialog.kt`

### Files modified

- `ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt`

- **`:ui` gate for `showButtons`** — still deferred. The rung 16e
