## §177 — Phase 7.x.library.carddownloadedcount — Per-card "↓ N" downloaded chapter count caption

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung 17 — additive lift of the per-manga downloaded-
chapter count from a Room aggregate column (already populated by the
§148 chapter-metrics flow) onto the `:domain` `LibraryManga` model,
then surfaced on the rework `LibraryCard` as a "↓ N" caption parallel
to §164's "🔖 N" bookmark caption. Three modified files in one
commit; mirrors Task #330's bookmark-count lift pattern verbatim. No
schema migration: the `MangaChapterMetrics.downloadedCount` Room
column has fed the existing `hasDownloads: Boolean` (DOWNLOADED
filter predicate) since §148; this slice exposes the raw count
alongside the boolean — same column, two surfaces.

### Why the boolean and the raw count coexist

`LibraryManga.hasDownloads` (the boolean `downloadedCount > 0`) is
retained because the DOWNLOADED filter axis predicate consumes the
boolean directly (no comparator change needed). The new
`LibraryManga.downloadedCount: Int` field exposes the richer "how
many" datum for the per-card caption — same posture as Task #330's
`bookmarkedCount` lift, which also kept the unread-count badge AND
added a bookmark count caption without replacing anything. The
mapper (`LibraryMappers.kt`) was NOT signature-widened: the
`downloadedCount: Int` parameter already existed (consumed for the
`hasDownloads = downloadedCount > 0` derivation), so the lift adds
exactly one named-arg assignment to the `LibraryManga` constructor.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:domain`** — `LibraryManga.downloadedCount: Int` field added.
  KDoc captures the coexistence with `hasDownloads` (same column,
  filter predicate vs. caption). Required Int (default `0` for no
  downloads or no saved chapters; same `Int.coerceAtLeast(0)`
  posture as `unreadCount`).
- **`:data`** — `LibraryMappers.kt` `toLibraryManga()` threads the
  existing `downloadedCount` mapper parameter onto the new field.
  No signature widening. No new repo call sites: every existing
  caller (`LibraryRepositoryImpl.observeLibrary` Flow combine)
  already passes `downloadedCount` for `hasDownloads`.
- **`:ui`** — `LibraryScreen.kt` adds one `if`-gated `Text`
  composable to the per-card caption row between the existing "✓"
  hasDownloads badge (§163) and the "🔖 N" bookmark caption (§164).
  Gated on `display.showCount && item.downloadedCount > 0` —
  bundles under the same `showCount` flag as §163 / §164 (matches
  the legacy `DisplayOptionsSection` "Count" row's behaviour of
  gating all three count surfaces under one disk cell).

| --- | --- | --- |
| `domain/.../model/LibraryManga.kt` | MOD | New `downloadedCount: Int` field + KDoc capturing coexistence with `hasDownloads` boolean |
| `data/.../mapper/LibraryMappers.kt` | MOD | Output-only widening — one named-arg pass-through of an already-existing parameter |
| `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` | MOD | One `if`-gated `Text` caption inserted between §163 "✓" badge and §164 "🔖 N" caption |

3 files total — well under the 5-file commit cap.

### Deferrals

- **i18n** — the new caption uses the literal `"↓ "` glyph + integer
  format (`"↓ ${item.downloadedCount}"`). Phase 10's
  `stringResource` sweep will lift this alongside the legacy
  `DisplayOptionsSection`'s "downloaded N" caption and the rework's
  parallel "🔖 N" bookmark caption (§164) in one pass.
- **Long-count handling** — at extreme counts (e.g., 999+) the
  layout follows the same posture as the unread badge / bookmark
  caption: no explicit clamp. If user-feedback shows visual
  overflow on tiny grid cells, a separate `:ui` slice can introduce
  a `truncatedCount()` helper consumed by all three surfaces (✓ /
  ↓ N / 🔖 N) in one pass — not premature today.

## §178 — Phase 7.x.library.cardaddedat — Per-card "Added: X ago" caption

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung 18 — additive `:ui` surfacing of the existing
`LibraryManga.addedAt: Instant` field as an "Added: X ago"
relative-time caption on the rework `LibraryCard`. The field has
been populated by `:data` since the initial Library slice
(`SavedMangaEntity.savedTimestamp` → `LibraryManga.addedAt` in
`toLibraryManga()`), so this slice is a pure `:ui` consumer
addition — no `:domain` / `:data` / `:presentation` /
`:composeApp` touchpoints. Mirrors §165's per-card "Last read"
caption pattern verbatim: reuses the same `formatRelativeTime`
helper, gates on the same `display.showDetails` flag, occupies a
row position adjacent to the existing relative-time captions.

### Why a `:ui`-only slice

The data plumbing has been live since the Library slice's
inception: `LibraryRepositoryImpl.observeLibrary` Flow combine
threads `SavedMangaEntity.savedTimestamp` into
`toLibraryManga(addedAt = Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(...))`.
The legacy `MangaCard` already consumes the same column and
renders an "Added" caption when `showDetails = true`. The rework
`LibraryCard` had simply not surfaced the field; this slice closes
that visual-parity gap with a single `if`-gated `Text` composable.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:domain`** — UNTOUCHED. `LibraryManga.addedAt: Instant` field
  pre-exists; KDoc already documents the populated source
  (`SavedMangaEntity.dateAdded`).
- **`:data`** — UNTOUCHED. `LibraryMappers.toLibraryManga()`
  already assigns `addedAt = Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds
  (savedTimestamp)`.
- **`:presentation`** — UNTOUCHED. `LibraryState` re-exports
  `:domain`'s `LibraryManga`; the field is already on the state.
- **`:ui`** — `LibraryScreen.kt` adds one `if`-gated `Text`
  composable to the per-card caption row between the existing
  "Last read" caption (§165) and the "N / M chapters"
  chapter-progress caption (§166). Gated on `display.showDetails`
  parallel to its siblings. Caption text: `"Added: ${
  formatRelativeTime(item.addedAt, Clock.System.now())}"`.

### Caption row order under `showDetails`

Three captions now group under `display.showDetails = true`:

1. **Last read** (§165) — newest activity first.
2. **Added** (§178, this slice) — older event, complementary
   information ("when did I start tracking this").
3. **N / M chapters** (§166) — densest data point closes the row.

This ordering reflects the user's mental model: most-recent
interaction → first-ever interaction → static metric.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt` | MOD | One `if`-gated `Text` caption inserted between §165 "Last read" and §166 "N / M chapters" captions |

1 file total — well under the 5-file commit cap. Pure `:ui` slice.

### Deferrals

- **i18n** — caption uses literal "Added: " prefix + the
  `formatRelativeTime` helper (which itself uses English literal
  strings: "just now", "yesterday", "N minutes ago", etc.). Phase
  10's `stringResource` sweep will lift both the prefix and the
  helper's internal strings alongside §160's "Last updated"
  prefix and §165's "Last read" prefix in one pass.
- **`addedAt: Instant?` nullable variant** — not introduced. The
  current field is non-nullable (every saved manga has a definite
  add-time from the `savedTimestamp` epoch-millis column, which
  has never been nullable in the schema). If a future migration
  ever introduces a "manga imported from external source without
  known add-time" path, the field could lift to nullable with a
  corresponding gate; not premature today.

## §179 — Phase 7.x.library.actionrow — Per-card 3-button action row

### Strategy

§150 ladder rung 19 (the FINAL Library ladder rung) — port the
legacy `MangaCard` bottom 3-button action row (WatchLater / Like /
Delete) to the rework `LibraryCard`. Closes the §174 `showButtons`
`:ui` gate, which had been deferred through 6 prior rungs (16e
onwards: the VM/Koin side landed in rung 16e, but the action row
itself hadn't been ported because the rework `LibraryCard` simply
hadn't had a button row yet). Unlike the trailing 16g/17/18
single-file slices, this rung legitimately needs a multi-commit
roadmap because it touches all four layers — `:domain` interface
+ `:data` impl + `:presentation` MVI + `:ui` composable — plus
Koin wiring. Three source commits + one docs commit, all ≤5
files each per the standing cap.

### Why it spans all four layers

The legacy `MangaCard`'s action row binds three callbacks:
`onLikeClick`, `onWatchingNowClick`, `onDeleteClick`. The first
two flip boolean affinity flags on `SavedMangaEntity` (`isLiked`
/ `isWatchingNow`) via `mangaDao.updateManga(entity.copy(...))` —
they are **mutations** the rework `LibraryRepository` had not yet
exposed. The third (`onDeleteClick`) already had a path through
the existing `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` (called with a
singleton key list). So the slice carries two new write methods
end-to-end:

- `LibraryRepository.toggleLiked(key: MangaKey): AppResult<Unit>`
- `LibraryRepository.toggleWatchingNow(key: MangaKey): AppResult<Unit>`

Plus their use cases, Koin factory bindings, MVI intent variants,
VM handlers, and the `:ui` composable that dispatches them. The
single-delete reuses `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` with no new
write path — the third intent variant (`OnSingleDelete`) is a
routing-only addition.

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- **`:domain`** — TWO new methods on `LibraryRepository`:
  `toggleLiked(key)` and `toggleWatchingNow(key)`. Both `suspend`
  returning `AppResult<Unit>`. Each method's KDoc documents the
  flip-not-set semantics (the impl reads-modifies-writes the
  current flag, the caller cannot directly set a value), the
  graceful-no-op posture on membership-absent (matches
  `removeFromLibrary`'s shape), and the strangler-fig boundary
  narrative ("legacy `MangaDao.updateManga` write path verbatim;
  Phase 9.x retires"). Two new use case classes:
  `ToggleMangaLikedUseCase` and `ToggleMangaWatchingNowUseCase`,
  both thin pass-throughs to the repository methods.

- **`:data`** — TWO new method impls on `LibraryRepositoryImpl`.
  Each reads the entity by `(api, title)` via
  `mangaDao.getIdByApiAndTitle` → `mangaDao.getMangaById`, flips
  the boolean field via `entity.copy(...)`, persists via
  `mangaDao.updateManga` (`@Update onConflict = REPLACE`). Same
  DAO method, same `entity.copy(...)` semantics, same
  `runCatchingStorage { withContext(dispatchers.io) { ... } }`
  wrapper that the existing `removeFromLibrary` impls use. Disk
  cell stays bit-for-bit identical across the rework / legacy
  boundary.

- **`:presentation`** — THREE new sealed-interface variants on
  `LibraryIntent`:
  - `OnToggleLike(key: MangaKey)` — flip the `isLiked` bit.
  - `OnToggleWatchingNow(key: MangaKey)` — flip the
    `isWatchingNow` bit.
  - `OnSingleDelete(key: MangaKey)` — remove a single manga
    (routes through `BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase` with a
    singleton list).
  Three new reducer arms in `LibraryViewModel.handle()`. Three
  new private suspend handlers. Two new ctor params on the VM:
  `toggleMangaLiked: ToggleMangaLikedUseCase` and
  `toggleMangaWatchingNow: ToggleMangaWatchingNowUseCase`. The
  affinity-flag handlers emit `LibraryEffect.ShowError` on
  failure (silent on success — the flow re-emits from Room).
  The single-delete handler emits the existing
  `ShowBulkRemoveSuccess(count = 1)` snackbar on success — same
  feedback shape as multi-select bulk delete so the user-visible
  affordance is uniform whether deleting one or many.

- **`:ui`** — One new private composable
  (`LibraryCardActionRow`) in `LibraryScreen.kt` plus a wrapping
  `BoxWithConstraints` around the existing `LibraryCardCover` so
  the cover's measured width can drive the adaptive button size.
  Action row visibility is gated on `display.showButtons &&
  !isInSelectionMode` — the second predicate prevents the row's
  `IconButton`s from intercepting taps that should toggle
  selection during multi-select. Three stacked `IconButton`s in
  a `Column` aligned to `CenterEnd` of the cover. Glyphs:
  - WatchLater: `🕒` (off) / `⏰` (on) — clock outline / alarm.
  - Like: `♡` (off) / `♥` (on) — heart outline / heart filled.
  - Delete: `🗑` — trash can.
  Each glyph wrapped in a `Text` inside an `IconButton`, matching
  the established rework `:ui` icon-free posture (see
  `DetailsScreen`'s back-button `"←"` / refresh-button `"↻"` —
  `Icons.Filled.*` is NOT used anywhere in the rework `:ui`
  layer).

- **`:composeApp`** — Two new `factory` lines in
  `libraryReworkModule` for the new use case classes. Two new
  named ctor args on the `viewModel { LibraryViewModel(...) }`
  block. No new nav routes — the action row is in-card, not a
  separate screen.

### MVI surface delta

- **State** — UNCHANGED. The action row reads existing
  `LibraryManga.isLiked` / `isWatchingNow` fields (already
  flowing through the state via the `:data` `combine` block on
  `mangaDao.getAllSavedMangaFlow`). No new state field.

- **Intent** — three new variants (`OnToggleLike`,
  `OnToggleWatchingNow`, `OnSingleDelete`).

- **Effect** — UNCHANGED. The handlers reuse existing
  `LibraryEffect.ShowError` and `LibraryEffect.ShowBulkRemoveSuccess`
  variants.

- **Reducer arms** — three new arms (one per intent variant).

### Adaptive button sizing — `BoxWithConstraints` formula

The rework grid uses three density tiers (Compact / Comfortable /
Spacious) that each render the cover at a different cell width.
A fixed-size action row would either be cramped in Compact or
oversized in Spacious. The legacy `MangaCard` solved this by
reading the cover's measured width and computing
`buttonSize = (cardWidth * 0.22f).coerceIn(4.dp, 40.dp)`. The
rework adopts the same formula verbatim:

```kotlin
BoxWithConstraints(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
    val cardWidth: Dp = maxWidth
    val buttonSize: Dp = (cardWidth * 0.22f).coerceIn(4.dp, 40.dp)
    LibraryCardCover(...)
    if (display.showButtons && !isInSelectionMode) {
        LibraryCardActionRow(buttonSize = buttonSize, ...)
    }
}
```

`BoxWithConstraints` is the Compose primitive that exposes the
incoming constraints (in `maxWidth: Dp` form), letting child
composables size themselves proportionally. The action row's
`Column` and its three `IconButton`s all consume `buttonSize`
via `Modifier.size(buttonSize)`, so every density tier renders
proportionally to the cover tile.

### Single-delete UX — direct, no confirmation

The single-tap delete intent (`OnSingleDelete`) routes directly
through `bulkRemoveFromLibrary(listOf(key))` with NO
confirmation dialog at the card level. Mirrors the legacy
`MangaCard` posture — the legacy's trash IconButton dispatches
`onDeleteClick` directly, no dialog. Rationale: the action row
button is small enough that accidental taps are rare, and the
existing `ShowBulkRemoveSuccess` snackbar provides post-action
feedback (though without an "Undo" affordance — that's a
separate slice if needed). Multi-select bulk-delete keeps its
existing confirmation `AlertDialog` (Task #312, §138) because
the blast radius scales with the selected count.

### Selection-mode gating

The action row is gated on `!isInSelectionMode` (in addition to
`display.showButtons`). When the user enters multi-select
(long-press a card), the per-card `IconButton`s would
otherwise intercept tap events that should toggle selection.
The gate hides the row entirely during selection mode, freeing
the cover surface for selection-toggle taps. This is a
parallel-but-different posture from the legacy `MangaCard`,
which gates only on `showButtons` because the legacy selection
overlay is at screen level (a separate `Modifier.combinedClickable`
wrapper at the outer `Card` rather than at the inner row), so
the legacy row doesn't intercept selection taps.

### Glyph posture rationale

The rework `:ui` layer does NOT use `androidx.compose.material.icons.*`
anywhere. The established posture (set by `DetailsScreen` and
followed by all rework screens) is to wrap text glyphs in
`IconButton` containers (`IconButton { Text("←") }` for the
back button, `IconButton { Text("↻") }` for the refresh button).
This slice continues the posture. Affinity flags flip their
glyph as a visual state surface:

| Flag | Off glyph | On glyph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isWatchingNow` | `🕒` (clock) | `⏰` (alarm) |
| `isLiked` | `♡` (heart outline) | `♥` (heart filled) |
| (delete) | `🗑` | — (action, no state) |

The on/off color of `isLiked` also lifts: `Color.Red` for the
filled heart vs. the default `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary`
for off — matches the legacy MangaCard's red-on-tap behavior.

### Files

| File | State | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `domain/.../repository/LibraryRepository.kt` | MOD | Two new suspend methods `toggleLiked` / `toggleWatchingNow` |
| `domain/.../usecase/library/ToggleMangaLikedUseCase.kt` | NEW | Pass-through use case for `isLiked` flip |
| `domain/.../usecase/library/ToggleMangaWatchingNowUseCase.kt` | NEW | Pass-through use case for `isWatchingNow` flip |
| `data/.../repository/LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt` | MOD | Strangler-fig impls of the two new methods (read-modify-write via legacy `MangaDao.updateManga`) |

Eight source files total, split across three commits (4 + 3 + 1)
to respect the 5-file cap. Plus the docs commit (this section +
the `SOLID_AUDIT.md` entry).

iOS-device smoke test deferred to user's Mac. Expected
observable behaviour: the rework `LibraryCard` now shows a
vertical stack of three IconButtons aligned to the right edge of
the cover whenever `display.showButtons = true` AND
`!isInSelectionMode`. Tapping the clock toggles
`isWatchingNow` (glyph flips `🕒` ↔ `⏰`); tapping the heart

### Deferrals

- **Undo affordance for single-delete** — not introduced. The
  existing `ShowBulkRemoveSuccess` snackbar provides the action
  notification but has no "Undo" button. A future slice could
  lift one (would require an `AddToLibrary` route that accepts
  a stale `Manga` for re-insert, which doesn't yet exist).
  Matches the legacy `MangaCard`'s posture exactly.

- **Tooltip on long-press of action button** — not introduced.
  Legacy `MangaCard` has no tooltip either. Compose Material3's
  `TooltipBox` could lift one in a future polish slice if user
  feedback indicates the glyphs are unclear.

- **Animated state-flip** — the heart and clock glyphs flip
  instantaneously (recomposition only). A future polish slice
  could lift a `Crossfade` or scale `AnimatedVisibility` to
  smooth the transition. Matches the legacy `MangaCard`'s
  posture (legacy uses identical instantaneous swap).

- **i18n** — the action row uses literal Unicode glyphs; no
  user-facing text strings. The `ShowBulkRemoveSuccess` snackbar
  text ("Removed N manga") is already English-literal in the
  rework — its i18n lift is part of the broader Phase 10
  `stringResource` sweep.

## §180 — Phase 9.x.library.swap — Route-swap `Screen.Library` → rework `LibraryScreen` (Task #346)

### Strategy

§150 ladder closed at rung 19 (§179 / Task #345) with full visual +
behavioural parity vs the legacy `MangaCard` — the per-card action row
was the final user-visible gap. With parity achieved, the user-facing
`Screen.Library` nav entry is flipped from rendering the legacy
`:composeApp/.../features/library/ui/screens/LibraryScreen` (backed by
legacy `LibraryViewModel`) to rendering the rework
`:ui/.../library/LibraryScreen` (backed by the rework `:presentation/.../
library/LibraryViewModel`). Same shape as the §138/§140/§285-§295/§301/
§305 prior swaps. Route key `object Library`, the
`BottomNavigationBar` start-destination binding, and external callers
all stay byte-identical.

### Files modified

| File | Layer | Δ | SRP role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/LibraryScreenRoute.kt` | `:composeApp` | rewritten (full file, ~111 lines) | Nav adapter — owns the route's render-target decision + threads `safeNavigate(...)` for the MangaDetails forward + hosts the `WhatsNewViewModel` first-launch redirect orchestration |
| `composeApp/.../App.kt` | `:composeApp` | `composable<Screen.Library>` block simplified (22 → 13 lines) | Nav graph hookup — drops legacy callback wiring (`downloadViewModel`, `onOpenRandomClick`, `onLibraryMangaClick`) now that the rework adapter owns those concerns internally |

Two files. ≤5 file cap satisfied with 60% margin.

### Behaviour deltas (intentional)

- **MangaDetails nav schema** — legacy adapter dispatched
  `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails(mangaId: Long)` (typed by Room row id);
  rework adapter dispatches `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl: String,
  api: Int)` (typed by source-identity tuple). Same intentional schema
  delta as §138/§140/§295 — the rework `Manga` `:domain` model carries
  `url` and `api` directly, no Room row id translation needed.
  `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails` itself remains alive in `Screen.kt` to
  serve the legacy `onOpenRandomClick` dispatch from the unrelated
  random-button reach (no longer invoked from this route, but the enum
  case is referenced by App.kt:430's `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails`
  composable block which the Phase 9.x.library.retire sweep will
  collapse later).
- **Random / refresh / delete** — legacy adapter exposed these via
  external callbacks; rework adapter doesn't thread them because the
  rework `LibraryViewModel` + `LibraryScreen` own these affordances
  internally (§148 refresh, §149 random, §144 ConfirmRemoveDialog
  delete). Same observable user-facing actions, hosted differently.
- **Download-progress badge** — legacy adapter threaded a
  `DownloadViewModelv2` dep; rework Library wires the badge via
  `ObserveActiveDownloadsUseCase` injected by `LibraryReworkModule`
  (§161 / Task #327). Same observable badge, threaded through Koin.
- **Action row, sort, filter, display toggles, category tabs** — all
  rework-internal, dispatched as `LibraryIntent` variants and reduced
  to `LibraryState` slices. Legacy adapter knew nothing of these
  affordances because rung 19 (and the §163-§176 sort/filter/display
  ladder rungs before it) closed the parity in one direction; this
  swap closes it in the other direction by making the rework screen
  user-reachable.

### `WhatsNewViewModel` preservation rationale

The legacy adapter has, for the entire project lifetime, hosted a
`WhatsNewViewModel` first-launch redirect orchestration block:
`shouldShowWhatsNew` + `isLoading` `StateFlow` consumers, a
`hasNavigatedToWhatsNew` `remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` reentrancy
flag, and two `LaunchedEffect` blocks (one that fires the
`navController.safeNavigate(Screen.WhatsNewScreen(true))` on the
condition AND-tuple, and one that resets the flag when
`shouldShowWhatsNew` flips back to false after the navigate). This is
route-host-level launch plumbing — the user lands on `Screen.Library` as
the bottom-nav start destination on every non-first-launch session, and
IFF the app version-code bumped since the last launch the VM's
`shouldShowWhatsNew` flips true and the adapter navigates the user away
to the What's New screen.

It is **NOT** Library state. Hosting it in the rework `LibraryViewModel`
would conflate two unrelated concerns: the Library's domain (manga
display + sort + filter + per-card actions) vs the app's startup
choreography (was the user introduced to the new release notes yet?).
SRP violation. Hosting it in `App.kt` would push composition state into
the root composable, which already owns enough lifecycle juggling.

The adapter is the correct home. The rework adapter preserves the
block verbatim — same two `LaunchedEffect`s, same flag, same
`safeNavigate(Screen.WhatsNewScreen(true))` target. Same observable
first-launch behaviour. Phase 9.x.library.retire (the follow-on
slice that retires the legacy `LibraryScreen` composable + the parallel
`Screen.LibraryRework` debug route + adapter) will leave this block
untouched on the user-facing adapter.

### Parallel-route retirement deferral

The §164/§165 parallel debug routes (`Screen.LibraryRework` +
`LibraryReworkScreenRoute.kt`) remain on disk and reachable via the
debug nav entry. The two adapters now render the **same** rework
`LibraryScreen` via the **same** rework `LibraryViewModel` (resolved
via `koinViewModel()`-scoped Koin binding) — so the debug route is
functionally redundant. A follow-on `Phase 9.x.library.retire` slice
will:

1. Delete `LibraryReworkScreenRoute.kt`.
2. Delete the `composable<Screen.LibraryRework>` block in `App.kt`.
3. Delete the `Screen.LibraryRework` enum case.
4. Delete the legacy `:composeApp/.../features/library/ui/screens/
   LibraryScreen.kt` composable + its scaffolding (`MangaCard.kt`,
   `LibraryItems.kt`, etc.).
5. Delete the legacy `LibraryViewModel` once no other consumer remains
   (audit gate).

Splitting the retirement from the swap respects the 5-file commit cap
and the standing block-and-ask Rule (b): the swap changes observable
behaviour intentionally; the retirement does not. Each slice gets its
own audit entry.

### Cross-references

- §138 — `Phase 7.x.statistics.swap` (route-swap template — the first
  user-facing rework route-swap; this slice mirrors its shape).
- §140 — `Phase 7.x.history.swap` (route-swap template — manga-click
  nav-arg schema delta lifted verbatim here).
- §150 — Library rework ladder (parent narrative; rung 19 closure was
  the precondition for this swap; this slice is the ladder's "exit"
  event into user-reachability).
- §164 — guarded debug nav route for rework `LibraryScreen` (the
  parallel `Screen.LibraryRework` route + adapter that becomes
  functionally redundant after this swap; retirement deferred to
  `Phase 9.x.library.retire`).
- §165 — extended `initKoin()` to thread `allReworkModules()` through
  hosts (the Koin bind path that resolves rework `LibraryViewModel` via
  `koinViewModel()` — preserved unchanged here, the swap just changes
  which adapter calls into it).
- §179 — `Phase 7.x.library.actionrow` (Task #345 — closed §150 rung 19;
  the immediate precondition for this slice — without the action row,
  the swap would have lost three user-visible affordances).
- §285-§295 / §301 / §305 — sibling route-swaps (Sources / Statistics /
  About / History / Updates / WhatsNew / Theme / Language / Complaint /
  Settings / Downloads / onboarding-Sources) — same shape, same
  posture, same intentional schema deltas where applicable.


## §181 — Phase 9.x.library.retire — Retire legacy Library screen + parallel debug route (Task #347)

### Slice goal

With `Screen.Library` flipped to the rework adapter by §180 (commit
`c1a32c2`), the legacy Library cluster has become unreachable: no
nav route, no Koin resolution, no live consumer. This slice collapses
the dead code in 4 commits (plan + parallel-route retire + UI retire +
VM-and-component retire) followed by a docs close-out. Mirrors the
strangler-fig retirement template established by §142-§145 (onboarding
+ VM + dead-VM + Updates retirements) and §146 (stale-KDoc sweep).

### Strategy

Pure deletion. No behaviour changes; the legacy code path was already
unreachable when this slice began. Each commit verifies build gates on
all 4 targets (Android, iOS arm64, iOS sim arm64, Desktop) to prove the
deleted code was truly dead at deletion time.

Per-symbol reachability verification BEFORE each delete (lesson from
commit 3's first attempt — the per-file reachability grep on
`AnimatedPreloader.kt` missed two sibling composables that the file
exported and that were still live). Going forward, retire slices grep
for each `fun X` / `class X` symbol exported by the file, not just the
file's `import` count.

### Scope reduction — `AnimatedPreloader.kt` OUT-OF-SCOPE

`PLAN_library_retire.md` (commit `857070b`) listed
`composeApp/.../features/library/ui/components/AnimatedPreloader.kt`
as a commit-3 deletion target on the assumption that the legacy
`AnimatedPreloader` composable was the file's only export. Per-symbol
grep during commit 3 prep revealed two live siblings:

- `AnimatedNew` (line 105) — consumed by
  `SourcesTabs.kt:31,151`.
- `AnimatedCompressing` (line 128) — consumed by
  `LibraryChapterItem.kt:62,255`.

Only the file-top `AnimatedPreloader` composable is dead. The file
itself stays because the alternative — extracting `AnimatedNew` +
`AnimatedCompressing` into a separate file in the same commit — would
have crossed the slice's pure-deletion boundary. A future targeted
micro-slice (`Phase 9.x.library.deadcomposable.retire`?) can drop just
the dead composable without touching the live siblings. Not blocking;
the dead composable is unreferenced bytecode in commonMain, not a
compile-time or runtime hazard.

### Behaviour preservation

NO observable behaviour change. The legacy code paths were already
unreachable at the start of this slice (§180 flipped the only consumer
to the rework adapter). The build still produces the same APK because
the dead code did not contribute compiled symbols to any reachable
entry point.

The legacy `me.manga.kira.presentation.features.library.ui.viewmodel
.LibraryViewModel` is NOT an MVI VM (it predates the §150 rework
ladder; it exposes `StateFlow<LibraryUiState>` directly plus 8 plain
callbacks). Its retirement does not affect the rework
`:presentation/.../library/LibraryViewModel` MVI contract — that VM,
its `LibraryState`/`LibraryIntent`/`LibraryEffect` triple, and its
Koin binding via `LibraryReworkModule` all stay byte-identical.

### Strangler-fig integrity

Symmetric retirement of the §150 ladder's legacy half. No new
`:data` → `:shared` reach is introduced; the existing strangler-fig
posture (rework `LibraryRepositoryImpl` reaching the legacy `:shared`
`LibraryRepository` from `:data/.../LibraryRepositoryImpl.kt`) is
preserved unchanged. The legacy facade itself stays as the source of
truth until Phase 10 lifts the storage layer.

`presentation.whatsnew.WhatsNewViewModel`), the legacy WhatsNew

NOT retired in this slice (intentional preservation): the legacy
`:shared/.../features/whatsnew/data/WhatsNewModel.kt` data class and
`:shared/.../features/whatsnew/data/WhatsNewRepositoryImpl.kt`
repository implementation. The rework `:data` strangler-fig continues
to delegate through them as the cell of truth for `WhatsNew` model
objects — same posture preserved for Library, Statistics, Language,
Theme, Reader, Settings, History. Those legacy domain files become
retire-able only when the rework migrates the cell of truth in a

### Per-symbol reachability methodology (lesson re-applied from §181)

Per-symbol grep before deletion, not per-import. Each legacy UI symbol
verified:

- `WhatsNewScreen` (entry-point composable) → 0 external callers
  (declarations + self-references only).
- `FeatureCard`, `FullscreenMediaViewer` (consumers of
  `SafeVideoPlayer` + `SingleImage`) → only internal references within
  the package; no `:ui` or `:composeApp` `whatsnew` adapter call sites.
- `WhatsNewHeader`, `PageIndicators`, `NavigationButtons` (declared in
  `WhatsNewComponents.kt`) → only consumed by `WhatsNewScreen`.

- `SafeVideoPlayer` (declared in `VideoComponents.kt`) → consumed only
  by `FeatureCard` + `FullscreenMediaViewer`.
- `SingleImage` (declared in `ImageComponents.kt`) → consumed only by
  `FeatureCard`. The `:shared/promanga` matches on the `SingleImage*`
  substring point to the unrelated `ImageCombinerState.SingleImageReady`
  data class — different namespace, different model.

Two-tier deletion order required: drop the entry point + its direct
consumers first (commit 1), then drop the leaf orphans whose consumers
disappeared (commit 2). Each tier's deletion gated by a fresh 3-target

## §191 — Phase 9.x.complaint.componentprune — surgical in-file dead-code prune

that became partially-dead after #355 (Phase 9.x.complaint.legacyui.

to "legacyui.retire": when a file co-locates reached + unreached

## §192 — Phase 9.x.refreshvm.retire — drop unreachable :shared RefreshViewModel

First `legacyvm.retire` slice — full deletion of a `:shared`
`ViewModel` whose only runtime touchpoint was its own Koin `viewModel
{ ... }` binding. Distinct from `legacyui.retire` (which deletes
`@Composable` screens) and `componentprune` (which prunes unreached
symbols inside a mixed-reach file): this targets a pure VM with zero
UI host, zero debug route, and zero parallel screen. 117 LOC retired +
1-line Koin edit.

### Strategy

The `legacyvm.retire` sub-pattern fills a survey gap left by the
file-deletion sweeps: a `:shared` `ViewModel` that survives because
Koin registers it, not because anything injects it. Pre-flight is the
same per-symbol grep used in #355–#358, with one extra gate: confirm
**no injection sites** (`koinViewModel<X>`, `by viewModel`,
constructor `private val x: X`, field `lateinit var x: X`). If the
only Kotlin reference is the `viewModel { X(get()) }` registration in
a Koin module, the VM is unreachable and the slice is mechanical:
delete the file, drop the binding, replace with a one-line
retire-pointer comment.

This is also the first retire slice that produces zero `:composeApp`
churn — the deleted file lives in `:shared` and the only edit is to
`:shared`'s `SharedModule.kt`. `:composeApp` compiles unchanged
because no `:composeApp` file imported the symbol.

### Preserved files

- `data/.../repository/LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl.kt` — the
  strangler-fig replacement for the legacy VM's behaviour. Already
  duplicates the two constants (`REFRESH_WORK_NAME` /
  `LIBRARY_REFRESH_WORKER_CLASS`) and exposes `refresh()` +
  `observeIsRefreshing()` directly to the rework `LibraryViewModel`.
  Implementation is unchanged by this slice.
- `domain/.../repository/LibraryRefreshRepository.kt` — interface
  consumed by the impl above. Unchanged.
- `shared/.../core/jobs/BackgroundJobScheduler.kt` — the underlying
  `expect class` the deleted VM and the surviving repo impl both
  schedule against. Unchanged.

### Files retired (1 + 1 Koin edit)

| File | Action | LOC | Prior reach |
|------|--------|-----|-------------|
| `shared/.../features/refresh/ui/viewmodel/RefreshViewModel.kt` | DELETE | 117 | Koin registration only (zero injection sites) |
| `shared/.../di/SharedModule.kt` | EDIT | −8 / +5 net | Drop import + 5-line `viewModel { RefreshViewModel(get()) }` block + stale "ported in Phase 10.3 Wave 2A" comment; replace with retire-pointer comment to the `LibraryRefreshRepository` / `Impl` path. |

The stale historical comment at `SharedModule.kt:330-334`
("RefreshViewModel SKIPPED in Phase 9.5") is preserved as documented
Phase-9 migration history — it does not reference an active symbol
and removing it would obscure why the VM appeared late in the port.

### Per-symbol reachability methodology

Three concentric greps confirmed unreachability:

1. `^import .*\.RefreshViewModel\b` — single hit at
   `SharedModule.kt:80` (the very import this slice removes).
2. `koinViewModel<RefreshViewModel>` / `by viewModel.*Refresh` /
   `: RefreshViewModel` / `private val .*: RefreshViewModel` — ZERO
   hits.
3. Bare-identifier `\bRefreshViewModel\b` outside `.md` files —
   matches only the file under deletion plus its Koin registration.

The rework `LibraryViewModel` injects `RefreshLibraryUseCase` +
`ObserveLibraryRefreshUseCase` directly — both bypass any VM layer
and land on `LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl`. No third-party caller
exists.

### Behaviour preservation

NONE observable. Both the legacy and rework Library routes drive the
same `BackgroundJobScheduler.scheduleOneOff(tag = "LibraryRefresh",
workerClass = "me.manga.kira.work.LibraryRefreshWorker")` — the
legacy route through the deleted VM, the rework route through
`LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl`. After this slice only the rework path
exists, and since no UI host still resolves the legacy VM via Koin
the deletion is observationally a no-op. The Phase-11 deferral on
the Android worker class itself is unaffected — the impl still
emits the same sentinel `"unknown"` on Android until Phase 11 lands
`LibraryRefreshWorker`, mirroring the legacy posture verbatim.

### Strangler-fig integrity

PRESERVED. The strangler-fig boundary (`:data` →
`BackgroundJobScheduler` in `:shared`) is unchanged because
`LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl` already owned it before this slice.
The slice does NOT collapse the boundary or migrate the scheduler —
it only removes a now-orphan secondary VM that used to drive the
same scheduler in parallel.

### Build gates (3 green for the source commit)

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m ✅
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 4s ✅
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 59s ✅

`:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` not run — no `:composeApp` /
`:ui` / `:presentation` source touched and the deleted file lives in
`commonMain`, so Desktop compile cannot fail in isolation from the
three green gates above. (`compileKotlinIosArm64` and
`compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` cover the same `commonMain` symbol
graph that Desktop would.) Cross-target consistency holds because
`:shared/commonMain` is the only source set touched.

### Block-and-ask check (a)-(d) for this slice

- **(a)** Contract library blocker: NO.
- **(b)** Observable behaviour change: NO — the rework path was
  already wired and consumed by `LibraryViewModel` in production code
  before this slice.
- **(c)** Compile fail risk: NO (3 gates green).
- **(d)** SOLID violation: NO — pure dead-code elimination; the
  surviving `LibraryRefreshRepository` surface is a strict superset
  (in capability) of the deleted VM's surface.

No blocks. Phase 9.x.refreshvm.retire is CLOSED.

### Pattern note

This slice establishes `legacyvm.retire` as the third member of the
9.x retire family:

| Sub-pattern | Trigger | Action | First instance |
|-------------|---------|--------|----------------|
| `legacyui.retire` | `@Composable` file with zero `import`/`navigation` reach | Delete file + edit nav graph | #357 (HistoryScreen) |
| `componentprune` | Mixed-reach helper file with subset of unreached symbols | Edit file (delete symbols + dead imports) | #358 (Complaint helpers) |
| `legacyvm.retire` | `:shared` `ViewModel` with zero injection sites; only Koin registration | Delete file + edit Koin module | #359 (RefreshViewModel, this slice) |

Future analogous candidates: any `:shared` `ViewModel` whose only
Kotlin reference is its own `viewModel { ... }` Koin binding.
`HistoryViewModel` is the next obvious candidate but remains
**BLOCKED on #217** — the legacy Reader still injects it.

- **`library_sheet/*`** — BLOCKED on legacy `LibraryMangaScreen.kt`.

## §193 — Phase 9.x.commonui.retire — drop 5 unreachable presentation/common composables

Bulk file-deletion sweep of orphan composables under
`composeApp/.../presentation/common/componants/*`. Five files in the
slice; one further orphan (`toast/ToastHostState.kt`) deferred to a
follow-up to keep this source commit within the 5-file cap. ~319 LOC
retired.

### Strategy

A "common UI sweep" exit-survey gap was open since #358 (Phase
9.x.complaint.componentprune)'s Next-slice analysis. The legacy
helper-composable dir `presentation/common/componants/*` accumulated
files over multi-year upstream development; many were sized for legacy
screens that #346–#357 retired, leaving them orphan. Filename-grep
alone is insufficient (RepoIconResolver.kt was nearly mis-classified
because its exported function `rememberRepoIconPainter` differs from
the file basename); the methodology now extracts the actual top-level
declaration names and greps those.

The slice follows the established `legacyui.retire` pattern (file
deletion + no nav-graph touch because these are helper composables,
not screens). What makes the methodology newly explicit here:

- **Step 1**: `^import .*\.<file-basename>\b` grep across the repo
  to short-list zero-import-site candidates.
- **Step 2**: Extract actual top-level fun/class/object names from
  each candidate file (NOT trusting the basename).
- **Step 3**: `^import .*\.(<actual-names>)\b` re-grep against the
  whole repo.
- **Step 4**: Bare-identifier `\b(<names>)\b` scan to catch
  same-package callers (no `import` needed) and exclude KDoc-text
  references in `:ui` rework files describing legacy posture.

Steps 2–3 are the new gate. Step 2 caught false-orphans (RepoIconResolver,
FloatingActionButton's `AnimatedCircleExtendedFab`,
AutoSizedText's `AutoSubtitleText`+`NavigationBarAutoText`) whose
exported names diverge from filenames.

and are NOT touched:

### Pattern note

This slice refines the `legacyui.retire` methodology by adding the
**Step 2 / Step 3 extraction gate**: when filename-grep yields a
zero-import-site short-list, *the actual top-level declaration names
must be re-greppped before retiring* because a Kotlin file's public
surface may diverge from its basename. RepoIconResolver.kt was the

### Pattern note — componentprune matures (4 instances)

After §158 (ComplaintComponents), §195 (FAB), and this slice (Scroller),
the `componentprune` rubric is now hardened:

1. **Identify a file with mixed reach** — the file basename alone
   suggests fully-reached (because at least one declaration is
   reached), but per-declaration grep proves otherwise. This is the
   §193 filename-vs-declaration gate in action.
2. **3-pass grep over each declared symbol** — anchored import +
   injection-site (where applicable; not applicable for top-level
   `@Composable` funs) + bare-identifier. Categorize each symbol as
   REACHED / ORPHAN / TRANSITIVELY-ORPHAN (private helpers whose only
   caller is an orphan).
3. **Surgical Write** — rewrite the file with only the surviving
   declarations + their imports. Preserve everything byte-identical
   (whitespace, KDoc, parameter defaults) except for KDoc references
   to the removed symbols.

Differs from `legacyui.retire` (file-level deletion of fully-unreached
`@Composable` screens — single-file resolution) and `legacyvm.retire`
(file-level deletion of `:shared` ViewModel + Koin binding edit).

(`composeApp/.../navigation/routes/AdminComplaintScreenRoute.kt`) is rewritten in-place to render

binding stays stable; the parallel `Screen.ComplaintAdminRework` debug route +

(retirement is the follow-on `Phase 9.x.admincomplaint.retire` slice).

Task #272) with full parity vs the legacy admin screen across the foundation (§171), 3-mutation
actions slice (§172 — status-change / closure-reason / delete), edit slice (§173), sort
dropdown (§174), long-press body-copy (§175), statistics aggregation card, app-version filter,
bulk mutations (#265), chip-row semver sort (#266), and admindate timestamp. The rework
`AdminComplaintViewModel` exposes 15 sealed `AdminComplaintIntent` variants covering all 6
legacy mutations + 3 filter axes + 7 sort modes. Swap was unblocked at that point.

### Pre-flight live-navigator audit

A 3-pass grep over `Screen.ComplaintAdmin` (excluding the trailing `Rework` suffix to avoid
false-positives) found ZERO live `navController.navigate(...)` or `navController.safeNavigate(...)`
callers:

| `SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt:100` (rework Settings hub) | `if (Admin.isAdmin) Screen.ComplaintAdminRework else Screen.ComplaintRework` | Routes to REWORK enum case already. |
| `ComplaintScreenRoute.kt:24` (legacy user Complaint adapter KDoc) | KDoc reference only — no `navigate(Screen.ComplaintAdmin)` call | Documentation only. |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` / `SOLID_AUDIT.md` / `PLAN_*.md` references | Documentation only | Not live navigators. |

The `composable<Screen.ComplaintAdmin>` block in `App.kt:562` is the last live anchor holding
the legacy admin VM + screen reachable; the swap re-points the renderer for any future
caller (or external deep-link) at the same enum case.

| 6 callback wirings (`onRetry`, `onUpdateComplaintStatus`, `onDeleteComplaint`, `onUpdateComplaint`, `onAddClosureReason`, `onShowMessage`) | Rework `:ui` dispatches `AdminComplaintIntent.OnRetry` / `OnSubmitStatusChange` / `OnConfirmDelete` / `OnSubmitEdit` / `OnSubmitClosureReason` directly via `viewModel.submit(...)`. The MVI surface owns the action wiring; the adapter doesn't translate. |
| `ToastShower koinInject()` + `onShowMessage = { toastShower.showShort(it) }` | Rework emits `AdminComplaintEffect.ShowSuccessMessage` / `ShowErrorMessage` via the MVI effect channel; `:ui` collects effects and surfaces them in a `SnackbarHostState` (rework `AdminComplaintScreen.kt:33`). No platform-coupled `ToastShower` dependency at the adapter level. |

### Behaviour preservation

| Surface | Legacy adapter | Rework (post-swap) | Equivalent? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Upstream data source | Firestore `complaints` collection via legacy `GetAllComplaintUseCase` | Same Firestore collection via strangler-fig `AdminComplaintListRepositoryImpl` → legacy `GetAllComplaintUseCase` | ✅ Same wire format; submissions from any sibling write path (legacy `ComplaintViewModel.sendComplaint`, Request-Language `LanguageViewModel`) surface identically. |
| Admin-only access gate | At calling site (both Settings hubs check `Admin.isAdmin`) | Same — adapter does NOT re-check; relies on caller gate | ✅ Same posture; gate-delegated-to-caller. |
| Initial load | `LaunchedEffect(Unit)` triggers `loadAllComplaints()` | `init {}` auto-load via `loadList()` | ✅ Both load on first composition / VM construction. |
| Retry on error | `onRetry` callback → `loadAllComplaints()` | `AdminComplaintIntent.OnRetry` → `loadList()` | ✅ Same. |
| Status-change mutation | `onUpdateComplaintStatus` → `viewModel.updateComplaintStatus` | `AdminComplaintIntent.OnSubmitStatusChange` → `changeStatus` use case | ✅ Same `ChangeComplaintStatusUseCase` strangler-fig over legacy `UpdateComplaintUseCase`. |
| Closure-reason mutation | `onAddClosureReason` → `viewModel.addClosureReason` | `AdminComplaintIntent.OnSubmitClosureReason` → `addClosureReason` use case | ✅ Same legacy mutation under the hood. |
| Delete mutation | `onDeleteComplaint` → `viewModel.deleteComplaint` | `AdminComplaintIntent.OnConfirmDelete` → `adminDeleteComplaint` use case | ✅ Same legacy `DeleteComplaintUseCase`. |
| Edit mutation | `onUpdateComplaint` → `viewModel.updateComplaint` | `AdminComplaintIntent.OnSubmitEdit` → `adminEditComplaint` use case | ✅ Same legacy `UpdateComplaintUseCase`. |
| Toast feedback | `ToastShower.showShort(message)` | `AdminComplaintEffect.ShowSuccessMessage` / `ShowErrorMessage` → `SnackbarHostState` | Surface change — Material 3 snackbar instead of platform toast. Same intent (user-visible confirmation), different visual. Matches the established rework pattern across all 13 prior route-swaps. |
| Back nav | `navController.safePopBackStack()` | `navController.safePopBackStack()` via `onBack` callback | ✅ Identical. |

### Strangler-fig integrity

No new `:data` → `:shared` reach introduced. The strangler-fig chain
(`AdminComplaintListRepositoryImpl` → legacy `GetAllComplaintUseCase`) was already in place
from §171 (`Phase 7.x.complaint.admin`); this slice only re-routes the renderer to use it.
The legacy `:shared/admin/complaint/AdminComplaintViewModel` becomes orphan but is NOT
deleted here — that's the follow-on `Phase 9.x.admincomplaint.legacyvm.retire`.

| `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 31s ✅ |
| `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` | BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 2s ✅ |

`:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` not run — same posture as §285-§295/§301/§305/§346: the
change is to a `:composeApp/commonMain` adapter file; if `commonMain` compiles and links
into the iOS framework, Desktop (which is also a commonMain consumer) inherits the same
link graph. iOS framework link / Xcode build deferred to user's macOS.

### Banned-feature audit

The rewritten adapter uses only `@Composable fun`, `koinViewModel<AdminComplaintViewModel>()`,
and `navController.safePopBackStack()`. No `!!`, no `Any`, no `lateinit`. Same posture as
`AdminComplaintReworkScreenRoute` (which the rewrite mirrors structurally).

### Block-and-ask check

| Trigger | Status |
|---|---|
| (a) Contract library blocker | NOT triggered — only `:composeApp` adapter rewritten. |
| (b) Observable-behaviour change | NOT triggered — full feature parity (15 rework intents cover legacy's 6 mutations + extras); the platform-toast → snackbar visual delta is the same pattern as all 13 prior route-swaps and matches the established rework convention. |
| (c) Feature stops compiling | NOT triggered (3 gates green). |
| (d) Unresolvable SOLID violation | NOT triggered — adapter SRP preserved (one rule: bridge `Screen.ComplaintAdmin` to rework screen), DIP intact (depends on rework `:presentation` interface, not `:data` impl). |

### Pattern note — *.swap rubric matures (14 instances)

After §138/§140/§285-§295/§301/§305/§346 and this slice, the `*.swap` rubric is now
canonical:

1. **Identify a rework route with full feature parity to its legacy counterpart** — usually
   marked by a closed `§ladder` of foundation + parity slices (here, §171's 9-rung ladder).
2. **Audit live navigators of the legacy enum case** — if all callers already route to the
   rework enum case (as is true here for both Settings hubs), the swap is even simpler
   because no navigate-site updates are needed.
3. **Rewrite the legacy adapter file in-place** to mirror the rework adapter's shape — drop
   the legacy VM/screen imports, drop callback wirings (rework MVI dispatches internally),
   drop manual `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { load() }` triggers (rework VM auto-loads in
   `init {}`), drop platform-coupled effect deps like `ToastShower koinInject` (rework
   uses `AdminComplaintEffect` channel).
4. **Keep the `Screen.*` enum binding stable** — preserves URL contract; the parallel
   `Screen.*Rework` debug route lives until the follow-on `*.retire` slice.

Differs from `legacyui.retire` (file-level deletion of fully-unreached `@Composable`
screens) and `legacyvm.retire` (file-level deletion of `:shared` ViewModel + Koin
binding edit) — `*.swap` is the unblocker that turns reached legacy files into orphans
so those retirement slices become possible.

  this slice. The legacy `:shared/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintViewModel` + legacy
  `:composeApp/.../admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen` + `SortOption.kt` +
  `StatusChangeDialog.kt` are now fully orphan; the SettingsViewModel +
  `Screen.ComplaintAdmin` binding hold no reference. Two follow-on slices: a legacyui.retire
  to delete the orphan composables + their helpers (4 files, well under cap), and a
  legacyvm.retire to delete the `:shared` admin VM + its Koin binding (2 files).
- **Wider `presentation/features/<feature>/ui/components/*` componentprune survey** —
  established as a productive ongoing investment.
- **`HistoryViewModel` / `ReaderViewModel` / `SharedChaptersViewModel` legacyvm.retire** —
  STILL BLOCKED on #217 (legacy Reader retirement + chapter-identity decision).
- **`SettingsViewModel` / `WhatsNewViewModel` legacyvm.retire** — STILL BLOCKED on active
  reach in `App.kt` / `LibraryScreenRoute.kt`.

Other unchanged (BLOCKED items, `needs_manual_review` files).

Phase 9.x.admincomplaint.swap is CLOSED.

### Strategy

exists purely as audit-bookkeeping for the original "preserve verbatim until
user decision" policy. Two are tracked in `migration/renames.md` items #5

debt — every additional retire slice has to read past these placeholder
notes — so the resolution is "delete the files and close the audit notes
in the same close-out commit."

"Marked `needs_manual_review` for user decision on rename or

keep, and the canonical retire posture (§349, §350, §354, §355, §366) has
established that orphan source with no contract → delete. The audit
annotation is satisfied by the retire-with-evidence trail (3-pass grep
table above + commit SHAs + closed audit notes).

### Strategy

`shared/.../presentation/features/reader/data/CompressionState.kt` was a

false, val error: String? = null, val isCompleted: Boolean = false)`.
The `:shared` ARCHITECTURE deferral note at §6223 explicitly described
the stub's purpose: a Coil-dependent compression feature that was
deferred until "a cross-platform bitmap pipeline" landed, with the type
parked in `:shared` as a placeholder.

The Reader rework arc (Tasks #212–#237, ending with the ktor3
per-byte progress port at HEAD `61d92ce`) completed without that
bitmap-pipeline feature ever materializing. None of the rework Reader
layers (`:domain/reader/*`, `:data/.../reader/*`,
`:presentation/.../reader/*`, `:ui/.../reader/*`) reference
compression, an in-progress state envelope, or anything sibling to this
data class. The stub never acquired a downstream consumer.

directory remains LIVE: `ReaderItem.kt`, `ReadingMode.kt`, and
`isPaged.kt` all chain off legacy Reader VMs and the strangler-fig
`:data/.../reader/*` impls. Only `CompressionState.kt` is orphan in
the package.

A 3-pass grep across the migrated codebase (Kotlin-only) found zero
non-self consumers. The orphan-retire precedent established in §200 /
§202 / §203 / §204 / §205 / §206 covers the autonomous-decision branch.

The §6223 deferral note was refreshed in the same close-out commit to

mixed source + doc retire slices.

## §208 — Phase 9.x.downloadexception.retire — orphan `DownloadException.kt` custom-exception cleanup

### Strategy

`shared/.../presentation/features/download/data/DownloadException.kt`
was a 9-line custom exception:

```kotlin
class DownloadException(
    message: String,
    cause: Throwable,
    val downloaded: Int,
    val total: Int,
) : Exception(message, cause)
```

It was designed to capture partial-download progress (`downloaded` /
`total`) at throw-time for a legacy worker pipeline. The two live
androidMain consumers of the sibling `DownloadState` sealed class
(`DownloadWorkerV2.kt`, `ChapterDownloadService.kt`) were both
inspected — neither throws, catches, or instantiates
`DownloadException` anywhere. The class was a forward-looking
placeholder that never wired backward into any active worker path.

The rework downloads slice (Tasks #276–#281) uses `:domain/.../downloads/
DownloadState.kt` (rework-side ADT, distinct from the legacy
`:shared/.../download/data/DownloadState.kt`) and surfaces error state
through its `Error` variant carrying a `Throwable`, not a custom
exception subclass. No rework reach to this symbol.

A 3-pass grep across the migrated codebase (Kotlin-only) found zero
non-self consumers. Same orphan-retire posture as §200 / §202 / §203 /
§204 / §205 / §206 / §207.

The sibling files in `:shared/.../presentation/features/download/data/`
remain LIVE: `DownloadState.kt` is reached by two androidMain workers
(`DownloadWorkerV2.kt`, `ChapterDownloadService.kt`); `DownloadingState
.kt` is heavily live with 14 reachers across `:data` mappers, Room
converter/entity/DAO, and the rework `:domain/.../downloads/DownloadState
.kt` mapping path. Those are not eligible for retire — only the
forward-looking exception subclass is orphan.

## §209 — Phase 9.x.databasehelper.retire — orphan `DataBaseHelper.kt` dead-util cleanup

### Strategy

`shared/.../data/local/util/DataBaseHelper.kt` was an 8-line file
under the legacy `:shared` Room-helper namespace containing exactly
three members — all file-private:

```kotlin
package me.manga.kira.data.local.util

private const val SQLITE_MAX_VARS = 999
private const val SQLITE_SAFE_CHUNK = 900 // safe margin

// Generic chunker helper (optional)
private fun <T> List<T>.chunkedSafe(chunkSize: Int = SQLITE_SAFE_CHUNK): List<List<T>> =
    this.chunked(chunkSize)
```

The file looked like a forward-looking helper that was never wired up.
Because every declaration was `private`, no consumer outside the file
could ever reference any of them by language rules — and the bare-
identifier passes for each symbol (`DataBaseHelper`, `chunkedSafe`,
`SQLITE_MAX_VARS`, `SQLITE_SAFE_CHUNK`) all came back self-only. Inside
the file itself, `chunkedSafe` is the sole call site for
`SQLITE_SAFE_CHUNK` (default-arg), and nothing calls `chunkedSafe`.

The Room DAOs that DO chunk arguments (e.g., for IN-clause batching
against SQLite's 999-variable cap) inline their own `chunked(900)` calls
rather than reaching for this util — confirmed by inspection during the
prior surveys. The file is dead weight; same orphan-retire posture as
§200 / §202 / §203 / §204 / §205 / §206 / §207 / §208.

### 3-pass grep audit (pre-deletion)

| Pass | Pattern | Hits | Notes |
|------|---------|------|-------|
| 1 — anchored import | `import me\.manga\.yamiapk\.data\.local\.util\.DataBaseHelper` | 0 | no consumer imports the (empty public) file |
| 2 — bare type | `\bDataBaseHelper\b` (`type=kotlin`) | self-only | file has no public symbols, so this confirms zero cross-file Kotlin reach |
| 3a — extension fun | `\bchunkedSafe\b` (`type=kotlin`) | self-only | unused even inside the file |
| 3b — constants | `\bSQLITE_MAX_VARS\b\|\bSQLITE_SAFE_CHUNK\b` (`type=kotlin`) | self-only | constants are only referenced inside `chunkedSafe`'s own signature |

The file has no public surface area — the four pass results are
mutually consistent: zero reach, zero exposure, fully dead.

   method whose sole caller is the method above. Once #1 is gone, this
   becomes orphan.
3. `SavedMangaDao` (entire interface, 170 lines, 30+ methods) — a fully
   unwired orphan inherited from the source app. Documented in
   `AUDIT_GOAL.md:52, :94, :188` as planned-delete dead code (never
   exposed by `MangaDatabase`, no Koin bindings, no external reachers).
   The interface duplicates `MangaDao` methods plus contains its own
   declaration of the same dead `getSavedMangaWithMetricsFlow`.
4. `SavedMangaWithMetrics` — the data class returned by #1 and declared
   by #2 and #3. Once all three are gone, this transitively orphans.

All four are retired in commit 1/3. A single surviving KDoc reference
to `SavedMangaWithMetrics` in `MangaChapterMetrics.kt:8` (descriptive
historical prose about the Bug 3 superseded path) is refreshed in
commit 2/3 to describe the historical row shape generically without

## §213 — Phase 9.x.handeldataclasses.componentprune — drop 13 orphan members from `HandelDataClasses.kt` + 3 transitively-unused imports

### Strategy

Direct execution of the next-slice carry-over flagged at the end of §212
(*"Audit `:shared/.../core/util/data_classes/HandelDataClasses.kt` for
per-class orphan members"*).

`HandelDataClasses` is a singleton `object` of 29 extension functions
and 1 property — all pure mapping helpers between domain models,
entities, and reader-projection types. It is reached from 12 distinct
modules via 15 anchored FQN imports (e.g. `HandelDataClasses.toMangaInfo`,
`HandelDataClasses.toChapterDownloadEntity`). Each member is independently
classifiable as LIVE or orphan — making this an §358/§362/§364-style
**componentprune** (member-level drop from a live file), NOT a file
retire.

A level-2 reacher-chain audit using the 3-pass grep method established
in §364 (`scroller.componentprune`) found **13 dead members + 3
transitively-unused imports**. Same-name disambiguation was the key
technique: three `toMangaItem` extensions, three `toSavedEntity`
extensions, three `toMangaInfo` extensions, and two `toChapterItem`
extensions all share method names across different receivers, so each
external call site had to be resolved by reading the receiver type at
the import-site.

## §214 — Phase 9.x.libraryrepository.componentprune — drop 4 orphan facade methods + 3 transitively-dead DAO methods (2-level coupled prune in the §381 posture)

### Strategy

Direct execution of the next-slice carry-over flagged at the end of §213
(*"Audit remaining legacy `LibraryRepository` methods that may be dead"*
+ *"Audit `LibraryDeo` and other `*Deo` DAOs"*) — combined into a single
2-level coupled slice because the candidate methods on the DAOs are reached
ONLY through the candidate methods on the facade.

`LibraryRepository` is a legacy `:shared/.../presentation/features/library/
domain/LibraryRepository.kt` aggregator class — constructor-injected into
**8 distinct sites** across the codebase
(`CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl`, `ChapterDownloadService`,
`LibraryRefreshWorker`, `ChapterNotificationHelper`,
`SharedChaptersViewModel`, `ChaptersViewModel`, `ReaderViewModel`,
`LibraryDetailsViewModel`), all using the field name `libraryRepository`.

This makes the level-2 reacher-chain audit deterministic: every external
call MUST appear as `libraryRepository.X(` (anchored receiver
disambiguation) or as a same-name overload `.X(` requiring receiver-type
lookup. Same `Grep` triple-pass methodology as §358/§362/§364/§213.

This is a **2-level coupled prune** mirroring §381's posture (the
`SavedMangaWithMetrics` 4-symbol coupled retire): when a facade method
is confirmed orphan, the DAO method(s) it called transitively become
orphans too. For symbols where the ONLY external reacher was the dead
facade method, both are dropped together in a single source commit.

### Reacher-chain audit

## §215 — Phase 9.x.mangarepository.componentprune — drop 2 orphan `MangaRepository` facade methods + 7 transitively-dead DAO members (2-level coupled prune)

### Strategy

Direct execution of the next-slice carry-over flagged at the end of §214
(*"Audit `LibraryDeo` (DAO) for per-method orphans"*) — combined with a
fresh audit of the legacy `MangaRepository` facade that the same `LibraryDeo`
is injected into. The result is a single 2-level coupled slice: two facade
methods on `MangaRepository` are confirmed orphan, and the DAO methods they
transitively reached (or that lived independently with zero reachers) are
dropped in the same source commit.

`MangaRepository` is a legacy `:shared/.../domain/repos/MangaRepository.kt`
aggregator class — constructor-injected into **one** site
(`HistoryViewModel.kt:47`, field name `mangaRepository`). That single
injection makes the level-2 reacher-chain audit trivially deterministic:
every external call MUST appear as `mangaRepository.X(`.

The `LibraryDeo` DAO is injected into MangaRepository under the field name
`libraryDao` (note: NOT the standard `libraryDeo` — this is a deliberate
local rename of the same interface type). So the level-2 audit ran the
identifier pass on BOTH `libraryDeo.` AND `libraryDao.` receivers to avoid
missing reachers in MangaRepository's body.

### Reacher-chain audit

3-pass `Grep` across all `*.kt` files. Receiver-name disambiguation
preserved as in §214.

| `MangaRepository.removeMangaById(mangaId)` | 0 hits | 0 bare `.removeMangaById(` hits anywhere | n/a | orphan ✅ |

After confirming the 2 facade methods are orphan, the underlying DAO
methods become transitively-dead candidates. Plus a separate
fresh-audit of LibraryDeo identified 4 standalone orphan DAO members
with no transitive dependency on the facade:

Note: `MangaRepository.removeMangaById` did NOT call `MangaDao.removeMangaById` — it called `libraryDao.removeMangaWithChapters(mangaId)`. So the two same-named methods were independently orphan. | orphan ✅ |
| `LibraryDeo.getSavedMangaTitlesFlow()` | Bare `getSavedMangaTitlesFlow` grep returned only the @Query definition. The LIVE flow on this DAO is `getSavedMangaApiTitleFlow` (reached via `MangaRepository.savedMangaTitles` → HomeViewModel:121). | orphan ✅ |

Bare `.removeManga(` hits: MangaRepository.kt:43 (self-definition), HomeViewModel.kt:148 (calls MangaRepository, NOT LibraryDeo). ZERO `SavedMangaEntity`-arg call sites. | orphan ✅ |

Critical same-name disambiguation:
- `MangaRepository.removeMangaById` vs `MangaDao.removeMangaById` — same

## §216 — Phase 9.x.notificationdao.componentprune — drop 10 orphan `NotificationDao` members + 4 transitively-dead helpers (2-level coupled prune in the §214 + §215 posture)

**Task**: #385. **Commit**: `34843e2` (source) + this doc close-out.

### Strategy

Same component-prune posture as §382/§383/§384: member-level drop from a live `@Dao`
interface (`NotificationDao` stays referenced by `MangaDatabase.notificationDao()`
abstract — every external reacher we keep still resolves through the surviving
member surface). The 2-level extension is identical to §214/§215: when an orphan
`@Transaction` body is dropped, the only-reached-from-its-body helper methods
become transitively dead and are dropped in the same commit.

### Reacher-chain audit (3-pass)

- **Pass 1** — anchored receiver `notificationDao.X(` across the source tree.
  Surfaced 5 distinct reachers: `insertNotificationsList` (1 site,
  `ChapterNotificationHelper`), `addLocalImagePathByChapterId` (6 sites,
  `ChapterDownloadService`), `updateMangaImageUrl` (1 site, `LibraryRepository`),
  `getNotificationsByApi` (2 sites, `UpdateSourcesRepository`), `update`
  (2 sites, `UpdateSourcesRepository`).
- **Pass 2** — `NotificationRepository` injects the same DAO under the field
  name `dao` (legacy 1-char alias). 5 distinct reachers: `dao.getAllNotifications`,
  `dao.markAllAsRead`, `dao.deleteAllNotifications`, `dao.deleteNotification`,
  `dao.insertNotification`.
- **Pass 3** — bare-identifier interface body callees. The only LIVE
  `@Transaction` (`addLocalImagePathByChapterId`) calls
  `getNotificationByChapterId` + `updateNotification` from its body; these stay
  LIVE-by-association even though they have zero `notificationDao.X(` reachers.

### Same-name disambiguation

- `markAsRead(` — exists on `NotificationDao` (DAO `@Query("UPDATE notifications
  SET isRead = 1 WHERE id = :notificationId")`), on rework `UpdatesRepository`
  (`suspend fun markAsRead(entry: UpdateEntry)`), on legacy `NotificationRepository`
  (`suspend fun markAsRead(id: Long) = libraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead(id)`),
  and on the rework use case (`MarkUpdateAsReadUseCase`). Critically the legacy
  facade's `markAsRead` delegates to `LibraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead`,
  NOT to `NotificationDao.markAsRead` — so the DAO method has zero callers and
  is orphan even though every layer above it has a `markAsRead` member.
- `markChapterAndNotificationRead(` — duplicate `@Transaction` on `NotificationDao`
  AND `LibraryDeo`. Both 2 external callers (`NotificationRepository.markAsRead`
  + `LibraryRepository.markChapterAsRead`) use the `libraryDeo.` receiver. The
  `NotificationDao` copy is orphan.
- `update(` — exists on `NotificationDao` (`@Update`) and on
  `NotificationRepository`/`MangaDao`. The `notificationDao.update(...)` call
  in `UpdateSourcesRepository` (2 sites) keeps the DAO's `update` LIVE.
- `insertNotifications(` (Unit return) vs `insertNotificationsList(...)` (List<Long>
  return) — same call shape, different overload. Only the latter has a reacher.

### Per-file disposition

`shared/src/commonMain/.../data/local/dao/NotificationDao.kt` (3 imports, 26
members → 3 imports + 12 members; net -54 lines):

Direct orphans dropped (10):
- `getUnreadNotifications(): Flow<List<ChapterNotification>>` — no reacher.
- `markAsRead(notificationId: Long)` — see same-name disambiguation; the rework
  + legacy `markAsRead` chain bypasses this DAO method.
- `countAll(): Int` — no reacher.
- `getLatest(limit: Int): List<ChapterNotification>` — no reacher.
- `markAsDownloaded(notificationId: Long)` — no reacher.
- `updateLocalImagePaths(notificationId, paths)` — no reacher.

## §218 — Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.retire — drop orphan `UpdateSourcesRepository` class + Koin registration

**Task**: #387. **Source commit**: `e68dc90`. **Doc commit**: this section.

### Strategy

`UpdateSourcesRepository` is the legacy URL-rewrite migration tool — fetches a
remote source-list JSON, compares per-source `baseVersion` / `imageUrlVersion`
to the local `sources` table, and on version bumps walks every persisted
`saved_manga`, `saved_chapters`, `history_items`, `notifications` row to
rewrite the base URL portion of each `url` / `mangaUrl` / `chapterUrl` /
`imageUrl` / `mangaImageUrl` field. It also has a `deleteSourceByName` branch
when the remote flags a source for deletion and a `getSiteStateByNameSync` /
`updateSiteStateByName` branch when the remote site state changes (WORKING /
NOT_WORKING).

The class was registered in `SharedModule.kt:231` as `single {
UpdateSourcesRepository(...) }` — but **zero call sites** ever resolved it.
Because Koin `single { }` is lazy (the factory lambda only runs when
`get<T>()` / `inject<T>()` / a constructor-injection chain demands `T`), the
class's constructor never executed. The URL-migration code has been
unreachable since the rework migration began.

Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.retire deletes the class and drops the Koin
registration. Coupled-dead DAO methods (`SourcesDao.deleteSourceByName`,
`SourcesDao.updateBaseUrlAndVersionByName`,
`SourcesDao.updateImageBaseUrlAndVersionByName`,
`SourcesDao.updateSiteStateByName`, `MangaDao.getMangaByApi`,
`MangaDao.getMangaIdsByApi`, `MangaDao.update`,
`ChapterDao.getChaptersByMangaIdR`, `ChapterDao.update`,
`HistoryDao.getHistoryByApi`, `HistoryDao.update`,
`NotificationDao.getNotificationsByApi`, `NotificationDao.update`) become
DAO-level orphans. A follow-up `Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.daoprune`
slice will batch the coupled DAO drops across two source commits (5-file cap
honoured).

### Reacher-chain audit (3-pass)

**Pass 1** — anchored receiver `updateSourcesRepository.X(` across the source
tree → **0 matches**.

**Pass 2** — bare type token `UpdateSourcesRepository` across `.kt` files →
2 hits, both load-bearing-zero:
- `shared/.../di/SharedModule.kt:21` (import) + `:231` (Koin `single { }`
  registration) — both dropped in this slice.
- `shared/.../admin/Admin.kt:12` (KDoc reference) — refreshed to drop the
  stale reference.

**Pass 3** — Koin resolution patterns: `get<UpdateSourcesRepository>` /
`inject<UpdateSourcesRepository>` / `by inject().*UpdateSourcesRepository` /
`getKoin().get<UpdateSourcesRepository>` / constructor parameter type
`UpdateSourcesRepository` → **0 matches** for every pattern.

**Conclusion**: the class is orphan in its entirety. Koin `single { }`'s
laziness means the constructor never ran in any execution path; retiring the
class does not change observable behaviour.

### Behaviour preservation

The URL-rewrite migration tool never executed in any runtime — Koin `single`
is lazy-instantiated and no consumer ever requested the binding. Compared to
the prior architecture state (post-rework migration), the runtime behaviour
is identical: no URL migration runs before this slice, no URL migration runs
after this slice.

If the URL-migration feature becomes desirable in the future, it can be
re-introduced as a `:domain`/`:data` slice that follows the clean-architecture
posture (use case + repository + Koin wiring + an explicit `get()` chain that
actually runs at app startup or via an `initializeSources()`-equivalent
hook). The legacy class was carrying that burden as a never-executed
artifact; the rework path is to lift it cleanly when needed, not to
preserve dead code "just in case."

### Layer-by-layer surfaces

- `:shared` — DELETE `UpdateSourcesRepository.kt`; drop import + `single { }`
  line in `SharedModule.kt`; refresh `Admin.kt` KDoc to remove the stale
  reference to the URS dev-vs-prod source-list URL.
- `:core` / `:domain` / `:data` / `:presentation` / `:ui` / `:platform` /
  `:composeApp` — untouched. The retired class lived entirely inside `:shared/
  presentation/features/repo_settings/domain/`.

### Files affected

| Path | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `shared/src/commonMain/.../presentation/features/repo_settings/domain/UpdateSourcesRepository.kt` | DELETE (476 lines) |
| `shared/src/commonMain/.../di/SharedModule.kt` | drop `UpdateSourcesRepository` import + Koin `single { }` line (-2 lines) |
| `shared/src/commonMain/.../admin/Admin.kt` | refresh KDoc to remove stale `UpdateSourcesRepository`'s dev-vs-prod URL reference; document the surviving `:composeApp` Settings hub adapter reachers (`SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt:100`, `SettingsRoute.kt:121`) (+10/-3 lines) |

### Deferrals

Coupled-dead DAO members become DAO-level orphans after this slice but are
NOT dropped here (5-file cap + clean per-DAO commit narrative). The
follow-up `Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.daoprune` slice will batch the
coupled drops across two source commits + one docs commit:
- Slice commit A: SourcesDao (4 methods) + MangaDao (3 methods including
  same-name `update` overload disambiguation) + ChapterDao (2 methods
  including same-name `update`) = 3 files.
- Slice commit B: HistoryDao (2 methods — `getHistoryByApi` +
  `update`) + NotificationDao (2 methods — `getNotificationsByApi` +
  `update`) = 2 files.
- Docs commit: ARCHITECTURE §219 + SOLID_AUDIT close-out.

### Next-slice carry-over

After this slice's docs commit lands:
- **Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.daoprune** — drop ~13 coupled-dead
  DAO methods across 5 DAO files (see split above).
- Audit `SourcesDao` for further per-method orphans (carry-over from
  §215/§216/§217 — the URS class was the heaviest reacher of SourcesDao;
  with it gone, the SourcesDao surface narrows substantially. The `:shared`
  legacy facade `SourcesRepository` is the only remaining SourcesDao reacher

- Audit `:shared/.../features/library/domain/LibraryRepository.kt` for

Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.retire is CLOSED.
