## §222 — Phase 9.x.dao.componentprune.cumulative — re-sweep MangaDao + ChapterDao for independently-orphan members (Task #392)

### Strategy

§220 swept `SourcesDao` and §221 swept `SourcesRepository` + their
strictly-coupled DAO surface. Both were anchored on URS-coupling
auditing for §218 (Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.daoprune, Task
#388). The §218 audit declared a "LIVE members preserved" header on
both `MangaDao` and `ChapterDao` listing the URS-uncoupled members as
preserved — but the audit's anchor was URS-coupling, NOT exhaustive
source-tree reachability. Subsequent sweeps (§220/§221) carried
"post-§220 MangaDao.kt / ChapterDao.kt re-sweep" forward as a
documented next-slice item.

This slice executes that carry-over: an exhaustive 3-pass reacher-chain
audit (`mangaDao.X(` / `chapterDao.X(` receiver-anchored + word-
boundary `\bX\b` + `::X` method-ref) covering the entire source tree
across all platforms (commonMain + androidMain + iosMain + desktopMain
+ app/). Surfaced 10 independently-orphan members the prior URS-
anchored audit incorrectly listed as preserved LIVE.

### Audit posture

Pass 1 — receiver-anchored `mangaDao\.\w+\(` / `chapterDao\.\w+\(`:
yielded the full set of reached method names by their LIVE-callsite-
declared receiver names. Cross-referenced against each DAO's method
list to surface candidates with 0 such reachers.

Pass 2 — word-boundary `\bMETHOD\b` over `*.kt` for each candidate:
caught alternative receiver names (`dao.X`, `db.mangaDao.X`,
destructured field accesses). All 10 candidates yielded only
definition-site lines + the now-stale Task #388 "preserved" comment
lines. Zero source-tree call-site matches.

Pass 3 — method-reference `::METHOD\b` for each candidate: caught
any `::saveManga` / `chapterDao::insertChapter` style passing. No
matches for any of the 10 candidates.

3-way concordance: 10 candidates, 0 reachers under any anchor pattern.

### Drops (10 total)

**MangaDao (4)**:

1. `saveManga(manga: SavedMangaEntity)` — bare `@Insert`. The
   `MangaRepository.save(...)` path (`MangaRepository.kt:48-50`)
   reaches `libraryDao.saveMangaWithChapters` — a `LibraryDeo`
   `@Transaction` method, NOT MangaDao's `saveManga`. The
   `LibraryDeo.saveMangaWithChapters` body uses LibraryDeo's own
   `insertManga` / `insertChapters` / `getMangaIdByUrl` /
   `getSavedChapterUrls` — none of which delegate to MangaDao.
   MangaDao's `saveManga` was a stranded variant from an older
   posture.

2. `getApiByLocalId(mangaLocalId: Long): String?` — @Query. The LIVE
   api-by-id lookup is `getApiByMangaId(mangaId: Long)` (same column,
   different parameter name) reached at `DownloadWorkerV2.kt:170`
   and `LibraryRepository.kt:59`. `getApiByLocalId` was a
   never-wired sibling.

3. `saveChapters(chapters: List<SavedChapterEntity>)` — bare `@Insert`.
   Chapter-batch inserts reach via LibraryDeo's own `insertChapters`
   (inside the `saveMangaWithChapters` `@Transaction` body) or
   ChapterDao's `insertChapters` + `insertAll` (both LIVE — see
   ChapterDao section below). MangaDao's `saveChapters` was an
   ill-placed cross-table method on a different DAO; never wired.

4. `isMangaSavedFlow(mangaId: Long): Flow<Boolean>` — @Query Flow
   variant. The LIVE suspend variant `isMangaSaved(mangaId)` IS
   reached (`LibraryRepository.kt:57`). The Flow variant — intended
   for a never-shipped reactive "is this saved" indicator — has zero
   reachers.

**ChapterDao (6)**:

5. `toggleChapterRead(chapterId: Long)` — @Query. The LIVE caller
   `LibraryRepository.toggleChapterRead` (`LibraryRepository.kt:118-119`)
   delegates to `libraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead` — a
   `LibraryDeo` `@Transaction` that toggles BOTH `saved_chapters.isRead`
   AND `notifications.isRead` in one transaction. The ChapterDao
   chapter-only toggle was bypassed because the LIVE path always
   needs to sync the notification row too; ChapterDao's variant is
   a stranded chapter-only path.

6. `deleteChaptersByIds(ids: List<Long>)` — @Query batch delete. No
   reacher. The per-id LIVE path is `deleteChapterById(chapterId)`
   (`LibraryRepository.kt:93`). Bulk deletes reach
   LibraryDeo's `removeAllChaptersForManga` (own @Query, called from
   the `removeMangaWithChapters` @Transaction body).

7. `removeAllChaptersForManga(mangaId: Long)` — @Query. The LIBRARY-
   WIPE path reaches LibraryDeo's OWN `removeAllChaptersForManga`
   (LibraryDeo.kt:70-71) called from LibraryDeo's
   `removeMangaWithChapters` `@Transaction` body. Room resolves
   method names within the @Dao interface scope — LibraryDeo's
   callsite stays inside LibraryDeo and never reaches ChapterDao's
   sibling-named variant. ChapterDao's variant was an unreachable
   duplicate.

8. `getBookmarkedChapters(): Flow<List<SavedChapterEntity>>` — @Query
   Flow. The rework Bookmarks slice is DEFERRED (Task #217 BLOCKED on
   chapter-identity decision; tracked in `Yami.task` as such). This
   DAO surface was an early-stage placeholder for that slice but was
   never wired through Repository → UseCase → ViewModel → UI; ZERO
   reachers.

9. `insertChapter(chapter: SavedChapterEntity): Long` — singular
   `@Insert`. The LIVE chapter-insert paths are batch
   `insertChapters` / `insertAll` (both LIVE on ChapterDao). The
   singular variant returns a `Long` id and was apparently intended
   for a never-shipped "add a single chapter inline" flow.

10. `getChaptersByIds(ids: List<Long>): List<SavedChapterEntity>` —
    @Query batch read. The LIVE per-id reads are
    `getChapterById(chapterId): Flow<SavedChapterEntity?>` and
    `getChapterByIdSuspend(chapterId): SavedChapterEntity?`. The
    batch variant was a never-wired sibling.

### Import cleanup

**MangaDao.kt**: dropped 2 imports rendered unused after the drops.

- `androidx.room.Insert` — the only `@Insert` annotations on this DAO
  were on `saveManga` and `saveChapters` (both dropped). `@Update` on
  `updateManga` is a separate annotation; that import remains.
- `me.manga.kira.data.local.entity.SavedChapterEntity` — the only
  reference was the parameter type on `saveChapters(chapters:
  List<SavedChapterEntity>)`. `SavedMangaEntity` remains LIVE
  (referenced by `updateManga`, `getAllSavedMangaFlow`, `getMangaById`).

**ChapterDao.kt**: import set unchanged. Every import (`Dao`, `Insert`,
`OnConflictStrategy`, `Query`, `Transaction`, `Flow`,
`SavedChapterEntity`) remains LIVE through the 19 preserved members.

### Header comment refresh

Replaced the stale "Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.daoprune" Task
#388 header on both DAOs with a fresh "Phase 9.x.dao.componentprune
.cumulative" Task #392 header. The new header:
- Names each of the 10 drops + the specific LIVE callsite of each
  preserved member (so future audits can verify in O(1) by inspection,
  not by full grep).
- Documents the audit posture (3-pass anchored greps).
- Explicitly calls out the prior URS-anchored audit's incorrect
  "preserved LIVE" claims, so future readers do not propagate them.

### Build gates

`gradlew.bat :composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid
:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64 :composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64
:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — joint 4-target gate: **BUILD
SUCCESSFUL in 1m 57s**, 138 actionable tasks (31 executed, 107
up-to-date). Room's KSP plugin regenerated `MangaDao_Impl.kt` and
`ChapterDao_Impl.kt` from the 23 remaining methods without complaint.
Zero new warnings introduced; all pre-existing warnings (named-arg
mismatches in source repositories, Compose deprecations) unchanged.

iOS-on-device smoke tests deferred to macOS (Windows-impossible).

### Behaviour preservation

The 10 dropped methods had ZERO source-tree reachers. No behaviour
observable from any LIVE callsite changes. Specifically:

- Reading-progress toggles continue through the LIVE
  `LibraryRepository.toggleChapterRead` →
  `libraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead` path.
- Manga + chapter saves continue through the LIVE
  `MangaRepository.save` → `libraryDao.saveMangaWithChapters` path.
- Per-id chapter reads continue through `getChapterById` /
  `getChapterByIdSuspend`.
- Library deletion continues through `LibraryRepository.removeManga`
  → `libraryDao.removeMangaWithChapters` (which internally calls
  LibraryDeo's `removeAllChaptersForManga`, not ChapterDao's).

### MVI contract

Not applicable — both DAOs sit below the MVI surface. No
state/intent/effect contracts touched.

### Strangler-fig integrity

The rework strangler-fig `:data` impls (`LibraryRepositoryImpl`,
`HistoryRepositoryImpl`, `UpdatesRepositoryImpl`, `DownloadsAction
RepositoryImpl`, `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl`, `Reading
SessionRepositoryImpl`, `SourcesRepositoryImpl`) all continue to reach
the legacy `:shared` facades through their existing call points;
none of the dropped DAO members had a `:data` reacher. Verified by
direct grep of every `legacy.X` callsite across `:data/.../repository/`:
no callsite touched any of the 10 dropped methods.

### SOLID posture (post-slice)

- **SRP**: Yes — each DAO interface is now precisely the set of
  query / mutation methods its consumers reach.
- **OCP**: Yes — surface shrinks. Closed under modification (the 23
  preserved methods preserve their exact signatures); open under
  extension via new methods.
- **LSP**: Yes — dropped members had no consumers; no substitutability
  contract to break.
- **ISP**: Yes — interfaces are narrower and aligned with actual
  consumer needs. Particularly:
  - MangaDao: 13 → 9 members (4 dropped).
  - ChapterDao: 25 → 19 members (6 dropped).
- **DIP**: Yes — both DAOs remain abstractions Room's KSP plugin
  generates impls for; the consumer-side `:shared` repositories and

## §224 — Phase 9.x.chapterdownloaddao.componentprune — `ChapterDownloadDao` orphan retire (completes DAO sweep cycle)

**Status**: Closed (Task #394).
**Commits**: `2b8204f` (source — drop 4 orphans), this docs commit (close-out + smoke-test
stale-ref fix).

### Strategy

Member-level retire on `shared/.../data/local/dao/ChapterDownloadDao.kt`, the last
un-swept sibling DAO in the cumulative `:shared/.../data/local/dao/` audit cycle that
spanned §219-§223. Same exhaustive 3-pass reacher-chain audit pattern (receiver-anchored
`chapterDownloadDao.X(` + `dao.X(`, bare word-boundary `\bX\b`, method-reference `::X`)
applied across the entire source tree. Each candidate verified zero-reach under every
anchor before the drop.

The audit surfaced a 4-of-21 orphan split. Each dropped member overlapped semantically
with a LIVE neighbour but was never wired into the actual download path. The download
plumbing (DownloadRepositoryImpl on Android, CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl on iOS +
Desktop, plus DownloadWorkerV2 / ChapterDownloadService / DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl)
exercises 17 LIVE members; the other 4 were leftover surface options.

### Audit findings — dropped members

| Member                              | LIVE neighbour (overlap)              | Rationale for orphan status                  |
|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `upsert(entity)` @Insert Unit       | `insert(download): Long`               | Workers need the rowId; bare-Unit never wired|
| `getAll()` Flow                     | `observeAllDownloads()` `ORDER BY id DESC` | UI needs reverse-chrono ordering           |
| `observeQueuedChapters(state)` Flow | `getAllQueuedChapterIds(state)` Flow   | Scheduler only needs IDs, not full entities  |
| `getCountByState(state)` Flow       | `getQueuedCount(queuedState)` Flow     | Only QUEUED state ever queried in practice   |

All 4 had ZERO reachers across all 3 anchor patterns. The lone occurrence outside the
DAO definition was a stale `ChapterDownloadDao.upsert()` reference in
`migration/runtime-smoke-test.md` row 17 — corrected to `ChapterDownloadDao.insert()`
in this close-out (matches the LIVE path at `DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:84` /
`CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:149`).

### Audit findings — LIVE members preserved (17 total)

| Member                              | Reach points                                                |
|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `insert(download): Long`            | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:84`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:149` |
| `insertAll(downloads): List<Long>`  | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:99`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:158` |
| `getNextQueuedChapter(state)`       | `DownloadWorkerV2:132`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:214` |
| `getDownloadByChapter(id)`          | `DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl:125`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:268` |
| `getQueuedCount(state)`             | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:66`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:128` |
| `deleteByChapterId(id)`             | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:91`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:164` |
| `observeRunningChapter(...)`        | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:63`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:122` |
| `getAllQueuedChapterIds(state)`     | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:67`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:112/130` |
| `updateStateAndProgress(...)`       | `DownloadWorkerV2:217/273/289`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:296` |
| `updateProgress(id, %)`             | `DownloadWorkerV2:259`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:291` |
| `updateState(id, state)`            | Internal LIVE via `updateFailure` @Transaction body         |
| `updateStateChId(id, state)`        | `DownloadWorkerV2:136`, `ChapterDownloadService:205/214/331/337`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:249` |
| `setErrorMsg(id, msg)`              | Internal LIVE via `updateFailure` @Transaction body         |
| `updateFailure(id, msg)` @Transaction | `ChapterDownloadService:219/231/237/342/353/358`, `DownloadRepositoryImpl:105`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:168/222/226/256/286` |
| `observeAllDownloads()`             | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:65/112/118`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:124/135/140` |
| `clearByState(state)`               | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:136/137`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:200/201` |
| `markAllRunningOrQueuedAsFailed(...)` | `DownloadRepositoryImpl:124`, `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl:172` |

Note: `updateState` + `setErrorMsg` are reached only inside the `updateFailure`
@Transaction body. This is the same "internal-LIVE-via-association" pattern seen in
§222 (ChapterDao's `markChaptersReadBatch` etc.) — Room resolves the call within the
@Dao interface scope, so the @Transaction body acts as an internal reacher even though
no external caller invokes the methods directly.

### Behaviour preservation

The 4 dropped methods had ZERO source-tree reachers. No behaviour observable from any
LIVE callsite changes. Specifically:

- Worker enqueue continues through the LIVE `insert(download): Long` path (returns
  rowId — required by `DownloadWorkerV2.kt`'s follow-on progress writes).
- UI download-list rendering continues through `observeAllDownloads()` ORDER BY id
  DESC.
- Scheduler wake-up continues through `getAllQueuedChapterIds(state)` IDs-only Flow
  (`CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:112`).
- Queued-count UI badges continue through `getQueuedCount(QUEUED)`.

### MVI contract

Not applicable — `ChapterDownloadDao` sits below the MVI surface.

### Strangler-fig integrity

The rework `:data` impl `DownloadsRepositoryImpl` / `DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl`
reach the legacy `DownloadRepository` facade and (in
`DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.kt:125`) the DAO directly. None of the 4 dropped
members were on these paths. Verified by direct inspection of every `legacy.X` and
`chapterDownloadDao.X` callsite in `:data/.../repository/`: no callsite touched any
of the 4 dropped methods.

### SOLID posture (post-slice)

- **SRP**: Yes — `ChapterDownloadDao` is now precisely the 17-method action +
  observation surface its consumers exercise.
- **OCP**: Yes — surface shrinks. Closed under modification (the 17 preserved methods
  preserve their exact signatures); open under extension via new methods.
- **LSP**: Yes — dropped members had no consumers; no substitutability contract to
  break (Room's KSP regenerates the impl from the trimmed Kotlin interface).
- **ISP**: Yes — interface narrows from 21 to 17 methods (~19% reduction). Each
  preserved method is consumed by at least one of the 5 LIVE callers.
- **DIP**: Yes — `ChapterDownloadDao` remains an abstraction Room's KSP plugin
  generates impls for; consumer-side dependencies on the abstraction unchanged.

## §225 — Phase 9.x.statisticsrepository.componentprune — drop orphan
`readMinutesFlow` re-export on legacy StatisticsRepository (Task #395)

### Strategy

The cumulative DAO sweep (§§219-§224, Tasks #392-#394) exhausted the
`:shared/.../data/local/dao/` tier — all 8 sibling DAOs swept. The
documented next-slice carry-over was the `:shared/.../features/*/domain/
*Repository.kt` legacy facade tier. Picked `StatisticsRepository`
(`:shared/.../presentation/features/statistics/domain/`) as the next
candidate because it has the smallest member-surface among the remaining
facades and its sole external consumer
(`ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl` — Phase 7.x.statistics strangler-fig)
is fresh in mind from §223.

Followed the same 3-pass receiver-anchored grep audit posture used for
the DAO sweeps:

1. Receiver-anchored: `statisticsRepository.X` / `legacy.X` / `repo.X`
   for each public member.
2. Bare word-boundary: `\bX\b` for each public member name.
3. Method-ref: `::X` for each public member name.

All three passes cover the entire source tree (`shared/`, `domain/`,
`data/`, `presentation/`, `ui/`, `composeApp/`).

### Audit summary — 11 public members → 10 LIVE / 1 dropped

| # | Member | Verdict | Reacher / rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `inLibraryFlow: Flow<Int>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:83` |
| 2 | `chaptersTotalFlow: Flow<Int>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:84` |
| 3 | `chaptersDownloadedFlow: Flow<Int>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:85` |
| 4 | `chaptersReadFlow: Flow<Int>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:86` |
| 5 | `chaptersBookmarkedFlow: Flow<Int>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:87` |
| 6 | `completedEntriesFlow: Flow<Int>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:88` |
| 7 | `startedEntriesFlow: Flow<Int>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:89` |
| 8 | `readMinutesFlow: Flow<Int>` | **DROPPED** | Public re-export of `dataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow`. ZERO external reachers. The only use was internal (`readDurationFlow` derivation at the prior line 46); inlined to read directly from the upstream. |
| 9 | `readDurationFlow: Flow<String>` | **LIVE** | `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:91` |
| 10 | `startReadingSession()` | **LIVE** | `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl.kt` Phase 6.4.x.statistics strangler-fig `start()` impl |
| 11 | `endReadingSession()` | **LIVE** | `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl.kt` matching `end()` impl |

### Why the orphan was a true orphan (semantic-overlap-with-internal-use pattern)

The `val readMinutesFlow: Flow<Int> = dataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow`
pass-through at the prior line 44 was a public property re-exporting an
upstream DataStoreHelper field. The receiver-anchored audit found ZERO
`statisticsRepository.readMinutesFlow` / `legacy.readMinutesFlow` /
`repo.readMinutesFlow` reachers; the bare-word audit surfaced 5 source
files referencing the name, but on inspection every one of those
references is a KDoc reference prefixed with the upstream type
(`DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow`) — those document the cell of truth,
not a consumption of the StatisticsRepository wrapper:

- `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:16` — `"DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow reads — same posture as..."`
- `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:56` — `"the upstream DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow emits..."`
- `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:74` — `"DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow.map { ... }"`
- `StatisticsViewModel.kt:29/31` — `"DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow.map { format }"` / `"DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow reads from a deterministic in-process settings store"`
- `ReadingStatisticsRepository.kt:13` — `"DataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow reads — same strangler-fig posture as..."`

The legitimate runtime upstream that `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl`
consumes is `legacy.readDurationFlow` (the formatted "Xh Ym" string,
member #9), NOT the wrapper minute-counter at member #8. The only call
site of the wrapper was internal at the prior line 46
(`readMinutesFlow.map { ... }` derivation), which the prune rewrites to
read the upstream directly: `dataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow.map {...}`.
Same emission semantics — multiplatform-settings `getIntFlow` is the
cell of truth either way.

### Why this is safe (and not a behaviour change)

`readDurationFlow` is the ONLY external consumer of the prior wrapper's
minute-counter shape. The prune does NOT change `readDurationFlow`'s
contract — same `Flow<String>`, same emission cadence, same "Xh Ym"
format, same `dataStoreHelper.readMinutesFlow` upstream. The wrapper
was a structurally redundant indirection layer; eliminating it
collapses 2 lines into 1 without altering observable semantics.

## §226 — Phase 9.x.notificationrepository.componentprune (Task #396)

### Strategy

The Phase 9.x.statisticsrepository.componentprune slice (Task #395, §225)
closed by carrying-over the next-slice candidate pool: the remaining
`:shared/.../features/*/domain/*Repository.kt` legacy facade classes
(NotificationRepository, SettingsRepository, DownloadRepository), plus
re-sweeps of MangaRepository and the never-swept `:shared/.../domain/
model/*.kt` data classes. Per the §225 next-slice ordering — pick the
target with the smallest public-surface and the cleanest semantic-overlap
case — `NotificationRepository` was the natural first pick (6 public
members, single-receiver consumer `UpdatesRepositoryImpl` already
audited).

### Audit results (3-pass reacher-chain — 6 members → 1 dropped + 1 coupled-dead callee dropped)

| Member | Anchored reach | Bare `\bX\b` | `::X` method-ref | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fun getGroupedNotifications(): Flow<List<Pair<String, List<ChapterNotification>>>>` | `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:86` | matches anchored | — | LIVE |
| `suspend fun markAsRead(id: Long)` | `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:91` | matches anchored | — | LIVE |
| `suspend fun markAllAsRead()` | `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:95` | matches anchored | — | LIVE |
| `suspend fun deleteAll()` | `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:103` | matches anchored | — | LIVE |
| `suspend fun delete(notification: ChapterNotification)` | `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:99` | matches anchored | — | LIVE |
| `suspend fun restore(notification: ChapterNotification)` | **ZERO** | KDoc-only at `:domain/repository/UpdatesRepository.kt:18/19/25` (explicit deliberate-omission documentation) | — | **DROPPED** |

### Semantic-overlap-with-deliberate-omission pattern

`restore()` is the first prune candidate this batch where the "no
reacher" finding is corroborated by **explicit KDoc rationale in a sibling
rework interface** rather than by purely-internal-use overlap (the
§224/§225 pattern). The rework `:domain/UpdatesRepository` interface
documents the omission in two separate places:

- Line 18-19: `"Inserts (ChapterNotificationHelper.queueNotification) and
  undo-restore (NotificationRepository.restore) are intentionally NOT on
  this interface (ISP)"`
- Line 25: `"No restore(entry) because the rework deliberately omits the
  undo-snackbar UX"`

The Phase 7.x.updates.undosnackbar slice (Task #298) added a Compose-side
`SnackbarHostState` undo affordance to the rework `UpdatesScreen` — but
that snackbar's "Undo" button on the rework path re-issues the delete
inverse via a different mechanism (re-emit through the source-of-truth
Room flow, not by re-inserting a previously-deleted row through a DAO
singular insert). The legacy notification-deletion flow had used
`restore()` to push a deleted row back into Room; the rework flow has no
equivalent need because the rework Flow-based observation re-emits the
remaining set immediately, and an in-memory "undo" buffer on the VM side
is sufficient.

This makes the `restore()` member a documented orphan since the Phase 7.x.
updates strangler-fig landed. The prior audit (Phase 9.x.notificationdao.
componentprune, Task #385) preserved `dao.insertNotification` LIVE
solely because `NotificationRepository.restore()` reached it; that
preservation is now invalidated.

### Coupled-dead callee retire

With `NotificationRepository.restore()` dropped, the singular @Insert
overload `NotificationDao.insertNotification(notification: ChapterNotification): Long`
loses its only reacher. Same-slice retire:

- `insertNotification(notification: ChapterNotification): Long` — singular
  @Insert. Dropped.
- `insertNotificationsList(notifications: List<ChapterNotification>): List<Long>`
  — plural batch @Insert, reached by `ChapterNotificationHelper.kt:110`
  (`notificationDao.insertNotificationsList(notifications)`). Stays
  LIVE — every remaining notification-creation path uses the batch
  overload (the helper batches per-manga refresh-fetch results into a
  single insert call regardless of count).

This is a tight 1-receiver + 1-coupled-callee slice: dropping both keeps
the audit-trail explicit (the `:shared` DAO file gets a third audit
sub-section recording this slice's coupled-dead retire), and the source
commit stays at 2 files (well within the 5-file cap).

### Inline-rewrite safety analysis

`restore()` was a single-line pass-through (`dao.insertNotification(notification)`).
No call-site context to preserve. The DAO singular insert's removal is
schema-safe: the @Insert annotation generates code at compile time, and
the underlying SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO notifications` statement
is still emitted by the LIVE batch `insertNotificationsList` (Room
generates a per-call statement for each element in the list,
semantically identical to N invocations of the singular @Insert).

### Files touched (2 — well within the 5-file cap)

1. `shared/.../features/notifications/domain/NotificationRepository.kt`
   — drop `restore()` body (lines 53-58 with KDoc), add 22-line Phase 9.x
   audit header documenting the drop + LIVE-preservation table.
2. `shared/.../data/local/dao/NotificationDao.kt` — drop singular
   `insertNotification` (lines 63-64 of pre-slice), update the prior
   Phase 9.x.notificationdao header (line 22 had listed
   `dao.insertNotification` as LIVE; that audit is now invalidated and a
   new sub-section records this slice's coupled-dead retire and adjusts
   the live-reacher count from 5 to 4).

### LIVE membership post-slice

`NotificationRepository` post-slice (5 of original 6 public members):

- `getGroupedNotifications()` — `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:86`.
- `markAsRead(id: Long)` — `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:91`.
- `markAllAsRead()` — `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:95`.
- `delete(notification)` — `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:99`.
- `deleteAll()` — `UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:103`.

`NotificationDao` post-slice (8 LIVE members):

- `insertNotificationsList` — `ChapterNotificationHelper.kt:110`.
- `updateNotification` — LIVE-by-association via
  `addLocalImagePathByChapterId` @Transaction body.
- `getAllNotifications` — `dao.getAllNotifications()` self-body call from
  `NotificationRepository.getGroupedNotifications`.
- `markAllAsRead` — `NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()`.
- `deleteNotification` — `NotificationRepository.delete(notification)`.
- `deleteAllNotifications` — `NotificationRepository.deleteAll()`.

### Pivot rationale

A negative audit is a valid stopping condition for the current target but
NOT for the slice — per the standing `/goal` Stop hook Rule 3, the audit
trail surfaces the next-closest productive target. The 22-member
SettingsRepository audit table identified `legacy SettingsViewModel` as
the **most-leveraged consumer** of SettingsRepository — 10 of its 13
members were dead-letter post Phase 7.x.settings.swap (Task #301) and had
ZERO external reachers. Pivoting there preserves slice productivity
without violating the audit's "all-22-LIVE" verdict.

## §228 — Phase 9.x.downloadrepository.componentprune (Task #398)

Three-pass receiver-anchored reacher-chain audit (`downloadRepository.X(`
/ `repository.X(` / `repo.X(` + bare `\bX\b` word-boundary + `::X`
method-ref) of the 15-member legacy `DownloadRepository` interface
surfaced **4 independently-orphan methods** + **7 coupled-dead
`DownloadViewModelv2` members** + **2 coupled-dead `ChapterDownloadDao`
callees**, all dropped in a single 5-file slice at the cap.

### Audit chain

The only external resolver of the legacy `DownloadRepository` is
`DownloadViewModelv2` (`shared/.../download/ui/test2/`), which is itself
resolved exactly once at `App.kt:283-284` via `koinViewModel()` and
threaded into `LibraryMangaScreenRoute` (the only Compose consumer
post-Phase 7.x.downloads.swap, Task #295). All non-VM receivers of
`DownloadRepository` are the two impls themselves
(`DownloadRepositoryImpl` android / `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl`
nonAndroid), so chain trace = `DownloadRepository.X` →
`DownloadViewModelv2.Y` → `LibraryMangaScreenRoute` (LIVE) **xor** no
reacher (ORPHAN).

The rework's parallel path is `:data DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl`,
which reaches the legacy `DownloadRepository` for exactly one method
(`deleteDownload(chapterId)` at line 142) — that interface method stays
LIVE; only the VM's wrapper around it was orphan.

### Per-member verdict

| Interface method                                  | Live? | Chain |
| ------------------------------------------------- | :---: | ----- |
| `observeRunningChapter()`                         |  ✅   | VM `runningChapter` → `LibraryMangaScreenRoute` |
| `observeAllDownloads()`                           |  ✅   | impls `observeRunningChapter` / `:data DownloadsRepositoryImpl` reach equivalent DAO |
| `isDownloading()`                                 |  ✅   | VM `isDownloading` → `LibraryMangaScreenRoute` |
| `queuedCount(): Flow<Int>`                        |  ❌   | VM `queuedCount` had zero external reacher; UI consumer was retired legacy DownloadsScreen (#352) |

| `enqueueChaptersDownload(chapters, title, api)`   |  ✅   | VM `downloadChapters` → `LibraryMangaScreenRoute` |
| `deleteDownload(chapterId)`                       |  ✅   | `:data DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.kt:142` (rework strangler-fig); VM wrapper was orphan but interface method LIVE |

share the same `Phase 9.x.downloadrepository.*` lineage (the negative
re-sweeps establish what is **not** prunable; the staleKdocSweep cleans
up references to the §398-retired members).

The 5-member `MangaRepository` was last swept in §224 (Task #384), which
retired 2 orphan methods. Per the §228 next-slice ordering, a re-sweep

strangler-fig builds (§157 → §232) had orphaned additional members.

### Task #399 (continued) — `:shared/.../domain/model/*.kt` data class audit — NEGATIVE

The 6 `@Serializable` data classes never swept by any prior slice were
surveyed:

- `PopularManga` (5 fields) — used as a source-repository return type
  across 30+ source-repo impls.
- `ChapterImage` (2 fields) — used by `ChapterItem.chaptersImages` field
  + 3 reachers (`HandelDataClasses`, `Dataclasses`, `MangamelloChapter
  Image`).
- `MangaInfo` (17 fields) — nav-route argument for Details navigation
  (`HomeScreenRoute` / `LibraryMangaScreenRoute` route arg type).
- `MangaItem` (8 fields) — used by source-repository search/popular APIs
  across 30+ reachers.
- `ReaderChapters` (11 fields) — nav-route argument for Reader navigation
  (`ChapterImagesScreenRoute` route arg type, see §65 / §66).
- `ChapterItem` (7 fields) — used as `MangaInfo.chapters` element +
  30+ source-repo constructor reachers.

Result: **all 6 are LIVE.** No drops productive.

**Why field-level pruning is blocked**: every member of every class is
either (a) read by at least one reacher in the live source tree, or (b)
implicitly load-bearing via the `@Serializable` wire format. Specifically,
`MangaInfo`, `MangaItem`, `ReaderChapters`, and `ChapterItem` are encoded
into the Compose navigation graph's nav-arg payload (see Phase 4 batch
4.2 KDoc on each file: "Where the source app passed this type via Bundle
on Android, the new Compose-Multiplatform navigation graph uses
kotlinx.serialization to encode route arguments"). Removing any field
would change the route-arg schema, which would silently break in-flight
state restoration after process death — exactly the trigger-(b)
observable-behaviour change the autonomous worker is forbidden from
making without explicit user consent. The audit is closed as NEGATIVE
without field-level investigation.

Verdict: NEGATIVE — no source change. Field-level pruning gated by
serialization-schema stability; whole-class pruning blocked by many
live reachers per class.

## §230 — Phase 9.x.historyvm.componentprune (Task #401)

### Strategy

Productive single-slice componentprune on the legacy `:shared` (presentation-tier) `HistoryViewModel.kt`. The §229 docs noted that all three queued candidates (SettingsVM retire, DownloadViewModelv2 retire, cumulative DAO re-sweep) are gated on out-of-scope structural moves. Per the `/goal` Stop hook Rule 3 (Deferring is NOT an allowed stopping reason), an alternative orphan-chain candidate was identified by surveying `shared/.../presentation/features/*/data/*.kt` for single-file orphans.

Discovery chain:
- `HistoryUiState.kt` (`shared/.../presentation/features/history/data/HistoryUiState.kt`) showed only one production reacher: the legacy `HistoryViewModel.kt` (self-reacher).
- 3-pass reacher-chain audit on legacy `HistoryViewModel`'s public surface revealed that the legacy `HistoryScreen.kt` (retired in Phase 9.x.history.legacyui.retire — Task #357) was its sole UI consumer for the `uiState` / `loadHistory` / `delete*` / `chapterDownloadedState` / `clearError` surface.
- The legacy `HistoryViewModel` remains constructed by the Koin module and reached by `ChapterImagesScreenRoute.kt:78` + `ReaderScreen.kt:148/171/506` for the **Reader's** chapter-read mark + history insert/update path. Those 4 LIVE members stay; the other 6 (plus the `init {}` block and the entire `HistoryUiState` data class) are dropped.

This is the canonical "satellite VM consumer post-legacy-screen-retirement" pattern: a `:shared` VM that was reached by both a now-retired legacy screen AND a still-live consumer (the Reader chapter-mark path) has its members partition cleanly into a LIVE Reader-path-only set and an orphan set tied to the retired UI.

## §231 — Phase 9.x.chaptersvm.componentprune (Task #402) — drop 5 orphan ChaptersViewModel members + 3 unused deps

### Strategy

Legacy `:shared` `ChaptersViewModel` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/common/viewmodel/ChaptersViewModel.kt`) was a 4-arg VM with 5 public StateFlow / suspend-fn members (`readingMode`, `setReadingMode`, `chapterImgs`, `bookmarked`, `getChaptersDataR`) plus 2 unassigned-Job? private fields and an `onCleared` override. A 3-pass receiver-anchored reacher-chain audit (`chaptersViewModel.X(` + bare `\bX\b` + `::X`) across the entire source tree confirmed the ONLY LIVE reacher of this VM is `chaptersViewModel.getChaptersDataR(url)` at `composeApp/.../navigation/routes/HomeScreenRoute.kt:177` (the `onSaveToggle` flow that enriches an `ApiMangaItem` with its `MangaInfo` before saving). The reading-mode side surface (`readingMode` StateFlow + `setReadingMode(mode)`) was duplicated work — the Reader stack owns its own `readerViewModel.readingMode` / `readerViewModel.setReadingMode` since Phase 6.4.x.mode (Task #219); the legacy VM's standalone copy was a parallel surface that the rework never reached. The `chapterImgs` / `bookmarked` StateFlows had no reachers at any point in the live tree.

### Audit chain table (pre-prune 7-member surface)

| Member | Pre-prune posture | Audit verdict | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getChaptersDataR(url): Flow<State<MangaInfo>>` | LIVE — `HomeScreenRoute.kt:177` | ✓ LIVE | Preserve verbatim |
| `readingMode: StateFlow<ReadingMode>` | StateFlow | ✗ ORPHAN — no `chaptersViewModel.readingMode` reacher (Reader owns `readerViewModel.readingMode`, ReaderScreen.kt:138) | Drop |
| `setReadingMode(mode)` | Persist | ✗ ORPHAN — no reacher (Reader picks via `readerViewModel.setReadingMode`, ReaderScreen.kt:480; rework Settings dispatches `SettingsIntent.OnReadingModeSelected`) | Drop |
| `chapterImgs: StateFlow<State<List<String>>>` | StateFlow | ✗ ORPHAN — no reacher (Reader UI consumes pages via `readerViewModel.state.pages`) | Drop |
| `bookmarked: StateFlow<Boolean>` | StateFlow | ✗ ORPHAN — no reacher (Reader owns `readerViewModel.bookmarked`, ReaderScreen.kt:139) | Drop |
| `init { settingsRepo.readingModeFlow ... }` | Side-effect | ✗ ORPHAN-coupled — only fed `_readingMode` | Drop |
| `onCleared()` override | LifecycleHook | ✗ ORPHAN-coupled — only cancelled the two unassigned `Job?` fields | Drop (default `ViewModel.onCleared()` is a no-op) |

The `currentJob: Job?` / `mangaDetailsJob: Job?` private fields were declared but never assigned anywhere in the body (always `null`) — `onCleared`'s `?.cancel()` calls were no-ops.

### Coupled-dead constructor-dep drops (transitively-orphan once body no longer references them)

| Constructor param | Pre-prune usage | Post-prune usage | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `libraryRepository: LibraryRepository` | NEVER used in body (already documented as such in pre-prune KDoc) | unchanged | DROP — pre-prune KDoc's "load-bearing for surrounding screen graph" rationale was incorrect (Koin `single { }` bindings are lazy) |
| `settingsRepo: SettingsRepository` | `init {}` + `setReadingMode(mode)` | both retired | DROP |
| `statisticsRepo: StatisticsRepository` | NEVER used in body | unchanged | DROP |
| `sourcesRepository: SourcesRepository` | `getChaptersDataR(url)` (the one LIVE member) | unchanged | PRESERVE |

### SharedModule binding update

Pre-prune (4-arg):

```kotlin
viewModel { ChaptersViewModel(get(), get(), get(), get()) }
```

Post-prune (1-arg, only `SourcesRepository`):

```kotlin
viewModel { ChaptersViewModel(get()) }
```

The Koin `viewModel { ... }` binding is a `factory<ViewModel>` under the hood — reducing the arg list does NOT change which singletons are eagerly resolved (all `single { }` bindings are lazy; the dropped `LibraryRepository` / `SettingsRepository` / `StatisticsRepository` singletons are still resolved by their OTHER consumers — e.g., `HistoryViewModel`, `LibraryDetailsViewModel`, the rework `:data` strangler-fig impls).

Post-§402, `ChaptersViewModel` is no longer a `LibraryRepository`-typed injection site (its `libraryRepository` constructor param was orphan and got dropped along with the rest of the VM's reading-mode/chapter-imgs/bookmarked surface). The comment is updated to note the 8→7 count change without re-running the underlying audit (the dropped facade methods were orphan across ALL 8 sites at audit time — including the now-retired ChaptersViewModel injection — so the audit conclusions are unaffected).

## §239 — Phase 9.x.whatsnewvm.componentprune (Task #410): legacy WhatsNewViewModel orphan-cascade prune

**Slice intent.** Continue the autonomous componentprune sweep over the
legacy `:shared` ViewModels. The next candidate per the §237 carry-over
queue is `shared/.../features/whatsnew/viewmodel/WhatsNewViewModel.kt`
(~256 lines). Unlike the prior `Library/Details/Home` legacy VMs which
had multiple LIVE route reachers, this VM is GATED on only ONE route
reach: the first-launch-redirect hook at `LibraryScreenRoute.kt:77` that
resolves `koinViewModel<WhatsNewViewModel>()` and consumes 2 StateFlow
getters for the redirect-gate condition. All other public surfaces
(6 methods + 2 StateFlows) are orphan.

**GATED-retire posture.** Full retire of the legacy VM is GATED by the
LIVE `koinViewModel<WhatsNewViewModel>()` resolution at
`LibraryScreenRoute.kt:77`. The route is the legacy Library route's
adapter which uses this VM as a side-channel observer for the first-
launch-redirect: when `versionName` bumps since the last seen version,
this VM auto-flips `shouldShowWhatsNew = true` and the adapter
navigates to `Screen.WhatsNewScreen(true)`. Lifting this cross-screen
redirect into the rework architecture requires a `Phase
9.x.library.whatsnewbridge` slice that the user has deferred — Library's
Phase 9 retire cycle must bottom out first.

**3-pass receiver-anchored reacher-chain audit.** Same pattern as Tasks
#407/#408/#409. The audit confirmed:

| VM symbol | External reachers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `shouldShowWhatsNew: StateFlow<Boolean>` | LibraryScreenRoute.kt:79 | LIVE |
| `isLoading: StateFlow<Boolean>` | LibraryScreenRoute.kt:80 | LIVE |
| `features: StateFlow<List<WhatsNewFeature>>` | none | ORPHAN |
| `loadError: StateFlow<String?>` | none | ORPHAN |
| `markWhatsNewAsSeen()` | none (rework adapter uses rework VM's `OnMarkSeen`) | ORPHAN |
| `forceShowWhatsNew()` | none | ORPHAN |
| `ensureFeaturesLoaded()` | none (only caller was `forceShowWhatsNew`) | ORPHAN |
| `retryLoadFeatures()` | none (rework adapter uses rework VM's `OnRetry`) | ORPHAN |
| `shouldShowBasedOnTime(): Boolean` | none | ORPHAN |
| `resetWhatsNew()` | none | ORPHAN |

**Independent orphans dropped (6).** All 6 public methods + 2 public
StateFlows had zero external reachers across all 3 audit passes:

1. `markWhatsNewAsSeen()` — Legacy mark-seen action. The bare-grep
   collisions with `markWhatsNewAsSeen` in docs/sibling-file KDocs are
   text references, not callers. The swap-completed
   `WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt:157` dispatches the REWORK
   `WhatsNewIntent.OnMarkSeen` instead, resolving against the rework VM
   (different package: `me.manga.kira.presentation.whatsnew`).
2. `forceShowWhatsNew()` — Public force-show debug helper. Zero
   reachers.
3. `retryLoadFeatures()` — Retry-fetch wrapper. Rework adapter routes
   retry through the rework VM's `WhatsNewIntent.OnRetry`.
4. `shouldShowBasedOnTime(): Boolean` — 30-day-since-last-show
   predicate. Never consulted by any adapter.
5. `resetWhatsNew()` — Clear-prefs-and-force-re-show debug helper.
6. `features` + paired `_features` backing field. Zero external
   readers; the rework adapter has its own feature flow via
   `GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase`.
7. `loadError` + paired `_loadError` backing field. Zero external
   readers.

(The independent count is 7 logical drops — 5 methods + 2 StateFlow
pairs. The 6th, `ensureFeaturesLoaded()`, is transitively-dead because
its only caller is `forceShowWhatsNew()`, not externally orphan.)

**Coupled-dead drops (transitively-dead).** Five additional surfaces
become dead once the public orphans + paired backing fields are gone:

- `ensureFeaturesLoaded()` — sole caller was `forceShowWhatsNew()`.
  Body's predicate `_features.value.isEmpty()` references the dropped
  field; the called `loadFeatures()` is preserved (still called by
  `checkIfShouldShowWhatsNew`).
- `loadDefaultFeatures()` — sole callers were inside `loadFeatures()`'s
  fallback branches (which are also removed since parsed features have
  no deposit site).
- `parseMediaType()` — sole caller was the
  `WhatsNewFeature(mediaType = parseMediaType(...))` construction inside
  `loadFeatures`'s mapNotNull (removed).
- `parseImageResourceName()` — sole caller was the same construction
  (removed).
- `hasLoadedFeatures: Boolean` field — readers were `ensureFeaturesLoaded`
  (dropped); writers were `loadFeatures` / `loadDefaultFeatures` /
  `retryLoadFeatures` / `resetWhatsNew` (3 of 4 dropped, the surviving
  write inside `loadFeatures` becomes orphan once readers are gone).
- `KEY_LAST_SHOWN_TIMESTAMP` companion const — readers were
  `markWhatsNewAsSeen` / `resetWhatsNew` / `shouldShowBasedOnTime` (all
  dropped).

**`loadFeatures()` body trim — observable-behaviour-preserving.** The
`LibraryScreenRoute.kt` redirect logic gates on `!isLoading`:

```kotlin
LaunchedEffect(shouldShowWhatsNew, isLoading) {
    if (shouldShowWhatsNew && !isLoading && !hasNavigatedToWhatsNew) {
        hasNavigatedToWhatsNew = true
        navController.safeNavigate(Screen.WhatsNewScreen(true))
    }
}
```

This means the suspend duration of the `loadFeatures` fetch is part of
the OBSERVABLE timing contract — the redirect happens AFTER the fetch
completes. To preserve this exactly, the fetch call
`remoteDataSource.fetchWhatsNewFeatures(languageCode)` is kept verbatim.
What's removed is the result-parsing branching (mapNotNull over
`response.features`, the `if (result.isSuccess) { ... } else { ... }`
deposit paths, the `loadDefaultFeatures()` fallback). None of these
have anywhere to deposit a parsed feature list now that `_features` is
retired. The result is implicitly discarded.

**Coupled import drops (5).** All transitively-dead:

- `kotlin.time.Clock` — sole users were 3 dropped methods.
- `kotlin.time.ExperimentalTime` — only the class-level `@OptIn(...)`
  annotation used it (guarding `Clock.System.now()` in the dropped
  methods). Annotation also dropped.
- `getDefaultFeatures` — sole user was `loadDefaultFeatures()`.
- `MediaType` — sole user was `parseMediaType()`.
- `WhatsNewFeature` — users were the dropped StateFlow type + dropped
  body construction.

| `isLoading: StateFlow<Boolean>` | public | `LibraryScreenRoute.kt:80` |
| `init { checkIfShouldShowWhatsNew() }` | n/a | initialise-on-construction |
| `checkIfShouldShowWhatsNew()` | private | sole writer of `_shouldShowWhatsNew = true` |
| `loadFeatures()` | private | sole writer of `_isLoading.value` |
| `getUserLanguageCode()` | private | called by `loadFeatures` |
| `_shouldShowWhatsNew` / `_isLoading` | private | backing fields for the LIVE StateFlows |
| `log: Logger` | private | used throughout |
| `TAG`, `KEY_LAST_SHOWN_VERSION_NAME` | private companion consts | used by retained code |

**Constructor unchanged.** All 4 deps (`ds: DataStoreHelper`,
`remoteDataSource: WhatsNewRemoteDataSource`, `prefs: SharedPrefsHelper`,
`appVersionProvider: AppVersionProvider`) remain LIVE-reached by
retained members. Koin binding in `SharedModule.kt` unchanged.

## §240 — Phase 9.x.downloadvmv2.componentprune (Task #411): drop duplicate `DownloadRepository` ctor-dep on legacy `DownloadViewModelv2`

**Slice intent.** Narrow the legacy `:shared` `DownloadViewModelv2` constructor
from a 2-arg `(repository, downloadRepo)` shape — both parameters of identical
type `DownloadRepository` resolved by Koin from the same singleton binding — to
a 1-arg `(repository)` shape. This is the same class of structural-redundancy
prune the cumulative §227 / §232 / §237 settings/manga/home audits used:
identify ctor slots that, after exhaustive reacher-chain audit, are confirmed
to be referentially-identical aliases of an already-bound dep, then collapse
them. The 9 LIVE external reachers (all in `LibraryMangaScreenRoute.kt`) are
preserved bit-identical — this is a pure inward refactor with no observable
behaviour change.

**Strategic context.** `DownloadViewModelv2` is the 10th and last fully-LIVE
legacy `:shared` ViewModel still under cumulative-prune attention this phase
(§228-§239 having previously visited History, Chapters, Manga, SharedChapters,
RepoSettings, WebView, MangaDerails, Home, LibraryDetails, and WhatsNew). It
remains LIVE because `LibraryMangaScreenRoute` — the legacy library-manga
details host route at `App.kt:283-284` — still resolves the VM via Koin and
threads it through to consume 9 distinct public surfaces (4 StateFlows + 5
functions). That host's full rework is GATED behind the Phase 9.x
`librarymanga.swap` slice (carry-over item, not in this phase's scope). Until
that swap lands, the legacy VM stays bound and reachable; only structural
redundancies inside the VM are prunable in the meantime, which is exactly
what this slice does.

**The redundancy identified.** Prior to this slice the VM declared two ctor
parameters of the same type:

```kotlin
class DownloadViewModelv2(
    private val repository: DownloadRepository,
    private val downloadRepo: DownloadRepository,
) : ViewModel() {
```

Both slots resolved at the Koin binding site
`viewModel { DownloadViewModelv2(get(), get()) }` (at `SharedModule.kt:333`).
Since `DownloadRepository` has no qualifier-discriminated bindings (verified by
absence of any `qualifier(...)` decoration in the SharedModule block + zero
hits on `named("downloadRepo")` etc. across the source tree), both `get()`
calls resolve to the SAME `DownloadRepository` singleton — the two slots were
referentially-identical aliases for the same instance.

**Reacher-chain audit (3-pass).**

| Pass | Pattern | Hits |
|------|---------|------|
| 1 | Receiver-anchored: `downloadRepo.X(` | 1 — `downloadRepo.onCancel(chapterId)` in `onCancelChapterTapped` body (line 105 pre-prune) |
| 2 | Bare word-boundary: `\bdownloadRepo\b` | 2 — the ctor declaration site + the `onCancelChapterTapped` reach. Zero hits anywhere else in the source tree |
| 3 | Callable-ref: `::downloadRepo` | 0 hits |

Cross-checked: the `downloadRepo` field is declared `private val`, so it
cannot be observed externally even via reflection-style patterns. Confirmed
exactly one internal call site; zero external reachers. The first ctor slot
`repository` is used at 8 internal sites (the 4 StateFlow definitions and
4 of the 5 launch-body bodies); the second slot is used at exactly 1
internal site. Both refer to the same Koin singleton.

**The prune.** Three coordinated changes in this slice:

1. `DownloadViewModelv2` ctor narrows from 2-arg to 1-arg by dropping
   `private val downloadRepo: DownloadRepository`.

2. The `onCancelChapterTapped` body's single use is rewritten from
   `downloadRepo.onCancel(chapterId)` to `repository.onCancel(chapterId)`.
   This is identical runtime behaviour — the same Koin singleton dispatches
   the same interface method — just routed through the surviving ctor slot.
   The `onCancel(chapterId)` method on the `DownloadRepository` interface
   is itself a documented LIVE member (per the §228 audit at
   `DownloadRepository.kt:74`, reached only by this VM).

3. The Koin binding at `SharedModule.kt:333` narrows from
   `viewModel { DownloadViewModelv2(get(), get()) }` to
   `viewModel { DownloadViewModelv2(get()) }`. The SharedModule.kt change is
   wrapped in a 6-line audit-trail comment block referencing this slice's
   audit header.

**Behaviour-preservation verification.** All 9 LIVE external surfaces preserved
bit-identical:

- StateFlows: `runningChapter`, `isDownloading`, `queuedChapterIds`,
  `networkAvailable` — declarations unchanged, all still pull from
  `repository` slot.
- Suspend dispatches: `downloadChapter`, `downloadChapters`,
  `cancelDownloads`, `cancelRunningDownload` — bodies unchanged, all still
  dispatch to `repository` slot.
- `onCancelChapterTapped` — body rewritten to route through `repository`
  slot instead of `downloadRepo` slot; runtime behaviour identical (same
  Koin singleton, same interface method, same suspend dispatch on
  `IODispatcher`).

The trailing `// 2) tell the Worker to stop that chapter's Job` numbered-step
TODO comment inside `onCancelChapterTapped` is preserved verbatim — this
slice prunes dead structure only, not documented future-work hints.

**Files touched (slice cap = 5):**

1. `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/features/download/ui/test2/DownloadViewModelv2.kt` —
   ctor narrowed; `onCancelChapterTapped` body retargeted; audit-header KDoc
   paragraph appended.
2. `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/SharedModule.kt` — Koin
   binding narrowed from `(get(), get())` to `(get())`; 6-line audit-trail
   comment added above the binding.

(2 files in the source slice; 2 more files in the docs close-out for §240 +
SOLID Phase 9.x.downloadvmv2.componentprune entry. Total 4 — within cap.)

**4-target build gate (Windows-reachable).** All four gates green:

- `:composeApp:compileDebugKotlinAndroid` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 5s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 48s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m 34s.
- `:composeApp:compileKotlinDesktop` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m 24s.

No new warnings; existing deprecated-API warnings unchanged from §239 baseline.

**Layer boundary.** This slice is entirely inside the legacy `:shared`
boundary (one VM file + one DI file). No `:domain` / `:data` / `:presentation`
/ `:ui` / `:composeApp` files are touched. The strangler-fig posture
established in earlier phases (legacy `:shared` VMs are pruned in place until
their consumer route hosts swap to the rework `:presentation` slices)
continues to hold.

**MVI contract.** Untouched. `DownloadViewModelv2` is a legacy plain-VM (not
an MVI surface); the rework `:presentation` `DownloadsViewModel` from §118
remains the authoritative MVI surface for downloads.

**SOLID posture.**

- **SRP.** The VM's single responsibility (forwarding LibraryMangaScreenRoute's
  download-action gestures to the `DownloadRepository` and exposing 4 read-only
  state observers) remains unchanged. The duplicate ctor slot did not split
  the responsibility — it duplicated a dep injection point. Removing the
  duplication tightens SRP conformance by removing a confusing apparent
  dependency that wasn't actually a separate dependency.
- **OCP.** The class remains open to extension (additional download-action
  methods can be added without modifying existing ones) and closed to
  modification (no existing method body was rewritten in a behaviour-changing
  way; `onCancelChapterTapped`'s body change is referentially-identical).
- **LSP.** N/A (no inheritance changes).
- **ISP.** Mildly improved: the ctor signature is now smaller, which means
  any test code or alternative wirers (e.g. preview-mode Koin overrides) need
  to provide fewer args. The DI binding at `SharedModule.kt:333` is one line
  shorter.
- **DIP.** Unchanged. The VM continues to depend on the `DownloadRepository`
  abstraction, not its implementation. The duplicate ctor slot didn't violate
  DIP — it just made the dependency declaration more verbose than necessary.
- **Tell-Don't-Ask.** Unchanged. The VM continues to issue suspend dispatches
  to the repo without querying its state.
- **Banned features.** No `!!`, `Any`, `lateinit`, or `Thread` introduced.
  All suspend dispatches continue to use `viewModelScope.launch(IODispatcher)`
  per the established pattern.
- **Idempotency.** Unchanged. All 5 action methods remain effectful suspend
  dispatches with no idempotency-guard wiring (which is the legacy posture;
  the rework `DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl` handles idempotency at the
  repo layer).

- 30 → 31 files touched cumulatively for symbol-level prunes (now including

- 15 GATED-retire VMs documented unchanged (the per-VM full-retire is gated

## §241 — Phase 9.x.readervm.componentprune (Task #412): drop 5 orphan members + narrow 1 to private on legacy `ReaderViewModel`

**Slice goal.** Prune dead public surface on the legacy `:shared`
`ReaderViewModel` (601 lines, by far the largest legacy VM still in
play). The receiver-anchored audit confirms the file remains LIVE
overall — its sole external consumer is `composeApp/.../reader/ui/
screens/ReaderScreen.kt`, which reaches 14 surfaces via
`koinViewModel()`. The dropped/narrowed 6 surfaces had ZERO external
receiver-anchored reaches across the entire source tree.

**Audit posture (3-pass).** Same shape as the §239–§240 sweeps:

1. **Pass 1 — receiver-anchored:** `\breaderViewModel\.[A-Za-z]+\b` →
   22 hits in `composeApp/.../reader/ui/screens/ReaderScreen.kt`
   confirming 14 LIVE members.
2. **Pass 2 — bare identifier:** `\bX\b` for each candidate. All 6
   targets resolved to declaration-site + internal-only uses
   (`loadChapter` lines 152/491/508/532, `_loadedChapterIndexes`
   internal uses, etc.). The KDoc-only mentions in
   `:presentation/.../ReaderState.kt`, `:ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.
   kt`, `composeApp/.../reader/ui/reading_modes/PagerImageItem.kt`,
   `HorizontalReadingMode.kt`, and `composeApp/.../reader/ui/
   screens/ReaderScreen.kt` are documentation cross-references
   (rework-parity comparison comments), NOT actual invocations.
3. **Pass 3 — callable-ref:** `::loadChapter|::isChapterLoading|::
   goToPreviousChapter|::clearList|::loadedChapterIndexes|::
   compressionStates` → ZERO matches.

**Dropped (orphan VM members, 5):**

| Surface | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `compressionStates: StateFlow<Map<String, Any?>>` + `_compressionStates` backing field + `@Suppress("PropertyName")` annotation | StateFlow (Phase 10.3 Cluster E note #3 "no-op empty map shim") | Three KDoc mentions in composeApp `ReaderScreen.kt:85`, `PagerImageItem.kt:32`, `HorizontalReadingMode.kt:27` are item-list captions of "no longer plumbed parameters" — documentation only, no `.collectAsState()` / `.value` / `::` reach |
| `loadedChapterIndexes: StateFlow<List<Int>>` (public accessor) | StateFlow read accessor | Private backing field `_loadedChapterIndexes: MutableStateFlow` STAYS — 8 internal uses by `initialize`, `goToNextChapter`, `goToChapter`, `onCleared` |
| `fun goToPreviousChapter(chaptersList, mangaApi)` | Function | Three KDoc-only mentions in composeApp/ui/presentation files are rework-parity comparisons, not invocations |

## §243 — Phase 9.x.dao.componentprune.cumulative.rewind — Post-Task #412 DAO orphan rewind audit (Task #414)

### Why this section

§242's next-candidate block (Task #413's close-out) flagged
**cumulative DAO re-sweep** as the highest-priority structural sweep
candidate post-Tasks #401-#412 VM componentprune cascade. The original
Phase 9.x.dao.componentprune.cumulative (Task #392) consumed the
explicit DAO orphans that were already external-reacher-zero at that
point in time; the rewind audit asks: *did the 12 VM componentprunes
(Tasks #401-#412) consume the last external reachers of any
previously-gated DAO members, making them new orphan candidates?*

### Audit scope

Re-audit ALL `@Dao`-annotated interfaces in
`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/local/dao/` using
the established 3-pass receiver-anchored grep pattern:

1. **Pass 1** — `receiver.X(` (most common DAO call form, e.g.
   `chapterDao.getChaptersByMangaId(mangaId)`).
2. **Pass 2** — `\bX\b` for bare-name receiver-elision (uncommon for
   DAO calls but possible inside extension functions).
3. **Pass 3** — `::X` for method-reference reachers (very uncommon for
   DAO methods but theoretically possible).

DAO files surveyed (all 8):

- `ChapterDao.kt` — audited
- `ChapterDownloadDao.kt` — audited (post-Task #394 final form)
- `HistoryDao.kt` — audited
- `LibraryDeo.kt` — audited (this slice's only finding)
- `NotificationDao.kt` — audited (post-Task #385 final form)
- `SourcesDao.kt` — audited (post-Task #389 final form)
- `StatisticsDao.kt` — audited (post-Task #393 final form)
- `LibrarySubscriptionDao` (in-file; embedded interface) — audited

### Candidates identified

5 candidates in `LibraryDeo.kt` (one DAO, no other DAO had any):

| Method (file:line) | Annotation | Body callers (intra-DAO) | External reachers |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| `getMangaIdByUrl(url)` (line 19) | `@Query` (suspend) | `saveMangaWithChapters` @Transaction body (line 38) | 0 |
| `deleteMangaById(id)` (line 60) | `@Query` (suspend) | `removeMangaWithChapters` @Transaction body (line 67) | 0 |
| `removeAllChaptersForManga(mangaId)` (line 71) | `@Query` (suspend) | `removeMangaWithChapters` @Transaction body (line 64) | 0 |
| `removeAllNotification(mangaId)` (line 74) | `@Query` (suspend) | `removeMangaWithChapters` @Transaction body (line 65) | 0 |
| `removeHistory(mangaId)` (line 76) | `@Query` (suspend) | `removeMangaWithChapters` @Transaction body (line 66) | 0 |

All 5 are abstract `@Query`-annotated methods that Room's annotation
processor implements at build time. Each has zero external callers
(no source-tree reacher under `libraryDao.`, `dao.`, or method-ref
form) — confirmed by the 3-pass grep. The ONLY in-source reaches are
the intra-DAO @Transaction body invocations listed above.

### Verdict — NOT actionable (false positive)

The 5 candidates **cannot be pruned**. Room's `@Transaction` method
bodies CANNOT inline raw SQL — by the Room contract, @Transaction
bodies compose by calling other DAO methods (which carry the SQL via
their own `@Query` / `@Insert` / `@Update` / `@Delete` annotations).
The @Transaction body is just a Kotlin function that Room wraps in a
`runInTransaction { ... }` block; it has no syntax for embedding SQL
inline.

ChapterDao.kt:27-28 explicitly documents this resolution rule in its
own audit header: *"Room resolves method names within the @Dao scope,
so the LibraryDeo callsite never reached ChapterDao's variant."* The
same rule applies in reverse: a LibraryDeo @Transaction body call to
`getMangaIdByUrl` resolves to LibraryDeo's own abstract method, which
must continue to exist for Room to generate the SQL impl.

The 3-pass audit's "zero external reachers" finding is technically
correct but **misclassifies the methods**: they are not orphans, they
are intra-DAO helpers required by the @Transaction methods to satisfy
Room's compose-by-call semantics.

### Why this verdict is correct (defence-in-depth)

Three independent reasons the 5 methods are load-bearing:

1. **Room contract** — @Transaction body callsites are real method
   invocations resolved against the @Dao's own method table. Removing
   any of the 5 would cause Room's compiler to fail with "unresolved
   reference" errors in the @Transaction bodies.

2. **No equivalent inline SQL syntax** — there is no Room API for
   "embed this SQL directly in this @Transaction body." Every SQL
   operation in Room is mediated by a @Query/@Insert/@Update/@Delete
   annotation on a method. The @Transaction body can only call those
   methods.

3. **Visibility narrowing not viable** — Kotlin interface abstract
   methods cannot be `private` (since impl is generated externally by
   Room's annotation processor). `internal` is theoretically possible
   but unprecedented in this codebase's DAO patterns (zero existing
   `internal fun` DAO members across all 8 DAO files), so adding it
   would introduce a new pattern variation purely for marginal
   documentation value — not worth the structural churn.

### Action taken

**None.** No source files changed. This slice is audit-only — it
records the rewind sweep's verdict and updates the next-candidate
queue so future sessions don't redo this audit.

### Build gates

N/A — no source changed, no build gate required. The four-target
matrix (Android, Desktop, iOS Arm64, iOS SimulatorArm64) remains green
at HEAD `3a200a6` from Task #413's source slice (verified by Task
#413's docs commit landing on that state without flagging regressions).

  slices: **108** (unchanged — this slice is a null-result audit).
- Files touched across all componentprune+staleKdocSweep slices:
  **37** (unchanged — no source files modified this slice).

## §244 — Phase 9.x.repo.componentprune.cumulative — Inter-repository orphan scan (Task #415)

### Slice intent

Per §243's next-candidate block, advance to the inter-repository
cumulative orphan sweep. The individual repository componentprunes in
Tasks #383-#398 (Library, Manga, History, Sources, Download, Statistics,
Notification) each pruned their own surface against the then-current
reacher graph; this cumulative pass scans the union of remaining members
against the updated reacher graph to surface orphans that only became
dead after some upstream prune (e.g. a member that was LIVE-via-a-VM-
member, but whose VM-member got dropped in a later VM componentprune).

### Audit methodology

Three-pass receiver-anchored grep across the ENTIRE `*.kt` tree
(including the live Android-only `:app/` module which `settings.gradle.
kts:32` confirms is in the build):

1. `\.X\s*\(` — call sites that match the method/property name.
2. `\bX\b` — bare identifier references (e.g. method refs, KDoc tags).
3. `::X` — member references.

The `:app/` module's explicit inclusion in the audit is load-bearing: a
prior Explore-agent audit (§243-era) suggested members in
`LibraryRepository` were dead because the agent's reacher search did
not enumerate `:app/`. The actual `:app/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt` and
`:app/ChapterNotificationHelper.kt` both reach into `LibraryRepository`,
keeping `insertChapterList`, `getAllSavedManga`, and `getChapterIdByUrl`
LIVE. This is a recurring failure mode for tooling-driven audits when
the tooling silently scopes itself to `:shared/commonMain` only.

### Audit findings — 9 candidates surfaced, 2 actionable

The Explore-agent draft surfaced 9 candidates across 3 repositories.
Independent 3-pass verification reduced this to 2 actionable prunes:

| Repository | Member | Verdict | Reason |
|------------|--------|---------|--------|
| LibraryRepository | `insertChapterList` | LIVE | `:app/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:252` + `:app/ChapterNotificationHelper.kt:80` |
| LibraryRepository | `getAllSavedManga` | LIVE | `:app/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:140` |
| LibraryRepository | `getChapterIdByUrl` | LIVE | `:app/ChapterNotificationHelper.kt:85` |
| SourcesRepository | `getUrl(name)` | **PRUNE** | Zero `.kt` reachers. Misleading `sourcesRepository.getBaseUrlFor` callsites in per-source repos use a parameter NAMED `sourcesRepository` but TYPED as `SourcesDao` — resolves to the DAO method, not this facade method. See `BaseManga.kt:36` for the type declaration. |
| SourcesRepository | `findRepoByHost(host)` | LIVE | `composeApp/.../App.kt:174` reaches it for Coil interceptor host lookup. |
| SourcesRepository | `repoTaps` | **PRUNE** | Zero `.kt` reachers post-Task #405. The audit table entry at `ARCHITECTURE.md:34461` claiming LIVE via `RepoSettingsViewModel.kt:31` is STALE — Task #405's `reposettingsvm.componentprune` already removed the using member. |
| NotificationRepository | (3 members) | LIVE | All 3 candidates have `:data/UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt` strangler-fig `legacy.X()` reachers. Strangler-fig delegates count as reachers; the Explore agent missed them. |

### Lessons learned — false-positive failure modes

The 7-of-9 false-positive rate documents 4 systemic gaps in tooling-
driven audits that future sessions should explicitly check before
accepting an Explore-agent recommendation:

1. **Missed `:app/` reachers** — the Android-only `:app/` module is a
   live build target (`settings.gradle.kts:32 include(":app")`) but
   Explore tends to scope searches to `:shared/`. Always verify
   `\bX\b` matches in `:app/*.kt` before pruning anything from a
   `:shared/` facade.

2. **Missed `:data/` strangler-fig reachers** — the rework `:data`
   impls (`UpdatesRepositoryImpl`, `HistoryRepositoryImpl`,
   `SourcesRepositoryImpl`, `ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl`,
   `ReadingSessionRepositoryImpl`, `DownloadsRepositoryImpl`) all
   reach into `:shared` legacy facades via `legacy.X()` calls. These
   are LIVE reachers — they're the strangler-fig boundary. Audits
   that grep for `repositoryName.X(` patterns will MISS the
   `legacy.X(` pattern variant.

3. **Missed `:composeApp/` reachers** — `composeApp/.../App.kt` and
   the various `*ReworkScreenRoute.kt` files reach into shared
   facades (e.g. `App.kt:174 sourcesRepository.findRepoByHost(...)`).
   The Coil singleton image-loader interceptor wiring lives in
   `App.kt` and routes through the legacy `SourcesRepository.repos`
   set + `findRepoByHost` for per-source header injection (MEMORY:
   `project_yami_okhttp_fetcher`).

4. **Stale ARCHITECTURE.md audit-table entries** — earlier audits
   that recorded a member as LIVE-via-VM-member can become stale
   when a later VM componentprune removes the using member. The
   audit table is a *snapshot* of the reacher graph at audit time,
   not a live document. `ARCHITECTURE.md:34461`'s `repoTaps |
   RepoSettingsViewModel.kt:31 | LIVE` is the canonical example —
   the table entry survived Task #405's prune of the using member.
   **Mitigation**: always re-verify with a fresh `\bX\b` grep
   against current source, never trust the audit table verbatim.

5. **Misleading parameter naming** — per-source repositories
   (`BaseManga.kt`, ~30 source repos) all declare a constructor
   parameter NAMED `sourcesRepository` but TYPED as `SourcesDao`,
   not `SourcesRepository`. `sourcesRepository.getBaseUrlFor(...)`
   calls resolve to `SourcesDao.getBaseUrlFor`, NOT the facade
   method. **Mitigation**: when verifying a `\bsourcesRepository\.X`
   match, read the call-site constructor to confirm the parameter
   type, not just the parameter name.

### Audit methodology

Per the §244 cheatsheet plus new data-class disciplines:

1. Three-pass receiver-anchored grep across the ENTIRE `*.kt` tree
   (including `:app/`): `\.X\s*\(`, `\bX\b`, `::X`.
2. `\.X\b` accessor-anchored grep — separates read sites from write
   sites. For data-class fields, every named-arg constructor call
   matches `\bX\b` (`X = value`) but only `\.X` accessor reads count
   as live reachers.
3. `\.copy\([^)]*X` mutation-anchored grep — catches hidden read+rewrite
   sites that pass the orphan field through without explicit `.X` reads.
4. `component\d+\(\)` destructuring grep — catches positional accessors
   for `val (a, b, c) = mangaInfo`-style consumers.
5. Full `:app/` + `:data/` + `:composeApp/` enumeration.

#### Why the 5 orphan fields aren't pruned in this slice

Blast radius vs. 5-file cap:

- Each of the 4 `MangaInfo` orphan fields is named-arg-constructed by
  ~50 source-repository files (`:shared/sources_repositry/*/*.kt`).
  Removing one field from `MangaInfo` requires deleting 1 line from
  each of those 50 files + 1 line from the type declaration + 1 line
  from `MangaDetailsMappers.kt` + write-site lines in
  `HandelDataClasses.kt` ≈ ~54 file-touches per field.
- Pruning all 5 fields at once = ~54 distinct files affected (the 50
  source repos overlap, so the file count doesn't multiply; field
  deletions pile onto the same files).
- The 5-file commit cap forces a multi-commit campaign of ~11 commits
  at exact-cap each — substantially larger than the established
  `Phase 9.x.dao.componentprune.cumulative` (10 members across 3-4 DAO
  files in 1 commit) or `Phase 9.x.repo.componentprune.cumulative`
  (2 members across 4 files in 1 commit).

The campaign warrants its own dedicated task entry —
`Phase 9.y.mangainfo.fieldprune.cumulative` — with explicit per-commit
grouping (e.g. AR source repos → EN source repos → ES/IT/PT → FR/RU/TR
→ IN/other → final declarations sweep), allowing iso-strict 5-file caps
and easier rollback if a field turns out to be silently consumed by a
code path the audit missed.

#### Serialization safety pre-flight (for the future field-prune slice)

Both `MangaInfo` and `ChapterItem` carry `@Serializable`. Removing a
field is a binary-incompatible change for any persisted JSON that
already contains the field. The future prune slice MUST:

1. Confirm no `MangaInfo` / `ChapterItem` JSON is persisted to disk in
   a way that survives across app versions (e.g.
   `kotlinx.serialization.json.Json` dumped to a DataStore file or to
   Room as a TEXT column).
2. If persisted, add `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }` to the relevant
   `Json` instance BEFORE removing the field, so old-shape JSON can
   round-trip through the new shape.

This is outside the survey slice's scope.

### Audit methodology cheatsheet (carry-forward for §246)

Additional disciplines learned during this survey:

1. **Named-arg writes vs. accessor reads** — for data-class field
   audits, the bareword `\bX\b` pattern matches every named-arg
   construction (`X = value`) PLUS every type declaration PLUS every
   accessor read. To isolate orphan candidates: grep `\.X\b` separately;
   if it returns zero or near-zero matches while `\bX\b` returns 50+,
   the field is write-only.

2. **`.copy(X = …)` mutation cross-check** — even when `.X` accessor
   reads are zero, a hidden `.copy(X = derived)` rewrite still
   constitutes a write+read coupling that must be flushed. Grep
   `\.copy\([^)]*X` to confirm no hidden mutations before declaring a
   field orphan.

3. **`componentN()` destructuring cross-check** — Kotlin data classes
   auto-generate `component1()`..`componentN()` for positional
   destructuring. If a consumer does `val (a, b, c) = mangaInfo`, the
   accessor reads are positional, not by-name. Grep
   `component\d+\(\)` in proximity to the type name to catch this.
   Confirmed zero destructuring sites on the audited types this slice.

4. **Rework-side disambiguation** — when the rework `:domain` type
   already drops a field (e.g. `Chapter.kt` dropping `chaptersImages`),
   that's a strong signal the field is already known-orphan; the audit
   task becomes "verify the legacy type retains it only for strangler-
   fig parity" rather than "discover whether it's live".

5. **Stale KDoc claims about dropped surfaces** — KDoc in the rework
   `:domain` layer that says "field X dropped in rework" refers to the
   rework type, NOT the underlying legacy Room entity. Always read
   `:shared`'s entity declaration + grep `\bX\b` across all consumers
   before assuming a "rework drops X" KDoc claim retires the legacy
   field too. `SourcesEntity.siteState` was the canonical example
   this slice — the rework `Source` drops it but legacy `HomeScreen.kt`
   still reads it 8 times.

## §246 — Phase 9.y.mangainfo.fieldprune.cumulative — execute deferred MangaInfo field prune (Task #417)

### Slice intent

Execute the deferred orphan-field prune queued by §245's next-candidate
block. The §245 model-layer survey flagged 4 write-only `MangaInfo`
fields as orphans; per-field zero-read re-verification at the start of
this campaign expanded the list to **6 fields** after `artist` and `tags`
came back clean too (`.artist\b` / `.tags\b` accessor reads returned
zero matches on the rework `:domain`/`:presentation`/`:ui` stack and on
every legacy consumer of the strangler-fig'd type). The final 6-field
set:

- `ratingCount: String` — listed in §245
- `otherNames: String` — listed in §245
- `favoritesCount: String` — listed in §245
- `yearOfProduction: String` — listed in §245
- `artist: String` — discovered during Slice 1 audit (§245 missed it)
- `tags: List<String>` — discovered during Slice 1 audit (§245 missed it)

The `ChapterItem.chaptersImages: List<ChapterImage>` orphan from §245
is NOT pruned in this campaign — it remains queued for a future
dedicated `Phase 9.y.chapteritem.fieldprune` slice. Scoping this
campaign to MangaInfo only keeps the strangler-fig mapper changes
homogeneous (single mapper, single data class, single rework `:domain`
type) and avoids touching ChapterItem's distinct reacher graph.

### Strategy: defaults-first prune

Per the §245 deferral rationale, each field deletion would have required
~54 file-touches in a single commit (50 source repos + mapper +
HandelDataClasses + declaration). The 5-file commit cap forced a
multi-commit defaults-first sequencing:

1. **Slice 1 (prep)** — add default values to the 6 orphan fields on
   the legacy `:shared` `MangaInfo` data class so the ~46 writer call
   sites keep compiling while successor slices drop the named-arg
   writes batch by batch. Same commit drops the 6 fields from the
   rework `:domain` `MangaDetails` (17 → 11 fields) and removes the 6
   mapper lines from `:data` `LegacyMangaInfo.toDomain()`. 3 files.
2. **Slices 2-11 (writers)** — drop the orphan named-arg writes from
   the source-repository constructor sites in groups of 5 files. The
   actual file groupings turned out to be slightly different from the
   §245 prediction (ar/ → en/ → es/it/pt → fr/ru/tr → in/other) due to
   how the per-file constructor sites distributed; the final
   sequencing was ar/ → ar+en/ → en/ → en+es/ → es+more → tr/ru/pt →
   pt/fr/ru/it/in → in+fr → 10 slices total (Slices 2-11), each
   ≤5 files.
3. **Slice 12 (final drop)** — remove the 6 field declarations from
   `MangaInfo.kt` itself, restoring the data class to its 11-field
   target shape (matching `MangaDetails`). Compile gate surfaced 2
   missed writer sites in `:shared/core/util/data_classes/Handel
   DataClasses.kt` (`MangaItem.toMangaInfo` at line 88+ and
   `SavedMangaEntity.toMangaInfo` at line 193+) that the audit's
   source-repository-only file scope missed; both patched in the same
   slice. 2 files.

The defaults-first sequencing means every intermediate slice was a
strict no-op behaviour change: the data class still carried the 6
fields with default `""`/`emptyList()` placeholders even as writer
sites stopped naming them. Build gates (Android + Desktop + iOS Arm64
+ iOS SimulatorArm64) ran green at every slice boundary.

### Audit honesty: §245 undercount reconciliation

§245's per-field findings table listed 4 MangaInfo orphans
(`ratingCount`, `otherNames`, `favoritesCount`, `yearOfProduction`).
The Slice 1 per-field re-audit added `artist` and `tags` to the list.

- `artist`: the §245 audit appears to have used the same regex
  template as for the 4 confirmed fields but stopped after 4 rows
  rather than enumerating all 17 MangaInfo fields. Grepping `\.artist`
  during Slice 1 returned zero accessor reads across the entire tree.
- `tags`: same explanation. `\.tags` returned zero accessor reads.
  The §245 table mentions "the rework `:domain` types already
  anticipate this" — and `MangaDetails` indeed did not carry `tags`
  or `artist`, but §245 didn't surface them as the survey's specific
  output, only as the rework's pre-existing strip.

Future model-layer surveys should enumerate ALL fields of each audited
type rather than stopping at "found enough orphans" — even when the
rework counterpart already drops the field, the survey should record
the legacy-side orphan status for sequencing.

### Serialization safety post-flight

Pre-flight (§245) required confirming no persisted JSON of the
8-field shape exists across app upgrades. This campaign's pre-flight
re-verified:

- `ChapterItem` is NOT persisted as JSON to DataStore or Room

  future-proofing / in-memory round-tripping only; no on-disk corpus
  of the 8-field shape exists.
