  in-memory `ChapterItem` to disk — it maps `SavedChapterEntity`
  (Room row) → `ChapterItem` (in-memory). Removing the
  `chaptersImages = …` block from the mapper body discards 1
  no-consumer in-memory field; the Room row's `localImagePaths`
  remains stored and retrievable via `SavedChapterEntity`
  directly when callers need page paths.

Therefore the 1-field removal + the `ChapterImage` data class
deletion is binary-compatible with all existing user installs. No
`ignoreUnknownKeys = true` migration was needed.

### Audit methodology cheatsheet update — discipline #16

Carrying forward §246 disciplines #1-#15. Adding the new discipline
discovered during Slice 2:

16. **Coupled-dead type retirement — drop the type along with its
    only anchor** — Slice 2's `chaptersImages` field drop also
    revealed `me.manga.kira.domain.model.ChapterImage` had zero
    remaining callers. The naive "field-prune only" scope would have
    left an orphan declaration to be cleaned up in a future slice;
    instead, the type was deleted in the SAME slice. Discipline: for
    every field-prune of a typed field (i.e. the field's type is a
    project-defined ADT, not a stdlib primitive), grep `import
    <fqn-of-type>` and `<typename>(` (constructor calls) across the
    entire `*.kt` tree AFTER the field drop. If both return 0, the
    type itself is coupled-dead and should be retired in the same
    slice. Same-name disambiguation is mandatory — confirm the type
    is not shadowed by an identically-named declaration in another
    package.

## §248 — Phase 9.y.coreplatform.modelsurvey.cumulative — :core + :platform model-layer null-result survey (Task #419)

### Why this section

§247's next-candidate block advances to entry (6) — the
`:core/.../model/*.kt` + `:platform/.../model/*.kt` model-layer
survey, mirroring §245's `:shared` methodology on the rework
modules. With §245-§247 having closed the `:shared` model-layer
field-prune campaign (118 symbols dropped + 1 coupled-dead type
retired), the question for this slice is: *do the rework `:core`
+ `:platform` modules have any orphan value-object declarations
or orphan fields that escaped the §245 sweep because they live
outside `:shared`?*

This entry documents the survey scope, per-declaration findings,
the null-result verdict, the OCP-extension-reserve architectural
commentary on `AppError`, and the advance of the next-candidate
queue to entry (7) — sealed/enum member survey.

### Audit scope

The "model-layer" filter targets value-object-shaped declarations
(data class, sealed class, enum, top-level `const val`/`val`).
SPI facade interfaces (`Logger`, `FeatureFlagProvider`,
`DispatcherProvider`, `NotificationPresenter`, `PushTokenProvider`,
all 24 `:platform` facades, etc.) are out-of-scope because their
semantics are defined by the receiver abstraction, not by data
shape.

Applying that filter to the directory inventory of both modules:

**`:core` in-scope (3 files)**:

- `core/.../result/AppResult.kt` — sealed `AppResult<out T>` with
  `Success(value)` + `Failure(error)`, plus 7 extension fns
  (`map`, `flatMap`, `onSuccess`, `onFailure`, `recover`,
  `appSuccess`, `appFailure`).
- `core/.../error/AppError.kt` — sealed `AppError` hierarchy:
  5 nested sealeds (`Network`, `Storage`, `Validation`, `Auth`,
  `Platform`) with 3-4 data-class subclasses each, plus 2 direct
  data-class subclasses (`Cancelled`, `Unexpected`). Abstract
  `cause: Throwable?` on the root.
- `core/.../util/heap/DeviceTier.kt` — enum
  `DeviceTier { LOW, MID, HIGH }` + 2 `internal const val Long`
  thresholds (`TIER_LOW_MAX_BYTES`, `TIER_MID_MAX_BYTES`) +
  top-level `fun classifyByTotalRam(totalRamBytes: Long): DeviceTier`.

**`:platform` in-scope (1 file)**:

- `platform/.../cbz/CbzSettings.kt` — data class `CbzSettings`
  with 5 fields (`maxParallelDecode`, `maxParallelCompress`,
  `regionDecodeThreshold`, `samplingThreshold`, `webpQuality`).

**Out-of-scope (SPI facade interfaces, surveyed and confirmed
not model-shaped)**: `:core` Logger / FeatureFlagProvider /
DispatcherProvider / IoDispatcher (expect val); `:platform` all
24 facades under toast/, intent/, filesystem/, locale/, storage/,
connectivity/, notification/, push/, image/, jobs/, cbz/CbzWriter
+CbzReader+getCbzSettings, device/DeviceTierProbe, review/,
update/, consent/, ads/, analytics/, crash/, remote/, version/.

### Audit methodology

3-pass receiver-anchored grep on every member of each in-scope
declaration:

| Pass | Pattern | Catches |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `\.X\(` / `\.field` | dotted-receiver access (most common) |
| 2 | `\bX\b` | bare-identifier references (rare for fields, common for type names in `when` arms) |
| 3 | `::X` | member references (very rare for value-object members) |

For sealed types, the audit ALSO verifies that the parent type
itself appears in exhaustive `when (it)` blocks across consumers,
because a parent-level `is AppError.Foo ->` arm catches every
subclass of `Foo` uniformly — orphan-looking subclasses can still
be LIVE-via-parent if any branch consumes the parent type.

### Per-declaration findings

| Declaration | Members | Reacher status | Verdict |
|-------------|---------|----------------|---------|
| `AppResult.Success(value)` | 1 field | Consumed via `is AppResult.Success` arms in `:data` + `:presentation` reacher graphs | LIVE — keep |
| `AppResult.Failure(error)` | 1 field | Consumed via `is AppResult.Failure` arms across same graphs | LIVE — keep |
| `AppResult` ext fns × 7 | map/flatMap/onSuccess/onFailure/recover/appSuccess/appFailure | All called via `.map { }` / `.flatMap { }` / etc. across `:data` repository impls + `:presentation` VMs | LIVE — keep |
| `AppError.cause: Throwable?` | abstract root field | Every subclass overrides it; consumed by exception-chain logging in `:data` mappers | LIVE — keep |
| `AppError.Network` (parent) + 4 subclasses | NoConnectivity / Timeout / Http(statusCode) / Serialization | Parent consumed by 3 `:ui` toUserMessage `is AppError.Network ->` arms; NoConnectivity/Timeout/Http have producers in `MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl` + `ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl`; Serialization is doc-only (KDoc reserves it) | LIVE-via-parent — keep (sealed-OCP) |
| `AppError.Storage` (parent) + 3 subclasses | NotFound(key) / Constraint(description) / Io | Parent consumed by 3 `:ui` toUserMessage arms; Io is LIVE via `LibraryRepositoryImpl.runCatchingAsResult` + `LibraryViewModel.kt:276-277` producers; NotFound + Constraint are OCP reserves | LIVE-via-parent — keep (sealed-OCP) |
| `AppError.Validation` (parent) + 3 subclasses | Required(field) / OutOfRange(field) / Format(field) | Parent consumed by 3 `:ui` toUserMessage arms; no subclass producers in current codebase BUT 3-arg constructors document the user-facing field axis — OCP reserves for future form-validation slices | LIVE-via-parent — keep (sealed-OCP) |

| `AppError.Platform` (parent) + 2 subclasses | PermissionDenied(permission) / FeatureUnavailable(feature) | Parent consumed by 3 `:ui` toUserMessage arms; no subclass producers in current codebase BUT subclass field axes (permission / feature) document KMP cross-platform failure modes — OCP reserves for future per-platform error-mapping | LIVE-via-parent — keep (sealed-OCP) |
| `AppError.Cancelled` | 0 fields beyond `cause` | Consumed by 3 `:ui` toUserMessage arms; no current `:data` producer (cooperative coroutine cancellation typically rethrows `CancellationException` unchanged per Kotlin contract, but the named branch reserves the explicit `AppResult.Failure` path for slices that need to surface cancellation as a result rather than an exception) | LIVE-via-consumer — keep |
| `AppError.Unexpected(message)` | 1 field | Consumed by 3 `:ui` toUserMessage arms + produced by 5 `:data` fallback sites (`MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl.kt:64,99,116` + `ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:79,121,133`) | LIVE — keep |
| `DeviceTier { LOW, MID, HIGH }` | 3 enum variants | All 3 consumed by `platform/.../cbz/getCbzSettings.kt` `when (tier)` branch | LIVE — keep |
| `TIER_LOW_MAX_BYTES`, `TIER_MID_MAX_BYTES` | 2 `internal const val Long` | Both consumed by `classifyByTotalRam` body in the same file | LIVE — keep |
| `classifyByTotalRam(totalRamBytes)` | top-level fn | Reached by all 3 `:platform` DeviceTierProbe actuals (AndroidDeviceTierProbe, DesktopDeviceTierProbe, IosDeviceTierProbe) | LIVE — keep |
| `CbzSettings(...)` | 5 fields | All 5 consumed by `shared/androidMain/.../OptimizedCbzManager.kt` across 11 reacher sites (lines 55, 56, 359, 360, 362, 363, 385, 391, 392, 438) | LIVE — keep |

### Verdict — NULL-RESULT survey

**No prunes recommended.** All 4 in-scope value-object
declarations across `:core` + `:platform` are fully live across
their member surface.

The AppError survey deserves additional architectural commentary
because the 3-pass grep surfaced ~12 subclass-level members with
ZERO `.kt` constructor producers (Network.Serialization,
Storage.{NotFound, Constraint}, Validation.{Required, OutOfRange,
Format}, Auth.{NotSignedIn, Forbidden, TokenExpired},
Platform.{PermissionDenied, FeatureUnavailable}, Cancelled). At
first read these look like classic orphan subclasses fit for
pruning — but the class-level KDoc on `AppError.kt:12-15`
explicitly documents the design:

> "SOLID rationale:
>  - ISP: subclasses are narrow and named after the failure
>    category, not the failing technology.
>  - OCP: **extending the hierarchy is allowed (sealed → callers
>    must exhaustively handle new cases), modifying existing
>    subclasses is not** — adding behavior should produce a new
>    subclass."

This is an explicit **sealed-OCP extension-reserve posture**.
The orphan-looking subclasses are pre-positioned so future
`:data` error-translation slices can produce them without:

1. Touching the sealed root (would force re-audit of every `when`
   site).
2. Touching the existing exhaustive `when (error)` consumers in
   the 3 `:ui` toUserMessage extensions (the
   `is AppError.Network ->` parent arm absorbs new subclasses
   uniformly).
3. Modifying existing subclasses (per the documented "modifying
   existing subclasses is not [allowed]" rule).

The parent sealed types (Network, Storage, Validation, Auth,
Platform) are LIVE via consumer arms in the 3 `:ui`
`AppError.toUserMessage()` extension functions:

- `ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt:1165-1173`
- `ui/.../details/DetailsScreen.kt:512-520`
- `ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt:1141-1149`

The arms match at the parent level (`is AppError.Network`,
`is AppError.Storage`, etc.), not the subclass level. This means
future subclasses slot in WITHOUT changing the exhaustive `when`
— Kotlin's compiler considers `is AppError.Network` exhaustive
for the Network sealed because the Network root is sealed and
the arm catches every subclass.

**Pruning these subclasses would VIOLATE the documented
OCP-extension-reserve design.** It would also recreate the same
`:data`-error-mapping gap that future slices need to fill: when a
Storage.NotFound error path emerges (e.g., a new "manga not found
in saved library" lookup), the rework system needs a typed slot
for it rather than collapsing every failure into Storage.Io or
Unexpected. The current state is a feature, not a bug.

This commentary parallels but does NOT contradict §247's
coupled-dead `ChapterImage` retirement: the difference is that
`ChapterImage` had a documented "retire-when-coupled-dead" status
(its only field was orphan-pending-prune, and the type itself
existed only to populate that one field), whereas AppError
subclasses have a documented "pre-position for future producers"
status. Both designs are honored by the SAME audit discipline
(#15 — audit ALL reacher-graph files including subclass
producers AND consumer `when` blocks) — the differing verdicts
follow from the differing class-header documentation, not from
inconsistent application of the discipline.

### Audit-honesty notes

- All 4 in-scope files were re-read in full this slice.
  AppError.kt's class-header KDoc (lines 12-15) explicitly
  documents the sealed-OCP extension reserve — this is not
  retroactive justification.
- The 3 `:ui` `toUserMessage()` extensions were enumerated by
  `grep -l 'AppError\.toUserMessage'` (3 files, all in
  `ui/src/commonMain/`) and each verified to consume the parent
  sealed types at the `is AppError.Foo ->` arm level, NOT the
  subclass arm level. Verification was per-file, not summary —
  the audit reads the `when (error)` block in each of the 3
  files to confirm.
- The CbzSettings audit honored discipline #15 by enumerating
  ALL 5 field reachers (11 sites across one consumer file) rather
  than stopping at the first reacher per field. Pattern matches
  the §245/§247 disciplines.
- Shadow legacy files exist in `:shared` for `DeviceTier`
  (`shared/.../core/util/heap/DeviceTier.kt` + `.android.kt` +
  `.desktop.kt` + `.ios.kt`) alongside the rework `:core`
  versions. The shadow files are out-of-scope for THIS slice
  (which targets ONLY the rework `:core`/`:platform` modules); a
  future `Phase 9.x.deviceshadow.retire` slice can drop them
  once a per-call-site reacher audit confirms no legacy consumer
  reaches them. Flagged in the next-candidate block.

### Action taken

**None.** No source files changed. This slice is audit-only — it
records the null-result finding, codifies the AppError
sealed-OCP-extension-reserve commentary for future surveys, and
advances the next-candidate queue.

## §249 — Phase 9.y.sealedenum.membersurvey.cumulative + Phase 9.y.adstate.retire — :shared sealed/enum member survey + 1 orphan retire (Tasks #420 + #421)

### Why this section

§248's next-candidate block advanced to entry (7) — the
sealed/enum member survey across the broader `:shared` surface.
Where §245 covered `:shared` value-object data classes and §248
covered `:core` + `:platform` value objects, this slice fills
the last remaining model-layer gap: sealed-class subclass
declarations and enum-entry declarations in `:shared` whose
runtime reachability depends on per-call-site `when (...)`
exhaustiveness rather than direct producer/consumer reaches.

Unlike §248's null-result, this slice surfaced ONE actionable
orphan — `shared/.../ad_mob/AdState.kt` — and the close-out is
a 2-commit cadence (plan + retire-with-docs) mirroring the
§371/§372 single-file precedent. The remaining ~15 sealed/enum
declarations across `:shared` are LIVE; deferred Tier-B
"shadow-legacy" and Tier-C "coupled-dead" candidates are flagged
for separate dedicated slices.

### Audit scope

The "sealed/enum member" filter targets:

- Sealed-class subclass declarations (`sealed class Foo` →
  `class Bar : Foo()` / `data object Baz : Foo()`).
- Enum declarations (`enum class X { A, B, C }`) including
  enum-class extension functions/properties.

Applied to `:shared/commonMain/.../**/*.kt`, the survey
identified 20 candidate files spanning ad_mob/, core/ads/,
core/util/heap/, core/util/jobs/, core/util/remote/,
core/util/consent/, presentation/features/whatsnew/,
sources_repositry/data/MangaSource.kt, presentation/features
/library/.../LibraryQueryFilters.kt, and ~10 other isolated
sealed/enum declarations.

### Audit methodology

Same 3-pass receiver-anchored grep as §245/§247/§248:

| Pass | Pattern | Catches |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | qualified-name (`AdState.Idle`, `Language.AR`, etc.) | dotted-receiver/enum-entry references |
| 2 | bare-identifier (`\bAdState\b` etc., filtered) | `import`-line + `when (it) -> is Foo ->` arms |
| 3 | `import.*<package>` | catches import-only usages + cross-validates the package's reach surface |

Each subtype is LIVE if Pass 1 OR Pass 2 yields at least one
runtime-reachable consumer (excluding `migration/` audit-doc
references which are historical artifacts).

### Tier classification

Survey results partitioned into 3 tiers:

- **Tier-A LIVE** (16 types): orthogonally reachable across
  `:shared` + `:platform` + rework modules. Examples:
  `MangaSource` enum (41 entries, all reached by source
  registry); `Language` enum (9 entries inside MangaSource
  constructor); `WhatsNewPage` enum + factory chain (live via
  `WhatsNewViewModel.observe()`); `LibraryQueryFilter` sealed
  (live via filter pipeline in legacy LibraryViewModel);
  `String.COLORS` ext + `Color.isDark()` ext (live via per-
  source color rendering in `:ui`); `Source.kt` interface +
  3 actuals; `SourceLanguage` enum; `MangaStatusEnum`; ~7
  other `:shared` sealed/enum members each reached by ≥1
  runtime consumer. KEEP.

- **Tier-B SHADOW-LEGACY** (5 deferred files): `:shared` legacy
  declarations whose rework `:core`/`:platform` counterparts
  exist but the legacy files remain on disk. Includes
  `shared/.../core/jobs/BackgroundJobScheduler.kt`,
  `shared/.../core/util/heap/DeviceTier.kt`,
  `shared/.../core/util/consent/ConsentFlowClient.kt`,
  legacy `shared/.../core/ads/AdProvider.kt`,
  `shared/.../core/util/remote/RemoteDocStore.kt`. These are
  NOT pruned in this slice — they require per-call-site
  reacher audits to confirm no legacy `:shared` consumer
  still reaches them, then a coordinated retire campaign.
  Deferred to `Phase 9.x.coreshadow.retire` (separate
  multi-slice campaign).

- **Tier-C COUPLED-DEAD** (7 files in WhatsNew legacy chain):
  the legacy `:shared/.../presentation/features/whatsnew/model/`
  + `.../widgets/MediaType.kt` chain is coupled-dead — the
  rework `:domain` `WhatsNewPage` + `:data`
  `WhatsNewRepositoryImpl` already replace the legacy model
  layer end-to-end, but the legacy files remain. Includes
  `WhatsNewPagesEnumD.kt`, `WhatsNewPage.kt`,
  `WhatsNewLink.kt`, `MediaContent.kt`, `MediaType.kt`,
  `WhatsNewPageFactory.kt`, sample-data file. Deferred to
  `Phase 9.x.whatsnew.legacymodels.retire` (single multi-file
  retire slice).

- **Tier-D ACTIONABLE** (1 file): `shared/.../ad_mob/AdState.kt`
  — pure orphan, zero consumers, sole inhabitant of the
  `ad_mob/` package. Retired in this slice.

### Per-file finding — Tier-D AdState retire

`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ad_mob/AdState.kt`
(33 lines) declares:

- `sealed class AdState` + 5 subclasses
  (`Idle`/`Loading`/`Ready`/`Showing`/`Error(message, code?)`)
  + 7 boolean ext-props (`isIdle`/`isLoading`/`isReady`/
  `isShowing`/`isError`/`canLoad`/`canShow`).
- `sealed class AdShowResult` + 3 subclasses
  (`RewardEarned(type, amount)`/`Dismissed`/`Failed(error)`).
- `sealed class AdLoadResult` + 2 subclasses
  (`Success`/`Failed(error, code?)`).

3-pass grep verdict:

| Pass | Pattern | Hits outside declaration + `migration/` |
|------|---------|------------------------------------------|
| 1 | `AdState.Idle`, `AdState.Loading`, ..., `AdShowResult.RewardEarned`, ..., `AdLoadResult.Success`, ... | **0** |
| 2 | `\bAdState\b`, `\bAdShowResult\b`, `\bAdLoadResult\b` | **0** |
| 3 | `import.*ad_mob` | **0** |

**Verdict: WHOLE-FILE ORPHAN.** Zero producers, zero consumers,
zero imports. The file is the sole inhabitant of the `ad_mob/`
package; deleting it retires the package directory entirely.

### Why the orphan exists

The legacy `AdShowResult`/`AdLoadResult` pair was replaced by
the rework `:core/ads/AdProvider.kt` `sealed class AdResult`
during Phase 5.z.4 (Task #191 — `Phase 5.z.4: AdProvider to
:platform`). The Phase-5 swap moved the consumer surface
(`AdProvider` interface + 3 `:platform` actuals) to the rework
modules but left the legacy `:shared/.../ad_mob/AdState.kt`
file behind. The 7 ext-props on `AdState` (`.isIdle`, etc.)
were never imported from outside the declaration file — they
were "convenience helpers" written defensively at the
declaration site but never referenced.

The rework `AdProvider.kt:7` does contain a `KDoc` reference to
the legacy package, but that reference points to the original
Android app's `app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/ad_mob/
AdCoordinator.kt` (the production legacy under `yami-manga-apk-
main/`), NOT to this `:shared` orphan file. Confirmed by
reading the KDoc verbatim — the path begins with `app/src/
main/java/` (the Android-only legacy tree), not
`shared/src/commonMain/` (the KMP `:shared` tree this orphan
lives in).

### Why this is NOT Tier-B shadow-legacy

Tier-B "shadow-legacy" files (BackgroundJobScheduler, DeviceTier,
ConsentFlowClient, RemoteDocStore, legacy AdProvider) are
**reachable from legacy `:shared` consumers** that have not yet
been retired — those legacy consumers still exist on disk and
still compile. Pruning a Tier-B file would break legacy
compilation. They require a coordinated retire campaign that
drops the consumer first, then the shadow file.

`ad_mob/AdState.kt` has **zero legacy consumers** — the 3-pass
grep confirmed zero `:shared` consumers reach it. It can be
deleted in isolation without breaking any legacy compilation
target.

### Audit discipline reinforced

This slice extends discipline #15 (audit ALL reacher-graph
files) and #17 (sealed-OCP-extension-reserve recognition)
with a NEW discipline:

> **Discipline #18 — Tier-D actionable-orphan discovery
> requires whole-file deletion of the package directory if
> the orphan is the sole inhabitant.**
> When the 3-pass grep confirms a sealed/enum declaration is
> a whole-file orphan AND that file is the sole inhabitant of
> its package directory, the retire MUST delete the directory
> alongside the file. Leaving an empty package directory
> creates a maintenance footgun (future IDE navigation lands
> on an empty dir; future audits re-survey the empty package
> for declarations and waste cycles). This slice retires
> `ad_mob/` directory entirely by deleting its sole file.

Discipline #18 is a corollary of discipline #15: where #15
says "audit ALL reacher-graph files," #18 says "audit
ALL package-directory siblings TOO — if the orphan is the
last file in its package, the directory itself becomes
orphan and must be removed alongside the source."

## §250 — Phase 9.y.coreshadow.invertedclassification.docs — campaign blocker: §249's Tier-B "shadow-legacy" classification is INVERTED — single-file docs commit pausing the retire campaign pending user direction (Task #423; supersedes §249 queue item (8))

### Why this section exists

§249's next-candidate block recommended item (8) — a 5-slice
`Phase 9.x.coreshadow.retire` campaign retiring 5 alleged
"Tier-B shadow-legacy" files:

- `shared/.../core/jobs/BackgroundJobScheduler.kt`
- `shared/.../core/util/heap/DeviceTier.kt`
- `shared/.../core/consent/ConsentFlowClient.kt`
- `shared/.../core/ads/AdProvider.kt`
- `shared/.../core/remote/RemoteDocStore.kt`

The §249 framing assumed these files were dead-on-the-vine
copies left behind by Phase 5.z.*'s relocation of the SPI
surface to `:platform/.../platform/*`. Pre-flight verification
for the campaign instead surfaced the OPPOSITE conclusion: the
legacy `:shared` facades are LIVE in the rework Koin graph,
and the rework `:platform` SPIs are the unused shadow.

Per the standing block-and-ask trigger (compile risk +
observable behavior change), the campaign is paused. This
single-file docs commit records the binding-graph evidence,
revises §249's classification, and surfaces the architectural
decision to the user.

`me.manga.kira.platform.consent.ConsentFlowClient`,
NOT `me.manga.kira.platform.jobs.BackgroundJobScheduler`,
NOT `me.manga.kira.platform.remote.RemoteDocStore` —
the rework `:platform` versions are imported nowhere.)

**Receipt 2 — `:shared` PlatformModule.android.kt binds the
LEGACY versions in the live Koin module:**

```kotlin
// shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/PlatformModule.android.kt:108-125
single { BackgroundJobScheduler(androidContext()) }    // ← LEGACY
single { RemoteDocStore() }                            // ← LEGACY
single { AdProvider(androidContext()) }                // ← LEGACY
single { ConsentFlowClient(androidContext()) }         // ← LEGACY
```

**Receipt 3 — `KoinInitializer.kt` (the rework Koin bootstrap
called by every host) includes the legacy `platformModule()`:**

```kotlin
// shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/KoinInitializer.kt:42
modules(allSharedModules() + platformModule() + extraModules)
//                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
//      Resolves to PlatformModule.{android,desktop,ios}.kt's
//      `actual fun platformModule()` — binds the 5 LEGACY facades.
```

`extraModules` is `allReworkModules()` (passed by each host's
`initKoin(allReworkModules()) { … }` per the KDoc at
`KoinInitializer.kt:15-18`). `allReworkModules()` is defined
in `composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/
ReworkModules.kt` and lists 15 feature modules but NO
`platformReworkModule`.

**Receipt 4 — Zero `:platform` SPI imports anywhere outside
`:platform` itself:**

```
Grep me\.manga\.yamiapk\.platform\. in composeApp/ → 0 hits
Grep me\.manga\.yamiapk\.platform\. in shared/    → 0 hits
Grep platformReworkModule in composeApp/          → 0 hits
```

The only `me.manga.kira.platform.*` imports in the whole
repository are the ~5 internal cross-package imports INSIDE
`:platform` itself (e.g., `:platform`'s
`DesktopConnectivityObserver` importing `:platform`'s
`ConnectivityObserver`). The rework `:platform` module has
107 source files (`git ls-files platform/src/` count), every
single one of which is unreachable from the live composition
root.

### Inverted classification

§249 said:

> Tier-B (5 files) — SHADOW-LEGACY orphans:
>   shared/.../core/jobs/BackgroundJobScheduler.kt
>   shared/.../core/util/heap/DeviceTier.kt
>   shared/.../core/consent/ConsentFlowClient.kt
>   shared/.../core/ads/AdProvider.kt
>   shared/.../core/remote/RemoteDocStore.kt

The evidence above demonstrates that these 5 files are
NOT shadow-legacy. They are LIVE. The 5 files in
`platform/.../platform/{jobs,consent,ads,remote,device}/`
(plus the other 20+ SPI surfaces and 80+ actuals in
`:platform`) are the shadow — the relocation Phase 5.z.*
performed created the SPI module but never wired its
bindings into Koin.

Phase 5.z.* (Tasks #188-#194 — completed) created the
`:platform/.../platform/*` interfaces and `expect/actual`
declarations. It did NOT create a `platformReworkModule`
that binds them, did NOT register such a module with
`KoinInitializer.kt`, and did NOT remove the legacy
bindings from `:shared/.../di/PlatformModule.*`.

Result: every consumer that needs `AdProvider`,
`ConsentFlowClient`, `BackgroundJobScheduler`, etc., still
resolves the LEGACY `:shared/.../core/*` instance. The
rework `:platform` module compiles, links, and ships in
the binary — but no instance is ever constructed at
runtime because no Koin definition references it.

### Two paths forward (decision required from user)

**Path A — Complete the Phase 5.z.* migration**

Create `platformReworkModule.{android,desktop,ios}.kt` in
`composeApp/.../di/` (or in `:platform` itself if the
module's actual files can be made `internal`). Each
target's actual rebinds:

```kotlin
single<me.manga.kira.platform.ads.AdProvider> {
    AndroidAdProvider(androidContext(), …)
}
single<me.manga.kira.platform.consent.ConsentFlowClient> {
    AndroidConsentFlowClient(androidContext(), …)
}
// … (15-20 SPIs to rebind per target)
```

Then:
1. Append `platformReworkModule()` to `allReworkModules()`.
2. Migrate every legacy `:shared` consumer that takes the
   legacy `me.manga.kira.core.ads.AdProvider` to take
   the rework `me.manga.kira.platform.ads.AdProvider`
   constructor argument (or use case interface).
3. Once no consumer references the legacy facade, drop the
   legacy binding from `:shared/.../di/PlatformModule.*`.
4. Retire the legacy file (`shared/.../core/ads/AdProvider.kt`).
5. Repeat for the other 4 Tier-B candidates.

Estimated scope: 20-30 commits at the standing 5-file cap,
distributed across 5-7 sub-phases (one per facade). Highest
cumulative impact (retires both the legacy `:shared`
versions AND closes the architectural gap from Phase 5.z.*).

**Path B — Retire `:platform` as the unused shadow**

Delete `:platform/src/{android,desktop,ios,common}Main/
kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/platform/*` — the unbound SPI
surface and its 80+ actuals. Drop the `:platform` module
declaration from `settings.gradle.kts`. Keep the legacy
`:shared/.../core/*` facades as the production code path.

Estimated scope: 1-3 commits (single module deletion).
Lowest disruption. Cost: throws away the Phase 5.z.*
work (Tasks #165-#195) without realizing the layer-boundary
benefit it was supposed to provide. The legacy `:shared`
module becomes the permanent home of platform SPIs, which
contradicts §61-§62's "Clean Architecture target: :platform
owns expect/actual" intent.

### Recommendation

The author recommends Path A. The Phase 5.z.* work was a
multi-week investment intended to lift platform SPIs out
of `:shared` into a dedicated module that other layers
(`:data`, `:presentation`) can depend on without inheriting
`:shared`'s legacy weight. Retiring `:platform` (Path B)
abandons that benefit and locks in the legacy structure.

That said, Path A is a large undertaking. The user may
reasonably prefer to pause the architectural rework here
(at the end of the Phase 7.x feature-port campaign,
which is COMPLETE per the §249 cumulative tally —
all 14 rework screens have shipped, all legacy screen
routes have been swapped, all reachable orphan-retire
slices have been executed) and accept the current state
as the steady-state codebase.

### Why this discovery surfaced now and not in §249

§249's audit method (3-pass receiver-anchored grep for
sealed-class subclass and enum-entry references) is
optimized for declarative-symbol reachability. It correctly
identified `AdState.kt` as a sealed-class orphan with zero
constructor calls. But the Tier-B classification step
(noting which `:shared/.../core/*` files have a "shadow"
counterpart in `:platform/.../platform/*`) was conducted by
filename-pattern matching, not by Koin-binding tracing.

The filename pattern (LEGACY at `:shared/.../core/X/X.kt`
vs. SHADOW at `:platform/.../platform/X/X.kt`) is the
correct visual cue for "two files exist with the same
purpose." But it gives no information about WHICH file is
the live one. Determining liveness requires tracing the
Koin binding graph from the composition root —
`KoinInitializer.kt:42` → `platformModule()` actuals →
which import paths the actuals use.

§249 inverted the classification because it didn't trace.
This commit's §250 corrects that.

### Audit discipline reinforced

This finding extends disciplines #15 (audit ALL
reacher-graph files) and #18 (sole-inhabitant package
retire) with a NEW discipline:

> **Discipline #19 — Tier classification of facade/SPI
> duplicates requires Koin-binding (or equivalent
> composition-root) tracing, not filename-pattern
> matching.**
> When two files exist with the same name in `:shared`
> and `:platform` (or any other layer pair), the audit
> MUST trace the live composition root (`KoinInitializer.
> kt:42` → `platformModule()` actuals → `import`
> statements) to determine which file is bound and
> resolvable at runtime. Filename-pattern matching alone
> is INSUFFICIENT: a file can compile, link, and ship in
> the binary while never being instantiated, because
> Koin (or any DI container) only constructs what is
> declaratively bound.

Concrete application: before retiring any `:shared/.../
core/X.kt` based on the existence of a `:platform/.../
platform/X.kt` counterpart, verify:
1. `platformModule()` for each target host (Android,
   Desktop, iOS) imports the `:platform` version (not the
   `:shared` version).
2. `allReworkModules()` includes a `platformReworkModule`
   that binds the `:platform` SPI to its actual.
3. Each consumer's constructor parameter takes the
   `:platform` type, not the `:shared` type.

If any of (1)-(3) fails, the `:platform` counterpart is the
shadow — not the `:shared` original.

### Transitive LIVE chain

that data source is also transitively LIVE:

|---|---|---|

### Survey methodology (applies disciplines #19 + #20 in full)

Single grep across `composeApp/src/` for the FQN-import pattern `^import me\.manga\.yamiapk\.\S+\.viewmodel\.\w+ViewModel`. Each match is a confirmed reacher. Bare-identifier matches inside same-package siblings are not needed for VMs because every VM is referenced from composeApp (a different module), which requires the FQN import.

Per **discipline #19** (Koin-binding tracing): each VM's `viewModel { ... }` Koin binding lives in `:shared/.../di/SharedModule.kt`, which is included by `allSharedModules()` in `KoinInitializer.kt:42` — so all 12 VMs are present in the live Koin graph regardless of consumer count. Discipline #19 alone cannot retire any VM; the consumer-side grep is required.

Per **discipline #20** (rework `:data` strangler-fig import check): VMs are presentation-layer types and are NEVER imported by rework `:data/*RepositoryImpl.kt` (verified by FQN grep across `:data/src/`, zero matches). Discipline #20 is a pure check this slice — no VM passes through rework `:data`.

### Why every legacy VM remains LIVE

Every legacy VM backs a legacy route that has NOT been swap-retired yet. The Phase 7.x swap campaign (Tasks #286-#306) ported the rework presentation/UI layer in parallel with the legacy stack but stopped short of route-swap retirement for the following live routes:

- `Screen.Home` → `HomeScreenRoute.kt` (reaches `ChaptersViewModel`, `MangaViewModel`, `HomeViewModel`, `RepoSettingsViewModel`)
- `Screen.MangaDetails` → `MangaDetailsScreenRoute.kt` (reaches `MangaDerailsViewModel`, `HomeViewModel`)
- `Screen.LibraryManga` → `LibraryMangaScreenRoute.kt` (reaches `HomeViewModel`, `LibraryDetailsViewModel`) + `LibraryMangaScreen.kt` (reaches `LibraryDetailsViewModel`)
- `Screen.ChapterImages` / `Screen.Reader` → `ChapterImagesScreenRoute.kt` + `ReaderScreen.kt` (reaches `SharedChaptersViewModel`, `HistoryViewModel`, `ReaderViewModel`)
- `Screen.WebView` → `WebViewScreenRoute.kt` (reaches `WebViewViewModel`)
- `Screen.Settings` (legacy entry point at `App.kt:225`) reaches `SettingsViewModel`
- `Screen.Library` redirect-hook in `LibraryScreenRoute.kt:14` reaches `WhatsNewViewModel` (gated per §239)

The route-swap retirement is its own campaign axis (Phase 9.x.routeswap.*) which has only begun for a subset of routes (Library, Statistics, About, Complaint, AdminComplaint, History — see §200+). Until each of the routes above is also swap-retired, its backing legacy VM stays LIVE.

The autonomous retire campaign has hit a triple-blocker. Continuing autonomously would require either:

Per the standing block-and-ask trigger for "observable behavior change," each route swap requires user authorization. Cannot be opened autonomously.

### Postscript content

Each surgical edit appends a `> **§253 postscript — …**` blockquote
**after** the original table/list/section, preserving the historical
content for audit-trail readability. The postscript cross-cites both
the §-number of the retiring slice and the commit SHA (`44d3a4e` /
`aa64692` / `b0c6e98` / `ecf1e65` / `659adbc`) so a future reader can
trace from the audit table forward to the actual retirement evidence.

### Audit-trail philosophy (`staleKdocSweep` discipline)

The repeated pattern across all six prior `staleKdocSweep` commits
(§229 / §242 / §311 / §391 / §413 / §400) plus this one (§253) is the
same — once a downstream slice retires a member, the upstream audit
sections that document the member's LIVE-ness become temporally
inaccurate but **historically accurate**. The audit trail's value comes
from being able to read the chain `prune-audit → reachers-table →
later-prune-fulfillment` and understand the decision process at each
point in time. Rewriting the original table in-place would destroy
that chain. The postscript approach preserves both the historical
verdict and the current-state truth.

This is the second `staleKdocSweep` after a multi-slice rework-parity
campaign (cf. §413 which swept after a 5-slice ReaderViewModel
campaign). The pattern of "let parity campaign land, then sweep the
docs cumulatively" is now firmly established as the audit-trail
hygiene discipline for compound retirements.

## §254 — Phase 9.x.dialogstate.retire — delete orphan `:shared/.../features/details/domain/DialogState.kt`

### Strategy

The `staleKdocSweep` commit at §253 closed out the deferred-docs item
from Slice 5 (§430). After that close-out, an immediate cascade-orphan
audit was run against the surviving `:shared/.../presentation/features/
details/` tree to surface any newly-unreachable members.

That audit found exactly one survivor in the entire subtree:

```
shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/
  features/details/
    └── domain/
        └── DialogState.kt      (3 lines, single enum, ZERO LIVE reachers)
```

The file's full body:

```kotlin
package me.manga.kira.presentation.features.details.domain

enum class DialogState { AdultWarning, MStep1, MStep2, None }
```

### Reach-chain audit (3-pass)

| Pass | Pattern | Hits | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (import) | `import.*DialogState` across entire repo | **0** | No code imports |
| 2 (bare) | `\bDialogState\b` across `*.kt` | 2 | Definition itself + 1 KDoc-text mention |
| 3 (any extension) | `DialogState` across the whole repo | 8 | The above 2 + 6 historical mentions in `ARCHITECTURE.md` / `SOLID_AUDIT.md` |

The single non-definition `.kt` mention was in
`ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/details/DetailsScreen.kt:667`
— a KDoc text reference inside the `AdultConfirmationDialog` composable's
documentation that compared the rework's plain dismiss to the legacy's
`DialogState.MStep1` progression. That mention was rewritten in this
slice to explicitly tombstone the enum reference (text now says "the
`MStep1` state on its since-retired `DialogState` enum — see §254").

The 6 `ARCHITECTURE.md` mentions break down as:

- **§48.3** (rework Details design rationale, lines ~4789-4823) — quotes
  the legacy `remember { mutableStateOf(DialogState.AdultWarning) }`
  block to explain the rework's `var adultDialogVisible by remember(...)`
  delta. This is **historical design-decision prose** that legitimately
  references the legacy enum to explain why the rework chose a `Boolean`
  flag. The prose remains accurate (the legacy enum DID exist and DID
  have those 4 cases); only its temporal framing is now past-tense.
  **NOT rewritten** — the audit-trail-preservation discipline (§253)
  applies here too.

- **§204** (next-slice-candidate carry-over, line ~32282) — historical
  orphan-survey entry that said `DialogState` was "blocked on MangaDetails
  rework swap". The block lifted at §430; the retire landed here. **NOT
  rewritten** — historical survey output.

- **§206** (next-slice-candidate block, line ~32447) — same posture as
  §204, same not-rewritten verdict.

- **`SOLID_AUDIT.md`** (line ~11146) — mentions "dialog state" lowercase
  in unrelated `LanguageState.kt` prose. Not a reach.

`shared/.../features/details/` were pruned by `rmdir` after the file
delete; git doesn't track empty dirs so this is implicit.

### Why this retire was safe to land without user direction

Per the Rule 3 "audit-trail surfaces the next productive target" discipline
established across §§370-421, an orphan whose 3-pass reach audit returns
zero LIVE imports + zero code reachers is **not** a route-swap candidate
or a behavior-change candidate — it's a tombstone. The block-and-ask
criteria (contract library blocker / observable behavior change / feature
stops compiling / unresolvable SOLID violation) all evaluate to false:

- **Contract library blocker** — `DialogState` is not a contract surface.
  It was a `:shared` legacy `MangaDetailsScreen` local-state type.
- **Observable behavior change** — the only consumer (legacy
  `MangaDetailsScreen.kt`) was deleted in §430. No active surface
  references the enum.
- **Feature stops compiling** — `DialogState`'s consumers are all gone;
  the file compiles in isolation but contributes nothing.
- **Unresolvable SOLID violation** — none; this is a leaf delete.

Per Rule 3 + the user's standing "no deferral" directive, the retire
proceeds.

### Build gates

Android Debug + iOS Arm64 + iOS SimulatorArm64 + Desktop. Source files
modified (`DetailsScreen.kt` KDoc), so this is NOT a docs-only commit
despite the change being trivially textual — `:ui` recompile required to
guarantee the KDoc edit didn't accidentally trip a `kotlinc` warning
about an unresolved reference inside backticks (kotlinc doesn't resolve
backticked KDoc symbols, but the linter precedent in §253's build-gate
section is to verify anyway).

### Carry-over

No carry-over. After this slice, the `:shared/.../presentation/features/
details/` subtree is **fully retired** — the entire feature now lives in
the rework `:domain` + `:data` + `:presentation` + `:ui` chain. Future
retire-chain work continues from the §252 waypoint per the queue items
already documented there.
